\section*{Number Meanings}

\noindent 1: Unity, God’s Sovereignty\par
\noindent Represents the oneness of God (Deuteronomy 6:4, "The Lord our God is one"). Symbolizes primacy and the beginning.\par
\noindent 2: Union, Division, or Witness\par
\noindent Signifies partnership or confirmation by two witnesses (Ecclesiastes 4:9; Matthew 18:16). Can also indicate contrast or division.\par
\noindent 3: Divine Completeness, Trinity\par
\noindent Reflects the Trinity (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) and divine perfection (Matthew 28:19; John 21:14, Jesus’ third appearance post-resurrection).\par
\noindent 4: Creation, Universality\par
\noindent Associated with the created world (four corners of the earth, four seasons; Revelation 7:1). Represents God’s creative works.\par
\noindent 5: Grace, God’s Goodness\par
\noindent Linked to God’s favor and grace (five offerings in Leviticus; Genesis 43:34, five portions for Benjamin). Often tied to human weakness met by divine strength.\par
\noindent 6: Humanity, Imperfection\par
\noindent Represents human effort or falling short of divine perfection (created on the sixth day, Genesis 1:26-31; 666 as the number of the beast, Revelation 13:18).\par
\noindent 7: Perfection, Completion\par
\noindent Denotes spiritual perfection and God’s completed work (seven days of creation, Genesis 2:2; seven seals in Revelation). Highly significant in Scripture.\par
\noindent 8: New Beginnings\par
\noindent Symbolizes renewal or a new order (eight people saved on Noah’s ark, Genesis 7:13; circumcision on the eighth day, Leviticus 12:3). Represents resurrection and "born again".\par
\noindent 9: Divine Completeness, Finality\par
\noindent Symbolizes divine completeness or finality (nine fruits of the Holy Spirit, Galatians 5:22-23; nine people with leprosy in Scripture).\par
\noindent 10: Divine Order, Completeness of Order\par
\noindent Represents a complete system or human responsibility (Ten Commandments, Exodus 20; ten plagues, Exodus 7-12).\par
\noindent 11: Disorder, Chaos, Judgment\par
\noindent Symbolizes disorder or judgment (eleven dukes of Edom; eleven officials offended by truth).\par
\noindent 12: God’s Government, Authority\par
\noindent Indicates divine authority or organization (twelve tribes of Israel, Genesis 49:28; twelve apostles, Matthew 10:1-2). Denotes the Creator's foundation or perfect authority\par
\noindent 13: Rebellion, Lawlessness\par
\noindent Symbolic of rebellion (Nimrod as generation 13 in Ham's line; thirteen things that defile a person).\par
\noindent 14: Double Spiritual Perfection\par
\noindent Multiplies the perfection of 7 (fourteen days for Passover; lineage from Abraham to Jesus in sets of 14).\par
\noindent 15: Rest After Deliverance\par
\noindent Symbolizes rest following deliverance (Feast of Unleavened Bread on Nisan 15). Key references: Genesis 15:12-16 (Abraham's vision), Exodus 12:40-42 (Exodus from Egypt).\par
\noindent 16: Love and Loving\par
\noindent Represents the duality of true love (16 qualities of God's love in 1 Corinthians 13:4-8). Key references: Genesis 46:18 (Jacob's migration), 1 Corinthians 13:4-8.\par
\noindent 17: Overcoming the Enemy, Victory\par
\noindent Represents complete victory (ten + seven; Day of Atonement themes).\par
\noindent 18: Bondage\par
\noindent Symbolizes physical or spiritual bondage (Israelites oppressed for 18 years). Key references: Judges 3:14, Luke 13:11-12 (woman healed after 18 years).\par
\noindent 19: God's Perfect Order in Judgment\par
\noindent Symbolizes perfect order concerning judgment (10 + 9). Key references: Joshua 19:38 (Naphtali's cities), Psalm 19 (heavens declare God's glory).\par
\noindent 20: Perfect Waiting\par
\noindent Symbolizes complete waiting (twice ten; age for Levite service).\par
\noindent 21: Great Wickedness, Rebellion, and Sin\par
\noindent Represents an outgrowth of sin and rebellion (21 sins in 2 Timothy 3:1-5). Key references: 2 Timothy 3:1-5, Revelation 21:21 (New Jerusalem).\par
\noindent 22: Light\par
\noindent Symbolizes light and revelation (22 Hebrew letters). Key references: Psalms 119:105, John 12:46.\par
\noindent 23: Divine Protection and Guidance\par
\noindent Symbolizes protection, blessing, and judgment (Psalm 23). Key references: Psalm 23, 1 Corinthians 10:8 (23,000 fell).\par
\noindent 24: Priesthood\par
\noindent Symbolizes the priesthood and worship (24 courses of priests). Key references: 1 Chronicles 23-24, Revelation 4:4 (24 elders).\par
\noindent 25: Grace Upon Grace\par
\noindent Symbolizes multiplied grace (25 cubits in Ezekiel's temple). Key references: John 1:16-17, Ezekiel 40:13.\par
\noindent 26: Eternal God (YHWH)\par
\noindent Symbolizes God's eternal nature (Gematria of YHWH=26). Key references: Genesis 1:26 (creation in God's image), Exodus (Moses as 26th generation).\par
\noindent 30: Dedication to a Task\par
\noindent Represents dedication or maturity (Jesus' ministry at 30; price of betrayal).\par
\noindent 33: God's Promises\par
\noindent Connected to divine promises (Jesus' age at death; 33 times "three" in Revelation).\par
\noindent 40: Testing, Trial, Preparation\par
\noindent Associated with periods of testing or probation (40 days of rain in Noah’s flood, Genesis 7:12; Jesus’ 40 days in the wilderness, Matthew 4:2).\par
\noindent 50: Holy Spirit, Pentecost, Deliverance\par
\noindent Linked to the outpouring of God's Spirit (Pentecost, 50 days after Passover; Jubilee every 50 years;).\par
\noindent 60: Threshold of Later Life, Pride\par
\noindent Represents entering life's final phase (threescore years; influences like pride in parables;).\par
\noindent 70: Completeness, Restoration\par
\noindent Represents fullness or a significant period (70 years of exile, Jeremiah 25:11; 70 disciples sent out, Luke 10:1).\par
\noindent 666: Perfection of Imperfection, Beast\par
\noindent Symbolizes ultimate human imperfection and Satan's system (mark of the Beast, Revelation 13:18)\par

\section*{Genesis}
\subsection*{Genesis 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth. \textsuperscript{2} But the earth was unsightly and unfurnished, and darkness was over the deep, and the Spirit of God moved over the water. \textsuperscript{3} And God said, Let there be light, and there was light. \textsuperscript{4} And God saw the light that it was good, and God divided between the light and the darkness. \textsuperscript{5} And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night, and there was evening and there was morning, the first day.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 1:1 Brenton note: Name of God: Elohim (אֱלֹהִים) — God; mighty one(s) Common English renderings: God. The most common opening name for God in Scripture; grammatically plural in form but regularly used with singular verbs for the one true God.\par
Genesis 1:1 Brenton note: Hebrew background: Elohim (אֱלֹהִים) = God; gods. Common English renderings: God; gods; divine beings. Morphologically plural but often takes singular verbs for the God of Israel.\par
Genesis 1:1 Brenton note: Hebrew background: erets (אֶרֶץ) = earth; land. Common English renderings: earth; land; country. May denote the whole earth or a specific territory depending on context.\par
Genesis 1:1 Brenton note: Hebrew background: shamayim (שָׁמַיִם) = heavens; sky. Common English renderings: heaven; heavens; sky. A plural form commonly used for the sky and heavenly realm.\par
Genesis 1:1 Brenton note: Hebrew background: bara (בָּרָא) = to create. Common English renderings: create. In the Hebrew Bible God is the usual subject of this verb.\par
Genesis 1:1 Brenton note: Greek background: theos (θεός) = God; god. Common English renderings: God; god. In context this lemma may denote the true God or a false god.\par
Genesis 1:1 Brenton note: Greek background: ouranos (οὐρανός) = heaven; sky. Common English renderings: heaven; heavens. The plural heavens often underlies English singular heaven.\par
Genesis 1:1 Brenton note: Greek background: gē (γῆ) = earth; land. Common English renderings: earth; land. Can mean the whole earth or a particular land.\par
Genesis 1:2 Brenton note: Hebrew background: ruach (רוּחַ) = spirit; wind; breath. Common English renderings: spirit; wind. A major term for spirit, breath, or wind, with meaning determined by context.\par
Genesis 1:2 Brenton note: Hebrew background: mayim (מַיִם) = water. Common English renderings: water; waters. Plural form often functioning as a mass noun.\par
Genesis 1:2 Brenton note: Hebrew background: choshekh (חֹשֶׁךְ) = darkness. Common English renderings: darkness. Frequently paired with light in literal and metaphorical contrast.\par
Genesis 1:2 Brenton note: Hebrew background: panim (פָּנִים) = face; presence. Common English renderings: face; presence. Plural form often used for personal presence or surface.\par
Genesis 1:2 Brenton note: Greek background: pneuma (πνεῦμα) = spirit; wind; breath. Common English renderings: Spirit; spirit; wind. Meaning is determined by context: divine Spirit, human spirit, wind, or breath.\par
Genesis 1:2 Brenton note: Greek background: hydōr (ὕδωρ) = water. Common English renderings: water. A common creation term that also carries symbolic force in Scripture.\par
Genesis 1:2 Brenton note: Greek background: skotos (σκότος) = darkness. Common English renderings: darkness. A major biblical image for darkness, ignorance, evil, and judgment.\par
Genesis 1:2 Brenton note: Greek background: prosōpon (πρόσωπον) = face; presence. Common English renderings: face; presence. Can mean face, appearance, or presence.\par
Genesis 1:3 Brenton note: Hebrew background: or (אוֹר) = light. Common English renderings: light. A major theological image for life, revelation, and salvation.\par
Genesis 1:3 Brenton note: Hebrew background: amar (אָמַר) = to say. Common English renderings: say. The most common verb of speech in biblical Hebrew.\par
Genesis 1:3 Brenton note: Greek background: phōs (φῶς) = light. Common English renderings: light. A major biblical image for creation, truth, holiness, and revelation.\par
Genesis 1:4 Brenton note: Gr. and between the darkness. Hebraism.\par
Genesis 1:4 Brenton note: Hebrew background: tov (טוֹב) = good. Common English renderings: good. Broad term for moral, functional, and aesthetic goodness.\par
Genesis 1:4 Brenton note: Hebrew background: ra’ah (רָאָה) = to see. Common English renderings: see. Can imply perception, provision, or concern.\par
Genesis 1:4 Brenton note: Hebrew background: badal (בָּדַל) = to divide; separate. Common English renderings: divide; separate. Creation and holiness term of distinction.\par
Genesis 1:4 TSK note: that, ;, the light from the darkness Heb. between the light and between the darkness\par
Genesis 1:5 Brenton note: Hebrew background: yom (יוֹם) = day. Common English renderings: day. Can mean daylight, a full day, or an era depending on context.\par
Genesis 1:5 Brenton note: Hebrew background: laylah (לַיְלָה) = night. Common English renderings: night. The regular counterpart to day in the creation account and beyond.\par
Genesis 1:5 Brenton note: Hebrew background: qara (קָרָא) = to call; proclaim; read. Common English renderings: call; proclaim; read. Very broad term for naming, summoning, and proclamation.\par
Genesis 1:5 Brenton note: Hebrew background: echad (אַחַד) = one. Common English renderings: one. Can denote singularity, unity, or firstness in sequence.\par
Genesis 1:5 Brenton note: Greek background: hēmera (ἡμέρα) = day. Common English renderings: day. Can refer to a day, daylight, or a defined time period.\par
Genesis 1:5 Brenton note: Greek background: nyx (νύξ) = night. Common English renderings: night. Used literally and sometimes figuratively for darkness.\par
Genesis 1:5 TSK note: and;, ; And the evening and the morning were Heb. And the evening was, and the morning was\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the water, and let it be a division between water and water, and it was so. \textsuperscript{7} And God made the firmament, and God divided between the water which was under the firmament and the water which was above the firmament. \textsuperscript{8} And God called the firmament Heaven, and God saw that it was good, and there was evening and there was morning, the second day.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 1:6 Brenton note: Hebrew background: tavekh (תָּוֶךְ) = midst; middle. Common English renderings: midst. Frequent relational term for being among or within.\par
Genesis 1:6 TSK note: Let there, ;, ;, ;, ; , ; firmament Heb. expansion\par
Genesis 1:7 Brenton note: Hebrew background: asah (עָשָׂה) = to do; make. Common English renderings: do; make. One of the most common verbs, used widely for God’s actions and human deeds.\par
Genesis 1:7 Brenton note: Hebrew background: tachat (תַּחַת) = under; instead of. Common English renderings: under; instead of. Spatial and substitutionary term.\par
Genesis 1:7 Brenton note: Hebrew background: ken (כֵּן) = so; thus; right; yes. Common English renderings: so; thus; yes. Its sound matches the English name Ken; the resemblance is coincidental, while the Hebrew word means so, thus, right, or yes.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} And God said, Let the water which is under the heaven be collected into one place, and let the dry land appear, and it was so. And the water which was under the heaven was collected into its places, and the dry land appeared. \textsuperscript{10} And God called the dry land Earth, and the gatherings of the waters he called Seas, and God saw that it was good. \textsuperscript{11} And God said, Let the earth bring forth the herb of grass bearing seed according to its kind and according to its likeness, and the fruit-tree bearing fruit whose seed is in it, according to its kind on the earth, and it was so. \textsuperscript{12} And the earth brought forth the herb of grass bearing seed according to its kind and according to its likeness, and the fruit tree bearing fruit whose seed is in it, according to its kind on the earth, and God saw that it was good. \textsuperscript{13} And there was evening and there was morning, the third day.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 1:9 Brenton note: Gr. meeting.\par
Genesis 1:9 Brenton note: Gr. their meetings.\par
Genesis 1:9 Brenton note: Hebrew background: maqom (מָקוֹם) = place. Common English renderings: place. Common term for location, sometimes reverentially for God’s place.\par
Genesis 1:9 Brenton note: Hebrew background: qavah (קָוָה) = to wait; hope. Common English renderings: wait; hope. Elsewhere a major hope term though this first use is from a different sense/etymology in some analyses.\par
Genesis 1:9 Brenton note: Hebrew background: el (אֶל) = to; toward. Common English renderings: to; unto. Direction marker preposition.\par
Genesis 1:10 Brenton note: Gr. systems.\par
Genesis 1:10 Brenton note: Hebrew background: yam (יָם) = sea. Common English renderings: sea. Also used for large bodies of water such as the Mediterranean.\par
Genesis 1:10 Brenton note: Greek background: thalassa (θάλασσα) = sea. Common English renderings: sea. A major creation and exodus term.\par
Genesis 1:11 Brenton note: Gr. sowing.\par
Genesis 1:11 Brenton note: Gr. Alex. + εἰς ὁμοιότητα.\par
Genesis 1:11 Brenton note: Hebrew background: ets (עֵץ) = tree; wood. Common English renderings: tree; wood. Context can emphasize living tree or timber/wood.\par
Genesis 1:11 Brenton note: Hebrew background: peri (פְּרִי) = fruit. Common English renderings: fruit. Used for produce, offspring, and metaphorical results.\par
Genesis 1:11 Brenton note: Hebrew background: zera (זֶרַע) = seed; offspring. Common English renderings: seed; offspring. A key covenant term for descendants and promise.\par
Genesis 1:11 Brenton note: Hebrew background: min (מִן) = from. Common English renderings: from; of. Preposition of source, separation, or partitive relation.\par
Genesis 1:11 Brenton note: Greek background: sperma (σπέρμα) = seed; offspring. Common English renderings: seed; offspring. Can mean seed for sowing or descendants.\par
Genesis 1:11 Brenton note: Greek background: karpos (καρπός) = fruit; produce; result. Common English renderings: fruit. Used literally of produce and figuratively of outcomes.\par
Genesis 1:11 Brenton note: Greek background: dendron (δένδρον) = tree. Common English renderings: tree. A common natural term with symbolic uses.\par
Genesis 1:11 Brenton note: Greek background: chortos (χόρτος) = grass; herbage. Common English renderings: grass. Used of grass, fodder, or green growth.\par
Genesis 1:11 Brenton note: Greek background: xylon (ξύλον) = wood; tree; timber. Common English renderings: tree; wood. Can mean wood, timber, tree, or wooden instrument.\par
Genesis 1:11 TSK note: Let the; , ; grass Heb. tender grass fruit\par
\end{quote}

Genesis 1:14 Brenton note: Hebrew background: ot (אוֹת) = sign; mark. Common English renderings: sign; token. Used for miraculous signs, covenant tokens, and symbolic markers.\par

Genesis 1:16 Brenton note: Hebrew background: memshalah (מֶמְשָׁלָה) = dominion; rule. Common English renderings: dominion; rule. Used for governmental authority and dominion.\par
Genesis 1:16 Brenton note: Hebrew background: qatan (קָטָן) = small; little; young. Common English renderings: small; little; least. Used of size, age, and status.\par
Genesis 1:16 Brenton note: Hebrew background: gadol (גָּדוֹל) = great; large. Common English renderings: great; large. Common term for greatness, size, and rank.\par
Genesis 1:16 Brenton note: Hebrew background: shenayim (שְׁנַיִם) = two. Common English renderings: two. Basic numeral, important in witness and pair contexts.\par
Genesis 1:16 Brenton note: Greek background: astēr (ἀστήρ) = star. Common English renderings: star. A celestial term with narrative and symbolic significance.\par
Genesis 1:16 Brenton note: Greek background: hēlios (ἥλιος) = sun. Common English renderings: sun. A creation term that also appears in poetic and apocalyptic contexts.\par
Genesis 1:16 Brenton note: Greek background: selēnē (σελήνη) = moon. Common English renderings: moon. The standard Greek term for moon.\par
Genesis 1:16 TSK note: to rule Heb. for the rule, etc.; , ;, ;, ;, ; , he made the stars also Or, with the stars also\par
Genesis 1:17 Brenton note: Hebrew background: natan (נָתַן) = to give. Common English renderings: give. Broad verb for giving, setting, appointing, and handing over.\par
Genesis 1:18 Brenton note: Hebrew background: mashal (מָשַׁל) = to rule; speak proverb. Common English renderings: rule. A different noun form gives proverb; the verb here is dominion.\par
\end{quote}

Genesis 1:20 Brenton note: Hebrew background: nephesh (נֶפֶשׁ) = soul; life; living being. Common English renderings: soul; life. Often denotes the living self or life rather than an abstract immaterial soul.\par
Genesis 1:20 Brenton note: Hebrew background: nephesh chayyah (נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה) = living creature. Common English renderings: living creature; living soul. Compound phrase used for animals and humanity as living beings.\par
Genesis 1:20 Brenton note: Hebrew background: of (עוֹף) = bird; flying creature. Common English renderings: fowl; bird. General term for flying creatures.\par

\subsection*{Genesis 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now the serpent was the most crafty of all the brutes on the earth, which the Lord God made, and the serpent said to the woman, Wherefore has God said, Eat not of every tree of the garden? \textsuperscript{2} And the woman said to the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden, \textsuperscript{3} but of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die. \textsuperscript{4} And the serpent said to the woman, Ye shall not surely die. \textsuperscript{5} For God knew that in whatever day ye should eat of it your eyes would be opened, and ye would be as gods, knowing good and evil. \textsuperscript{6} And the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes to look upon and beautiful to contemplate, and having taken of its fruit she ate, and she gave to her husband also with her, and they ate. \textsuperscript{7} And the eyes of both were opened, and they perceived that they were naked, and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons to go round them. \textsuperscript{8} And they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden in the afternoon; and both Adam and his wife hid themselves from the face of the Lord God in the midst of the trees of the garden. \textsuperscript{9} And the Lord God called Adam and said to him, Adam, where art thou? \textsuperscript{10} And he said to him, I heard thy voice as thou walkedst in the garden, and I feared because I was naked and I hid myself. \textsuperscript{11} And God said to him, Who told thee that thou wast naked, unless thou hast eaten of the tree concerning which I charged thee of it alone not to eat? \textsuperscript{12} And Adam said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me—she gave me of the tree and I ate. \textsuperscript{13} And the Lord God said to the woman, Why hast thou done this? And the woman said, The serpent deceived me and I ate.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{14} And the Lord God said to the serpent, Because thou hast done this thou art cursed above all cattle and all the brutes of the earth, on thy breast and belly thou shalt go, and thou shalt eat earth all the days of thy life. \textsuperscript{15} And I will put enmity between thee and the woman and between thy seed and her seed, he shall watch against thy head, and thou shalt watch against his heel. \textsuperscript{16} And to the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy pains and thy groanings; in pain thou shalt bring forth children, and thy submission shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee. \textsuperscript{17} And to Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened to the voice of thy wife, and eaten of the tree concerning which I charged thee of it only not to eat—of that thou hast eaten, cursed is the ground in thy labours, in pain shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life. \textsuperscript{18} Thorns and thistles shall it bring forth to thee, and thou shalt eat the herb of the field. \textsuperscript{19} In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat thy bread until thou return to the earth out of which thou wast taken, for earth thou art and to earth thou shalt return. \textsuperscript{20} And Adam called the name of his wife Life, because she was the mother of all living. \textsuperscript{21} And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife garments of skin, and clothed them.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{8} And Cain said to Abel his brother, Let us go out into the plain; and it came to pass that when they were in the plain Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. \textsuperscript{9} And the Lord God said to Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? and he said, I know not, am I my brother's keeper? \textsuperscript{10} And the Lord said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood cries to me out of the ground. \textsuperscript{11} And now thou art cursed from the earth which has opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand. \textsuperscript{12} When thou tillest the earth, then it shall not continue to give its strength to thee: thou shalt be groaning and trembling on the earth. \textsuperscript{13} And Cain said to the Lord God, My crime is too great for me to be forgiven. \textsuperscript{14} If thou castest me out this day from the face of the earth, and I shall be hidden from thy presence, and I shall be groaning and trembling upon the earth, then it will be that any one that finds me shall slay me. \textsuperscript{15} And the Lord God said to him, Not so, any one that slays Cain shall suffer seven-fold vengeance; and the Lord God set a mark upon Cain that no one that found him might slay him. \textsuperscript{16} So Cain went forth from the presence of God and dwelt in the land of Nod over against Edem.\par

\subsection*{Genesis 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} This is the genealogy of men in the day in which God made Adam; in the image of God he made him: \textsuperscript{2} male and female he made them, and blessed them; and he called his name Adam, in the day in which he made them. \textsuperscript{3} And Adam lived two hundred and thirty years, and begot a son after his own form, and after his own image, and he called his name Seth. \textsuperscript{4} And the days of Adam, which he lived after his begetting Seth, were seven hundred years; and he begot sons and daughters. \textsuperscript{5} And all the days of Adam which he lived were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died. \textsuperscript{6} Now Seth lived two hundred and five years, and begot Enos. \textsuperscript{7} And Seth lived after his begetting Enos, seven hundred and seven years, and he begot sons and daughters. \textsuperscript{8} And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died. \textsuperscript{9} And Enos lived an hundred and ninety years, and begot Cainan. \textsuperscript{10} And Enos lived after his begetting Cainan, seven hundred and fifteen years, and he begot sons and daughters. \textsuperscript{11} And all the days of Enos were nine hundred and five years, and he died. \textsuperscript{12} And Cainan lived an hundred and seventy years, and he begot Maleleel. \textsuperscript{13} And Cainan lived after his begetting Maleleel, seven hundred and forty years, and he begot sons and daughters. \textsuperscript{14} And all the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 5:1 Brenton note: Gr. book of generation.\par
Genesis 5:1 Brenton note: Hebrew background: sefer (סֵפֶר) = book; scroll; document. Common English renderings: book; bill; scroll. Written record term of lasting importance.\par
Genesis 5:1 TSK note: book The original word rendered "book, " signifies a register, account, history, or any kind of writing., ; in the likeness\par
Genesis 5:2 Brenton note: Alex. their.\par
Genesis 5:3 Brenton note: Hebrew background: shanah (שָׁנָה) = year. Common English renderings: year. Basic time term, also used verbally for repetition in another stem.\par
Genesis 5:3 Brenton note: Hebrew background: me’ah (מֵאָה) = hundred. Common English renderings: hundred. Common counting term in narrative and law.\par
Genesis 5:3 Brenton note: Greek background: etos (ἔτος) = year. Common English renderings: year. A basic chronological term.\par
Genesis 5:3 TSK note: am 130, bc 3874 hundred The chronology differs in the Hebrew Text, the Samaritan, the LXX, and Josephus. The LXX adds 100 years to each of the patriarchs Adam, Seth, Enos, Cainan, Mahalaleel, and Enoch, before the birth of their sons; while they take 20 from the age of Methuselah, and add 6 to that of Lamech Thus the space from the creation to the deluge is made 2, 242 years, according to the Vatican copy, but 2, 262 by the Alexandrine; and the sum total by Josephus is 2, 265, by the Samaritan 1, 307, and the Hebrew Text, 1, 656. The sum total from the Deluge to the 70th year of Terah, according to these authorities, is, Heb. 292; Sam. 942; Sept. Vat. 1, 172; Alex. 1, 072, and Josephus 1, 002. in his, ;, ; called\par

Genesis 5:4 Brenton note: Hebrew background: achar (אַחַר) = after; behind. Common English renderings: after. Temporal and spatial after-ness term.\par
Genesis 5:5 TSK note: am 930, bc 3074 nine, ; and he died\par
Genesis 5:9 Brenton note: Name meaning: Kenan (Kenan) — Possession; smith; spear Continues the line; name echoes the acquired theme of the pre-flood world.\par
Genesis 5:9 TSK note: am 325, bc 3679 Cainan Heb. Kenan\par
Genesis 5:12 Brenton note: Name meaning: Mahalalel (Mahalalel) — Praise of God; the shining one of God His very name is a shout of praise in a darkening world.\par
Genesis 5:12 TSK note: am 395, bc 3609 Mahalaleel Gr. Maleleel\par
\end{quote}

\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And all the earth was one lip, and there was one language to all. \textsuperscript{2} And it came to pass as they moved from the east, they found a plain in the land of Senaar, and they dwelt there. \textsuperscript{3} And a man said to his neighbour, Come, let us make bricks and bake them with fire. \noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Abram went up out of Egypt, he and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the wilderness. \textsuperscript{2} And Abram was very rich in cattle, and silver, and gold. \textsuperscript{3} And he went to the place whence he came, into the wilderness as far as Bæthel, as far as the place where his tent was before, between Bæthel and Aggai, \textsuperscript{4} to the place of the altar, which he built there at first, and Abram there called on the name of the Lord. \textsuperscript{5} And Lot who went out with Abram had sheep, and oxen, and tents. \textsuperscript{6} And the land was not large enough for them to live together, because their possessions were great; and the land was not large enough for them to live together. \textsuperscript{7} And there was a strife between the herdmen of Abram's cattle, and the herdmen of Lot's cattle, and the Chananites and the Pherezites then inhabited the land. \textsuperscript{8} And Abram said to Lot, Let there not be a strife between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen, for we are brethren. \textsuperscript{9} Lo! is not the whole land before thee? Separate thyself from me; if thou goest to the left, I will go to the right, and if thou goest to the right, I will go to the left. \textsuperscript{10} And Lot having lifted up his eyes, observed all the country round about Jordan, that it was all watered, before God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrha, as the garden of the Lord, and as the land of Egypt, until thou come to Zogora. \textsuperscript{11} And Lot chose for himself all the country round Jordan, and Lot went from the east, and they were separated each from his brother. And Abram dwelt in the land of Chanaan. \textsuperscript{12} And Lot dwelt in a city of the neighbouring people, and pitched his tent in Sodom. \textsuperscript{13} But the men of Sodom were evil, and exceedingly sinful before God. \textsuperscript{14} And God said to Abram after Lot was separated from him, Look up with thine eyes, and behold from the place where thou now art northward and southward, and eastward and seaward; \textsuperscript{15} for all the land which thou seest, I will give it to thee and to thy seed for ever. \textsuperscript{16} And I will make thy seed like the dust of the earth; if any one is able to number the dust of the earth, then shall thy seed be numbered. \textsuperscript{17} Arise and traverse the land, both in the length of it and in the breadth; for to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever. \textsuperscript{18} And Abram having removed his tent, came and dwelt by the oak of Mambre, which was in Chebrom, and he there built an altar to the Lord.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize

\subsection*{Genesis 14}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And it came to pass in the reign of Amarphal king of Sennaar, and Arioch king of Ellasar, that Chodollogomor king of Elam, and Thargal king of nations, \textsuperscript{2} made war with Balla king of Sodom, and with Barsa king of Gomorrha, and with Sennaar, king of Adama, and with Symobor king of Seboim and the king of Balac, this is Segor. \textsuperscript{3} All these met with one consent at the salt valley; this is now the sea of salt. \textsuperscript{4} Twelve years they served Chodollogomor, and the thirteenth year they revolted. \textsuperscript{5} And in the fourteenth year came Chodollogomor, and the kings with him, and cut to pieces the giants in Astaroth, and Carnain, and strong nations with them, and the Ommæans in the city Save. \textsuperscript{6} And the Chorrhæans in the mountains of Seir, to the turpentine tree of Pharan, which is in the desert. \textsuperscript{7} And having turned back they came to the well of judgment; this is Cades, and they cut in pieces all the princes of Amalec, and the Amorites dwelling in Asasonthamar. \textsuperscript{8} And the king of Sodom went out, and the king of Gomorrha, and king of Adama, and king of Seboim, and king of Balac, this is Segor, and they set themselves in array against them for war in the salt valley, \textsuperscript{9} against Chodollogomor king of Elam, and Thargal king of nations, and Amarphal king of Sennaar, and Arioch king of Ellasar, the four kings against the five. \textsuperscript{10} Now the salt valley consists of slime-pits. And the king of Sodom fled and the king of Gomorrha, and they fell in there: and they that were left fled to the mountain country. \textsuperscript{11} And they took all the cavalry of Sodom and Gomorrha, and all their provisions, and departed. \textsuperscript{12} And they took also Lot the son of Abram's brother, and his baggage, and departed, for he dwelt in Sodom.\par

Genesis 14:3 Brenton note: Greek background: halas (ἅλας) = salt. Common English renderings: salt. A common substance with covenantal and symbolic associations.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{13} And one of them that had been rescued came and told Abram the Hebrew; and he dwelt by the oak of Mamre the Amorite the brother of Eschol, and the brother of Aunan, who were confederates with Abram. \textsuperscript{14} And Abram having heard that Lot his nephew had been taken captive, numbered his own home-born servants three hundred and eighteen, and pursued after them to Dan. \textsuperscript{15} And he came upon them by night, he and his servants, and he smote them and pursued them as far as Choba, which is on the left of Damascus. \textsuperscript{16} And he recovered all the cavalry of Sodom, and he recovered Lot his nephew, and all his possessions, and the women and the people. \textsuperscript{17} And the king of Sodom went out to meet him, after he returned from the slaughter of Chodollogomor, and the kings with him, to the valley of Saby; this was the plain of the kings.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{18} And Melchisedec king of Salem brought forth loaves and wine, and he was the priest of the most high God. \textsuperscript{19} And he blessed Abram, and said, Blessed be Abram of the most high God, who made heaven and earth, \textsuperscript{20} and blessed be the most high God who delivered thine enemies into thy power. And Abram gave him the tithe of all. \textsuperscript{21} And the king of Sodom said to Abram, Give me the men, and take the horses to thyself. \textsuperscript{22} And Abram said to the king of Sodom, I will stretch out my hand to the Lord the most high God, who made the heaven and the earth, \textsuperscript{23} that I will not take from all thy goods from a string to a shoe-latchet, lest thou shouldest say, I have made Abram rich. \textsuperscript{24} Except what things the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men that went with me, Eschol, Aunan, Mambre, these shall take a portion.\par

\subsection*{Genesis 15}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And after these things the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram, I shield thee, thy reward shall be very great. \textsuperscript{2} And Abram said, Master and Lord, what wilt thou give me? whereas I am departing without a child, but the son of Masek my home-born female slave, this Eliezer of Damascus is mine heir . \textsuperscript{3} And Abram said, I am grieved since thou hast given me no seed, but my home-born servant shall succeed me. \textsuperscript{4} And immediately there was a voice of the Lord to him, saying, This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come out of thee shall be thine heir. \textsuperscript{5} And he brought him out and said to him, Look up now to heaven, and count the stars, if thou shalt be able to number them fully, and he said, Thus shall thy seed be. \textsuperscript{6} And Abram believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness. \textsuperscript{7} And he said to him, I am God that brought thee out of the land of the Chaldeans, so as to give thee this land to inherit. \textsuperscript{8} And he said, Master and Lord, how shall I know that I shall inherit it? \textsuperscript{9} And he said to him, Take for me an heifer in her third year, and a she-goat in her third year, and a ram in his third year, and a dove and a pigeon. \textsuperscript{10} So he took to him all these, and divided them in the midst, and set them opposite to each other, but the birds he did not divide. \textsuperscript{11} And birds came down upon the bodies, even upon the divided parts of them, and Abram sat down by them. \textsuperscript{12} And about sunset a trance fell upon Abram, and lo! a great gloomy terror falls upon him. \textsuperscript{13} And it was said to Abram, Thou shalt surely know that thy seed shall be a sojourner in a land not their own, and they shall enslave them, and afflict them, and humble them four hundred years. \textsuperscript{14} And the nation whomsoever they shall serve I will judge; and after this, they shall come forth hither with much property. \textsuperscript{15} But thou shalt depart to thy fathers in peace, nourished in a good old age. \textsuperscript{16} And in the fourth generation they shall return hither, for the sins of the Amorites are not yet filled up, even until now. \textsuperscript{17} And when the sun was about to set, there was a flame, and behold a smoking furnace and lamps of fire, which passed between these divided pieces. \textsuperscript{18} In that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, To thy seed I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates. \textsuperscript{19} The Kenites, and the Kenezites, and the Kedmoneans, \textsuperscript{20} and the Chettites, and the Pherezites, and the Raphaim, \textsuperscript{21} and the Amorites, and the Chananites, and the Evites, and the Gergesites, and the Jebusites.\par

Genesis 15:1 Brenton note: Greek background: logos (λόγος) = word; speech; matter. Common English renderings: word; saying; matter. A broad term for word, message, report, or matter.\par

Genesis 15:15 Brenton note: Greek background: eirēnē (εἰρήνη) = peace. Common English renderings: peace. A key biblical term for peace, wholeness, and well-being.\par

\subsection*{Genesis 16}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Sara the wife of Abram bore him no children; and she had an Egyptian maid, whose name was Agar. \textsuperscript{2} And Sara said to Abram, Behold, the Lord has restrained me from bearing, go therefore in to my maid, that I may get children for myself through her. And Abram hearkened to the voice of Sara. \textsuperscript{3} So Sara the wife of Abram having taken Agar the Egyptian her handmaid, after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Chanaan, gave her to Abram her husband as a wife to him. \textsuperscript{4} And he went in to Agar, and she conceived, and saw that she was with child, and her mistress was dishonoured before her. \textsuperscript{5} And Sara said to Abram, I am injured by thee; I gave my handmaid into thy bosom, and when I saw that she was with child, I was dishonoured before her. The Lord judge between me and thee. \textsuperscript{6} And Abram said to Sara, Behold thy handmaid is in thy hands, use her as it may seem good to thee. And Sara afflicted her, and she fled from her face.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{7} And an angel of the Lord found her by the fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Sur. \textsuperscript{8} And the angel of the Lord said to her, Agar, Sara's maid, whence comest thou, and whither goest thou? and she said, I am fleeing from the face of my mistress Sara. \textsuperscript{9} And the angel of the Lord said to her, Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands. \textsuperscript{10} And the angel of the Lord said to her, I will surely multiply thy seed, and it shall not be numbered for multitude. \textsuperscript{11} And the angel of the Lord said to her, Behold, thou art with child, and shalt bear a son, and shalt call his name Ismael, for the Lord hath hearkened to thy humiliation. \textsuperscript{12} He shall be a wild man, his hands against all, and the hands of all against him, and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren. \textsuperscript{13} And she called the name of the Lord God who spoke to her, Thou art God who seest me; for she said, For I have openly seen him that appeared to me. \textsuperscript{14} Therefore she called the well, The well of him whom I have openly seen; behold it is between Cades and Barad. \textsuperscript{15} And Agar bore a son to Abram; and Abram called the name of his son which Agar bore to him, Ismael. \textsuperscript{16} And Abram was eighty-six years old, when Agar bore Ismael to Abram.\par

\subsection*{Genesis 17}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Abram was ninety-nine years old, and the Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, I am thy God, be well-pleasing before me, and be blameless. \textsuperscript{2} And I will establish my covenant between me and thee, and I will multiply thee exceedingly. \textsuperscript{3} And Abram fell upon his face, and God spoke to him, saying, \textsuperscript{4} And I, behold! my covenant is with thee, and thou shalt be a father of a multitude of nations. \textsuperscript{5} And thy name shall no more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraam, for I have made thee a father of many nations. \textsuperscript{6} And I will increase thee very exceedingly, and I will make nations of thee, and kings shall come out of thee. \textsuperscript{7} And I will establish my covenant between thee and thy seed after thee, to their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be thy God, and the God of thy seed after thee. \textsuperscript{8} And I will give to thee and to thy seed after thee the land wherein thou sojournest, even all the land of Chanaan for an everlasting possession, and I will be to them a God. \textsuperscript{9} And God said to Abraam, Thou also shalt fully keep my covenant, thou and thy seed after thee for their generations. \textsuperscript{10} And this is the covenant which thou shalt fully keep between me and you, and between thy seed after thee for their generations; every male of you shall be circumcised. \textsuperscript{11} And ye shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be for a sign of a covenant between me and you. \textsuperscript{12} And the child of eight days old shall be circumcised by you, every male throughout your generations, and the servant born in the house and he that is bought with money, of every son of a stranger, who is not of thy seed. \textsuperscript{13} He that is born in thy house, and he that is bought with money shall be surely circumcised, and my covenant shall be on your flesh for an everlasting covenant. \textsuperscript{14} And the uncircumcised male, who shall not be circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul shall be utterly destroyed from its family, for he has broken my covenant. \textsuperscript{15} And God said to Abraam, Sara thy wife—her name shall not be called Sara, Sarrha shall be her name. \textsuperscript{16} And I will bless her, and give thee a son of her, and I will bless him, and he shall become nations, and kings of nations shall be of him. \textsuperscript{17} And Abraam fell upon his face, and laughed; and spoke in his heart, saying, Shall there be a child to one who is a hundred years old, and shall Sarrha who is ninety years old, bear? \textsuperscript{18} And Abraam said to God, Let this Ismael live before thee. \textsuperscript{19} And God said to Abraam, Yea, behold, Sarrha thy wife shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name Isaac; and I will establish my covenant with him, for an everlasting covenant, to be a God to him and to his seed after him. \textsuperscript{20} And concerning Ismael, behold, I have heard thee, and, behold, I have blessed him, and will increase him and multiply him exceedingly; twelve nations shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation. \textsuperscript{21} But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarrha shall bear to thee at this time, in the next year. \textsuperscript{22} And he left off speaking with him, and God went up from Abraam.\par

Genesis 17:8 TSK note: And I, ;, wherein thou art a stranger Heb. of thy sojournings, everlasting;, ; their\par
Genesis 17:12 TSK note: he that is eight days old Heb. a son of eight days, ; , ; is born\par
Genesis 17:15 TSK note: As, ; Sarah i.e. princess\par
Genesis 17:16 TSK note: And I, ; give be a mother of nations Heb. become nations, ; kings\par

By this Abraham did not express his unbelief or weakness of faith, but his joy at the prospect of the fulfilment of so glorious a promise; and to this our Lord evidently alludes, .\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{23} And Abraam took Ismael his son, and all his home-born servants , and all those bought with money, and every male of the men in the house of Abraam, and he circumcised their foreskins in the time of that day, according as God spoke to him. \textsuperscript{24} And Abraam was ninety-nine years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin. \textsuperscript{25} And Ismael his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin. \textsuperscript{26} And at the period of that day, Abraam was circumcised, and Ismael his son, \textsuperscript{27} and all the men of his house, both those born in the house, and those bought with money of foreign nations.\par

Genesis 17:23 Brenton note: Greek background: oikia (οἰκία) = house; household. Common English renderings: house. Closely related to οἶκος, often emphasizing the dwelling.\par

\subsection*{Genesis 18}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And God appeared to him by the oak of Mambre, as he sat by the door of his tent at noon. \textsuperscript{2} And he lifted up his eyes and beheld, and lo! three men stood before him; and having seen them he ran to meet them from the door of his tent, and did obeisance to the ground. \textsuperscript{3} And he said, Lord, if indeed I have found grace in thy sight, pass not by thy servant. \textsuperscript{4} Let water now be brought, and let them wash your feet, and do ye refresh yourselves under the tree. \textsuperscript{5} And I will bring bread, and ye shall eat, and after this ye shall depart on your journey, on account of which refreshment ye have turned aside to your servant. And he said, So do, as thou hast said. \textsuperscript{6} And Abraam hasted to the tent to Sarrha, and said to her, Hasten, and knead three measures of fine flour, and make cakes. \textsuperscript{7} And Abraam ran to the kine, and took a young calf, tender and good, and gave it to his servant, and he hasted to dress it. \textsuperscript{8} And he took butter and milk, and the calf which he had dressed; and he set them before them, and they did eat, and he stood by them under the tree.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 18:1 TSK note: appeared, ; Mamre, and he sat In these verses we have a delightful picture of genuine and primitive hospitality. A venerable father sits at the tent door, not only to enjoy the current of refreshing air, but that if he saw any weary and exhausted travellers, he might invite them to rest and refresh themselves during the heat of the day, and the same custom still continues in the east. It was not the custom, nor was there any necessity, for strangers to knock at the door, or to speak first, but to stand till they were invited.\par
Genesis 18:2 Brenton note: Hebrew background: hishtachavah (הִשְׁתַּחֲוָה) = to bow down; worship. Common English renderings: worship; bow down. A physical act of prostration often expressing worship.\par
Genesis 18:2 Brenton note: Hebrew background: yatsav (יָצַב) = to stand firm; station oneself. Common English renderings: stand; set. Often for positioning oneself or something.\par
Genesis 18:2 Brenton note: Greek background: proskyneō (προσκυνέω) = to worship; bow down. Common English renderings: worship. The standard biblical verb for bowing down or worshiping.\par
Genesis 18:2 TSK note: And he, ; three, ; he ran bowed\par
Genesis 18:3 Brenton note: Greek background: kyrios (κύριος) = lord; master. Common English renderings: Lord; lord; master. This lemma can denote a human master or the divine title, depending on context.\par
Genesis 18:4 TSK note: wash your feet In those ancient times, shoes such as ours, were not in use; and the foot was protected only with sandals or soles, fastened round the foot with straps. It was, therefore, not only necessary from motives of cleanliness, but also a very great refreshment, in so hot a country, to get the feet washed at the end of a day's journey; and this is the first thing that Abraham proposes., ; tree Rest in the shade was the second requisite for the refreshment of a weary traveller.\par
Genesis 18:5 Brenton note: Hebrew background: sa’ad (סָעַד) = to support; sustain. Common English renderings: stay; sustain. Often of sustaining with food or divine support.\par
Genesis 18:5 TSK note: And I, ; bread This was the third requisite, and is introduced in its proper order; as eating immediately after exertion or fatigue is very unwholesome. comfort Heb. stay, ; are ye come Heb. ye have passed\par
Genesis 18:6 TSK note: Make ready quickly Heb. hasten three\par
Genesis 18:7 Brenton note: Hebrew background: par (פַּר) = bull. Common English renderings: bullock; bull. Frequent in sacrificial legislation.\par
Genesis 18:7 Brenton note: Greek background: moschos (μόσχος) = calf. Common English renderings: calf. A common sacrificial and pastoral term.\par
Genesis 18:8 Brenton note: Hebrew background: chalav (חָלָב) = milk. Common English renderings: milk. A staple food and symbol of abundance.\par
Genesis 18:8 Brenton note: Hebrew background: amad (עָמַד) = to stand. Common English renderings: stand. Standing implies readiness, endurance, or appearance before God.\par
Genesis 18:8 TSK note: he took; stood;, ; and they\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} And he said to him, Where is Sarrha thy wife? And he answered and said, Behold! in the tent. \textsuperscript{10} And he said, I will return and come to thee according to this period seasonably, and Sarrha thy wife shall have a son; and Sarrha heard at the door of the tent, being behind him. \textsuperscript{11} And Abraam and Sarrha were old, advanced in days, and the custom of women ceased with Sarrha. \textsuperscript{12} And Sarrha laughed in herself, saying, The thing has not as yet happened to me, even until now, and my lord is old. \textsuperscript{13} And the Lord said to Abraam, Why is it that Sarrha has laughed in herself, saying, Shall I then indeed bear? but I am grown old. \textsuperscript{14} Shall anything be impossible with the Lord? At this time I will return to thee seasonably, and Sarrha shall have a son. \textsuperscript{15} But Sarrha denied, saying, I did not laugh, for she was afraid. And he said to her, Nay, but thou didst laugh.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 18:11 Brenton note: Hebrew background: orach (אֹרַח) = path; way. Common English renderings: path. Often poetic synonym for דרך.\par
Genesis 18:11 Brenton note: Hebrew background: zaqen (זָקֵן) = old; elder. Common English renderings: old; elder. Can denote age or community leadership.\par
Genesis 18:12 Brenton note: Gr. The difference turns on the word עדנה. Heb. pleasure. Gr. until now.\par
Genesis 18:14 Brenton note: Greek background: kairos (καιρός) = appointed time; season. Common English renderings: time; season. Often signifies a fitting, appointed, or decisive time.\par
Genesis 18:14 Brenton note: Greek background: rhēma (ῥῆμα) = word; saying; utterance. Common English renderings: word; saying. Often denotes a spoken word or specific utterance.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} And the men having risen up from thence looked towards Sodom and Gomorrha. And Abraam went with them, attending them on their journey. \textsuperscript{17} And the Lord said, Shall I hide from Abraam my servant what things I intend to do? \textsuperscript{18} But Abraam shall become a great and populous nation, and in him shall all the nations of the earth be blest. \textsuperscript{19} For I know that he will order his sons, and his house after him, and they will keep the ways of the Lord, to do justice and judgment, that the Lord may bring upon Abraam all things whatsoever he has spoken to him. \textsuperscript{20} And the Lord said, The cry of Sodom and Gomorrha has been increased towards me, and their sins are very great. \textsuperscript{21} I will therefore go down and see, if they completely correspond with the cry which comes to me, and if not, that I may know. \textsuperscript{22} And the men having departed thence, came to Sodom; and Abraam was still standing before the Lord. \textsuperscript{23} And Abraam drew nigh and said, Wouldest thou destroy the righteous with the wicked, and shall the righteous be as the wicked? \textsuperscript{24} Should there be fifty righteous in the city, wilt thou destroy them? wilt thou not spare the whole place for the sake of the fifty righteous, if they be in it? \textsuperscript{25} By no means shalt thou do as this thing is so as to destroy the righteous with the wicked, so the righteous shall be as the wicked: by no means. Thou that judgest the whole earth, shalt thou not do right? \textsuperscript{26} And the Lord said, If there should be in Sodom fifty righteous in the city, I will spare the whole city, and the whole place for their sakes. \textsuperscript{27} And Abraam answered and said, Now I have begun to speak to my Lord, and I am earth and ashes. \textsuperscript{28} But if the fifty righteous should be diminished to forty-five, wilt thou destroy the whole city because of the five wanting ? And he said, I will not destroy it, if I should find there forty-five. \textsuperscript{29} And he continued to speak to him still, and said, But if there should be found there forty? And he said, I will not destroy it for the forty's sake. \textsuperscript{30} And he said, Will there be anything against me , Lord, if I shall speak? but if there be found there thirty? And he said, I will not destroy it for the thirty's sake. \textsuperscript{31} And he said, Since I am able to speak to the Lord, what if there should be found there twenty? And he said, I will not destroy it, if I should find there twenty. \textsuperscript{32} And he said, Will there be anything against me , Lord, if I speak yet once? but if there should be found there ten? And he said, I will not destroy it for the ten's sake. \textsuperscript{33} And the Lord departed, when he left off speaking to Abraam, and Abraam returned to his place.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 18:19 Brenton note: Hebrew background: mishpat (מִשְׁפָּט) = judgment; justice; ordinance. Common English renderings: judgment; justice. A central legal and ethical term for judgment, justice, and due order.\par
Genesis 18:19 TSK note: For I;, ;, ; command;, ; , ; , ;, that the\par
Genesis 18:20 Brenton note: Hebrew background: kaved (כָּבֵד) = heavy; weighty; honored. Common English renderings: heavy; grievous; weighty. Its sound resembles the English word caved; this is a sound coincidence only, while the Hebrew root conveys heaviness, severity, or honor depending on context.\par
Genesis 18:21 Brenton note: Gr. συντελοῦνται. Heb. עשי כלה. A. V. have done altogether.\par
Genesis 18:21 TSK note: I will go down This is spoken figuratively; and as the Jewish writers speak, according to the language of men. So eyes, ears, hands, and other members of the body are attributed to God, for effecting those things which men cannot accomplish without these members., ;, ; see; , ; I will know\par
Genesis 18:22 Brenton note: Hebrew background: panah (פָּנָה) = to turn. Common English renderings: turn. Literal and figurative turning term.\par
Genesis 18:22 TSK note: the men, stood The two, whom we suppose to have been created angels, departed at this time; and accordingly two entered Sodom at evening: while the one, called Jehovah throughout the chapter, continued with Abraham, who "stood yet before the Lord." - Scott.\par
Genesis 18:25 Brenton note: Hebrew background: shofet (שֹׁפֵט) = judge. Common English renderings: judge. Both judicial official and, in context, God as judge.\par
Genesis 18:25 Brenton note: Greek background: krisis (κρίσις) = judgment; decision. Common English renderings: judgment. Can denote judicial process, decision, or judgment.\par
Genesis 18:25 TSK note: be far that the, ;, ;, ; Shall;, ;, ; Judge\par
Genesis 18:27 Brenton note: Hebrew background: anah (עָנָה) = to answer; respond. Common English renderings: answer. One of several roots spelled this way; this one means respond.\par
Genesis 18:32 Brenton note: Hebrew background: eser (עֶשֶׂר) = ten. Common English renderings: ten. Basic numeral, also associated with completeness and commandments.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Genesis 19}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And the two angels came to Sodom at evening. And Lot sat by the gate of Sodom, and Lot having seen them, rose up to meet them, and he worshipped with his face to the ground, and said, \textsuperscript{2} Lo! my lords, turn aside to the house of your servant, and rest from your journey, and wash your feet, and having risen early in the morning ye shall depart on your journey. And they said, Nay, but we will lodge in the street. \textsuperscript{3} And he constrained them, and they turned aside to him, and they entered into his house, and he made a feast for them, and baked unleavened cakes for them, and they did eat. \textsuperscript{4} But before they went to sleep, the men of the city, the Sodomites, compassed the house, both young and old, all the people together. \textsuperscript{5} And they called out Lot, and said to him, Where are the men that went in to thee this night? bring them out to us that we may be with them. \textsuperscript{6} And Lot went out to them to the porch, and he shut the door after him, \textsuperscript{7} and said to them, By no means, brethren, do not act villanously. \textsuperscript{8} But I have two daughters, who have not known a man. I will bring them out to you, and do ye use them as it may please you, only do not injury to these men, to avoid which they came under the shelter of my roof. \textsuperscript{9} And they said to him, Stand back there, thou camest in to sojourn, was it also to judge? Now then we would harm thee more than them. And they pressed hard on the man, even Lot, and they drew nigh to break the door. \textsuperscript{10} And the men stretched forth their hands and drew Lot in to them into the house, and shut the door of the house. \textsuperscript{11} And they smote the men that were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great, and they were wearied with seeking the door. \textsuperscript{12} And the men said to Lot, Hast thou here sons-in-law, or sons or daughters, or if thou hast any other friend in the city, bring them out of this place. \textsuperscript{13} For we are going to destroy this place; for their cry has been raised up before the Lord, and the Lord has sent us to destroy it. \textsuperscript{14} And Lot went out, and spoke to his sons-in-law who had married his daughters, and said, Rise up, and depart out of this place, for the Lord is about to destroy the city; but he seemed to be speaking absurdly before his sons-in-law. \textsuperscript{15} But when it was morning, the angels hastened Lot, saying, Arise and take thy wife, and thy two daughters whom thou hast, and go forth; lest thou also be destroyed with the iniquities of the city. \textsuperscript{16} And they were troubled, and the angels laid hold on his hand, and the hand of his wife, and the hands of his two daughters, in that the Lord spared him.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 19:1 Brenton note: Hebrew background: sha’ar (שַׁעַר) = gate. Common English renderings: gate. Important for city life, judgment, and public authority.\par
Genesis 19:1 TSK note: And there came two angels. Or, rather, "the two angels came, " referring to those mentioned in the preceding chapter, and there called "men." It seems (from ), that these two angels were sent to Sodom, while the third, who was the Lord or Jehovah, remained with Abraham., rose; bowed\par
Genesis 19:2 TSK note: turn wash Nay Instead of lo, nay, some manuscripts have lo, to him. "And they said unto him, for we lodge in the street; " where, nevertheless, the negation is understood. Knowing the disposition of the inhabitants, and appearing in the character of mere travellers, they preferred the open street to any house; but not yet willing to make themselves known, as Lot pressed them vehemently, and as they knew him to be a righteous man, they consented to take shelter under his hospitable roof.\par
Genesis 19:6 TSK note: Lot door Two words are here used for door. The first pethach, which is the door-way, at which Lot went out; the latter, deleth, the leaf of the door, which he shut after him when out.\par
Genesis 19:8 Brenton note: Lit. beams.\par
Genesis 19:8 Brenton note: Greek background: skia (σκιά) = shadow. Common English renderings: shadow. Used literally and figuratively for shelter or transience.\par
Genesis 19:11 Brenton note: Hebrew background: yaga (יָגַע) = to toil; grow weary. Common English renderings: labor; weary. Used for fatigue and fruitless struggle.\par
Genesis 19:11 TSK note: with blindness The word sanverim, rendered "blindness, " and which occurs only here, and in, is supposed to denote dazzlings, deceptions, or confusions of sight from excessive light; being derived by Schultens, who is followed by Parkhurst, from the Arabic sana, to pour forth, diffuse, and nor, light. Dr. Geddes, to the same purpose, thinks it is compounded of the Arabic sana, which signifies a flash, and or, light. The Targums, in both places where it occurs, render it by eruptions, or flashes of light, or as Mercer, in Robertson, explains the Chaldee word, irradiations.; that they\par
Genesis 19:13 Brenton note: See Note, Lam. 3. 21.\par
Genesis 19:13 Brenton note: αὐτήν. Scil. πόλιν.\par
Genesis 19:13 Brenton note: Hebrew background: avad (אָבַד) = to perish; destroy. Common English renderings: perish; destroy. A key judgment and loss term.\par
Genesis 19:15 TSK note: hastened, ; are here Heb. are found iniquity or, punishment\par
Genesis 19:16 Brenton note: Hebrew background: chazaq (חָזַק) = to be strong; strengthen. Common English renderings: be strong; strengthen. Used for courage, force, and hardened resolve.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} And it came to pass when they brought them out, that they said, Save thine own life by all means; look not round to that which is behind, nor stay in all the country round about, escape to the mountain, lest perhaps thou be overtaken together with them. \textsuperscript{18} And Lot said to them, I pray, Lord, \textsuperscript{19} since thy servant has found mercy before thee, and thou hast magnified thy righteousness, in what thou doest towards me that my soul may live,—but I shall not be able to escape to the mountain, lest perhaps the calamity overtake me and I die. \textsuperscript{20} Behold this city is near for me to escape thither, which is a small one, and there shall I be preserved, is it not little? and my soul shall live because of thee. \textsuperscript{21} And he said to him, Behold, I have had respect to thee also about this thing, that I should not overthrow the city about which thou hast spoken. \textsuperscript{22} Hasten therefore to escape thither, for I shall not be able to do anything until thou art come thither; therefore he called the name of that city, Segor. \textsuperscript{23} The sun was risen upon the earth, when Lot entered into Segor. \textsuperscript{24} And the Lord rained on Sodom and Gomorrha brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven. \textsuperscript{25} And he overthrew these cities, and all the country round about, and all that dwelt in the cities, and the plants springing out of the ground. \textsuperscript{26} And his wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt. \textsuperscript{27} And Abraam rose up early to go to the place, where he had stood before the Lord. \textsuperscript{28} And he looked towards Sodom and Gomorrha, and towards the surrounding country, and saw, and behold a flame went up from the earth, as the smoke of a furnace. \textsuperscript{29} And it came to pass that when God destroyed all the cities of the region round about, God remembered Abraam, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow, when the Lord overthrew those cities in which Lot dwelt.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 19:19 Brenton note: Hebrew background: chesed (חֶסֶד) = steadfast love; covenant mercy; lovingkindness. Common English renderings: mercy; lovingkindness. A major covenant term for loyal love, mercy, and faithful kindness.\par
Genesis 19:19 Brenton note: Greek background: eleos (ἔλεος) = mercy; compassion. Common English renderings: mercy. Frequently used of divine mercy and covenant compassion.\par
Genesis 19:19 Brenton note: Greek background: sōzō (σῴζω) = to save; rescue. Common English renderings: save. A central salvation verb represented by its lexical form.\par
Genesis 19:21 Brenton note: Gr. thy countenance.\par
Genesis 19:21 TSK note: I; , ; , thee Heb. thy face that\par
Genesis 19:22 TSK note: for; called, ; Zoar i.e. little\par
Genesis 19:24 Brenton note: Greek background: pyr (πῦρ) = fire. Common English renderings: fire. Used literally and often symbolically for judgment or purification.\par
Genesis 19:24 TSK note: the Lord; , ;, ; brimstone The word rendered "brimstone, " (q.d. brennestone, or brinnestone, id est burning-stone), is always rendered by the LXX "sulphur, " and seems to denote a meteorous inflammable matter.\par
Genesis 19:26 TSK note: looked This unhappy woman, says the Rev. T. Scott, "looked back, " contrary to God's express command, perhaps with a hope of returning, which latter supposition is favoured by our Lord's words, "Let him not return back. Remember Lot's wife." She was, therefore, instantaneously struck dead and petrified, and thus remained to after ages a visible monument of the Divine displeasure.; and\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} And Lot went up out of Segor, and dwelt in the mountain, he and his two daughters with him, for he feared to dwell in Segor; and he dwelt in a cave, he and his two daughters with him. \textsuperscript{31} And the elder said to the younger, Our father is old, and there is no one on the earth who shall come in to us, as it is fit in all the earth. \textsuperscript{32} Come and let us make our father drink wine, and let us sleep with him, and let us raise up seed from our father. \textsuperscript{33} So they made their father drink wine in that night, and the elder went in and lay with her father that night, and he knew not when he slept and when he rose up. \textsuperscript{34} And it came to pass on the morrow, that the elder said to the younger, Behold, I slept yesternight with our father, let us make him drink wine in this night also, and do thou go in and sleep with him, and let us raise up seed of our father. \textsuperscript{35} So they made their father drink wine in that night also, and the younger went in and slept with her father, and he knew not when he slept, nor when he arose. \textsuperscript{36} And the two daughters of Lot conceived by their father. \textsuperscript{37} And the elder bore a son, and called his name Moab, saying, He is of my father. This is the father of the Moabites to this present day. \textsuperscript{38} And the younger also bore a son, and called his name Amman, saying, The son of my family. This is the father of the Ammanites to this present day.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 19:37 TSK note: am 2108, bc 1896 Moab This name is generally interpreted of the father; from mo, of, and av, a father. Moabites\par
Genesis 19:38 TSK note: Benammi i.e., Son of my people, from ben, a son, and ammi, my people. children\par

\subsection*{Genesis 20}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Abraam removed thence to the southern country, and dwelt between Cades and Sur, and sojourned in Gerara. \textsuperscript{2} And Abraam said concerning Sarrha his wife, She is my sister, for he feared to say, She is my wife, lest at any time the men of the city should kill him for her sake. So Abimelech king of Gerara sent and took Sarrha. \textsuperscript{3} And God came to Abimelech by night in sleep, and said, Behold, thou diest for the woman, whom thou hast taken, whereas she has lived with a husband. \textsuperscript{4} But Abimelech had not touched her, and he said, Lord, wilt thou destroy an ignorantly sinning and just nation? \textsuperscript{5} Said he not to me, She is my sister, and said she not to me, He is my brother? with a pure heart and in the righteousness of my hands have I done this. \textsuperscript{6} And God said to him in sleep, Yea, I knew that thou didst this with a pure heart, and I spared thee, so that thou shouldest not sin against me, therefore I suffered thee not to touch her. \textsuperscript{7} But now return the man his wife; for he is a prophet, and shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live; but if thou restore her not, know that thou shalt die and all thine. \textsuperscript{8} And Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and he spoke all these words in their ears, and all the men feared exceedingly. \textsuperscript{9} And Abimelech called Abraam and said to him, What is this that thou hast done to us? Have we sinned against thee, that thou hast brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin? Thou hast done to me a deed, which no one ought to do. \textsuperscript{10} And Abimelech said to Abraam, What hast thou seen in me that thou hast done this? \textsuperscript{11} And Abraam said, Why I said, Surely there is not the worship of God in this place, and they will slay me because of my wife. \textsuperscript{12} For truly she is my sister by my father, but not by my mother, and she became my wife. \textsuperscript{13} And it came to pass when God brought me forth out of the house of my father, that I said to her, This righteousness thou shalt perform to me, in every place into which we may enter, say of me, He is my brother. \textsuperscript{14} And Abimelech took a thousand pieces of silver, and sheep, and calves, and servants, and maid-servants, and gave them to Abraam, and he returned him Sarrha his wife. \textsuperscript{15} And Abimelech said to Abraam, Behold, my land is before thee, dwell wheresoever it may please thee. \textsuperscript{16} And to Sarrha he said, Behold, I have given thy brother a thousand pieces of silver, those shall be to thee for the price of thy countenance, and to all the women with thee, and speak the truth in all things. \textsuperscript{17} And Abraam prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his women servants, and they bore children. \textsuperscript{18} Because the Lord had fast closed from without every womb in the house of Abimelech, because of Sarrha Abraam's wife.\par

From, it appears to have been situated in the angle where the south and west sides of Canaan met, and to have been not far from Gaza. Jerome, in his Hebrew Traditions on Genesis, says, from Gerar to Jerusalem was three days' journey. There was a wood near Gerar, spoken of by Theodoret; and a brook ( ), on which was a monastery, noticed by Sozomen.\par

\subsection*{Genesis 21}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And the Lord visited Sarrha, as he said, and the Lord did to Sarrha, as he spoke. \textsuperscript{2} And she conceived and bore to Abraam a son in old age, at the set time according as the Lord spoke to him. \textsuperscript{3} And Abraam called the name of his son that was born to him, whom Sarrha bore to him, Isaac. \textsuperscript{4} And Abraam circumcised Isaac on the eighth day, as God commanded him. \textsuperscript{5} And Abraam was a hundred years old when Isaac his son was born to him. \textsuperscript{6} And Sarrha said, The Lord has made laughter for me, for whoever shall hear shall rejoice with me. \textsuperscript{7} And she said, Who shall say to Abraam that Sarrha suckles a child? for I have born a child in my old age. \textsuperscript{8} And the child grew and was weaned, and Abraam made a great feast the day that his son Isaac was weaned. \textsuperscript{9} And Sarrha having seen the son of Agar the Egyptian who was born to Abraam, sporting with Isaac her son, \textsuperscript{10} then she said to Abraam, Cast out this bondwoman and her son, for the son of this bondwoman shall not inherit with my son Isaac. \textsuperscript{11} But the word appeared very hard before Abraam concerning his son. \textsuperscript{12} But God said to Abraam, Let it not be hard before thee concerning the child, and concerning the bondwoman; in all things whatsoever Sarrha shall say to thee, hear her voice, for in Isaac shall thy seed be called. \textsuperscript{13} And moreover I will make the son of this bondwoman a great nation, because he is thy seed. \textsuperscript{14} And Abraam rose up in the morning and took loaves and a skin of water, and gave them to Agar, and he put the child on her shoulder, and sent her away, and she having departed wandered in the wilderness near the well of the oath. \textsuperscript{15} And the water failed out of the skin, and she cast the child under a fir tree. \textsuperscript{16} And she departed and sat down opposite him at a distance, as it were a bow-shot, for she said, Surely I cannot see the death of my child: and she sat opposite him, and the child cried aloud and wept. \textsuperscript{17} And God heard the voice of the child from the place where he was, and an angel of God called Agar out of heaven, and said to her, What is it, Agar? fear not, for God has heard the voice of the child from the place where he is. \textsuperscript{18} Rise up, and take the child, and hold him in thine hand, for I will make him a great nation. \textsuperscript{19} And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of springing water; and she went and filled the skin with water, and gave the child drink. \textsuperscript{20} And God was with the child, and he grew and dwelt in the wilderness, and became an archer. \textsuperscript{21} And he dwelt in the wilderness, and his mother took him a wife out of Pharan of Egypt.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{22} And it came to pass at that time that Abimelech spoke, and Ochozath his friend, and Phichol the chief captain of his host, to Abraam, saying, God is with thee in all things, whatsoever thou mayest do. \textsuperscript{23} Now therefore swear to me by God that thou wilt not injure me, nor my seed, nor my name, but according to the righteousness which I have performed with thee thou shalt deal with me, and with the land in which thou hast sojourned. \textsuperscript{24} And Abraam said, I will swear. \textsuperscript{25} And Abraam reproved Abimelech because of the wells of water, which the servants of Abimelech took away. \textsuperscript{26} And Abimelech said to him, I know not who has done this thing to thee, neither didst thou tell it me, neither heard I it but only to-day. \textsuperscript{27} And Abraam took sheep and calves, and gave them to Abimelech, and both made a covenant. \textsuperscript{28} And Abraam set seven ewe-lambs by themselves. \textsuperscript{29} And Abimelech said to Abraam, What are these seven ewe-lambs which thou hast set alone? \textsuperscript{30} And Abraam said, Thou shalt receive the seven ewe-lambs of me, that they may be for me as a witness, that I dug this well. \textsuperscript{31} Therefore he named the name of that place, The Well of the Oath, for there they both swore. \textsuperscript{32} And they made a covenant at the well of the oath. \subsection*{Genesis 22}

And he said, What is it, son? And both having gone together, \textsuperscript{9} came to the place which God spoke of to him; and there Abraam built the altar, and laid the wood on it, and having bound the feet of Isaac his son together, he laid him on the altar upon the wood. \textsuperscript{10} And Abraam stretched forth his hand to take the knife to slay his son. \textsuperscript{11} And an angel of the Lord called him out of heaven, and said, Abraam, Abraam. And he said, Behold, I am here . \textsuperscript{12} And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the child, neither do anything to him, for now I know that thou fearest God, and for my sake thou hast not spared thy beloved son. \textsuperscript{13} And Abraam lifted up his eyes and beheld, and lo! a ram caught by his horns in a plant of Sabec; and Abraam went and took the ram, and offered him up for a whole-burnt-offering in the place of Isaac his son.\par

nay, do thou bury thy dead. \textsuperscript{16} And Abraam hearkened to Ephron, and Abraam rendered to Ephron the money, which he mentioned in the ears of the sons of Chet, four hundred didrachms of silver approved with merchants. \textsuperscript{17} And the field of Ephron, which was in Double Cave, which is opposite Mambre, the field and the cave, which was in it, and every tree which was in the field, and whatever is in its borders round about, were made sure \textsuperscript{18} to Abraam for a possession, before the sons of Chet, and all that entered into the city. \textsuperscript{19} After this Abraam buried Sarrha his wife in the Double Cave of the field, which is opposite Mambre, this is Chebron in the land of Chanaan. \textsuperscript{20} So the field and the cave which was in it were made sure to Abraam for possession of a burying place, by the sons of Chet.\par

Ephron, though a chief man, might have been personally unknown to Abraham; but now he answers for himself, making a free tender of the field and cave to Abraham, in the presence of all the people, which amounted to a legal conveyance to the Patriarch. audience Heb. ears all that, ; his\par
Genesis 23:11 Brenton note: Gr. be with me.\par
Genesis 23:15 TSK note: is worth Though the words "is worth" are not in the Text, yet they are clearly implied, to adapt the Hebrew to the English idiom. A shekel, according to the general opinion, was equal in value to about 2s. 6d. of our money, but according to Dr. Prideaux, 3s. English. In those early times, money was given in weight; for it is said ( ) that "Abraham weighed, " wayishkal, the silver; and hence, we find that it was a certain weight which afterwards passed as a current coin; for the word shekel is not only used to denote a piece of silver, but also to weigh. shekels\par
Genesis 23:17 Brenton note: Hebrew background: saviv (סָבִיב) = around; surrounding. Common English renderings: round about. Preposition/adverb for surrounding space.\par
\end{quote}
