Tell me if there is room for us to lodge with thy father. \textsuperscript{24} And she said to him, I am the daughter of Bathuel the son of Melcha, whom she bore to Nachor. \textsuperscript{25} And she said to him, We have both straw and much provender, and a place for resting. \textsuperscript{26} And the man being well pleased, worshipped the Lord, \textsuperscript{27} and said, Blessed be the Lord the God of my master Abraam, who has not suffered his righteousness to fail, nor his truth from my master, and the Lord has brought me prosperously to the house of the brother of my lord. \textsuperscript{28} And the damsel ran and reported to the house of her mother according to these words. \textsuperscript{29} And Rebecca had a brother whose name was Laban; and Laban ran out to meet the man, to the well. \textsuperscript{30} And it came to pass when he saw the ear-rings and the bracelets on the hands of his sister, and when he heard the words of Rebecca his sister, saying, Thus the man spoke to me, that he went to the man, as he stood by the camels at the well. \textsuperscript{31} And he said to him, Come in hither, thou blessed of the Lord, why standest thou without, whereas I have prepared the house and a place for the camels? \textsuperscript{32} And the man entered into the house, and unloaded the camels, and gave the camels straw and provender, and water to wash his feet, and the feet of the men that were with him. \textsuperscript{33} And he set before them loaves to eat; but he said, I will not eat, until I have told my errand. And he said, Speak on.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 24:15 Brenton note: i. e. Nachor.\par
Genesis 24:16 TSK note: fair to look upon Heb. good of countenance, known\par
Genesis 24:21 TSK note: wondering at;, ;, to wit i.e. "to know, " or "to learn" the Lord\par
Genesis 24:22 Brenton note: Greek background: drachmē (δραχμή) = drachma. Common English renderings: piece of silver. A coin or weight term.\par
Genesis 24:22 TSK note: took; , earring or, jewel for the forehead, ; From the word being in the singular number, it is not likely to have been an ear-ring, or a "jewel for the forehead, " but "a jewel for the nose, a nose-ring, " which is in use throughout Arabia and Persia, particularly among young women. It is very properly translated επιρρινον, "an ornament for the nose, " by Symmachus; and Sir John Chardin informs us, that "it is a custom in almost all the East, for the women to wear rings in their noses, in the left nostril, which is bored low down in the middle. These rings are of gold, and have commonly two pearls and one ruby between, placed in the ring. I never saw a girl or young woman in Arabia or in all Persia, who did not wear a ring after this manner in her nostril." of half bracelets The word rendered "bracelet, " from a root which signifies "to join or couple together, " may imply whatever may clasp round the arms and legs; for rings and ornaments are worn round both by females in India and Persia. The small part of the leg, and the whole arm, from the shoulder to the wrist, are generally decorated in this way. As these were given to Rebekah for "her hands, " it sufficiently distinguishes them from similar ornaments for the ankles.\par
Genesis 24:23 Brenton note: Hebrew background: yesh (יֵשׁ) = there is; there exists. Common English renderings: there is. Its sound is close to the English word yes, though the Hebrew particle actually expresses existence rather than agreement.\par
Genesis 24:27 Brenton note: Hebrew background: emet (אֱמֶת) = truth; faithfulness. Common English renderings: truth. A covenantally rich term for reliability and truth.\par
Genesis 24:27 Brenton note: Greek background: alētheia (ἀλήθεια) = truth. Common English renderings: truth. Can denote truthfulness, reliability, or what is true.\par

Genesis 24:28 TSK note: of, her mother's Some have conjectured from this, that her father Bethuel was dead; and the person called Bethuel ( ), was a younger brother. This is possible; but as Dr. A. Clarke remarks, the mother's house might be mentioned were even the father alive; for in Asiatic countries, the women have apartments entirely separate from those of the men, in which their little children and grown-up daughters reside with them. This was probably the case here; though, from the whole narrative, it is very probable that Bethuel was dead, as the whole business appears to be conducted by Rebekah's brothers.\par
Genesis 24:32 TSK note: he ungirded i.e. Laban ungirded straw Straw, by the eastern mode of threshing, was cut or shattered, and reduced to a kind of chaff. With this, sometimes mixed with a little barley, the eastern people still feed their labouring beasts, as they anciently did. wash\par

and hereby shall I know that thou hast wrought mercy with my master Abraam. \textsuperscript{45} And it came to pass before I had done speaking in my mind, straightway Rebecca came forth, having her pitcher on her shoulders; and she went down to the well, and drew water; and I said to her, Give me to drink. \textsuperscript{46} And she hasted and let down her pitcher on her arm from her head, and said, Drink thou, and I will give thy camels drink; and I drank, and she gave the camels drink. \textsuperscript{47} And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter art thou? tell me; and she said, I am daughter of Bathuel the son of Nachor, whom Melcha bore to him; and I put on her the ear-rings, and the bracelets on her hands. \textsuperscript{48} And being well-pleased I worshipped the Lord, and I blessed the Lord the God of my master Abraam, who has prospered me in a true way, so that I should take the daughter of my master's brother for his son. \textsuperscript{49} If then ye will deal mercifully and justly with my lord, tell me , and if not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand or to the left.\par

Genesis 24:37 TSK note: And my, ; Canaanites The Canaanites were infected with gross idolatry; and consequently, not proper persons with whom to form so intimate a connection; especially as Jehovah had shown Abraham that they were filling up the measure of their iniquity, and were doomed to destruction.\par
Genesis 24:38 TSK note: But, my father's i.e., Where the family of Haran his brother had settled; and where he himself had remained some time with his father Terah. Nahor did not dwell at Ur of the Chaldees, but at Haran in Mesopotamia. The true worship of God seems to have been in some measure preserved in this family, though afterwards corrupted.\par
Genesis 24:39 TSK note: Peradventure We may see, says Calmet, by this and other passages of Scripture ( ), what the sentiments of the ancients were relative to an oath. They believed that they were bound precisely by what was spoken, and had no liberty to interpret the intentions of those by whom the oath was made.\par
Genesis 24:41 Brenton note: Hebrew background: alah (אָלָה) = oath-curse; imprecation; curse. Common English renderings: curse; oath. Its sound closely resembles the English rendering Allah; this is only a phonetic resemblance in English, while the Hebrew term refers to an oath-curse or imprecation.\par
Genesis 24:44 TSK note: Both; the woman, ;, appointed Those events, which appear to us the effect of choice, contrivance, or chance, are matters of appointment with God; and the persuasion of this does not prevent, but rather encourage, the use of all proper means; at the same time that it confines us to proper means, and delivers the mind from useless anxiety about consequences.\par

\subsection*{Genesis 26}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And there was a famine in the land, besides the former famine, which was in the time of Abraam; and Isaac went to Abimelech the king of the Phylistines to Gerara. \textsuperscript{2} And the Lord appeared to him and said, Go not down to Egypt, but dwell in the land, which I shall tell thee of. \textsuperscript{3} And sojourn in this land; and I will be with thee, and bless thee, for I will give to thee and to thy seed all this land; and I will establish my oath which I swore to thy father Abraam. \textsuperscript{4} And I will multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven; and I will give to thy seed all this land, and all the nations of the earth shall be blest in thy seed. \textsuperscript{5} Because Abraam thy father hearkened to my voice, and kept my injunctions, and my commandments, and my ordinances, and my statutes. \textsuperscript{6} And Isaac dwelt in Gerara. \textsuperscript{7} And the men of the place questioned him concerning Rebecca his wife, and he said, She is my sister, for he feared to say, She is my wife, lest at any time the men of the place should slay him because of Rebecca, because she was fair. \textsuperscript{8} And he remained there a long time, and Abimelech the king of Gerara leaned to look through the window, and saw Isaac sporting with Rebecca his wife. \textsuperscript{9} And Abimelech called Isaac, and said to him, Is she then thy wife? why hast thou said, She is my sister? And Isaac said to him, I did so , for I said, Lest at any time I die on her account. \textsuperscript{10} And Abimelech said to him, Why hast thou done this to us? one of my kindred within a little had lain with thy wife, and thou wouldest have brought a sin of ignorance upon us. \textsuperscript{11} And Abimelech charged all his people, saying, Every man that touches this man and his wife shall be liable to death. \textsuperscript{12} And Isaac sowed in that land, and he found in that year barley an hundred-fold, and the Lord blessed him. \textsuperscript{13} And the man was exalted, and advancing he increased, till he became very great. \textsuperscript{14} And he had cattle of sheep, and cattle of oxen, and many tilled lands, and the Phylistines envied him. \textsuperscript{15} And all the wells which the servants of his father had dug in the time of his father, the Phylistines stopped them, and filled them with earth. \textsuperscript{16} And Abimelech said to Isaac, Depart from us, for thou art become much mightier than we. \textsuperscript{17} And Isaac departed thence, and rested in the valley of Gerara, and dwelt there.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 26:1 TSK note: am 2200, bc 1804 the first And Isaac Abimelech\par

Genesis 26:12 TSK note: sowed The author of the "History of the Piratical States of Barbary" observes (p. 44), that the Moors of that country are divided into tribes like the Arabians, and like them dwell in tents, formed into itinerant villages; that "these wanderers farm lands of the inhabitants of the towns, sow and cultivate them, paying their rent with the produce, such as fruits, corn, wax, etc. They are very skilful in choosing the most advantageous soils for every season, and very careful to avoid the Turkish troops, the violence of the one little suiting the simplicity of the other." It is natural to suppose, that Isaac possessed the like sagacity, when he sowed in the land of Gerar, and received that year an hundred-fold. received Heb. found an hundredfold, ; , ; blessed\par
Genesis 26:13 TSK note: And the man waxed great Dr. Adam Clarke remarks, that there is a strange and observable occurrence of the same term in the original, which is literally, "And the man was GREAT, and he went, going on, and was GREAT, until that he was exceeding GREAT." How simple is this language, and yet how forcible! waxed great; went forward Heb. went going\par
Genesis 26:14 TSK note: had possession, ;, ;, ; servants or, husbandry envied\par
Genesis 26:15 TSK note: his father's had stopped In those countries, a well of water was a great acquisition; and hence, this mode of injuring new settlers, or revenging themselves on their enemies, is still resorted to among the inhabitants.\par
Genesis 26:16 TSK note: Go Dr. A. Clarke observes, that this is the first instance on record of what was termed among the Greeks, ostracism, i.e., the banishment of person from the state, of whose power, influence, or riches, the people were jealous. mightier\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{18} And Isaac dug again the wells of water, which the servants of his father Abraam had dug, and the Phylistines had stopped them, after the death of his father Abraam; and he gave them names, according to the names by which his father named them. \textsuperscript{19} And the servants of Isaac dug in the valley of Gerara, and they found there a well of living water. \textsuperscript{20} And the shepherds of Gerara strove with the shepherds of Isaac, saying that the water was theirs; and they called the name of the well, Injury, for they injured him. \textsuperscript{21} And having departed thence he dug another well, and they strove also for that; and he named the name of it, Enmity. \textsuperscript{22} And he departed thence and dug another well; and they did not strive about that; and he named the name of it, Room, saying, Because now the Lord has made room for us, and has increased us upon the earth.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 26:18 TSK note: in the days Houbigant contends, that instead of bimey, "in the days, " we should read, avdey, "servants; " agreeably to the Samaritan, Septuagint, Syriac, and Vulgate: "And Isaac digged again the wells of water which the servants of Abraham his father had digged." and he\par

Genesis 26:22 TSK note: digged The wells in Arabia are generally dug in the rock. Their mouths are about six feet in diameter, and they are from nineteen to twenty feet in depth. But Niebuhr informs us, that many wells are from 160 to 170 feet deep. Rehoboth i.e. Room the Lord, be fruitful\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} And he went up thence to the well of the oath. \textsuperscript{24} And the Lord appeared to him in that night, and said, I am the God of Abraam thy father; fear not, for I am with thee, and I will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for the sake of Abraam thy father. \textsuperscript{25} And he built there an altar, and called on the name of the Lord, and there he pitched his tent, and there the servants of Isaac dug a well in the valley of Gerara. \textsuperscript{26} And Abimelech came to him from Gerara, and so did Ochozath his friend, and Phichol the commander-in-chief of his army. \textsuperscript{27} And Isaac said to them, Wherefore have ye come to me? whereas ye hated me, and sent me away from you. \textsuperscript{28} And they said, We have surely seen that the Lord was with thee, and we said, Let there be an oath between us and thee, and we will make a covenant with thee, \textsuperscript{29} that thou shalt do no wrong by us, as we have not abhorred thee, and according as we have treated thee well, and have sent thee forth peaceably; and now thou art blessed of the Lord. \textsuperscript{30} And he made a feast for them, and they ate and drank. \textsuperscript{31} And they arose in the morning, and swore each to his neighbour; and Isaac sent them forth, and they departed from him in safety. \textsuperscript{32} And it came to pass in that day, that the servants of Isaac came and told him of the well which they had dug; and they said, We have not found water. \textsuperscript{33} And he called it, Oath: therefore he called the name of that city, the Well of Oath, until this day.\par

\subsection*{Genesis 27}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And it came to pass after Isaac was old, that his eyes were dimmed so that he could not see; and he called Esau, his elder son, and said to him, My son; and he said, Behold, I am here . \textsuperscript{2} And he said, Behold, I am grown old, and know not the day of my death. \textsuperscript{3} Now then take thy weapons, both thy quiver and thy bow, and go into the plain, and get me venison, \textsuperscript{4} and make me meats, as I like them, and bring them to me that I may eat, that my soul may bless thee, before I die. \textsuperscript{5} And Rebecca heard Isaac speaking to Esau his son; and Esau went to the plain to procure venison for his father. \textsuperscript{6} And Rebecca said to Jacob her younger son, Behold, I heard thy father speaking to Esau thy brother, saying, \textsuperscript{7} Bring me venison, and prepare me meats, that I may eat and bless thee before the Lord before I die. \textsuperscript{8} Now then, my son, hearken to me, as I command thee. \textsuperscript{9} And go to the cattle and take for me thence two kids, tender and good, and I will make them meats for thy father, as he likes. \textsuperscript{10} And thou shalt bring them in to thy father, and he shall eat, that thy father may bless thee before he dies. \textsuperscript{11} And Jacob said to his mother Rebecca, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I a smooth man. \textsuperscript{12} Peradventure my father may feel me, and I shall be before him as one ill-intentioned, and I shall bring upon me a curse, and not a blessing. \textsuperscript{13} And his mother said to him, On me be thy curse, son; only hearken to my voice, and go and bring them me. \textsuperscript{14} So he went and took and brought them to his mother; and his mother made meats, as his father liked them .\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 27:1 TSK note: am 2244, bc 1760 dim; eldest son\par
Genesis 27:3 TSK note: I, take me Heb. hunt\par
Genesis 27:4 Brenton note: Hebrew background: nafshi (נַפְשִׁי) = my soul; my life. Common English renderings: my soul; my life. Represents נפש in a common suffixed form in devotional contexts.\par
Genesis 27:4 TSK note: that I may eat The blessing, says Dr. A. Clarke, which Isaac was to confer on his son, was a species of divine right, and must be communicated with appropriate ceremonies. As eating and drinking were used among the Asiatics on almost all religious occasions, and especially in making and confirming covenants, it is reasonable to suppose, that something of this kind was essentially necessary on this occasion; and that Isaac could not convey the right, till he had eaten of the meat provided for the purpose by him who was to receive the blessing. that my\par
Genesis 27:9 Brenton note: Greek background: tragos (τράγος) = goat. Common English renderings: goat. A standard term for goat, often in sacrificial contexts.\par

Genesis 27:12 Brenton note: Greek background: eulogia (εὐλογία) = blessing; praise. Common English renderings: blessing. A word of blessing or the blessing conferred.\par
Genesis 27:12 Brenton note: Greek background: katara (κατάρα) = curse. Common English renderings: curse. The opposite of blessing in covenant and judgment language.\par
Genesis 27:12 Brenton note: Greek background: pseudos (ψεῦδος) = lie; falsehood. Common English renderings: lie. A noun for falsehood and deceit.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{15} And Rebecca having taken the fine raiment of her elder son Esau which was with her in the house, put it on Jacob her younger son. \textsuperscript{16} And she put on his arms the skins of the kids, and on the bare parts of his neck. \textsuperscript{17} And she gave the meats, and the loaves which she had prepared, into the hands of Jacob her son. \textsuperscript{18} And he brought them to his father, and said, Father; and he said, Behold I am here ; who art thou, son? \textsuperscript{19} And Jacob said to his father, I, Esau thy first-born, have done as thou toldest me; rise, sit, and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me. \textsuperscript{20} And Isaac said to his son, What is this which thou hast quickly found? And he said, That which the Lord thy God presented before me. \textsuperscript{21} And Isaac said to Jacob, Draw nigh to me, and I will feel thee, son, if thou art my son Esau or not. \textsuperscript{22} And Jacob drew nigh to his father Isaac, and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau. \textsuperscript{23} And he knew him not, for his hands were as the hands of his brother Esau, hairy; and he blessed him, \textsuperscript{24} and he said, Art thou my son Esau? and he said, I am . \textsuperscript{25} And he said, Bring hither, and I will eat of thy venison, son, that my soul may bless thee; and he brought it near to him, and he ate, and he brought him wine, and he drank. \textsuperscript{26} And Isaac his father said to him, Draw nigh to me, and kiss me, son. \textsuperscript{27} And he drew nigh and kissed him, and smelled the smell of his garments, and blessed him, and said, Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of an abundant field, which the Lord has blessed. \textsuperscript{28} And may God give thee of the dew of heaven, and of the fatness of the earth, and abundance of corn and wine. \textsuperscript{29} And let nations serve thee, and princes bow down to thee, and be thou lord of thy brother, and the sons of thy father shall do thee reverence; accursed is he that curses thee, and blessed is he that blesses thee.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 27:15 TSK note: goodly raiment Heb. desirable, ; The Septuagint translates it "a goodly robe, " which was a long garment that great men used to wear (; ). The priest afterwards in the law had "holy garments" to minister in ( ). Whether the first-born before the law had such to minister in is not certain: for, had they been common garments, why did not Esau himself or his wives keep them? But being, in likelihood, holy robes, received from their ancestors, the mother of the family kept them in sweet chests, from moths and the like; whereupon it is said ( ), "Isaac smelled the smell of his garments."\par
Genesis 27:16 Brenton note: Hebrew background: tsavvar (צַוָּאר) = neck. Common English renderings: neck. Image for obstinacy, ornamentation, or embrace.\par
Genesis 27:16 TSK note: skins Travellers inform us, that the Eastern goats have long, fine, and beautiful hair, of the most delicate silky softness; indeed the animals generally in those hot countries are not covered with so thick a coat of hair as they are in more northerly regions; so that Isaac might easily be deceived, when his eyes were dim, and his feeling no less impaired than his sight.\par
Genesis 27:20 TSK note: Because; to me Heb. before me\par
Genesis 27:22 TSK note: The voice How wonderful, says Mr. Scott, is that difference which there is betwixt the faces and the voices of the several individuals of the human species! Scarcely any two of the innumerable millions are exactly alike in either, and yet the difference cannot be defined or described! The power, wisdom, and kindness of our Creator should be admired and adored in this remarkable circumstance; for they are very visible. This description of Jacob is not unaptly accommodated to the character of a hypocrite. His voice, his language, is that of a Christian; his hands, or conduct, that of an ungodly man, but the judgment will proceed from God, the Judge of all, at the last day, as in the present case, not by the voice, but by the hands.\par
Genesis 27:27 TSK note: blessed the smell of a field A field where aromatic plants, flowers, fruits, and spices grew in abundance, with which these garments (see note on ) of Esau might probably have been perfumed by being laid up with them., ; which\par
Genesis 27:28 Brenton note: Greek background: sitos (σῖτος) = grain; wheat. Common English renderings: corn; wheat. Often denotes grain in general or wheat specifically.\par
Genesis 27:28 TSK note: of the dew, ; , ; the fatness, ; plenty\par
Genesis 27:29 TSK note: Let people, ;, ; be lord, ; , ; *title; cursed\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} And it came to pass after Isaac had ceased blessing his son Jacob, it even came to pass, just when Jacob had gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting. \textsuperscript{31} And he also had made meats and brought them to his father; and he said to his father, Let my father arise and eat of his son's venison, that thy soul may bless me. \textsuperscript{32} And Isaac his father said to him, Who art thou? And he said, I am thy first-born son Esau. \textsuperscript{33} And Isaac was amazed with very great amazement, and said, Who then is it that has procured venison for me and brought it to me? and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and I have blessed him, and he shall be blessed. \textsuperscript{34} And it came to pass when Esau heard the words of his father Isaac, he cried out with a great and very bitter cry, and said, Bless, I pray thee, me also, father. \textsuperscript{35} And he said to him, Thy brother has come with subtlety, and taken thy blessing. \textsuperscript{36} And he said, Rightly was his name called Jacob, for lo! this second time has he supplanted me; he has both taken my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing; and Esau said to his father, Hast thou not left a blessing for me, father? \textsuperscript{37} And Isaac answered and said to Esau, If I have made him thy lord, and have made all his brethren his servants, and have strengthened him with corn and wine, what then shall I do for thee, son? \textsuperscript{38} And Esau said to his father, Hast thou only one blessing, father? \subsection*{Genesis 28}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Isaac having called for Jacob, blessed him, and charged him, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of the Chananites. \textsuperscript{2} Rise and depart quickly into Mesopotamia, to the house of Bathuel the father of thy mother, and take to thyself thence a wife of the daughters of Laban thy mother's brother. \textsuperscript{3} And may my God bless thee, and increase thee, and multiply thee, and thou shalt become gatherings of nations. \textsuperscript{4} And may he give thee the blessing of my father Abraam, even to thee and to thy seed after thee, to inherit the land of thy sojourning, which God gave to Abraam. \textsuperscript{5} So Isaac sent away Jacob, and he went into Mesopotamia to Laban the son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebecca the mother of Jacob and Esau.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 28:3 Brenton note: Hebrew background: qahal (קָהָל) = assembly. Common English renderings: assembly; congregation. A gathered community term, especially covenantal.\par
Genesis 28:3 TSK note: God, ; and make, ;, a multitude Heb. an assembly\par
Genesis 28:4 TSK note: the blessing, ; , ; wherein thou art a stranger Heb. of thy sojournings, which\par
Genesis 28:5 TSK note: sent away Jacob Whoever observes Jacob's life, after he had surreptitiously obtained his father's blessing, will perceive that he enjoyed very little worldly felicity. His brother purposed to murder him, to avoid which he was forced to flee from his father's house; his uncle Laban deceived him, as he had deceived his father, and treated him with great rigour; after a servitude of 21 years, he was obliged to leave him in a clandestine manner, not without danger of being brought back, or murdered by his enraged brother; no sooner were these fears over, than he experienced the baseness of his son Reuben, in defiling his bed; he had next to bewail the treachery and cruelty of Simeon and Levi toward the Shechemites; then he had to feel the loss of his beloved wife; he was next imposed upon by his own sons, and had to lament the supposed untimely end of Joseph; and to complete all, he was forced by famine to go into Egypt, and there died, in a strange land. So just, wonderful, and instructive are all the ways of Providence! Padanaram\par
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Genesis 29}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Jacob started and went to the land of the east to Laban, the son of Bathuel the Syrian, and the brother of Rebecca, mother of Jacob and Esau. \textsuperscript{2} And he looks, and behold! a well in the plain; and there were there three flocks of sheep resting at it, for out of that well they watered the flocks, but there was a great stone at the mouth of the well. \textsuperscript{3} And there were all the flocks gathered, and they used to roll away the stone from the mouth of the well, and water the flocks, and set the stone again in its place on the mouth of the well. \textsuperscript{4} And Jacob said to them, Brethren, whence are ye? and they said, We are of Charrhan. \textsuperscript{5} And he said to them, Know ye Laban, the son of Nachor? and they said, We do know him . \textsuperscript{6} And he said to them, Is he well? And they said, He is well. And behold Rachel his daughter came with the sheep. \textsuperscript{7} And Jacob said, It is yet high day, it is not yet time that the flocks be gathered together; water ye the flocks, and depart and feed them. \textsuperscript{8} And they said, We shall not be able, until all the shepherds be gathered together, and they shall roll away the stone from the mouth of the well, then we will water the flocks. \textsuperscript{9} While he was yet speaking to them, behold, Rachel the daughter of Laban came with her father's sheep, for she fed the sheep of her father. \textsuperscript{10} And it came to pass when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban, his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban, his mother's brother, that Jacob came and rolled away the stone from the mouth of the well, and watered the sheep of Laban, his mother's brother. \textsuperscript{11} And Jacob kissed Rachel, and cried with a loud voice and wept. \textsuperscript{12} And he told Rachel that he was the near relative of her father, and the son of Rebecca; and she ran and reported to her father according to these words. \textsuperscript{13} And it came to pass when Laban heard the name of Jacob, his sister's son, he ran to meet him, and embraced and kissed him, and brought him into his house; and he told Laban all these sayings. \textsuperscript{14} And Laban said to him, Thou art of my bones and of my flesh; and he was with him a full month.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 29:1 Brenton note: Gr. having lifted up his feet, went, etc.\par
Genesis 29:1 TSK note: Jacob, ; went on his journey Heb. lifted up his feet came, ; , ; people Heb. children east The district of Mesopotamia, and the whole country beyond the Euphrates, are called Kedem, or the East, in the Sacred Writings.\par
Genesis 29:2 TSK note: a well, ; , there; a great stone In Arabia, and other places in the East, they cover up their wells of water, lest the sand, which is put in motion by the winds, should fill and quite stop them up. So great was their care not to leave the well open any length of time, that they waited till the flocks were all gathered together before they began to draw water; and when they had finished, the well was immediately closed again.\par
Genesis 29:3 TSK note: the flocks Instead of haadarim, "the flocks, " the Samaritan reads haroim, "the shepherds, " as does also the Arabic in Walton's Polyglott. This verse describes what was usually done by some mutual compact among the shepherds, and shows the purpose for which the flocks lay by the well; for the stone was not removed till all the flocks had been collected. Scott.\par
Genesis 29:6 TSK note: Is he well Heb. there peace to him\par
Genesis 29:7 TSK note: Lo; it is yet high day Heb. yet the day is great\par
Genesis 29:9 TSK note: Rachel;, ; for she kept them In those primitive times, a pastoral life was not only considered useful but honourable. Nor was it beneath the dignity of the daughters of the most opulent chiefs to carry water from the well, or tend the sheep. Jacob, Moses, and David were shepherds.\par
Genesis 29:13 TSK note: tidings Heb. hearing he ran kissed;, ; all these\par
Genesis 29:14 Brenton note: Gr. month of days.\par
Genesis 29:14 TSK note: art my, ; , ; the space of a month Heb. a month of days\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} And Laban said to Jacob, Surely thou shalt not serve me for nothing, because thou art my brother; tell me what thy reward is to be. \textsuperscript{16} Now Laban had two daughters, the name of the elder was Lea, and the name of the younger, Rachel. \textsuperscript{17} And the eyes of Lea were weak. But Rachel was beautiful in appearance, and exceedingly fair in countenance. \textsuperscript{18} And Jacob loved Rachel, and said, I will serve thee seven years for thy younger daughter Rachel. \textsuperscript{19} And Laban said to him, It is better that I should give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man; dwell with me. \textsuperscript{20} And Jacob served for Rachel seven years, and they were before him as a few days, by reason of his loving her. \textsuperscript{21} And Jacob said to Laban, Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in to her. \textsuperscript{22} And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a marriage-feast. \textsuperscript{23} And it was even, and he took his daughter Lea, and brought her in to Jacob, and Jacob went in to her. \textsuperscript{24} And Laban gave to his daughter Lea, Zelpha his handmaid, as a handmaid for her. \textsuperscript{25} And it was morning, and behold it was Lea; and Jacob said to Laban, What is this that thou hast done to me? did I not serve thee for Rachel? and wherefore hast thou deceived me? \textsuperscript{26} And Laban answered, It is not done thus in our country, to give the younger before the elder. \textsuperscript{27} Fulfil then her sevens, and I will give to thee her also in return for thy labour, which thou labourest with me, yet seven other years. \textsuperscript{28} And Jacob did so, and fulfilled her sevens; and Laban gave him his daughter Rachel to wife. \textsuperscript{29} And Laban gave to his daughter his handmaid Balla, for a handmaid to her. \textsuperscript{30} And he went in to Rachel; and he loved Rachel more than Lea; and he served him seven other years.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 29:18 TSK note: loved, I will serve In ancient times, it was a custom among many nations to give dowries for their wives; but Jacob, being poor, offered for Rachel seven year's service.\par
Genesis 29:20 TSK note: am 2251, bc 1753 served; for the love\par
Genesis 29:21 TSK note: Give me my days, go in\par
Genesis 29:27 Brenton note: Hebrew background: avodah (עֲבֹדָה) = service; work; worship. Common English renderings: service; work. Can denote labor or cultic service.\par
Genesis 29:28 TSK note: fulfilled her week The public marriage feast made on this occasion, seems to have formed the regular method of recognising the marriage, and lasted seven days. It would therefore have been improper to have broken off the solemnities to which all the men of the place had been invited ( ) and probably Laban wished to keep the fraud from the public eye. It is perfectly plain that Jacob did not serve seven years more before he got Rachel to wife.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{31} And when the Lord God saw that Lea was hated, he opened her womb; but Rachel was barren. \textsuperscript{32} And Lea conceived and bore a son to Jacob; and she called his name, Ruben; saying, Because the Lord has looked on my humiliation, and has given me a son, now then my husband will love me. \textsuperscript{33} And she conceived again, and bore a second son to Jacob; and she said, Because the Lord has heard that I am hated, he has given to me this one also; and she called his name, Simeon. \textsuperscript{34} And she conceived yet again, and bore a son, and said, In the present time my husband will be with me, for I have born him three sons; therefore she called his name, Levi. \textsuperscript{35} And having conceived yet again, she bore a son, and said, Now yet again this time will I give thanks to the Lord; therefore she called his name, Juda; and ceased bearing.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 29:31 TSK note: saw was hated, ; , ; he opened\par
Genesis 29:32 Brenton note: Name meaning: Reuben (Reuven) — Behold a son Leah’s first son; hoped it would win Jacob’s love.\par
Genesis 29:32 TSK note: am 2252, bc 1752 his name, ; Reuben that is, see a son looked\par
Genesis 29:33 Brenton note: Name meaning: Simeon (Shimon) — Heard The LORD heard that Leah was hated.\par
Genesis 29:33 TSK note: am 2253, bc 1751 Because, called, Simeon that is, Hearing\par
Genesis 29:34 Brenton note: Name meaning: Levi (Levi) — Joined; attached Leah hoped her husband would be joined to her; tribe of priests.\par
Genesis 29:34 Brenton note: Hebrew background: Levi (לֵוִי) = Levi; Levite. Common English renderings: Levi; Levite. Tribal name later associated with priestly service.\par
Genesis 29:34 TSK note: am 2254, bc 1750 was, ;, ; Levi that is, joined\par
Genesis 29:35 Brenton note: Name meaning: Judah (Yehudah) — Praise Royal tribe and ancestor of Messiah.\par
Genesis 29:35 Brenton note: Hebrew background: Yehudah (יְהוּדָה) = Judah. Common English renderings: Judah. Tribal name central to kingship and messianic expectation.\par
Genesis 29:35 Brenton note: Hebrew background: yadah (יָדָה) = to praise; give thanks; confess. Common English renderings: praise; thank; confess. Depending on stem, can denote thanksgiving or confession.\par
Genesis 29:35 TSK note: am 2255, bc 1749 called, ; Judah that is, Praise left bearing Heb. stood from bearing, ; That is, for a time; for she had several children afterwards. (See note on and following.)\par

\subsection*{Genesis 30}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Rachel having perceived that she bore Jacob no children, was jealous of her sister; and said to Jacob, Give me children; and if not, I shall die. \textsuperscript{2} And Jacob was angry with Rachel, and said to her, Am I in the place of God, who has deprived thee of the fruit of the womb? \textsuperscript{3} And Rachel said to Jacob, Behold my handmaid Balla, go in to her, and she shall bear upon my knees, and I also shall have children by her. \textsuperscript{4} And she gave him Balla her maid, for a wife to him; and Jacob went in to her. \textsuperscript{5} And Balla, Rachel's maid, conceived, and bore Jacob a son. \textsuperscript{6} And Rachel said, God has given judgment for me, and hearkened to my voice, and has given me a son; therefore she called his name, Dan. \textsuperscript{7} And Balla, Rachel's maid, conceived yet again, and bore a second son to Jacob. \textsuperscript{8} And Rachel said, God has helped me, and I contended with my sister and prevailed; and she called his name, Nephthalim. \textsuperscript{9} And Lea saw that she ceased from bearing, and she took Zelpha her maid, and gave her to Jacob for a wife; and he went in to her. \textsuperscript{10} And Zelpha the maid of Lea conceived, and bore Jacob a son. \textsuperscript{11} And Lea said, It is happily: and she called his name, Gad. \textsuperscript{12} And Zelpha the maid of Lea conceived yet again, and bore Jacob a second son. \textsuperscript{13} And Lea said, I am blessed, for the women will pronounce me blessed; and she called his name, Aser. \textsuperscript{14} And Ruben went in the day of barley-harvest, and found apples of mandrakes in the field, and brought them to his mother Lea; and Rachel said to Lea her sister, Give me of thy son's mandrakes. \textsuperscript{15} And Lea said, Is it not enough for thee that thou hast taken my husband, wilt thou also take my son's mandrakes? And Rachel said, Not so: let him lie with thee to-night for thy son's mandrakes. \textsuperscript{16} And Jacob came in out of the field at even; and Lea went forth to meet him, and said, Thou shalt come in to me this day, for I have hired thee for my son's mandrakes; and he lay with her that night. \textsuperscript{17} And God hearkened to Lea, and she conceived, and bore Jacob a fifth son. \textsuperscript{18} And Lea said, God has given me my reward, because I gave my maid to my husband; and she called his name Issachar, which is, Reward. \textsuperscript{19} And Lea conceived again, and bore Jacob a sixth son. \textsuperscript{20} And Lea said, God has given me a good gift in this time; my husband will choose me, for I have born him six sons: and she called his name, Zabulon. \textsuperscript{21} And after this she bore a daughter; and she called her name, Dina. \textsuperscript{22} And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and he opened her womb. \textsuperscript{23} And she conceived, and bore Jacob a son; and Rachel said, God has taken away my reproach. \textsuperscript{24} And she called his name Joseph, saying, Let God add to me another son.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 30:1 Brenton note: Hebrew background: qana (קָנָא) = to be jealous; zealous. Common English renderings: jealous; zealous. Can express sinful envy or righteous zeal.\par
Genesis 30:1 TSK note: when Rachel envied Envy and jealousy are most tormenting passions to the breast which harbours them, vexatious to all around, and introductory to much impatience and ungodliness. "Who is able to stand before envy?"; , or else I die\par
Genesis 30:3 TSK note: Behold, she shall; have children by her Heb. be built up by her, *marg.\par
Genesis 30:6 TSK note: am 2256, bc 1748 God;, ; Dan that is, Judging\par
Genesis 30:8 TSK note: great wrestlings Heb. wrestlings of God, ; *marg. and she, ; Naphtali that is, My wrestling, ;, Nephthalim\par
Genesis 30:9 TSK note: am 2256, bc 1748 left, gave her\par
Genesis 30:11 TSK note: she, ; Gad that is, A troop, or company\par
Genesis 30:13 Brenton note: Hebrew background: chevel (חֶבֶל) = cord; region; sorrow. Common English renderings: line; lot; sorrow. A varied term for measuring line, territory, or pain.\par
Genesis 30:13 TSK note: am 2257, bc 1747 Happy am I Heb. In my happiness, will call.; and she, ; Asher that is, Happy\par
Genesis 30:14 TSK note: am 2256, bc 1748 mandrakes The mandrake may be the Hebrew dudaim . It is so rendered by all the ancient versions, and is a species of melon, of an agreeable odour. Hasselquist, speaking of Nazareth in Galilee, says, "What I found most remarkable at this village was the great number of mandrakes which grew in a vale below it. I had not the pleasure of seeing this plant in blossom, the fruit now (May 5th, O. S.) hanging ripe on the stem, which lay withered on the ground. From the season in which this mandrake blossoms and ripens fruit, one might form a conjecture that it was Rachel's dudaim . These were brought her in the wheat harvest, which in Galilee is in the month of May, about this time, and the mandrake was now in fruit." The Abbee Mariti describes it as growing "low like a lettuce, to which its leaves have a great resemblance, except that they have a dark green colour. The flowers are purple, and the root is for the most part forked. The fruit, when ripe in the beginning of May, is of the size and colour of a small apple, exceedingly ruddy, and of a most agreeable odour. Our guide thought us fools for suspecting it to be unwholesome." Give me\par
Genesis 30:18 TSK note: and she, ; Issachar that is, An hire\par
Genesis 30:20 TSK note: am cir, 2258, bc cir, 1746 now will, and she, ;, ; Zebulun that is, Dwelling, Zabulon\par
Genesis 30:21 TSK note: am cir, 2259, bc 1745 and called, Dinah that is, Judgment\par
Genesis 30:23 Brenton note: Hebrew background: cherpah (חֶרְפָּה) = reproach; disgrace. Common English renderings: reproach; shame. Often a social disgrace removed by divine intervention.\par
Genesis 30:23 TSK note: "Be fruitful and multiply, " was the blessing of God: barrenness therefore was reckoned a reproach The intense desire of having children, observable among the Jewish women, arose not only from this reproach of barrenness, but from the hope of being the mother of the promised seed, and Him in whom all the nations of the earth were to be blessed.\par
Genesis 30:24 Brenton note: Name meaning: Joseph (Yosef) — He adds; may He add God added to his blessings despite betrayal; savior of his family.\par
Genesis 30:24 TSK note: And she, ; Joseph that is, Adding\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} And it came to pass when Rachel had born Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, Send me away, that I may go to my place and to my land. \textsuperscript{26} Restore my wives and my children, for whom I have served thee, that I may depart, for thou knowest the service wherewith I have served thee. \textsuperscript{27} And Laban said to him, If I have found grace in thy sight, I would augur well , for the Lord has blessed me at thy coming in. \textsuperscript{28} Appoint me thy wages, and I will give them . \textsuperscript{29} And Jacob said, Thou knowest in what things I have served thee, and how many cattle of thine are with me. \textsuperscript{30} For it was little thou hadst before my time, and it is increased to a multitude, and the Lord God has blessed thee since my coming; now then, when shall I set up also my own house? \textsuperscript{31} And Laban said to him, What shall I give thee? and Jacob said to him, Thou shalt not give me anything; if thou wilt do this thing for me, I will again tend thy flocks and keep them. \textsuperscript{32} Let all thy sheep pass by to-day, and separate thence every grey sheep among the rams, and every one that is speckled and spotted among the goats— this shall be my reward. \textsuperscript{33} And my righteousness shall answer for me on the morrow, for it is my reward before thee: whatever shall not be spotted and speckled among the goats, and grey among the rams, shall be stolen with me. \textsuperscript{34} And Laban said to him, Let it be according to thy word. \textsuperscript{35} And he separated in that day the spotted and speckled he-goats, and all the spotted and speckled she-goats, and all that was grey among the rams, and every one that was white among them, and he gave them into the hand of his sons. \textsuperscript{36} And he set a distance of a three days' journey between them and Jacob. And Jacob tended the cattle of Laban that were left behind. \textsuperscript{37} And Jacob took to himself green rods of storax tree and walnut and plane-tree; and Jacob peeled in them white stripes; and as he drew off the green, the white stripe which he had made appeared alternate on the rods. \textsuperscript{38} And he laid the rods which he had peeled, in the hollows of the watering-troughs, that whensoever the cattle should come to drink, as they should have come to drink before the rods, the cattle might conceive at the rods. \textsuperscript{39} So the cattle conceived at the rods, and the cattle brought forth young speckled, and streaked and spotted with ash-coloured spots . \textsuperscript{40} And Jacob separated the lambs, and set before the sheep a speckled ram, and every variegated one among the lambs, and he separated flocks for himself alone, and did not mingle them with the sheep of Laban. \textsuperscript{41} And it came to pass in the time wherein the cattle became pregnant, conceiving in the belly, Jacob put the rods before the cattle in the troughs, that they might conceive by the rods. \textsuperscript{42} But he did not put them in indiscriminately whenever the cattle happened to bring forth, but the unmarked ones were Laban's, and the marked ones Jacob's. \textsuperscript{43} And the man became very rich, and he had many cattle, and oxen, and servants, and maid-servants, and camels, and asses.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 30:25 TSK note: Send me away, mine, and to\par
Genesis 30:27 Brenton note: Stay thou, perhaps understood. Heb. I have argued that, etc.\par
Genesis 30:28 Brenton note: Lit. thy wages to or with me.\par
Genesis 30:30 Brenton note: So A. V. but Gr. and Heb. literally, at my foot.\par
Genesis 30:30 Brenton note: Hebrew background: me’at (מְעַט) = little; few. Common English renderings: little; few. A term of smallness or insufficiency.\par
Genesis 30:30 TSK note: increased Heb. broken forth, and the since my coming Heb. at my foot, when\par
Genesis 30:32 Brenton note: Hebrew background: keves (כֶּבֶשׂ) = lamb. Common English renderings: lamb. Important sacrificial animal term.\par
Genesis 30:33 Brenton note: Hearken to or obey me.\par
Genesis 30:33 TSK note: righteousness; answer in time to come Heb. to-morrow, that shall be Supply the ellipsis by inserting "if found, " after "stolen, " and the sense will be clear.\par
Genesis 30:35 TSK note: he removed From this it appears, that, as Jacob had agreed to take all the parti-coloured for his wages, and was now only beginning to act upon this agreement, and consequently had as yet no right to any of the cattle, therefore Laban separated from the flock all such cattle as Jacob might afterwards claim in consequence of his bargain, leaving only the black and white with Jacob. the hand\par
Genesis 30:36 Brenton note: Gr. and between. Hebraism.\par
Genesis 30:37 Brenton note: Apparently the nom. absol.\par
Genesis 30:37 Brenton note: Greek background: rhabdos (ῥάβδος) = rod; staff. Common English renderings: rod; staff. Used literally of staff or rod and figuratively of authority.\par
Genesis 30:37 TSK note: Jacob green poplar Livneh is the white poplar, so called from the whiteness of its leaves, bark, and wood, from lavan to be white., hasel, Jerome, Hiller, Celsius, Dr. Shaw, Bochart, and other learned men, say, that luz is not the "hazel" but the almond-tree, as the word denotes both in Arabic and Syriac. chestnut tree The Heb. word ârmon, signifies "the plane-tree, " so called from the bark naturally peeling off, and leaving the trunk naked, as its root âram, signifies.\par
Genesis 30:40 Brenton note: Hebrew background: paras (פָּרַשׂ) = to spread; separate. Common English renderings: spread; divide. Literal and cultic separation term.\par
Genesis 30:41 Brenton note: The meaning of the Hebrew seems to be, when the cattle were weak from any cause. The LXX. by assigning the yeaning time as the cause, have obscured the passage. Of course Jacob would not put them in then.\par
Genesis 30:41 TSK note: whensoever the stronger cattle did conceive As the means which Jacob used would not in general produce similar effects, nay, probably the experiment was never in any other instance tried with effect, it is more in harmony with Divine truth to suppose that he was directed by some Divine intimation; and rendered successful, if not by a direct miracle, yet at least by the Lord's giving a new and uncommon bias to the tendency of natural causes.\par
Genesis 30:43 TSK note: The Lord will, in one way or other, honour those who simply trust his providence.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Genesis 31}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Jacob heard the words of the sons of Laban, saying, Jacob has taken all that was our father's, and of our father's property has he gotten all this glory. \textsuperscript{2} And Jacob saw the countenance of Laban, and behold it was not toward him as before. \textsuperscript{3} And the Lord said to Jacob, Return to the land of thy father, and to thy family, and I will be with thee. \textsuperscript{4} And Jacob sent and called Lea and Rachel to the plain where the flocks were. \textsuperscript{5} And he said to them, I see the face of your father, that it is not toward me as before, but the God of my father was with me. \textsuperscript{6} And ye too know that with all my might I have served your father. \textsuperscript{7} But your father deceived me, and changed my wages for the ten lambs, yet God gave him not power to hurt me. \textsuperscript{8} If he should say thus, The speckled shall be thy reward, then all the cattle would bear speckled; and if he should say, The white shall be thy reward, then would all the cattle bear white. \textsuperscript{9} So God has taken away all the cattle of your father, and given them to me. \textsuperscript{10} And it came to pass when the cattle conceived and were with young, that I beheld with mine eyes in sleep, and behold the he-goats and the rams leaping on the sheep and the she-goats, speckled and variegated and spotted with ash-coloured spots. \textsuperscript{11} And the angel of God said to me in a dream, Jacob; and I said, What is it? \textsuperscript{12} And he said, Look up with thine eyes, and behold the he-goats and the rams leaping on the sheep and the she-goats, speckled and variegated and spotted with ash-coloured spots; for I have seen all things that Laban does to thee. \textsuperscript{13} I am God that appeared to thee in the place of God, where thou anointedst a pillar to me, and vowedst to me there a vow; now then arise and depart out of this land, depart into the land of thy nativity, and I will be with thee. \textsuperscript{14} And Rachel and Lea answered and said to him, Have we yet a part or inheritance in the house of our father? \textsuperscript{15} Are we not considered strangers by him? for he has sold us, and quite devoured our money. \textsuperscript{16} All the wealth and the glory which God has taken from our father, it shall be our's and our children's; now then do whatsoever God has said to thee. \textsuperscript{17} And Jacob arose and took his wives and his children up on the camels; \textsuperscript{18} and he took away all his possessions and all his store, which he had gotten in Mesopotamia, and all that belonged to him, to depart to Isaac his father in the land of Chanaan. \textsuperscript{19} And Laban went to shear his sheep; and Rachel stole her father's images. \textsuperscript{20} And Jacob hid the matter from Laban the Syrian, so as not to tell him that he ran away. \textsuperscript{21} And he departed himself and all that belonged to him, and passed over the river, and went into the mountain Galaad. \textsuperscript{22} But it was told Laban the Syrian on the third day, that Jacob was fled. \textsuperscript{23} And having taken his brethren with him, he pursued after him seven days' journey, and overtook him on Mount Galaad. \textsuperscript{24} And God came to Laban the Syrian in sleep by night, and said to him, Take heed to thyself that thou speak not at any time to Jacob evil things. \textsuperscript{25} And Laban overtook Jacob; and Jacob pitched his tent in the mountain; and Laban stationed his brothers in the mount Galaad. \textsuperscript{26} And Laban said to Jacob, What hast thou done? wherefore didst thou run away secretly, and pillage me, and lead away my daughters as captives taken with the sword? \textsuperscript{27} Whereas if thou hadst told me, I would have sent thee away with mirth, and with songs, and timbrels, and harp. \textsuperscript{28} And I was not counted worthy to embrace my children and my daughters; now then thou hast wrought foolishly. \textsuperscript{29} And now my hand has power to hurt thee; but the God of thy father spoke to me yesterday, saying, Take heed to thyself that thou speak not evil words to Jacob. \textsuperscript{30} Now then go on thy way, for thou hast earnestly desired to depart to the house of thy father; wherefore hast thou stolen my gods? \textsuperscript{31} And Jacob answered and said to Laban, Because I was afraid; for I said, Lest at any time thou shouldest take away thy daughters from me, and all my possessions. \textsuperscript{32} And Jacob said, With whomsoever thou shalt find thy gods, he shall not live in the presence of our brethren; take notice of what I have of thy property, and take it; and he observed nothing with him, but Jacob knew not that his wife Rachel had stolen them. \textsuperscript{33} And Laban went in and searched in the house of Lea, and found them not; and he went out of the house of Lea, and searched in the house of Jacob, and in the house of the two maid-servants, and found them not; and he went also into the house of Rachel. \textsuperscript{34} And Rachel took the idols, and cast them among the camels' packs, and sat upon them. \textsuperscript{35} And she said to her father, Be not indignant, Sir; I cannot rise up before thee, for it is with me according to the manner of women. Laban searched in all the house, and found not the images. \textsuperscript{36} And Jacob was angry, and strove with Laban; and Jacob answered and said to Laban, What is my injustice, and what my sin, that thou hast pursued after me, \textsuperscript{37} and that thou hast searched all the furniture of my house? what hast thou found of all the furniture of thine house? set it here between thy relations and my relations, and let them decide between us two. \textsuperscript{38} These twenty years have I been with thee; thy sheep, and thy she-goats have not failed in bearing; I devoured not the rams of thy cattle. \textsuperscript{39} That which was taken of beasts I brought not to thee; I made good of myself the thefts of the day, and the thefts of the night. \textsuperscript{40} I was parched with heat by day, and chilled with frost by night, and my sleep departed from my eyes. \textsuperscript{41} These twenty years have I been in thy house; I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years among thy sheep, and thou didst falsely rate my wages for ten lambs. \textsuperscript{42} Unless I had the God of my father Abraam, and the fear of Isaac, now thou wouldest have sent me away empty; God saw my humiliation, and the labour of my hands, and rebuked thee yesterday.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 31:1 Brenton note: Hebrew background: kavod (כָּבוֹד) = glory; honor; weight. Common English renderings: glory; honor. Literally conveys heaviness; theologically used of divine glory.\par
Genesis 31:1 Brenton note: Greek background: doxa (δόξα) = glory; honor. Common English renderings: glory. The term can denote splendor, honor, or reputation.\par
Genesis 31:1 TSK note: Jacob; , ;, ; glory "Glory" is here used for "wealth, " riches, or property; since those who possess riches, generally make them the subject of glory. The original word cavod, signifies both "glory" and "weight."\par
Genesis 31:2 Brenton note: Gr. yesterday and the day before. Hebraism.\par
Genesis 31:2 TSK note: countenance; it was as before Heb. as yesterday and the day before, ; *marg.\par
Genesis 31:7 TSK note: ten times The Hebrew, âsereth monim, is literally, as Aquila renders, "ten numbers; " and Symmachus, "ten times in number; " which probably implies an indefinite number. (See note on .); God\par
Genesis 31:10 TSK note: a dream, ; rams or, he-goats ringstreaked grisled The original word, beroodim, from barad, "hail" means marked with white spots like hail; to which our word grisled, from the old French gresle, now grκle, hail, perfectly agrees; hence greslκ, spotted with white on a dark ground.\par

Genesis 31:16 Brenton note: Greek background: ploutos (πλοῦτος) = riches; wealth. Common English renderings: riches. Denotes wealth or abundance.\par

The Targums of Onkelos and Jonathan render it, tzalmanaya, "images; " the LXX and Theodoret, ειδολον, "idols; " Aquilla, μορφωματα, "figures; " and the Persian, asterlabha, "astrolabes."\par
Genesis 31:20 TSK note: unawares to Laban Heb. the heart of Laban (See note on ).\par
Genesis 31:24 TSK note: the Syrian; dream, ;, ; , ;, Take heed, ; either good or bad Heb. from good to bad\par
Genesis 31:27 Brenton note: Hebrew background: shir (שִׁיר) = song; to sing. Common English renderings: song; sing. Noun and verb forms are common in worship and celebration.\par
Genesis 31:27 TSK note: Wherefore, ; steal away from me Heb. hast stolen me, *marg. that I with mirth; tabret\par
Genesis 31:29 Brenton note: Greek background: dynamis (δύναμις) = power; might; force. Common English renderings: power; might. Can mean strength, capability, or miraculous power.\par
Genesis 31:29 TSK note: the power; the God, ; , yesternight Take\par
Genesis 31:32 TSK note: whomsoever This was rash, and might have produced fatal effects; but Jacob was partial to Rachel, and did not suspect her; and he was indignant at being accused of a crime which he deeply abhorred. Scott., before, ; , For Jacob\par
Genesis 31:34 TSK note: had taken, furniture The word, car, rendered "furniture, " properly denotes "a large round pannier, " placed one on each side of a camel, for a person, especially women, to ride in. It is a hamper, like a cradle, having a back, head, and sides, like a great chair. Moryson describes them as "two long chairs like cradles, covered with red cloth, to hang on the two sides of the camel." Hanway calls them kedgavays, which "are a kind of covered chairs, which the Persians hang over their camels in the manner of panniers, and are big enough for one person to sit in." Thevenot, who calls then counes, says that they lay over them a cover, which keeps then both from the rain and sun; and Maillet describes them as covered cages, hanging on each side of a camel. The late Editor of Calmet has furnished a correct delineation of these cars, as seen on one side of a camel, copied from Dalton's Prints of Egyptian Figures. searched Heb. felt\par
Genesis 31:35 TSK note: my lord; , rise up; custom\par
Genesis 31:36 Brenton note: Hebrew background: pesha (פֶּשַׁע) = transgression; rebellion. Common English renderings: transgression; trespass. Carries the idea of revolt against rightful authority.\par
Genesis 31:39 TSK note: torn of, ; I bare or stolen\par
Genesis 31:42 Brenton note: Hebrew background: pachad (פַּחַד) = fear; dread. Common English renderings: fear; dread. Strong fear term, sometimes a divine epithet in Jacob’s speech.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{43} And Laban answered and said to Jacob, The daughters are my daughters, and the sons my sons, and the cattle are my cattle, and all things which thou seest are mine, and the property of my daughters; what shall I do to them to-day, or their children which they bore? \textsuperscript{44} Now then come, let me make a covenant, both I and thou, and it shall be for a witness between me and thee; and he said to him, Behold, there is no one with us; behold, God is witness between me and thee. \textsuperscript{45} And Jacob having taken a stone, set it up for a pillar. \textsuperscript{46} And Jacob said to his brethren, Gather stones; and they gathered stones and made a heap, and ate there upon the heap; and Laban said to him, This heap witnesses between me and thee to-day. \textsuperscript{47} And Laban called it, the Heap of Testimony; and Jacob called it, the Witness Heap. \textsuperscript{48} And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and the pillar, which I have set between me and thee; this heap witnesses, and this pillar witnesses; therefore its name was called, the Heap witnesses. \textsuperscript{49} And the vision of which he said—Let God look to it between me and thee, because we are about to depart from each other,— \textsuperscript{50} If thou shalt humble my daughters, if thou shouldest take wives in addition to my daughters, see, there is no one with us looking on. God is witness between me and thee. \textsuperscript{52} For if I should not cross over unto thee, neither shouldest thou cross over to me, for mischief beyond this heap and this pillar. \textsuperscript{53} The God of Abraam and the God of Nachor judge between us; and Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac. \textsuperscript{54} And he offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and called his brethren, and they ate and drank, and slept in the mountain.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 31:44 TSK note: let us, ; a witness, ;, ;, ; God can put a bridle into the mouth of wicked man to restrain their malice; and then, though they have no love for his people, they will pretend to it, and try to make a merit of necessity. Scott.\par
Genesis 31:46 TSK note: brethren, Gather, ; an heap The word gal, rendered "heap, " properly signifies a round heap or circle; probably like the Druidical remains in this country, which have been traced in India, Persia, Western Asia, Greece, and Northern Europe. These usually consist of irregular circles of large stones, with a principal one in the midst; the former probably being used for seats, and the latter for an altar; corresponding to the stone set up as a pillar by Jacob, and the heap of stones collected by his brethren. They appear to have been used, as Gilgal undoubtedly was (; , ; ., . ) as temples, and as places for holding councils, and assembling the people. For a satisfactory elucidation of this subject, consult the Fragments to Calmet, Nos. 156, 735, 736.\par

Genesis 31:48 TSK note: This heap Galeed or, Gilead\par
Genesis 31:49 TSK note: Mizpah i.e. a beacon, or watch-tower, Mizpeh\par
Genesis 31:53 TSK note: God of Abraham, ; their father For avihem, "Their father, " several manuscripts read avichem, "Your father, " for Terah was an idolater (see note on ). judge sware, fear\par
Genesis 31:54 Brenton note: Hebrew background: zevach (זֶבַח) = sacrifice; slaughter offering. Common English renderings: sacrifice. Often a fellowship-type slaughter offering.\par
Genesis 31:54 Brenton note: Greek background: thysia (θυσία) = sacrifice. Common English renderings: sacrifice. A key sacrificial term, literal and theological.\par
Genesis 31:54 TSK note: offered sacrifice or, killed beasts did eat\par
\end{quote}

\noindent \textsuperscript{4} And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother to the land of Seir, to the country of Edom. \textsuperscript{5} And he charged them, saying, Thus shall ye say to my lord Esau: Thus saith thy servant Jacob; I have sojourned with Laban and tarried until now. \textsuperscript{6} And there were born to me oxen, and asses, and sheep, and men-servants and women-servants; and I sent to tell my lord Esau, that thy servant might find grace in thy sight. \textsuperscript{7} And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to thy brother Esau, and lo! he comes to meet thee, and four hundred men with him. \textsuperscript{8} And Jacob was greatly terrified, and was perplexed; and he divided the people that was with him, and the cows, and the camels, and the sheep, into two camps. \textsuperscript{9} And Jacob said, If Esau should come to one camp, and smite it, the other camp shall be in safety. \textsuperscript{10} And Jacob said, God of my father Abraam, and God of my father Isaac, O Lord, thou art he that said to me, Depart quickly to the land of thy birth, and I will do thee good. \textsuperscript{11} Let there be to me a sufficiency of all the justice and all the truth which thou hast wrought with thy servant; for with this my staff I passed over this Jordan, and now I am become two camps. \textsuperscript{12} Deliver me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau, for I am afraid of him, lest haply he should come and smite me, and the mother upon the children. \textsuperscript{13} But thou saidst, I will do thee good, and will make thy seed as the sand of the sea, which shall not be numbered for multitude. \textsuperscript{14} And he slept there that night, and took of the gifts which he carried with him , and sent out to Esau his brother, \textsuperscript{15} two hundred she-goats, twenty he-goats, two hundred sheep, twenty rams, \textsuperscript{16} milch camels, and their foals, thirty, forty kine, ten bulls, twenty asses, and ten colts. \textsuperscript{17} And he gave them to his servants each drove apart; and he said to his servants, Go on before me, and put a space between drove and drove. \textsuperscript{18} And he charged the first, saying, If Esau my brother meet thee, and he ask thee, saying, Whose art thou? and whither wouldest thou go, and whose are these possessions advancing before thee? \textsuperscript{19} Thou shalt say, Thy servant Jacob's; he hath sent gifts to my lord Esau, and lo! he is behind us. \textsuperscript{20} And he charged the first and the second and the third, and all that went before him after these flocks, saying, Thus shall ye speak to Esau when ye find him; \textsuperscript{21} and ye shall say, Behold thy servant Jacob comes after us. For he said, I will propitiate his countenance with the gifts going before his presence, and afterwards I will behold his face, for peradventure he will accept me. \textsuperscript{22} So the presents went on before him, but he himself lodged that night in the camp. \textsuperscript{23} And he rose up in that night, and took his two wives and his two servant-maids, and his eleven children, and crossed over the ford of Jaboch. \textsuperscript{24} And he took them, and passed over the torrent, and brought over all his possessions.\par

Genesis 32:14 TSK note: This was a princely present. The "thirty milch camels" were particularly valuable; for among the Arabs they constitute a principal part of their riches; being every way so serviceable, that the providence of God appears peculiarly kind and wise in providing such animals for those countries, where no other animal could be of equal service. The she-camel gives milk continually, not ceasing even when with young; the milk of which, when mixed with three parts of water, affords the most pleasant and wholesome beverage.\par

And he said, The children with which God has mercifully blessed thy servant. \textsuperscript{6} And the maid-servants and their children drew near and did reverence. \textsuperscript{7} And Lea and her children drew near and did reverence; and after this drew near Rachel and Joseph, and did reverence. \textsuperscript{8} And he said, What are these things to thee, all these companies that I have met? And he said, That thy servant might find grace in thy sight, my lord. \textsuperscript{9} And Esau said, I have much, my brother; keep thine own. \textsuperscript{10} And Jacob said, If I have found grace in thy sight, receive the gifts through my hands; therefore have I seen thy face, as if any one should see the face of God, and thou shalt be well-pleased with me. \textsuperscript{11} Receive my blessings, which I have brought thee, because God has had mercy on me, and I have all things; and he constrained him, and he took them . \textsuperscript{12} And he said, Let us depart, and proceed right onward. \textsuperscript{13} And he said to him, My lord knows, that the children are very tender, and the flocks and the herds with me are with young; if then I shall drive them hard one day, all the cattle will die. \textsuperscript{14} Let my lord go on before his servant, and I shall have strength on the road according to the ease of the journey before me, and according to the strength of the children, until I come to my lord to Seir. \textsuperscript{15} And Esau said, I will leave with thee some of the people who are with me. Genesis 34:12 TSK note: Ask me On the practice of purchasing wives, Deut. Lam. Roque says, "Properly speaking, a young man who would marry must purchase his wife; and fathers among the Arabs are never so happy as when they have many daughters. They form part of the riches of the house. Accordingly, when a young man would treat with a person whose daughter he is inclined to marry, he says to him, 'Will you give me your daughter for fifty sheep, for six camels, or for a dozen cows?' according to the rank of her family, and the circumstances of him who desires to marry her." dowry\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} And the sons of Jacob answered to Sychem and Emmor his father craftily, and spoke to them, because they had defiled Dina their sister. \textsuperscript{14} And Symeon and Levi, the brothers of Dina, said to them, We shall not be able to do this thing, to give our sister to a man who is uncircumcised, for it is a reproach to us. \textsuperscript{15} Only on these terms will we conform to you, and dwell among you, if ye also will be as we are, in that every male of you be circumcised. \textsuperscript{16} And we will give our daughters to you, and we will take of your daughters for wives to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will be as one race. \textsuperscript{17} But if ye will not hearken to us to be circumcised, we will take our daughter and depart. \textsuperscript{18} And the words pleased Emmor, and Sychem the son of Emmor. \textsuperscript{19} And the young man delayed not to do this thing, for he was much attached to Jacob's daughter, and he was the most honourable of all in his father's house. \textsuperscript{20} And Emmor and Sychem his son came to the gate of their city, and spoke to the men of their city, saying, \textsuperscript{21} These men are peaceable, let them dwell with us upon the land, and let them trade in it, and behold the land is extensive before them; we will take their daughters to us for wives, and we will give them our daughters. \textsuperscript{22} Only on these terms will the men conform to us to dwell with us so as to be one people, if every male of us be circumcised, as they also are circumcised. \textsuperscript{23} And shall not their cattle and their herds, and their possessions, be ours? only in this let us conform to them, and they will dwell with us. \textsuperscript{24} And all that went in at the gate of their city hearkened to Emmor and Sychem his son, and they were circumcised in the flesh of their foreskin every male.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 34:19 Brenton note: Gr. word.\par
Genesis 34:19 Brenton note: Hebrew background: chafets (חָפֵץ) = to delight in; desire. Common English renderings: delight; desire. Used of pleasure, will, and divine delight.\par
Genesis 34:23 Brenton note: Gr. quadrupeds.\par
Genesis 34:24 TSK note: hearkened In thus falling into this measure, the Shechemites must either have had great affection for their chief and his son, or have been under the influence of the most passive obedience. The petty princes of Asia have always been absolute and despotic; their subjects paying them the most prompt and blind obedience. The following instance will sufficiently illustrate and confirm this statement: Abu Thaher, chief of the Carmathians, about the year 930, with only 500 horse, went to lay siege to Bagdad. The khalif's general marched out to seize him; but before the attack, sent an officer to summon him to surrender. "How many men has the khalif's general?" said Abu Thaher; "30, 000, " replied the officer. "Among them all, " says the Carmathian chief, "has he got three like mine?" Then ordering his followers to approach, he commanded one to stab himself, another to throw himself from a precipice, and a third to plunge into the Tigris. All three instantly obeyed, and perished! Then turning to the officer, he said, "He who has such troops need not value the number of his enemies!" went out, every male\par
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 36:31 TSK note: the kings, ;, ;, ; before there Moses may here allude to the promise which God made to Jacob ( ), that kings should proceed from him; and here states that these kings reigned before that prophecy began to be fulfilled.\par
Genesis 36:33 TSK note: am cir, 2135, bc cir, 1869 Bozrah, Bezer, or Bostra, was situated in Arabia Deserta, and the eastern part of Edom; and, according to Eusebius, was 24 miles from Edrei. It afterwards belonged to Moab, and was given by Moses to Reuben, but again reverted to Edom. It is now called Boszra; and is described by Burckhardt as the largest town in the Haouran, including its ruins, though only inhabited by about twelve or fifteen families. It is situated in the open plain, two hours distant from Aare, and is at present the last inhabited place in the south-east extremity of the Haouran. It is of an oval shape, it greatest length being from east to west; and its circumference three quarters of an hour.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Jacob dwelt in the land where his father sojourned, in the land of Chanaan. \textsuperscript{2} And these are the generations of Jacob. And they hated him still more for his dreams and for his words. \textsuperscript{9} And he dreamed another dream, and related it to his father, and to his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed another dream: as it were the sun, and the moon, and the eleven stars did me reverence. \textsuperscript{10} And his father rebuked him, and said to him, What is this dream which thou hast dreamed? shall indeed both I and thy mother and thy brethren come and bow before thee to the earth? \textsuperscript{11} And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying. \textsuperscript{12} And his brethren went to feed the sheep of their father to Sychem. \textsuperscript{13} And Israel said to Joseph, Do not thy brethren feed their flock in Sychem? Come, I will send thee to them; and he said to him, Behold, I am here . \textsuperscript{14} And Israel said to him, Go and see if thy brethren and the sheep are well, and bring me word; and he sent him out of the valley of Chebron, and he came to Sychem. \textsuperscript{15} And a man found him wandering in the field; and the man asked him, saying, What seekest thou? \textsuperscript{16} And he said, I am seeking my brethren; tell me where they feed their flocks . \textsuperscript{17} And the man said to him, They have departed hence, for I heard them saying, Let us go to Dothaim; and Joseph went after his brethren, and found them in Dothaim.\par

This drug is abundant in Syria, and here Moses joins with it resin, honey, and myrrh; which agrees with the nature of the storax, which is the resin of a tree of the same name, of a reddish colour, and peculiarly pleasant fragrance. balm Tzeri, which in Arabic, as a verb, is to flow, seems to be a common name, as balm or balsam with us, for many of those oily, resinous substances, which flow spontaneously, or by incision, from various trees or plants; accordingly the ancients have generally interpreted it resin. myrrh Lot, is probably, as Junius, Deut. Dieu, Celsius, and Ursinus contend, the same as the Arabic ladan, Greek λαδανον, and Latin ladanum .\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{26} And Judas said to his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood? \textsuperscript{27} Come, let us sell him to these Ismaelites, but let not our hands be upon him, because he is our brother and our flesh; and his brethren hearkened. \textsuperscript{28} And the men, the merchants of Madian, went by, and they drew and lifted Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ismaelites for twenty pieces of gold; and they brought Joseph down into Egypt. \textsuperscript{29} And Ruben returned to the pit, and sees not Joseph in the pit; and he rent his garments. \textsuperscript{30} And he returned to his brethren and said, The boy is not; and I, whither am I yet to go? \textsuperscript{31} And having taken the coat of Joseph, they slew a kid of the goats, and stained the coat with the blood. \textsuperscript{32} And they sent the coat of many colours; and they brought it to their father, and said, This have we found; know if it be thy son's coat or no. \textsuperscript{33} And he recognised it, and said, It is my son's coat, an evil wild beast has devoured him; a wild beast has carried off Joseph. \textsuperscript{34} And Jacob rent his clothes, and put sackcloth on his loins, and mourned for his son many days. \textsuperscript{35} And all his sons and his daughters gathered themselves together, and came to comfort him; but he would not be comforted, saying, I will go down to my son mourning to Hades; and his father wept for him. \textsuperscript{36} And the Madianites sold Joseph into Egypt; to Petephres, the eunuch of Pharao, captain of the guard.\par
