\subsection*{Genesis 38}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And it came to pass at that time that Judas went down from his brethren, and came as far as to a certain man of Odollam, whose name was Iras. \textsuperscript{2} And Judas saw there the daughter of a Chananitish man, whose name was Sava; and he took her, and went in to her. \textsuperscript{3} And she conceived and bore a son, and called his name, Er. \textsuperscript{4} And she conceived and bore a son again; and called his name, Aunan. \textsuperscript{5} And she again bore a son; and called his name, Selom: and she was in Chasbi when she bore them. \textsuperscript{6} And Judas took a wife for Er his first-born, whose name was Thamar. \textsuperscript{7} And Er, the first-born of Judas, was wicked before the Lord; and God killed him. \textsuperscript{8} And Judas said to Aunan, Go in to thy brother's wife, and marry her as her brother-in-law, and raise up seed to thy brother. \textsuperscript{9} And Aunan, knowing that the seed should not be his—it came to pass when he went in to his brother's wife, that he spilled it upon the ground, so that he should not give seed to his brother's wife. \textsuperscript{10} And his doing this appeared evil before God; and he slew him also.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 38:1 TSK note: am 2265, bc 1739 it came As there cannot be above 23 years from the selling of Joseph, unto Israel's going down into Egypt; and as it is impossible that Judah should take a wife, and by her have three sons successively, and Shelah, the youngest, marriageable when Judah begat Pharez of Tamar, and Pharez be grown up, married, and have two sons, all within so short a period; Mr. Ainsworth conceives that the time here spoken of is soon after Jacob's coming to Shechem ( ). We have accordingly adapted the chronology to correspond with that time. turned; , Adullamite An inhabitant of Adullam, a city of Canaan, afterwards given to Judah, situated in the southern part of that tribe, west of Hebron.\par

Genesis 38:7 Brenton note: Greek background: kakia (κακία) = badness; malice. Common English renderings: malice; evil. Often denotes moral badness or malice.\par
Genesis 38:10 TSK note: displeased Heb. was evil in the eyes of, ; , ; him also\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} And Judas said to Thamar, his daughter-in-law, Sit thou a widow in the house of thy father-in-law, until Selom my son be grown; for he said, Lest he also die as his brethren; and Thamar departed, and sat in the house of her father. \textsuperscript{12} And the days were fulfilled, and Sava the wife of Judas died; and Judas, being comforted, went to them that sheared his sheep, himself and Iras his shepherd the Odollamite, to Thamna. \textsuperscript{13} And it was told Thamar his daughter-in-law, saying, Behold, thy father-in-law goeth up to Thamna, to shear his sheep. \textsuperscript{14} And having taken off the garments of her widowhood from her, she put on a veil, and ornamented her face, and sat by the gates of Ænan, which is in the way to Thamna, for she saw that Selom was grown; but he gave her not to him for a wife. \textsuperscript{15} And when Judas saw her, he thought her to be a harlot; for she covered her face, and he knew her not. \textsuperscript{16} And he went out of his way to her, and said to her, Let me come in to thee; for he knew not that she was his daughter-in-law; and she said, What wilt thou give me if thou shouldest come in to me? \textsuperscript{17} And he said, I will send thee a kid of the goats from my flock; and she said, Well , if thou wilt give me an earnest, until thou send it. \textsuperscript{18} And he said, What is the earnest that I shall give thee? and she said, Thy ring, and thy bracelet, and the staff in thy hand; and he gave them to her, and went in to her, and she conceived by him. \textsuperscript{19} And she arose and departed, and took her veil from off her, and put on the garments of her widowhood. \textsuperscript{20} And Judas sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his shepherd the Odollamite, to receive the pledge from the woman; and he found her not. \textsuperscript{21} And he asked the men of the place, Where is the harlot who was in Ænan by the way-side? and they said, There was no harlot here. \textsuperscript{22} And he returned to Judas, and said, I have not found her; and the men of the place say, There is no harlot here. \textsuperscript{23} And Judas said, Let her have them, but let us not be ridiculed; I sent this kid, but thou hast not found her. \textsuperscript{24} And it came to pass after three months, that it was told Judas, saying, Thamar thy daughter-in-law has grievously played the harlot, and behold she is with child by whoredom; and Judas said, Bring her out, and let her be burnt. \textsuperscript{25} And as they were bringing her, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, I am with child by the man whose these things are; and she said, See whose is this ring and bracelet and staff. \textsuperscript{26} And Judas knew them , and said, Thamar is cleared rather than I, forasmuch as I gave her not to Selom my son: and he knew her not again. \textsuperscript{27} And it came to pass when she was in labour, that she also had twins in her womb. \textsuperscript{28} And it came to pass as she was bringing forth, one thrust forth his hand, and the midwife having taken hold of it, bound upon his hand a scarlet thread , saying, This one shall come out first. \textsuperscript{29} And when he drew back his hand, then immediately came forth his brother; and she said, Why has the barrier been cut through because of thee? and she called his name, Phares. \textsuperscript{30} And after this came forth his brother, on whose hand was the scarlet thread; and she called his name, Zara.\par

\subsection*{Genesis 39}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Petephres the eunuch of Pharao, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ismaelites, who brought him down thither. \textsuperscript{2} And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house with his lord the Egyptian. \textsuperscript{3} And his master knew that the Lord was with him, and the Lord prospers in his hands whatsoever he happens to do. \textsuperscript{4} And Joseph found grace in the presence of his lord, and was well-pleasing to him; and he set him over his house, and all that he had he gave into the hand of Joseph. \textsuperscript{5} And it came to pass after that he was set over his house, and over all that he had, that the Lord blessed the house of the Egyptian for Joseph's sake; and the blessing of the Lord was on all his possessions in the house, and in his field. \textsuperscript{6} And he committed all that he had into the hands of Joseph; and he knew not of anything that belonged to him, save the bread which he himself ate. And Joseph was handsome in form, and exceedingly beautiful in countenance. \textsuperscript{7} And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph, and said, Lie with me. \textsuperscript{8} But he would not; but said to his master's wife, If because of me my master knows nothing in his house, and has given into my hands all things that belong to him: \textsuperscript{9} and in this house there is nothing above me, nor has anything been kept back from me, but thou, because thou art his wife—how then shall I do this wicked thing, and sin against God? \textsuperscript{10} And when she talked with Joseph day by day, and he hearkened not to her to sleep with her, so as to be with her, \textsuperscript{11} it came to pass on a certain day, that Joseph went into the house to do his business, and there was no one of the household within. \textsuperscript{12} And she caught hold of him by his clothes, and said, Lie with me; and having left his clothes in her hands, he fled, and went forth. \textsuperscript{13} And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his clothes in her hands, and fled, and gone forth, \textsuperscript{14} that she called those that were in the house, and spoke to them, saying, See, he has brought in to us a Hebrew servant to mock us—he came in to me, saying, Lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice. \textsuperscript{15} And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, having left his clothes with me, he fled, and went forth out. \textsuperscript{16} So she leaves the clothes by her, until the master came to his house. \textsuperscript{17} And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, The Hebrew servant, whom thou broughtest in to us, came in to me to mock me, and said to me, I will lie with thee. \textsuperscript{18} And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, having left his clothes with me, he fled and departed forth. \textsuperscript{19} And it came to pass, when his master heard all the words of his wife, that she spoke to him, saying, Thus did thy servant to me, that he was very angry.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 39:1 Brenton note: Gr. chief cook. The same Hebrew word טבח signifies a cook, who was also a butcher; and a guardsman, who was also an executioner.\par

Joseph's beauty is so celebrated in the East, that a handsome man is frequently compared to him; and the Persian poets vie with each other in descriptions of his comeliness.\par

Genesis 39:14 TSK note: he hath The base affection of this woman being disappointed, was changed into rancorous hatred, and she exults in the opportunity of being revenged on Joseph. She begins her accusation in the affected language of offended modesty, rage, and disdain, by charging her husband, whom we may reasonably assume she did not greatly love, with being an accessory to the indignity she pretended to have received: "He hath brought in a Hebrew, " a very abomination to an Egyptian, "to mock us, " insult and treat me in a base, unworthy manner. an Hebrew, ; he came;, ; , ;, ; , loud Heb. great\par
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Genesis 40}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And it came to pass after these things, that the chief cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the chief baker trespassed against their lord the king of Egypt. \textsuperscript{2} And Pharao was wroth with his two eunuchs, with his chief cupbearer, and with his chief baker. \textsuperscript{3} And he put them in ward, into the prison, into the place whereinto Joseph had been led. \textsuperscript{4} And the chief keeper of the prison committed them to Joseph, and he stood by them; and they were some days in the prison. \textsuperscript{5} And they both had a dream in one night; and the vision of the dream of the chief cupbearer and chief baker, who belonged to the king of Egypt, who were in the prison, was this. \textsuperscript{6} Joseph went in to them in the morning, and saw them, and they had been troubled. \textsuperscript{7} And he asked the eunuchs of Pharao who were with him in the prison with his master, saying, Why is it that your countenances are sad to-day? \textsuperscript{8} And they said to him, We have seen a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said to them, Is not the interpretation of them through God? tell them then to me. \textsuperscript{9} And the chief cupbearer related his dream to Joseph, and said, In my dream a vine was before me. \textsuperscript{10} And in the vine were three stems; and it budding shot forth blossoms; the clusters of grapes were ripe. \textsuperscript{11} And the cup of Pharao was in my hand; and I took the bunch of grapes, and squeezed it into the cup, and gave the cup into Pharao's hand. \textsuperscript{12} And Joseph said to him, This is the interpretation of it. The three stems are three days. \textsuperscript{13} Yet three days and Pharao shall remember thy office, and he shall restore thee to thy place of chief cupbearer, and thou shalt give the cup of Pharao into his hand, according to thy former high place, as thou wast wont to be cupbearer. \textsuperscript{14} But remember me of thyself, when it shall be well with thee, and thou shalt deal mercifully with me, and thou shalt make mention of me to Pharao, and thou shalt bring me forth out of this dungeon. \textsuperscript{15} For surely I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here I have done nothing, but they have cast me into this pit. \textsuperscript{16} And the chief baker saw that he interpreted aright; and he said to Joseph, I also saw a dream, and methought I took up on my head three baskets of mealy food. \textsuperscript{17} And in the upper basket there was the work of the baker of every kind which Pharao eats; and the fowls of the air ate them out of the basket that was on my head. \textsuperscript{18} And Joseph answered and said to him, This is the interpretation of it; The three baskets are three days. \textsuperscript{19} Yet three days, and Pharao shall take away thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree, and the birds of the sky shall eat thy flesh from off thee. \textsuperscript{20} And it came to pass on the third day that it was Pharao's birth-day, and he made a banquet for all his servants, and he remembered the office of the cupbearer and the office of the baker in the midst of his servants. \textsuperscript{21} And he restored the chief cupbearer to his office, and he gave the cup into Pharao's hand. \textsuperscript{22} And he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph interpreted to them. \textsuperscript{23} Yet did not the chief cupbearer remember Joseph, but forgot him.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 40:1 TSK note: it came; the butler Mashkeh, from shakah, to give drink, is the same as saky among the Arabians and Persians, and signifies a cup-bearer.\par
Genesis 40:2 TSK note: wroth;, ; the chief of the butlers\par
Genesis 40:3 TSK note: the place, where Joseph was bound Or, "where Joseph was confined, " for he doubtless had his personal liberty. This place, we learn from the preceding chapter ( ), was the king's prison. All the officers in the employment of the ancient kings of Egypt, according to Diodorus Siculus, were taken from the most illustrious families of the priesthood in the country; no slave or common person being ever permitted to serve in the presence of the king. As these persons were of the most noble families, it is natural to expect they would be put, when accused, into the state prison.\par
Genesis 40:4 TSK note: the captain, ; a season Yamim, literally days; how long is uncertain, though the word may signify, as many suppose, a complete year (see note on and see note on ); and as Pharaoh called them to an account on his birthday ( ), Calmet supposes they had offended on the preceding birthday, and thus had been one whole year in prison.\par
Genesis 40:5 Brenton note: Gr. saw.\par
Genesis 40:7 TSK note: Wherefore; look ye so sadly to day Heb. are your faces evil\par
Genesis 40:8 Brenton note: Hebrew background: patar (פָּתַר) = to interpret. Common English renderings: interpret. Especially associated with dream interpretation.\par
Genesis 40:9 Brenton note: Gr. sleep.\par
Genesis 40:10 Brenton note: Greek background: anthos (ἄνθος) = flower; blossom. Common English renderings: flower. A natural image often associated with transience.\par
Genesis 40:11 Brenton note: Greek background: potērion (ποτήριον) = cup. Common English renderings: cup. Literal cup and figurative portion both occur.\par
Genesis 40:11 TSK note: And I took etc. From this we find that wine anciently was the mere expressed juice of the grape, without fermentation. The saky, or cup-bearer, took the bunch, pressed the juice into the cup, and instantly delivered it to his master. pressed; hand\par
Genesis 40:13 TSK note: within shall; lift up thine head or, reckon, *marg. *marg.\par
Genesis 40:14 TSK note: think on me Heb. remember me with thee on me; show\par
Genesis 40:16 TSK note: the chief white baskets or, baskets full of holes\par
Genesis 40:17 TSK note: bakemeats Heb. meat of Pharaoh, the work of a baker, or cook\par
Genesis 40:19 TSK note: within lift up thy head from off thee or, reckon thee and take thy office from thee hang thee, ; , ; and the birds\par
Genesis 40:20 TSK note: third day, birthday; lifted up or, reckoned, *marg.\par
Genesis 40:23 Brenton note: Hebrew background: shakach (שָׁכַח) = to forget. Common English renderings: forget. Used literally and covenantally for neglect or unfaithfulness.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Genesis 41}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And it came to pass after two full years that Pharao had a dream. He thought he stood upon the bank of the river. \textsuperscript{2} And lo, there came up as it were out of the river seven cows, fair in appearance, and choice of flesh, and they fed on the sedge. \textsuperscript{3} And other seven cows came up after these out of the river, ill-favoured and lean-fleshed, and fed by the other cows on the bank of the river. \textsuperscript{4} And the seven ill-favoured and lean cows devoured the seven well-favoured and choice-fleshed cows; and Pharao awoke. \textsuperscript{5} And he dreamed again. And, behold, seven ears came up on one stalk, choice and good. \textsuperscript{6} And, behold, seven ears thin and blasted with the wind, grew up after them. \textsuperscript{7} And the seven thin ears and blasted with the wind devoured the seven choice and full ears; and Pharao awoke, and it was a dream. \textsuperscript{8} And it was morning, and his soul was troubled; and he sent and called all the interpreters of Egypt, and all her wise men; and Pharao related to them his dream, and there was no one to interpret it to Pharao. \textsuperscript{9} And the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharao, saying, I this day remember my fault: \textsuperscript{10} Pharao was angry with his servants, and put us in prison in the house of the captain of the guard, both me and the chief baker. \textsuperscript{11} And we had a dream both in one night, I and he; we saw, each according to his dream. \textsuperscript{12} And there was there with us a young man, a Hebrew servant of the captain of the guard; and we related to him our dreams , and he interpreted them to us. \textsuperscript{13} And it came to pass, as he interpreted them to us, so also it happened, both that I was restored to my office, and that he was hanged. \textsuperscript{14} And Pharao having sent, called Joseph; and they brought him out from the prison, and shaved him, and changed his dress, and he came to Pharao. \textsuperscript{15} And Pharao said to Joseph, I have seen a vision, and there is no one to interpret it; but I have heard say concerning thee that thou didst hear dreams and interpret them. \textsuperscript{16} And Joseph answered Pharao and said, Without God an answer of safety shall not be given to Pharao. \textsuperscript{17} And Pharao spoke to Joseph, saying, In my dream methought I stood by the bank of the river; \textsuperscript{18} and there came up as it were out of the river, seven cows well-favoured and choice-fleshed, and they fed on the sedge. \textsuperscript{19} And behold seven other cows came up after them out of the river, evil and ill-favoured and lean-fleshed, such that I never saw worse in all the land of Egypt. \textsuperscript{20} And the seven ill-favoured and thin cows ate up the seven first good and choice cows. \textsuperscript{21} And they went into their bellies; and it was not perceptible that they had gone into their bellies, and their appearance was ill-favoured, as also at the beginning; and after I awoke I slept, \textsuperscript{22} and saw again in my sleep, and as it were seven ears came up on one stem, full and good. \textsuperscript{23} And other seven ears, thin and blasted with the wind, sprang up close to them. \textsuperscript{24} And the seven thin and blasted ears devoured the seven fine and full ears: so I spoke to the interpreters, and there was no one to explain it to me.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 41:1 Brenton note: Gr. years of days.\par
Genesis 41:1 TSK note: am 2289, bc 1715 two full years Shenathayim yamim, "two years of days, " two complete solar revolutions; as a month of days is a full month. that Pharaoh, ; , 7:1-8:27; the river\par
Genesis 41:2 Brenton note: The Hebrew word which the LXX. have here written in Greek characters without translating it, is rendered in the place A. V. by meadow, in Job 8. 11, the only other passage where it occurs, by flag.\par
Genesis 41:2 TSK note: there came a meadow Or, rather, "on, or among the reeds or sedges; " for so achoo is generally supposed to denote (see note on ); so called, according to Mr. Parkhurst, from its fitness for making ropes, or the like, to connect or join things together, from achah, to join, connect. Thus the Latin juncus, a bulrush, a jungendo, from joining, for the same reason. He supposes it to be that sort of reed growing near the Nile which Hasselquist describes as "having scarce any branches, but numerous leaves, which are narrow, smooth, channelled on the upper surface, and the plant about eleven feet high. The Egyptians make ropes of the leaves."\par
Genesis 41:5 Brenton note: Greek background: stachys (στάχυς) = ear of grain. Common English renderings: ear of grain. An agricultural term for a grain head.\par
Genesis 41:5 TSK note: seven ears A species of wheat, which grows in Egypt, bears, when perfect, seven ears on one stalk, as its natural conformation. It differs from ours in having a solid stem, or at least a stem full of pith, in order to yield sufficient nourishment and support to so great a weight as the ears which it bears. rank Heb. fat\par
Genesis 41:8 Brenton note: Or, tell.\par
Genesis 41:8 TSK note: his spirit;, ; the magicians of Egypt The word here used ( chartummim ) may mean no more than interpreters of abstruse or difficult subjects; especially of dreams and visions, which formed a considerable part of the ancient pagan religion; and the Egyptian priests were the first who professed this art. The word may be of affinity with, or derived from, the Persian chiradmand, wise, learned, judicious, intelligent, from chirad, understanding, judgment, and mand, endowed with. They seem to have been such persons as Josephus calls sacred scribes; or professors of sacred learning., ;, ; , ;, ; the wise men; but there\par
Genesis 41:11 Brenton note: Gr. saw.\par
Genesis 41:14 TSK note: sent;, and they brought him hastily Heb. made him run, ; he shaved\par
Genesis 41:15 Brenton note: Gr. men saying.\par
Genesis 41:15 TSK note: I have heard; , that thou canst understand a dream to interpret it or, when thou hearest a dream, thou canst interpret it\par
Genesis 41:21 Brenton note: Gr. they were.\par
Genesis 41:21 TSK note: eaten them up Heb. come to the inward parts of them, ; still\par
Genesis 41:23 TSK note: withered or, small thin; , blasted All the mischief done to corn or fruit by blasting, smutting, mildew, etc. are attributed to the east wind (see parallel passages). In Egypt it is peculiarly destructive, because it comes through the parched deserts of Arabia, often destroying vast numbers of people. The destructive nature of the Sam, Simoom, Smoom, or Samiel, is mentioned by almost all travellers. When this pestilential wind advances, its approach is indicated by a redness in the air. The principal stream of the blast always moves in a line of about 20 yards in breadth, and 12 feet above the surface of the earth; but its parching influence pervades all places to a considerable distance. The only means of preservation from its noxious influence is to lie flat, with the face upon the ground, till the blast be over. Camels and other animals instinctively perceive its approach, and bury their mouths and nostrils in the ground. It rarely last more than seven or eight minutes, but so poisonous are its effects, that it instantly suffocates those who are unfortunate enough to inhale it.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} And Joseph said to Pharao, The dream of Pharao is one; whatever God does, he has shewn to Pharao. \textsuperscript{26} The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years; the dream of Pharao is one. \textsuperscript{27} And the seven thin kine that came up after them are seven years; and the seven thin and blasted ears are seven years; there shall be seven years of famine. \textsuperscript{28} And as for the word which I have told Pharao, whatsoever God intends to do, he has shewn to Pharao: \textsuperscript{29} behold, for seven years there is coming great plenty in all the land of Egypt. \textsuperscript{30} But there shall come seven years of famine after these, and they shall forget the plenty that shall be in all Egypt, and the famine shall consume the land. \textsuperscript{31} And the plenty shall not be known in the land by reason of the famine that shall be after this, for it shall be very grievous. \textsuperscript{32} And concerning the repetition of the dream to Pharao twice, it is because the saying which is from God shall be true, and God will hasten to accomplish it. \textsuperscript{33} Now then, look out a wise and prudent man, and set him over the land of Egypt. \textsuperscript{34} And let Pharao make and appoint local governors over the land; and let them take up a fifth part of all the produce of the land of Egypt for the seven years of the plenty. \textsuperscript{35} And let them gather all the food of these seven good years that are coming, and let the corn be gathered under the hand of Pharao; let food be kept in the cities. \textsuperscript{36} And the stored food shall be for the land against the seven years of famine, which shall be in the land of Egypt; and the land shall not be utterly destroyed by the famine. \textsuperscript{37} And the word was pleasing in the sight of Pharao, and in the sight of all his servants.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 41:26 TSK note: are or, signify, ; good ears are seven the dream is one\par
Genesis 41:30 TSK note: seven years, ; shall be, ; consume\par
Genesis 41:31 TSK note: the plenty It is well known, that in Egypt there is scarcely any rain, the country depending for its fertility upon the overflowing of the Nile; and that the fertility is in proportion to the duration and quality of the overflow, in order to saturate the land and prepare for the seed. Pliny has given a scale, by which the plenty or dearth may be ascertained; which may be considered as perfectly correct. The ordinary height of the inundations is 16 cubits. When the waters are lower than this standard, they do not overflow the whole ground; when above this standard they are too long in running off. In the first case, the ground is not saturated; by the second, the waters are detained so long on the ground that seed-time is lost. The province marks both. If it rise only 12 cubits, a famine is the consequence; at 13 hunger prevails; 14 produces general rejoicing; 15 perfect security; and 16 all the luxuries of life. grievous Heb. heavy\par
Genesis 41:32 TSK note: doubled, ; it is because;, ; established by or, prepared of\par
Genesis 41:33 Brenton note: Greek background: sophos (σοφός) = wise. Common English renderings: wise. The adjective for wise or skillful.\par
Genesis 41:34 TSK note: officers or, overseers, ; and take\par

\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{38} And Pharao said to all his servants, Shall we find such a man as this, who has the Spirit of God in him? \textsuperscript{39} And Pharao said to Joseph, Since God has shewed thee all these things, there is not a wiser or more prudent man than thou. \textsuperscript{40} Thou shalt be over my house, and all my people shall be obedient to thy word; only in the throne will I excel thee. \textsuperscript{41} And Pharao said to Joseph, Behold, I set thee this day over all the land of Egypt. \textsuperscript{42} And Pharao took his ring off his hand, and put it on the hand of Joseph, and put on him a robe of fine linen, and put a necklace of gold about his neck. \textsuperscript{43} And he mounted him on the second of his chariots, and a herald made proclamation before him; and he set him over all the land of Egypt. \textsuperscript{44} And Pharao said to Joseph, I am Pharao; without thee no one shall lift up his hand on all the land of Egypt. \textsuperscript{45} And Pharao called the name of Joseph, Psonthomphanech; and he gave him Aseneth, the daughter of Petephres, priest of Heliopolis, to wife. \textsuperscript{46} And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharao, king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharao, and went through all the land of Egypt. \textsuperscript{47} And the land produced, in the seven years of plenty, whole handfuls of corn . \textsuperscript{48} And he gathered all the food of the seven years, in which was the plenty in the land of Egypt; and he laid up the food in the cities; the food of the fields of a city round about it he laid up in it. \textsuperscript{49} And Joseph gathered very much corn as the sand of the sea, until it could not be numbered, for there was no number of it .\par

Genesis 41:45 TSK note: Zaphnathpaaneah Which in Coptic signifies a revealer of secrets, or, the man to whom secrets are revealed. Jerome says this name signified in Egyptian, Savatorem mundi, "the Saviour of the world; " and Psotem - phaneh, in Coptic, is certainly "salvation of the world, " from C Ω T, for σωτηρια, salvation, em, the sign of the genitive case, and ΦΕΝΕΗ, world. If this interpretation be correct, Pharaoh must have meant Egypt by the world, or which Joseph might be justly termed the Saviour. We know that the Romans called their empire Universis Orbis-Orbis Terrarum, "all the world:" the Chinese say the same of their empire at the present day, and the phrase is used in the East: Nadir Shah is described on his coins as "Conqueror of the World, " i.e., Persia. See the same phraseology applied to Syria, Palestine, etc.; priest of or, prince, ; *marg., *Heb: On;, Aven\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{3} And the ten brethren of Joseph went down to buy corn out of Egypt. \textsuperscript{4} But Jacob sent not Benjamin, the brother of Joseph, with his brethren; for he said, Lest, haply, disease befal him. \textsuperscript{5} And the sons of Israel came to buy with those that came, for the famine was in the land of Chanaan. \textsuperscript{6} And Joseph was ruler of the land; he sold to all the people of the land. And the brethren of Joseph, having come, did reverence to him, bowing with the face to the ground. \textsuperscript{7} And when Joseph saw his brethren, he knew them, and estranged himself from them, and spoke hard words to them; and said to them, Whence are ye come? And they said, Out of the land of Chanaan, to buy food. \textsuperscript{8} And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him. \textsuperscript{9} And Joseph remembered his dream, which he saw; and he said to them, Ye are spies; to observe the marks of the land are ye come. \textsuperscript{10} But they said, Nay, Sir, we thy servants are come to buy food; \textsuperscript{11} we are all sons of one man; we are peaceable, thy servants are not spies. \textsuperscript{12} And he said to them, Nay, but ye are come to observe the marks of the land. \textsuperscript{13} And they said, We thy servants are twelve brethren, in the land of Chanaan; and, behold, the youngest is with our father to-day, but the other one is not. \textsuperscript{14} And Joseph said to them, This is it that I spoke to you, saying, ye are spies; \textsuperscript{15} herein shall ye be manifested; by the health of Pharao, ye shall not depart hence, unless your younger brother come hither. \textsuperscript{16} Send one of you, and take your brother; and go ye to prison, till your words be clear, whether ye speak the truth or not; but, if not, by the health of Pharao, verily ye are spies. \textsuperscript{17} And he put them in prison three days. \textsuperscript{18} And he said to them on the third day, This do, and ye shall live, for I fear God. \textsuperscript{19} If ye be peaceable, let one of your brethren be detained in prison; but go ye, and carry back the corn ye have purchased. \textsuperscript{20} And bring your younger brother to me, and your words shall be believed; but, if not, ye shall die. And they did so. \textsuperscript{21} And each said to his brother, Yes, indeed, for we are in fault concerning our brother, when we disregarded the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we hearkened not to him; and therefore has this affliction come upon us. \textsuperscript{22} And Ruben answered them, saying, Did I not speak to you, saying, Hurt not the boy, and ye heard me not? and, behold, his blood is required. \textsuperscript{23} But they knew not that Joseph understood them; for there was an interpreter between them. \textsuperscript{24} And Joseph turned away from them, and wept; and again he came to them, and spoke to them; and he took Symeon from them, and bound him before their eyes.\par

Genesis 42:23 TSK note: he spake unto them by an interpreter Heb. an interpreter was between them, The mailitz does not seem to have been an interpreter in our sense of the term; as we have many evidences in this book that the Egyptians, Hebrews, Canaanites, and Syrians, could understand each other in a general way; and it appears from several passages in this very chapter (particularly ), that Joseph and his brethren understood each others' language, as his brethren and Joseph's steward also did (, etc; compare and ). It seems to denote an officer who is called in Abyssinia, according to Mr. Bruce, Kal Hatze, "the voice or word of the king, " who always stands at the side of a lattice window of a balcony, within which the king sits; who is never seen, but who speaks through a hole in the side of it, covered in the inside with a curtain, to this officer, by whom he speaks to the persons present.\par

And their heart was wonder-struck, and they were troubled, saying one to another, What is this that God has done to us? \textsuperscript{29} And they came to their father, Jacob, into the land of Chanaan, and reported to him all that had happened to them, saying, \textsuperscript{30} The man, the lord of the land, spoke harsh words to us, and put us in prison as spies of the land. \textsuperscript{31} And we said to him, We are men of peace, we are not spies. \textsuperscript{32} We are twelve brethren, sons of our father; one is not, and the youngest is with his father to-day in the land of Chanaan. \textsuperscript{33} And the man, the lord of the land, said to us, Herein shall I know that ye are peaceable; leave one brother here with me, and having taken the corn ye have purchased for your family, depart. \textsuperscript{34} And bring to me your younger brother; then I shall know that ye are not spies, but that ye are men of peace: and I will restore you your brother, and ye shall trade in the land. \textsuperscript{35} And it came to pass as they were emptying their sacks, there was each man's bundle of money in his sack; and they and their father saw their bundles of money, and they were afraid. \textsuperscript{36} And their father Jacob said to them, Ye have bereaved me. Joseph is not, Symeon is not, and will ye take Benjamin? all these things have come upon me. \textsuperscript{37} And Ruben spoke to his father, saying, Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to thee; give him into my hand, and I will bring him back to thee. \textsuperscript{38} But he said, My son shall not go down with you, because his brother is dead, and he only has been left; and suppose it shall come to pass that he is afflicted by the way by which ye go, then ye shall bring down my old age with sorrow to Hades.\par

Genesis 42:27 TSK note: the inn, ; , inn Malon, from loon, to stay, abide, lodge, denotes any place to stay and lodge in, particularly a place where travellers usually stop to lodge, which is generally near a well, where they fill their girbehs, or leathern bottles, with fresh water, and having unladen and clogged their camels, asses, etc., permit them to crop any little verdure there may be in the place, keeping watch over them by turns. Our word inn here gives us a false idea, there were no such places of entertainment in the desert which Joseph's brethren had to pass; nor are there any at the present day. The only accommodation such a place affords is either a well, or a khan, or caravanserai, which is generally no more than four bare walls, perfectly exposed, the place being open at the top, and furnishing a wretched lodging, and even these, it is probable, were not in use at this early period.\par

They are more than I can bear.\par

\end{quote}

Devash, honey, is supposed by some not to have been that produced by bees, but a syrup produced from ripe dates. The Jewish doctors observe, that the word in signifies dates; and the Arabians, at this day, call the choicest dates preserved with butter, dabous, and the honey obtained from them, dibs, or dabs . \begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 44:5 Brenton note: Gr. in which.\par
Genesis 44:5 TSK note: divineth or, maketh trial, *marg.; In the East, there is an ancient tradition, that there was a Cup which possessed the strange property of representing in it the whole world, and all the things which were then doing. The cup is called Jami Jemsheed, "the cup of Jemsheed, " a very ancient king of Persia; and they say that it was discovered, filled with the elixir of immortality, when digging to lay the foundations of Persepolis. The Persian poets are full of allusions to this cup, which they style Jem jehan nima, the cup shewing the universe; and to it they ascribe all the prosperity of their ancient monarchs. Many of the Mahometan princes and governors affect still to have information by means of a cup. Now, though it cannot be admitted that Joseph practised divination, yet, according to the superstition of those times, supernatural influence might be attributed to HIS CUP.\par
Genesis 44:10 Brenton note: Hebrew background: zakhah (זָכָה) = to be clean; innocent. Common English renderings: be pure; innocent. Used for acquittal or purity.\par
\end{quote}

Genesis 44:18 TSK note: Oh my Lord "No paraphrase, " says Dr. A. Clarke, "can heighten the effect of Judah's address to Joseph. To add, would be to diminish its excellence; to attempt to explain, would be to obscure its beauties; to clothe the ideas in other language than that of Judah, and his translators in our Bible, would ruin its energy, and destroy its influence. It is perhaps one of the most tender, affecting pieces of natural oratory ever spoken or penned, and we need not wonder to find that, when Joseph heard it, he could not refrain himself, but wept aloud. His soul must have been insensible beyond what is common to human nature, had he not immediately yielded to a speech so delicately tender, and so powerfully impressive." let thy, ; anger; as Pharaoh\par

Indeed the whole speech is exquisitely beautiful, and perhaps the most complete pattern of genuine natural eloquence extant in any language. When we read this generous speech, we forgive Judah all the past, and cannot refuse to say, "Thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise." a child, and his brother, he alone\par

And his brethren could not answer him, for they were troubled. \textsuperscript{4} And Joseph said to his brethren, Draw nigh to me; and they drew nigh; and he said, I am your brother Joseph, whom ye sold into Egypt. \textsuperscript{5} Now then be not grieved, and let it not seem hard to you that ye sold me hither, for God sent me before you for life. \textsuperscript{6} For this second year there is famine on the earth, and there are yet five years remaining, in which there is to be neither ploughing, nor mowing. \textsuperscript{7} For God sent me before you, that there might be left to you a remnant upon the earth, even to nourish a great remnant of you. \textsuperscript{8} Now then ye did not send me hither, but God; and he hath made me as a father of Pharao, and lord of all his house, and ruler of all the land of Egypt. \textsuperscript{9} Hasten, therefore, and go up to my father, and say to him, These things saith thy son Joseph; God has made me lord of all the land of Egypt; come down therefore to me, and tarry not. \textsuperscript{10} And thou shalt dwell in the land of Gesem of Arabia; and thou shalt be near me, thou and thy sons, and thy sons' sons, thy sheep and thine oxen, and whatsoever things are thine. \textsuperscript{11} And I will nourish thee there: for the famine is yet for five years; lest thou be consumed, and thy sons, and all thy possessions. \textsuperscript{12} Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you. \textsuperscript{13} Report, therefore, to my father all my glory in Egypt, and all things that ye have seen, and make haste and bring down my father hither. \textsuperscript{14} And he fell on his brother Benjamin's neck, and wept on him; and Benjamin wept on his neck. \textsuperscript{15} And he kissed all his brethren, and wept on them; and after these things his brethren spoke to him.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 45:2 TSK note: wept aloud Heb. gave forth his voice in weeping, "This, " says Sir J. Chardin, "is exactly the genius of the people of Asia; their sentiments of joy or grief are properly transports, and their transports are ungoverned, excessive, and truly outrageous. When anyone returns from a long journey or dies, his family burst into cries that may be heard twenty doors off; and this is renewed at different times, and continues many days, according to the vigour of the passion. Sometimes they cease all at once, and then begin as suddenly, with a greater shrillness and loudness than one could easily imagine."\par

Clarke thinks it may mean here prepared meat; some made-up dish, delicacies, confectionaries, etc. In Asiatic countries they have several curious methods of preserving flesh by potting, by which it may be kept, for any length of time, sweet and wholesome. Some delicacy, similar to the savoury meat which Isaac loved, may here be intended; sent to Jacob in consideration of his age, and to testify the respect of his son; for of other kinds of meat he could have no need, as he had large flocks and herds, and could kill a lamb, kid, etc. when he pleased.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{13} And there was no corn in all the land, for the famine prevailed greatly; and the land of Egypt, and the land of Chanaan, fainted for the famine. \textsuperscript{14} And Joseph gathered all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and the land of Chanaan, in return for the corn which they bought, and he distributed corn to them; and Joseph brought all the money into the house of Pharao. \textsuperscript{15} And all the money failed out of the land of Egypt, and out of the land of Chanaan; and all the Egyptians came to Joseph, saying, Give us bread, and why do we die in thy presence? for our money is spent. \textsuperscript{16} And Joseph said to them, Bring your cattle, and I will give you bread for your cattle, if your money is spent. \textsuperscript{17} And they brought their cattle to Joseph; and Joseph gave them bread in return for their horses, and for their sheep, and for their oxen, and for their asses; and Joseph maintained them with bread for all their cattle in that year. \textsuperscript{18} And that year passed, and they came to him in the second year, and said to him, Must we then be consumed from before our lord? for if our money has failed, and our possessions, and our cattle, brought to thee our lord, and there has not been left to us before our lord more than our own bodies and our land, we are indeed destitute . \textsuperscript{19} In order, then, that we die not before thee, and the land be made desolate, buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharao: give seed that we may sow, and live and not die, so our land shall not be made desolate. \textsuperscript{20} And Joseph bought all the land of the Egyptians, for Pharao; for the Egyptians sold their land to Pharao; for the famine prevailed against them, and the land became Pharao's. \textsuperscript{21} And he brought the people into bondage to him, for servants, from one extremity of Egypt to the other, \textsuperscript{22} except only the land of the priests; Joseph bought not this, for Pharao gave a portion in the way of gift to the priests; and they ate their portion which Pharao gave them; therefore they sold not their land. \textsuperscript{23} And Joseph said to all the Egyptians, Behold, I have bought you and your land this day for Pharao; take seed for you, and sow the land. \textsuperscript{24} And there shall be the fruits of it; and ye shall give the fifth part to Pharao, and the four remaining parts shall be for yourselves, for seed for the earth, and for food for you, and all that are in your houses. \textsuperscript{25} And they said, Thou hast saved us; we have found favour before our lord, and we will be servants to Pharao. \textsuperscript{26} And Joseph appointed it to them for an ordinance until this day; to reserve a fifth part for Pharao, on the land of Egypt, except only the land of the priests, that was not Pharao's.\par

As the people had not grain for their own sustenance, consequently they could have none for their cattle. \subsection*{Genesis 50}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Joseph fell upon his father's face, and wept on him, and kissed him. \textsuperscript{2} And Joseph commanded his servants the embalmers to embalm his father; and the embalmers embalmed Israel. \textsuperscript{3} And they fulfilled forty days for him, for so are the days of embalming numbered; and Egypt mourned for him seventy days. \textsuperscript{4} And when the days of mourning were past, Joseph spoke to the princes of Pharao, saying, If I have found favour in your sight, speak concerning me in the ears of Pharao, saying, \textsuperscript{5} My father adjured me, saying, In the sepulchre which I dug for myself in the land of Chanaan, there thou shalt bury me; now then I will go up and bury my father, and return again. \textsuperscript{6} And Pharao said to Joseph, Go up, bury thy father, as he constrained thee to swear. \textsuperscript{7} So Joseph went up to bury his father; and all the servants of Pharao went up with him, and the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt. \textsuperscript{8} And all the household of Joseph, and his brethren, and all the house of his father, and his kindred; and they left behind the sheep and the oxen in the land of Gesem. \textsuperscript{9} And there went up with him also chariots and horsemen; and there was a very great company. \textsuperscript{10} And they came to the threshing-floor of Atad, which is beyond Jordan; and they bewailed him with a great and very sore lamentation; and he made a mourning for his father seven days. \textsuperscript{11} And the inhabitants of the land of Chanaan saw the mourning at the floor of Atad, and said, This is a great mourning to the Egyptians; therefore he called its name, The mourning of Egypt, which is beyond Jordan. \textsuperscript{12} And thus his sons did to him. \textsuperscript{13} So his sons carried him up into the land of Chanaan, and buried him in the double cave, which cave Abraam bought for possession of a burying place, of Ephrom the Chettite, before Mambre. \textsuperscript{14} And Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brethren, and those that had gone up with him to bury his father.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Genesis 50:2 TSK note: the physicians The Hebrew ropheim, from rapha, to heal, is literally the healers, those whose business it was to heal, or restore the body from sickness, by administering proper medicines; and when death took place, to heal or preserve it from decomposition by embalming. The word chanat, to embalm, is also used in Arabic to express the reddening of leather; somewhat analogous to our tanning; which is probably the grand principal in embalming. embalmed\par
Genesis 50:3 TSK note: forty days We learn from the Greek historians, that the time of mourning was while the body remained with the embalmers, which Herodotus says was seventy days. During this time the body lay in nitre, the use of which was to dry up all its superfluous and noxious moisture, and when, in the space of 30 days, this was sufficiently effected, the remaining forty, the time mentioned by Diodorus, were employed in anointing it with gums and spices to preserve it, which was properly the embalming. This sufficiently explains the phraseology of the text. mourned Heb. wept threescore\par
Genesis 50:4 TSK note: the days Joseph found grace\par
Genesis 50:5 TSK note: made me I die, ; I have; bury me; , let me go\par
Genesis 50:10 TSK note: the threshingfloor This place was situated, according to Jerome, between the Jordan and the city of Jericho, two miles from the former, and three from the latter, where Bethagla was afterwards built. Procopius of Gaza states the same. As aataad signifies thorns, the place might have been remarkable for their production; though all the versions except the Arabic consider it as a proper name. As Moses wrote or revised his history on the east side of Jordan, the term beyond Jordan, in his five books, means westward of Jordan; but in other parts of Scripture it generally means eastward. beyond; seven days\par
Genesis 50:11 TSK note: the Canaanites, Abelmizraim i.e. The mourning of the Egyptians, beyond Jordan\par
\end{quote}

\section*{Exodus}
\subsection*{Exodus 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} These are the names of the sons of Israel that came into Egypt together with Jacob their father; they came in each with their whole family. \textsuperscript{2} Ruben, Simeon, Levi, Judas, \textsuperscript{3} Issachar, Zabulon, Benjamin, \textsuperscript{4} Dan and Nephthalim, Gad and Aser. \textsuperscript{5} But Joseph was in Egypt. And all the souls born of Jacob were seventy-five. \textsuperscript{6} And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation. \textsuperscript{7} And the children of Israel increased and multiplied, and became numerous and grew exceedingly strong, and the land multiplied them. \textsuperscript{8} And there arose up another king over Egypt, who knew not Joseph. \textsuperscript{9} And he said to his nation, Behold, the race of the children of Israel is a great multitude, and is stronger than we: \textsuperscript{10} come then, let us deal craftily with them, lest at any time they be increased, and whensoever war shall happen to us, these also shall be added to our enemies, and having prevailed against us in war, they will depart out of the land. \textsuperscript{11} And he set over them task-masters, who should afflict them in their works; and they built strong cities for Pharao, both Pitho, and Ramesses, and On, which is Heliopolis. \textsuperscript{12} But as they humbled them, by so much they multiplied, and grew exceedingly strong; and the Egyptians greatly abhorred the children of Israel. \textsuperscript{13} And the Egyptians tyrannised over the children of Israel by force. \textsuperscript{14} And they embittered their life by hard labours, in the clay and in brick-making, and all the works in the plains, according to all the works, wherein they caused them to serve with violence.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Exodus 1:5 TSK note: loins Heb. thigh, ; *marg. seventy\par
Exodus 1:8 Brenton note: Hebrew background: chadash (חָדָשׁ) = new. Common English renderings: new. Important for covenant renewal and future hope.\par
Exodus 1:8 TSK note: a new king Probably Rameses Miamum, or his son Amenophis, who succeeded him about this period; and by his not knowing Joseph is meant his not acknowledging his obligation to him.\par
Exodus 1:10 Brenton note: Hebrew background: milchamah (מִלְחָמָה) = war; battle. Common English renderings: war; battle. Used for human war and the LORD’s warfare.\par
Exodus 1:12 TSK note: But the more etc. Heb. and as they afflicted them, so they multiplied, etc.; grieved\par
Exodus 1:14 TSK note: their lives, ; , ; , in mortar, ; was with rigour\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} And the king of the Egyptians spoke to the midwives of the Hebrews; the name of the one was, Sepphora; and the name of the second, Phua. \textsuperscript{16} And he said, When ye do the office of midwives to the Hebrew women, and they are about to be delivered, if it be a male, kill it; but if a female, save it. \textsuperscript{17} But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt appointed them; and they saved the male children alive. \textsuperscript{18} And the king of Egypt called the midwives, and said to them, Why is it that ye have done this thing, and saved the male children alive? \textsuperscript{19} And the midwives said to Pharao, The Hebrew women are not as the women of Egypt, for they are delivered before the midwives go in to them. So they bore children. \textsuperscript{20} And God did well to the midwives, and the people multiplied, and grew very strong. \textsuperscript{21} And as the midwives feared God, they established for themselves families. \textsuperscript{22} And Pharao charged all his people, saying, Whatever male child shall be born to the Hebrews, cast into the river; and every female, save it alive.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Exodus 1:16 TSK note: and see them Or, rather, "and ye see them by the stone-troughs; " for so ovnayim, from aven, a stone, seems to signify (compare ), in which they washed the new-born infants. See this subject fully illustrated in Fragments to Calmet, Nos. 312, 313. then ye shall\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Exodus 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And there was a certain man of the tribe of Levi, who took to wife one of the daughters of Levi. \textsuperscript{2} And she conceived, and bore a male child; and having seen that he was fair, they hid him three months. \textsuperscript{3} And when they could no longer hide him, his mother took for him an ark, and besmeared it with bitumen, and cast the child into it, and put it in the ooze by the river. \textsuperscript{4} And his sister was watching from a distance, to learn what would happen to him.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Exodus 2:1 TSK note: am 2432, bc 1572 of the house\par
Exodus 2:3 Brenton note: i. e. a peculiar kind, more resembling vegetable pitch.\par
Exodus 2:3 TSK note: could not;, ; an ark bulrushes Gome, is the papyrus, so famous in all antiquity. It grows on the banks of the Nile, and in marshy grounds; the stalk rises to the height of six or seven cubits above the water, is triangular, and terminates in a crown of small filaments, resembling hair. This reed was of the greatest use to the Egyptians; the pith serving them for food, and the woody part to build vessels with; which vessels frequently appear on various monuments of Egyptian antiquity. That boats were made of this reed is also attested by Pliny and others. with slime\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} And the daughter of Pharao came down to the river to bathe; and her maids walked by the river's side, and having seen the ark in the ooze, she sent her maid, and took it up. \textsuperscript{6} And having opened it, she sees the babe weeping in the ark: and the daughter of Pharao had compassion on it, and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children. \textsuperscript{7} And his sister said to the daughter of Pharao, Wilt thou that I call to thee a nurse of the Hebrews, and shall she suckle the child for thee? \textsuperscript{8} And the daughter of Pharao said, Go: and the young woman went, and called the mother of the child. \textsuperscript{9} And the daughter of Pharao said to her, Take care of this child, and suckle it for me, and I will give thee the wages; and the woman took the child, and suckled it. \textsuperscript{10} And when the boy was grown, she brought him to the daughter of Pharao, and he became her son; and she called his name, Moses, saying, I took him out of the water.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Exodus 2:5 TSK note: daughter herself As the word herself is not in the original, Dr. A. Clarke is of opinion that it was for the purpose of washing, not her person, but her clothes, that Pharaoh's daughter came to the river; which was an employment not beneath even king's daughters in those primitive times. when she\par
Exodus 2:6 Brenton note: Greek background: brephos (βρέφος) = infant; babe. Common English renderings: babe; infant. Used for very young children and infants.\par
Exodus 2:10 Brenton note: Name meaning: Moses (Mosheh) — Drawn out Drawn out of the Nile; drew Israel out of Egypt.\par
Exodus 2:10 TSK note: and he; Moses Drawn out Because\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} And it came to pass in that length of time, that Moses having grown, went out to his brethren the sons of Israel: and having noticed their distress, he sees an Egyptian smiting a certain Hebrew of his brethren the children of Israel. \textsuperscript{12} And having looked round this way and that way, he sees no one; and he smote the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand. \textsuperscript{13} And having gone out the second day he sees two Hebrew men fighting; and he says to the injurer, Wherefore smitest thou thy neighbour? \textsuperscript{14} And he said, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us? wilt thou slay me as thou yesterday slewest the Egyptian? Then Moses was alarmed, and said, If it be thus, this matter has become known. \textsuperscript{15} And Pharao heard this matter, and sought to slay Moses; and Moses departed from the presence of Pharao, and dwelt in the land of Madiam; and having come into the land of Madiam, he sat on the well. \textsuperscript{16} And the priest of Madiam had seven daughters, feeding the flock of their father Jothor; and they came and drew water until they filled their pitchers, to water the flock of their father Jothor. \textsuperscript{17} And the shepherds came, and were driving them away; and Moses rose up and rescued them, and drew water for them, and watered their sheep. \textsuperscript{18} And they came to Raguel their father; and he said to them, Why have ye come so quickly to-day? \textsuperscript{19} And they said, An Egyptian delivered us from the shepherds, and drew water for us and watered our sheep. \textsuperscript{20} And he said to his daughters, And where is he? and why have ye left the man? call him therefore, that he may eat bread. \textsuperscript{21} And Moses was established with the man, and he gave Sepphora his daughter to Moses to wife. \textsuperscript{22} And the woman conceived and bore a son, and Moses called his name Gersam, saying, I am a sojourner in a strange land. \textsuperscript{23} And in those days after a length of time, the king of Egypt died; and the children of Israel groaned because of their tasks, and cried, and their cry because of their tasks went up to God. \textsuperscript{24} And God heard their groanings, and God remembered his covenant made with Abraam and Isaac and Jacob. \textsuperscript{25} And God looked upon the children of Israel, and was made known to them.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Exodus 2:12 TSK note: he looked slew If the Egyptian killed the Hebrew, Moses only acted agreeably to the divine law ( ) in thus slaying the Egyptian; nor did he violate the law of Egypt; for, according to Diodorus Siculus (1. 1. § 17), "he who saw a man killed, or violently assaulted on the highway, and did not rescue him, if he could, was punished with death." Moses, therefore, in this transaction, acted as a brave and good man; especially as at this time there was little probability of obtaining justice on an Egyptian murderer.\par
Exodus 2:13 Brenton note: Hebrew background: rasha (רָשָׁע) = wicked; guilty. Common English renderings: wicked; ungodly. Describes moral guilt and opposition to righteousness.\par
Exodus 2:14 TSK note: Who, ;, ; , ;, a prince Heb. a man a prince Moses\par
Exodus 2:16 TSK note: the priest or, prince, ;, *marg. they came\par
Exodus 2:22 TSK note: Gershom i.e. a stranger here, for he said\par
Exodus 2:23 Brenton note: Hebrew background: za’aq (זָעַק) = to cry out. Common English renderings: cry. Near-synonym of צעק in distress contexts.\par
Exodus 2:23 TSK note: am cir, 2504, bc cir, 1500 in process; the king; sighed; cry\par
Exodus 2:25 TSK note: looked; God For elohim, God, Houbigant reads aleyhem, unto them; which is countenanced by the LXX, Vulgate, Chaldee, Coptic, and Arabic, and appears to have been the original reading. had respect Heb. knew\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Exodus 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Moses was feeding the flock of Jothor his father-in-law, the priest of Madiam; and he brought the sheep nigh to the wilderness, and came to the mount of Choreb. \textsuperscript{2} And an angel of the Lord appeared to him in flaming fire out of the bush, and he sees that the bush burns with fire,—but the bush was not consumed. \textsuperscript{3} And Moses said, I will go near and see this great sight, why the bush is not consumed. \textsuperscript{4} And when the Lord saw that he drew nigh to see, the Lord called him out of the bush, saying, Moses, Moses; and he said, What is it? \textsuperscript{5} And he said, Draw not nigh hither: loose thy sandals from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground. \textsuperscript{6} And he said, I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraam, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob; and Moses turned away his face, for he was afraid to gaze at God. \textsuperscript{7} And the Lord said to Moses, I have surely seen the affliction of my people that is in Egypt, and I have heard their cry caused by their task-masters; for I know their affliction. \textsuperscript{8} And I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them out of that land, and to bring them into a good and wide land, into a land flowing with milk and honey, into the place of the Chananites, and the Chettites, and Amorites, and Pherezites, and Gergesites, and Evites, and Jebusites. \textsuperscript{9} And now, behold, the cry of the children of Israel is come to me, and I have seen the affliction with which the Egyptians afflict them. \textsuperscript{10} And now come, I will send thee to Pharao king of Egypt, and thou shalt bring out my people the children of Israel from the land of Egypt.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Exodus 3:1 TSK note: am 2513, bc 1491 kept;, ; his father, ; the mountain, ; Horeb\par
Exodus 3:2 Brenton note: Gr. fire of flame.\par
Exodus 3:5 Brenton note: Hebrew background: qodesh (קֹדֶשׁ) = holiness; holy thing; sanctuary. Common English renderings: holiness; holy place; sanctuary. Related noun denoting holiness or holy sphere.\par
Exodus 3:5 Brenton note: Hebrew background: qadosh (קָדוֹשׁ) = holy; set apart. Common English renderings: holy. The core Hebrew holiness term for what is set apart to God.\par
Exodus 3:5 Brenton note: Greek background: hagios (ἅγιος) = holy. Common English renderings: holy; saint. A major holiness term for what is set apart to God.\par
Exodus 3:6 Brenton note: Name of God: Elohe Yaakov (אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב) — God of Jacob Common English renderings: God of Jacob. A key covenant formula tying God’s present action to His promises to the fathers.\par
Exodus 3:6 TSK note: I am, ;, ; , ; , thy father Though the word avicha, "thy father, " is here used in the singular, yet St. Stephen, quoting this passage ( ), uses the plural, ο Θεος των πατρων σου, "the God of thy fathers; " and that this is the meaning, the following words prove. This reading is confirmed by the Samaritan and Coptic. hid\par
Exodus 3:7 TSK note: I have, ; , ; by reason I know\par
Exodus 3:8 TSK note: I am, ;, ; , deliver, ;, unto a good, ;, ;, ;, ;, ; , ; Canaanites\par
Exodus 3:9 Brenton note: Hebrew background: lachats (לָחַץ) = to oppress; press. Common English renderings: oppress. Pressure imagery behind oppression language.\par
Exodus 3:9 TSK note: the cry, and I have\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} And Moses said to God, Who am I, that I should go to Pharao king of Egypt, and that I should bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt? \textsuperscript{12} And God spoke to Moses, saying, I will be with thee, and this shall be the sign to thee that I shall send thee forth,—when thou bringest out my people out of Egypt, then ye shall serve God in this mountain. \textsuperscript{13} And Moses said to God, Behold, I shall go forth to the children of Israel, and shall say to them, The God of our fathers has sent me to you; and they will ask me, What is his name? What shall I say to them? \textsuperscript{14} And God spoke to Moses, saying, I am THE BEING; and he said, Thus shall ye say to the children of Israel, THE BEING has sent me to you. \textsuperscript{15} And God said again to Moses, Thus shalt thou say to the sons of Israel, The Lord God of our fathers, the God of Abraam, and God of Isaac, and God of Jacob, has sent me to you: this is my name for ever, and my memorial to generations of generations. \textsuperscript{16} Go then and gather the elders of the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them, The Lord God of our fathers has appeared to me, the God of Abraam, and God of Isaac, and God of Jacob, saying, I have surely looked upon you, and upon all the things which have happened to you in Egypt. \textsuperscript{17} And he said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of the Egyptians to the land of the Chananites and the Chettites, and Amorites and Pherezites, and Gergesites, and Evites, and Jebusites, to a land flowing with milk and honey. \textsuperscript{18} And they shall hearken to thy voice, and thou and the elders of Israel shall go in to Pharao king of Egypt, and thou shalt say to him, The God of the Hebrews has called us; we will go then a journey of three days into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to our God. \textsuperscript{19} But I know that Pharao king of Egypt will not let you go, save with a mighty hand; \textsuperscript{20} and I will stretch out my hand, and smite the Egyptians with all my wonders, which I shall work among them, and after that he will send you forth. \textsuperscript{21} And I will give this people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, and whenever ye shall escape, ye shall not depart empty. \textsuperscript{22} But every woman shall ask of her neighbour and fellow lodger, articles of gold and silver, and apparel; and ye shall put them upon your sons and upon your daughters,—and spoil ye the Egyptians.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Exodus 3:12 TSK note: Certainly, ;, ; , ; token; , ; , ye shall Exod. 19:1-40:38; Lev. 1:1-27:34; Num. 1:1-10:36\par
Exodus 3:14 Brenton note: Name of God: Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh (אֶהְיֶה אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה) — I AM THAT I AM; I WILL BE WHAT I WILL BE Common English renderings: I AM THAT I AM. God’s self-revelation to Moses from the burning bush, emphasizing His self-existence and faithfulness.\par
Exodus 3:15 TSK note: The Lord, ; , ; this is my name for ever The name here referred to is that which immediately precedes, ιδεδ, Yehowah, which we translate "Lord", the name by which God had been known from the creation of the world ( ), and by which he is known to the present day. ιδεδ, Yehowah, from δεδ, hawah, to be, subsist, signifies "He who is", or "subsists", i.e., eminently and in a manner superior to all other beings; and is essentially the same with ΰδιδ, eheyeh, "I AM", in the preceding verse., ;, my memorial\par
Exodus 3:17 TSK note: I will bring, ;, unto the land\par
Exodus 3:18 TSK note: and they, ; and thou The Lord, met, ;, ;, ; three days', that we may\par
Exodus 3:19 TSK note: will not, no, not by a mighty hand or, but by a strong hand, 7:1-14:31\par
Exodus 3:20 TSK note: Acts 7:1-13:42 stretch, ; smite, ;, ; , ; after that\par
Exodus 3:22 TSK note: But, ; borrow Or, rather ask or demand, as the word ωΡΰμ properly signifies; and is so rendered by the LXX, Vulgate, and Geneva and Barker's Bible. The other ancient versions are the same as the Hebrew. spoil; the Egyptians or, Egypt\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Exodus 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Moses answered and said, If they believe me not, and do not hearken to my voice (for they will say, God has not appeared to thee), what shall I say to them? \textsuperscript{2} And the Lord said to him, What is this thing that is in thine hand? and he said, A rod. \textsuperscript{3} And he said, Cast it on the ground: and he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent, and Moses fled from it. \textsuperscript{4} And the Lord said to Moses, Stretch forth thine hand, and take hold of its tail: so he stretched forth his hand and took hold of the tail, \textsuperscript{5} and it became a rod in his hand,—that they may believe thee, that the God of thy fathers has appeared to thee, the God of Abraam, and God of Isaac, and God of Jacob. \textsuperscript{6} And the Lord said again to him, Put thine hand into thy bosom; and he put his hand into his bosom, and brought his hand out of his bosom, and his hand became as snow. \textsuperscript{7} And he said again, Put thy hand into thy bosom; and he put his hand into his bosom, and brought his hand out of his bosom, and it was again restored to the complexion of his other flesh. \textsuperscript{8} And if they will not believe thee, nor hearken to the voice of the first sign, they will believe thee because of the voice of the second sign. \textsuperscript{9} And it shall come to pass if they will not believe thee for these two signs, and will not hearken to thy voice, that thou shalt take of the water of the river and pour it upon the dry land, and the water which thou shalt take from the river shall be blood upon the dry land. \textsuperscript{10} And Moses said to the Lord, I pray, Lord, I have not been sufficient in former times, neither from the time that thou hast begun to speak to thy servant: I am weak in speech, and slow-tongued. \textsuperscript{11} And the Lord said to Moses, Who has given a mouth to man, and who has made the very hard of hearing, and the deaf, the seeing and the blind? have not I, God? \textsuperscript{12} And now go and I will open thy mouth, and will instruct thee in what thou shalt say. \textsuperscript{13} And Moses said, I pray thee, Lord, appoint another able person whom thou shalt send. \textsuperscript{14} And the Lord was greatly angered against Moses, and said, Lo! is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he will surely speak to thee; and, behold, he will come forth to meet thee, and beholding thee he will rejoice within himself. \textsuperscript{15} And thou shalt speak to him; and thou shalt put my words into his mouth, and I will open thy mouth and his mouth, and I will instruct you in what ye shall do. \textsuperscript{16} And he shall speak for thee to the people, and he shall be thy mouth, and thou shalt be for him in things pertaining to God. \textsuperscript{17} And this rod that was turned into a serpent thou shalt take in thine hand, wherewith thou shalt work miracles.\par

Exodus 4:10 TSK note: eloquent Heb. a man of words, ; , heretofore Heb. since yesterday, nor since the third day, slow of speech\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{18} And Moses went and returned to Jothor his father-in-law, and says, I will go and return to my brethren in Egypt, and will see if they are yet living. And Jothor said to Moses, Go in health. And in those days after some time, the king of Egypt died. \textsuperscript{19} And the Lord said to Moses in Madiam, Go, depart into Egypt, for all that sought thy life are dead. \textsuperscript{20} And Moses took his wife and his children, and mounted them on the beasts, and returned to Egypt; and Moses took the rod which he had from God in his hand. \textsuperscript{21} And the Lord said to Moses, When thou goest and returnest to Egypt, see—all the miracles I have charged thee with, thou shalt work before Pharao: and I will harden his heart, and he shall certainly not send away the people. \textsuperscript{22} And thou shalt say to Pharao, These things saith the Lord, Israel is my first-born. \textsuperscript{23} And I said to thee, Send away my people, that they may serve me: now if thou wilt not send them away, see, I will slay thy first-born son. \textsuperscript{24} And it came to pass that the angel of the Lord met him by the way in the inn, and sought to slay him. \textsuperscript{25} And Sepphora having taken a stone cut off the foreskin of her son, and fell at his feet and said, The blood of the circumcision of my son is staunched: \textsuperscript{26} and he departed from him, because she said, The blood of the circumcision of my son is staunched. \textsuperscript{27} And the Lord said to Aaron, Go into the wilderness to meet Moses; and he went and met him in the mount of God, and they kissed each other. \textsuperscript{28} And Moses reported to Aaron all the words of the Lord, which he sent, and all the things which he charged him. \textsuperscript{29} And Moses and Aaron went and gathered the elders of the children of Israel. \textsuperscript{30} And Aaron spoke all these words, which God spoke to Moses, and wrought the miracles before the people. \textsuperscript{31} And the people believed and rejoiced, because God visited the children of Israel, and because he saw their affliction: and the people bowed and worshipped.\par

Jether, Let me go and see; Go in peace; In the LXX and Coptic, the following addition is made to this verse: Μετα δε τας ημερας τας πολλας εκεινας ετελευτησεν ο βασιλευς Αιγυπτου, "After these many days, the king of Egypt died." This was probably an ancient side-note, which crept into the text, as it appeared to throw light on the next verse.\par
Exodus 4:19 TSK note: Midian A country in Arabia Petrea, on the eastern coast of the Red Sea, near Mount Sinai. This place is still called by the Arabs the Land of Midian, or of Jethro. Abulfeda, speaking of Midian, says, "Madyan is a city, in ruins, on the shore of the Red Sea, on the opposite side to Tabuc, from which it is distant about six days' journey. At Midian may be seen the famous well at which Moses watered the flocks of Shoaib (Jethro). This city was the capital of the tribe of Midian in the days of the Israelites." for all\par

Exodus 4:24 TSK note: the inn; The account in this and the two following verses, although rather obscure, seems to imply, that on their way to the land of Egypt, an angel appeared to Moses, and sought to kill his son, on account of his father's non-observance of the Lord's positive command to Abraham, that every man child of the Jewish nation, or born in his house in servitude, should be circumcised on the eighth day; and the Zipporah, at the command of Moses, immediately fulfilled the injunction, and thus averted the wrath of God, denounced against the disobedient: "The uncircumcised man child, whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people." the Lord; sought\par
Exodus 4:25 TSK note: a sharp stone or, knife, cast it Heb. made it touch. a bloody\par

\end{quote}
\subsection*{Exodus 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And after this went in Moses and Aaron to Pharao, and they said to him, These things says the Lord God of Israel, Send my people away, that they may keep a feast to me in the wilderness. \textsuperscript{2} And Pharao said, Who is he that I should hearken to his voice, so that I should send away the children of Israel? I do not know the Lord, and I will not let Israel go. \textsuperscript{3} And they say to him, The God of the Hebrews has called us to him: we will go therefore a three days' journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the Lord our God, lest at any time death or slaughter happen to us. \textsuperscript{4} And the king of Egypt said to them, Why do ye, Moses and Aaron, turn the people from their works? depart each of you to your works. \textsuperscript{5} And Pharao said, Behold now, the people is very numerous; let us not then give them rest from their work. \textsuperscript{6} And Pharao gave orders to the task-masters of the people and the accountants, saying, \textsuperscript{7} Ye shall no longer give straw to the people for brick-making as yesterday and the third day; but let them go themselves, and collect straw for themselves. \textsuperscript{8} And thou shalt impose on them daily the rate of brick-making which they perform: thou shalt not abate anything, for they are idle; therefore have they cried, saying, Let us arise and do sacrifice to our God. \textsuperscript{9} Let the works of these men be made grievous, and let them care for these things, and not care for vain words.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Exodus 5:2 Brenton note: Gr. do not let, etc.\par
Exodus 5:2 TSK note: Who; , ; , I know not; neither\par
Exodus 5:4 TSK note: wherefore; , let Taphreeoo, from pard, to loose, disengage; and which we render let, from the Anglo-Saxon lettan, to hinder. Ye hinder the people from their work: "Get you unto your burdens." "Let religion alone and mind your work." The language not only of tyranny, but of thoughtless irreligion. burdens\par
Exodus 5:6 TSK note: taskmasters Nogesim, literally, exactors, oppressors. These taskmasters were Egyptians ( ), but the officers were Hebrews. ., ; officers Shoterim, from the Arabic saytara, to overlook, superintend, seems to denote, as musaytar in Arabic also does, overseers, superintendents. They may have been somewhat like the chiefs of trades, who are found in every city in the East; where every trade has a head, who is entrusted with authority over them, and is in some measure answerable for them to Government. Compare .\par
Exodus 5:7 TSK note: straw The straw was mixed with clay, in order to make the bricks. This is expressly affirmed by Philo (vit. Mos.) who was himself a native of Alexandria, in Egypt. He says, describing the oppression of the Israelites, that some were obliged to work in clay, and others to gather straw for the formation of bricks, πλινθου γαρ αχυρα δεσμος, because straw is the binding of the brick. Philo's account is confirmed by Dr. Shaw, who says that "some of the Egyptian pyramids are made of brick, the composition whereof is only a mixture of clay, mud, and straw, slightly blended and kneaded together, and afterwards baked in the sun. The straw, which keeps the bricks together, and still preserves its original colour, seems to be a proof that these bricks were never burnt or made in kilns." The same materials are now used for building in Egypt. Mr. Baumgarten says, "The houses are for the most part of bricks that are only hardened by the heat of the sun, and mixed with straw to make them firm."\par
Exodus 5:8 TSK note: tale Tale denotes number, from the Anglo-Saxon taellan, to number, count, etc. ye shall lay\par
Exodus 5:9 Brenton note: Hebrew background: sheqer (שֶׁקֶר) = falsehood; lie. Common English renderings: lie; falsehood. Moral and legal term for deception.\par
Exodus 5:9 TSK note: Let there more work be laid upon the men Heb. Let the work be heavy upon the men vain words\par
\end{quote}
