\noindent \textsuperscript{27} And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites in their places, to bring them to Jerusalem, to keep a feast of dedication and gladness with thanksgiving, and they sounded cymbals with songs, and had psalteries and harps. \textsuperscript{28} And the sons of the singers were assembled both from the neighbourhood round about to Jerusalem, and from the villages, \textsuperscript{29} and from the country: for the singers built themselves villages by Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{30} And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people, and the porters, and the wall.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{31} And they brought up the princes of Juda on the wall, and they appointed two great companies for thanksgiving, and they passed on the right hand on the wall of the dung-gate. \textsuperscript{32} And after them went Osaia, and half the princes of Juda, \textsuperscript{33} and Azarias, and Esdras, and Mesollam, \textsuperscript{34} and Juda, and Benjamin, and Samaias and Jeremia. \textsuperscript{35} And some of the sons of the priests with trumpets, Zacharias son of Jonathan, son of Samaias, son of Matthania, son of Michaia, son of Zacchur, son of Asaph: \textsuperscript{36} and his brethren, Samaia, and Oziel, Gelol, Jama, Aia, Nathanael, and Juda, Anani, to praise with the hymns of David the man of God; \textsuperscript{37} and Esdras the scribe was before them, at the gate, to praise before them, and they went up by the steps of the city of David, in the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, even to the water-gate \textsuperscript{39} of Ephraim, and to the fish-gate, and by the tower of Anameel, and as far as the sheep-gate. \textsuperscript{42} And the singers were heard, and were numbered. \textsuperscript{43} And in that day they offered great sacrifices, and rejoiced; for God had made them very joyful: and their wives and their children rejoiced: and the joy in Jerusalem was heard from afar off.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{44} And in that day they appointed men over the treasuries, for the treasures, the first-fruits, and the tithes, and for the chiefs of the cities who were assembled among them, to furnish portions for the priests and Levites: for there was joy in Juda over the priests and over the Levites that waited. \textsuperscript{45} And they kept the charges of their God, and the charges of the purification, and ordered the singers and the porters, according to the commandments of David and his son Solomon. \textsuperscript{46} For in the days of David Asaph was originally first of the singers, and they sang hymns and praise to God. \textsuperscript{47} And all Israel in the days of Zorobabel, and in the days of Neemias, gave the portions of the singers and the porters, a daily rate: and consecrated them to the Levites: and the Levites consecrated them to the sons of Aaron.\par
\subsection*{Ezra and Nehemiah 23}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} In that day they read in the book of Moses in the ears of the people; and it was found written in it, that the Ammonites and Moabites should not enter into the congregation of God for ever; \textsuperscript{2} because they met not the children of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them: but our God turned the curse into a blessing. \textsuperscript{3} And it came to pass, when they heard the law, that they were separated, even every alien in Israel.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} And before this time Eliasib the priest dwelt in the treasury of the house of our God, connected with Tobias; \textsuperscript{5} and he made himself a great treasury, and there they were formerly in the habit of bestowing the offerings, and the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithe of the corn, and the wine, and the oil, the ordered portion of the Levites, and singers, and porters; and the first-fruits of the priests. \textsuperscript{6} But in all this time I was not in Jerusalem; for in the thirty-second year of Arthasastha king of Babylon I came to the king, and after a certain time I made my request of the king; \textsuperscript{7} and I came to Jerusalem, and I understood the mischief which Eliasib had done in the case of Tobias, in making for him a treasury in the court of the house of God.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} And it appeared very evil to me: so I cast forth all the furniture of the house of Tobias from the treasury. \textsuperscript{9} And I gave orders, and they purified the treasuries: and I restored thither the vessels of the house of God, and the offerings, and the frankincense.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} And I understood that the portion of the Levites had not been given: and they had fled every one to his field, the Levites and the singers doing the work. \textsuperscript{11} And I strove with the commanders, and said, Wherefore has the house of God been abandoned? and I assembled them, and set them in their place. \textsuperscript{12} And all Juda brought a tithe of the wheat and the wine and the oil into the treasuries, \textsuperscript{13} to the charge of Selemia the priest, and Sadoc the scribe, and Phadæa of the Levites: and next to them was Anan the son of Zacchur, son of Matthanias; for they were accounted faithful: it was their office to distribute to their brethren.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} Remember me, O God, in this, and let not my kindness be forgotten which I have wrought in regard to the house of the Lord God.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} In those days I saw in Juda men treading wine-presses on the sabbath, and carrying sheaves, and loading asses with both wine, and grapes, and figs, and every kind of burden, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the sabbath-day: \textsuperscript{16} and I testified in the day of their sale. Also there dwelt in it men bringing fish, and selling every kind of merchandise to the children of Juda and in Jerusalem on the sabbath. \textsuperscript{17} And I strove with the free children of Juda, and said to them, What is this evil thing which ye do, and profane the sabbath-day? \textsuperscript{18} Did not your fathers thus, and our God brought upon them and upon us and upon this city all these evils? and do ye bring additional wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} And it came to pass, when the gates were set up in Jerusalem, before the sabbath, that I spoke, and they shut the gates; and I gave orders that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and I set some of my servants at the gates, that none should bring in burdens on the sabbath-day. \textsuperscript{20} So all the merchants lodged, and carried on traffic without Jerusalem once or twice. \textsuperscript{21} Then I testified against them, and said to them, Why do ye lodge in front of the wall? if ye do so again, I will stretch out my hand upon you. From that time they came not on the sabbath. \textsuperscript{22} And I told the Levites who were purifying themselves, and came and kept the gates, that they should sanctify the sabbath-day.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} And in those days I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab: \textsuperscript{24} and their children spoke half in the language of Ashdod, and did not know how to speak in the Jewish language. \textsuperscript{25} And I strove with them and cursed them; and I smote some of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying , Ye shall not give your daughters to their sons, and ye shall not take of their daughters to your sons. \textsuperscript{26} Did not Solomon king of Israel sin thus? though there was no king like him among many nations, and he was beloved of God, and God made him king over all Israel; yet strange women turned him aside. \textsuperscript{27} So we will not hearken to you to do all this evil, to break covenant with our God,—to marry strange wives.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} And Elisub the high priest, one of the sons of Joada, being son-in-law of Sanaballat the Uranite, I chased him away from me. \textsuperscript{29} Remember them, O God, for their false connection with the priesthood, and the breaking the covenant of the priesthood, and for defiling the Levites.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} So I purged them from all foreign connection, and established courses for the priests and the Levites, every man according to his work. \textsuperscript{31} And the offering of the wood-bearers was at certain set times, and in the times of the first-fruits. Remember me, O our God, for good.\par
\section*{NEHEMIAH}
\subsection*{NEHEMIAH 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} The words of Neemias the son of Chelcia. And it came to pass in the month Chaseleu, of the twentieth year, that I was in Susan the palace. \textsuperscript{2} And Anani, one of my brethren, came, he and some men of Juda; and I asked them concerning those that had escaped, who had been left of the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{3} And they said to me, The remnant, even those that are left of the captivity, are there in the land, in great distress and reproach: and the walls of Jerusalem are thrown down, and its gates are burnt with fire. \textsuperscript{4} And it came to pass, when I heard these words, that I sat down and wept, and mourned for several days, and continued fasting and praying before the God of heaven. \textsuperscript{5} And I said, Nay, I pray thee, O Lord God of heaven, the mighty, the great and terrible, keeping thy covenant and mercy to them that love him, and to those that keep his commandments: \textsuperscript{6} let now thine ear be attentive, and thine eyes open, that thou mayest hear the prayer of thy servant, which I pray before thee at this time, this day both day and night, for the children of Israel thy servants, and make confession for the sins of the children of Israel, which we have sinned against thee: both I and the house of my father have sinned. \textsuperscript{7} We have altogether broken covenant with thee, and we have not kept the commandments, and the ordinances, and the judgments, which thou didst command thy servant Moses. \textsuperscript{8} Remember, I pray thee, the word wherewith thou didst charge thy servant Moses, saying, If ye break covenant with me , I will disperse you among the nations. \textsuperscript{9} But if ye turn again to me, and keep my commandments, and do them; if ye should be scattered under the utmost bound of heaven, thence will I gather them, and I will bring them into the place which I have chosen to cause my name to dwell there. \textsuperscript{10} Now they are thy servants and thy people, whom thou hast redeemed with thy great power, and with thy strong hand. \textsuperscript{11} Turn not away , I pray thee, O Lord, but let thine ear be attentive to the prayer of thy servant, and to the prayer of thy servants, who desire to fear thy name: and prosper, I pray thee, thy servant this day, and cause him to find mercy in the sight of this man. Now I was the king's cup-bearer.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
NEHEMIAH 1:2 TSK note: Hanani I asked, that had escaped\par
NEHEMIAH 1:3 TSK note: the province, ;, ; in great;, ; , reproach; , the wall\par
NEHEMIAH 1:4 TSK note: I sat down; , ; the God\par
NEHEMIAH 1:6 TSK note: thine ear; , ; day and night;, ;, ; confess, ; , ; both I\par
NEHEMIAH 1:7 TSK note: dealt; corruptly; the commandments;, ; , which thou\par
NEHEMIAH 1:9 TSK note: if ye turn;, ; yet will I;, ;, ;, ;, ; will bring; the place\par
NEHEMIAH 1:10 TSK note: Now these; , ; whom; thy strong\par
NEHEMIAH 1:11 TSK note: Let now;, who desire; grant;, ;, ; For I was The office of cup-bearer was one of great trust, honour, and emolument, in the Persian court. To be in such a place of trust he must have been in the king's confidence; for no eastern potentate would have a cup-bearer to whom he could not trust his life, poison being often administered in that way. It was an office much desired, because it gave access to the king in those seasons of hilarity when men are most disposed to grant favours.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{NEHEMIAH 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And it came to pass in the month Nisan of the twentieth year of king Arthasastha, that the wine was before me: and I took the wine, and gave it to the king: and there was not another before him. \textsuperscript{2} And the king said to me, Why is thy countenance sad, and dost thou not control thyself? and now this is nothing but sorrow of heart. Then I was very much alarmed, \textsuperscript{3} and I said to the king, Let the king live for ever: why should not my countenance be said, forasmuch as the city, even the home of the sepulchres of my fathers, has been laid waste, and her gates have been devoured with fire? \textsuperscript{4} And the king said to me, For what dost thou ask thus? So I prayed to the God of heaven. \textsuperscript{5} And I said to the king, If it seem good to the king, and if thy servant shall have found favour in thy sight, I ask that thou wouldest send him into Juda, to the city of the sepulchres of my fathers; then will I rebuild it. \textsuperscript{6} And the king, and his concubine that sat next to him, said to me, For how long will thy journey be, and when wilt thou return? and the proposal was pleasing before the king, and he sent me away, and I appointed him a time. \textsuperscript{7} And I said to the king, If it seem good to the king, let him give me letters to the governors beyond the river, so as to forward me till I come to Juda; \textsuperscript{8} and a letter to Asaph the keeper of the garden which belongs to the king, that he may give me timber to cover the gates, and for the wall of the city, and for the house into which I shall enter. And the king gave to me, according as the good hand of God was upon me . \textsuperscript{9} And I came to the governors beyond the river, and I gave them the king's letters. (Now the king had sent with me captains of the army and horsemen.) \textsuperscript{10} And Sanaballat the Aronite heard it , and Tobia the servant, the Ammonite, and it was grievous to them that a man was come to seek good for the children of Israel. \textsuperscript{11} So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days. \textsuperscript{12} And I rose up by night, I and a few men with me; and I told no man what God put into my heart to do with Israel; and there was no beast with me, except the beast which I rode upon. \textsuperscript{13} And I went forth by the gate of the valley by night, and to the mouth of the well of fig trees, and to the dung-gate: and I mourned over the wall of Jerusalem which they were destroying, and her gates were devoured with fire. \textsuperscript{14} And I passed on to the fountain gate, and to the king's pool; and there was no room for the beast to pass under me. \textsuperscript{15} And I went up by the wall of the brook by night, and mourned over the wall, and passed through the gate of the valley, and returned. \textsuperscript{16} And the sentinels knew not why I went, nor what I was doing; and until that time I told it not to the Jews, or to the priests, or to the nobles, or to the captains, or to the rest of the men who wrought the works. \textsuperscript{17} Then I said to them, Ye see this evil, in which we are, how Jerusalem is desolate, and her gates have been set on fire: come, and let us build throughout the wall of Jerusalem, and we shall be no longer a reproach. \textsuperscript{18} And I told them of the hand of God which was good upon me, also about the words of the king which he spoke to me: and I said, Let us arise and build. And their hands were strengthened for the good work . \textsuperscript{19} And Sanaballat the Aronite, and Tobia the servant, the Ammonite, and Gesam the Arabian, heard it , and they laughed us to scorn, and came to us, and said, What is this thing that ye are doing? are ye revolting against the king? \textsuperscript{20} And I answered them, and said to them, The God of heaven, he shall prosper us, and we his servants are pure, and we will build: but ye have no part, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
NEHEMIAH 2:1 TSK note: Nisan the twentieth;, I took up\par
NEHEMIAH 2:2 TSK note: Why is thy sorrow Then I Probably the king spoke as if he had some suspicion that Nehemiah harboured some bad design, and that his face indicated some conceived treachery, or remorse; and, indeed, the words rendered sad, and sorrow of heart, might be rendered evil, and wickedness of heart.\par
NEHEMIAH 2:3 TSK note: Let the king Far from wishing ill to my master, I wish him to live forever.;, the city;, ; the place\par
NEHEMIAH 2:4 TSK note: For what;, ; So I prayed\par
NEHEMIAH 2:5 TSK note: If it please;, and if thy\par
NEHEMIAH 2:6 TSK note: the queen Heb. the wife, It was probably Esther who was present at this time, and who seconded Nehemiah's request. So it pleased, ;, I set him a time It is probable that this time was no more than six months, or a year; after which he either returned, or had his leave of absence lengthened, as we find he was twelve years governor of the Jews.\par
NEHEMIAH 2:7 TSK note: let letters;, that they may\par
NEHEMIAH 2:8 TSK note: the wall, the house, the king\par
NEHEMIAH 2:9 TSK note: to the governors Now the\par
NEHEMIAH 2:10 TSK note: Sanballat, Horonite;, the servant; the Ammonite it grieved;, ; , ;, there was come\par
NEHEMIAH 2:12 TSK note: I arose; , ; neither; my God This pious and noble-minded man attributes every thing to God. If he purposed any good, it was because God put it into his heart; if he did or received any good, it was because the good hand of his God was upon him; if he expected any good, it was because he earnestly prayed God to remember him for good.\par
NEHEMIAH 2:13 TSK note: the gate, ; the dung port This was the gate on the eastern side of the city, through which the filth was carried to the brook Kidron and valley of Hinnom., the walls\par
NEHEMIAH 2:14 TSK note: the gate of the fountain The gate leading either to the fountain of Siloam, on the east of the city, or to that of Gihon, on the west.;, ; the king's pool Probably the aqueduct made by Hezekiah to bring the waters of Gihon to the city of David.\par
NEHEMIAH 2:15 TSK note: the brook The brook Kidron, ; the gate The gate leading to the valley of Jehoshaphat, east of the city, through which the brook Kidron flows. It was by this gate he went out; so that he went round the whole of the city, and entered by the same gate.\par
NEHEMIAH 2:17 TSK note: Ye see, come, ; a reproach\par
NEHEMIAH 2:18 TSK note: the hand So they strengthened\par
NEHEMIAH 2:19 TSK note: Sanballat, Geshem, Gashmu they;, ; will ye rebel\par
NEHEMIAH 2:20 TSK note: The God; , ; ye have no; memorial;, ; , ; When Nehemiah had prayed for the relief of his countrymen, and perhaps in David's words, he did not sit still and say, "Let God now do his own work, for I have no more to do; " but set himself to do what he could towards it; and here we find that the people were of one heart with Nehemiah. Our prayers must be seconded with our serious endeavours, or else we mock God. Nearly four months had passed, namely, from Chisleu to Nisan (November to March), before Nehemiah made his application to the king for leave to go to Jerusalem; either because the winter was not a proper time for such a journey, and he would not make a motion till he could pursue it, or because it was so long before his month of waiting upon the king came, and there was no coming into his presence until called for, . We are not thus limited to certain moments in our addresses to the King of kings, but have liberty of access to him at all times; to the throne of grace we never come unseasonably.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{NEHEMIAH 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then Eliasub the high priest, and his brethren the priests, rose up, and built the sheep-gate; they sanctified it, and set up the doors of it; even to the tower of the hundred they sanctified it , to the tower of Anameel. \textsuperscript{2} And they builded by the side of the men of Jericho, and by the side of the sons of Zacchur, the son of Amari. \textsuperscript{3} And the sons of Asana built the fish-gate; they roofed it, and covered in its doors, and bolts, and bars. \textsuperscript{4} And next to them the order reached to Ramoth the son of Uria, the son of Accos, and next to them Mosollam son of Barachias the son of Mazebel took his place: and next to them Sadoc the son of Baana took his place. \textsuperscript{5} And next to them the Thecoim took their place; but the Adorim applied not their neck to their service. \textsuperscript{6} And Joida the son of Phasec, and Mesulam son of Basodia, repaired the old gate; they covered it in, and set up its doors, and its bolts, and its bars. \textsuperscript{7} And next to them repaired Maltias the Gabaonite, and Evaron the Meronothite, the men of Gabaon and Maspha, to the throne of the governor on this side the river. \textsuperscript{8} And next to him Oziel the son of Arachias of the smiths, carried on the repairs: and next to them Ananias the son of one of the apothecaries repaired, and they finished Jerusalem to the broad wall. \textsuperscript{9} And next to them repaired Raphaea the son of Sur, the ruler of half the district round about Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{10} And next to them repaired Jedaia the son of Eromaph, and that in front of his house: and next to him repaired Attuth son of Asabania. \textsuperscript{11} And next to him repaired Melchias son of Heram, and Asub son of Phaat Moab, even to the tower of the furnaces. \textsuperscript{12} And next to him repaired Sallum the son of Alloes, the ruler of half the district round about Jerusalem, he and his daughters. \textsuperscript{13} Anun and the inhabitants of Zano repaired the gate of the valley: they built it, and set up its doors, and its bolts, and its bars, and a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the dung-gate. \textsuperscript{14} And Melchia the son of Rechab, the ruler of the district round about Beth-accharim, repaired the dung-gate, he and his sons; and they covered it, and set up its doors, and its bolts, and its bars. \textsuperscript{15} But Solomon the son of Choleze repaired the gate of the fountain, the ruler of part of Maspha; he built it, and covered it, and set up its doors and its bars, and the wall of the pool of the skins by the meadow of the king, and as far as the steps that lead down from the city of David. \textsuperscript{16} After him repaired Neemias son of Azabuch, ruler of half the district round about Bethsur, as far as the garden of David's sepulchre, and as far as the artificial pool, and as far as the house of the mighty men. \textsuperscript{17} After him repaired the Levites, even Raum the son of Bani: next to him repaired Asabia, ruler of half the district round about Keila, in his district. \textsuperscript{18} And after him repaired his brethren, Benei son of Enadad, ruler of half the district round about Keila. \textsuperscript{19} And next to him repaired Azur the son of Joshua, ruler of Masphai, another portion of the tower of ascent, where it meets the corner. \textsuperscript{20} After him repaired Baruch the son of Zabu, a second portion, from the corner as far as the door of the house of Eliasub the high priest. \textsuperscript{21} After him repaired Meramoth the son of Uria the son of Accos, a second part from the door of the house of Eliasub, to the end of the house of Eliasub. \textsuperscript{22} And after him repaired the priests, the men of Ecchechar. \textsuperscript{23} And after him repaired Benjamin and Asub over against their house: and after him repaired Azarias son of Maasias the son of Ananias, the parts near to his house. \textsuperscript{24} After him repaired Bani the son of Adad, another portion from the house of Azaria as far as the corner and to the turning, \textsuperscript{25} of Phalach the son of Uzai, opposite the corner, and where is also the tower that projects from the king's house, even the upper one of the prison-house: and after him repaired Phadaea the son of Phoros. \textsuperscript{26} And the Nathinim dwelt in Ophal, as far as the garden of the water-gate eastward, and there is the projecting tower. \textsuperscript{27} And after them the Thecoim repaired, another portion opposite the great projecting tower, even as far as the wall of Ophla. \textsuperscript{28} The priests repaired above the horse-gate, every man over against his own house. \textsuperscript{29} And after him Sadduc the son of Emmer repaired opposite his own house: and after him repaired Samaea son of Sechenia, guard of the east-gate. \textsuperscript{30} After him repaired Anania son of Selemia, and Anom, the sixth son of Seleph, another portion: after him Mesulam the son of Barachia repaired over against his treasury. \textsuperscript{31} After him repaired Melchia the son of Sarephi as far as the house of the Nathinim, and the chapmen over against the gate of Maphecad, and as far as the steps of the corner. But, after all which learned men have written on this subject, which is but of little interest, we scarcely know anything about these gates. What they were, why called by these names, or in what part of the wall they were situated, beyond what may be learned from the parallel passages.; sanctified it; *title, the tower\par

NEHEMIAH 3:7 TSK note: the Gibeonite; Mizpah; the throne That is, probably, the palace of the Persian governor, west of the Euphrates; the term throne being used to signify any royal abode. For Sir J. Chardin, describing a splendid tent erected by the king of Persia, says "that there was an inscription wrought upon the cornice of the anti-chamber, which gave it the appellation of the throne of the second Solomon." Sitting upon a throne has, however, sometimes been granted to governors.\par

NEHEMIAH 3:14 TSK note: the dung gate, the ruler, Bethhaccerem Beth-haccerem was a town of Judah, situated on a mountain, between Jerusalem and Tekoa, according to Jerome on . Dr. Pococke conjectures that the Mountain of the Franks, called also the Mount of Bethulia, from a village of that name near it, west-north-west of Tekoa, is the ancient Beth-haccerem; the position of which seems to agree with the citadel of Herodium, built by Herod, on a moderate-sized hill, sixty furlongs from Jerusalem.\par

Dr. Richardson represents the pool of Siloam as occurring higher up the valley of Jehoshaphat, towards the north, than the well of Nehemiah, a little beyond the village of Siloa, and nearly opposite the tombs of Jehoshaphat and Zechariah., Shiloah, ;, Siloam the stairs\par

The names of those who repaired the walls are commemorated, because it was an undertaking of piety, virtue, and courage, to restore the holy city., the turning\par

From the remotest period of the history of the Jews, they had artists in all the elegant and ornamental trades; and it appears that goldsmiths, apothecaries, and merchants were formed into companies in the time of Nehemiah.\par

\subsection*{NEHEMIAH 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now it came to pass, when Sanaballat heard that we were building the wall, that it was grievous to him, and he was very angry, and railed against the Jews. \textsuperscript{2} And he said before his brethren (that is the army of the Samaritans) Is it true that these Jews are building their city? do they indeed offer sacrifices? will they prevail? and will they this day restore the stones, after they have been burnt and made a heap of rubbish? \textsuperscript{3} And Tobias the Ammanite came near to him, and said to them, Do they sacrifice or eat in their place? shall not a fox go up and pull down their wall of stones? \textsuperscript{4} Hear, O our God, for we have become a scorn; and return thou their reproach upon their head, and make them a scorn in a land of captivity, \textsuperscript{5} and do not cover their iniquity. \textsuperscript{7} But it came to pass, when Sanaballat and Tobia, and the Arabians, and the Ammanites, heard that the building of the walls of Jerusalem was advancing, and that the breaches began to be stopped, that it appeared very grievous to them. \textsuperscript{8} And all of them assembled together, to come to fight against Jerusalem, and to destroy it utterly. \textsuperscript{9} So we prayed to our God and set watchmen against them day and night, because of them. \textsuperscript{10} And Juda said, The strength of the enemies is broken, yet there is much rubbish, and we shall not be able to build the wall. \textsuperscript{11} And they that afflicted us said, They shall not know, and they shall not see, until we come into the midst of them, and slay them, and cause the work to cease. \textsuperscript{12} And it came to pass, when the Jews who lived near them came, that they said to us, They are coming up against us from every quarter. \textsuperscript{13} So I set men in the lowest part of the place behind the wall in the lurking-places, I even set the people according to their families, with their swords, their spears, and their bows. \textsuperscript{14} And I looked, and arose, and said to the nobles, and to the captains, and to the rest of the people, Be not afraid of them: remember our great and terrible God, and fight for your brethren, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses. \textsuperscript{15} And it came to pass, when our enemies heard that it was made known to us, and God had frustrated their counsel, that we all returned to the wall, every man to his work. \textsuperscript{16} And it came to pass from that day that half of them that had been driven forth, wrought the work, and half of them kept guard; and there were spears, and shields, and bows, and breast-plates, and rulers behind the whole house of Juda, \textsuperscript{17} even of them that were building the wall:—and those who carried the burdens were under arms: each with one hand wrought his work, and with the other held his dart. \textsuperscript{18} And the builders wrought each man having his sword girt upon his loins, and so they built: and the trumpeter with his trumpet next to him. \textsuperscript{19} And I said to the nobles, and to the rulers, and to the rest of the people, The work is great and abundant, and we are dispersed upon the wall, each at a great distance from his brother. \textsuperscript{20} In whatsoever place ye shall hear the sound of the cornet, thither gather yourselves together to us; and our God shall fight for us. \textsuperscript{21} So we continued labouring at the work: and half of them held the spears from the rising of the morning until the stars appeared. \textsuperscript{22} And at that time I said to the people, Lodge ye every man with his servant in the midst of Jerusalem, and let the night be a watch-time to you, and the day a work-time. \textsuperscript{23} And I was there , and the watchmen behind me, and there was not a man of us that put off his garments.\par

\subsection*{NEHEMIAH 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And the cry of the people and their wives was great against their brethren the Jews. \textsuperscript{2} And some said, We are numerous with our sons and our daughters; so we will take corn, and eat, and live. \textsuperscript{3} And some said, As to our fields and vineyards and houses, let us pledge them , and we will take corn, and eat. \textsuperscript{4} And some said, We have borrowed money for the king's tributes:—our fields, and our vineyards, and houses are pledged . \textsuperscript{5} And now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, our children are as their children: yet, behold, we are reducing our sons and our daughters to slavery, and some of our daughters are enslaved: and there is no power of our hands, for our fields and our vineyards belong to the nobles. \textsuperscript{6} And I was much grieved as I heard their cry and these words. \textsuperscript{7} And my heart took counsel within me, and I contended against the nobles, and the princes, and I said to them, Should every man demand of his brother what ye demand? And I appointed against them a great assembly, \textsuperscript{8} and I said to them, We of our free-will have redeemed our brethren the Jews that were sold to the Gentiles; and do ye sell your brethren? and shall they be delivered to us? And they were silent, and found no answer. \textsuperscript{9} And I said, The thing which ye do is not good; ye will not so walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the Gentiles our enemies. \textsuperscript{10} Both my brethren, and my acquaintances, and I, have lent them money and corn: let us now leave off this exaction. \textsuperscript{11} Restore to them, I pray, as at this day, their fields, and their vineyards, and their olive-yards, and their houses, and bring forth to them corn and wine and oil of the money. \textsuperscript{12} And they said, We will restore, and we will not exact of them; we will do thus as thou sayest. Then I called the priests, and bound them by oath to do according to this word. \textsuperscript{13} And I shook out my garment, and said, So may God shake out every man who shall not keep to this word, from his house, and from his labours, he shall be even thus shaken out, as an outcast and empty. And all the congregation said, Amen, and they praised the Lord: and the people did this thing. \textsuperscript{14} From the day that he charged me to be their ruler in the land of Juda, from the twentieth year even to the thirty-second year of Arthasastha, twelve years, I and my brethren ate not provision extorted from them. \textsuperscript{15} But as for the former acts of extortion wherein those who were before me oppressed them, they even took of them their last money, forty didrachms for bread and wine; and the very outcasts of them exercised authority over the people: but I did not so, because of the fear of God. \textsuperscript{16} Also in the work of the wall I treated them not with rigor, I bought not land: and all that were gathered together came thither to the work. \textsuperscript{17} And the Jews, to the number of a hundred and fifty men, besides those coming to us from the nations round about, were at my table. \textsuperscript{18} And there came to me for one day one calf, and I had six choice sheep and a goat; and every ten days wine in abundance of all sorts: yet with these I required not the bread of extortion, because the bondage was heavy upon this people. \textsuperscript{19} Remember me, O God, for good, in all that I have done to this people.\par

Another author states that this is the lowest rate of interest in Syria. The usual rate is 20; and it is sometimes as high as 30 percent.\par

Pococke says that the bey of Tunis had daily twelve sheep, with fish and fowls, soups, oranges, eggs, onions, boiled rice, etc., etc. His nobles dined with him; after they had done, the servants sat down; and when they had finished, the poor took what was left. Here the bey's twelve sheep are equal to Nehemiah's one ox and six choice sheep; and probably the mode of living between the two was nearly alike. \subsection*{NEHEMIAH 6}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now it came to pass, when Sanaballat, and Tobias, and Gesam the Arabian, and the rest of our enemies, heard that I had built the wall, and that there was no opening left therein; ( but hitherto I had not set up the doors on the gates;) \textsuperscript{2} that Sanaballat and Gesam sent to me, saying, Come and let us meet together in the villages in the plain of Ono. But they were plotting to do me mischief. \textsuperscript{3} So I sent messengers to them, saying, I am doing a great work, and I shall not be able to come down, lest the work should cease: as soon as I shall have finished it, I will come down to you. \textsuperscript{4} And they sent to me again to this effect; and I sent them word accordingly. \textsuperscript{5} Then Sanaballat sent his servant to me with an open letter in his hand. \textsuperscript{6} And in it was written, It has been reported among the Gentiles that thou and the Jews are planning to revolt: therefore thou art building the wall, and thou wilt be a king to them. \textsuperscript{7} And moreover thou has appointed prophets to thyself, that thou mightest dwell in Jerusalem as a king over Juda: and now these words will be reported to the king. Now then, come, let us take counsel together. \textsuperscript{8} And I sent to him, saying, It has not happened according to these words, even as thou sayest, for thou framest them falsely out of thy heart. \textsuperscript{9} For all were trying to alarm us, saying, Their hands shall be weakened from this work, and it shall not be done. Now therefore I have strengthened my hands. \textsuperscript{10} And I came into the house of Semei the son of Dalaia the Son of Metabeel, and he was shut up; and he said, Let us assemble together in the house of God, in the midst of it, and let us shut the doors of it; for they are coming by night to slay thee. \textsuperscript{11} And I said, Who is the man that shall enter into the house, that he may live? \textsuperscript{12} And I observed, and, behold, God had not sent him, for the prophecy was a fable devised against me: \textsuperscript{13} and Tobias and Sanaballat had hired against me a multitude, that I might be frightened, and do this, and sin, and become to them an ill name, that they might reproach me. \textsuperscript{14} Remember, O God, Tobias and Sanaballat, according to these their deeds, and the prophetess Noadia, and the rest of the prophets who tried to alarm me. \textsuperscript{15} So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty-two days. \textsuperscript{16} And it came to pass, when all our enemies heard of it , that all the nations round about us feared, and great alarm fell upon them, and they knew that it was of our God that this work should be finished. \textsuperscript{17} And in those days letters came to Tobias from many nobles of Juda, and those of Tobias came to them. \textsuperscript{18} For many in Juda were bound to him by oath, because he was son-in-law of Sechenias the son of Herae; and Jonan his son had taken the daughter of Mesulam the son of Barachia to wife. \textsuperscript{19} And they reported his words to me, and carried out my words to him: and Tobias sent letters to terrify me.\par

\subsection*{NEHEMIAH 7}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And it came to pass, when the wall was built, and I had set up the doors, and the porters and the singers and the Levites were appointed, \textsuperscript{2} that I gave charge to Ananias my brother, and Ananias the ruler of the palace, over Jerusalem: for he was a true man, and one that feared God beyond many. \textsuperscript{3} And I said to them, The gates of Jerusalem shall not be opened till sunrise; and while they are still watching, let the doors be shut, and bolted; and set watches of them that dwell in Jerusalem, every man at his post, and every man over against his house. \textsuperscript{4} Now the city was wide and large; and the people were few in it, and the houses were not built. \textsuperscript{5} And God put it into my heart, and I gathered the nobles, and the rulers, and the people, into companies: and I found a register of the company that came up first, and I found written in it as follows: \textsuperscript{6} Now these are the children of the country, that came up from captivity, of the number which Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon carried away, and they returned to Jerusalem and to Juda, every man to his city; \textsuperscript{7} with Zorobabel, and Jesus, and Neemia, Azaria, and Reelma, Naemani, Mardochaeus, Balsan, Maspharath, Esdra, Boguia, Inaum, Baana, Masphar, men of the people of Israel. Nathinim, and all Israel, dwelt in their cities.\par

This addition is not found in the Hebrew, or any ancient version. It is also wanting in the Paris and Complutensian Polyglotts; but is found in the Editio Prima of the Vulgate. What follows, however, seems to relate to a distinct oblation from that recorded in Ezra; and was probably made after the people were registered by Nehemiah, who was the Tirshatha, or governor, at this time, as Zerubbabel had been at the first return of the Jews from captivity. Blessed be God that our faith and hope are not built upon the niceties of names and numbers, genealogy and chronology, but on the great things of the law and gospel. \subsection*{NEHEMIAH 8}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And the seventh month arrived, and the children of Israel were settled in their cities; and all the people were gathered as one man to the broad place before the water-gate, and they told Esdras the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the Lord commanded Israel. \textsuperscript{2} So Esdras the priest brought the law before the congregation both of men and women, and every one who had understanding was present to hearken, on the first day of the seventh month. \textsuperscript{3} And he read in it from the time of sun-rise to the middle of the day, before the men and the women; and they understood it , and the ears of all the people were attentive to the book of the law. \textsuperscript{4} And Esdras the scribe stood on a wooden stage, and there stood next to him Mattathias, and Samaeas, and Ananias, and Urias, and Chelcia, and Massia, on his right hand; and on his left Phadaeas, and Misael, and Melchias, and Asom, and Asabadma, and Zacharias, and Mesollam. \textsuperscript{5} And Esdras opened the book before all the people, for he was above the people; and it came to pass when he had opened it, that all the people stood. \textsuperscript{6} And Esdras blessed the Lord, the great God: and all the people answered, and said, Amen, lifting up their hands: and they bowed down and worshipped the Lord with their face to the ground. \textsuperscript{7} And Jesus and Banaias and Sarabias instructed the people in the law, and the people stood in their place. \textsuperscript{8} And they read in the book of the law of God, and Esdras taught, and instructed them distinctly in the knowledge of the Lord, and the people understood the law in the reading. \textsuperscript{9} And Neemias, and Esdras the priest and scribe, and the Levites, and they that instructed the people, spoke and said to all the people, It is a holy day to the Lord our God; do not mourn, nor weep. For all the people wept when they heard the words of the law. \textsuperscript{10} And the governor said to them, Go, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions to them that have nothing; for the day is holy to our Lord: and faint not, for the Lord is our strength. \textsuperscript{11} And the Levites caused all the people to be silent, saying, Be silent, for it is a holy day, and despond not. \textsuperscript{12} So all the people departed to eat, and to drink, and to send portions, and to make great mirth, for they understood the words which he made known to them. \textsuperscript{13} And on the second day the heads of families assembled with all the people, also the priests and Levites, to Esdras the scribe, to attend to all the words of the law. \textsuperscript{14} And they found written in the law which the Lord commanded Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths, in the feast in the seventh month: \textsuperscript{15} and that they should sound with trumpets in all their cities, and in Jerusalem. And Esdras said, Go forth to the mountain, and bring branches of olive, and branches of cypress trees, and branches of myrtle, and branches of palm trees, and branches of every thick tree, to make booths, according to that which was written. \textsuperscript{16} And the people went forth, and brought them , and made booths for themselves, each one upon his roof, and in their courts, and in the courts of the house of God, and in the streets of the city, and as far as the gate of Ephraim. \textsuperscript{17} And all the congregation who had returned from the captivity, made booths, and dwelt in booths: for the children of Israel had not done so from the days of Jesus the son of Naue until that day: and there was great joy. \textsuperscript{18} And Esdras read in the book of the law of God daily, from the first day even to the last day: and they kept the feast seven days; and on the eighth day a solemn assembly, according to the ordinance.\par

\subsection*{NEHEMIAH 9}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now on the twenty-fourth day of this month the children of Israel assembled with fasting, and in sackcloths, and with ashes on their head. \textsuperscript{2} And the children of Israel separated themselves from every stranger, and stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers. \textsuperscript{3} And they stood in their place, and read in the book of the law of the Lord their god: and they confessed their sins to the Lord, and worshipped the Lord their God. \textsuperscript{4} And there stood upon the stairs, of the Levites, Jesus, and the sons of Cadmiel, Sechenia the son of Sarabia, sons of Choneni; and they cried with a loud voice to the Lord their God. \textsuperscript{5} And the Levites, Jesus and Cadmiel, said, Rise up, bless the Lord our God forever and ever: and let them bless thy glorious name, and exalt it with all blessing and praise. \textsuperscript{6} And Esdras said, Thou art the only true Lord; thou madest the heaven, and the heaven of heavens, and all their array, the earth, and all things that are in it, the seas, and all things in them; and thou quickenest all things, and the hosts of heaven worship thee. \textsuperscript{7} Thou art the Lord God, thou didst choose Abram, and broughtest him out of the land of the Chaldeans, and gavest him the name of Abraam: \textsuperscript{8} and thou foundest his heart faithful before thee, and didst make a covenant with him to give to him and to his seed the land of the Chananites, and the Chettites, and Amorites, and Pherezites, and Jebusites, and Gergesites; and thou hast confirmed thy words, for thou art righteous. \textsuperscript{9} And thou sawest the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and thou heardest their cry at the Red Sea. \textsuperscript{10} And thou shewedst signs and wonders in Egypt, on Pharao and all his servants, and on all the people of his land: for thou knowest that they behaved insolently against them: and thou madest thyself a name, as at this day. \textsuperscript{11} And thou didst cleave the sea before them, and they passed through the midst of the sea on dry land; and thou didst cast into the deep them that were about to pursue them, as a stone in the mighty water. \textsuperscript{12} And thou guidedst them by day by a pillar of cloud, and by night by a pillar of fire, to enlighten for them the way wherein they should walk. \textsuperscript{13} Also thou camest down upon mount Sina, and thou spakest to them out of heaven, and gavest them right judgments, and laws of truth, ordinances, and good commandments. \textsuperscript{14} And thou didst make known to them thy holy sabbath; thou didst enjoin upon them commandments, and ordinances, and a law, by the hand of thy servant Moses. \textsuperscript{15} And thou gavest them bread from heaven for their food, and thou broughtest them forth water from a rock for their thirst; and thou badest them go in to inherit the land over which thou stretchedst out thy hand to give it them. \textsuperscript{16} But they and our fathers behaved proudly, and hardened their neck, and did not hearken to thy commandments, \textsuperscript{17} and refused to listen, and remembered not thy wonders which thou wroughtest with them; and they hardened their neck, and appointed a leader to return to their slavery in Egypt: but thou, O God, art merciful and compassionate, long-suffering, and abundant in mercy, and thou didst not forsake them. \textsuperscript{18} And still farther they even made to themselves a molten calf, and said, These are the gods that brought us up out of Egypt: and they wrought great provocations. \textsuperscript{19} Yet thou in thy great compassions didst not forsake them in the wilderness: thou didst not turn away from them the pillar of the cloud by day, to guide them in the way, nor the pillar of fire by night, to enlighten for them the way wherein they should walk. \textsuperscript{20} And thou gavest thy good Spirit to instruct them, and thou didst not withhold thy manna from their mouth, and gavest them water in their thirst. \textsuperscript{21} And thou didst sustain them forty years in the wilderness; thou didst not allow anything to fail them: their garments did not wax old, and their feet were not bruised. \textsuperscript{22} Moreover, thou gavest them kingdoms, and didst divide nations to them: and they inherited the land of Seon king of Esebon, and the land of Og king of Basan. \textsuperscript{23} And thou didst multiply their children as the stars of heaven, and broughtest them into the land of which thou spokest to their fathers; \textsuperscript{24} And they inherited it: and thou didst destroy from before them the dwellers in the land of the Chananites, and thou gavest into their hands them and their kings, and the nations of the land, to do unto them as it pleased them. \textsuperscript{25} And they took lofty cities, and inherited houses full of all good things, wells dug, vineyards, and oliveyards, and every fruit tree in abundance: so they ate, and were filled, and grew fat, and rioted in thy great goodness. \textsuperscript{26} But they turned, and revolted from thee, and cast thy law behind their backs; and they slew thy prophets, who testified against them to turn them back to thee, and they wrought great provocations. \textsuperscript{27} Then thou gavest them into the hand of them that afflicted them, and they did afflict them: and they cried to thee in the time of their affliction, and thou didst hear them from thy heaven, and in thy great compassions gavest them deliverers, and didst save them from the hand of them that afflicted them. \textsuperscript{28} But when they rested, they did evil again before thee: so thou leftest them in the hands of their enemies, and they ruled over them: and they cried again to thee, and thou heardest them from heaven, and didst deliver them in thy great compassions. \textsuperscript{29} And thou didst testify against them, to bring them back to thy law: but they hearkened not, but sinned against thy commandments and thy judgments, which if a man do, he shall live in them; and they turned their back, and hardened their neck, and heard not. \textsuperscript{30} Yet thou didst bear long with them many years, and didst testify to them by thy Spirit by the hand of thy prophets: but they hearkened not; so thou gavest them into the hand of the nations of the land. \textsuperscript{31} But thou in thy many mercies didst not appoint them to destruction, and didst not forsake them; for thou art strong, and merciful, and pitiful. \textsuperscript{32} And now, O our God, the powerful, the great, the mighty, and the terrible, keeping thy covenant and thy mercy, let not all the trouble seem little in thy sight which has come upon us, and our kings, and our princes, and our priests, and our prophets, and our fathers, and upon all thy people, from the days of the kings of Assur even to this day. \textsuperscript{33} But thou art righteous in all the things that come upon us; for thou hast wrought faithfully, but we have greatly sinned. \textsuperscript{34} And our kings, and our princes, and our priests, and our fathers, have not performed thy law, and have not given heed to thy commandments, and have not kept thy testimonies which thou didst testify to them. \textsuperscript{35} And they did not serve thee in thy kingdom, and in thy great goodness which thou gavest to them, and in the large and fat land which thou didst furnish before them, and they turned not from their evil devices. \textsuperscript{36} Behold, we are servants this day, and as for the land which thou gavest to our fathers to eat the fruit of it and the good things of it, behold, we are servants upon it: \textsuperscript{37} and its produce is abundant for the kings whom thou didst appoint over us because of our sins; and they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle, as it pleases them, and we are in great affliction. \textsuperscript{38} And in regard to all these circumstances we make a covenant, and write it , and our princes, our Levites, and our priests, set their seal to it .\par

\subsection*{NEHEMIAH 11}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And the chiefs of the people dwelt in Jerusalem: and the rest of the people cast lots, to bring one of every ten to dwell in Jerusalem the holy city, and nine parts in the other cities. \textsuperscript{2} And the people blessed all the men that volunteered to dwell in Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{3} Now these are the chiefs of the province who dwelt in Jerusalem, and in the cities of Juda; every man dwelt in his possession in their cities: Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the Nathinim, and the children of the servants of Solomon. \textsuperscript{4} And there dwelt in Jerusalem some of the children of Juda, and of the children of Benjamin. Of the children of Juda; Athaia son of Azia, the son of Zacharia, the son of Samaria, the son of Saphatia, the son of Maleleel, and some of the sons of Phares; \textsuperscript{5} and Maasia son of Baruch, son of Chalaza, son of Ozia, son of Adaia, son of Joarib, son of Zacharias, son of Seloni. \textsuperscript{6} All the sons of Phares who dwelt in Jerusalem were four hundred and sixty-eight men of might. \textsuperscript{7} And these were the children of Benjamin; Selo son of Mesulam, son of Joad, son of Phadaia, son of Coleia, son of Maasias, son of Ethiel, son of Jesia. \textsuperscript{8} And after him Gebe, Seli, nine hundred and twenty-eight. \textsuperscript{9} And Joel son of Zechri was overseer over them: and Juda son of Asana was second in the city. \textsuperscript{10} Of the priests: both Jadia son of Joarib, and Jachin. \textsuperscript{11} Saraia, son of Elchia, son of Mesulam, son of Sadduc, son of Marioth, son of Aetoth, was over the house of God. \textsuperscript{12} And their brethren doing the work of the house were eight hundred and twenty-two: and Adaia son of Jeroam, son of Phalalia, son of Amasi, son of Zacharia, son of Phassur, son of Melchia, \textsuperscript{13} and his brethren, chiefs of families, two hundred and forty-two: and Amasia son of Esdriel, son of Mesarimith, son of Emmer, \textsuperscript{14} and his brethren, mighty men of war, a hundred and twenty-eight: and their overseer was Badiel son of one of the great men. \textsuperscript{15} And of the Levites; Samaia, son of Esricam, \textsuperscript{17} Matthanias son of Micha, and Jobeb son of Samui, \textsuperscript{18} two hundred and eighty-four. \textsuperscript{19} And the porters; Acub, Telamin, and their brethren, a hundred and seventy-two. \textsuperscript{22} And the overseer of the Levites was the son of Bani, son of Ozi, son of Asabia, the son of Micha. \begin{quote}\footnotesize
NEHEMIAH 11:1 TSK note: the rulers; cast lots Jerusalem certainly had many inhabitants at this time, but not sufficient to preserve the city, which was now encompassed with a wall, the building of which was going on fast. Nehemiah, therefore, obliged one-tenth of the country people to come and dwell in it, that the population might be sufficient for the defence of the city. Some volunteered their services, which was at that time considered a sacrifice to patriotism; as Jerusalem then afforded very few advantages, and was a place of considerable danger. Hence "the people blessed them that willingly offered themselves."; one of ten the holy\par

NEHEMIAH 12:27 TSK note: am 3559, bc 445 the dedication Jerusalem was the holy city, and the wall was built under the immediate superintendence and blessing of Jehovah. It was therefore proper that it should be dedicated to that God who was there worshipped by solemn praises, prayers, and sacrifices. The dedication seems to have consisted in processions of the most eminent persons around the walls, with thanksgivings to God, who had enabled them to bring the work to so happy a conclusion; and, no doubt, to all this were added a particular consecration of the city to God, and the most earnest invocation that He would take it under His guardianship, and defend it and its inhabitants against their enemies.; *title out;, ;, ; gladness; , ; thanksgivings\par

\subsection*{NEHEMIAH 13}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} In that day they read in the book of Moses in the ears of the people; and it was found written in it, that the Ammonites and Moabites should not enter into the congregation of God for ever; \textsuperscript{2} because they met not the children of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them: but our God turned the curse into a blessing. \textsuperscript{3} And it came to pass, when they heard the law, that they were separated, even every alien in Israel. \textsuperscript{4} And before this time Eliasib the priest dwelt in the treasury of the house of our God, connected with Tobias; \textsuperscript{5} and he made himself a great treasury, and there they were formerly in the habit of bestowing the offerings, and the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithe of the corn, and the wine, and the oil, the ordered portion of the Levites, and singers, and porters; and the first-fruits of the priests. \textsuperscript{6} But in all this time I was not in Jerusalem; for in the thirty-second year of Arthasastha king of Babylon I came to the king, and after a certain time I made my request of the king; \textsuperscript{7} and I came to Jerusalem, and I understood the mischief which Eliasib had done in the case of Tobias, in making for him a treasury in the court of the house of God. \textsuperscript{8} And it appeared very evil to me: so I cast forth all the furniture of the house of Tobias from the treasury. \textsuperscript{9} And I gave orders, and they purified the treasuries: and I restored thither the vessels of the house of God, and the offerings, and the frankincense. \textsuperscript{10} And I understood that the portion of the Levites had not been given: and they had fled every one to his field, the Levites and the singers doing the work. \textsuperscript{11} And I strove with the commanders, and said, Wherefore has the house of God been abandoned? and I assembled them, and set them in their place. \textsuperscript{12} And all Juda brought a tithe of the wheat and the wine and the oil into the treasuries, \textsuperscript{13} to the charge of Selemia the priest, and Sadoc the scribe, and Phadaea of the Levites: and next to them was Anan the son of Zacchur, son of Matthanias; for they were accounted faithful: it was their office to distribute to their brethren. \textsuperscript{14} Remember me, O God, in this, and let not my kindness be forgotten which I have wrought in regard to the house of the Lord God. \textsuperscript{15} In those days I saw in Juda men treading wine-presses on the sabbath, and carrying sheaves, and loading asses with both wine, and grapes, and figs, and every kind of burden, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the sabbath-day: \textsuperscript{16} and I testified in the day of their sale. Also their dwelt in it men bringing fish, and selling every kind of merchandise to the children of Juda and in Jerusalem on the sabbath. \textsuperscript{17} And I strove with the free children of Juda, and said to them, What is this evil thing which ye do, and profane the sabbath-day? \textsuperscript{18} Did not your fathers thus, and our God brought upon them and upon us and upon this city all these evils? and do ye bring additional wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath? \textsuperscript{19} And it came to pass, when the gates were set up in Jerusalem, before the sabbath, that I spoke, and they shut the gates; and I gave orders that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and I set some of my servants at the gates, that none should bring in burdens on the sabbath-day. \textsuperscript{20} So all the merchants lodged, and carried on traffic without Jerusalem once or twice. \textsuperscript{21} Then I testified against them, and said to them, Why do ye lodge in front of the wall? if ye do so again, I will stretch out my hand upon you. From that time they came not on the sabbath. \textsuperscript{22} and I told the Levites who were purifying themselves, and came and kept the gates, that they should sanctify the sabbath-day. Remember me, O God, for these things, and spare me according to the abundance of thy mercy. \textsuperscript{23} And in those days I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab: \textsuperscript{24} and their children spoke half in the language of Ashdod, and did not know how to speak in the Jewish language. \textsuperscript{25} And I strove with them and cursed them; and I smote some of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, Ye shall not give your daughters to their sons, and ye shall not take of their daughters to your sons. \textsuperscript{26} Did not Solomon king of Israel sin thus? though there was no king like him among many nations, and he was beloved of God, and God made him king over all Israel; yet strange women turned him aside. \textsuperscript{27} So we will not hearken to you to do all this evil, to break covenant with our God, —to marry strange wives. \textsuperscript{28} and Elisub the high priest, one of the sons of Joada, being son-in-law of Sanaballat the Uranite, I chased him away from me. \textsuperscript{29} Remember them, O God, for their false connection with the priesthood, and the breaking the covenant of the priesthood, and for defiling the Levites. \textsuperscript{30} So I purged them from all foreign connection, and established courses for the priests and the Levites, every man according to his work. \textsuperscript{31} And the offering of the wood-bearers was at certain set times, and in the times of the first-fruits. Remember me, O our God, for good.\par

\begin{quote}\footnotesize

Vashti had not generally disobeyed the king, therefore she could be no precedent for the general conduct of the Persian women. She disobeyed only in one particular; and this, to serve a purpose, Memucan draws into a general consequence, and the rest came into the conclusion, being either too intoxicated to be able to discern right from wrong, or too intent on reducing women to a state of vassalage, to neglect the present favourable opportunity. done wrong\par

\subsection*{Esther (Greek) 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And after this king Artaxerxes highly honoured Aman son of Amadathes, the Bugæan, and exalted him, and set his seat above all his friends. \textsuperscript{2} And all in the palace did him obeisance, for so the king had given orders to do: but Mardochæus did not do him obeisance. \textsuperscript{3} And they in the king's palace said to Mardochæus, Mardochæus, why dost thou transgress the commands of the king?\par

Esther (Greek) 3:2 TSK note: the king's servants Dr. Shaw, speaking of the cities in the East, says, "If we quit the streets, and enter into any of the principal houses, we shall first pass through a porch, or gate-way, with benches on each side, where the master of the family receives visits, and despatches business; few persons, not even the nearest relations, having admission any farther, except upon extraordinary occasions." These servants were probably officers who here waited the king's call; and it is likely that Mordecai was one of them., bowed; bowed not Yichra welo yishtachaweh, "bowed not down, nor prostrated himself, " or worshipped him. Had this meant only civil reverence the king would not have needed to command it; nor would Mordecai have refused it; there was, therefore, some kind of divine honour intended, such as was paid to the Persian kings, and which even the Greeks refused, as express adoration.\par
\end{quote}

\noindent \textsuperscript{7} And he made a decree in the twelfth year of the reign of Artaxerxes, and cast lots daily and monthly, to slay in one day the race of Mardochæus: and the lot fell on the fourteenth day of the month which is Adar. \textsuperscript{8} And he spoke to king Artaxerxes, saying, There is a nation scattered among the nations in all thy kingdom, and their laws differ from those of all the other nations; and they disobey the laws of the king; and it is not expedient for the king to let them alone. \textsuperscript{9} If it seem good to the king, let him make a decree to destroy them: and I will remit into the king's treasury ten thousand talents of silver. \textsuperscript{10} And the king took off his ring, and gave it into the hands of Aman, to seal the decrees against the Jews. \textsuperscript{11} And the king said to Aman, Keep the silver, and treat the nation as thou wilt.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Esther (Greek) 3:7 TSK note: the first month in the twelfth, they cast Pur; Adar\par
Esther (Greek) 3:8 TSK note: scattered abroad;, ; , ; their laws;, for the king's profit to Heb. meet, or equal for the king to, etc\par
Esther (Greek) 3:9 TSK note: that they may be destroyed Heb. to destroy them and I will pay Heb. and I will weigh, ; Here Haman is obliged to acknowledge that there would be a loss to the revenue, which he was willing to make up out of his own property. Ten thousand talents of silver, counted by the Babylonish talent, amount to 2, 119, 000£.; but reckoned by the Jewish talent, they amount to double that sum. In those days, silver and gold were more plentiful than at present; and we have many instances of individuals possessing almost incredible riches. Herodotus relates, that when Xerxes went into Greece, Pythius the Lydian had 2, 000 talents of silver, and 4, 000, 000 of gold darics, which unitedly amount to nearly 5, 500, 000£. Plutarch tells us, that after Crassus had dedicated the tenth of all he had to Hercules, he entertained the Roman people at 10, 000 tables, and distributed to every citizen as much corn as was sufficient for three months; and, after all these expenses, he had 7, 100; Roman talents left, which amount to more than 1, 500, 000£. Lentulus the augur is said to have possessed no less than 3, 333, 333£. 6s. 8d. Apicius was worth more than 916, 671£ 13s. 4d.; and, after having spent in his kitchen 833, 333£ 6s. 8d. he considered the remainder too little for his support, and poisoned himself! ten thousand\par
\end{quote}

\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Then Mardochæus said to Achrathæus, Go, and say to her, Esther, say not to thyself that thou alone wilt escape in the kingdom, more than all the other Jews. \textsuperscript{14} For if thou shalt refuse to hearken on this occasion, help and protection will be to the Jews from another quarter; but thou and thy father's house will perish: and who knows, if thou hast been made queen for this very occasion? \textsuperscript{15} And Esther sent the man that came to her to Mardochæus, saying, \textsuperscript{16} Go and assemble the Jews that are in Susa, and fast ye for me, and eat not and drink not for three days, night and day: and I also and my maidens will fast; and then I will go in to the king contrary to the law, even if I must die. \textsuperscript{17} So Mardochæus went and did all that Esther commanded him.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Esther (Greek) 4:14 TSK note: then shall; , ; , ; , enlargement Heb. respiration, ; but thou, ;, whether;, ; for such a time; The fact related in this verse was unquestionably the reason why Esther was raised to regal honours, by the overruling providence of God. She was therefore bound in gratitude to do this service for God, else she would not have answered the end of her elevation, and she need not fear the miscarriage of the enterprise, for if God designed her for it, he would surely bear her through and give success. It appeared by the event that Mordecai spoke prophetically, when he modestly conjectured that Esther came to the kingdom that she might be the instrument of the Jews' deliverance. Mordecai thoroughly believed that it was a cause which one way or other would certainly be carried, and which, therefore, she might safely venture upon. Instruments might fail, but God's covenant cannot. There is a wise design in all the providences of God, which is unknown to us till it is accomplished; but it will prove in the issue that all is intended for and centre in the good of those who trust in Him.\par
Esther (Greek) 4:16 TSK note: present Heb. found fast; , ; eat nor drink; , I also; if I perish If I lose my life in the attempt to save my people, I shall lose it cheerfully. I see it is my duty to make the attempt; and, come what will, I am resolved to do it.\par
\end{quote}

Olearius, describing an entertainment at the Persian court, says, "The floor of the hall was covered with cotton cloth, which was covered with all sorts of fruits and sweetmeats in basons of gold. With them was served up excellent Shiraz wine. After an hour's time, the sweetmeats were removed, to make way for the more substantial part of the entertainment, such as rice, boiled and roast mutton, etc. When the company had been at table an hour and a half, warm water was brought, in a ewer of gold, for washing; and grace being said, they began to retire without speaking a word, according to the custom of the country."\par
\end{quote}

Esther (Greek) 8:15 TSK note: royal apparel, ; , ; blue or, violet, and with a great crown Mordecai was now made the chief minister, or vizier, instead of Haman; and was accordingly invested with the "royal apparel, " in conformity to the custom of the East. So we are informed, in the History of the Revolt of Ali Bey, that on the election of a new sheikh bellet, or chief of the country, in Egypt, the pasha who approves of him invests him with a robe of valuable fur. Perhaps the crown was one of the insignia of the office of vizier. Concerning the blue, fine linen, and purple; see note on, and see note on . the city Haman was too proud to be popular. Few lamented his fall.\par
Esther (Greek) 8:16 TSK note: Jews, ; had light That is, prosperity and hope. The dark cloud which had so long hung over them was dispelled; and again the sunshine of prosperity beamed upon them.\par
Esther (Greek) 8:17 TSK note: a feast, ; many of the people; for the fear\par
\end{quote}

\noindent \textsuperscript{16} And the rest of the Jews who were in the kingdom assembled, and helped one another, and obtained rest from their enemies: for they destroyed fifteen thousand of them on the thirteenth day of Adar, but took no spoil. \textsuperscript{17} And they rested on the fourteenth of the same month, and kept it as a day of rest with joy and gladness. \textsuperscript{18} And the Jews in the city Susa assembled also on the fourteenth day and rested; and they kept also the fifteenth with joy and gladness. \textsuperscript{19} On this account then it is that the Jews dispersed in every foreign land keep the fourteenth of Adar as a holy day with joy, sending portions each to his neighbour.\par

Thus, when the Grand Emir found that it incommoded M. D'Arvieux to eat with him, he desired him to take his own time for eating, and sent him from his kitchen what he liked best.\par
\end{quote}

\noindent \textsuperscript{23} And the Jews consented to this accordingly as Mardochæus wrote to them, \textsuperscript{24} shewing how Aman the son of Amadathes the Macedonian fought against them, how he made a decree and cast lots to destroy them utterly; \textsuperscript{25} also how he went in to the king, telling him to hang Mardochæus: but all the calamities he tried to bring upon the Jews came upon himself, and he was hanged, and his children. \textsuperscript{26} Therefore these days were called Phruræ, because of the lots; (for in their language they are called Phruræ;) because of the words of this letter, and because of all they suffered on this account, and all that happened to them. \textsuperscript{27} And Mardochæus established it, and the Jews took upon themselves, and upon their seed, and upon those that were joined to them to observe it , neither would they on any account behave differently: but these days were to be a memorial kept in every generation, and city, and family, and province. \textsuperscript{28} And these days of the Phruræ, said they , shall be kept for ever, and their memorial shall not fail in any generation.\par

Esther (Greek) 10:2 TSK note: all the acts, advanced him Heb. made him great, ; in the book, ; Media, which comprehended the modern Azerbijan and part of Irak, was a celebrated country of Asia, bounded on the north by the Caspian Sea and Armenia, west by Assyria, south by Susiana and Persia, and east by Hyrcania and Parthia, extending from 30 degrees to 37 degrees n lat. and 45 degrees to 53 degrees e long. Persia Proper, now Fars, was but a small province, being bounded on the north by Media, west by Susiana, south by the Persian Gulf, and east by Caramania, extending from 27 degrees to 33 degrees n lat. and 50 degrees to 55 degrees e long. But the Persian empire in its ancient state extended from the Hellespont to the Indus, above 2, 800 miles, and from Pontus to the shores of Arabia, above 2, 000 miles; comprehending a multitude of various nations.\par

\subsection*{Job 7}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Is not the life of man upon earth a state of trial? and his existence as that of a hireling by the day? \textsuperscript{2} Or as a servant that fears his master, and one who has grasped a shadow? or as a hireling waiting for his pay? \textsuperscript{3} So have I also endured months of vanity, and nights of pain have been appointed me. \textsuperscript{4} Whenever I lie down, I say, When will it be day? and whenever I rise up, again I say when will it be evening? and I am full of pains from evening to morning. \textsuperscript{5} And my body is covered with loathsome worms; and I waste away, scraping off clods of dust from my eruption. \textsuperscript{6} And my life is lighter than a word, and has perished in vain hope. \textsuperscript{7} Remember then that my life is breath, and mine eye shall not yet again see good. \textsuperscript{8} The eye of him that sees me shall not see me again : thine eyes are upon me, and I am no more. \textsuperscript{9} I am as a cloud that is cleared away from the sky: for if a man go down to the grave, he shall not come up again: \textsuperscript{10} and he shall surely not return to his own house, neither shall his place know him any more. \textsuperscript{11} Then neither will I refrain my mouth: I will speak being in distress; being in anguish I will disclose the bitterness of my soul.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{23} For oh that my words were written, and that they were recorded in a book for ever, \textsuperscript{24} with an iron pen and lead, or graven in the rocks! \textsuperscript{25} For I know that he is eternal who is about to deliver me, \textsuperscript{26} and to raise up upon the earth my skin that endures these sufferings : for these things have been accomplished to me of the Lord; \textsuperscript{27} which I am conscious of in myself, which mine eye has seen, and not another, but all have been fulfilled to me in my bosom.\par

In process of time, public monuments were written on rolls of lead ( plumbeis voluminibus ); and those of a private nature on linen books, or tables covered with wax."\par

\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Job 28:25 TSK note: To make the weight etc. God has given an atmosphere to the earth, which, possessing a certain degree of gravity perfectly suited to the necessities of all animals, vegetables, and fluids, should be the cause, in His hands, of preserving animal and vegetable life; for by it the blood circulates in the veins of animals, and the juices in the tubes of vegetables. Without this atmospheric pressure there could be no respiration; and the elasticity of the particles of air in animal and vegetable bodies, would rupture the vessels in which they are contained, and destroy both kinds of life.; he weigheth He has exactly proportioned the aqueous surface of the earth to the terrene parts, for the purpose of evaporation, etc.\par

\subsection*{Job 30}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} But now the youngest have laughed me to scorn, now they reprove me in their turn, whose fathers I set at nought; whom I did not deem worthy to be with my shepherd dogs. \textsuperscript{2} Yea, why had I the strength of their hands? for them the full term of life was lost. \textsuperscript{3} One is childless in want and famine, such as they that fled but lately the distress and misery of drought. \textsuperscript{4} Who compass the salt places on the sounding shore , who had salt herbs for their food, and were dishonourable and of no repute, in want of every good thing; who also ate roots of trees by reason of great hunger.\par

\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Thieves have risen up against me, \textsuperscript{6} whose houses were the caves of the rocks, who lived under the wild shrubs. \textsuperscript{7} They will cry out among the rustling bushes . \textsuperscript{8} They are sons of fools and vile men, whose name and glory are quenched from off the earth. \textsuperscript{9} But now I am their music, and they have me for a by-word. \textsuperscript{10} And they stood aloof and abhorred me, and spared not to spit in my face. \textsuperscript{11} For he has opened his quiver and afflicted me: they also have cast off the restraint of my presence. \textsuperscript{12} They have risen up against me on the right hand of their offspring; they have stretched out their foot, and directed against me the ways of their destruction. \textsuperscript{13} My paths are ruined; for they have stripped off my raiment: he has shot at me with his weapons. \textsuperscript{14} And he has pleaded against me as he will: I am overwhelmed with pains. \textsuperscript{15} My pains return upon me ; my hope is gone like the wind, and my safety as a cloud.\par

Celsius and Scheuchzer are inclined to think it the paliurus, a shrub growing sometimes to a considerable height in desert places. "One of the inconveniences of the vegetable thickets of Egypt is, " says Denon, "that it is difficult to remain in them, as nine tenths of the trees and plants are armed with inexorable thorns, which suffer only an unquiet enjoyment of the shadow which is so constantly desirable."\par
