\subsection*{Job 31}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} I made a covenant with mine eyes, and I will not think upon a virgin. \textsuperscript{2} Now what portion has God given from above? and is there an inheritance given of the Mighty One from the highest? \textsuperscript{3} Alas! destruction to the unrighteous, and rejection to them that do iniquity. \textsuperscript{4} Will he not see my way, and number all my steps? \textsuperscript{5} But if I had gone with scorners, and if too my foot has hasted to deceit: \textsuperscript{6} (for I am weighed in a just balance, and the Lord knows my innocence:) \textsuperscript{7} if my foot has turned aside out of the way, or if mine heart has followed mine eye, and if too I have touched gifts with my hands; \textsuperscript{8} then let me sow, and let others eat; and let me be uprooted on the earth. \textsuperscript{9} If my heart has gone forth after another man's wife, and if I laid wait at her doors; \textsuperscript{10} then let my wife also please another, and let my children be brought low. \textsuperscript{11} For the rage of anger is not to be controlled, in the case of defiling another man's wife. \textsuperscript{12} For it is a fire burning on every side, and whomsoever it attacks, it utterly destroys.\par

\subsection*{Job 38}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And after Elius had ceased from speaking, the Lord spoke to Job through the whirlwind and clouds, saying ,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} Who is this that hides counsel from me, and confines words in his heart, and thinks to conceal them from me? \textsuperscript{3} Gird thy loins like a man; and I will ask thee, and do thou answer me.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Where wast thou when I founded the earth? tell me now, if thou hast knowledge, \textsuperscript{5} who set the measures of it, if thou knowest? or who stretched a line upon it? \textsuperscript{6} On what are its rings fastened? and who is he that laid the corner-stone upon it? \textsuperscript{7} When the stars were made, all my angels praised me with a loud voice. \textsuperscript{8} And I shut up the sea with gates, when it rushed out, coming forth out of its mother's womb. \textsuperscript{9} And I made a cloud its clothing, and swathed it in mist. \textsuperscript{10} And I set bounds to it, surrounding it with bars and gates. \textsuperscript{11} And I said to it, Hitherto shalt thou come, but thou shalt not go beyond, but thy waves shall be confined within thee.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Job 38:4 TSK note: Where, I;, ;, hast Heb. knowest\par
Job 38:6 TSK note: Whereupon; , ; foundations Heb. sockets, fastened Heb. made to sink, or\par
Job 38:7 TSK note: the morning, the sons, ; shouted\par
Job 38:10 TSK note: brake up for it my decreed place or, established my decree upon it\par
Job 38:11 TSK note: Hitherto Thus far shall thy flux and reflux extend. The tides are marvellously limited and regulated, not only by the lunar and solar attraction, but by the quantum of time required to remove any part of the earth's surface, by its rotation round its axis, from under the immediate attractive influence of the sun and moon. Hence the attraction of the sun and moon, and the gravitation of the sea to its own centre, which prevent too great a flux on the one hand, and too great reflux on the other, are some of those bars and doors by which its proud waves are stayed, and prevented from coming farther., ; but, ;, ; , thy proud waves Heb. the pride of thy waves\par
\end{quote}

\noindent \textsuperscript{22} But hast thou gone to the treasures of snow? and hast thou seen the treasures of hail? \textsuperscript{23} And is there a store of them , for thee against the time of thine enemies, for the day of wars and battle? \textsuperscript{24} And whence proceeds the frost? or whence is the south wind dispersed over the whole world under heaven? \textsuperscript{25} And who prepared a course for the violent rain, and a way for the thunders; \textsuperscript{26} to rain upon the land where there is no man, the wilderness, where there is not a man in it; so as to feed the untrodden and uninhabited land , \textsuperscript{27} and cause it to send forth a crop of green herbs?\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Job 38:26 TSK note: To cause It is well known that rain falls copiously in thunder storms. The flash is first seen, the clap is next heard, and last the rain descends; though in fact they all take place at the same time. The lightning traverses all space in no perceivable succession of time. Sound is propagated at the rate of 1, 142 feet in a second. Rain travels still more slowly, and will be seen sooner or later according to the weight of the drops, and the distance of the cloud. Now as water is composed of two elastic airs or gases, called oxygen and hydrogen, in the proportion of 88+ of the former and 11, 3/4 of the latter in 100 parts, the electric spark, or matter of lightning, passing through the atmosphere, ignites and decomposes those gases, which explode; and the water falls down in the form of rain. This explosion, as well as the rushing in of the circumambient air to restore the equilibrium, will account for the clap and peal; and thus by the lightning of thunder God causes it to rain on the earth. on the wilderness\par
\end{quote}

Psalms 18:9 TSK note: He bowed Jehovah is here represented as a mighty warrior going forth to fight the battles of David. When He descended to the engagement, the very heavens bowed to render his descent more awful: His military tent was substantial darkness; the voice of His thunder was the warlike alarm which sounded to battle; the chariot in which He rode was the thick clouds of heaven, conducted by cherubs, and carried on by the irresistible force and rapid wings of an impetuous tempest; and the darts and weapons He employed were thunder-bolts, lightnings, fiery hail, deluging rains, and stormy winds! No wonder that when God arose all His enemies were scattered, and those that hated Him fled before Him., ; darkness\par
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Psalms 26}

\noindent \textsuperscript{2} When evil-doers drew nigh against me to eat up my flesh, my persecutors and mine enemies, they fainted and fell. \textsuperscript{3} Though an army should set itself in array against me, my heart shall not be afraid: though war should rise up against me, in this am I confident. \textsuperscript{4} One thing have I asked of the Lord, this will I earnestly seek: that I should dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, that I should behold the fair beauty of the Lord, and survey his temple. \textsuperscript{5} For in the day of mine afflictions he hid me in his tabernacle: he sheltered me in the secret of his tabernacle; he set me up on a rock. \textsuperscript{6} And now, behold, he has lifted up mine head over mine enemies: I went round and offered in his tabernacle the sacrifice of joy; I will sing, even sing psalms to the Lord.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{2} O Lord, I have hoped in thee; let me never be ashamed: deliver me in thy righteousness and rescue me. \textsuperscript{3} Incline thine ear to me; make haste to rescue me: be thou to me for a protecting God, and for a house of refuge to save me. \textsuperscript{4} For thou art my strength and my refuge; and thou shalt guide me for thy name's sake, and maintain me. \textsuperscript{5} Thou shalt bring me out of the snare which they have hidden for me; for thou, O Lord, art my defender. \textsuperscript{6} Into thine hands I will commit my spirit: thou hast redeemed me, O Lord God of truth. \textsuperscript{7} Thou hast hated them that idly persist in vanities: but I have hoped in the Lord. \textsuperscript{8} I will exult and be glad in thy mercy: for thou hast looked upon mine affliction; thou hast saved my soul from distresses. \textsuperscript{9} And thou hast not shut me up into the hands of the enemy: thou hast set my feet in a wide place.\par

Make thy face to shine upon thy servant: save me in thy mercy. \textsuperscript{18} O Lord, let me not be ashamed, for I have called upon thee: let the ungodly be ashamed, and brought down to Hades. \textsuperscript{19} Let the deceitful lips become dumb, which speak iniquity against the righteous with pride and scorn.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} How abundant is the multitude of thy goodness, O Lord, which thou hast laid up for them that fear thee! thou hast wrought it out for them that hope on thee, in the presence of the sons of men. \textsuperscript{21} Thou wilt hide them in the secret of thy presence from the vexation of man: thou wilt screen them in a tabernacle from the contradiction of tongues. \textsuperscript{22} Blessed be the Lord: for he has magnified his mercy in a fortified city. \textsuperscript{23} But I said in my extreme fear, I am cast out from the sight of thine eyes: therefore thou didst hearken, O Lord, to the voice of my supplication when I cried to thee.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{1} A Psalm of David.\par

\subsection*{Psalms 34}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} A Psalm of David.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} Take hold of shield and buckler, and arise for my help. \textsuperscript{3} Bring forth a sword, and stop the way against them that persecute me: say to my soul, I am thy salvation. \textsuperscript{4} Let them that seek my soul be ashamed and confounded: let them that devise evils against me be turned back and put to shame. \textsuperscript{5} Let them be as dust before the wind, and an angel of the Lord afflicting them. \textsuperscript{6} Let their way be dark and slippery, and an angel of the Lord persecuting them. \textsuperscript{7} For without cause they have hid for me their destructive snare: without a cause they have reproached my soul.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Psalms 34:5 TSK note: They; and were, ; lightened or, flowed unto him their\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{8} Let a snare which they know not come upon them: and the gin which they hid take them; and let them fall into the very same snare. \textsuperscript{9} But my soul shall exult in the Lord: it shall delight in his salvation. \textsuperscript{10} All my bones shall say, O Lord, who is like to thee? delivering the poor out of the hand of them that are stronger than he, yea, the poor and needy one from them that spoil him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Unjust witnesses arose, and asked me of things I knew not. \textsuperscript{12} They rewarded me evil for good, and bereavement to my soul. \textsuperscript{13} But I, when they troubled me, put on sackcloth, and humbled my soul with fasting: and my prayer shall return to my own bosom. \textsuperscript{14} I behaved agreeably towards them as if it had been our neighbour or brother: I humbled myself as one mourning and sad of countenance. \textsuperscript{15} Yet they rejoiced against me, and plagues were plentifully brought against me, and I knew it not: they were scattered, but repented not. \textsuperscript{16} They tempted me, they sneered at me most contemptuously, they gnashed their teeth upon me.\par

\begin{quote}\footnotesize

Pause.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{10} But now thou hast cast off, and put us to shame; and thou wilt not go forth with our hosts. \textsuperscript{11} Thou hast turned us back before our enemies; and they that hated us spoiled for themselves. \textsuperscript{12} Thou madest us as sheep for meat; and thou scatteredst us among the nations. \textsuperscript{13} Thou hast sold thy people without price, and there was no profit by their exchange. \textsuperscript{14} Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and derision to them that are round about us. \textsuperscript{15} Thou hast made us a proverb among the Gentiles, a shaking of the head among the nations. \textsuperscript{16} All the day my shame is before me, and the confusion of my face has covered me, \textsuperscript{17} because of the voice of the slanderer and reviler; because of the enemy and avenger.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} All these things are come upon us: but we have not forgotten thee, neither have we dealt unrighteously in thy covenant. \textsuperscript{19} And our heart has not gone back; but thou hast turned aside our paths from thy way. \textsuperscript{20} For thou hast laid us low in a place of affliction, and the shadow of death has covered us. \textsuperscript{21} If we have forgotten the name of our God, and if we have spread out our hands to a strange god; shall not God search these things out? \textsuperscript{22} for he knows the secrets of the heart. \textsuperscript{23} For, for thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for slaughter.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} Awake, wherefore sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, and do not cast us off for ever. \textsuperscript{25} Wherefore turnest thou thy face away, and forgettest our poverty and our affliction? \textsuperscript{26} For our soul has been brought down to the dust; our belly has cleaved to the earth. \textsuperscript{27} Arise, O Lord, help us, and redeem us for thy name's sake.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{3} Let the mountains and the hills raise peace to thy people: \textsuperscript{4} he shall judge the poor of the people in righteousness, and save the children of the needy; and shall bring low the false accuser. \textsuperscript{5} And he shall continue as long as the sun, and before the moon for ever. \textsuperscript{6} He shall come down as rain upon a fleece; and as drops falling upon the earth. \textsuperscript{7} In his days shall righteousness spring up; and abundance of peace till the moon be removed. \textsuperscript{8} And he shall have dominion from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth. \textsuperscript{9} The Ethiopians shall fall down before him; and his enemies shall lick the dust. \textsuperscript{10} The kings of Tharsis, and the isles, shall bring presents: the kings of the Arabians and Saba shall offer gifts. \textsuperscript{11} And all kings shall worship him; all the Gentiles shall serve him. \textsuperscript{12} For he has delivered the poor from the oppressor; and the needy who had no helper. \textsuperscript{13} He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall deliver the souls of the needy. \textsuperscript{14} He shall redeem their souls from usury and injustice: and their name shall be precious before him. \textsuperscript{15} And he shall live, and there shall be given him of the gold of Arabia: and men shall pray for him continually; and all the day shall they praise him. \textsuperscript{16} There shall be an establishment on the earth on the tops of the mountains: the fruit thereof shall be exalted above Libanus, and they of the city shall flourish as grass of the earth.\par

Psalms 71:3 TSK note: my strong habitation Heb. to me for a rock of habitation, ; thou hast, ; my rock\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who alone does wonders. \textsuperscript{19} And blessed is his glorious name for ever, even for ever and ever: and all the earth shall be filled with his glory. So be it, so be it. \textsuperscript{20} The hymns of David the son of Jessæ are ended.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{2} But my feet were almost overthrown; my goings very nearly slipped. \textsuperscript{3} For I was jealous of the transgressors, beholding the tranquillity of sinners.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} For there is no sign of reluctance in their death: and they have firmness under their affliction. \textsuperscript{5} They are not in the troubles of other men; and they shall not be scourged with other men. \textsuperscript{6} Therefore pride has possessed them; they have clothed themselves with their injustice and ungodliness. \textsuperscript{7} Their injustice shall go forth as out of fatness: they have fulfilled their intention. \textsuperscript{8} They have taken counsel and spoken in wickedness: they have uttered unrighteousness loftily. \textsuperscript{9} They have set their mouth against heaven, and their tongue has gone through upon the earth. \textsuperscript{10} Therefore shall my people return hither: and full days shall be found with them. \textsuperscript{11} And they said, How does God know? and is there knowledge in the Most High? \textsuperscript{12} Behold, these are the sinners, and they that prosper always: they have possessed wealth.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Surely thou hast appointed judgments to them because of their crafty dealings: thou hast cast them down when they were lifted up. \textsuperscript{19} How have they become desolate! suddenly they have failed: they have perished because of their iniquity. \textsuperscript{20} As the dream of one awakening, O Lord, in thy city thou wilt despise their image.\par

\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Psalms 77:10 TSK note: This is etc. Or, as Dr. Waterland renders, "This my affliction is a change of the right hand of the Most High, " i.e., it proceeds from a change of God's conduct towards me. De Dieu renders, Precari, hoc meum est; mutare dextram Altissimì "To pray, this is my business. To change the right hand of the Most High." I can do nothing else than pray: God is the Ruler of events. Mr. N. M. Berlin translates, Dolere meum hoc est: mutare est dextre Altissimi . "To grieve is my portion. To change (my condition) belongs to the right hand of the Most High.", ; the years\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} And they sinned yet more against him; they provoked the Most High in the wilderness. \textsuperscript{18} And they tempted God in their hearts, in asking meat for the desire of their souls. \textsuperscript{19} They spoke also against God, and said, Will God be able to prepare a table in the wilderness? \textsuperscript{20} Forasmuch as he smote the rock, and the waters flowed, and the torrents ran abundantly; will he be able also to give bread, or prepare a table for his people?\par

Psalms 77:17 TSK note: poured out like water, Heb. were poured forth with water, thine\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{21} Therefore the Lord heard, and was provoked: and fire was kindled in Jacob, and wrath went up against Israel. \textsuperscript{22} Because they believed not in God, and trusted not in his salvation. \textsuperscript{23} Yet he commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven, \textsuperscript{24} and rained upon them manna to eat, and gave them the bread of heaven. \textsuperscript{25} Man ate angels' bread; he sent them provision to the full.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{26} He removed the south wind from heaven; and by his might he brought in the south-west wind. \textsuperscript{27} And he rained upon them flesh like dust, and feathered birds like the sand of the seas. \textsuperscript{28} And they fell into the midst of their camp, round about their tents. \textsuperscript{29} So they ate, and were completely filled; and he gave them their desire.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} They were not disappointed of their desire: but when their food was yet in their mouth, \textsuperscript{31} then the indignation of God rose up against them, and slew the fattest of them, and overthrew the choice men of Israel.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{32} In the midst of all this they sinned yet more, and believed not his miracles. \textsuperscript{33} And their days were consumed in vanity, and their years with anxiety.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{34} When he slew them, they sought him: and they returned and called betimes upon God. \textsuperscript{35} And they remembered that God was their helper, and the most high God was their redeemer. \textsuperscript{36} Yet they loved him only with their mouth, and lied to him with their tongue. \textsuperscript{37} For their heart was not right with him, neither were they steadfast in his covenant.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{38} But he is compassionate, and will forgive their sins, and will not destroy them : yea, he will frequently turn away his wrath, and will not kindle all his anger. \textsuperscript{39} And he remembered that they are flesh; a wind that passes away, and returns not.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Psalms 77:38 Brenton note: Gr. be propitious, or, merciful to.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{40} How often did they provoke him in the wilderness, and anger him in a dry land! \textsuperscript{41} Yea, they turned back, and tempted God, and provoked the Holy One of Israel. \textsuperscript{42} They remembered not his hand, the day in which he delivered them from the hand of the oppressor. \textsuperscript{43} How he had wrought his signs in Egypt, and his wonders in the field of Tanes: \textsuperscript{44} and had changed their rivers into blood; and their streams, that they should not drink. \textsuperscript{45} He sent against them the dog-fly, and it devoured them; and the frog, and it spoiled them. \textsuperscript{46} And he gave their fruit to the canker worm, and their labours to the locust. \textsuperscript{47} He killed their vines with hail, and their sycamores with frost. \textsuperscript{48} And he gave up their cattle to hail, and their substance to the fire. \textsuperscript{49} He sent out against them the fury of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and affliction, a message by evil angels. \textsuperscript{50} He made a way for his wrath; he spared not their souls from death, but consigned their cattle to death; \textsuperscript{51} and smote every first-born in the land of Egypt; the first-fruits of their labours in the tents of Cham. \textsuperscript{52} And he removed his people like sheep; he led them as a flock in the wilderness. \textsuperscript{53} And he guided them with hope, and they feared not: but the sea covered their enemies. \textsuperscript{54} And he brought them in to the mountain of his sanctuary, this mountain which his right hand had purchased. \textsuperscript{55} And he cast out the nations from before them, and made them to inherit by a line of inheritance, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.\par

Psalms 77:44 Brenton note: Gr. rains, or, showers.\par

Nothing is recorded in the history of Israel concerning the cowardice of the Ephraimites, as distinct from that of the other tribes. Psalms 78:11 Brenton note: i. e. men appointed to die.\par
Psalms 78:12 TSK note: Marvellous, ; Exod. 7:1-12:51;, ; Zoan, the ancient capital of the Pharaohs, where Moses wrought so many miracles, is rendered by the Chaldee, Tanium, LXX Τανις, Vulgate, Tanis, and Coptic, Tane, from the Coptic, ten, plain, flat, level; being situated in the low ground of the Delta, on one of the eastern branches of the Nile, bearing its own name, near a large lake, now called the lake of Menzala, 44 miles west of Pelusium, and 169 miles east of Alexandria, according to the Antonine Itinerary, and three miles from the Mediterranean, according to the Geograph. Nubiens. Clim. 3, par. 3. There are ruins still remaining to mark the site of Zoan, or Tanis, called San by the Arabs; comprising broken obelisks, capitals of the Corinthian order, a granite monument, etc.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{2} Attend, O Shepherd of Israel, who guidest Joseph like a flock; thou who sittest upon the cherubs, manifest thyself; \textsuperscript{3} before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasse, stir up thy power, and come to deliver us. \textsuperscript{4} Turn us, O God, and cause thy face to shine; and we shall be delivered.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Psalms 79:3 TSK note: Their; , and there etc. Either there was no friend or relation left to bury them, or none was allowed to perform this last sad office. The despotism of eastern princes often proceeds to such a degree of extravagance as to fill the mind with astonishment and horror. In Morocco, no person dares to bury the body of a malefactor without an order from the emperor; and Windus, speaking of a man who was to have been sawn in two, informs us, that "his body must have remained to be eaten by the dogs, if the emperor had not pardoned him."\par
\end{quote}

\noindent \textsuperscript{9} For thou, O Lord, art my hope: thou, my soul, hast made the Most High thy refuge. \textsuperscript{10} No evils shall come upon thee, and no scourge shall draw nigh to thy dwelling. \textsuperscript{11} For he shall give his angels charge concerning thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. \textsuperscript{12} They shall bear thee up on their hands, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone. \textsuperscript{13} Thou shalt tread on the asp and basilisk: and thou shalt trample on the lion and dragon.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Psalms 90:9 TSK note: For passed Heb. turned we spend The Vulgate has, Anni nostri sicut aranea mediatabuntur, "Our years pass away like those of the spider." Our plans and operations are like the spider's web. Life is as frail, and the thread of it as brittle, as one of those which constitute the well-wrought and curious, but fragile habitation of that insect. All the versions have the word spider, but it is not found in any Hebrew manuscripts, or edition yet collated. The Hebrew might be rendered, "We consume our lives with a groan, " kemo hegeh . a tale Heb. a meditation\par
Psalms 90:10 TSK note: The days etc. Heb. As for the days of our years, in them are seventy years, ; yet; for; *marg.\par

\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Psalms 104:17 TSK note: the birds; as for; the stork The stork is a species of the ardea or heron genus, about the size of a goose in its body, but when erect, about three or four feet high; its general colour is white; extremity of the wings, and small part of the head, black; legs, very long, red, and naked a great way up; the toes four, long and connected, with flat nails like those of a man; beak long, jagged, red, and somewhat compressed; the upper and under chaps both of a length, with a furrow from the nostrils. It feeds on serpents, frogs, and insects, on which account it might be deemed unclean; lays four eggs, and sits thirty days; migrates about August, and returns in spring; and is remarkable for its love to its parents, whom it never forsakes, but feeds and cherishes when old; whence it had the name chaseedah, which denotes kindness or piety, and stork, from the Greek στοργη, natural affection.\par
Psalms 104:18 Brenton note: Gr. humbled.\par
Psalms 104:18 Brenton note: Or, his body, see Heb.\par
Psalms 104:18 TSK note: the wild goats The yaal, is the ibex, or rock goat, so called from alah, to ascend, because it is famous for mounting to the tops of the highest rocks. Its general appearance is that of the tame goat, of a dusky brown colour; but the male is larger, with long horns, bending backwards.; the conies\par
Psalms 104:20 TSK note: makest, ;, ; of the forest do creep forth Heb. thereof do trample on the forest\par
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Psalms 107}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Song of a Psalm by David.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Psalms 107:1 TSK note: am 3468, bc 536 (Title), The author of this Psalm is unknown; but it was evidently written to commemorate the return of the Jews from the Babylonian captivity; and it may easily be perceived that it must have been sung in alternate parts, having a double burden, or two intercalary verses often recurring. Bp. Lowth considers it as written "after the method of the ancient pastorals, where, be the subject of their verse what it will, each swain endeavours to excel the other; and one may perceive their thoughts and expressions gradually to rise upon each other." "No doubt, " he adds, "the composition of this Psalm is admirable throughout; and the descriptive part of it adds at least its share of beauty to the whole; but what is most to be admired is its conciseness, and withal the expressiveness of the diction, which strikes the imagination with illimitable elegance. The weary and bewildered traveller - the miserable captive in the dungeon - the sick and dying man - the seaman foundering in a storm - are described in so affecting a manner, that they far exceed anything of the kind, though never so much laboured." Give, ;, ;, good; for his mercy\par
\end{quote}

\noindent \textsuperscript{2} Let now the house of Israel say, that he is good: for his mercy endures for ever. \textsuperscript{3} Let now the house of Aaron say, that he is good: for his mercy endures for ever. \textsuperscript{4} Let now all that fear the Lord say, that he is good: for his mercy endures for ever.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} I called on the Lord out of affliction: and he hearkened to me, so as to bring me into a wide place. \textsuperscript{6} The Lord is my helper; and I will not fear what man shall do to me. \textsuperscript{7} The Lord is my helper; and I shall see my desire upon mine enemies. \textsuperscript{8} It is better to trust in the Lord than to trust in man. \textsuperscript{9} It is better to hope in the Lord, than to hope in princes.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} All nations compassed me about: but in the name of the Lord I repulsed them. \textsuperscript{11} They completely compassed me about: but in the name of the Lord I repulsed them. \textsuperscript{12} They compassed me about as bees do a honeycomb, and they burst into flame as fire among thorns: but in the name of the Lord I repulsed them. \textsuperscript{13} I was thrust, and sorely shaken, that I might fall: but the Lord helped me.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{19} Open to me the gates of righteousness: I will go into them, and give praise to the Lord. \textsuperscript{20} This is the gate of the Lord: the righteous shall enter by it. \textsuperscript{21} I will give thanks to thee; because thou hast heard me, and art become my salvation. \textsuperscript{22} The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner. \textsuperscript{23} This has been done of the Lord; and it is wonderful in our eyes. \textsuperscript{24} This is the day which the Lord has made: let us exult and rejoice in it. \textsuperscript{25} O Lord, save now: O Lord, send now prosperity. \textsuperscript{26} Blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord: we have blessed you out of the house of the Lord.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Render a recompence to thy servant: so shall I live, and keep thy words. \textsuperscript{18} Unveil thou mine eyes, and I shall perceive wondrous things out of thy law. \textsuperscript{19} I am a stranger in the earth: hide not thy commandments from me. \textsuperscript{20} My soul has longed exceedingly for thy judgments at all times. \textsuperscript{21} Thou hast rebuked the proud: cursed are they that turn aside from thy commandments. \textsuperscript{22} Remove from me reproach and contempt; for I have sought out thy testimonies. \textsuperscript{23} For princes sat and spoke against me: but thy servant was meditating on thine ordinances. \textsuperscript{24} For thy testimonies are my meditation, and thine ordinances are my counsellors.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{25} My soul has cleaved to the ground; quicken thou me according to thy word. \textsuperscript{26} I declared my ways, and thou didst hear me; teach me thine ordinances. \textsuperscript{27} Instruct me in the way of thine ordinances; and I will meditate on thy wondrous works. \textsuperscript{28} My soul has slumbered for sorrow; strengthen thou me with thy words. \textsuperscript{29} Remove from me the way of iniquity; and be merciful to me by thy law. \textsuperscript{30} I have chosen the way of truth; and have not forgotten thy judgments. \textsuperscript{31} I have cleaved to thy testimonies, O Lord; put me not to shame. \textsuperscript{32} I ran the way of thy commandments, when thou didst enlarge my heart.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{33} Teach me, O Lord, the way of thine ordinances, and I will seek it out continually. \textsuperscript{34} Instruct me, and I will search out thy law, and will keep it with my whole heart. \textsuperscript{35} Guide me in the path of thy commandments; for I have delighted in it. \textsuperscript{36} Incline mine heart to thy testimonies, and not to covetousness. \textsuperscript{37} Turn away mine eyes that I may not behold vanity: quicken thou me in thy way. \textsuperscript{38} Confirm thine oracle to thy servant, that he may fear thee. \textsuperscript{39} Take away my reproach which I have feared: for thy judgments are good. \textsuperscript{40} Behold, I have desired thy commandments: quicken me in thy righteousness.\par

Psalms 118:33 Brenton note: sc. as a lawgiver.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{41} And let thy mercy come upon me, O Lord; even thy salvation, according to thy word. \textsuperscript{42} And so I shall render an answer to them that reproach me: for I have trusted in thy words. \textsuperscript{43} And take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth; for I have hoped in thy judgments. \textsuperscript{44} So shall I keep thy law continually, for ever and ever. \textsuperscript{45} I walked also at large: for I sought out thy commandments. \textsuperscript{46} And I spoke of thy testimonies before kings, and was not ashamed. \textsuperscript{47} And I meditated on thy commandments, which I loved exceedingly. \textsuperscript{48} And I lifted up my hands to thy commandments which I loved; and I meditated in thine ordinances.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{49} Remember thy words to thy servant, wherein thou hast made me hope. \textsuperscript{50} This has comforted me in mine affliction: for thine oracle has quickened me. \textsuperscript{51} The proud have transgressed exceedingly; but I swerved not from thy law. \textsuperscript{52} I remembered thy judgments of old, O Lord; and was comforted. \textsuperscript{53} Despair took hold upon me, because of the sinners who forsake thy law. \textsuperscript{54} Thine ordinances were my songs in the place of my sojourning. \textsuperscript{55} I remembered thy name, O Lord, in the night, and kept thy law. \textsuperscript{56} This I had, because I diligently sought thine ordinances.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{57} Thou art my portion, O Lord: I said that I would keep thy law. \textsuperscript{58} I besought thy favour with my whole heart: have mercy upon me according to thy word. \textsuperscript{59} I thought on thy ways, and turned my feet to thy testimonies. \textsuperscript{60} I prepared myself, (and was not terrified,) to keep thy commandments. \textsuperscript{61} The snares of sinners entangled me: but I forgot not thy law. \textsuperscript{62} At midnight I arose, to give thanks to thee for the judgments of thy righteousness. \textsuperscript{63} I am a companion of all them that fear thee, and of them that keep thy commandments. \textsuperscript{64} O Lord, the earth is full of thy mercy: teach me thine ordinances.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Psalms 118:58 Brenton note: Gr. presence, or, countenance.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{65} Thou hast wrought kindly with thy servant, O Lord, according to thy word. \textsuperscript{66} Teach me kindness, and instruction, and knowledge: for I have believed thy commandments. \textsuperscript{67} Before I was afflicted, I transgressed; therefore have I kept thy word. \textsuperscript{68} Good art thou, O Lord; therefore in thy goodness teach me thine ordinances. \textsuperscript{69} The injustice of the proud has been multiplied against me: but I will search out thy commandments with all my heart. \textsuperscript{70} Their heart has been curdled like milk; but I have meditated on thy law. \textsuperscript{71} It is good for me that thou hast afflicted me; that I might learn thine ordinances. \textsuperscript{72} The law of thy mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{73} Thy hands have made me, and fashioned me: instruct me, that I may learn thy commandments. \textsuperscript{74} They that fear thee will see me and rejoice: for I have hoped in thy words. \textsuperscript{75} I know, O Lord, that thy judgments are righteousness, and that thou in truthfulness hast afflicted me. \textsuperscript{76} Let, I pray thee, thy mercy be to comfort me, according to thy word to thy servant. \textsuperscript{77} Let thy compassions come to me, that I may live: for thy law is my meditation. \textsuperscript{78} Let the proud be ashamed; for they transgressed against me unjustly: but I will meditate in thy commandments. \textsuperscript{79} Let those that fear thee, and those that know thy testimonies, turn to me. \textsuperscript{80} Let mine heart be blameless in thine ordinances, that I may not be ashamed.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{81} My soul faints for thy salvation: I have hoped in thy words. \textsuperscript{82} Mine eyes failed in waiting for thy word, saying, When wilt thou comfort me? \textsuperscript{83} For I am become as a bottle in the frost: yet I have not forgotten thine ordinances. \textsuperscript{84} How many are the days of thy servant? when wilt thou execute judgment for me on them that persecute me? \textsuperscript{85} Transgressors told me idle tales ; but not according to thy law, O Lord. \textsuperscript{86} All thy commandments are truth; they persecuted me unjustly; help thou me. \textsuperscript{87} They nearly made an end of me in the earth; but I forsook not thy commandments. \textsuperscript{88} Quicken me according to thy mercy; so shall I keep the testimonies of thy mouth.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{89} Thy word, O Lord, abides in heaven for ever. \textsuperscript{90} Thy truth endures to all generations; thou hast founded the earth, and it abides. \textsuperscript{91} The day continues by thy arrangement; for all things are thy servants. \textsuperscript{92} Were it not that thy law is my meditation, then I should have perished in mine affliction. \textsuperscript{93} I will never forget thine ordinances; for with them thou hast quickened me. \textsuperscript{94} I am thine, save me; for I have sought out thine ordinances. \textsuperscript{95} Sinners laid wait for me to destroy me; but I understood thy testimonies. \textsuperscript{96} I have seen an end of all perfection; but thy commandment is very broad.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{97} How I have loved thy law, O Lord! it is my meditation all the day. \textsuperscript{98} Thou hast made me wiser than mine enemies in thy commandment; for it is mine for ever. \textsuperscript{99} I have more understanding than all my teachers; for thy testimonies are my meditation. \textsuperscript{100} I understand more than the aged; because I have sought out thy commandments. \textsuperscript{101} I have kept back my feet from every evil way, that I might keep thy words. \textsuperscript{102} I have not declined from thy judgments; for thou hast instructed me.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Psalms 118:102 Brenton note: That is, as a lawgiver.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{103} How sweet are thine oracles to my throat! more so than honey to my mouth! \textsuperscript{104} I gain understanding by thy commandments: therefore I have hated every way of unrighteousness.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{105} Thy law is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths. \textsuperscript{106} I have sworn and determined to keep the judgments of thy righteousness. \textsuperscript{107} I have been very greatly afflicted, O Lord: quicken me, according to thy word. \textsuperscript{108} Accept, I pray thee, O Lord, the freewill-offerings of my mouth, and teach me thy judgments. \textsuperscript{109} My soul is continually in thine hands; and I have not forgotten thy law. \textsuperscript{110} Sinners spread a snare for me; but I erred not from thy commandments. \textsuperscript{111} I have inherited thy testimonies for ever; for they are the joy of my heart. \textsuperscript{112} I have inclined my heart to perform thine ordinances for ever, in return for thy mercies .\par

Psalms 118:112 Brenton note: See Heb.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{113} I have hated transgressors; but I have loved thy law. \textsuperscript{114} Thou art my helper and my supporter; I have hoped in thy words. \textsuperscript{115} Depart from me, ye evil-doers; for I will search out the commandments of my God. \textsuperscript{116} Uphold me according to thy word, and quicken me; and make me not ashamed of my expectation. \textsuperscript{117} Help me, and I shall be saved; and I will meditate in thine ordinances continually. \textsuperscript{118} Thou hast brought to nought all that depart from thine ordinances; for their inward thought is unrighteous. \textsuperscript{119} I have reckoned all the sinners of the earth as transgressors; therefore have I loved thy testimonies. \textsuperscript{120} Penetrate my flesh with thy fear; for I am afraid of thy judgments.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{121} I have done judgment and justice; deliver me not up to them that injure me. \textsuperscript{122} Receive thy servant for good: let not the proud accuse me falsely. \textsuperscript{123} Mine eyes have failed for thy salvation, and for the word of thy righteousness. \textsuperscript{124} Deal with thy servant according to thy mercy, and teach me thine ordinances. \textsuperscript{125} I am thy servant; instruct me, and I shall know thy testimonies. \textsuperscript{126} It is time for the Lord to work: they have utterly broken thy law. \textsuperscript{127} Therefore have I loved thy commandments more than gold, or the topaz. \textsuperscript{128} Therefore I directed myself according to all thy commandments: I have hated every unjust way.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{129} Thy testimonies are wonderful: therefore my soul has sought them out. \textsuperscript{130} The manifestation of thy words will enlighten, and instruct the simple. \textsuperscript{131} I opened my mouth, and drew breath: for I earnestly longed after thy commandments. \textsuperscript{132} Look upon me and have mercy upon me, after the manner of them that love thy name. \textsuperscript{133} Order my steps according to thy word: and let not any iniquity have dominion over me. \textsuperscript{134} Deliver me from the false accusation of men: so will I keep thy commandments. \textsuperscript{135} Cause thy face to shine upon thy servant: and teach me thine ordinances. \textsuperscript{136} Mine eyes have been bathed in streams of water, because I kept not thy law.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{137} Righteous art thou, O Lord, and upright are thy judgments. \textsuperscript{138} Thou hast commanded righteousness and perfect truth, as thy testimonies. \textsuperscript{139} Thy zeal has quite wasted me: because mine enemies have forgotten thy words. \textsuperscript{140} Thy word has been very fully tried; and thy servant loves it. \textsuperscript{141} I am young and despised: yet I have not forgotten thine ordinances. \textsuperscript{142} Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is truth. \textsuperscript{143} Afflictions and distresses found me: but thy commandments were my meditation. \textsuperscript{144} Thy testimonies are an everlasting righteousness: instruct me, and I shall live.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{145} I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O Lord: I will search out thine ordinances. \textsuperscript{146} I cried to thee; save me, and I will keep thy testimonies. \textsuperscript{147} I arose before the dawn, and cried: I hoped in thy words. \textsuperscript{148} Mine eyes prevented the dawn, that I might meditate on thine oracles. \textsuperscript{149} Hear my voice, O Lord, according to thy mercy; quicken me according to thy judgment. \textsuperscript{150} They have drawn nigh who persecuted me unlawfully; and they are far removed from thy law. \textsuperscript{151} Thou art near, O Lord; and all thy ways are truth. \textsuperscript{152} I have known of old concerning thy testimonies, that thou hast founded them for ever.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Psalms 118:151 Brenton note: Alex. ἐντολαί, commands.\par
Psalms 118:152 Brenton note: Gr. of.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{153} Look upon mine affliction, and rescue me; for I have not forgotten thy law. \textsuperscript{154} Plead my cause, and ransom me: quicken me because of thy word. \textsuperscript{155} Salvation is far from sinners: for they have not searched out thine ordinances. \textsuperscript{156} Thy mercies, O Lord, are many: quicken me according to thy judgment. \textsuperscript{157} Many are they that persecute me and oppress me: but I have not declined from thy testimonies. \textsuperscript{158} I beheld men acting foolishly, and I pined away; for they kept not thine oracles. \textsuperscript{159} Behold, I have loved thy commandments, O Lord: quicken me in thy mercy. \textsuperscript{160} The beginning of thy words is truth; and all the judgments of thy righteousness endure for ever.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{161} Princes persecuted me without a cause, but my heart feared because of thy words. \textsuperscript{162} I will exult because of thine oracles, as one that finds much spoil. \textsuperscript{163} I hate and abhor unrighteousness; but I love thy law. \textsuperscript{164} Seven times in a day have I praised thee because of the judgments of thy righteousness. \textsuperscript{165} Great peace have they that love thy law: and there is no stumbling-block to them. \textsuperscript{166} I waited for thy salvation, O Lord, and have loved thy commandments. \textsuperscript{167} My soul has kept thy testimonies, and loved them exceedingly. \textsuperscript{168} I have kept thy commandments and thy testimonies; for all my ways are before thee, O Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{169} Let my supplication come near before thee, O Lord; instruct me according to thine oracle. \textsuperscript{170} Let my petition come in before thee, O Lord; deliver me according to thine oracle. \textsuperscript{171} Let my lips utter a hymn, when thou shalt have taught me thine ordinances. \textsuperscript{172} Let my tongue utter thine oracles; for all thy commandments are righteous. \textsuperscript{173} Let thine hand be prompt to save me; for I have chosen thy commandments. \textsuperscript{174} I have longed after thy salvation, O Lord; and thy law is my meditation. \textsuperscript{175} My soul shall live, and shall praise thee; and thy judgments shall help me. \textsuperscript{176} I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek thy servant; for I have not forgotten thy commandments.\par

Psalms 119:1 TSK note: am 3560, bc 444 (Title), This Psalm, which was probably composed by Ezra, is another of the alphabetical Psalms. It consists of twenty-two parts, answering to the number of the Hebrew letters; every part being divided into eight verses, and each verse beginning with that letter which forms the title of the part; that is, the first part of eight verses with ΰ, the second with α, etc. It is an elegant, important, and useful composition; the chief subjects of which are the excellence of God's laws, and the happiness of those who observe them. Psalms 136:7 Brenton note: Gr. empty, empty.\par
Psalms 136:8 TSK note: The sun; to rule Heb. for the rulings\par
Psalms 136:9 TSK note: The moon and stars The sun is the monarch of day, the state of light; the moon of the night, the state of darkness. The rays of the sun falling on the atmosphere, are refracted and diffused over the whole of the hemisphere of the earth immediately under his orb; while those rays of that vast luminary which, because of the earth's smallness in comparison with the sun, are diffused on all sides beyond the earth, falling on the opaque disc of the moon, are reflected back on the lower hemisphere, or the part of the earth opposite the sun. But the reflected light being 50, 000 times less in intensity than that of the sun, there is a sufficient distinction between day and night, though each is ruled and determined by one of these two great lights.\par
\end{quote}

The Lord looses the fettered ones: \textsuperscript{8} the Lord gives wisdom to the blind:\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{2} For he has strengthened the bars of thy gates; he has blessed thy children within thee. \textsuperscript{3} He makes thy borders peaceful, and fills thee with the flour of wheat. \textsuperscript{4} He sends his oracle to the earth: his word will run swiftly. \textsuperscript{5} He gives snow like wool: he scatters the mist like ashes. \textsuperscript{6} Casting forth his ice like morsels: who shall stand before his cold? \textsuperscript{7} He shall send out his word, and melt them: he shall blow with his wind, and the waters shall flow. \textsuperscript{8} He sends his word to Jacob, his ordinances and judgments to Israel. \textsuperscript{9} He has not done so to any other nation; and he has not shewn them his judgments.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{2} Praise ye him, all his angels: praise ye him, all his hosts. \textsuperscript{3} Praise him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars and light. \textsuperscript{4} Praise him, ye heavens of heavens, and the water that is above the heavens. \textsuperscript{5} Let them praise the name of the Lord: for he spoke, and they were made; he commanded, and they were created. \textsuperscript{6} He has established them for ever, even for ever and ever: he has made an ordinance, and it shall not pass away.\par

\subsection*{Psalms 151}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} This Psalm is a genuine one of David, though supernumerary, composed when he fought in single combat with Goliad.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Psalms 151:1 Brenton note: Alex. Goliath.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} My hands formed a musical instrument, and my fingers tuned a psaltery. \textsuperscript{3} And who shall tell my Lord? the Lord himself, he himself hears. \textsuperscript{4} He sent forth his angel, and took me from my father's sheep, and he anointed me with the oil of his anointing. \textsuperscript{5} My brothers were handsome and tall; but the Lord did not take pleasure in them. \textsuperscript{6} I went forth to meet the Philistine; and he cursed me by his idols. \textsuperscript{7} But I drew his own sword, and beheaded him, and removed reproach from the children of Israel.\par
\section*{Proverbs}
\subsection*{Proverbs 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} The Proverbs of Solomon son of David, who reigned in Israel; \textsuperscript{2} to know wisdom and instruction, and to perceive words of understanding; \textsuperscript{3} to receive also hard sayings, and to understand true justice, and how to direct judgment; \textsuperscript{4} that he might give subtlety to the simple, and to the young man discernment and understanding. \textsuperscript{5} For by the hearing of these a wise man will be wiser, and the man of understanding will gain direction; \textsuperscript{6} and will understand a parable, and a dark speech; the sayings of the wise also, and riddles.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 1:3 Brenton note: Gr. turnings, q. d. knotty words. See Heb.\par
Proverbs 1:4 Brenton note: Or, discretion.\par
Proverbs 1:4 TSK note: subtlety, ;, ; to the, ;, ;, ; discretion or, advisement\par
Proverbs 1:6 TSK note: a proverb, ;, ; the interpretation or, an eloquent speech. the words dark\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; and there is good understanding to all that practise it: and piety toward God is the beginning of discernment; but the ungodly will set at nought wisdom and instruction. \textsuperscript{8} Hear, my son, the instruction of thy father, and reject not the rules of thy mother. \textsuperscript{9} For thou shalt receive for thine head a crown of graces, and a chain of gold round thy neck.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 1:7 Brenton note: Or, sum, or, top.\par
Proverbs 1:7 TSK note: fear; , ; beginning or, principal part but\par
Proverbs 1:9 TSK note: they, ; an ornament Heb. an adding\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} My son, let not ungodly men lead thee astray, neither consent thou to them . \textsuperscript{11} If they should exhort thee, saying, Come with us, partake in blood, and let us unjustly hide the just man in the earth: \textsuperscript{12} and let us swallow him alive, as Hades would , and remove the memorial of him from the earth: \textsuperscript{13} let us seize on his valuable property, and let us fill our houses with spoils: \textsuperscript{14} but do thou cast in thy lot with us, and let us all provide a common purse, and let us have one pouch: \textsuperscript{15} go not in the way with them, but turn aside thy foot from their paths: \textsuperscript{17} for nets are not without cause spread for birds. \textsuperscript{18} For they that are concerned in murder store up evils for themselves; and the overthrow of transgressors is evil. \textsuperscript{19} These are the ways of all that perform lawless deeds; for by ungodliness they destroy their own life.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 1:11 TSK note: let us lay, ;, ; , let us lurk\par
Proverbs 1:15 Brenton note: For ver 16, see Appendix.\par
Proverbs 1:17 TSK note: in vain; sight of any bird Heb. eyes of everything that hath a wing\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} Wisdom sings aloud in passages, and in the broad places speaks boldly. \textsuperscript{21} And she makes proclamation on the top of the walls, and sits by the gates of princes; and at the gates of the city boldly says, \textsuperscript{22} So long as the simple cleave to justice, they shall not be ashamed: but the foolish being lovers of haughtiness, having become ungodly have hated knowledge, and are become subject to reproofs. \textsuperscript{23} Behold, I will bring forth to you the utterance of my breath, and I will instruct you in my speech.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 1:20 TSK note: Wisdom Heb. Wisdoms, that is, excellent wisdom, ; , ; crieth\par
Proverbs 1:22 TSK note: How;, ; ye simple, ; , ; the scorners, ; fools\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} Since I called, and ye did not hearken; and I spoke at length, and ye gave no heed; \textsuperscript{25} but ye set at nought my counsels, and disregarded my reproofs; \textsuperscript{26} therefore I also will laugh at your destruction; and I will rejoice against you when ruin comes upon you: \textsuperscript{27} yea when dismay suddenly comes upon you, and your overthrow shall arrive like a tempest; and when tribulation and distress shall come upon you, or when ruin shall come upon you. \textsuperscript{28} For it shall be that when ye call upon me, I will not hearken to you: wicked men shall seek me, but shall not find me . \textsuperscript{29} For they hated wisdom, and did not choose the word of the Lord: \textsuperscript{30} neither would they attend to my counsels, but derided my reproofs. \textsuperscript{31} Therefore shall they eat the fruits of their own way, and shall be filled with their own ungodliness. \textsuperscript{32} For because they wronged the simple, they shall be slain; and an inquisition shall ruin the ungodly. \textsuperscript{33} But he that hearkens to me shall dwell in confidence, and shall rest securely from all evil.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 1:27 TSK note: your fear, ; , ; as a; distress\par
Proverbs 1:28 TSK note: shall they;, ; , ; , ; they shall seek\par
Proverbs 1:32 TSK note: the turning; , and the;, ;, ; prosperity or, ease\par
Proverbs 1:33 Brenton note: Gr. hope. See Ps. 16.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} My son, if thou wilt receive the utterance of my commandment, and hide it with thee; \textsuperscript{2} thine ear shall hearken to wisdom; thou shalt also apply thine heart to understanding, and shalt apply it to the instruction of thy son.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} For if thou shalt call to wisdom, and utter thy voice for understanding; \textsuperscript{4} and if thou shalt seek it as silver, and search diligently for it as for treasures; \textsuperscript{5} then shalt thou understand the fear of the Lord, and find the knowledge of God.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 2:3 TSK note: if, ; , ; liftest up thy voice Heb. givest thy voice\par
Proverbs 2:5 Brenton note: Greek background: epignōsis (ἐπίγνωσις) = full knowledge; recognition. Common English renderings: knowledge. Often denotes fuller or more exact knowledge.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} For the Lord gives wisdom; and from his presence come knowledge and understanding, \textsuperscript{7} and he treasures up salvation for them that walk uprightly: he will protect their way; \textsuperscript{8} that he may guard the righteous ways: and he will preserve the way of them that fear him. \textsuperscript{9} Then shalt thou understand righteousness, and judgment; and shalt direct all thy course aright.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 2:9 Brenton note: Lit. all good a les.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} For if wisdom shall come into thine understanding, and discernment shall seem pleasing to thy soul, \textsuperscript{11} good counsel shall guard thee, and holy understanding shall keep thee; \textsuperscript{12} to deliver thee from the evil way, and from the man that speaks nothing faithfully.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 2:10 Brenton note: Greek background: nous (νοῦς) = mind; understanding. Common English renderings: mind. A term for mind, perception, or understanding.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Alas for those who forsake right paths, to walk in ways of darkness; \textsuperscript{14} who rejoice in evils, and delight in wicked perverseness; \textsuperscript{15} whose paths are crooked, and their courses winding; \textsuperscript{16} to remove thee far from the straight way, and to estrange thee from a righteous purpose. My son, let not evil counsel overtake thee, \textsuperscript{17} of her who has forsaken the instruction of her youth, and forgotten the covenant of God. \textsuperscript{18} For she has fixed her house near death, and guided her wheels near Hades with the giants. \textsuperscript{19} None that go by her shall return, neither shall they take hold of right paths, for they are not apprehended of the years of life. \textsuperscript{20} For had they gone in good paths, they would have found the paths of righteousness easy. \textsuperscript{21} For the upright shall dwell in the earth, and the holy shall be left behind in it. \textsuperscript{22} The paths of the ungodly shall perish out of the earth, and transgressors shall be driven away from it.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 2:15 Brenton note: Lit. wheel tracks. Compare Heb. 12. 13.\par
Proverbs 2:18 Brenton note: See Heb.\par
Proverbs 2:19 Brenton note: Singular variation from Heb.\par
Proverbs 2:20 Brenton note: Gr. smooth.\par
Proverbs 2:22 TSK note: the wicked;, ;, ; rooted or, plucked up, *marg.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} My son, forget not my laws; but let thine heart keep my words: \textsuperscript{2} for length of existence, and years of life, and peace, shall they add to thee. \textsuperscript{3} Let not mercy and truth forsake thee; but bind them about thy neck: \textsuperscript{4} so shalt thou find favour: and do thou provide things honest in the sight of the Lord, and of men.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 3:2 TSK note: length, ; , ; long life Heb. years of life, and peace\par
Proverbs 3:4 Brenton note: Alex. + 'and write them on the table of thine heart.'\par
Proverbs 3:4 Brenton note: See Rom. 12. 17.\par
Proverbs 3:4 TSK note: shalt, ; good understanding or, good success, *marg.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Trust in God with all thine heart; and be not exalted in thine own wisdom. \textsuperscript{6} In all thy ways acquaint thyself with her, that she may rightly direct thy paths. \textsuperscript{7} Be not wise in thine own conceit; but fear God, and depart from all evil. \textsuperscript{8} Then shall there be health to thy body, and good keeping to thy bones.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 3:6 Brenton note: Gr. divide. See 2 Tim 2. 13.\par
Proverbs 3:8 Brenton note: Hebrew background: marpe (מַרְפֵּא) = healing; remedy. Common English renderings: health; healing. Noun for healing or cure.\par
Proverbs 3:8 TSK note: shall, ; health Heb. medicine thy marrow Heb. watering, or moistening\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Honour the Lord with thy just labours, and give him the first of thy fruits of righteousness: \textsuperscript{10} that thy storehouses may be completely filled with corn, and that thy presses may burst forth with wine.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; nor faint when thou art rebuked of him: \textsuperscript{12} for whom the Lord loves, he rebukes, and scourges every son whom he receives.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Blessed is the man who has found wisdom, and the mortal who knows prudence. \textsuperscript{14} For it is better to traffic for her, than for treasures of gold and silver. \textsuperscript{15} And she is more valuable than precious stones: no evil thing shall resist her: she is well known to all that approach her, and no precious thing is equal to her in value. \textsuperscript{16} For length of existence and years of life are in her right hand; and in her left hand are wealth and glory: \textsuperscript{17} Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are peaceful. \textsuperscript{18} She is a tree of life to all that lay hold upon her; and she is a secure help to all that stay themselves on her, as on the Lord.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 3:13 TSK note: is the, ;, ; getteth Heb. draweth out\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} God by wisdom founded the earth, and by prudence he prepared the heavens. \textsuperscript{20} By understanding were the depths broken up, and the clouds dropped water.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} My son, let them not pass from thee , but keep my counsel and understanding: \textsuperscript{22} that thy soul may live, and that there may be grace round thy neck; \textsuperscript{23} that thou mayest go confidently in peace in all thy ways, and that thy foot may not stumble. \textsuperscript{24} For if thou rest, thou shalt be undismayed; and if thou sleep, thou shalt slumber sweetly. \textsuperscript{25} And thou shalt not be afraid of alarm coming upon thee, neither of approaching attacks of ungodly men. \textsuperscript{26} For the Lord shall be over all thy ways, and shall establish thy foot that thou be not moved.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 3:21 Brenton note: See Heb. 2. 1.\par
Proverbs 3:24 Brenton note: Gr. sit down.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} Forbear not to do good to the poor, whensoever thy hand may have power to help him . \textsuperscript{28} Say not, Come back another time, to-morrow I will give; while thou art able to do him good: for thou knowest not what the next day will bring forth. \textsuperscript{29} Devise not evil against thy friend, living near thee and trusting in thee.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 3:27 TSK note: Withhold; , them to whom it is due Heb. the owners thereof in the\par
Proverbs 3:29 TSK note: Devise not evil or, Practise no evil\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} Be not ready to quarrel with a man without a cause, lest he do thee some harm.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{31} Procure not the reproaches of bad men, neither do thou covet their ways. \textsuperscript{32} For every transgressor is unclean before the Lord; neither does he sit among the righteous. \textsuperscript{33} The curse of God is in the houses of the ungodly; but the habitations of the just are blessed. \textsuperscript{34} The Lord resists the proud; but he gives grace to the humble. \textsuperscript{35} The wise shall inherit glory; but the ungodly have exalted their own dishonour.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 3:31 TSK note: Envy, ;, ; the oppressor Heb. a man of violence, choose\par
Proverbs 3:34 Brenton note: See 1 Pet. 5. 5.\par
Proverbs 3:35 TSK note: wise; but; shall be the promotion of fools Heb. exalteth the fools\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know understanding. \textsuperscript{2} For I give you a good gift; forsake ye not my law. \textsuperscript{3} For I also was a son obedient to my father, and loved in the sight of my mother: \textsuperscript{4} who spoke and instructed me, saying , Let our speech be fixed in thine heart, keep our commandments, forget them not: \textsuperscript{5} and do not neglect the speech of my mouth. \textsuperscript{6} And forsake it not, and it shall cleave to thee: love it, and it shall keep thee. \textsuperscript{8} Secure it, and it shall exalt thee: honour it, that it may embrace thee; \textsuperscript{9} that it may give unto thy head a crown of graces, and may cover thee with a crown of delight.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 4:5 Brenton note: See Appendix - Alexandrian codex has: “Get wisdom, get understanding, forget not, nor decline from the words of my mouth.”\par
Proverbs 4:8 Brenton note: Lit. dig a trench about her, see Heb.\par
Proverbs 4:9 TSK note: give, ; a crown etc. or, she shall compass thee with a crown of glory\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} Hear, my son, and receive my words; and the years of thy life shall be increased, that the resources of thy life may be many. \textsuperscript{11} For I teach thee the ways of wisdom; and I cause thee to go in right paths. \textsuperscript{12} For when thou goest, thy steps shall not be straitened; and when thou runnest, thou shalt not be distressed. \textsuperscript{13} Take hold of my instruction; let it not go,—but keep it for thyself for thy life.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 4:11 Brenton note: Gr. wheel-tracks, see chap 2. 18; Heb. 12. 13.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} Go not in the ways of the ungodly, neither covet the ways of transgressors. \textsuperscript{15} In whatever place they shall pitch their camp, go not thither; but turn from them, and pass away. \textsuperscript{16} For they cannot sleep, unless they have done evil: their sleep is taken away, and they rest not. \textsuperscript{17} For these live upon the bread of ungodliness, and are drunken with wine of transgression. \textsuperscript{18} But the ways of the righteous shine like light; they go on and shine, until the day be fully come. \textsuperscript{19} But the ways of the ungodly are dark; they know not how they stumble.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 4:18 Brenton note: Gr. order itself aright.\par
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Proverbs 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} My son, attend to my wisdom, and apply thine ear to my words; \textsuperscript{2} that thou mayest keep good understanding, and the discretion of my lips gives thee a charge.\par

\subsection*{Proverbs 6}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} My son, if thou become surety for thy friend, thou shalt deliver thine hand to an enemy. \textsuperscript{2} For a man's own lips become a strong snare to him, and he is caught with the lips of his own mouth. \textsuperscript{3} My son, do what I command thee, and deliver thyself; for on thy friend's account thou art come into the power of evil men : faint not, but stir up even thy friend for whom thou art become surety. \textsuperscript{4} Give not sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber with thine eyelids; \textsuperscript{5} that thou mayest deliver thyself as a doe out of the toils, and as a bird out of a snare.\par

Proverbs 6:1 TSK note: if thou be, ;, ; thou hast To strike, or join hands, was an ancient form of entering into contracts in all counties and all ages.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{6} Go to the ant, O sluggard; and see, and emulate his ways, and become wiser than he. \textsuperscript{7} For whereas he has no husbandry, nor any one to compel him, and is under no master, \textsuperscript{8} he prepares food for himself in the summer, and lays by abundant store in harvest. \textsuperscript{9} How long wilt thou lie, O sluggard? and when wilt thou awake out of sleep? \textsuperscript{10} Thou sleepest a little, and thou restest a little, and thou slumberest a short time , and thou foldest thine arms over thy breast a little. \textsuperscript{11} Then poverty comes upon thee as an evil traveller, and want as a swift courier:\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 6:6 TSK note: the ant The ant has been famous in all ages for its social habits, foresight, economy and industry. Collecting their food at the proper seasons, they bite off the ends of the grain to prevent it from germinating, and lay it up in cells till needed.; thou\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} A foolish man and a transgressor goes in ways that are not good. \textsuperscript{13} And the same winks with the eye, and makes a sign with his foot, and teaches with the beckonings of his fingers. \textsuperscript{14} His perverse heart devises evils: at all times such a one causes troubles to a city. \textsuperscript{15} Therefore his destruction shall come suddenly; overthrow and irretrievable ruin.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{16} For he rejoices in all things which God hates, and he is ruined by reason of impurity of soul. \textsuperscript{17} The eye of the haughty, a tongue unjust, hands shedding the blood of the just; \textsuperscript{18} and a heart devising evil thoughts, and feet hastening to do evil,— are hateful to God . \textsuperscript{19} An unjust witness kindles falsehoods, and brings on quarrels between brethren.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{20} My son, keep the laws of thy father, and reject not the ordinances of thy mother: \textsuperscript{21} but bind them upon thy soul continually, and hang them as a chain about thy neck. \textsuperscript{22} Whensoever thou walkest, lead this along and let it be with thee; and when thou sleepest let it keep thee; that it may talk with thee when thou wakest. \textsuperscript{23} For the commandment of the law is a lamp and a light; a way of life; reproof also and correction: \textsuperscript{24} to keep thee continually from a married woman, and from the calumny of a strange tongue.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{25} Let not the desire of beauty overcome thee, neither be thou caught by thine eyes, neither be captivated with her eyelids. \textsuperscript{26} For the value of a harlot is as much as of one loaf; and a woman hunts for the precious souls of men. \textsuperscript{27} Shall any one bind fire in his bosom, and not burn his garments? \textsuperscript{28} or will any one walk on coals of fire, and not burn his feet? \textsuperscript{29} So is he that goes in to a married woman; he shall not be held guiltless, neither any one that touches her. \textsuperscript{30} It is not to be wondered at if one should be taken stealing, for he steals that when hungry he may satisfy his soul: \textsuperscript{31} but if he should be taken, he shall repay sevenfold, and shall deliver himself by giving all his goods. \textsuperscript{32} But the adulterer through want of sense procures destruction to his soul. \textsuperscript{33} He endures both pain and disgrace, and his reproach shall never be wiped off. \textsuperscript{34} For the soul of her husband is full of jealousy: he will not spare in the day of vengeance. \textsuperscript{35} He will not forego his enmity for any ransom: neither will he be reconciled for many gifts.\par

\subsection*{Proverbs 7}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} My son, keep my words, and hide with thee my commandments. \textsuperscript{2} keep my commandments, and thou shalt live; and keep my words as the pupils of thine eyes. \textsuperscript{3} And bind them on thy fingers, and write them on the table of thine heart.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 7:2 TSK note: Keep; , ; as the As the pupil of the eye, the hole or the opening of the uveous coat, or iris, through which the rays of light pass, and falling upon the retina, there depict every object in its natural colour, as upon a piece of white paper. Now the pupil of the eye being essentially necessary to sight, and easily injured, it is not only, in common with the other parts, deeply entrenched in the skull, ramparted with the forehead and cheek bones, defended by the eyebrows, eyelids, and eyelashes, and placed so as to be best protected by the hands, but, by a wonderful mechanism, is contracted or dilated by the muscular power of the iris, without which an excess of light would cause instant blindness.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Say that wisdom is thy sister, and gain prudence as an acquaintance for thyself; \textsuperscript{5} that she may keep thee from the strange and wicked woman, if she should assail thee with flattering words.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} For she looks from a window out of her house into the streets, at one whom she may see of the senseless ones, a young man void of understanding, \textsuperscript{7} passing by the corner in the passages near her house, \textsuperscript{8} and speaking, in the dark of the evening, \textsuperscript{9} when there happens to be the stillness of night and of darkness: \textsuperscript{10} and the woman meets him having the appearance of a harlot, that causes the hearts of young men to flutter. \textsuperscript{11} And she is fickle, and debauched, and her feet abide not at home. \textsuperscript{12} For at one time she wanders without, and at another time she lies in wait in the streets, at every corner. \textsuperscript{13} Then she caught him, and kissed him, and with an impudent face said to him, \textsuperscript{14} I have a peace-offering; to-day I pay my vows: \textsuperscript{15} therefore I came forth to meet thee, desiring thy face; and I have found thee. \textsuperscript{16} I have spread my bed with sheets, and I have covered it with double tapestry from Egypt. \textsuperscript{17} I have sprinkled my couch with saffron, and my house with cinnamon. \textsuperscript{18} Come, and let us enjoy love until the morning; come, and let us embrace in love. \textsuperscript{19} For my husband is not at home, but is gone on a long journey, \textsuperscript{20} having taken in his hand a bundle of money: after many days he will return to his house.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 7:6 TSK note: at the; casement Eshnav, rather a lattice, so called from the Arabic shanaba, " to be cool, " because of its use in keeping the apartments cool.\par
Proverbs 7:7 Brenton note: Gr. of.\par
Proverbs 7:7 TSK note: the simple, ;, ; the youths Heb. the sons void\par
Proverbs 7:9 TSK note: the twilight; evening Heb. evening of the day, *marg.\par
Proverbs 7:13 TSK note: she, ;, ; with an impudent face said Heb. she strengthened her face and said\par
Proverbs 7:14 TSK note: I have peace offerings with me Heb. Peace-offerings are upon me, ; this\par

\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} So with much converse she prevailed on him to go astray, and with the snares of her lips she forced him from the right path . \textsuperscript{22} And he followed her, being gently led on, and that as an ox is led to the slaughter, and as a dog to bonds, or as a hart shot in the liver with an arrow: \textsuperscript{23} and he hastens as a bird into a snare, not knowing that he is running for his life.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 7:22 TSK note: straightway Heb. suddenly as an as a Dr. Grey, making a slight alteration in the text, renders, "as a dog to the chain, and as a deer, till a dart strike through his liver; " and Dr. Hunt, "Or as a hart boundeth into the toils, till a dart strike through his liver." The LXX, Chaldee, Syriac, and Arabic, concur in this interpretation. The circumstance of the dart, as applied to the deer, is beautiful and proper, which otherwise we are at a loss to dispose of; and this creature, of all others, was the most proper to be noticed on this occasion; for the usual representation which the Egyptians made of a man overthrown by flattery and fair speeches was the picture of a heart captivated and ensnared by the sound of music. the correction\par
Proverbs 7:23 TSK note: a dart as a bird; knoweth\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} Now then, my son, hearken to me, and attend to the words of my mouth. \textsuperscript{25} Let not thine heart turn aside to her ways: \textsuperscript{26} for she has wounded and cast down many, and those whom she has slain are innumerable. \textsuperscript{27} Her house is the way of hell, leading down to the chambers of death.\par

\subsection*{Proverbs 8}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Thou shalt proclaim wisdom, that understanding may be obedient to thee. \textsuperscript{2} For she is on lofty eminences, and stands in the midst of the ways. \textsuperscript{3} For she sits by the gates of princes, and sings in the entrances, saying , \textsuperscript{4} You, O men, I exhort; and utter my voice to the sons of men. \textsuperscript{5} O ye simple, understand subtlety, and ye that are untaught, imbibe knowledge. \textsuperscript{6} Hearken to me; for I will speak solemn truths ; and will produce right sayings from my lips. \textsuperscript{7} For my throat shall meditate truth; and false lips are an abomination before me. \textsuperscript{8} All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing in them wrong or perverse. \textsuperscript{9} They are all evident to those that understand, and right to those that find knowledge. \textsuperscript{10} Receive instruction, and not silver; and knowledge rather than tried gold. \textsuperscript{11} For wisdom is better than precious stones; and no valuable substance is of equal worth with it.\par

\end{quote}

\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Wealth and glory belong to me; yea, abundant possessions and righteousness. \textsuperscript{19} It is better to have my fruit than to have gold and precious stones; and my produce is better than choice silver. \textsuperscript{20} I walk in ways of righteousness, and am conversant with the paths of judgment; \textsuperscript{21} that I may divide substance to them that love me, and may fill their treasures with good things.\par

\subsection*{Proverbs 9}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Wisdom has built a house for herself, and set up seven pillars. \textsuperscript{2} She has killed her beasts; she has mingled her wine in a bowl, and prepared her table. \textsuperscript{3} She has sent forth her servants, calling with a loud proclamation to the feast, saying, \textsuperscript{4} Whoso is foolish, let him turn aside to me: and to them that want understanding she says, \textsuperscript{5} Come, eat of my bread, and drink wine which I have mingled for you.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{1} A wise son makes his father glad: but a foolish son is a grief to his mother. \textsuperscript{2} Treasures shall not profit the lawless: but righteousness shall deliver from death. \textsuperscript{3} The Lord will not famish a righteous soul: but he will overthrow the life of the ungodly.\par
