\noindent \textsuperscript{6} The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the just: but untimely grief shall cover the mouth of the ungodly. \textsuperscript{7} The memory of the just is praised; but the name of the ungodly man is extinguished. \textsuperscript{8} A wise man in heart will receive commandments; but he that is unguarded in his lips shall be overthrown in his perverseness. \textsuperscript{9} He that walks simply, walks confidently; but he that perverts his ways shall be known. \textsuperscript{10} He that winks with his eyes deceitfully, procures griefs for men; but he that reproves boldly is a peacemaker. \textsuperscript{11} There is a fountain of life in the hand of a righteous man; but destruction shall cover the mouth of the ungodly.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{12} Hatred stirs up strife; but affection covers all that do not love strife. \textsuperscript{13} He that brings forth wisdom from his lips smites the fool with a rod. \textsuperscript{14} The wise will hide discretion; but the mouth of the hasty draws near to ruin. \textsuperscript{15} The wealth of rich men is a strong city; but poverty is the ruin of the ungodly. \textsuperscript{16} The works of the righteous produce life; but the fruits of the ungodly produce sins. \textsuperscript{17} Instruction keeps the right ways of life; but instruction unchastened goes astray.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Righteous lips cover enmity; but they that utter railings are most foolish. \textsuperscript{19} By a multitude of words thou shalt not escape sin; but if thou refrain thy lips thou wilt be prudent. \textsuperscript{20} The tongue of the just is tried silver; but the heart of the ungodly shall fail. \textsuperscript{21} The lips of the righteous know sublime truths : but the foolish die in want. \textsuperscript{22} The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the righteous; it enriches him , and grief of heart shall not be added to it .\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{23} A fool does mischief in sport; but wisdom brings forth prudence for a man.\par

Proverbs 10:23 Brenton note: Gr. laughter.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} The ungodly is engulphed in destruction; but the desire of the righteous is acceptable. \textsuperscript{25} When the storm passes by, the ungodly vanishes away; but the righteous turns aside and escapes for ever. \textsuperscript{26} As a sour grape is hurtful to the teeth, and smoke to the eyes, so iniquity hurts those that practise it. \textsuperscript{27} The fear of the Lord adds length of days: but the years of the ungodly shall be shortened. \textsuperscript{28} Joy rests long with the righteous: but the hope of the ungodly shall perish. \textsuperscript{29} The fear of the Lord is a strong hold of the saints: but ruin comes to them that work wickedness.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 10:26 TSK note: vinegar, as smoke As the acidity of vinegar causes the unpleasantness and pain to the teeth, and by softening and dissolving the alkali of the bone, impairs their texture, and renders them incapable of mastication; and as smoke, by irritating the tender vessels, causes the eyes to smart, and prevents distinct vision; so a sluggish messenger is a continual vexation and loss to those by whom he is employed. so\par
Proverbs 10:27 TSK note: fear, ;, prolongeth Heb. addeth the years\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} The righteous shall never fail: but the ungodly shall not dwell in the earth. \textsuperscript{31} The mouth of the righteous drops wisdom: but the tongue of the unjust shall perish. \textsuperscript{32} The lips of just men drop grace: but the mouth of the ungodly is perverse.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 10:32 TSK note: know; but, frowardness Heb. Frowardnesses\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 11}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} False balances are an abomination before the Lord: but a just weight is acceptable unto him. \textsuperscript{2} Wherever pride enters, there will be also disgrace: but the mouth of the lowly meditates wisdom. \textsuperscript{3} When a just man dies he leaves regret: but the destruction of the ungodly is speedy, and causes joy. \textsuperscript{5} Righteousness traces out blameless paths: but ungodliness encounters unjust dealing.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 11:1 TSK note: A false balance is Heb. Balances of deceit, are, ; a just weight Heb. a perfect stone\par
Proverbs 11:2 Brenton note: See Appendix.\par
Proverbs 11:3 Brenton note: the Alexandrine text reads: “The integrity of the upright shall guide them, but the overthrow of the rebellious shall spoil them.”\par
Proverbs 11:3 Brenton note: Comp. Heb.\par
Proverbs 11:5 Brenton note: Gr. right divides.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} The righteousness of upright men delivers them: but transgressors are caught in their own destruction. \textsuperscript{7} At the death of a just man his hope does not perish: but the boast of the ungodly perishes. \textsuperscript{8} A righteous man escapes from a snare, and the ungodly man is delivered up in his place. \textsuperscript{9} In the mouth of ungodly men is a snare to citizens: but the understanding of righteous men is prosperous. \textsuperscript{10} In the prosperity of righteous men a city prospers: \textsuperscript{11} but by the mouths of ungodly men it is overthrown.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 11:9 TSK note: An hypocrite Or rather, as chanaiph properly signifies, a wicked, profligate person, an infidel., ;, ;, ; through\par
Proverbs 11:10 Brenton note: See Appendix which gives the Alexandrine text as: “[note - Part of verse 10.]— but at the destruction of the wicked there is exultation.”\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} A man void of understanding sneers at his fellow citizens: but a sensible man is quiet. \textsuperscript{13} A double-tongued man discloses the secret counsels of an assembly: but he that is faithful in spirit conceals matters. \textsuperscript{14} They that have no guidance fall like leaves: but in much counsel there is safety.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 11:12 TSK note: that, ; , ; void of wisdom Heb. destitute of heart a man\par
Proverbs 11:13 Brenton note: See chap 20. 27.\par
Proverbs 11:13 TSK note: A tale bearer, Heb. He that walketh being a talebearer, ; revealeth, ; he\par
Proverbs 11:14 Brenton note: Or, governance.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} A bad man does harm wherever he meets a just man: and he hates the sound of safety. \textsuperscript{16} A gracious wife brings glory to her husband: but a woman hating righteousness is a theme of dishonour. The slothful come to want: but the diligent support themselves with wealth. \textsuperscript{17} A merciful man does good to his own soul: but the merciless destroys his own body.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 11:15 TSK note: that is surety, smart Heb. be sore broken suretiship Heb. those that strike hands\par
Proverbs 11:16 Brenton note: Gr. raises.\par
Proverbs 11:16 Brenton note: Gr. manly.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} An ungodly man performs unrighteous works: but the seed of the righteous is a reward of truth. \textsuperscript{19} A righteous son is born for life: but the persecution of the ungodly ends in death. \textsuperscript{20} Perverse ways are an abomination to the Lord: but all they that are blameless in their ways are acceptable to him. \textsuperscript{21} He that unjustly strikes hands shall not be unpunished: but he that sows righteousness shall receive a faithful reward. \textsuperscript{22} As an ornament in a swine's snout, so is beauty to an ill-minded woman. \textsuperscript{23} All the desire of the righteous is good: but the hope of the ungodly shall perish.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 11:22 TSK note: a jewel; is without Heb. departed from\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} There are some who scatter their own, and make it more: and there are some also who gather, yet have less. \textsuperscript{25} Every sincere soul is blessed: but a passionate man is not graceful. \textsuperscript{26} May he that hoards corn leave it to the nation: but blessing be on the head of him that gives it . \textsuperscript{27} He that devises good counsels seeks good favour: but as for him that seeks after evil, evil shall overtake him. \textsuperscript{28} He that trusts in wealth shall fall; but he that helps righteous men shall rise. \textsuperscript{29} He that deals not graciously with his own house shall inherit the wind; and the fool shall be servant to the wise man. \textsuperscript{30} Out of the fruit of righteousness grows a tree of life; but the souls of transgressors are cut off before their time. \textsuperscript{31} If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 11:24 Brenton note: Gr. diminished.\par
Proverbs 11:25 TSK note: liberal soul Heb. soul of blessing\par
Proverbs 11:27 TSK note: diligently Shochair, properly, "rising early to seek" what is greatly desired. he that seeketh\par
Proverbs 11:28 Brenton note: See 1 Tim. 5. 8.\par
Proverbs 11:30 TSK note: fruit, and; winneth Heb. taketh\par
Proverbs 11:31 Brenton note: See 1 Pet.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 12}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} He that loves instruction loves sense, but he that hates reproofs is a fool. \textsuperscript{2} He that has found favour with the Lord is made better; but a transgressor shall be passed over in silence. \textsuperscript{3} A man shall not prosper by wickedness; but the roots of the righteous shall not be taken up. \textsuperscript{4} A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband; but as a worm in wood, so a bad woman destroys her husband.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 12:2 Brenton note: Or. better is he, etc.\par
Proverbs 12:3 TSK note: shall not be established;, the root\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} The thoughts of the righteous are true judgments; but ungodly men devise deceits.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} The words of ungodly men are crafty; but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them. \textsuperscript{7} When the ungodly is overthrown, he vanishes away; but the houses of the just remain. \textsuperscript{8} The mouth of an understanding man is praised by a man; but he that is dull of heart is had in derision. \textsuperscript{9} Better is a man in dishonour serving himself, than one honouring himself and wanting bread.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 12:8 TSK note: commended;, ; , ; he, ;, ; of a perverse heart Heb. perverse of heart\par
Proverbs 12:9 TSK note: He that is etc. Or, rather, as in the old translation "He that is despised, and is his own servant, is better than he that boasteth himself and wanteth bread; " with which the versions generally agree. That is, it is better to be in lowness and obscurity, and to support oneself by manual labour, than to want the necessaries of life, through a foolish vanity, or the pride of birth, which refuses to labour. despised\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} A righteous man has pity for the lives of his cattle; but the bowels of the ungodly are unmerciful. \textsuperscript{11} He that tills his own land shall be satisfied with bread; but they that pursue vanities are void of understanding.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 12:10 TSK note: righteous; but; tender mercies or, bowels\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} The desires of the ungodly are evil; but the roots of the godly are firmly set. \textsuperscript{13} For the sin of his lips a sinner falls into snares; but a righteous man escapes from them. \textsuperscript{14} The soul of a man shall be filled with good from the fruits of his mouth; and the recompence of his lips shall be given to him. \textsuperscript{15} The ways of fools are right in their own eyes; but a wise man hearkens to counsels. \textsuperscript{16} A fool declares his wrath the same day; but a prudent man hides his own disgrace. \textsuperscript{17} A righteous man declares the open truth; but an unjust witness is deceitful.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 12:12 TSK note: desireth, ;, ; net or, fortress, the root\par
Proverbs 12:13 TSK note: wicked is snared by the transgression of his lips Heb. snare of the wicked is in the transgression of lips, ; , ; but\par
Proverbs 12:16 TSK note: fool's, ; presently Heb. in that day but\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Some wound as they speak, like swords; but the tongues of the wise heal. \textsuperscript{19} True lips establish testimony; but a hasty witness has an unjust tongue. \textsuperscript{20} There is deceit in the heart of him that imagines evil; but they that love peace shall rejoice. \textsuperscript{21} No injustice will please a just man; but the ungodly will be filled with mischief. \textsuperscript{22} Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord; but he that deals faithfully is accepted with him. \textsuperscript{23} An understanding man is a throne of wisdom; but the heart of fools shall meet with curses.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} The hand of chosen men shall easily obtain rule; but the deceitful shall be for a prey. \textsuperscript{25} A terrible word troubles the heart of a righteous man; but a good message rejoices him. \textsuperscript{26} A just arbitrator shall be his own friend; but mischief shall pursue sinners; and the way of ungodly men shall lead them astray. \textsuperscript{27} A deceitful man shall catch no game; but a blameless man is a precious possession. \textsuperscript{28} In the ways of righteousness is life; but the ways of those that remember injuries lead to death.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 12:24 TSK note: hand, ;, but, slothful or, deceitful\par
Proverbs 12:26 TSK note: righteous, ; excellent or, abundant but\par
Proverbs 12:27 Brenton note: Gr. pure.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 13}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} A wise son is obedient to his father: but a disobedient son will be destroyed. \textsuperscript{2} A good man shall eat of the fruits of righteousness: but the lives of transgressors shall perish before their time. \textsuperscript{3} He that keeps his own mouth keeps his own life: but he that is hasty with his lips shall bring terror upon himself. \textsuperscript{4} Every slothful man desires, but the hands of the active are diligent. \textsuperscript{5} A righteous man hates an unjust word: but an ungodly man is ashamed, and will have no confidence. \textsuperscript{7} There are some who, having nothing, enrich themselves: and there are some who bring themselves down in the midst of much wealth.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 13:5 Brenton note: See Appendix for Alexandrine text shown as: “Righteousness preserves the simple in the way, but sin makes worthless the ungodly.”\par
Proverbs 13:7 TSK note: is that maketh himself rich, ; that maketh himself poor\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} A man's own wealth is the ransom of his life: but the poor endures not threatening. \textsuperscript{9} The righteous always have light: but the light of the ungodly is quenched. \textsuperscript{10} A bad man does evil with insolence: but they that are judges of themselves are wise. \textsuperscript{11} Wealth gotten hastily with iniquity is diminished: but he that gathers for himself with godliness shall be increased. The righteous is merciful, and lends. \textsuperscript{12} Better is he that begins to help heartily, than he that promises and leads another to hope: for a good desire is a tree of life. \textsuperscript{13} He that slights a matter shall be slighted of it: but he that fears the commandment has health of soul .\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 13:8 Brenton note: Or, comes not in for.\par
Proverbs 13:11 TSK note: Wealth, ;, ; he, ; by labour Heb. with the hand\par
Proverbs 13:13 TSK note: despiseth, ; , ;, ; he; rewarded Heb. in peace\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} The law of the wise is a fountain of life: but the man void of understanding shall die by a snare. \textsuperscript{15} Sound discretion gives favour, and to know the law is the part of a sound understanding: but the ways of scorners tend to destruction.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} Every prudent man acts with knowledge: but the fool displays his own mischief. \textsuperscript{17} A rash king shall fall into mischief: but a wise messenger shall deliver him. \textsuperscript{18} Instruction removes poverty and disgrace: but he that attends to reproofs shall be honoured. \textsuperscript{19} The desires of the godly gladden the soul, but the works of the ungodly are far from knowledge. \textsuperscript{20} If thou walkest with wise men thou shalt be wise: but he that walks with fools shall be known. \textsuperscript{21} Evil shall pursue sinners; but good shall overtake the righteous. \textsuperscript{22} A good man shall inherit children's children; and the wealth of ungodly men is laid up for the just. \textsuperscript{23} The righteous shall spend many years in wealth: but the unrighteous shall perish suddenly.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 13:16 TSK note: prudent, ; a fool, ; layeth Heb. spreadeth\par
Proverbs 13:17 TSK note: wicked, ;, ;, ; but, ; a faithful ambassador Heb. an ambassador of faithfulness\par
Proverbs 13:19 TSK note: The desire; it is depart\par
Proverbs 13:20 TSK note: that; but, ;, ;, ;, ; destroyed Heb. broken\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} He that spares the rod hates his son: but he that loves, carefully chastens him . \textsuperscript{25} A just man eats and satisfies his soul: but the souls of the ungodly are in want.\par
\subsection*{Proverbs 14}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Wise women build houses: but a foolish one digs hers down with her hands. \textsuperscript{2} He that walks uprightly fears the Lord; but he that is perverse in his ways shall be dishonoured. \textsuperscript{3} Out of the mouth of fools comes a rod of pride; but the lips of the wise preserve them. \textsuperscript{4} Where no oxen are, the cribs are clean; but where there is abundant produce, the strength of the ox is apparent. \textsuperscript{5} A faithful witness does not lie; but an unjust witness kindles falsehoods. \textsuperscript{6} Thou shalt seek wisdom with bad men, and shalt not find it; but discretion is easily available with the prudent.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} All things are adverse to a foolish man; but wise lips are the weapons of discretion. \textsuperscript{8} The wisdom of the prudent will understand their ways; but the folly of fools leads astray. \textsuperscript{9} The houses of transgressors will need purification; but the houses of the just are acceptable.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 14:9 Brenton note: Gr. shall owe. See Job 6. 21.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} If a man's mind is intelligent, his soul is sorrowful; and when he rejoices, he has no fellowship with pride. \textsuperscript{11} The houses of ungodly men shall be utterly destroyed; but the tabernacles of them that walk uprightly shall stand. \textsuperscript{12} There is a way which seems to be right with men, but the ends of it reach to the depth of hell. \textsuperscript{13} Grief mingles not with mirth; and joy in the end comes to grief. \textsuperscript{14} A stout-hearted man shall be filled with his own ways; and a good man with his own thoughts. \textsuperscript{15} The simple believes every word: but the prudent man betakes himself to after-thought. \textsuperscript{16} A wise man fears, and departs from evil; but the fool trusts in himself, and joins himself with the transgressor. \textsuperscript{17} A passionate man acts inconsiderately; but a sensible man bears up under many things.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 14:10 Brenton note: Or, heart be sensitive.\par
Proverbs 14:10 TSK note: heart, ; , ; his etc. Heb. the bitterness of his soul, and\par
Proverbs 14:12 Brenton note: Gr. come.\par
Proverbs 14:14 Brenton note: Lit. bold-hearted.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Fools shall have mischief for their portion; but the prudent shall take fast hold of understanding. \textsuperscript{19} Evil men shall fall before the good; and the ungodly shall attend at the gates of the righteous. \textsuperscript{20} Friends will hate poor friends; but the friends of the rich are many. \textsuperscript{21} He that dishonours the needy sins: but he that has pity on the poor is most blessed. \textsuperscript{22} They that go astray devise evils: but the good devise mercy and truth. The framers of evil do not understand mercy and truth: but compassion and faithfulness are with the framers of good. \textsuperscript{23} With every one who is careful there is abundance: but the pleasure-taking and indolent shall be in want. \textsuperscript{24} A prudent man is the crown of the wise: but the occupation of fools is evil.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 14:20 TSK note: poor, ;, but, ;, the rich hath many friends Heb. many are the lovers of the rich.\par
Proverbs 14:21 TSK note: that despiseth, ;, ; , he that hath\par
Proverbs 14:24 Brenton note: Greek background: mōria (μωρία) = foolishness. Common English renderings: foolishness. Used for folly or foolishness.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} A faithful witness shall deliver a soul from evil: but a deceitful man kindles falsehoods. \textsuperscript{26} In the fear of the Lord is strong confidence: and he leaves his children a support. \textsuperscript{27} The commandment of the Lord is a fountain of life; and it causes men to turn aside from the snare of death.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} In a populous nation is the glory of a king: but in the failure of people is the ruin of a prince. \textsuperscript{29} A man slow to wrath abounds in wisdom: but a man of impatient spirit is very foolish. \textsuperscript{30} A meek-spirited man is a healer of the heart: but a sensitive heart is a corruption of the bones. \textsuperscript{31} He that oppresses the needy provokes his Maker: but he that honours him has pity upon the poor. \textsuperscript{32} The ungodly shall be driven away in his wickedness: but he who is secure in his own holiness is just.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 14:29 TSK note: slow, ; , but, ; hasty Heb. short exalteth\par
Proverbs 14:32 Brenton note: Comp. Heb.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{33} There is wisdom in the good heart of a man: but in the heart of fools it is not discerned. \textsuperscript{34} Righteousness exalts a nation: but sins diminish tribes. \textsuperscript{35} An understanding servant is acceptable to a king; and by his good behaviour he removes disgrace.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 14:34 TSK note: Righteousness, ; but, ; , 22:1-23:49 any people Heb. nations\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 15}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Anger slays even wise men; yet a submissive answer turns away wrath: but a grievous word stirs up anger. \textsuperscript{2} The tongue of the wise knows what is good: but the mouth of the foolish tells out evil things.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 15:2 TSK note: tongue, ; poureth Heb. belcheth, or, bubbleth\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} The eyes of the Lord behold both the evil and the good in every place. \textsuperscript{4} The wholesome tongue is a tree of life, and he that keeps it shall be filled with understanding. \textsuperscript{5} A fool scorns his father's instruction: but he that keeps his commandments is more prudent. In abounding righteousness is great strength: but the ungodly shall utterly perish from the earth.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 15:4 Brenton note: Gr. the healing of the tongue.\par
Proverbs 15:4 Brenton note: Gr. spirit.\par
Proverbs 15:4 TSK note: A wholesome Heb. The healing of the, ; a tree; a breach\par
Proverbs 15:5 Brenton note: Gr. with the roots wholly torn up.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} In the houses of the righteous is much strength: but the fruits of the ungodly shall perish. \textsuperscript{7} The lips of the wise are bound by discretion: but the hearts of the foolish are not safe. \textsuperscript{8} The sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord; but the prayers of them that walk honestly are acceptable with him. \textsuperscript{9} The ways of an ungodly man are an abomination to the Lord; but he loves those that follow after righteousness. \textsuperscript{10} The instruction of the simple is known by them that pass by; but they that hate reproofs die disgracefully.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 15:6 TSK note: the house, ; in the revenues\par
Proverbs 15:10 TSK note: Correction or, Instruction grievous, ;, ;, and he\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Hell and destruction are manifest to the Lord; how shall not also be the hearts of men? \textsuperscript{12} An uninstructed person will not love those that reprove him; neither will he associate with the wise. \textsuperscript{13} When the heart rejoices the countenance is cheerful; but when it is in sorrow, the countenance is sad. \textsuperscript{14} An upright heart seeks discretion; but the mouth of the uninstructed will experience evils.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} The eyes of the wicked are always looking for evil things; but the good are always quiet. \textsuperscript{16} Better is a small portion with the fear of the Lord, than great treasures without the fear of the Lord . \textsuperscript{17} Better is an entertainment of herbs with friendliness and kindness, than a feast of calves, with enmity. \textsuperscript{18} A passionate man stirs up strife; but he that is slow to anger appeases even a rising one. \textsuperscript{19} The ways of sluggards are strewn with thorns; but those of the diligent are made smooth. \textsuperscript{20} A wise son gladdens his father; but a foolish son sneers at his mother. \textsuperscript{21} The ways of a foolish man are void of sense; but a wise man proceeds on his way aright. \textsuperscript{22} They that honour not councils put off deliberation; but counsel abides in the hearts of counsellors.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 15:18 Brenton note: Gr. future.\par
Proverbs 15:19 TSK note: way of the slothful, ;, the way of the righteous, ;, ;, made plain Heb. raised up as a causey\par
Proverbs 15:21 TSK note: joy, destitute of wisdom Heb. void of heart, *marg. a man\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} A bad man will by no means attend to counsel; neither will he say anything seasonable, or good for the common weal .\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 15:23 Brenton note: Or, obey.\par
Proverbs 15:23 TSK note: joy, ; in due season Heb. in his season, ; how\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} The thoughts of the wise are ways of life, that he may turn aside and escape from hell. \textsuperscript{25} The Lord pulls down the houses of scorners; but he establishes the border of the widow. \textsuperscript{26} An unrighteous thought is abomination to the Lord; but the sayings of the pure are held in honour. \textsuperscript{27} A receiver of bribes destroys himself; but he that hates the receiving of bribes is safe.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 15:26 TSK note: thoughts, ; but;, ; pleasant words Heb. words of pleasantness\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} The hearts of the righteous meditate faithfulness; but the mouth of the ungodly answers evil things. \textsuperscript{29} God is far from the ungodly; but he hearkens to the prayers of the righteous.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} The eye that sees rightly rejoices the heart; and a good report fattens the bones. \textsuperscript{32} He that rejects instruction hates himself; but he that minds reproofs loves his soul. \textsuperscript{33} The fear of the Lord is instruction and wisdom; and the highest honour will correspond therewith.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 15:30 TSK note: light; , a good, ; the bones\par
Proverbs 15:32 TSK note: refuseth, ; instruction or, correction, ; heareth or, obeyeth, ;, ; getteth understanding Heb. possesseth an heart, *marg.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 16}
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} All the works of the humble man are manifest with God; but the ungodly shall perish in an evil day. \textsuperscript{5} Every one that is proud in heart is unclean before God, and he that unjustly strikes hands with hand shall not be held guiltless. \textsuperscript{7} The beginning of a good way is to do justly; and it is more acceptable with God than to offer sacrifices. \textsuperscript{8} He that seeks the Lord shall find knowledge with righteousness: and they that rightly seek him shall find peace. \textsuperscript{9} All the works of the Lord are done with righteousness; and the ungodly man is kept for the evil day.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 16:5 TSK note: that, ; though unpunished Heb. held innocent\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} There is an oracle upon the lips of a king; and his mouth shall not err in judgment. \textsuperscript{11} The poise of the balance is righteousness with the Lord; and his works are righteous measures. \textsuperscript{12} An evil-doer is an abomination to a king; for the throne of rule is established by righteousness. \textsuperscript{13} Righteous lips are acceptable to a king; and he loves right words. \textsuperscript{14} The anger of a king is a messenger of death; but a wise man will pacify him. \textsuperscript{15} The son of a king is in the light of life; and they that are in favour with him are as a cloud of latter rain. \textsuperscript{16} The brood of wisdom is more to be chosen than gold, and the brood of prudence more to be chosen than silver. \textsuperscript{17} The paths of life turn aside from evil; and the ways of righteousness are length of life. He that receives instruction shall be in prosperity; and he that regards reproofs shall be made wise. He that keeps his ways, preserves his own soul; and he that loves his life will spare his mouth.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 16:10 TSK note: A divine sentence Heb. Divination, ;, ; , ; transgresseth\par
Proverbs 16:16 Brenton note: Or, Abodes. Comp. Heb. See Luke 13. 35.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Pride goes before destruction, and folly before a fall. \textsuperscript{19} Better is a meek-spirited man with lowliness, than one who divides spoils with the proud. \textsuperscript{20} He who is skilful in business finds good: but he that trusts in God is most blessed. \textsuperscript{21} Men call the wise and understanding evil: but they that are pleasing in speech shall hear more. \textsuperscript{22} Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessors; but the instruction of fools is evil. \textsuperscript{23} The heart of the wise will discern the things which proceed from his own mouth; and on his lips he will wear knowledge. \textsuperscript{24} Good words are honeycombs, and the sweetness thereof is a healing of the soul.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 16:19 Brenton note: Or, affliction.\par
Proverbs 16:23 TSK note: heart, ;, ; teacheth Heb. maketh wise\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} There are ways that seem to be right to a man, but the end of them looks to the depth of hell. \textsuperscript{26} A man who labours, labours for himself, and drives from him his own ruin. \textsuperscript{27} But the perverse bears destruction upon his own mouth: a foolish man digs up evil for himself, and treasures fire on his own lips. \textsuperscript{28} A perverse man spreads mischief, and will kindle a torch of deceit with mischiefs; and he separates friends. \textsuperscript{29} A transgressor tries to ensnare friends, and leads them in ways that are not good.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 16:26 TSK note: He Heb. The soul of him laboureth, ; craveth it of him Heb. boweth unto him\par
Proverbs 16:27 TSK note: An ungodly man Heb. a man of Belial, ; diggeth; in\par
Proverbs 16:28 TSK note: froward, ; soweth Heb. sendeth forth a whisperer\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} And the man that fixes his eyes devises perverse things, and marks out with his lips all evils: he is a furnace of wickedness. \textsuperscript{31} Old age is a crown of honour, but it is found in the ways of righteousness. \textsuperscript{32} A man slow to anger is better than a strong man ; and he that governs his temper better than he that takes a city. \textsuperscript{33} All evils come upon the ungodly into their bosoms; but all righteous things come of the Lord.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 16:31 Brenton note: Gr. boasting.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 17}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Better is a morsel with pleasure in peace, than a house full of many good things and unjust sacrifices, with strife. \textsuperscript{2} A wise servant shall have rule over foolish masters, and shall divide portions among brethren. \textsuperscript{3} As silver and gold are tried in a furnace, so are choice hearts with the Lord. \textsuperscript{4} A bad man hearkens to the tongue of transgressors: but a righteous man attends not to false lips. \textsuperscript{5} He that laughs at the poor provokes him that made him; and he that rejoices at the destruction of another shall not be held guiltless: but he that has compassion shall find mercy.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 17:1 TSK note: a dry; an house sacrifices or, good cheer with\par
Proverbs 17:5 TSK note: mocketh, ; and; , ; unpunished Heb. held innocent, *marg.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} Children's children are the crown of old men; and their fathers are the glory of children. \textsuperscript{7} Faithful lips will not suit a fool; nor lying lips a just man. \textsuperscript{8} Instruction is to them that use it a gracious reward: and whithersoever it may turn, it shall prosper. \textsuperscript{9} He that conceals injuries seeks love; but he that hates to hide them separates friends and kindred. \textsuperscript{10} A threat breaks down the heart of a wise man; but a fool, though scourged, understands not. \textsuperscript{11} Every bad man stirs up strifes: but the Lord will send out against him an unmerciful messenger.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 17:7 TSK note: Excellent speech Heb. A lip of excellency, ; much, ; lying lips Heb. a lip of lying\par
Proverbs 17:8 TSK note: gift;, ; precious stone Heb. stone of grace whithersoever\par
Proverbs 17:9 Brenton note: Comp. Heb.\par
Proverbs 17:9 TSK note: that covereth; seeketh or, procureth but\par
Proverbs 17:10 TSK note: or, A reproof aweth more a wise man, than to strike a fool an hundred times.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} Care may befall a man of understanding; but fools will meditate evils. \textsuperscript{13} Whoso rewards evil for good, evil shall not be removed from his house. \textsuperscript{14} Rightful rule gives power to words; but sedition and strife precede poverty. \textsuperscript{15} He that pronounces the unjust just, and the just unjust, is unclean and abominable with God. \textsuperscript{16} Why has the fool wealth? for a senseless man will not be able to purchase wisdom. \textsuperscript{17} Have thou a friend for every time, and let brethren be useful in distress; for on this account are they born. \textsuperscript{18} A foolish man applauds and rejoices over himself, as he also that becomes surety would make himself responsible for his own friends.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} A lover of sin rejoices in strifes; \textsuperscript{20} and the hard-hearted man comes not in for good. A man of a changeful tongue will fall into mischiefs; \textsuperscript{21} and the heart of a fool is grief to its possessor. A father rejoices not over an uninstructed son; but a wise son gladdens his mother. \textsuperscript{22} A glad heart promotes health; but the bones of a sorrowful man dry up. \textsuperscript{23} The ways of a man who unjustly receives gifts in his bosom do not prosper; and an ungodly man perverts the ways of righteousness. \textsuperscript{24} The countenance of a wise man is sensible; but the eyes of a fool go to the ends of the earth. \textsuperscript{25} A foolish son is a cause of anger to his father, and grief to her that bore him.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 17:20 Brenton note: Or, meets not with good men.\par
Proverbs 17:20 TSK note: He that hath a froward heart Heb. The froward of heart, ; and he\par
Proverbs 17:22 TSK note: merry, ; like a medicine Heb. to a medicine a broken\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{26} It is not right to punish a righteous man, nor is it holy to plot against righteous princes. \textsuperscript{27} He that forbears to utter a hard word is discreet, and a patient man is wise. \textsuperscript{28} Wisdom shall be imputed to a fool who asks after wisdom: and he who holds his peace shall seem to be sensible.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 17:27 TSK note: spareth, ;, an excellent spirit or, a cool spirit\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 18}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} A man who wishes to separate from friends seeks excuses; but at all times he will be liable to reproach. \textsuperscript{2} A senseless man feels no need of wisdom, for he is rather led by folly. \textsuperscript{3} When an ungodly man comes into a depth of evils, he despises them ; but dishonour and reproach come upon him. \textsuperscript{4} A word in the heart of a man is a deep water, and a river and fountain of life spring forth. \textsuperscript{5} It is not good to accept the person of the ungodly, nor is it holy to pervert justice in judgment.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 18:1 TSK note: Through etc. or, He that separateth himself seeketh, according to his desire and intermeddleth in every business.; seeketh;, ; intermeddleth\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} The lips of a fool bring him into troubles, and his bold mouth calls for death. \textsuperscript{7} A fool's mouth is ruin to him, and his lips are a snare to his soul. \textsuperscript{8} Fear casts down the slothful; and the souls of the effeminate shall hunger. \textsuperscript{9} A man who helps not himself by his labour is brother of him that ruins himself. \textsuperscript{10} The name of the Lord is of great strength; and the righteous running to it are exalted. \textsuperscript{11} The wealth of a rich man is a strong city; and its glory casts a broad shadow. \textsuperscript{12} Before ruin a man's heart is exalted, and before honour it is humble. \textsuperscript{13} Whoso answers a word before he hears a cause , it is folly and reproach to him. \textsuperscript{14} A wise servant calms a man's anger; but who can endure a faint-hearted man? \textsuperscript{15} The heart of the sensible man purchases discretion; and the ears of the wise seek understanding. \textsuperscript{16} A man's gift enlarges him, and seats him among princes. \textsuperscript{17} A righteous man accuses himself at the beginning of his speech, but when he has entered upon the attack, the adversary is reproved.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 18:8 TSK note: words, ; , talebearer or, whisperer as wounds or, like as when men are wounded innermost parts Heb. chambers\par
Proverbs 18:9 TSK note: that is slothful, ; is brother\par
Proverbs 18:10 Brenton note: Gr. having run.\par
Proverbs 18:10 TSK note: name;, ;, ; a strong, ;, ; the righteous, ; safe Heb. set aloft\par
Proverbs 18:13 TSK note: that;, ;, ; , ; answereth a matter Heb. returneth a word\par
Proverbs 18:16 Brenton note: See Ps. 118. 32.\par
Proverbs 18:17 Brenton note: Comp. Mark 14. ult. and margin, with 2 Tim. 4. 14-17.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} A silent man quells strifes, and determines between great powers. \textsuperscript{19} A brother helped by a brother is as a strong and high city; and is as strong as a well -founded palace. \textsuperscript{20} A man fills his belly with the fruits of his mouth; and he shall be satisfied with the fruits of his lips. \textsuperscript{21} Life and death are in the power of the tongue; and they that rule it shall eat the fruits thereof. \textsuperscript{22} He that has found a good wife has found favours, and has received gladness from God.\par
\subsection*{Proverbs 19}
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} The folly of a man spoils his ways: and he blames God in his heart.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Wealth acquires many friends; but the poor is deserted even of the friend he has. \textsuperscript{5} A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that accuses unjustly shall not escape. \textsuperscript{6} Many court the favour of kings; but every bad man becomes a reproach to another man. \textsuperscript{7} Every one who hates his poor brother shall also be far from friendship. Good understanding will draw near to them that know it, and a sensible man will find it. He that does much harm perfects mischief; and he that uses provoking words shall not escape.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 19:5 TSK note: false, ; unpunished Heb. held innocent\par
Proverbs 19:6 TSK note: will, ; and, ;, ; him that giveth gifts Heb. a man of gifts\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} He that procures wisdom loves himself; and he that keeps wisdom shall find good. \textsuperscript{9} A false witness shall not be unpunished; and whosoever shall kindle mischief shall perish by it. \textsuperscript{10} Delight does not suit a fool, nor is it seemly if a servant should begin to rule with haughtiness. \textsuperscript{11} A merciful man is long-suffering; and his triumph overtakes transgressors. \textsuperscript{12} The threatening of a king is like the roaring of a lion; but as dew on the grass, so is his favour.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 19:8 TSK note: wisdom Heb. an heart, ; loveth; he that keepeth\par
Proverbs 19:11 Brenton note: Gr. boasting comes upon.\par
Proverbs 19:11 TSK note: discretion or, prudence deferreth, ; and\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} A foolish son is a disgrace to his father: vows paid out of the hire of a harlot are not pure. \textsuperscript{14} Fathers divide house and substance to their children: but a wife is suited to a man by the Lord. \textsuperscript{15} Cowardice possesses the effeminate man ; and the soul of the sluggard shall hunger. \textsuperscript{16} He that keeps the commandment keeps his own soul; but he that despises his ways shall perish. \textsuperscript{17} He that has pity on the poor lends to the Lord; and he will recompense to him according to his gift. \textsuperscript{18} Chasten thy son, for so he shall be hopeful; and be not exalted in thy soul to haughtiness. \textsuperscript{19} A malicious man shall be severely punished, and if he commit injury, he shall also lose his life.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 19:15 Brenton note: Or, keeps down.\par
Proverbs 19:16 TSK note: keepeth the, ; , ; , ;, ; , ; keepeth his, ; he that despiseth\par
Proverbs 19:17 TSK note: that hath, ; lendeth, ; , ; that which he hath given or, his deed\par
Proverbs 19:18 TSK note: Chasten, ; for his crying or, to his destruction, or, to cause him to die\par
Proverbs 19:19 TSK note: man, ;, ; do it again Heb. add\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} Hear, son, the instruction of thy father, that thou mayest be wise at thy latter end. \textsuperscript{21} There are many thoughts in a man's heart; but the counsel of the Lord abides for ever. \textsuperscript{22} Mercy is a fruit to a man: and a poor man is better than a rich liar. \textsuperscript{23} The fear of the Lord is life to a man: and he shall lodge without fear in places where knowledge is not seen. \textsuperscript{24} He that unjustly hides his hands in his bosom, will not even bring them up to his mouth. \textsuperscript{25} When a pestilent character is scourged, a simple man is made wiser: and if thou reprove a wise man, he will understand discretion.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 19:23 Brenton note: Or, 'but he that is without fear (sc. of the Lord) shall dwell' etc.\par
Proverbs 19:23 TSK note: fear, ;, ;, ; shall abide, ; , ; he shall\par
Proverbs 19:25 TSK note: Smite;, beware Heb. be cunning reprove\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{26} He that dishonours his father, and drives away his mother, shall be disgraced and shall be exposed to reproach. \textsuperscript{27} A son who ceases to attend to the instruction of a father will cherish evil designs. \textsuperscript{28} He that becomes surety for a foolish child will despise the ordinance: and the mouth of ungodly men shall drink down judgments. \textsuperscript{29} Scourges are preparing for the intemperate, and punishments likewise for fools.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 19:28 TSK note: An ungodly witness Heb. a witness of Belial, ; scorneth, ; the\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 20}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Wine is an intemperate thing, and strong drink full of violence: but every fool is entangled with them. \textsuperscript{2} The threat of a king differs not from the rage of a lion; and he that provokes him sins against his own soul. \textsuperscript{3} It is a glory to a man to turn aside from railing; but every fool is entangled with such matters. \textsuperscript{4} A sluggard when reproached is not ashamed: so also he who borrows corn in harvest.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 20:4 TSK note: sluggard, cold or, winter therefore\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Counsel in a man's heart is deep water; but a prudent man will draw it out. \textsuperscript{6} A man is valuable, and a merciful man precious: but it is hard to find a faithful man. \textsuperscript{7} He that walks blameless in justice, shall leave his children blessed. \textsuperscript{8} Whenever a righteous king sits on the throne, no evil thing can stand before his presence. \textsuperscript{9} Who will boast that he has a pure heart? or who will boldly say that he is pure from sins?\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 20:6 TSK note: proclaim, ; , ; goodness or, bounty but\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} A large and small weight, and divers measures, are even both of them unclean before the Lord; and so is he that makes them. \textsuperscript{11} A youth when in company with a godly man, will be restrained in his devices, and then his way will be straight. \textsuperscript{12} The ear hears, and the eye sees: even both of them are the Lord's work. \textsuperscript{13} Love not to speak ill, lest thou be cut off: open thine eyes, and be filled with bread.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 20:10 Brenton note: Gr. double.\par
Proverbs 20:10 TSK note: Divers weights, and divers measures Heb. a stone and a stone, an ephah and an ephah, both, ; abomination\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} A double weight is an abomination to the Lord; and a deceitful balance is not good in his sight. \textsuperscript{24} A man's goings are directed of the Lord: how then can a mortal understand his ways? \textsuperscript{25} It is a snare to a man hastily to consecrate some of his own property: for in that case repentance comes after vowing. \textsuperscript{26} A wise king utterly crushes the ungodly, and will bring a wheel upon them.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 20:23 TSK note: weights; a false balance Heb. balances of deceit\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} The spirit of man is a light of the Lord, who searches the inmost parts of the belly. \textsuperscript{28} Mercy and truth are a guard to a king, and will surround his throne with righteousness. \textsuperscript{29} Wisdom is an ornament to young men; and grey hairs are the glory of old men. \textsuperscript{30} Bruises and contusions befall bad men; and plagues shall come into the inward parts of their belly.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 20:27 Brenton note: Comp. chap 11. 13.\par
Proverbs 20:27 TSK note: spirit; candle or, lamp, searching\par
Proverbs 20:30 TSK note: cleanseth away evil Heb. is a purging medicine against evil stripes\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 21}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} As a rush of water, so is the king's heart in God's hand: he turns it whithersoever he may desire to point out. \textsuperscript{2} Every man seems to himself righteous; but the Lord directs the hearts. \textsuperscript{3} To do justly and to speak truth, are more pleasing to God than the blood of sacrifices. \textsuperscript{4} A high-minded man is stout-hearted in his pride; and the lamp of the wicked is sin. \textsuperscript{6} He that gathers treasures with a lying tongue pursues vanity on to the snares of death. \textsuperscript{7} Destruction shall lodge with the ungodly; for they refuse to do justly. \textsuperscript{8} To the froward God sends froward ways; for his works are pure and right. \textsuperscript{9} It is better to dwell in a corner on the house-top, than in plastered rooms with unrighteousness, and in an open house. \textsuperscript{10} The soul of the ungodly shall not be pitied by any man. \textsuperscript{11} When an intemperate man is punished the simple becomes wiser: and a wise man understanding will receive knowledge. \textsuperscript{12} A righteous man understands the hearts of the ungodly: and despises the ungodly for their wickedness.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 21:4 TSK note: An high look Heb. Haughtiness of eyes, ; , ; and the, ; plowing of the wicked or, light of the wicked\par
Proverbs 21:7 TSK note: robbery, ;, ; , ; destroy them Heb. saw them, or, dwell with them, because\par
Proverbs 21:9 Brenton note: Gr. in the open air.\par
Proverbs 21:9 TSK note: better, brawling woman in a wide house Heb. woman of contentions in a house of society\par
Proverbs 21:10 TSK note: soul, ;, ; findeth no favour Heb. is not favoured\par
Proverbs 21:11 TSK note: the scorner; , ; , ; , ; when the wise\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} He that stops his ears from hearing the poor, himself also shall cry, and there shall be none to hear him . \textsuperscript{14} A secret gift calms anger: but he that forbears to give stirs up strong wrath. \textsuperscript{15} It is the joy of the righteous to do judgment: but a holy man is abominable with evil-doers. \textsuperscript{16} A man that wanders out of the way of righteousness, shall rest in the congregation of giants. \textsuperscript{17} A poor man loves mirth, loving wine and oil in abundance; \textsuperscript{18} and a transgressor is the abomination of a righteous man. \textsuperscript{19} It is better to dwell in a wilderness than with a quarrelsome and talkative and passionate woman. \textsuperscript{20} A desirable treasure will rest on the mouth of the wise; but foolish men will swallow it up. \textsuperscript{21} The way of righteousness and mercy will find life and glory. \textsuperscript{22} A wise man assaults strong cities, and demolishes the fortress in which the ungodly trusted. \textsuperscript{23} He that keeps his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from trouble.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 21:16 Brenton note: Heb. Rephaim. see Appendix. Note on 2 Kings 5. 18.\par
Proverbs 21:18 Brenton note: Gr. `off-scouring;' perhaps `ransom,' q. d. that which cleans.\par
Proverbs 21:19 TSK note: better;, ; wilderness Heb. land of the desert\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} A bold and self-willed and insolent man is called a pest: and he that remembers injuries is a transgressor. \textsuperscript{25} Desires kill the sluggard; for his hands do not choose to do anything. \textsuperscript{26} An ungodly man entertains evil desires all the day: but the righteous is unsparingly merciful and compassionate. \textsuperscript{27} The sacrifices of the ungodly are abomination to the Lord, for they offer them wickedly. \textsuperscript{28} A false witness shall perish; but an obedient man will speak cautiously. \textsuperscript{29} An ungodly man impudently withstands with his face; but the upright man himself understands his ways. \textsuperscript{30} There is no wisdom, there is no courage, there is no counsel against the ungodly. \textsuperscript{31} A horse is prepared for the day of battle; but help is of the Lord.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 21:24 TSK note: haughty, ; proud wrath Heb. the wrath of pride\par
Proverbs 21:27 Brenton note: Or, unlawfully.\par
Proverbs 21:27 TSK note: sacrifice, ;, ; , ;, ; with a wicked mind Heb. in wickedness\par
Proverbs 21:28 TSK note: false witness Heb. witness of lies, ; the man\par
Proverbs 21:29 Brenton note: See Alex. ungodly.\par
Proverbs 21:29 TSK note: hardeneth, ;, he directeth or, he considereth\par
Proverbs 21:31 TSK note: horse, ; but, safety or, victory, *marg.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 22}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} A fair name is better than much wealth, and good favour is above silver and gold. \textsuperscript{2} The rich and the poor meet together; but the Lord made them both. \textsuperscript{3} An intelligent man seeing a bad man severely punished is himself instructed, but fools pass by and are punished. \textsuperscript{4} The fear of the Lord is the offspring of wisdom, and wealth, and glory, and life. \textsuperscript{5} Thistles and snares are in perverse ways; but he that keeps his soul will refrain from them. \textsuperscript{7} The rich will rule over the poor, and servants will lend to their own masters.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 22:1 TSK note: name; loving favour rather than or, favour is better than, etc.\par
Proverbs 22:4 TSK note: By etc. Heb. The reward of humility, etc.\par
Proverbs 22:7 TSK note: rich, ;, ;, the borrower; lender Heb. man that lendeth\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} He that sows wickedness shall reap troubles; and shall fully receive the punishment of his deeds. \textsuperscript{9} He that has pity on the poor shall himself be maintained; for he has given of his own bread to the poor. \textsuperscript{10} Cast out a pestilent person from the council, and strife shall go out with him; for when he sits in the council he dishonours all.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 22:8 TSK note: that;, ; the rod of his anger shall fail or, with the rod of his anger he shall be consumed\par
Proverbs 22:9 TSK note: He that hath a bountiful eye Heb. Good of eye\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} The Lord loves holy hearts, and all blameless persons are acceptable with him: a king rules with his lips. \textsuperscript{12} But the eyes of the Lord preserve discretion; but the transgressor despises wise words. \textsuperscript{13} The sluggard makes excuses, and says, There is a lion in the ways, and murderers in the streets. \textsuperscript{14} The mouth of a transgressor is a deep pit; and he that is hated of the Lord shall fall into it. \textsuperscript{15} Folly is attached to the heart of a child, but the rod and instruction are then far from him.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 22:11 TSK note: that; for the grace of his lips or, and hath grace in his lips, ; the king\par
Proverbs 22:12 TSK note: eyes; , ; he;, ; words or, matters\par
Proverbs 22:13 TSK note: The slothful That is, the slothful man uses any pretext, however improbable, to indulge his love of ease and indolence.\par
Proverbs 22:14 TSK note: mouth, ; a deep pit That is, it is like a deep pit, or pitfall, in which animals are often taken alive. abhorred\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} He that oppresses the poor, increases his own substance, yet gives to the rich so as to make it less.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 22:16 TSK note: that oppresseth, ; , he that giveth\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Incline thine ear to the words of wise men: hear also my word, and apply thine heart, \textsuperscript{18} that thou mayest know that they are good: and if thou lay them to heart, they shall also gladden thee on thy lips. \textsuperscript{19} That thy hope may be in the Lord, and he may make thy way known to thee. \textsuperscript{20} And do thou too repeatedly record them for thyself on the table of thine heart, for counsel and knowledge. \textsuperscript{21} I therefore teach thee truth, and knowledge good to hear; that thou mayest answer words of truth to them that question thee.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 22:18 TSK note: it is, ;, ; within thee Heb. within thy belly, ; fitted\par
Proverbs 22:19 TSK note: thy; , ; even to thee or, trust thou also\par
Proverbs 22:21 Brenton note: See 1 Pet. 3. 15.\par
Proverbs 22:21 TSK note: I; answer them that send unto thee or, those that send thee\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} Do no violence to the poor, for he is needy: neither dishonour the helpless man in the gates. \textsuperscript{23} For the Lord will plead his cause, and thou shalt deliver thy soul in safety.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 22:22 TSK note: Rob; oppress; , ; in the gate That is, in the court of justice, which, as we have already seen, was held at the gates of cities in the East.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} Be not companion to a furious man; neither lodge with a passionate man: \textsuperscript{25} lest thou learn of his ways, and get snares to thy soul.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{26} Become not surety from respect of a man's person. \textsuperscript{27} For if those have not whence to give compensation, they will take the bed that is under thee. \textsuperscript{28} Remove not the old landmarks, which thy fathers placed.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 22:28 Brenton note: Gr. eternal.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{29} It is fit that an observant man and one diligent in his business should attend on kings, and not attend on slothful men.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 22:29 TSK note: a man, ; , ; he shall stand That is, he shall have the honour of serving kings; as the phrase denotes. mean men Heb. obscure men\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 23}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} If thou sit to sup at the table of a prince, consider attentively the things set before thee: \textsuperscript{2} and apply thine hand, knowing that it behoves thee to prepare such meats : but if thou art very insatiable, \textsuperscript{3} desire not his provisions; for these belong to a false life.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} If thou art poor, measure not thyself with a rich man; but refrain thyself in thy wisdom. \textsuperscript{5} If thou shouldest fix thine eye upon him, he will disappear; for wings like an eagle's are prepared for him, and he returns to the house of his master. \textsuperscript{6} Sup not with an envious man, neither desire thou his meats: \textsuperscript{7} so he eats and drinks as if any one should swallow a hair, and do not bring him in to thyself, nor eat thy morsel with him: \textsuperscript{8} for he will vomit it up, and spoil thy fair words.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 23:5 TSK note: thou; set thine eyes upon Heb. cause thine eyes to fly upon, etc. "He expresses it in such a way, " says Abp. Tillotson, "as if a rich man sat brooding over an estate till it was fledged, and gotten itself wings to fly away." that which;, ; riches\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Say nothing in the ears of a fool, lest at any time he sneer at thy wise words. \textsuperscript{10} Remove not the ancient landmarks; and enter not upon the possession of the fatherless: \textsuperscript{11} for the Lord is their redeemer; he is mighty, and will plead their cause with thee. \textsuperscript{12} Apply thine heart to instruction, and prepare thine ears for words of discretion.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 23:10 TSK note: Remove;, ; landmark or, bound fatherless\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Refrain not from chastening a child; for if thou beat him with the rod, he shall not die. \textsuperscript{14} For thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from death.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} Son, if thy heart be wise, thou shalt also gladden my heart; \textsuperscript{16} and thy lips shall converse with my lips, if they be right. \textsuperscript{17} Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day. \textsuperscript{18} For if thou shouldest keep these things, thou shalt have posterity; and thine hope shall not be removed.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 23:15 TSK note: My son, ; if, ;, ; even mine or, even I will rejoice\par
Proverbs 23:18 TSK note: surely; end or, reward, ; thine\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} Hear, my son, and be wise, and rightly direct the thoughts of thine heart. \textsuperscript{20} Be not a wine-bibber, neither continue long at feasts, and purchases of flesh: \textsuperscript{21} for every drunkard and whoremonger shall be poor; and every sluggard shall clothe himself with tatters and ragged garments.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 23:19 TSK note: and guide, in the way That is "in the right way."\par
Proverbs 23:20 TSK note: not, ;, ; , ; flesh Heb. their flesh\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} Hearken, my son, to thy father which begot thee, and despise not thy mother because she is grown old. \textsuperscript{24} A righteous father brings up his children well; and his soul rejoices over a wise son. \textsuperscript{25} Let thy father and thy mother rejoice over thee, and let her that bore thee be glad.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{26} My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways. \textsuperscript{27} For a strange house is a vessel full of holes; and a strange well is narrow. \textsuperscript{28} For such a one shall perish suddenly; and every transgressor shall be cut off.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 23:28 TSK note: as for a prey or, as a robber, ; increaseth\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{29} Who has woe? who trouble? who has quarrels? and who vexations and disputes? who has bruises without a cause? whose eyes are livid? \textsuperscript{30} Are not those of them that stay long at wine? are not those of them that haunt the places where banquets are? Be not drunk with wine; but converse with just men, and converse with them openly. \textsuperscript{31} For if thou shouldest set thine eyes on bowls and cups, thou shalt afterwards go more naked than a pestle. \textsuperscript{32} But at last such a one stretches himself out as one smitten by a serpent, and venom is diffused through him as by a horned serpent.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 23:30 Brenton note: Gr. in public walks.\par
Proverbs 23:30 TSK note: tarry; mixed That is, not wine diluted and lowered with water, but made stronger and more inebriating, by the addition of more powerful ingredients, as honey, spices, myrrh, defrutum, opiates, etc.\par
Proverbs 23:32 TSK note: At;, ; , ; biteth; , an adder or, a cockatrice\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{33} Whenever thine eyes shall behold a strange woman, then thy mouth shall speak perverse things. \textsuperscript{34} And thou shalt lie as in the midst of the sea, and as a pilot in a great storm. \textsuperscript{35} And thou shalt say, They smote me, and I was not pained; and they mocked me, and I knew it not: when will it be morning, that I may go and seek those with whom I may go in company?\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 23:35 TSK note: stricken;, I felt it not Heb. I knew it not, I will\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 24}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} My son, envy not bad men, nor desire to be with them. \textsuperscript{2} For their heart meditates falsehoods, and their lips speak mischiefs. \textsuperscript{3} A house is built by wisdom, and is set up by understanding. \textsuperscript{4} By discretion the chambers are filled with all precious and excellent wealth. \textsuperscript{5} A wise man is better than a strong man; and a man who has prudence than a large estate. \textsuperscript{6} War is carried on with generalship, and aid is supplied to the heart of a counsellor.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 24:5 TSK note: A wise, ;, strong Heb. in strength increaseth strength Heb. strengtheneth might.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Wisdom and good understanding are in the gates of the wise: the wise turn not aside from the mouth of the Lord, \textsuperscript{8} but deliberate in council. Death befalls uninstructed men . \textsuperscript{9} The fool also dies in sins; and uncleanness attaches to a pestilent man. \textsuperscript{10} He shall be defiled in the evil day, and in the day of affliction, until he be utterly consumed.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Deliver them that are led away to death, and redeem them that are appointed to be slain; spare not thy help . \textsuperscript{12} But if thou shouldest say, I know not this man; know that the Lord knows the hearts of all; and he that formed breath for all, he knows all things, who renders to every man according to his works. \textsuperscript{13} My son, eat honey, for the honeycomb is good, that thy throat may be sweetened. \textsuperscript{14} Thus shalt thou perceive wisdom in thy soul: for if thou find it, thine end shall be good, and hope shall not fail thee.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 24:12 TSK note: doth not he that, ; , ; , that keepeth, ;, ; and shall\par
Proverbs 24:13 TSK note: eat, ; to thy taste Heb. upon thy palate\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} Bring not an ungodly man into the dwelling of the righteous: neither be deceived by the feeding of the belly. \textsuperscript{16} For a righteous man will fall seven times, and rise again : but the ungodly shall be without strength in troubles. \textsuperscript{17} If thine enemy should fall, rejoice not over him, neither be elated at his overthrow. \textsuperscript{18} For the Lord will see it , and it will not please him, and he will turn away his wrath from him. \textsuperscript{19} Rejoice not in evil-doers, neither be envious of sinners. \textsuperscript{20} For the evil man shall have no posterity: and the light of the wicked shall be put out.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 24:18 TSK note: displease him Heb. be evil in his eyes and he\par
Proverbs 24:19 TSK note: Fret or, Keep not company with the wicked.; , ; neither\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} My son, fear God and the king; and do not disobey either of them. \textsuperscript{22} For they will suddenly punish the ungodly, and who can know the vengeance inflicted by both?\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 24:21 TSK note: fear; meddle;, ; given to change Heb. changers\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} And this thing I say to you that are wise for you to learn: It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment. \textsuperscript{24} He that says of the ungodly, He is righteous, shall be cursed by peoples, and hateful among the nations. \textsuperscript{25} But they that reprove him shall appear more excellent, and blessing shall come upon them; \textsuperscript{26} and men will kiss lips that answer well. \textsuperscript{27} Prepare thy works for thy going forth, and prepare thyself for the field; and come after me, and thou shalt rebuild thine house. \textsuperscript{28} Be not a false witness against thy fellow citizen, neither exaggerate with thy lips. \textsuperscript{29} Say not, As he has treated me, so will I treat him, and I will avenge myself on him for that wherein he has injured me. \textsuperscript{30} A foolish man is like a farm, and a senseless man is like a vineyard. \textsuperscript{31} If thou let him alone, he will altogether remain barren and covered with weeds; and he becomes destitute, and his stone walls are broken down. \textsuperscript{32} Afterwards I reflected, I looked that I might receive instruction. \textsuperscript{33} The sluggard says , I slumber a little, and I sleep a little, and for a little while I fold my arms across my breast. \textsuperscript{34} But if thou do this, thy poverty will come speedily; and thy want like a swift courier.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 24:25 TSK note: them; , ; , a good blessing Heb. a blessing of good\par
Proverbs 24:26 TSK note: shall, ; , giveth a right answer Heb. answereth right words\par
Proverbs 24:31 Brenton note: Gr. grass.\par
Proverbs 24:32 TSK note: considered it Heb. set my heart, ; , I looked\par
Proverbs 24:34 TSK note: thy poverty, armed man Heb. a man of shield\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{35} The horse-leech had three dearly-beloved daughters: and these three did not satisfy her; and the fourth was not contented so as to say, Enough. \textsuperscript{36} The grave, and the love of a woman, and the earth not filled with water; water also and fire will not say, It is enough.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{37} The eye that laughs to scorn a father, and dishonours the old age of a mother, let the ravens of the valleys pick it out, and let the young eagles devour it. \textsuperscript{38} Moreover there are three things impossible for me to comprehend, and the fourth I know not: \textsuperscript{39} the track of a flying eagle; and the ways of a serpent on a rock; and the paths of a ship passing through the sea; and the ways of a man in youth. \textsuperscript{40} Such is the way of an adulterous woman, who having washed herself from what she has done, says she has done nothing amiss.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{41} By three things the earth is troubled, and the fourth it cannot bear: \textsuperscript{42} if a servant reign; or a fool be filled with food; \textsuperscript{43} or if a maid-servant should cast out her own mistress; and if a hateful woman should marry a good man.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{44} And there are four very little things upon the earth, but these are wiser than the wise: \textsuperscript{45} the ants which are weak, and yet prepare their food in summer; \textsuperscript{46} the rabbits also are a feeble race, who make their houses in the rocks. \textsuperscript{47} The locusts have no king, and yet march orderly at one command. \textsuperscript{48} And the eft, which supports itself by its hands, and is easily taken, dwells in the fortresses of kings.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{49} And there are three things which go well, and a fourth which passes along finely. \textsuperscript{50} A lion's whelp, stronger than all other beasts, which turns not away, nor fears any beast; \textsuperscript{51} and a cock walking in boldly among the hens, and a goat leading the herd; and a king publicly speaking before a nation.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{52} If thou abandon thyself to mirth, and stretch forth thine hand in a quarrel, thou shalt be disgraced. \textsuperscript{53} Milk out milk, and there shall be butter, and if thou wring one's nostrils there shall come out blood: so if thou extort words, there will come forth quarrels and strifes.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{54} My words have been spoken by God—the oracular answer of a king, whom his mother instructed.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{55} What wilt thou keep, my son, what? the words of God. My firstborn son, I speak to thee: what? son of my womb? what? son of my vows? \textsuperscript{56} Give not thy wealth to women, nor thy mind and living to remorse. Do all things with counsel: drink wine with counsel. \textsuperscript{57} Princes are prone to anger: let them then not drink wine: \textsuperscript{58} lest they drink, and forget wisdom, and be not able to judge the poor rightly. \textsuperscript{59} Give strong drink to those that are in sorrow, and the wine to drink to those in pain: \textsuperscript{60} that they may forget their poverty, and may not remember their troubles any more. \textsuperscript{61} Open thy mouth with the word of God, and judge all fairly. \textsuperscript{62} Open thy mouth and judge justly, and plead the cause of the poor and weak.\par
\subsection*{Proverbs 25}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} These are the miscellaneous instructions of Solomon, which the friends of Ezekias king of Judea copied out.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 25:1 Brenton note: Possibly genuine, q. d. beyond doubt.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} The glory of God conceals a matter: but the glory of a king honours business. \textsuperscript{3} Heaven is high, and earth is deep, and a king's heart is unsearchable. \textsuperscript{4} Beat the drossy silver, and it shall be made entirely pure. \textsuperscript{5} Slay the ungodly from before the king, and his throne shall prosper in righteousness.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 25:3 TSK note: heaven;, ; is unsearchable Heb. there is no searching\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} Be not boastful in the presence of the king, and remain not in the places of princes; \textsuperscript{7} for it is better for thee that it should be said, Come up to me, than that one should humble thee in the presence of the prince; speak of that which thine eyes have seen.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 25:6 TSK note: Put not forth thyself Heb. Set not out thy glory, in the presence\par
Proverbs 25:7 TSK note: that it; Come Be humble; affect not high things; keep thyself quiet; and thou shalt live at ease, in safety, and in peace. than\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} Get not suddenly into a quarrel, lest thou repent at last. \textsuperscript{9} Whenever thy friend shall reproach thee, retreat backward, despise him not; \textsuperscript{10} lest thy friend continue to reproach thee, so thy quarrel and enmity shall not depart, but shall be to thee like death.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 25:9 TSK note: with a secret to another or, the secret of another\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} As a golden apple in a necklace of sardius, so is it to speak a wise word. \textsuperscript{12} In an ear-ring of gold a precious sardius is also set; so is a wise word to an obedient ear. \textsuperscript{13} As a fall of snow in the time of harvest is good against heat, so a faithful messenger refreshes those that send him; for he helps the souls of his employers.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 25:11 TSK note: word, ; fitly spoken Heb. spoken upon his wheels is like Rather "is like golden apples ( tappuchim, in Arabic, tuffach ), in baskets ( maskeeyoth, in Arabic, shakeekat ), of silver." A word spoken with propriety, opportunely, and suitably to the occasion, is as much in its place, and as conspicuously beautiful, as the golden fruit which appears through the apertures of an exquisitely wrought silver basket.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} As winds and clouds and rains are most evident objects , so is he that boasts of a false gift. \textsuperscript{15} In long-suffering is prosperity to kings, and a soft tongue breaks the bones. \textsuperscript{16} Having found honey, eat only what is enough, lest haply thou be filled, and vomit it up. \textsuperscript{17} Enter sparingly into thy friend's house, lest he be satiated with thy company, and hate thee. \textsuperscript{18} As a club, and a dagger, and a pointed arrow, so also is a man who bears false witness against his friend. \textsuperscript{19} The way of the wicked and the foot of the transgressor shall perish in an evil day.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 25:14 TSK note: boasteth; , ;, ; , of a false gift Heb. in a gift of falsehood\par
Proverbs 25:15 Brenton note: Greek background: makrothymia (μακροθυμία) = longsuffering; patience. Common English renderings: longsuffering. Literally long-tempered, especially toward persons.\par
Proverbs 25:15 TSK note: long, ; , ; the bone Rather, "a bone; " that is, soft and conciliating language will often accomplish the most difficult things.\par
Proverbs 25:17 TSK note: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's or, Let thy foot be seldom in thy neighbour's, ; weary Heb. full\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} As vinegar is bad for a sore, so trouble befalling the body afflicts the heart.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} If thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink; \textsuperscript{22} for so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee with good. \textsuperscript{23} The north wind raises clouds; so an impudent face provokes the tongue. \textsuperscript{24} It is better to dwell on a corner of the roof, than with a railing woman in an open house. \textsuperscript{25} As cold water is agreeable to a thirsting soul, so is a good message from a land far off. \textsuperscript{26} As if one should stop a well, and corrupt a spring of water, so is it unseemly for a righteous man to fall before an ungodly man. \textsuperscript{27} It is not good to eat much honey; but it is right to honour venerable sayings. \textsuperscript{28} As a city whose walls are broken down, and which is unfortified, so is a man who does anything without counsel.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 25:22 TSK note: For Not to consume, but to melt him into kindness; a metaphor taken from smelting metalic ores. the Lord\par
Proverbs 25:23 TSK note: north driveth etc. or, bringeth forth rain; so doth a backbiting tongue an angry countenance, Monconys says, that when travelling on the second of January, 1648, from Tripoli in Syria, between Lebanon and the sea, it rained without ceasing, while the north wind blew directly in his face. so\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Proverbs 26}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} As dew in harvest, and as rain in summer, so honour is not seemly for a fool. \textsuperscript{2} As birds and sparrows fly, so a curse shall not come upon any one without a cause. \textsuperscript{3} As a whip for a horse, and a goad for an ass, so is a rod for a simple nation. \textsuperscript{4} Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou become like him. \textsuperscript{5} Yet answer a fool according to his folly, lest he seem wise in his own conceit. \textsuperscript{6} He that sends a message by a foolish messenger procures for himself a reproach from his own ways. \textsuperscript{7} As well take away the motion of the legs, as transgression from the mouth of fools. \textsuperscript{8} He that binds up a stone in a sling, is like one that gives glory to a fool. \textsuperscript{9} Thorns grow in the hand of a drunkard, and servitude in the hand of fools. \textsuperscript{10} All the flesh of fools endures much hardship; for their fury is brought to nought. \textsuperscript{11} As when a dog goes to his own vomit, and becomes abominable, so is a fool who returns in his wickedness to his own sin. \textsuperscript{12} I have seen a man who seemed to himself to be wise; but a fool had more hope than he. \textsuperscript{13} A sluggard when sent on a journey says, There is a lion in the ways, and there are murderers in the streets.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Proverbs 26:3 TSK note: According to our notions, we should rather say, a bridle for the horse, and a whip for the ass; but it should be considered, that the Eastern asses are not only much more beautiful, but better goers that ours; and being active and well broken, they need only a bridle to guide them; whereas their horses being scarce, and often caught wild, and badly broken, are much less manageable, and need the correction of the whip.\par
Proverbs 26:5 TSK note: a fool; , ;, ;, ; lest, ; conceit Heb. eyes\par
