\subsection*{Joel 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Sound the trumpet in Sion, make a proclamation in my holy mountain, and let all the inhabitants of the land be confounded: for the day of the Lord is near; \textsuperscript{2} for a day of darkness and gloominess is near, a day of cloud and mist: a numerous and strong people shall be spread upon the mountains as the morning; there has not been from the beginning one like it, and after it there shall not be again even to the years of many generations. \textsuperscript{3} Before them is a consuming fire, and behind them is a flame kindled: the land before them is as a paradise of delight, and behind them a desolate plain: and there shall none of them escape.\par

Joel 2:2 Brenton note: Gr. age.\par
Joel 2:2 TSK note: A day of darkness "The quantity of these insects, " says a French author, "is incredible to all who have not themselves witnessed their astonishing numbers; the whole earth is covered with them for the space of several leagues. The noise they make in browsing on the trees and herbage may be heard at a great distance, and resembles that of an army in secret. Wherever their myriads spread, the verdure of the country disappears; trees and plants, stripped of their leaves and reduced to their naked boughs and stems, cause the dreary image of winter to succeed in an instant to the rich scenery of spring. When these clouds of locusts take their flight, to surmount any obstacles or to traverse more rapidly a desert soil, the heavens may literally be said to be obscured by them.", ; , ; as a great, there;, ; many generations Heb. generation and generation, ; *marg.\par

\section*{Jonas}
\subsection*{Jonas 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now the word of the Lord came to Jonas the son of Amathi, saying, \textsuperscript{2} Rise, and go to Nineve, the great city, and preach in it; for the cry of its wickedness is come up to me. \textsuperscript{3} But Jonas rose up to flee to Tharsis from the presence of the Lord. And he went down to Joppa, and found a ship going to Tharsis: and he paid his fare, and went up into it, to sail with them to Tharsis from the presence of the Lord.\par

Jonas 1:3 TSK note: to flee; , ; , ; from, ;, ; Joppa; Tarshish As Jonah embarked at Joppa, a seaport on the Mediterranean, it was probably either Tarsus in Cilicia, or rather Tartessus in Spain, to which he intended to flee. \subsection*{Jonas 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And the word of the Lord came to Jonas the second time, saying, \textsuperscript{2} Rise, go to Nineve, the great city, and preach in it according to the former preaching which I spoke to thee of. \textsuperscript{3} And Jonas arose, and went to Nineve, as the Lord had spoken. Now Nineve was an exceeding great city, of about three days' journey. \textsuperscript{4} And Jonas began to enter into the city about a day's journey, and he proclaimed, and said, Yet three days, and Nineve shall be overthrown.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Jonas 3:2 TSK note: Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, was situated on the eastern bank of the river Tigris, opposite the present Mosul, about 280 miles north of Babylon, 400 ne of Damascus, in latitude 36 degrees 20 minutes n longitude 73 degrees 10 minutes e. It was not only a very ancient ( ), but also a very great city. Strabo says that it was much larger than Babylon, the circuit of which he estimates at 385 furlongs; and, according to Diodorus Siculus, it was an oblong parallelogram, extending 150 furlongs in length, 90 in breadth, and 480 in circumference, i.e., about 20 miles long, 12 broad, and 60 in compass. This agrees with the account given here of its being "an exceeding great city of three days' journey, " i.e., in circuit; for 20 miles a day was the common computation for a pedestrian. It was surrounded by large walls 100 feet high, so broad that three chariots could drive abreast on them, and defended by 1, 500 towers 200 feet in height. See notes on Nahum., ; preach\par
Jonas 3:3 Brenton note: Lit. a great city to God. Acts 7. 20.\par
Jonas 3:3 TSK note: So *marg. *marg. *marg. arose; an exceeding great city Heb. a city great of God\par
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Aggæus 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came by the hand of the prophet Aggæus, saying, Speak to Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, of the tribe of Juda, and to Jesus the son of Josedec, the high priest, saying, \textsuperscript{2} Thus saith the Lord Almighty, saying, This people say, The time is not come to build the house of the Lord. \textsuperscript{3} And the word of the Lord came by the hand of the prophet Aggæus, saying,\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Aggæus 1:1 Brenton note: Or, Joshua.\par
Aggæus 1:1 TSK note: second, ;, ; the sixth Elul the sixth month of the ecclesiastical year, answering to a part of September. by Haggai Heb. by the hand of Haggai, ; unto, ;, Salathiel, ; , Zorobabel, Salathiel, governor or, captain, ;, Joshua, ;, Josedech, Jehozadak\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Is it time for you to dwell in your ceiled houses, whereas our house is desolate?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} And now thus saith the Lord Almighty; Consider your ways, I pray you. \textsuperscript{6} Ye have sown much, but brought in little; ye have eaten, and are not satisfied; ye have drunk, and are not satisfied with drink, ye have clothed yourselves, and have not become warm thereby: and he that earns wages has gathered them into a bag full of holes.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Aggæus 1:5 TSK note: thus, ; Consider your ways Heb. Set your heart on your ways, *marg. *marg.\par
Aggæus 1:6 Brenton note: Gr. in them.\par
Aggæus 1:6 TSK note: have, ; , ; , eat; with holes Heb. pierced through\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Thus saith the Lord Almighty; Consider your ways. \textsuperscript{8} Go up to the mountain, and cut timber; build the house, and I will take pleasure in it, and be glorified, saith the Lord. \textsuperscript{9} Ye looked for much, and there came little; and it was brought into the house, and I blew it away. Therefore thus saith the Lord Almighty, Because my house is desolate, and ye run every one into his own house; \textsuperscript{10} therefore shall the sky withhold dew, and the earth shall keep back her produce. \textsuperscript{11} And I will bring a sword upon the land, and upon the mountains, and upon the corn, and upon the wine, and upon the oil, and all that the earth produces, and upon the men, and upon the cattle, and upon all the labours of their hands.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Aggæus 1:8 TSK note: to;, ; and build; and I will take; , I will be\par
Aggæus 1:9 TSK note: Ye looked They had used all proper means in the cultivation of their lands, and had "sown much; " but when they rationally entertained the most sanguine expectations of a large increase, they were strangely disappointed; and even what they had brought home was unaccountably wasted, as if the Lord had "blown upon it, " and driven it away! And the reason was, because they neglected the temple, and left it in ruins, whilst they eagerly employed themselves in building and decorating their own houses; therefore they were visited by drought and famine, and by various diseases on man and beast., ; blow upon it or, blow it away, ; Why; Because\par
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Aggæus 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the Lord spoke by Aggæus the prophet, saying, \textsuperscript{2} Speak now to Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, of the tribe of Juda, and to Jesus the son of Josedec, the high priest, and to all the remnant of the people, saying,\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Aggæus 2:1 TSK note: the seventh, the prophet Heb. the hand of the prophet, etc.\par
Aggæus 2:2 Brenton note: Or, Joshua.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} Who is there of you that saw this house in her former glory? and how do ye now look upon it, as it were nothing before your eyes? \textsuperscript{4} Yet now be strong, O Zorobabel, saith the Lord; and strengthen thyself, O Jesus the high priest, the son of Josedec; and let all the people of the land strengthen themselves, saith the Lord, and work, for I am with you, saith the Lord Almighty; \textsuperscript{5} and my Spirit remains in the midst of you; be of good courage.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Aggæus 2:3 Brenton note: Gr. not existing.\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} For thus saith the Lord Almighty; Yet once I will shake the heaven, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land ; \textsuperscript{7} and I will shake all nations, and the choice portions of all the nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory, saith the Lord Almighty. \textsuperscript{8} Mine is the silver, and mine the gold, saith the Lord Almighty. \textsuperscript{9} For the glory of this house shall be great, the latter more than the former, saith the Lord Almighty: and in this place will I give peace, saith the Lord Almighty, even peace of soul for a possession to every one that builds, to raise up this temple.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Aggæus 2:6 TSK note: Yet; it is;, ; and I\par
Aggæus 2:7 Brenton note: Or, objects.\par
Aggæus 2:7 TSK note: I will shake;, ; and the, ; , ; I will fill\par
Aggæus 2:9 Brenton note: Or, salvation.\par
Aggæus 2:9 TSK note: glory; saith Whoever compares the description of the temple of Solomon, in the first book of Kings, with the most splendid accounts of the second temple, however adorned with costly stones and other magnificent decorations in after ages, must perceive that the former, being wholly overlaid with pure gold, was incomparably more glorious than the latter in its greatest magnificence; and the Jews themselves allow that the ark of the covenant, fire from heaven, the Urim and Thummim the anointing oil, the Shechinah or visible glory, and the spirit of prophecy, which distinguished the former temple, were wanting in this. In nothing, in fact, could the second temple excel the first in glory, except in the personal presence of "the Desire of all nations, " He who is "the glory of the Lord, " and the true temple, "in whom dwells all the fulness of the Godhead bodily, " and who was the true Shechinah of which that of Solomon's temple was merely a type. And if it be admitted that the presence of the promised Messiah was intended, then it will follow that "Jesus of Nazareth" was He; for the second temple, in which as the "Prince of peace" he preached peace and reconciliation with God, has been utterly destroyed for upwards of seventeen hundred years. give\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} On the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the Lord came to Aggæus the prophet, saying, \textsuperscript{11} Thus saith the Lord Almighty; Inquire now of the priests concerning the law, saying, \textsuperscript{12} If a man should take holy flesh in the skirt of his garment, and the skirt of his garment should touch bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any meat, shall it be holy? And the priests answered and said, No. \textsuperscript{13} And Aggæus said, If a defiled person who is unclean by reason of a dead body, touch any of these, shall it be defiled? And the priests answered and said, It shall be defiled. \textsuperscript{14} And Aggæus answered and said, So is this people, and so is this nation before me, saith the Lord; and so are all the works of their hands: and whosoever shall approach them, shall be defiled [because of their early burdens: they shall be pained because of their toils; and ye have hated him that reproved in the gates]. \textsuperscript{15} And now consider, I pray you, from this day and beforetime, before they laid a stone on a stone in the temple of the Lord, what manner of men ye were. \textsuperscript{16} When ye cast into the corn-bin twenty measures of barley, and there were only ten measures of barley: and ye went to the vat to draw out fifty measures, and there were but twenty. \textsuperscript{17} I smote you with barrenness, and with blasting, and all the works of your hands with hail; yet ye returned not to me, saith the Lord.\par

Aggæus 2:16 TSK note: when one came to an\par
Aggæus 2:17 TSK note: with blasting;, ; with hail; in all; yet\par
\end{quote}
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Set your hearts now to think from this day and upward, from the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, even from the day when the foundation of the temple of the Lord was laid; \textsuperscript{19} consider in your hearts, whether this shall be known on the corn-floor, and whether yet the vine, and the fig-tree, and the pomegranate, and the olive-trees that bear no fruit are with you : from this day will I bless you .\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} And the word of the Lord came the second time to Aggæus the prophet, on the four and twentieth day of the month, saying, \textsuperscript{21} Speak to Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, of the tribe of Juda, saying,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} and I will overthrow the thrones of kings, and I will destroy the power of the kings of the nations; and I will overthrow chariots and riders; and the horses and their riders shall come down, every one by the sword striving against his brother. \textsuperscript{23} In that day, saith the Lord Almighty, I will take thee, O Zorobabel, the son of Salathiel, my servant, saith the Lord, and will make thee as a seal: for I have chosen thee, saith the Lord Almighty.\par

\section*{Zacharias}

\noindent \textsuperscript{4} And I will bring it forth, saith the Lord Almighty, and it shall enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him that swears falsely by my name: and it shall rest in the midst of his house, and shall consume it, and the timber of it, and the stones of it.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} And the angel that talked with me went forth, and said to me, Lift up thine eyes, and see this that goes forth. \textsuperscript{6} And I said, What is it? And he said, This is the measure that goes forth. And he said, This is their iniquity in all the earth. \textsuperscript{7} And behold a talent of lead lifted up: and behold a woman sat in the midst of the measure. \textsuperscript{8} And he said, This is iniquity. And he cast it into the midst of the measure, and cast the weight of lead on the mouth of it. \textsuperscript{9} And I lifted up mine eyes, and saw, and, behold, two women coming forth, and the wind was in their wings; and they had stork's wings: and they lifted up the measure between the earth and the sky. \textsuperscript{10} And I said to the angel that spoke with me, Whither do these carry away the measure? \textsuperscript{11} And he said to me, To build it a house in the land of Babylon, and to prepare a place for it ; and they shall set it there on its own base.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Zacharias 5:6 TSK note: This is an ephah "The meaning of this vision, " says Archbishop Newcome, "seems to be, that the Babylonish captivity had happened on account of the wickedness of the Jews, and that a like dispersion would befall them if they relapsed into like crimes." The woman who sat in the ephah was an emblem of the Jewish nation; the casting the weight of lead on the mouth of the ephah seems to mean the condemnation of the Jews, after they had filled up the measure of their iniquities by crucifying the Messiah; the "two women, with wings like a stork, and the wind in their wings, " seem emblematical of the Roman armies and the rapidity of their conquests; and their lifting up the ephah and carrying it through the air, to build it a house in Shinar or Babylon, where it was fixed on its own basis, represents the taking of Jerusalem, the dispersion of the Jews, and the long continuance of that calamity, as a just punishment of their unbelief.\par
Zacharias 5:7 Brenton note: Heb. and Gr. one woman. see ver. 9.\par
Zacharias 5:7 TSK note: talent or, weighty piece, is;, ; Hosea 1:1-3:5\par
Zacharias 5:11 Brenton note: Gr. preparation.\par
\end{quote}

Zacharias 14:21 TSK note: every;, ; no more, ; *marg.; , in the; The predictions contained in this chapter seem to relate to events which gradually extend from the death of Christ to the glorious days of the millennium - the destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans, whose armies were composed of many nations, which was "the day of the Lord, " in which he came "to destroy those who would not that he should reign over them, " ( ); the subversion of the Roman empire, after being the executioners of the Divine vengeance on the Jews, by God's stirring up the barbarous nations to invade them ( ); the effusion of Divine knowledge from Jerusalem, by the promulgation of the Gospel ( ); the rebuilding and replenishing of Jerusalem ( ); the destruction of the nations who shall fight against her ( ); the conversion of the remnant of those nations to the Lord ( ); and the peace and purity of the universal church in the latter days ( ).\par
\end{quote}

\noindent \textsuperscript{10} The year is completed, and ye have brought all the produce into the storehouses; but there shall be the plunder thereof in its house: return now on this behalf, saith the Lord Almighty, see if I will not open to you the torrents of heaven, and pour out my blessing upon you, until ye are satisfied. \textsuperscript{11} And I will appoint food for you, and I will not destroy the fruit of your land; and your vine in the field shall not fail, saith the Lord Almighty. \textsuperscript{12} And all nations shall call you blessed: for ye shall be a desirable land, saith the Lord Almighty.\par

\noindent \textsuperscript{20} But to you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise, and healing shall be in his wings: and ye shall go forth, and bound as young calves let loose from bonds. \textsuperscript{21} And ye shall trample the wicked; for they shall be ashes underneath your feet in the day which I appoint, saith the Lord Almighty. \textsuperscript{22} And, behold, I will send to you Elias the Thesbite, before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes; \textsuperscript{23} who shall turn again the heart of the father to the son, and the heart of a man to his neighbour, lest I come and smite the earth grievously.\par

\section*{Matthew}
\subsection*{Matthew 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham. \textsuperscript{2} Abraham brings forth Isaac; and Isaac brings forth Jacob; and Jacob brings forth Judas and his brethren; \textsuperscript{3} And Judas brings forth Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares brings forth Esrom; and Esrom brings forth Aram; \textsuperscript{4} And Aram brings forth Aminadab; and Aminadab brings forth Naasson; and Naasson brings forth Salmon; \textsuperscript{5} And Salmon brings forth Booz of Rachab; and Booz brings forth Obed of Ruth; and Obed brings forth Jesse; \textsuperscript{6} And Jesse brings forth David the king; and David the king brings forth Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias; \textsuperscript{7} And Solomon brings forth Roboam; and Roboam brings forth Abia; and Abia brings forth Asa; \textsuperscript{8} And Asa brings forth Josaphat; and Josaphat brings forth Joram; and Joram brings forth Ozias; \textsuperscript{9} And Ozias brings forth Joatham; and Joatham brings forth Achaz; and Achaz brings forth Ezekias; \textsuperscript{10} And Ezekias brings forth Manasses; and Manasses brings forth Amon; and Amon brings forth Josias; \textsuperscript{11} And Josias brings forth Jechonias and his brethren, about the time they were carried away to Babylon: \textsuperscript{12} And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias brings forth Salathiel; and Salathiel brings forth Zorobabel; \textsuperscript{13} And Zorobabel brings forth Abiud; and Abiud brings forth Eliakim; and Eliakim brings forth Azor; \textsuperscript{14} And Azor brings forth Sadoc; and Sadoc brings forth Achim; and Achim brings forth Eliud; \textsuperscript{15} And Eliud brings forth Eleazar; and Eleazar brings forth Matthan; and Matthan brings forth Jacob; \textsuperscript{16} And Jacob brings forth Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ. \textsuperscript{17} So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Christ are fourteen generations. \textsuperscript{18} Now the birth of Jesus Christ was likewise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{19} Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a public example, was minded to put her away privately. \textsuperscript{20} But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, you son of David, fear not to take unto you Mary your wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{21} And she shall bring forth a son, and you shall call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. \textsuperscript{22} Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, \textsuperscript{23} Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us. \textsuperscript{24} Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife: \textsuperscript{25} And had sexual contact with her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem, \textsuperscript{2} Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him. \textsuperscript{3} When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him. \textsuperscript{4} And when he had gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people together, he demanded of them where Christ should be born. \textsuperscript{5} And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet, \textsuperscript{6} And you Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, are not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of you shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel. \textsuperscript{7} Then Herod, when he had privately called the wise men, enquired of them diligently what time the star appeared. \textsuperscript{8} And he sent them to Bethlehem, and said, Go and search diligently for the young child; and when all of you have found him, bring me word again, that I may come and worship him also. \textsuperscript{9} When they had heard the king, they departed; and, lo, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was. \textsuperscript{10} When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy. \textsuperscript{11} And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense and myrrh. \textsuperscript{12} And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way. \textsuperscript{13} And when they were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appears to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be you there until I bring you word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him. \textsuperscript{14} When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt: \textsuperscript{15} And was there until the death of Herod: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet, saying, Out of Egypt have I called my son. \textsuperscript{16} Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding angry, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men. \textsuperscript{17} Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, \textsuperscript{18} In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not. \textsuperscript{19} But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appears in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, \textsuperscript{20} Saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel: for they are dead which sought the young child's life. \textsuperscript{21} And he arose, and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel. \textsuperscript{22} But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee: \textsuperscript{23} And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea, \textsuperscript{2} And saying, Repent all of you: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. \textsuperscript{3} For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Isaiah, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare all of you the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. \textsuperscript{4} And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his food was locusts and wild honey. \textsuperscript{5} Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan, \textsuperscript{6} And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins. \textsuperscript{7} But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who has warned you to flee from the wrath to come? \textsuperscript{8} Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: \textsuperscript{9} And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham. \textsuperscript{10} And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which brings not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. \textsuperscript{11} I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance. but he that comes after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) and with fire: \textsuperscript{12} Whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire. \textsuperscript{13} Then comes Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him. \textsuperscript{14} But John forbad him, saying, I have need to be baptized of you, and come you to me? \textsuperscript{15} And Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becomes us to fulfill all righteousness. Then he suffered him. \textsuperscript{16} And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up immediately out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit (o. pneuma) of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him: \textsuperscript{17} And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then was Jesus led up of the spirit (o. pneuma) into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil. \textsuperscript{2} And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungered. \textsuperscript{3} And when the tempter came to him, he said, If you be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread. \textsuperscript{4} But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word (o. rhema) that proceeds out of the mouth of God. \textsuperscript{5} Then the devil takes him up into the holy city, and sets him on a pinnacle of the temple, \textsuperscript{6} And says unto him, If you be the Son of God, cast yourself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning you: and in their hands they shall bear you up, lest at any time you dash your foot against a stone. \textsuperscript{7} Jesus said unto him, It is written again, You shall not tempt the Lord your God. \textsuperscript{8} Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them; \textsuperscript{9} And says unto him, All these things will I give you, if you will fall down and worship me. \textsuperscript{10} Then says Jesus unto him, Get you behind, Satan: for it is written, You shall worship the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve. \textsuperscript{11} Then the devil left him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him. \textsuperscript{12} Now when Jesus had heard that John was cast into prison, he departed into Galilee; \textsuperscript{13} And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim: \textsuperscript{14} That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, saying, \textsuperscript{15} The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles; \textsuperscript{16} The people which sat in darkness saw great light; and to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up. \textsuperscript{17} From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. \textsuperscript{18} And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. \textsuperscript{19} And he says unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. \textsuperscript{20} And they immediately left their nets, and followed him. \textsuperscript{21} And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. \textsuperscript{22} And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him. \textsuperscript{23} And Jesus went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people. \textsuperscript{24} And his fame went throughout all Syria: and they brought unto him all sick people that were taken with divers diseases and torments, and those which were possessed with devils, and those which were lunatic, and those that had the palsy; and he healed them. \textsuperscript{25} And there followed him great multitudes of people from Galilee, and from Decapolis, and from Jerusalem, and from Judaea, and from beyond Jordan.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And seeing the multitudes, he went up into a mountain: and when he was set, his disciples came unto him: \textsuperscript{2} And he opened his mouth, and taught them, saying, \textsuperscript{3} Blessed are the poor in spirit: (o. pneuma) for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. \textsuperscript{4} Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted. \textsuperscript{5} Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth. \textsuperscript{6} Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled. \textsuperscript{7} Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy. \textsuperscript{8} Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God. \textsuperscript{9} Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God. \textsuperscript{10} Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. \textsuperscript{11} Blessed are all of you, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil (o. rhema) against you falsely, for my sake. \textsuperscript{12} Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you. \textsuperscript{13} All of you are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men. \textsuperscript{14} All of you are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid. \textsuperscript{15} Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it gives light unto all that are in the house. \textsuperscript{16} Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven. \textsuperscript{17} Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfill. \textsuperscript{18} For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled. \textsuperscript{19} Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven. \textsuperscript{20} For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, all of you shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven. \textsuperscript{21} All of you have heard that it was said of them of old time, You shall not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment: \textsuperscript{22} But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, You fool, shall be in danger of hell fire. \textsuperscript{23} Therefore if you bring your gift to the altar, and there remember that your brother has ought against you; \textsuperscript{24} Leave there your gift before the altar, and go your way; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift. \textsuperscript{25} Agree with yours adversary quickly, while you are in the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and you be cast into prison. \textsuperscript{26} Verily I say unto you, You shall by no means come out thence, till you have paid the uttermost farthing. \textsuperscript{27} All of you have heard that it was said by them of old time, You shall not commit adultery: \textsuperscript{28} But I say unto you, That whosoever looks on a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart. \textsuperscript{29} And if your right eye offend you, pluck it out, and cast it from you: for it is profitable for you that one of your members should perish, and not that your whole body should be cast into hell. \textsuperscript{30} And if your right hand offend you, cut it off, and cast it from you: for it is profitable for you that one of your members should perish, and not that your whole body should be cast into hell. \textsuperscript{31} It has been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement: \textsuperscript{32} But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause (o. logos) of fornication, causes her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced commits adultery. \textsuperscript{33} Again, all of you have heard that it has been said by them of old time, You shall not renounce swearing yourself, but shall perform unto the Lord yours oaths: \textsuperscript{34} But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: \textsuperscript{35} Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. \textsuperscript{36} Neither shall you swear by your head, because you can not make one hair white or black. \textsuperscript{37} But let your communication (o. logos) be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these comes of evil. \textsuperscript{38} All of you have heard that it has been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: \textsuperscript{39} But I say unto you, That all of you resist not evil: but whosoever shall strike you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also. \textsuperscript{40} And if any man will sue you at the law, and take away your coat, let him have your cloak also. \textsuperscript{41} And whosoever shall compel you to go a mile, go with him two. \textsuperscript{42} Give to him that asks you, and from him that would borrow of you turn not you away. \textsuperscript{43} All of you have heard that it has been said, You shall love your neighbour, and hate yours enemy. \textsuperscript{44} But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; \textsuperscript{45} That all of you may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he makes his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the just and on the unjust. \textsuperscript{46} For if all of you love them which love you, what reward have all of you? do not even the publicans the same? \textsuperscript{47} And if all of you salute your brethren only, what do all of you more than others? do not even the publicans so? \textsuperscript{48} Be all of you therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 6}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Take heed that all of you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise all of you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven. \textsuperscript{2} Therefore when you do yours alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. \textsuperscript{3} But when you do alms, let not your left hand know what your right hand does: \textsuperscript{4} That yours alms may be in secret: and your Father which sees in secret himself shall reward you openly. \textsuperscript{5} And when you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. \textsuperscript{6} But you, when you pray, enter into your closet, and when you have shut your door, pray to your Father which is in secret; and your Father which sees in secret shall reward you openly. \textsuperscript{7} But when all of you pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking. \textsuperscript{8} Be not all of you therefore like unto them: for your Father knows what things all of you have need of, before all of you ask him. \textsuperscript{9} After this manner therefore pray all of you: Our Father which are in heaven, Hallowed be your name. \textsuperscript{10} Your kingdom come, Your will be done in earth, as it is in heaven. \textsuperscript{11} Give us this day our daily bread. \textsuperscript{12} And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. \textsuperscript{13} And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen. \textsuperscript{14} For if all of you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you: \textsuperscript{15} But if all of you forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses. \textsuperscript{16} Moreover when all of you fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. \textsuperscript{17} But you, when you fast, anoint yours head, and wash your face; \textsuperscript{18} That you appear not unto men to fast, but unto your Father which is in secret: and your Father, which sees in secret, shall reward you openly. \textsuperscript{19} Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust does corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: \textsuperscript{20} But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust does corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: \textsuperscript{21} For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. \textsuperscript{22} The light of the body is the eye: if therefore yours eye be single, your whole body shall be full of light. \textsuperscript{23} But if yours eye be evil, your whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you be darkness, how great is that darkness! \textsuperscript{24} No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. All of you cannot serve God and mammon. \textsuperscript{25} Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what all of you shall eat, or what all of you shall drink; nor yet for your body, what all of you shall put on. Is not the life more than food, and the body than raiment? \textsuperscript{26} Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are all of you not much better than they? \textsuperscript{27} Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature? \textsuperscript{28} And why take all of you thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin: \textsuperscript{29} And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. \textsuperscript{30} Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and tomorrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O all of you of little faith? \textsuperscript{31} Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed? \textsuperscript{32} (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knows that all of you have need of all these things. \textsuperscript{33} But seek all of you first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. \textsuperscript{34} Take therefore no thought for the next day: for the next day shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 7}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Judge not, that all of you be not judged. \textsuperscript{2} For with what judgment all of you judge, all of you shall be judged: and with what measure all of you mete, it shall be measured to you again. \textsuperscript{3} And why behold you the splinter that is in your brother's eye, but consider not the beam that is in yours own eye? \textsuperscript{4} Or how will you say to your brother, Let me pull out the splinter out of yours eye; and, behold, a beam is in yours own eye? \textsuperscript{5} You hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of yours own eye; and then shall you see clearly to cast out the splinter out of your brother's eye. \textsuperscript{6} Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast all of you your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and return and rend you. \textsuperscript{7} Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and all of you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you: \textsuperscript{8} For every one that asks receives; and he that seeks finds; and to him that knocks it shall be opened. \textsuperscript{9} Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone? \textsuperscript{10} Or if he ask a fish, will he give him a serpent? \textsuperscript{11} If all of you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him? \textsuperscript{12} Therefore all things whatsoever all of you would that men should do to you, do all of you even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets. \textsuperscript{13} Enter all of you in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leads to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: \textsuperscript{14} Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leads unto life, and few there be that find it. \textsuperscript{15} Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. \textsuperscript{16} All of you shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? \textsuperscript{17} Even so every good tree brings forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree brings forth evil fruit. \textsuperscript{18} A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. \textsuperscript{19} Every tree that brings not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. \textsuperscript{20} Wherefore by their fruits all of you shall know them. \textsuperscript{21} Not every one that says unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that does the will of my Father which is in heaven. \textsuperscript{22} Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in your name? and in your name have cast out devils? and in your name done many wonderful works? \textsuperscript{23} And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, all of you that work iniquity. \textsuperscript{24} Therefore whosoever hears these sayings (o. logos) of mine, and does them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: \textsuperscript{25} And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock. \textsuperscript{26} And every one that hears these sayings (o. logos) of mine, and does them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand: \textsuperscript{27} And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it. \textsuperscript{28} And it came to pass, when Jesus had ended these sayings, (o. logos) the people were astonished at his doctrine: \textsuperscript{29} For he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.\par

\end{quote}
\subsection*{Matthew 8}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} When he was come down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him. \textsuperscript{2} And, behold, there came a leper and worshipped him, saying, Lord, if you will, you can make me clean. \textsuperscript{3} And Jesus put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be you clean. And immediately his leprosy was cleansed. \textsuperscript{4} And Jesus says unto him, See you tell no man; but go your way, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them. \textsuperscript{5} And when Jesus was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him, \textsuperscript{6} And saying, Lord, my servant lies at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented. \textsuperscript{7} And Jesus says unto him, I will come and heal him. \textsuperscript{8} The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that you should come under my roof: but speak the word (o. logos) only, and my servant shall be healed. \textsuperscript{9} For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goes; and to another, Come, and he comes; and to my servant, Do this, and he does it. \textsuperscript{10} When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel. \textsuperscript{11} And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven. \textsuperscript{12} But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. \textsuperscript{13} And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go your way; and as you have believed, so be it done unto you. And his servant was healed in the very same hour. \textsuperscript{14} And when Jesus was come into Peter's house, he saw his wife's mother laid, and sick of a fever. \textsuperscript{15} And he touched her hand, and the fever left her: and she arose, and ministered unto them. \textsuperscript{16} When the even was come, they brought unto him many that were possessed with devils: and he cast out the spirits (o. pneuma) with his word, (o. logos) and healed all that were sick: \textsuperscript{17} That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, saying, Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses. \textsuperscript{18} Now when Jesus saw great multitudes about him, he gave commandment to depart unto the other side. \textsuperscript{19} And a certain scribe came, and said unto him, Master, I will follow you anywhere you go. \textsuperscript{20} And Jesus says unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man has not where to lay his head. \textsuperscript{21} And another of his disciples said unto him, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father. \textsuperscript{22} But Jesus said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead. \textsuperscript{23} And when he was entered into a ship, his disciples followed him. \textsuperscript{24} And, behold, there arose a great tempest in the sea, insomuch that the ship was covered with the waves: but he was asleep. \textsuperscript{25} And his disciples came to him, and awoke him, saying, Lord, save us: we perish. \textsuperscript{26} And he says unto them, Why are all of you fearful, O all of you of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm. \textsuperscript{27} But the men marvelled, saying, What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him! \textsuperscript{28} And when he was come to the other side into the country of the Gergesenes, there met him two possessed with devils, coming out of the tombs, exceeding fierce, so that no man might pass by that way. \textsuperscript{29} And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with you, Jesus, you Son of God? are you come here to torment us before the time? \textsuperscript{30} And there was a good way off from them an herd of many swine feeding. \textsuperscript{31} So the devils besought him, saying, If you cast us out, suffer us to go away into the herd of swine. \textsuperscript{32} And he said unto them, Go. And when they were come out, they went into the herd of swine: and, behold, the whole herd of swine ran violently down a steep place into the sea, and perished in the waters. \textsuperscript{33} And they that kept them fled, and went their ways into the city, and told every thing, and what was befallen to the possessed of the devils. \textsuperscript{34} And, behold, the whole city came out to meet Jesus: and when they saw him, they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.\par

Matthew 8:5 TSK note: entered, ; a centurion This was a Roman military title; and therefore this officer may be concluded to have been a Gentile. (See fuller particulars under .)\par
Matthew 8:11 TSK note: That;, ;, ;, ;, ; , ;, ; , ; shall sit Ανακλιθηαονται ( κλινο ), shall recline, i.e., at table; referring to the recumbent posture used by the easterners at their meals., ; in\par

Matthew 8:17 NT quotation aligns more closely with the Hebrew here; cf. Brenton LXX: “Isaiah 53:4 He bears our sins, and is pained for us: yet we accounted him to be in trouble, and in suffering, and in affliction.”\par
Matthew 8:17 Masoretic/Hebrew comparison: “Isaiah 53:4 Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows”\par
Matthew 8:28 TSK note: when; Gergesenes Some are of opinion that Gergasa was the country of the ancient Girgashites; but it is more probable the Gergesenes was introduced by Origen upon mere conjecture; as before him most copies seem to have read Gadarenes, agreeable to the Parallel Passages and the ancient Syriac version. Gadara, says Josephus, was the metropolis of Peraea, or the region beyond Jordan; and he also observes that it was sixty furlongs, or about eight miles from Tiberias. It is therefore rightly placed opposite Tiberias, at the southeast end of the lake. Pliny says it was called Hippodion, was one of the cities of Decapolis, and had the river Hieromax, or Jarmouk, flowing before it. It was of heathen jurisdiction; whence perhaps it was destroyed by the Jews; but was rebuilt by Pompey, and joined to the province of Syria. Augustus afterwards gave it to Herod, on whose death it was again annexed to Syria. It is now called Om Keis; its ruins are in a very mutilated state, and when visited by Burckhardt it had not a single inhabitant. The remains of the sepulchral caverns in which the demoniacs abode are still to be seen., ; coming;, so\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Matthew 9}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And he entered into a ship, and passed over, and came into his own city. \textsuperscript{2} And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; your sins be forgiven you. \textsuperscript{3} And, behold, certain of the scribes said within themselves, This man blasphemes. \textsuperscript{4} And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think all of you evil in your hearts? \textsuperscript{5} For whether is easier, to say, Your sins be forgiven you; or to say, Arise, and walk? \textsuperscript{6} But that all of you may know that the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins, (then says he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up your bed, and go unto yours house. \textsuperscript{7} And he arose, and departed to his house. \textsuperscript{8} But when the multitudes saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men. \textsuperscript{9} And as Jesus passed forth from thence, he saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he says unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him. \textsuperscript{10} And it came to pass, as Jesus sat at food in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples. \textsuperscript{11} And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eats your Master with publicans and sinners? \textsuperscript{12} But when Jesus heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick. \textsuperscript{13} But go all of you and learn what that means, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance. \textsuperscript{14} Then came to him the disciples of John, saying, Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples fast not? \textsuperscript{15} And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bride-chamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast. \textsuperscript{16} No man puts a piece of new cloth unto an old garment, for that which is put in to fill it up takes from the garment, and the rent is made worse. \textsuperscript{17} Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runs out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved. \textsuperscript{18} While he spoke these things unto them, behold, there came a certain ruler, and worshipped him, saying, My daughter is even now dead: but come and lay your hand upon her, and she shall live. \textsuperscript{19} And Jesus arose, and followed him, and so did his disciples. \textsuperscript{20} And, behold, a woman, which was diseased with an issue of blood twelve years, came behind him, and touched the hem of his garment: \textsuperscript{21} For she said within herself, If I may but touch his garment, I shall be whole. \textsuperscript{22} But Jesus turned him about, and when he saw her, he said, Daughter, be of good comfort; your faith has made you whole. And the woman was made whole from that hour. \textsuperscript{23} And when Jesus came into the ruler's house, and saw the minstrels and the people making a noise, \textsuperscript{24} He said unto them, Give place: for the maid is not dead, but sleeps. And they laughed him to scorn. \textsuperscript{25} But when the people were put forth, he went in, and took her by the hand, and the maid arose. \textsuperscript{26} And the fame hereof went abroad into all that land. \textsuperscript{27} And when Jesus departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, You son of David, have mercy on us. \textsuperscript{28} And when he was come into the house, the blind men came to him: and Jesus says unto them, Believe all of you that I am able to do this? They said unto him, Yea, Lord. \textsuperscript{29} Then touched he their eyes, saying, According to your faith be it unto you. \textsuperscript{30} And their eyes were opened; and Jesus strictly charged them, saying, See that no man know it. \textsuperscript{31} But they, when they were departed, spread abroad his fame in all that country. \textsuperscript{32} As they went out, behold, they brought to him a dumb man possessed with a devil. \textsuperscript{33} And when the devil was cast out, the dumb spoke: and the multitudes marvelled, saying, It was never so seen in Israel. \textsuperscript{34} But the Pharisees said, He casts out devils through the prince of the devils. \textsuperscript{35} And Jesus went about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every sickness and every disease among the people. \textsuperscript{36} But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd. \textsuperscript{37} Then says he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is abundant, but the labourers are few; \textsuperscript{38} Pray all of you therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 10}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, (o. pneuma) to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease. \textsuperscript{2} Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother; \textsuperscript{3} Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus; \textsuperscript{4} Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. \textsuperscript{5} These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter all of you not: \textsuperscript{6} But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. \textsuperscript{7} And as all of you go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand. \textsuperscript{8} Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely all of you have received, freely give. \textsuperscript{9} Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses, \textsuperscript{10} Nor pouch for your journey, neither two coats, neither shoes, nor yet staves: for the workman is worthy of his food. \textsuperscript{11} And into whatsoever city or town all of you shall enter, enquire who in it is worthy; and there abide till all of you go thence. \textsuperscript{12} And when all of you come into an house, salute it. \textsuperscript{13} And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you. \textsuperscript{14} And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, (o. logos) when all of you depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet. \textsuperscript{15} Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city. \textsuperscript{16} Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be all of you therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. \textsuperscript{17} But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues; \textsuperscript{18} And all of you shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles. \textsuperscript{19} But when they deliver you up, take no thought how or what all of you shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what all of you shall speak. \textsuperscript{20} For it is not all of you that speak, but the Spirit (o. pneuma) of your Father which speaks in you. \textsuperscript{21} And the brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child: and the children shall rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death. \textsuperscript{22} And all of you shall be hated of all men for my name's sake: but he that endures to the end shall be saved. \textsuperscript{23} But when they persecute you in this city, flee all of you into another: for verily I say unto you, All of you shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come. \textsuperscript{24} The disciple is not above his master, nor the servant above his lord. \textsuperscript{25} It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of his household? \textsuperscript{26} Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known. \textsuperscript{27} What I tell you in darkness, that speak all of you in light: and what all of you hear in the ear, that preach all of you upon the housetops. \textsuperscript{28} And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell. \textsuperscript{29} Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father. \textsuperscript{30} But the very hairs of your head are all numbered. \textsuperscript{31} Fear all of you not therefore, all of you are of more value than many sparrows. \textsuperscript{32} Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. \textsuperscript{33} But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven. \textsuperscript{34} Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. \textsuperscript{35} For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. \textsuperscript{36} And a man's foes shall be they of his own household. \textsuperscript{37} He that loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me. \textsuperscript{38} And he that takes not his cross, and follows after me, is not worthy of me. \textsuperscript{39} He that finds his life shall lose it: and he that loses his life for my sake shall find it. \textsuperscript{40} He that receives you receives me, and he that receives me receives him that sent me. \textsuperscript{41} He that receives a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet's reward; and he that receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man's reward. \textsuperscript{42} And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 11}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And it came to pass, when Jesus had made an end of commanding his twelve disciples, he departed thence to teach and to preach in their cities. \textsuperscript{2} Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples, \textsuperscript{3} And said unto him, Are you he that should come, or do we look for another? \textsuperscript{4} Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and show John again those things which all of you do hear and see: \textsuperscript{5} The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them. \textsuperscript{6} And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me. \textsuperscript{7} And as they departed, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went all of you out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind? \textsuperscript{8} But what went all of you out in order to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings' houses. \textsuperscript{9} But what went all of you out in order to see? A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet. \textsuperscript{10} For this is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before your face, which shall prepare your way before you. \textsuperscript{11} Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there has not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he. \textsuperscript{12} And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent take it by force. \textsuperscript{13} For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John. \textsuperscript{14} And if all of you will receive it, this is Elijah, which was in order to come. \textsuperscript{15} He that has ears to hear, let him hear. \textsuperscript{16} But unto which shall I liken this generation? It is like unto children sitting in the markets, and calling unto their fellows, \textsuperscript{17} And saying, We have piped unto you, and all of you have not danced; we have mourned unto you, and all of you have not lamented. \textsuperscript{18} For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He has a devil. \textsuperscript{19} The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a wine indulger, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children. \textsuperscript{20} Then began he to reproach the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not: \textsuperscript{21} Woe unto you, Chorazin! woe unto you, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes. \textsuperscript{22} But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you. \textsuperscript{23} And you, Capernaum, which are exalted unto heaven, shall be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in you, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day. \textsuperscript{24} But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for you. \textsuperscript{25} At that time Jesus answered and said, I thank you, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hid these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them unto babes. \textsuperscript{26} Even so, Father: for so it seemed good in your sight. \textsuperscript{27} All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knows the Son, but the Father; neither knows any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him. \textsuperscript{28} Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. \textsuperscript{29} Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and all of you shall find rest unto your souls. \textsuperscript{30} For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 12}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} At that time Jesus went on the sabbath day through the corn; and his disciples were an hungered, and began to pluck the ears of corn and to eat. \textsuperscript{2} But when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto him, Behold, your disciples do that which is not lawful to do upon the sabbath day. \textsuperscript{3} But he said unto them, Have all of you not read what David did, when he was an hungered, and they that were with him; \textsuperscript{4} How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the showbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests? \textsuperscript{5} Or have all of you not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless? \textsuperscript{6} But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple. \textsuperscript{7} But if all of you had known what this means, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, all of you would not have condemned the guiltless. \textsuperscript{8} For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day. \textsuperscript{9} And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue: \textsuperscript{10} And, behold, there was a man which had his hand withered. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him. \textsuperscript{11} And he said unto them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out? \textsuperscript{12} How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. \textsuperscript{13} Then says he to the man, Stretch forth yours hand. And he stretched it forth; and it was restored whole, like the other. \textsuperscript{14} Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him. \textsuperscript{15} But when Jesus knew it, he withdrew himself from thence: and great multitudes followed him, and he healed them all; \textsuperscript{16} And charged them that they should not make him known: \textsuperscript{17} That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Isaiah the prophet, saying, \textsuperscript{18} Behold my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit (o. pneuma) upon him, and he shall show judgment to the Gentiles. \textsuperscript{19} He shall not strive, nor cry; neither shall any man hear his voice in the streets. \textsuperscript{20} A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory. \textsuperscript{21} And in his name shall the Gentiles trust. \textsuperscript{22} Then was brought unto him one possessed with a devil, blind, and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the blind and dumb both spoke and saw. \textsuperscript{23} And all the people were amazed, and said, Is not this the son of David? \textsuperscript{24} But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, This fellow does not cast out devils, but by Beelzebub the prince of the devils. \textsuperscript{25} And Jesus knew their thoughts, and said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand: \textsuperscript{26} And if Satan cast out Satan, he is divided against himself; how shall then his kingdom stand? \textsuperscript{27} And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges. \textsuperscript{28} But if I cast out devils by the Spirit (o. pneuma) of God, then the kingdom of God has come unto you. \textsuperscript{29} Or else how can one enter into a strong man's house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house. \textsuperscript{30} He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathers not with me scatters abroad. \textsuperscript{31} Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) shall not be forgiven unto men. \textsuperscript{32} And whosoever speaks a word (o. logos) against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come. \textsuperscript{33} Either make the tree good, and his fruit good; or else make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by his fruit. \textsuperscript{34} O generation of vipers, how can all of you, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks. \textsuperscript{35} A good man out of the good treasure of the heart brings forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure brings forth evil things. \textsuperscript{36} But I say unto you, That every idle word (o. rhema) that men shall speak, they shall give account (o. logos) thereof in the day of judgment. \textsuperscript{37} For by your words (o. logos) you shall be justified, and by your words (o. logos) you shall be condemned. \textsuperscript{38} Then certain of the scribes and of the Pharisees answered, saying, Master, we would see a sign from you. \textsuperscript{39} But he answered and said unto them, An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas: \textsuperscript{40} For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. \textsuperscript{41} The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here. \textsuperscript{42} The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here. \textsuperscript{43} When the unclean spirit (o. pneuma) is gone out of a man, he walks through dry places, seeking rest, and finds none. \textsuperscript{44} Then he says, I will return into my house from whence I came out; and when he has come, he finds it empty, swept, and garnished. \textsuperscript{45} Then goes he, and takes with himself seven other spirits (o. pneuma) more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation. \textsuperscript{46} While he yet talked to the people, behold, his mother and his brethren stood without, desiring to speak with him. \textsuperscript{47} Then one said unto him, Behold, your mother and your brethren stand without, desiring to speak with you. \textsuperscript{48} But he answered and said unto him that told him, Who is my mother? and who are my brethren? \textsuperscript{49} And he stretched forth his hand toward his disciples, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren! \textsuperscript{50} For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.\par
