\subsection*{Matthew 13}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} The same day went Jesus out of the house, and sat by the sea side. \textsuperscript{2} And great multitudes were gathered together unto him, so that he went into a ship, and sat; and the whole multitude stood on the shore. \textsuperscript{3} And he spoke many things unto them in parables, saying, Behold, a sower went forth to sow; \textsuperscript{4} And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up: \textsuperscript{5} Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth: \textsuperscript{6} And when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away. \textsuperscript{7} And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them: \textsuperscript{8} But other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold. \textsuperscript{9} Who has ears to hear, let him hear. \textsuperscript{10} And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speak you unto them in parables? \textsuperscript{11} He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given. \textsuperscript{12} For whosoever has, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever has not, from him shall be taken away even that he has. \textsuperscript{13} Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand. \textsuperscript{14} And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah, which says, By hearing all of you shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing all of you shall see, and shall not perceive: \textsuperscript{15} For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. \textsuperscript{16} But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear. \textsuperscript{17} For verily I say unto you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which all of you see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which all of you hear, and have not heard them. \textsuperscript{18} Hear all of you therefore the parable of the sower. \textsuperscript{19} When any one hears the word (o. logos) of the kingdom, and understands it not, then comes the wicked one, and catches away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side. \textsuperscript{20} But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that hears the word, (o. logos) and soon with joy receives it; \textsuperscript{21} Yet has he not root in himself, but endures for a while: for when tribulation or persecution arises because of the word, (o. logos) by and by he is offended. \textsuperscript{22} He also that received seed among the thorns is he that hears the word; (o. logos) and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, (o. logos) and he becomes unfruitful. \textsuperscript{23} But he that received seed into the good ground is he that hears the word, (o. logos) and understands it; which also bears fruit, and brings forth, some an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty. \textsuperscript{24} Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field: \textsuperscript{25} But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way. \textsuperscript{26} But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also. \textsuperscript{27} So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, did not you sow good seed in your field? from whence then has it tares? \textsuperscript{28} He said unto them, An enemy has done this. The servants said unto him, Will you then that we go and gather them up? \textsuperscript{29} But he said, Nay; lest while all of you gather up the tares, all of you root up also the wheat with them. \textsuperscript{30} Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather all of you together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn. \textsuperscript{31} Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: \textsuperscript{32} Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof. \textsuperscript{33} Another parable spoke he unto them; The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened. \textsuperscript{34} All these things spoke Jesus unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spoke he not unto them: \textsuperscript{35} That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world. \textsuperscript{36} Then Jesus sent the multitude away, and went into the house: and his disciples came unto him, saying, Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field. \textsuperscript{37} He answered and said unto them, He that sows the good seed is the Son of man; \textsuperscript{38} The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one; \textsuperscript{39} The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels. \textsuperscript{40} As therefore the tares are gathered and burned in the fire; so shall it be in the end of this world. \textsuperscript{41} The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity; \textsuperscript{42} And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth. \textsuperscript{43} Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who has ears to hear, let him hear. \textsuperscript{44} Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man has found, he hides, and for joy thereof goes and sells all that he has, and buys that field. \textsuperscript{45} Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls: \textsuperscript{46} Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it. \textsuperscript{47} Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind: \textsuperscript{48} Which, when it was full, they drew to shore, and sat down, and gathered the good into vessels, but cast the bad away. \textsuperscript{49} So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just, \textsuperscript{50} And shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth. \textsuperscript{51} Jesus says unto them, Have all of you understood all these things? They say unto him, Yea, Lord. \textsuperscript{52} Then said he unto them, Therefore every scribe which is instructed unto the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which brings forth out of his treasure things new and old. \textsuperscript{53} And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence. \textsuperscript{54} And when he was come into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they were astonished, and said, Whence has this man this wisdom, and these mighty works? \textsuperscript{55} Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas? \textsuperscript{56} And his sisters, are they not all with us? Whence then has this man all these things? \textsuperscript{57} And they were offended in him. But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house. \textsuperscript{58} And he did not many mighty works there because of their unbelief.\par

Matthew 13:2 TSK note: great, ; so; a ship Το πλοιον, "the ship" or boat; which Mr. Wakefield supposes was a particular vessel kept on the lake for the use of Christ and his disciples.\par
Matthew 13:3 TSK note: in, ; , ; , ; , ;, ; *marg. parables A parable, παραβολη, from παρα, near, and βαλλω, I cast, or put, has been justly defined to be a comparison or similitude, in which one thing is compared with another, especially spiritual things with natural, by which means those spiritual things are better understood, and make a deeper impression on a honest and attentive mind. In a parable, a resemblance in the principal incidents is all that is required; smaller matters being considered as a sort of drapery. Maimonides, in Moreh Nevochim, gives an excellent rule on this head: "Fix it as a principle to attach yourself to the grand object of the parable, without attempting to make a particular application of all the circumstances and terms which it comprehends." a sower\par

\subsection*{Matthew 14}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} At that time Herod the tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus, \textsuperscript{2} And said unto his servants, This is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead; and therefore mighty works do show forth themselves in him. \textsuperscript{3} For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias' sake, his brother Philip's wife. \textsuperscript{4} For John said unto him, It is not lawful for you to have her. \textsuperscript{5} And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet. \textsuperscript{6} But when Herod's birthday was kept, the daughter of Herodias danced before them, and pleased Herod. \textsuperscript{7} Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatsoever she would ask. \textsuperscript{8} And she, being before instructed of her mother, said, Give me here John Baptist's head in a charger. \textsuperscript{9} And the king was sorry: nevertheless for the oath's sake, and them which sat with him at food, he commanded it to be given her. \textsuperscript{10} And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison. \textsuperscript{11} And his head was brought in a charger, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother. \textsuperscript{12} And his disciples came, and took up the body, and buried it, and went and told Jesus. \textsuperscript{13} When Jesus heard of it, he departed thence by ship into a desert place apart: and when the people had heard thereof, they followed him on foot out of the cities. \textsuperscript{14} And Jesus went forth, and saw a great multitude, and was moved with compassion toward them, and he healed their sick. \textsuperscript{15} And when it was evening, his disciples came to him, saying, This is a desert place, and the time is now past; send the multitude away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves victuals. \textsuperscript{16} But Jesus said unto them, They need not depart; give all of you them to eat. \textsuperscript{17} And they say unto him, We have here but five loaves, and two fishes. \textsuperscript{18} He said, Bring them here to me. \textsuperscript{19} And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude. \textsuperscript{20} And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full. \textsuperscript{21} And they that had eaten were about five thousand men, beside women and children. \textsuperscript{22} And immediately Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away. \textsuperscript{23} And when he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into a mountain apart to pray: and when the evening was come, he was there alone. \textsuperscript{24} But the ship was now in the midst of the sea, tossed with waves: for the wind was contrary. \textsuperscript{25} And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea. \textsuperscript{26} And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear. \textsuperscript{27} But immediately Jesus spoke unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid. \textsuperscript{28} And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be you, bid me come unto you on the water. \textsuperscript{29} And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus. \textsuperscript{30} But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. \textsuperscript{31} And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O you of little faith, wherefore did you doubt? \textsuperscript{32} And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased. \textsuperscript{33} Then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Truthfully you are the Son of God. \textsuperscript{34} And when they were gone over, they came into the land of Gennesaret. \textsuperscript{35} And when the men of that place had knowledge of him, they sent out into all that country round about, and brought unto him all that were diseased; \textsuperscript{36} And besought him that they might only touch the hem of his garment: and as many as touched were made perfectly whole.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Matthew 14:1 TSK note: Herod This was Herod Antipas, the son of Herod the Great, by Malthace, and tetrarch of Galilee and Perea, which produced a revenue of 200 talents a year. He married the daughter of Aretas, king of Arabia, whom he divorced in order to marry Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, who was still living. Aretas, to revenge the affront which Herod had offered his daughter, declared war against him, and vanquished him after an obstinate engagement. This defeat, Josephus assures us, the Jews considered as a punishment for the death of John the Baptist. Having gone to Rome to solicit the title of king, he was accused by Agrippa of carrying on a correspondence with Artabanus king of Parthia, against the Romans, and was banished by the emperor Caius to Lyons, and thence to Spain, where he and Herodias died in exile., ;, ; Tetrarch\par
Matthew 14:2 TSK note: This, ; do show forth themselves in him or, are wrought by him\par
Matthew 14:3 Brenton note: Name meaning: Herodias (Herodias) — Heroic Manipulative figure who sought John’s head.\par
Matthew 14:3 TSK note: Herod; Herodias' This infamous woman was the daughter of Aristobulus and Bernice, and granddaughter of Herod the Great. his Philip's Herod Philip, son of Herod the Great and Mariamne.\par
Matthew 14:6 TSK note: birthday;, ; the daughter danced before them Gr. in the midst\par
Matthew 14:9 TSK note: the king; sorry, ; , ; , the oath's\par
Matthew 14:10 TSK note: and beheaded, ; the prison Josephus informs us that John the Baptist was imprisoned and beheaded by Herod in the strong castle of Machaerus, which he describes as situated about 60 stadia east of Jordan, not far from where the river discharges itself into the Dead Sea.\par
Matthew 14:19 TSK note: he commanded;, ; looking, ; he blessed\par
Matthew 14:25 TSK note: the fourth watch The Jews at this time divided the night into four watches; the first was from six o'clock in the evening till nine, the second from nine to twelve, the third from twelve till three, and the fourth from three till six; so that it probably began to be daylight before our Lord came to his disciples.; walking This suspension of the laws of gravitation was a proper manifestation of omnipotence.\par
Matthew 14:30 TSK note: when; , ; boisterous or, strong Lord\par
Matthew 14:31 TSK note: stretched; , ; and caught; , ; O thou\par
Matthew 14:34 TSK note: when the land of Gennesaret was a fertile district, in which were situated the cities of Tiberias and Capernaum, extending along the western shore of the lake to which it gave name, about 30 stadia, or nearly four miles, in length, and twenty stadia, or two miles and a half, in breadth, according to Josephus.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Matthew 15}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying, \textsuperscript{2} Why do your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread. \textsuperscript{3} But he answered and said unto them, Why do all of you also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? \textsuperscript{4} For God commanded, saying, Honour your father and mother: and, He that curses father or mother, let him die the death. \textsuperscript{5} But all of you say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever you might be profited by me; \textsuperscript{6} And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have all of you made the commandment of God of no effect by your tradition. \textsuperscript{7} All of you hypocrites, well did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying, \textsuperscript{8} This people draws nigh unto me with their mouth, and honors me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. \textsuperscript{9} But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. \textsuperscript{10} And he called the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand: \textsuperscript{11} Not that which goes into the mouth defiles a man; but that which comes out of the mouth, this defiles a man. \textsuperscript{12} Then came his disciples, and said unto him, Know you that the Pharisees were offended, after they heard this saying? (o. logos) \textsuperscript{13} But he answered and said, Every plant, which my heavenly Father has not planted, shall be rooted up. \textsuperscript{14} Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch. \textsuperscript{15} Then answered Peter and said unto him, Declare unto us this parable. \textsuperscript{16} And Jesus said, Are all of you also yet without understanding? \textsuperscript{17} Do not all of you yet understand, that whatsoever enters in at the mouth goes into the belly, and is cast out into the draught? \textsuperscript{18} But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man. \textsuperscript{19} For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies: \textsuperscript{20} These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashed hands defiles not a man. \textsuperscript{21} Then Jesus went thence, and departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon. \textsuperscript{22} And, behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, you son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a devil. \textsuperscript{23} But he answered her not a word. (o. logos) And his disciples came and besought him, saying, Send her away; for she cries after us. \textsuperscript{24} But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. \textsuperscript{25} Then came she and worshipped him, saying, Lord, help me. \textsuperscript{26} But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children's bread, and to cast it to dogs. \textsuperscript{27} And she said, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table. \textsuperscript{28} Then Jesus answered and said unto her, O woman, great is your faith: be it unto you even as you will. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour. \textsuperscript{29} And Jesus departed from thence, and came nigh unto the sea of Galilee; and went up into a mountain, and sat down there. \textsuperscript{30} And great multitudes came unto him, having with them those that were lame, blind, dumb, physically disabled, and many others, and cast them down at Jesus' feet; and he healed them: \textsuperscript{31} Insomuch that the multitude wondered, when they saw the dumb to speak, the physically disabled to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see: and they glorified the God of Israel. \textsuperscript{32} Then Jesus called his disciples unto him, and said, I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days, and have nothing to eat: and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way. \textsuperscript{33} And his disciples say unto him, Whence should we have so much bread in the wilderness, as to fill so great a multitude? \textsuperscript{34} And Jesus says unto them, How many loaves have all of you? And they said, Seven, and a few little fishes. \textsuperscript{35} And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground. \textsuperscript{36} And he took the seven loaves and the fishes, and gave thanks, and brake them, and gave to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude. \textsuperscript{37} And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken food that was left seven baskets full. \textsuperscript{38} And they that did eat were four thousand men, beside women and children. \textsuperscript{39} And he sent away the multitude, and took ship, and came into the coasts of Magdala.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Matthew 15:2 Brenton note: Greek background: paradosis (παράδοσις) = tradition; handing over. Common English renderings: tradition. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par
Matthew 15:2 TSK note: transgress, ; , ; tradition Tradition, in Latin traditio from trado I deliver, hand down, exactly agreeing with the original παραδοσις, from παραδιδωμι, I deliver, transmit. Among the Jews it signifies what is called oral law, which they say has been successively handed down from Moses, through every generation, to Judah the Holy, who compiled and digested it into the Mishneh, to explain which the two Gemaras, or Talmuds, called the Jerusalem and Babylonish, were composed. Of the estimation in which these were held by the Jews, the following may serve as an example: "The words of the Scribes are lovely beyond the words of the law, for the words of the law are weighty and light, but the words of the Scribes are all weighty."\par

\subsection*{Matthew 16}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} The Pharisees also with the Sadducees came, and tempting desired him that he would show them a sign from heaven. \textsuperscript{2} He answered and said unto them, When it is evening, all of you say, It will be fair weather: for the sky is red. \textsuperscript{3} And in the morning, It will be foul weather to day: for the sky is red and lowering. O all of you hypocrites, all of you can discern the face of the sky; but can all of you not discern the signs of the times? \textsuperscript{4} A wicked and adulterous generation seeks after a sign; and there shall no sign be given unto it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas. And he left them, and departed. \textsuperscript{5} And when his disciples were come to the other side, they had forgotten to take bread. \textsuperscript{6} Then Jesus said unto them, Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees. \textsuperscript{7} And they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have taken no bread. \textsuperscript{8} Which when Jesus perceived, he said unto them, O all of you of little faith, why reason all of you among yourselves, because all of you have brought no bread? \textsuperscript{9} Do all of you not yet understand, neither remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets all of you took up? \textsuperscript{10} Neither the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many baskets all of you took up? \textsuperscript{11} How is it that all of you do not understand that I spoke it not to you concerning bread, that all of you should beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees? \textsuperscript{12} Then understood they how that he bade them not beware of the leaven of bread, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees. \textsuperscript{13} When Jesus came into the coasts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of man am? \textsuperscript{14} And they said, Some say that you are John the Baptist: some, Elijah; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets. \textsuperscript{15} He says unto them, But whom say all of you that I am? \textsuperscript{16} And Simon Peter answered and said, You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. \textsuperscript{17} And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed are you, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood has not revealed it unto you, but my Father which is in heaven. \textsuperscript{18} And I say also unto you, That you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. \textsuperscript{19} And I will give unto you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever you shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever you shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven. \textsuperscript{20} Then charged he his disciples that they should tell no man that he was Jesus the Christ. \textsuperscript{21} From that time forth began Jesus to show unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day. \textsuperscript{22} Then Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from you, Lord: this shall not be unto you. \textsuperscript{23} But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get you behind me, Satan: you are an offence unto me: for you savour not the things that be of God, but those that be of men. \textsuperscript{24} Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. \textsuperscript{25} For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it. \textsuperscript{26} For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul? \textsuperscript{27} For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works. \textsuperscript{28} Verily I say unto you, There be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.\par

Matthew 16:13 TSK note: came; Caesarea Philippi Cesarea Philippi was anciently called Paneas, from the mountain of Panium, or Hermon, at the foot of which it was situated, near the springs of Jordan; but Philip the tetrarch, the son of Herod the Great, having rebuilt it, gave it the name of Cesarea in honour of Tiberius, the reigning emperor, and he added his own name to it, to distinguish it from another Cesarea on the coast of the Mediterranean. It was afterwards named Neronias by the young Agrippa, in honour of Nero; and in the time of William of Tyre, it was called Belinas. It was, according to Josephus, a day's journey from Sidon, and 120 stadia from the lake of Phiala; and, according to Abulfeda, a journey of a day and a half from Damascus. Many have confounded it with Dan, or Leshem; but Eusebius and Jerome expressly affirm that Dan was four miles from Paneas, on the road to Tyre. It is now called Banias, and is described, by Seetzen, as a hamlet of about twenty miserable huts, inhabited by Mohammedans; but Burckhardt says it contains about 150 houses, inhabited by Turks, Greeks, etc. Whom I the\par

\subsection*{Matthew 17}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And after six days Jesus takes Peter, James, and John his brother, and brings them up into an high mountain apart, \textsuperscript{2} And was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light. \textsuperscript{3} And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elijah talking with him. \textsuperscript{4} Then answered Peter, and said unto Jesus, Lord, it is good for us to be here: if you will, let us make here three tabernacles; one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah. \textsuperscript{5} While he yet spoke, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear all of you him. \textsuperscript{6} And when the disciples heard it, they fell on their face, and were sore afraid. \textsuperscript{7} And Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid. \textsuperscript{8} And when they had lifted up their eyes, they saw no man, save Jesus only. \textsuperscript{9} And as they came down from the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying, Tell the vision to no man, until the Son of man be risen again from the dead. \textsuperscript{10} And his disciples asked him, saying, Why then say the scribes that Elijah must first come? \textsuperscript{11} And Jesus answered and said unto them, Elijah truly shall first come, and restore all things. \textsuperscript{12} But I say unto you, That Elijah has come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed. Likewise shall also the Son of man suffer of them. \textsuperscript{13} Then the disciples understood that he spoke unto them of John the Baptist. \textsuperscript{14} And when they were come to the multitude, there came to him a certain man, kneeling down to him, and saying, \textsuperscript{15} Lord, have mercy on my son: for he is lunatic, and sore vexed: for frequently he falls into the fire, and often into the water. \textsuperscript{16} And I brought him to your disciples, and they could not cure him. \textsuperscript{17} Then Jesus answered and said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him here to me. \textsuperscript{18} And Jesus rebuked the devil; and he departed out of him: and the child was cured from that very hour. \textsuperscript{19} Then came the disciples to Jesus apart, and said, Why could not we cast him out? \textsuperscript{20} And Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If all of you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, all of you shall say unto this mountain, Remove behind to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you. \textsuperscript{21} Nevertheless this kind goes not out but by prayer and fasting. \textsuperscript{22} And while they abode in Galilee, Jesus said unto them, The Son of man shall be betrayed into the hands of men: \textsuperscript{23} And they shall kill him, and the third day he shall be raised again. And they were exceeding sorry. \textsuperscript{24} And when they were come to Capernaum, they that received tribute money came to Peter, and said, Does not your master pay tribute? \textsuperscript{25} He says, Yes. And when he was come into the house, Jesus prevented him, saying, What think you, Simon? of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers? \textsuperscript{26} Peter says unto him, Of strangers. Jesus says unto him, Then are the children free. \textsuperscript{27} Notwithstanding, lest we should offend them, go you to the sea, and cast an hook, and take up the fish that first comes up; and when you have opened his mouth, you shall find a piece of money: that take, and give unto them for me and you.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 18}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} At the same time came the disciples unto Jesus, saying, Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven? \textsuperscript{2} And Jesus called a little child unto him, and set him in the midst of them, \textsuperscript{3} And said, Verily I say unto you, Except all of you be converted, and become as little children, all of you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. \textsuperscript{4} Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven. \textsuperscript{5} And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receives me. \textsuperscript{6} But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea. \textsuperscript{7} Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must essentially be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence comes! \textsuperscript{8} Wherefore if your hand or your foot offend you, cut them off, and cast them from you: it is better for you to enter into life halt or physically disabled, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire. \textsuperscript{9} And if yours eye offend you, pluck it out, and cast it from you: it is better for you to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire. \textsuperscript{10} Take heed that all of you despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven. \textsuperscript{11} For the Son of man has come to save that which was lost. \textsuperscript{12} How think all of you? if a man have an hundred sheep, and one of them be gone astray, does he not leave the ninety and nine, and goes into the mountains, and seeks that which is gone astray? \textsuperscript{13} And if so be that he find it, verily I say unto you, he rejoices more of that sheep, than of the ninety and nine which went not astray. \textsuperscript{14} Even so it is not the will of your Father which is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish. \textsuperscript{15} Moreover if your brother shall trespass against you, go and tell him his fault between you and him alone: if he shall hear you, you have gained your brother. \textsuperscript{16} But if he will not hear you, then take with you one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word (o. rhema) may be established. \textsuperscript{17} And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto you as an heathen man and a publican. \textsuperscript{18} Verily I say unto you, Whatsoever all of you shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever all of you shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven. \textsuperscript{19} Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as concerning any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven. \textsuperscript{20} For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them. \textsuperscript{21} Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times? \textsuperscript{22} Jesus says unto him, I say not unto you, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven. \textsuperscript{23} Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, which would take account (o. logos) of his servants. \textsuperscript{24} And when he had begun to reckon, one was brought unto him, which owed him ten thousand talents. \textsuperscript{25} But forasmuch as he had not to pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made. \textsuperscript{26} The servant therefore fell down, and worshipped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay you all. \textsuperscript{27} Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt. \textsuperscript{28} But the same servant went out, and found one of his fellow servants, which owed him an hundred pence: and he laid hands on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that you owe. \textsuperscript{29} And his fellow servant fell down at his feet, and besought him, saying, Have patience with me, and I will pay you all. \textsuperscript{30} And he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay the debt. \textsuperscript{31} So when his fellow servants saw what was done, they were very sorry, and came and told unto their lord all that was done. \textsuperscript{32} Then his lord, after that he had called him, said unto him, O you wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt, because you desired me: \textsuperscript{33} Should not you also have had compassion on your fellow servant, even as I had pity on you? \textsuperscript{34} And his lord was angry, and delivered him to the tormentors, till he should pay all that was due unto him. \textsuperscript{35} So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if all of you from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 19}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these sayings, (o. logos) he departed from Galilee, and came into the coasts of Judaea beyond Jordan; \textsuperscript{2} And great multitudes followed him; and he healed them there. \textsuperscript{3} The Pharisees also came unto him, tempting him, and saying unto him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause? \textsuperscript{4} And he answered and said unto them, Have all of you not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female, \textsuperscript{5} And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they two shall be one flesh? \textsuperscript{6} Wherefore they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let not man put asunder. \textsuperscript{7} They say unto him, Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away? \textsuperscript{8} He says unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so. \textsuperscript{9} And I say unto you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, commits adultery: and whoso marries her which is put away does commit adultery. \textsuperscript{10} His disciples say unto him, If the case of the man be so with his wife, it is not good to marry. \textsuperscript{11} But he said unto them, All men cannot receive this saying, (o. logos) save they to whom it is given. \textsuperscript{12} For there are some eunuchs, which were so born from their mother's womb: and there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men: and there be eunuchs, which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven's sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it. \textsuperscript{13} Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put his hands on them, and pray: and the disciples rebuked them. \textsuperscript{14} But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven. \textsuperscript{15} And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence. \textsuperscript{16} And, behold, one came and said unto him, Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life? \textsuperscript{17} And he said unto him, Why call you me good? there is none good but one, that is, God: but if you will enter into life, keep the commandments. \textsuperscript{18} He says unto him, Which? Jesus said, You shall do no murder, You shall not commit adultery, You shall not steal, You shall not bear false witness, \textsuperscript{19} Honour your father and your mother: and, You shall love your neighbour as yourself. \textsuperscript{20} The young man says unto him, All these things have I kept from my youth up: what lack I yet? \textsuperscript{21} Jesus said unto him, If you will be perfect, go and sell that you have, and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me. \textsuperscript{22} But when the young man heard that saying, (o. logos) he went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions. \textsuperscript{23} Then said Jesus unto his disciples, Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven. \textsuperscript{24} And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. \textsuperscript{25} When his disciples heard it, they were exceedingly amazed, saying, Who then can be saved? \textsuperscript{26} But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible. \textsuperscript{27} Then answered Peter and said unto him, Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed you; what shall we have therefore? \textsuperscript{28} And Jesus said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That all of you which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, all of you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. \textsuperscript{29} And every one that has forsaken houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name's sake, shall receive an hundredfold, and shall inherit everlasting life. \textsuperscript{30} But many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 20}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard. \textsuperscript{2} And when he had agreed with the labourers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard. \textsuperscript{3} And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the marketplace, \textsuperscript{4} And said unto them; Go all of you also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right I will give you. And they went their way. \textsuperscript{5} Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hour, and did likewise. \textsuperscript{6} And about the eleventh hour he went out, and found others standing idle, and says unto them, Why stand all of you here all the day idle? \textsuperscript{7} They say unto him, Because no man has hired us. He says unto them, Go all of you also into the vineyard; and whatsoever is right, that shall all of you receive. \textsuperscript{8} So when even was come, the lord of the vineyard says unto his steward, Call the labourers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first. \textsuperscript{9} And when they came that were hired about the eleventh hour, they received every man a penny. \textsuperscript{10} But when the first came, they supposed that they should have received more; and they likewise received every man a penny. \textsuperscript{11} And when they had received it, they murmured against the goodman of the house, \textsuperscript{12} Saying, These last have wrought but one hour, and you have made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day. \textsuperscript{13} But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do you no wrong: did not you agree with me for a penny? \textsuperscript{14} Take that yours is, and go your way: I will give unto this last, even as unto you. \textsuperscript{15} Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? Is yours eye evil, because I am good? \textsuperscript{16} So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen. \textsuperscript{17} And Jesus going up to Jerusalem took the twelve disciples apart in the way, and said unto them, \textsuperscript{18} Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be betrayed unto the chief priests and unto the scribes, and they shall condemn him to death, \textsuperscript{19} And shall deliver him to the Gentiles to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify him: and the third day he shall rise again. \textsuperscript{20} Then came to him the mother of Zebedees children with her sons, worshipping him, and desiring a certain thing of him. \textsuperscript{21} And he said unto her, What will you? She says unto him, Grant that these my two sons may sit, the one on your right hand, and the other on the left, in your kingdom. \textsuperscript{22} But Jesus answered and said, All of you know not what all of you ask. Are all of you able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able. \textsuperscript{23} And he says unto them, All of you shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father. \textsuperscript{24} And when the ten heard it, they were moved with indignation against the two brethren. \textsuperscript{25} But Jesus called them unto him, and said, All of you know that the princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them. \textsuperscript{26} But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister; \textsuperscript{27} And whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant: \textsuperscript{28} Even as the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many. \textsuperscript{29} And as they departed from Jericho, a great multitude followed him. \textsuperscript{30} And, behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Jesus passed by, cried out, saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, you son of David. \textsuperscript{31} And the multitude rebuked them, because they should hold their peace: but they cried the more, saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, you son of David. \textsuperscript{32} And Jesus stood still, and called them, and said, What will all of you that I shall do unto you? \textsuperscript{33} They say unto him, Lord, that our eyes may be opened. \textsuperscript{34} So Jesus had compassion on them, and touched their eyes: and immediately their eyes received sight, and they followed him.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 21}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And when they drew nigh unto Jerusalem, and were come to Bethphage, unto the mount of Olives, then sent Jesus two disciples, \textsuperscript{2} Saying unto them, Go into the village opposite to you, and immediately all of you shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose them, and bring them unto me. \textsuperscript{3} And if any man say ought unto you, all of you shall say, The Lord has need of them; and immediately he will send them. \textsuperscript{4} All this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, \textsuperscript{5} Tell all of you the daughter of Sion, Behold, your King comes unto you, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass. \textsuperscript{6} And the disciples went, and did as Jesus commanded them, \textsuperscript{7} And brought the ass, and the colt, and put on them their clothes, and they set him thereon. \textsuperscript{8} And a very great multitude spread their garments in the way; others cut down branches from the trees, and scattered them in the way. \textsuperscript{9} And the multitudes that went before, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest. \textsuperscript{10} And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, Who is this? \textsuperscript{11} And the multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet of Nazareth of Galilee. \textsuperscript{12} And Jesus went into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves, \textsuperscript{13} And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but all of you have made it a den of thieves. \textsuperscript{14} And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple; and he healed them. \textsuperscript{15} And when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, and saying, Hosanna to the son of David; they were sore displeased, \textsuperscript{16} And said unto him, Hear you what these say? And Jesus says unto them, Yea; have all of you never read, Out of the mouth of babes and infants you have perfected praise? \textsuperscript{17} And he left them, and went out of the city into Bethany; and he lodged there. \textsuperscript{18} Now in the morning as he returned into the city, he hungered. \textsuperscript{19} And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on you henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away. \textsuperscript{20} And when the disciples saw it, they marvelled, saying, How soon is the fig tree withered away! \textsuperscript{21} Jesus answered and said unto them, Verily I say unto you, If all of you have faith, and doubt not, all of you shall not only do this which is done to the fig tree, but also if all of you shall say unto this mountain, Be you removed, and be you cast into the sea; it shall be done. \textsuperscript{22} And all things, whatsoever all of you shall ask in prayer, believing, all of you shall receive. \textsuperscript{23} And when he was come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came unto him as he was teaching, and said, By what authority do you these things? and who gave you this authority? \textsuperscript{24} And Jesus answered and said unto them, I also will ask you one thing, (o. logos) which if all of you tell me, I in like wise will tell you by what authority I do these things. \textsuperscript{25} The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven, or of men? And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say unto us, Why did all of you not then believe him? \textsuperscript{26} But if we shall say, Of men; we fear the people; for all hold John as a prophet. \textsuperscript{27} And they answered Jesus, and said, We cannot tell. And he said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things. \textsuperscript{28} But what think all of you? A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to day in my vineyard. \textsuperscript{29} He answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented, and went. \textsuperscript{30} And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not. \textsuperscript{31} Whether of them two did the will of his father? They say unto him, The first. Jesus says unto them, Verily I say unto you, That the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you. \textsuperscript{32} For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and all of you believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and all of you, when all of you had seen it, repented not afterward, that all of you might believe him. \textsuperscript{33} Hear another parable: There was a certain householder, which planted a vineyard, and hedged it round about, and dug a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country: \textsuperscript{34} And when the time of the fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, that they might receive the fruits of it. \textsuperscript{35} And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another. \textsuperscript{36} Again, he sent other servants more than the first: and they did unto them likewise. \textsuperscript{37} But last of all he sent unto them his son, saying, They will reverence my son. \textsuperscript{38} But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance. \textsuperscript{39} And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him. \textsuperscript{40} When the lord therefore of the vineyard comes, what will he do unto those husbandmen? \textsuperscript{41} They say unto him, He will miserably destroy those wicked men, and will let out his vineyard unto other husbandmen, which shall render him the fruits in their seasons. \textsuperscript{42} Jesus says unto them, Did all of you never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes? \textsuperscript{43} Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof. \textsuperscript{44} And whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder. \textsuperscript{45} And when the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables, they perceived that he spoke of them. \textsuperscript{46} But when they sought to lay hands on him, they feared the multitude, because they took him for a prophet.\par

Matthew 21:17 TSK note: he left; Bethany was a village to the east of the mount of Olives, on the road to Jericho; fifteen stadia ( ) or nearly two miles, as Jerome states, from Jerusalem. This village is now small and poor, and the cultivation of the soil around it is much neglected; but it is a pleasant, romantic spot, shaded by the mount of Olives, and abounding in vines and long grass. It consists of from thirty to forty dwellings inhabited by about 600; Mohammedans, for whose use there is a neat little mosque standing on an eminence. Here they shew the ruins of a sort of castle as the house of Lazarus, and a grotto as his tomb; and the house of Simon the leper, of Mary Magdalene and of Martha, and the identical tree which our Lord cursed, are among the monkish curiosities of the place.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 22}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Jesus answered and spoke unto them again by parables, and said, \textsuperscript{2} The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain king, which made a marriage for his son, \textsuperscript{3} And sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the wedding: and they would not come. \textsuperscript{4} Again, he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell them which are bidden, Behold, I have prepared my dinner: my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come unto the marriage. \textsuperscript{5} But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his farm, another to his merchandise: \textsuperscript{6} And the remnant took his servants, and pleaded them spitefully, and slew them. \textsuperscript{7} But when the king heard thereof, he was angry: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city. \textsuperscript{8} Then says he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they which were bidden were not worthy. \textsuperscript{9} Go all of you therefore into the highways, and as many as all of you shall find, bid to the marriage. \textsuperscript{10} So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guest. \textsuperscript{11} And when the king came in to see the guest, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment: \textsuperscript{12} And he says unto him, Friend, how came you in here not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless. \textsuperscript{13} Then said the king to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into outer darkness, there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. \textsuperscript{14} For many are called, but few are chosen. \textsuperscript{15} Then went the Pharisees, and took counsel how they might entangle him in his talk. (o. logos) \textsuperscript{16} And they sent out unto him their disciples with the Herodians, saying, Master, we know that you are true, and teach the way of God in truth, neither care you for any man: for you regard not the person of men. \textsuperscript{17} Tell us therefore, What think you? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not? \textsuperscript{18} But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, Why tempt all of you me, all of you hypocrites? \textsuperscript{19} Show me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a penny. \textsuperscript{20} And he says unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? \textsuperscript{21} They say unto him, Caesar's. Then says he unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's. \textsuperscript{22} When they had heard these words, they marvelled, and left him, and went their way. \textsuperscript{23} The same day came to him the Sadducees, which say that there is no resurrection, and asked him, \textsuperscript{24} Saying, Master, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother. \textsuperscript{25} Now there were with us seven brethren: and the first, when he had married a wife, deceased, and, having no issue, left his wife unto his brother: \textsuperscript{26} Likewise the second also, and the third, unto the seventh. \textsuperscript{27} And last of all the woman died also. \textsuperscript{28} Therefore in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her. \textsuperscript{29} Jesus answered and said unto them, All of you do go astray, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God. \textsuperscript{30} For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven. \textsuperscript{31} But as concerning the resurrection of the dead, have all of you not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying, \textsuperscript{32} I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living. \textsuperscript{33} And when the multitude heard this, they were astonished at his doctrine. \textsuperscript{34} But when the Pharisees had heard that he had put the Sadducees to silence, they were gathered together. \textsuperscript{35} Then one of them, which was a lawyer, asked him a question, tempting him, and saying, \textsuperscript{36} Master, which is the great commandment in the law? \textsuperscript{37} Jesus said unto him, You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind. \textsuperscript{38} This is the first and great commandment. \textsuperscript{39} And the second is like unto it, You shall love your neighbour as yourself. \textsuperscript{40} On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets. \textsuperscript{41} While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them, \textsuperscript{42} Saying, What think all of you of Christ? whose son is he? They say unto him, The son of David. \textsuperscript{43} He says unto them, How then does David in spirit (o. pneuma) call him Lord, saying, \textsuperscript{44} The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit you on my right hand, till I make yours enemies your footstool? \textsuperscript{45} If David then call him Lord, how is he his son? \textsuperscript{46} And no man was able to answer him a word, (o. logos) neither durst any man from that day forth ask him any more questions.\par

Matthew 22:19 Brenton note: Greek background: nomisma (νόμισμα) = coin; legal tender. Common English renderings: money; coin. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par
Matthew 22:19 TSK note: a penny "In value sevenpence halfpenny."\par
Matthew 22:21 TSK note: Render; are Caesar's This conclusion is drawn from their own maxims and premises. They held that "wherever the money of any king is current, there the inhabitants acknowledge that king for their lord." Now, by admitting that this was Cesar's coin, and by consenting to receive it as the current coin of their country, they in fact acknowledged their subjection to his government, and of course their obligation to pay the tribute demanded of them. This answer was full of consummate wisdom, and it completely defeated the insidious designs of his enemies. He avoided rendering himself odious to the Jewish people by opposing their notions of liberty, or appearing to pay court to the emperor, without exposing himself to the charge of sedition and disaffection to the Roman government. and\par

\subsection*{Matthew 23}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then spoke Jesus to the multitude, and to his disciples, \textsuperscript{2} Saying The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat: \textsuperscript{3} All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not all of you after their works: for they say, and do not. \textsuperscript{4} For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers. \textsuperscript{5} But all their works they do in order to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments, \textsuperscript{6} And love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues, \textsuperscript{7} And greetings in the markets, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi. \textsuperscript{8} But be not all of you called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Christ; and all you are brethren. \textsuperscript{9} And call no man your father upon the earth: for one is your Father, which is in heaven. \textsuperscript{10} Neither be all of you called masters: for one is your Master, even Christ. \textsuperscript{11} But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant. \textsuperscript{12} And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be brought low; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted. \textsuperscript{13} But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for all of you shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for all of you neither go in yourselves, neither suffer all of you them that are entering to go in. \textsuperscript{14} Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for all of you devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore all of you shall receive the greater damnation. \textsuperscript{15} Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for all of you compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, all of you make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves. \textsuperscript{16} Woe unto you, all of you blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor! \textsuperscript{17} All of you fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gold, or the temple that santifies the gold? \textsuperscript{18} And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever swears by the gift that is upon it, he is guilty. \textsuperscript{19} All of you fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gift, or the altar that santifies the gift? \textsuperscript{20} Whoso therefore shall swear by the altar, swears by it, and by all things thereon. \textsuperscript{21} And whoso shall swear by the temple, swears by it, and by him that dwells therein. \textsuperscript{22} And he that shall swear by heaven, swears by the throne of God, and by him that sits thereon. \textsuperscript{23} Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for all of you pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought all of you to have done, and not to leave the other undone. \textsuperscript{24} All of you blind guides, which strain out a gnat, and swallow a camel. \textsuperscript{25} Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for all of you make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. \textsuperscript{26} You blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also. \textsuperscript{27} Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for all of you are like unto whitewashed sepulchers, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness. \textsuperscript{28} Even so all of you also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within all of you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity. \textsuperscript{29} Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because all of you build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchers of the righteous, \textsuperscript{30} And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets. \textsuperscript{31} Wherefore all of you be witnesses unto yourselves, that all of you are the children of them which killed the prophets. \textsuperscript{32} Fill all of you up then the measure of your fathers. \textsuperscript{33} All of you serpents, all of you generation of vipers, how can all of you escape the damnation of hell? \textsuperscript{34} Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them all of you shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall all of you scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city: \textsuperscript{35} That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom all of you slew between the temple and the altar. \textsuperscript{36} Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation. \textsuperscript{37} O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you that kill the prophets, and stone them which are sent unto you, how often would I have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and all of you would not! \textsuperscript{38} Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. \textsuperscript{39} For I say unto you, All of you shall not see me henceforth, till all of you shall say, Blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord.\par

The root is fusiform and long; stems, erect-groved, jointed, branched, and about two feet in height; leaves, doubly pinnated, sweet and odorous; flowers, flat, terminal umbels; corolla, five ovate, concave, yellow petals, with apexes inflected; germen, like that of fennel; seeds, scarcely the length of a carraway seed, but broader and flatter, of a brown colour, aromatic, sweetish odour, and warmish, pungent taste. cummin Gr. κυμινομ Cummin is a plant of the same class as dill. It rises eight or ten inches on a slender round procumbent, branching stem; leaves, a dark green, narrow, linear, and pointed; flowers, purple, in numerous four rayed umbels; corolla, five unequal petals, inflected, and notched at the apex; seeds, oblong, striated, of a brown colour, strong, heavy odour, and warm, bitterish taste. the weightier, ; these\par

\subsection*{Matthew 24}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Jesus went out, and departed from the temple: and his disciples came to him in order to show him the buildings of the temple. \textsuperscript{2} And Jesus said unto them, See all of you not all these things? verily I say unto you, There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down. \textsuperscript{3} And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of your coming, and of the end of the world? \textsuperscript{4} And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you. \textsuperscript{5} For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many. \textsuperscript{6} And all of you shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that all of you be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. \textsuperscript{7} For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places. \textsuperscript{8} All these are the beginning of sorrows. \textsuperscript{9} Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and all of you shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. \textsuperscript{10} And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. \textsuperscript{11} And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many. \textsuperscript{12} And because iniquity shall abound, the love (o. agape) of many shall wax cold. \textsuperscript{13} But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved. \textsuperscript{14} And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come. \textsuperscript{15} When all of you therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso reads, let him understand:) \textsuperscript{16} Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains: \textsuperscript{17} Let him which is on the housetop not come down to take any thing out of his house: \textsuperscript{18} Neither let him which is in the field return back to take his clothes. \textsuperscript{19} And woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days! \textsuperscript{20} But pray all of you that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day: \textsuperscript{21} For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be. \textsuperscript{22} And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened. \textsuperscript{23} Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Christ, or there; believe it not. \textsuperscript{24} For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall show great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect. \textsuperscript{25} Behold, I have told you before. \textsuperscript{26} Wherefore if they shall say unto you, Behold, he is in the desert; go not forth: behold, he is in the secret chambers; believe it not. \textsuperscript{27} For as the lightning comes out of the east, and shines even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. \textsuperscript{28} For where ever the carcass is, there will the eagles be gathered together. \textsuperscript{29} Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken: \textsuperscript{30} And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. \textsuperscript{31} And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other. \textsuperscript{32} Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and puts forth leaves, all of you know that summer is nigh: \textsuperscript{33} So likewise all of you, when all of you shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors. \textsuperscript{34} Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled. \textsuperscript{35} Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words (o. logos) shall not pass away. \textsuperscript{36} But of that day and hour knows no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only. \textsuperscript{37} But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. \textsuperscript{38} For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, \textsuperscript{39} And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. \textsuperscript{40} Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left. \textsuperscript{41} Two women shall be grinding at the mill; the one shall be taken, and the other left. \textsuperscript{42} Watch therefore: for all of you know not what hour your Lord does come. \textsuperscript{43} But know this, that if the goodman of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up. \textsuperscript{44} Therefore be all of you also ready: for in such an hour as all of you think not the Son of man comes. \textsuperscript{45} Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has made ruler over his household, to give them food in due season? \textsuperscript{46} Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he comes shall find so doing. \textsuperscript{47} Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods. \textsuperscript{48} But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delays his coming; \textsuperscript{49} And shall begin to strike his fellow servants, and to eat and drink with the drunken; \textsuperscript{50} The lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looks not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of, \textsuperscript{51} And shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.\par
