\subsection*{Matthew 25}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom. \textsuperscript{2} And five of them were wise, and five were foolish. \textsuperscript{3} They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them: \textsuperscript{4} But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. \textsuperscript{5} While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept. \textsuperscript{6} And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom comes; go all of you out to meet him. \textsuperscript{7} Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps. \textsuperscript{8} And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out. \textsuperscript{9} But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go all of you rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves. \textsuperscript{10} And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut. \textsuperscript{11} Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us. \textsuperscript{12} But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not. \textsuperscript{13} Watch therefore, for all of you know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man comes. \textsuperscript{14} For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods. \textsuperscript{15} And unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and immediately took his journey. \textsuperscript{16} Then he that had received the five talents went and traded with the same, and made them other five talents. \textsuperscript{17} And likewise he that had received two, he also gained other two. \textsuperscript{18} But he that had received one went and dug in the earth, and hid his lord's money. \textsuperscript{19} After a long time the lord of those servants comes, and reckons (o. logos) with them. \textsuperscript{20} And so he that had received five talents came and brought other five talents, saying, Lord, you delivered unto me five talents: behold, I have gained beside them five talents more. \textsuperscript{21} His lord said unto him, Well done, you good and faithful servant: you have been faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things: enter you into the joy of your lord. \textsuperscript{22} He also that had received two talents came and said, Lord, you delivered unto me two talents: behold, I have gained two other talents beside them. \textsuperscript{23} His lord said unto him, Well done, good and faithful servant; you have been faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things: enter you into the joy of your lord. \textsuperscript{24} Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew you that you are an hard man, reaping where you have not sown, and gathering where you have not scattered: \textsuperscript{25} And I was afraid, and went and hid your talent in the earth: lo, there you have that is yours. \textsuperscript{26} His lord answered and said unto him, You wicked and slothful servant, you knew that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I have not scattered: \textsuperscript{27} You ought therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with interest. \textsuperscript{28} Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which has ten talents. \textsuperscript{29} For unto every one that has shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but from him that has not shall be taken away even that which he has. \textsuperscript{30} And cast all of you the useless servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. \textsuperscript{31} When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory: \textsuperscript{32} And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats: \textsuperscript{33} And he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left. \textsuperscript{34} Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, all of you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: \textsuperscript{35} For I was an hungered, and all of you gave me food: I was thirsty, and all of you gave me drink: I was a stranger, and all of you took me in: \textsuperscript{36} Naked, and all of you clothed me: I was sick, and all of you visited me: I was in prison, and all of you came unto me. \textsuperscript{37} Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we you an hungered, and fed you? or thirsty, and gave you drink? \textsuperscript{38} When saw we you a stranger, and took you in? or naked, and clothed you? \textsuperscript{39} Or when saw we you sick, or in prison, and came unto you? \textsuperscript{40} And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as all of you have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, all of you have done it unto me. \textsuperscript{41} Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, all of you cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels: \textsuperscript{42} For I was an hungered, and all of you gave me no food: I was thirsty, and all of you gave me no drink: \textsuperscript{43} I was a stranger, and all of you took me not in: naked, and all of you clothed me not: sick, and in prison, and all of you visited me not. \textsuperscript{44} Then shall they also answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we you an hungered, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister unto you? \textsuperscript{45} Then shall he answer them, saying, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as all of you did it not to one of the least of these, all of you did it not to me. \textsuperscript{46} And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 26}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these sayings, (o. logos) he said unto his disciples, \textsuperscript{2} All of you know that after two days is the feast of the passover, and the Son of man is betrayed to be crucified. \textsuperscript{3} Then assembled together the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders of the people, unto the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas, \textsuperscript{4} And consulted that they might take Jesus by subtlety, and kill him. \textsuperscript{5} But they said, Not on the feast day, lest there be an uproar among the people. \textsuperscript{6} Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, \textsuperscript{7} There came unto him a woman having an alabaster box of very precious ointment, and poured it on his head, as he sat at food. \textsuperscript{8} But when his disciples saw it, they had indignation, saying, To what purpose is this waste? \textsuperscript{9} For this ointment might have been sold for much, and given to the poor. \textsuperscript{10} When Jesus understood it, he said unto them, Why trouble all of you the woman? for she has wrought a good work upon me. \textsuperscript{11} For all of you have the poor always with you; but me all of you have not always. \textsuperscript{12} For in that she has poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial. \textsuperscript{13} Verily I say unto you, Where ever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, there shall also this, that this woman has done, be told for a memorial of her. \textsuperscript{14} Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests, \textsuperscript{15} And said unto them, What will all of you give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver. \textsuperscript{16} And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him. \textsuperscript{17} Now the first day of the feast of unleavened bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying unto him, Where will you that we prepare for you to eat the passover? \textsuperscript{18} And he said, Go into the city to such a man, and say unto him, The Master says, My time is at hand; I will keep the passover at your house with my disciples. \textsuperscript{19} And the disciples did as Jesus had appointed them; and they made ready the passover. \textsuperscript{20} Now when the even was come, he sat down with the twelve. \textsuperscript{21} And as they did eat, he said, Verily I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me. \textsuperscript{22} And they were exceeding sorrowful, and began every one of them to say unto him, Lord, is it I? \textsuperscript{23} And he answered and said, He that dips his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me. \textsuperscript{24} The Son of man goes as it is written of him: but woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born. \textsuperscript{25} Then Judas, which betrayed him, answered and said, Master, is it I? He said unto him, You have said. \textsuperscript{26} And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body. \textsuperscript{27} And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink all of you all of it; \textsuperscript{28} For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. \textsuperscript{29} But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom. \textsuperscript{30} And when they had sung an hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives. \textsuperscript{31} Then says Jesus unto them, All you shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad. \textsuperscript{32} But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee. \textsuperscript{33} Peter answered and said unto him, Though all men shall be offended because of you, yet will I never be offended. \textsuperscript{34} Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto you, That this night, before the cock crow, you shall deny me three times. \textsuperscript{35} Peter said unto him, Though I should die with you, yet will I not deny you. Likewise also said all the disciples. \textsuperscript{36} Then comes Jesus with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and says unto the disciples, Sit all of you here, while I go and pray yonder. \textsuperscript{37} And he took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and very heavy. \textsuperscript{38} Then says he unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry all of you here, and watch with me. \textsuperscript{39} And he went a little farther, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as you will. \textsuperscript{40} And he comes unto the disciples, and finds them asleep, and says unto Peter, What, could all of you not watch with me one hour? \textsuperscript{41} Watch and pray, that all of you enter not into temptation: the spirit (o. pneuma) indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak. \textsuperscript{42} He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, your will be done. \textsuperscript{43} And he came and found them asleep again: for their eyes were heavy. \textsuperscript{44} And he left them, and went away again, and prayed the third time, saying the same words. (o. logos) \textsuperscript{45} Then comes he to his disciples, and says unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners. \textsuperscript{46} Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that does betray me. \textsuperscript{47} And while he yet spoke, lo, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and elders of the people. \textsuperscript{48} Now he that betrayed him gave them a sign, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he: hold him fast. \textsuperscript{49} And forthwith he came to Jesus, and said, Hail, master; and kissed him. \textsuperscript{50} And Jesus said unto him, Friend, wherefore are you come? Then came they, and laid hands on Jesus and took him. \textsuperscript{51} And, behold, one of them which were with Jesus stretched out his hand, and drew his sword, and struck a servant of the high priest's, and stroke off his ear. \textsuperscript{52} Then said Jesus unto him, Put up again your sword into his place: for all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword. \textsuperscript{53} Think you that I cannot now pray to my Father, and he shall presently give me more than twelve legions of angels? \textsuperscript{54} But how then shall the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must be? \textsuperscript{55} In that same hour said Jesus to the multitudes, Are all of you come out as against a thief with swords and staves in order to take me? I sat daily with you teaching in the temple, and all of you laid no hold on me. \textsuperscript{56} But all this was done, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples forsook him, and fled. \textsuperscript{57} And they that had laid hold on Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were assembled. \textsuperscript{58} But Peter followed him far off unto the high priest's palace, and went in, and sat with the servants, to see the end. \textsuperscript{59} Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council, sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death; \textsuperscript{60} But found none: yea, though many false witnesses came, yet found they none. At the last came two false witnesses, \textsuperscript{61} And said, This fellow said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days. \textsuperscript{62} And the high priest arose, and said unto him, Answer you nothing? what is it which these witness against you? \textsuperscript{63} But Jesus held his peace, And the high priest answered and said unto him, I adjure you by the living God, that you tell us whether you be the Christ, the Son of God. \textsuperscript{64} Jesus says unto him, You have said: nevertheless I say unto you, Hereafter shall all of you see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven. \textsuperscript{65} Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He has spoken blasphemy; what further need have we of witnesses? behold, now all of you have heard his blasphemy. \textsuperscript{66} What think all of you? They answered and said, He is guilty of death. \textsuperscript{67} Then did they spit in his face, and buffeted him; and others stroke him with the palms of their hands, \textsuperscript{68} Saying, Prophesy unto us, you Christ, Who is he that stroke you? \textsuperscript{69} Now Peter sat without in the palace: and a damsel came unto him, saying, You also were with Jesus of Galilee. \textsuperscript{70} But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what you says. \textsuperscript{71} And when he was gone out into the porch, another maid saw him, and said unto them that were there, This fellow was also with Jesus of Nazareth. \textsuperscript{72} And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man. \textsuperscript{73} And after a while came unto him they that stood by, and said to Peter, Surely you also are one of them; for your speech betrayed you. \textsuperscript{74} Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew. \textsuperscript{75} And Peter remembered the word (o. rhema) of Jesus, which said unto him, Before the cock crow, you shall deny me three times. And he went out, and wept bitterly.\par

\subsection*{Matthew 27}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} When the morning was come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death: \textsuperscript{2} And when they had bound him, they led him away, and delivered him to Pontius Pilate the governor. \textsuperscript{3} Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, \textsuperscript{4} Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see you to that. \textsuperscript{5} And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself. \textsuperscript{6} And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful in order to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood. \textsuperscript{7} And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in. \textsuperscript{8} Wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day. \textsuperscript{9} Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued, whom they of the children of Israel did value; \textsuperscript{10} And gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord appointed me. \textsuperscript{11} And Jesus stood before the governor: and the governor asked him, saying, Are you the King of the Jews? And Jesus said unto him, You says. \textsuperscript{12} And when he was accused of the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing. \textsuperscript{13} Then said Pilate unto him, Hear you not how many things they witness against you? \textsuperscript{14} And he answered him to not a word; (o. rhema) insomuch that the governor marvelled greatly. \textsuperscript{15} Now at that feast the governor was known to release unto the people a prisoner, whom they would. \textsuperscript{16} And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas. \textsuperscript{17} Therefore when they were gathered together, Pilate said unto them, Whom will all of you that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ? \textsuperscript{18} For he knew that for envy they had delivered him. \textsuperscript{19} When he was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have you nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him. \textsuperscript{20} But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude that they should ask Barabbas, and destroy Jesus. \textsuperscript{21} The governor answered and said unto them, Whether of the two will all of you that I release unto you? They said, Barabbas. \textsuperscript{22} Pilate says unto them, What shall I do then with Jesus which is called Christ? They all say unto him, Let him be crucified. \textsuperscript{23} And the governor said, Why, what evil has he done? But they cried out the more, saying, Let him be crucified. \textsuperscript{24} When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see all of you to it. \textsuperscript{25} Then answered all the people, and said, His blood be on us, and on our children. \textsuperscript{26} Then released he Barabbas unto them: and when he had scourged Jesus, he delivered him to be crucified. \textsuperscript{27} Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the common hall, and gathered unto him the whole band of soldiers. \textsuperscript{28} And they stripped him, and put on him a scarlet robe. \textsuperscript{29} And when they had intertwined a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand: and they bowed the knee before him, and mocked him, saying, Hail, King of the Jews! \textsuperscript{30} And they spit upon him, and took the reed, and stroke him on the head. \textsuperscript{31} And after that they had mocked him, they took the robe off from him, and put his own raiment on him, and led him away to crucify him. \textsuperscript{32} And as they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name: him they compelled to bear his cross. \textsuperscript{33} And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull, \textsuperscript{34} They gave him vinegar to drink mingled with gall: and when he had tasted thereof, he would not drink. \textsuperscript{35} And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots. \textsuperscript{36} And sitting down they watched him there; \textsuperscript{37} And set up over his head his accusation written, THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS. \textsuperscript{38} Then were there two thieves crucified with him, one on the right hand, and another on the left. \textsuperscript{39} And they that passed by reviled him, wagging their heads, \textsuperscript{40} And saying, You that destroys the temple, and build it in three days, save yourself. If you be the Son of God, come down from the cross. \textsuperscript{41} Likewise also the chief priests mocking him, with the scribes and elders, said, \textsuperscript{42} He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him. \textsuperscript{43} He trusted in God; let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of God. \textsuperscript{44} The thieves also, which were crucified with him, cast the same in his teeth. \textsuperscript{45} Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour. \textsuperscript{46} And about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? \textsuperscript{47} Some of them that stood there, when they heard that, said, This man calls for Elijah. \textsuperscript{48} And immediately one of them ran, and took a sponge, and filled it with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink. \textsuperscript{49} The rest said, Let be, let us see whether Elijah will come to save him. \textsuperscript{50} Jesus, when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{51} And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in two from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent; \textsuperscript{52} And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose, \textsuperscript{53} And came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many. \textsuperscript{54} Now when the centurion, and they that were with him, watching Jesus, saw the earthquake, and those things that were done, they feared greatly, saying, Truly this was the Son of God. \textsuperscript{55} And many women were there beholding far off, which followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering unto him: \textsuperscript{56} Among which was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedees children. \textsuperscript{57} When the even was come, there came a rich man of Arimathaea, named Joseph, who also himself was Jesus' disciple: \textsuperscript{58} He went to Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded the body to be delivered. \textsuperscript{59} And when Joseph had taken the body, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, \textsuperscript{60} And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb, and departed. \textsuperscript{61} And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting opposite to the tomb. \textsuperscript{62} Now the next day, that followed the day of the preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees came together unto Pilate, \textsuperscript{63} Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again. \textsuperscript{64} Command therefore that the tomb be made sure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away, and say unto the people, He has risen from the dead: so the last error shall be worse than the first. \textsuperscript{65} Pilate said unto them, All of you have a watch: go your way, make it as sure as all of you can. \textsuperscript{66} So they went, and made the tomb sure, sealing the stone, and setting a watch.\par

Matthew 27:2 Brenton note: Name meaning: Pilate (Pilatus) — Armed with a spear Roman judge who washed his hands of Jesus.\par
Matthew 27:2 TSK note: bound;, ;, ; delivered;, ; Pontius Pilate Pontius Pilate governed Judea ten years under the emperor Tiberius, from his 13th to his 23rd year ad 26 to 36; but, having exercised great cruelties against the Samaritans, they complained to Vitellius, governor of Syria, who sent Marcellus, one of his friends, to superintend Judea, and ordered Pilate to Rome, to give an account of his conduct to Tiberius. The emperor was dead before he arrived; but it is an ancient tradition, that he was banished to Vienne in Dauphiny, where he was reduced to such extremity that he killed himself with his own sword two years after.\par
Matthew 27:4 TSK note: I have sinned;, ;, ; the innocent, ; , ; What; see\par
Matthew 27:6 TSK note: It is not; to put; because The Jews considered it was strictly forbidden by the Divine law to bring any filthy or iniquitous gain into the temple. For this reason they now refused to allow this money to be placed in the chest in the temple, amongst the former contributions for its repairs. In this, they were right enough, but by the very act of refusing this money, they proved themselves to be gross perverters of the spirit of God's requirements. They saw not that it was much less lawful for them, who had hired Judas to this sordid action, to be employed in the service of the temple. Those that "bear the vessels of the Lord, " ought to be holy. Thus our Lord's words, "Ye blind guides! ye strain at a gnat and swallow a camel."\par
Matthew 27:9 TSK note: Jeremy The words here quoted are not found in Jeremiah, but in Zechariah; and a variety of conjectures have been formed, in order to reconcile this discrepancy. The most probable opinion seems to be, that the name of the prophet was originally omitted by the Evangelist, and that the name of Jeremiah was added by some subsequent copyist. It is omitted in two manuscripts of the twelfth century, in the Syriac, later Persic, two of the Itala, and in some other Latin copies; and what renders it highly probable that the original reading was δια, του, προφητον, by the prophet, is, that Matthew frequently omits the name of the prophet in his quotations. See note on;, ; . This omission is approved of by Bengel, Dr. A. Clarke, and Horne. And they thirty; of the children of Israel did value or, bought of the children of Israel\par

\subsection*{Matthew 28}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the tomb. \textsuperscript{2} And, behold, there was a great earthquake: for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it. \textsuperscript{3} His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow: \textsuperscript{4} And for fear of him the keepers did shake, and became as dead men. \textsuperscript{5} And the angel answered and said unto the women, Fear not all of you: for I know that all of you seek Jesus, which was crucified. \textsuperscript{6} He is not here: for he has risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay. \textsuperscript{7} And go quickly, and tell his disciples that he has risen from the dead; and, behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there shall all of you see him: lo, I have told you. \textsuperscript{8} And they departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy; and did run to bring his disciples word. \textsuperscript{9} And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him. \textsuperscript{10} Then said Jesus unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me. \textsuperscript{11} Now when they were going, behold, some of the watch came into the city, and showed unto the chief priests all the things that were done. \textsuperscript{12} And when they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave large money unto the soldiers, \textsuperscript{13} Saying, Say all of you, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept. \textsuperscript{14} And if this come to the governor's ears, we will persuade him, and secure you. \textsuperscript{15} So they took the money, and did as they were taught: and this saying (o. logos) is commonly reported among the Jews until this day. \textsuperscript{16} Then the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, into a mountain where Jesus had appointed them. \textsuperscript{17} And when they saw him, they worshipped him: but some doubted. \textsuperscript{18} And Jesus came and spoke unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. \textsuperscript{19} Go all of you therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit: (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{20} Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world. Amen.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Matthew 28:1 TSK note: the end The Hebrew word Schabbath from which our English word is derived, signifies rest, and is applied to all solemn festivals, equally with that one day of every week devoted to the worship of God;, "they polluted my sabbaths." Three evangelists say, the transaction recorded in this verse, occurred upon the first day of the week, early in the morning, about sunrising, and John says, while it was yet dark. Οψε, σαββατων, does not signify "in the evening of sabbath, " but "sabbaths." Hence, the great feast having been concluded, the term "end of the sabbaths" denotes the time very clearly. Again, it may be observed that the Jews, speaking of their passover, sometimes speak according to their civil computation, wherein they measured their days from sun-rising to sun-rising. Sometimes according to their sacred computation, which was from sun-set to sun-set. This reconciles, which seems to make the fourteenth day of the first month, the first day of unleavened bread.;, ; Mary Magdalene\par

\end{quote}
\section*{Mark}
\subsection*{Mark 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God; \textsuperscript{2} As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before your face, which shall prepare your way before you. \textsuperscript{3} The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare all of you the way of the Lord, make his paths straight. \textsuperscript{4} John did baptize in the wilderness, and preach the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins. \textsuperscript{5} And there went out unto him all the land of Judaea, and they of Jerusalem, and were all baptized of him in the river of Jordan, confessing their sins. \textsuperscript{6} And John was clothed with camel's hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey; \textsuperscript{7} And preached, saying, There comes one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose. \textsuperscript{8} I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{9} And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized of John in Jordan. \textsuperscript{10} And immediately coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit (o. pneuma) like a dove descending upon him: \textsuperscript{11} And there came a voice from heaven, saying, You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. \textsuperscript{12} And immediately the spirit (o. pneuma) drives him into the wilderness. \textsuperscript{13} And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him. \textsuperscript{14} Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God, \textsuperscript{15} And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent all of you, and believe the gospel. \textsuperscript{16} Now as he walked by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. \textsuperscript{17} And Jesus said unto them, Come all of you after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men. \textsuperscript{18} And immediately they forsook their nets, and followed him. \textsuperscript{19} And when he had gone a little farther thence, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets. \textsuperscript{20} And immediately he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants, and went after him. \textsuperscript{21} And they went into Capernaum; and immediately on the sabbath day he entered into the synagogue, and taught. \textsuperscript{22} And they were astonished at his doctrine: for he taught them as one that had authority, and not as the scribes. \textsuperscript{23} And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit; (o. pneuma) and he cried out, \textsuperscript{24} Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with you, you Jesus of Nazareth? are you come to destroy us? I know you who you are, the Holy One of God. \textsuperscript{25} And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold your peace, and come out of him. \textsuperscript{26} And when the unclean spirit (o. pneuma) had torn him, and cried with a loud voice, he came out of him. \textsuperscript{27} And they were all amazed, insomuch that they questioned among themselves, saying, What thing is this? what new doctrine is this? for with authority commands he even the unclean spirits, (o. pneuma) and they do obey him. \textsuperscript{28} And immediately his fame spread abroad throughout all the region round about Galilee. \textsuperscript{29} And forthwith, when they were come out of the synagogue, they entered into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John. \textsuperscript{30} But Simon's wife's mother lay sick of a fever, and soon they tell him of her. \textsuperscript{31} And he came and took her by the hand, and lifted her up; and immediately the fever left her, and she ministered unto them. \textsuperscript{32} And at even, when the sun did set, they brought unto him all that were diseased, and them that were possessed with devils. \textsuperscript{33} And all the city was gathered together at the door. \textsuperscript{34} And he healed many that were sick of divers diseases, and cast out many devils; and suffered not the devils to speak, because they knew him. \textsuperscript{35} And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed. \textsuperscript{36} And Simon and they that were with him followed after him. \textsuperscript{37} And when they had found him, they said unto him, All men seek for you. \textsuperscript{38} And he said unto them, Let us go into the next towns, that I may preach there also: for therefore came I forth. \textsuperscript{39} And he preached in their synagogues throughout all Galilee, and cast out devils. \textsuperscript{40} And there came a leper to him, beseeching him, and kneeling down to him, and saying unto him, If you will, you can make me clean. \textsuperscript{41} And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and says unto him, I will; be you clean. \textsuperscript{42} And as soon as he had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed. \textsuperscript{43} And he strictly charged him, and forthwith sent him away; \textsuperscript{44} And says unto him, See you say nothing to any man: but go your way, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing those things which Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them. \textsuperscript{45} But he went out, and began to publish it much, and to blaze abroad the matter, (o. logos) insomuch that Jesus could no more openly enter into the city, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from every quarter.\par

\subsection*{Mark 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And again he entered into Capernaum after some days; and it was noised that he was in the house. \textsuperscript{2} And immediately many were gathered together, insomuch that there was no room to receive them, no, not so much as about the door: and he preached the word (o. logos) unto them. \textsuperscript{3} And they come unto him, bringing one sick of the palsy, which was borne of four. \textsuperscript{4} And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay. \textsuperscript{5} When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, your sins be forgiven you. \textsuperscript{6} But there was certain of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts, \textsuperscript{7} Why does this man thus speak blasphemies? who can forgive sins but God only? \textsuperscript{8} And immediately when Jesus perceived in his spirit (o. pneuma) that they so reasoned within themselves, he said unto them, Why reason all of you these things in your hearts? \textsuperscript{9} Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Your sins be forgiven you; or to say, Arise, and take up your bed, and walk? \textsuperscript{10} But that all of you may know that the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins, (he says to the sick of the palsy,) \textsuperscript{11} I say unto you, Arise, and take up your bed, and go your way into yours house. \textsuperscript{12} And immediately he arose, took up the bed, and went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion. \textsuperscript{13} And he went forth again by the sea side; and all the multitude resorted unto him, and he taught them. \textsuperscript{14} And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him. \textsuperscript{15} And it came to pass, that, as Jesus sat at food in his house, many publicans and sinners sat also together with Jesus and his disciples: for there were many, and they followed him. \textsuperscript{16} And when the scribes and Pharisees saw him eat with publicans and sinners, they said unto his disciples, How is it that he eats and drinks with publicans and sinners? \textsuperscript{17} When Jesus heard it, he says unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance. \textsuperscript{18} And the disciples of John and of the Pharisees used to fast: and they come and say unto him, Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples fast not? \textsuperscript{19} And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bride-chamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast. \textsuperscript{20} But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days. \textsuperscript{21} No man also sews a piece of new cloth on an old garment: else the new piece that filled it up takes away from the old, and the rent is made worse. \textsuperscript{22} And no man puts new wine into old bottles: else the new wine does burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be ruined: but new wine must be put into new bottles. \textsuperscript{23} And it came to pass, that he went through the corn fields on the sabbath day; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of corn. \textsuperscript{24} And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful? \textsuperscript{25} And he said unto them, Have all of you never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungered, he, and they that were with him? \textsuperscript{26} How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the showbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him? \textsuperscript{27} And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: \textsuperscript{28} Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Mark 2:5 TSK note: saw; , ; he said; , ; Son The Jews believed that not only death but all disease was the consequence of sin. "There is no death without sin, nor any chastisement without iniquity; " and that "no diseased person could be healed of his disease till his sins were blotted out." Our Lord, therefore, as usual, appeals to their received opinions, and asserts his high dignity, by first forgiving the sins, and then healing the body of the paralytic.; sins\par
Mark 2:14 TSK note: he saw; Alphaeus; receipt of custom or, place where the custom was received Follow me\par
Mark 2:17 TSK note: They that are whole;, ;, I came\par
Mark 2:20 TSK note: the bridegroom; , ; , be taken; , ;, and\par
Mark 2:21 TSK note: seweth; new or, raw, or, unwrought\par
Mark 2:26 TSK note: Abiathar It appears from the passage referred to here, that Ahimelech was then high priest at Nob; and from other passages, that Abiathar was his son. Various conjectures have been formed in order to solve this difficulty; and some, instead of untying, have cut the knot, by pronouncing it an interpolation. The most probable opinion seems to be, that both father and son had two names, the father being also called Abiathar; and this appears almost certain from;, where Ahimelech seems evidently termed Abiathar, while Abiathar is called Ahimelech or Abimelech. (Compare .), ;, ; , which is not lawful\par

But they held their peace. \textsuperscript{5} And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, he says unto the man, Stretch forth yours hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand was restored whole as the other. \textsuperscript{6} And the Pharisees went forth, and immediately took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him. \textsuperscript{7} But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judaea, \textsuperscript{8} And from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea, and from beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him. \textsuperscript{9} And he spoke to his disciples, that a small ship should wait on him because of the multitude, lest they should crowd upon him. \textsuperscript{10} For he had healed many; insomuch that they pressed upon him in order to touch him, as many as had plagues. \textsuperscript{11} And unclean spirits, (o. pneuma) when they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, You are the Son of God. \textsuperscript{12} And he strictly charged them that they should not make him known. \textsuperscript{13} And he goes up into a mountain, and calls unto him whom he would: and they came unto him. \textsuperscript{14} And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach, \textsuperscript{15} And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils: \textsuperscript{16} And Simon he surnamed Peter; \textsuperscript{17} And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder: \textsuperscript{18} And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite, \textsuperscript{19} And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house. \textsuperscript{20} And the multitude comes together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread. \textsuperscript{21} And when his friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself. \textsuperscript{22} And the scribes which came down from Jerusalem said, He has Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casts he out devils. \textsuperscript{23} And he called them unto him, and said unto them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan? \textsuperscript{24} And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand. \textsuperscript{25} And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand. \textsuperscript{26} And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but has an end. \textsuperscript{27} No man can enter into a strong man's house, and spoil his goods, except he will first bind the strong man; and then he will spoil his house. \textsuperscript{28} Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith whatsoever they shall blaspheme: \textsuperscript{29} But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) has never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation. \textsuperscript{30} Because they said, He has an unclean spirit. \subsection*{Mark 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And he began again to teach by the sea side: and there was gathered unto him a great multitude, so that he entered into a ship, and sat in the sea; and the whole multitude was by the sea on the land. \textsuperscript{2} And he taught them many things by parables, and said unto them in his doctrine, \textsuperscript{3} Hearken; Behold, there went out a sower to sow: \textsuperscript{4} And it came to pass, as he sowed, some fell by the way side, and the fowls of the air came and devoured it up. \textsuperscript{5} And some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth: \textsuperscript{6} But when the sun was up, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away. \textsuperscript{7} And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit. \textsuperscript{8} And other fell on good ground, and did yield fruit that sprang up and increased; and brought forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred. \textsuperscript{9} And he said unto them, He that has ears to hear, let him hear. \textsuperscript{10} And when he was alone, they that were about him with the twelve asked of him the parable. \textsuperscript{11} And he said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables: \textsuperscript{12} That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them. \textsuperscript{13} And he said unto them, Know all of you not this parable? and how then will all of you know all parables? \textsuperscript{14} The sower sows the word. (o. logos) \textsuperscript{15} And these are they by the way side, where the word (o. logos) is sown; but when they have heard, Satan comes immediately, and takes away the word (o. logos) that was sown in their hearts. \textsuperscript{16} And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, (o. logos) immediately receive it with gladness; \textsuperscript{17} And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution arises for the word's sake, (o. logos) immediately they are offended. \textsuperscript{18} And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, (o. logos) \textsuperscript{19} And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, (o. logos) and it becomes unfruitful. \textsuperscript{20} And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, (o. logos) and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred. \textsuperscript{21} And he said unto them, Is a candle brought to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick? \textsuperscript{22} For there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested; neither was any thing kept secret, but that it should come abroad. \textsuperscript{23} If any man have ears to hear, let him hear. \textsuperscript{24} And he said unto them, Take heed what all of you hear: with what measure all of you mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given. \textsuperscript{25} For he that has, to him shall be given: and he that has not, from him shall be taken even that which he has. \textsuperscript{26} And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground; \textsuperscript{27} And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knows not how. \textsuperscript{28} For the earth brings forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear. \textsuperscript{29} But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come. \textsuperscript{30} And he said, Unto which shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it? \textsuperscript{31} It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, is less than all the seeds that be in the earth: \textsuperscript{32} But when it is sown, it grows up, and becomes greater than all herbs, and shoots out great branches; so that the fowls of the air may lodge under the shadow of it. \textsuperscript{33} And with many such parables spoke he the word (o. logos) unto them, as they were able to hear it. \textsuperscript{34} But without a parable spoke he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples. \textsuperscript{35} And the same day, when the even was come, he says unto them, Let us pass over unto the other side. \textsuperscript{36} And when they had sent away the multitude, they took him even as he was in the ship. And there were also with him other little ships. \textsuperscript{37} And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full. \textsuperscript{38} And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, care you not that we perish? \textsuperscript{39} And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. \textsuperscript{40} And he said unto them, Why are all of you so fearful? how is it that all of you have no faith? \textsuperscript{41} And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?\par

\subsection*{Mark 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And they came over unto the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes. \textsuperscript{2} And when he was come out of the ship, immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit, (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{3} Who had his dwelling among the tombs; and no man could bind him, no, not with chains: \textsuperscript{4} Because that he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been plucked asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: neither could any man tame him. \textsuperscript{5} And always, night and day, he was in the mountains, and in the tombs, crying, and cutting himself with stones. \textsuperscript{6} But when he saw Jesus far off, he ran and worshipped him, \textsuperscript{7} And cried with a loud voice, and said, What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the most high God? I adjure you by God, that you torment me not. \textsuperscript{8} For he said unto him, Come out of the man, you unclean spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{9} And he asked him, What is your name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many. \textsuperscript{10} And he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country. \textsuperscript{11} Now there was there nigh unto the mountains a great herd of swine feeding. \textsuperscript{12} And all the devils besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them. \textsuperscript{13} And forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits (o. pneuma) went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea. \textsuperscript{14} And they that fed the swine fled, and told it in the city, and in the country. And they went out to see what it was that was done. \textsuperscript{15} And they come to Jesus, and see him that was possessed with the devil, and had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid. \textsuperscript{16} And they that saw it told them how it befell to him that was possessed with the devil, and also concerning the swine. \textsuperscript{17} And they began to pray him to depart out of their coasts. \textsuperscript{18} And when he was come into the ship, he that had been possessed with the devil prayed him that he might be with him. \textsuperscript{19} Nevertheless Jesus suffered him not, but says unto him, Go home to your friends, and tell them how great things the Lord has done for you, and has had compassion on you. \textsuperscript{20} And he departed, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him: and all men did marvel. \textsuperscript{21} And when Jesus was passed over again by ship unto the other side, much people gathered unto him: and he was nigh unto the sea. \textsuperscript{22} And, behold, there comes one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name; and when he saw him, he fell at his feet, \textsuperscript{23} And besought him greatly, saying, My little daughter lies at the point of death: I pray you, come and lay your hands on her, that she may be healed; and she shall live. \textsuperscript{24} And Jesus went with him; and much people followed him, and thronged him. \textsuperscript{25} And a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years, \textsuperscript{26} And had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing improved, but rather grew worse, \textsuperscript{27} When she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment. \textsuperscript{28} For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole. \textsuperscript{29} And immediately the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague. \textsuperscript{30} And Jesus, immediately knowing in himself that virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in the press, and said, Who touched my clothes? \textsuperscript{31} And his disciples said unto him, You see the multitude thronging you, and says you, Who touched me? \textsuperscript{32} And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing. \textsuperscript{33} But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth. \textsuperscript{34} And he said unto her, Daughter, your faith has made you whole; go in peace, and be whole of your plague. \textsuperscript{35} While he yet spoke, there came from the ruler of the synagogue's house certain which said, Your daughter is dead: why trouble you the Master any further? \textsuperscript{36} As soon as Jesus heard the word (o. logos) that was spoken, he says unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe. \textsuperscript{37} And he suffered no man to follow him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James. \textsuperscript{38} And he comes to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and sees the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly. \textsuperscript{39} And when he was come in, he says unto them, Why make all of you this disturbance, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleeps. \textsuperscript{40} And they laughed him to scorn. But when he had put them all out, he takes the father and the mother of the damsel, and them that were with him, and enters in where the damsel was lying. \textsuperscript{41} And he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto you, arise. \textsuperscript{42} And immediately the damsel arose, and walked; for she was of the age of twelve years. And they were astonished with a great astonishment. \textsuperscript{43} And he charged them strictly that no man should know it; and commanded that something should be given her to eat.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Mark 5:2 TSK note: out; a man Matthew gives a brief account of two demoniacs who were dispossessed on this occasion; but Mark and Luke omit the mention of one (who was perhaps not so remarkable). That these wretched men were not merely mad, as some suppose, but really possessed of evil spirits, appears clearly from the language employed, as well as from the narrative itself. Matthew expressly affirms that they were "possessed with devils, " or demoniacs, δαιμονιζομενοι; Mark says he had "an unclean spirit, " i.e., a fallen spirit; and Luke asserts, that he "had devils (or demons) a long time, " and was called Legion, "because many devils were entered into him." With supernatural strength the demons burst asunder the chains and fetters with which he was bound; they address Christ as the "Son of the most high God; " they beseech him to suffer them to enter into the swine; and when he had given them leave, they "went out and entered into the swine, " etc. with\par
Mark 5:7 TSK note: What; Son, ; , I adjure; that\par
Mark 5:22 Brenton note: Name meaning: Jairus (Yair) — He enlightens His daughter was raised.\par
Mark 5:25 TSK note: a certain; an issue, twelve\par
Mark 5:26 TSK note: had suffered No person will wonder at this account when he considers the therapeutics of the Jewish physicians, in reference to diseases of this kind (for an account of which, see Drs. Lightfoot and Clarke). She was, therefore, a fit patient for the Great Physician.;, nothing\par
Mark 5:35 TSK note: there came thy daughter, why;, the Master\par
Mark 5:40 TSK note: they; , ; when;, ; he taketh He took just so many as prudence required, and as were sufficient to prove the reality of the cure; to have permitted the presence of more, might have savoured of ostentation.\par
Mark 5:41 TSK note: took; Talitha cumi θμιϊΰ χεξι, which is pure Syriac, the same as in the Syriac version, the proper translation of which is given by the evangelist. Damsel\par
Mark 5:43 TSK note: he charged, ;, ;, ; and commanded This was to shew that she had not only returned to life, but was also restored to perfect health; and to intimate, that though raised to life by extraordinary power, she must be continued in existence, as before, by the use of ordinary means. The advice of a heathen, on another subject, is quite applicable: Nec Deus intersit, nisi dignus vindice nodus incideriṫ "When the miraculous power of God is necessary, let it be resorted to; when not necessary, let the ordinary means be used." To act otherwise would be to tempt God. Given\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{Mark 6}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him. \textsuperscript{2} And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence has this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands? \textsuperscript{3} Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him. \textsuperscript{4} But Jesus, said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house. \textsuperscript{5} And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them. \textsuperscript{6} And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching. \textsuperscript{7} And he called unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and gave them power over unclean spirits; (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{8} And commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no pouch, no bread, no money in their purse: \textsuperscript{9} But be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats. \textsuperscript{10} And he said unto them, In what place whatsoever all of you enter into an house, there abide till all of you depart from that place. \textsuperscript{11} And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when all of you depart thence, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city. \textsuperscript{12} And they went out, and preached that men should repent. \textsuperscript{13} And they cast out many devils, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them. \textsuperscript{14} And king Herod heard of him; (for his name was spread abroad:) and he said, That John the Baptist was risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works do show forth themselves in him. \textsuperscript{15} Others said, That it is Elijah. And others said, That it is a prophet, or as one of the prophets. \textsuperscript{16} But when Herod heard thereof, he said, It is John, whom I beheaded: he has risen from the dead. \textsuperscript{17} For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for Herodias' sake, his brother Philip's wife: for he had married her. \textsuperscript{18} For John had said unto Herod, It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife. \textsuperscript{19} Therefore Herodias had a quarrel against him, and would have killed him; but she could not: \textsuperscript{20} For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just man and an holy, and observed him; and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly. \textsuperscript{21} And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief estates of Galilee; \textsuperscript{22} And when the daughter of the said Herodias came in, and danced, and pleased Herod and them that sat with him, the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever you will, and I will give it you. \textsuperscript{23} And he swore unto her, Whatsoever you shall ask of me, I will give it you, unto the half of my kingdom. \textsuperscript{24} And she went forth, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptist. \textsuperscript{25} And she came in immediately with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that you give me by and by in a charger the head of John the Baptist. \textsuperscript{26} And the king was exceeding sorry; yet for his oath's sake, and for their sakes which sat with him, he would not reject her. \textsuperscript{27} And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison, \textsuperscript{28} And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother. \textsuperscript{29} And when his disciples heard of it, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb. \textsuperscript{30} And the apostles gathered themselves together unto Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught. \textsuperscript{31} And he said unto them, Come all of you yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat. \textsuperscript{32} And they departed into a desert place by ship privately. \textsuperscript{33} And the people saw them departing, and many knew him, and ran on foot thither out of all cities, and advanced before them, and came together unto him. \textsuperscript{34} And Jesus, when he came out, saw much people, and was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things. \textsuperscript{35} And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him, and said, This is a desert place, and now the time is far passed: \textsuperscript{36} Send them away, that they may go into the country round about, and into the villages, and buy themselves bread: for they have nothing to eat. \textsuperscript{37} He answered and said unto them, Give all of you them to eat. And they say unto him, Shall we go and buy two hundred pennyworth of bread, and give them to eat? \textsuperscript{38} He says unto them, How many loaves have all of you? go and see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes. \textsuperscript{39} And he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass. \textsuperscript{40} And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties. \textsuperscript{41} And when he had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all. \textsuperscript{42} And they did all eat, and were filled. \textsuperscript{43} And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes. \textsuperscript{44} And they that did eat of the loaves were about five thousand men. \textsuperscript{45} And immediately he constrained his disciples to get into the ship, and to go to the other side before unto Bethsaida, while he sent away the people. \textsuperscript{46} And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray. \textsuperscript{47} And when even was come, the ship was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land. \textsuperscript{48} And he saw them toiling in rowing; for the wind was contrary unto them: and about the fourth watch of the night he comes unto them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them. \textsuperscript{49} But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out: \textsuperscript{50} For they all saw him, and were troubled. And immediately he talked with them, and says unto them, Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid. \textsuperscript{51} And he went up unto them into the ship; and the wind ceased: and they were sore amazed in themselves beyond measure, and wondered. \textsuperscript{52} For they considered not the miracle of the loaves: for their heart was hardened. \textsuperscript{53} And when they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore. \textsuperscript{54} And when they were come out of the ship, immediately they knew him, \textsuperscript{55} And ran through that whole region round about, and began to carry about in beds those that were sick, where they heard he was. \textsuperscript{56} And anywhere he entered, into villages, or cities, or country, they laid the sick in the streets, and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him were made whole.\par

Mark 6:3 TSK note: this; carpenter, ; James; Juda; Simon; offended\par

Mark 6:8 TSK note: take;, save Matthew says that they were to take "neither two coats, neither shoes, nor yet staves; " but this precept plainly means, "Go just as you are; take no other coat, shoes, or staff than what you already have." money "The word signifieth a piece of brass money in value something less than a farthing., but here it is taken in general for money."\par
Mark 6:9 Brenton note: Greek background: sandalion (σανδάλιον) = sandal. Common English renderings: sandal; shoe. This lemma is not attested in the canonical Greek Old Testament.\par
Mark 6:9 TSK note: be shod sandals The sandal consisted only of a sole, fastened about the foot and ankle with straps.\par
Mark 6:11 TSK note: whosoever; , ;, It shall;, ; , ; and Gr. or in the day\par

Mark 6:19 TSK note: Herodias; a quarrel or, an inward grudge\par

Mark 6:27 TSK note: the king an executioner or, one of his guard, Σπεκουλατωρ, in Latin, speculator, from speculor, to look about, spy, properly denotes a sentinel; and as these sentinels kept guard at the palaces of kings, and the residences of Roman governors, so they were employed in other offices besides guarding, and usually performed that of executioners. As, however, we learn from Josephus, that Herod was at this very time engaged in war with Aretas, king of Arabia, in consequence of Herod's having divorced his daughter in order to marry Herodias, his brother Philip's wife; and as this event occurred at an entertainment given at the castle of Machaerus, while his army was on its march against his father-in-law; we are furnished with an additional reason why a speculator, or sentinel, should have been employed as an executioner; and are thus enabled to discover such a latent and undesigned coincidence as clearly evinces the truth of the evangelical narrative.\par
Mark 6:37 TSK note: give; , ; Shall, ; pennyworth "The Roman penny is sevenpence halfpenny; as, marg."\par
Mark 6:40 TSK note: by hundreds It is generally supposed that they were so arranged as to be a hundred in rank, or depth, and fifty in front, or file; which would make the number just five thousand, and will reconcile this account with Luke's, who only speaks of their sitting down by fifties.\par
Mark 6:45 TSK note: straightway;, unto Bethsaida or, over against Bethsaida, Bethsaida, according to Josephus, was situated on the sea of Gennesaret, in the lower Gaulonitis (consequently on the east of the lake, as Pliny states), and at the beginning of the mountainous country; and it was raised from a village to the honour of a city by Philip, and called Julias in honour of the emperor's daughter. Some learned men, however, are of opinion that the Bethsaida mentioned in the gospels was a different place; and that it was situated on the western shore of the sea of Tiberias, in Galilee, near Chorazin and Capernaum, with which it is associated (, . ); and Bishop Pococke mentions the ruins of a town or large village in the plain of Huttin, about two miles west of the lake, still bearing the name of Baitsida, which he thinks occupies its site.\par

\subsection*{Mark 7}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{2} And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is to say, with unwashed, hands, they found fault. \textsuperscript{3} For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands often, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders. \textsuperscript{4} And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there be, which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, brazen vessels, and of tables. \textsuperscript{5} Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not your disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashed hands? \textsuperscript{6} He answered and said unto them, Well has Isaiah prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. \textsuperscript{7} Nevertheless in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men. \textsuperscript{8} For laying aside the commandment of God, all of you hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things all of you do. \textsuperscript{9} And he said unto them, Full well all of you reject the commandment of God, that all of you may keep your own tradition. \textsuperscript{10} For Moses said, Honour your father and your mother; and, Whoso curses father or mother, let him die the death: \textsuperscript{11} But all of you say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever you might be profited by me; he shall be free. \textsuperscript{12} And all of you suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother; \textsuperscript{13} Making the word (o. logos) of God of no effect through your tradition, which all of you have delivered: and many such like things do all of you. \textsuperscript{14} And when he had called all the people unto him, he said unto them, Hearken unto me every one of you, and understand: \textsuperscript{15} There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man. \textsuperscript{16} If any man have ears to hear, let him hear. \textsuperscript{17} And when he was entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable. \textsuperscript{18} And he says unto them, Are all of you so without understanding also? Do all of you not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without enters into the man, it cannot defile him; \textsuperscript{19} Because it enters not into his heart, but into the belly, and goes out into the draught, purging all meats? \textsuperscript{20} And he said, That which comes out of the man, that defiles the man. \textsuperscript{21} For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, \textsuperscript{22} Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: \textsuperscript{23} All these evil things come from within, and defile the man. \textsuperscript{24} And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid. \textsuperscript{25} For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, (o. pneuma) heard of him, and came and fell at his feet: \textsuperscript{26} The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter. \textsuperscript{27} But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children's bread, and to cast it unto the dogs. \textsuperscript{28} And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children's crumbs. \textsuperscript{29} And he said unto her, For this saying (o. logos) go your way; the devil is gone out of your daughter. \textsuperscript{30} And when she was come to her house, she found the devil gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed. \textsuperscript{31} And again, departing from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the coasts of Decapolis. \textsuperscript{32} And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an barrier in his speech; and they plead to him to put his hand upon him. \textsuperscript{33} And he took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spit, and touched his tongue; \textsuperscript{34} And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and says unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened. \textsuperscript{35} And immediately his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spoke plain. \textsuperscript{36} And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published it; \textsuperscript{37} And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He has done all things well: he makes both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.\par

Mark 7:2 TSK note: defiled or, common, they found\par
Mark 7:3 TSK note: oft or, diligently, Gr. With the fist, Up to the elbow, Theophylact. Πυγμη, the fist; which Dr. Lightfoot illustrates by a tradition from the Talmudical tracts, that when they washed their hands, they washed the fist up to the joint of the arm, ςγ τψχ . The Jews laid great stress on these washings, or baptisms, βαπτισμους, considering eating with unwashen hands no ordinary crime, and feigning that an evil spirit, called Shibta, has a right to sit on the food of him who thus eats, and render it hurtful. the tradition\par
Mark 7:4 TSK note: except; , ; pots "Gr. Sextarius; about a pint and a half." tables or, beds\par
Mark 7:11 TSK note: It is Corban Rather, "Let it be a corban " a formula common among the Jews on such occasions; by which the Pharisees released a child from supporting his parents; and even deemed it sacrilege if he afterwards gave anything for their use.\par
Mark 7:15 TSK note: There Though it is very true, says Dr. Doddridge, that a man may bring guilt upon himself by eating to excess, and a Jew, by eating what was forbidden by the Mosaic law; yet still the pollution would arise from the wickedness of the heart, and be just proportionable to it, which is all our Lord asserts. nothing; , ; , but\par
Mark 7:22 TSK note: covetousness, wickedness Gr. covetousnesses, wickednesses an evil, ; , ; pride, ; foolishness\par
Mark 7:26 TSK note: Greek or, Gentile, ; a Syrophenician\par
Mark 7:33 TSK note: he took, ; , ; put This was clearly a symbolical action; for these remedies evidently could not, by their natural efficacy, avail to produce so wonderful an effect. As the ears of the deaf appear closed, he applies his fingers to intimate that he would open them; and as the tongue of the dumb seems to be tied, or to cleave to the palate, he touches it, to intimate he would give loose and free motion to it. He accommodated himself to the weakness of those who might not indeed doubt his power, but fancy some external sign was requisite to healing. It was also thus made manifest, that this salutiferous power came from Himself, and that He who by one word, εφφαθα, had healed the man, must be Divine.\par
Mark 7:34 TSK note: looking;, he sighed; , ; Ephphatha, Be opened\par
