\subsection*{Luke 24}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came unto the tomb, bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them. \textsuperscript{2} And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb. \textsuperscript{3} And they entered in, and found not the body of the Lord Jesus. \textsuperscript{4} And it came to pass, as they were much perplexed thereabout, behold, two men stood by them in shining garments: \textsuperscript{5} And as they were afraid, and bowed down their faces to the earth, they said unto them, Why seek all of you the living among the dead? \textsuperscript{6} He is not here, but has risen: remember how he spoke unto you when he was yet in Galilee, \textsuperscript{7} Saying, The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again. \textsuperscript{8} And they remembered his words, (o. rhema) \textsuperscript{9} And returned from the tomb, and told all these things unto the eleven, and to all the rest. \textsuperscript{10} It was Mary Magdalene and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and other women that were with them, which told these things unto the apostles. \textsuperscript{11} And their words (o. rhema) seemed to them as idle tales, and they believed them not. \textsuperscript{12} Then arose Peter, and ran unto the tomb; and stooping down, he beheld the linen clothes laid by themselves, and departed, wondering in himself at that which was come to pass. \textsuperscript{13} And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs. \textsuperscript{14} And they talked together of all these things which had happened. \textsuperscript{15} And it came to pass, that, while they communed together and reasoned, Jesus himself drew near, and went with them. \textsuperscript{16} But their eyes were held that they should not know him. \textsuperscript{17} And he said unto them, What manner of communications (o. logos) are these that all of you have one to another, as all of you walk, and are sad? \textsuperscript{18} And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Are you only a stranger in Jerusalem, and have not known the things which are come to pass there in these days? \textsuperscript{19} And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word (o. logos) before God and all the people: \textsuperscript{20} And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him. \textsuperscript{21} But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel: and beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done. \textsuperscript{22} Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the tomb; \textsuperscript{23} And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive. \textsuperscript{24} And certain of them which were with us went to the tomb, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not. \textsuperscript{25} Then he said unto them, O fools, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken: \textsuperscript{26} Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory? \textsuperscript{27} And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself. \textsuperscript{28} And they drew nigh unto the village, where they went: and he made as though he would have gone further. \textsuperscript{29} But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them. \textsuperscript{30} And it came to pass, as he sat at food with them, he took bread, and blessed it, and brake, and gave to them. \textsuperscript{31} And their eyes were opened, and they knew him; and he vanished out of their sight. \textsuperscript{32} And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures? \textsuperscript{33} And they rose up the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and them that were with them, \textsuperscript{34} Saying, The Lord has risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon. \textsuperscript{35} And they told what things were done in the way, and how he was known of them in breaking of bread. \textsuperscript{36} And as they thus spoke, Jesus himself stood in the midst of them, and says unto them, Peace be unto you. \textsuperscript{37} But they were terrified and affrighted, and supposed that they had seen a spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{38} And he said unto them, Why are all of you troubled? and why do thoughts arise in your hearts? \textsuperscript{39} Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit (o. pneuma) has not flesh and bones, as all of you see me have. \textsuperscript{40} And when he had thus spoken, he showed them his hands and his feet. \textsuperscript{41} And while they yet believed not for joy, and wondered, he said unto them, Have all of you here any food? \textsuperscript{42} And they gave him a piece of a broiled fish, and of an honeycomb. \textsuperscript{43} And he took it, and did eat before them. \textsuperscript{44} And he said unto them, These are the words (o. logos) which I spoke unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me. \textsuperscript{45} Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures, \textsuperscript{46} And said unto them, Thus it is written, and thus it was essential for Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day: \textsuperscript{47} And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{48} And all of you are witnesses of these things. \textsuperscript{49} And, behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you: but tarry all of you in the city of Jerusalem, until all of you be imbued with power from on high. \textsuperscript{50} And he led them out as far as to Bethany, and he lifted up his hands, and blessed them. \textsuperscript{51} And it came to pass, while he blessed them, he was parted from them, and carried up into heaven. \textsuperscript{52} And they worshipped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy: \textsuperscript{53} And were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Luke 24:4 TSK note: two men; (see note on .)\par
Luke 24:5 TSK note: they, ;, ; the living or, him that liveth\par
Luke 24:13 TSK note: two; Emmaus was situated, according to the testimony both of Luke and Josephus, sixty furlongs from Jerusalem, that is, about seven miles and a half. It has generally been confounded with Emmaus, a city of Judah, afterwards called Nicopolis; but Reland has satisfactorily shown that they were distinct places; the latter, according to the old Itinerary of Palestine, being situated 10 miles from Lydda, and 22 miles from Jerusalem. D'Arvieux states, that going from Jerusalem to Rama, he took the right from the high road to Rama, at some little distance from Jerusalem, and "travelled a good league over rocks and flint stones, to the end of the valley of terebinthine trees, " until he reached Emmaus; which "seems, by the ruins which surround it, to have been formerly larger that it was in our Saviour's time. The Christians, while masters of the Holy Land, re-established it a little, and built several churches. Emmaus was not worth the trouble of having come out of the way to see it."\par
Luke 24:18 Brenton note: Name meaning: Cleopas (Kleopas) — Glory of the father Disciple on the Emmaus road.\par
Luke 24:25 TSK note: O fools Rather, inconsiderate men, ανοητοι, justly termed such, because they had not attended to the description of the Messiah by the prophets, nor to His teaching and miracles, as proofs that He alone was the person described.\par
Luke 24:28 TSK note: he made That is, he was directing his steps as if to go onwards; and so he doubtless would, had he not been withheld by their friendly importunities. There is not the smallest ground for founding a charge of dissimulation against our Saviour, or affording any encouragement to dissimulation in others.\par
Luke 24:31 TSK note: their eyes; vanished out of their sight or, ceased to be seen of them\par
Luke 24:34 TSK note: Saying From, we learn that the apostles did not believe the testimony even of the two disciples from Emmaus, while it is here asserted they were saying, when they entered the room, "The Lord is risen" etc. This difficulty is removed by rendering interrogatively, "Has the Lord risen, " etc? hath\par
Luke 24:44 TSK note: These, ;, ;, ; while, that all, ;, ; , ; in the law, ; , ; , ;, ;, in the prophets;, ;, ;, ;, ;, ;, ; , ;, in the psalms\par
\end{quote}
\section*{John}
\subsection*{John 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} In the beginning was the Word, (o. logos) and the Word (o. logos) was with God, and the Word (o. logos) was God. \textsuperscript{2} The same was in the beginning with God. \textsuperscript{3} All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made. \textsuperscript{4} In him was life; and the life was the light of men. \textsuperscript{5} And the light shines in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not. \textsuperscript{6} There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. \textsuperscript{7} The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe. \textsuperscript{8} He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light. \textsuperscript{9} That was the true Light, which lights every man that comes into the world. \textsuperscript{10} He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not. \textsuperscript{11} He came unto his own, and his own received him not. \textsuperscript{12} But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name: \textsuperscript{13} Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. \textsuperscript{14} And the Word (o. logos) was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth. \textsuperscript{15} John bare witness of him, and cried, saying, This was he of whom I spoke, He that comes after me is preferred before me: for he was before me. \textsuperscript{16} And of his fullness have all we received, and grace for grace. \textsuperscript{17} For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ. \textsuperscript{18} No man has seen God at any time, the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him. \textsuperscript{19} And this is the record of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, Who are you? \textsuperscript{20} And he confessed, and denied not; but confessed, I am not the Christ. \textsuperscript{21} And they asked him, What then? Are you Elijah? And he says, I am not. Are you that prophet? And he answered, No. \textsuperscript{22} Then said they unto him, Who are you? that we may give an answer to them that sent us. What says you of yourself? \textsuperscript{23} He said, I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Isaiah. \textsuperscript{24} And they which were sent were of the Pharisees. \textsuperscript{25} And they asked him, and said unto him, Why baptize you then, if you be not that Christ, nor Elijah, neither that prophet? \textsuperscript{26} John answered them, saying, I baptize with water: but there stands one among you, whom all of you know not; \textsuperscript{27} He it is, who coming after me is preferred before me, whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose. \textsuperscript{28} These things were done in Bethabara beyond Jordan, where John was baptizing. \textsuperscript{29} The next day John sees Jesus coming unto him, and says, Behold the Lamb of God, which takes away the sin of the world. \textsuperscript{30} This is he of whom I said, After me comes a man which is preferred before me: for he was before me. \textsuperscript{31} And I knew him not: but that he should be made manifest to Israel, therefore am I come baptizing with water. \textsuperscript{32} And John bare record, saying, I saw the Spirit (o. pneuma) descending from heaven like a dove, and it abode upon him. \textsuperscript{33} And I knew him not: but he that sent me to baptize with water, the same said unto me, Upon whom you shall see the Spirit (o. pneuma) descending, and remaining on him, the same is he which baptizes with the Holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{34} And I saw, and bare record that this is the Son of God. \textsuperscript{35} Again the next day after John stood, and two of his disciples; \textsuperscript{36} And looking upon Jesus as he walked, he says, Behold the Lamb of God! \textsuperscript{37} And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus. \textsuperscript{38} Then Jesus turned, and saw them following, and says unto them, What seek all of you? They said unto him, Rabbi, (which is to say, being interpreted, Master,) where dwell you? \textsuperscript{39} He says unto them, Come and see. They came and saw where he dwelt, and abode with him that day: for it was about the tenth hour. \textsuperscript{40} One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother. \textsuperscript{41} He first finds his own brother Simon, and says unto him, We have found the Messiah, which is, being interpreted, the Christ. \textsuperscript{42} And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, he said, You are Simon the son of Jona: you shall be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone. \textsuperscript{43} The day following Jesus would go forth into Galilee, and finds Philip, and says unto him, Follow me. \textsuperscript{44} Now Philip was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter. \textsuperscript{45} Philip finds Nathanael, and says unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph. \textsuperscript{46} And Nathanael said unto him, Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip says unto him, Come and see. \textsuperscript{47} Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and says of him, Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile! \textsuperscript{48} Nathanael says unto him, Whence know you me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before that Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you. \textsuperscript{49} Nathanael answered and says unto him, Rabbi, you are the Son of God; you are the King of Israel. \textsuperscript{50} Jesus answered and said unto him, Because I said unto you, I saw you under the fig tree, believe you? you shall see greater things than these. \textsuperscript{51} And he says unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter all of you shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.\par

\subsection*{John 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there: \textsuperscript{2} And both Jesus was called, and his disciples, to the marriage. \textsuperscript{3} And when they wanted wine, the mother of Jesus says unto him, They have no wine. \textsuperscript{4} Jesus says unto her, Woman, what have I to do with you? mine hour is not yet come. \textsuperscript{5} His mother says unto the servants, Whatsoever he says unto you, do it. \textsuperscript{6} And there were set there six water pots of stone, after the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three firkins apiece. \textsuperscript{7} Jesus says unto them, Fill the water pots with water. And they filled them up to the brim. \textsuperscript{8} And he says unto them, Draw out now, and bear unto the governor of the feast. And they bare it. \textsuperscript{9} When the ruler of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and knew not whence it was: (but the servants which drew the water knew;) the governor of the feast called the bridegroom, \textsuperscript{10} And says unto him, Every man at the beginning does set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but you have kept the good wine until now. \textsuperscript{11} This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him. \textsuperscript{12} After this he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, and his brethren, and his disciples: and they continued there not many days. \textsuperscript{13} And the Jews' passover was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{14} And found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting: \textsuperscript{15} And when he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers' money, and overthrew the tables; \textsuperscript{16} And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things behind; make not my Father's house an house of merchandise. \textsuperscript{17} And his disciples remembered that it was written, The zeal of yours house has eaten me up. \textsuperscript{18} Then answered the Jews and said unto him, What sign show you unto us, seeing that you do these things? \textsuperscript{19} Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. \textsuperscript{20} Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and will you rear it up in three days? \textsuperscript{21} But he spoke of the temple of his body. \textsuperscript{22} When therefore he was risen from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this unto them; and they believed the scripture, and the word (o. logos) which Jesus had said. \textsuperscript{23} Now when he was in Jerusalem at the passover, in the feast day, many believed in his name, when they saw the miracles which he did. \textsuperscript{24} But Jesus did not commit himself unto them, because he knew all men, \textsuperscript{25} And needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man.\par

\subsection*{John 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews: \textsuperscript{2} The same came to Jesus by night, and said unto him, Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher come from God: for no man can do these miracles that you do, except God be with him. \textsuperscript{3} Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. \textsuperscript{4} Nicodemus says unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother's womb, and be born? \textsuperscript{5} Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, (o. pneuma) he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. \textsuperscript{6} That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit (o. pneuma) is spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{7} Marvel not that I said unto you, All of you must be born again. \textsuperscript{8} The wind (o. pneuma) blows where it decides, and you hear the sound thereof, but can not tell whence it comes, and where it goes: so is every one that is born of the Spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{9} Nicodemus answered and said unto him, How can these things be? \textsuperscript{10} Jesus answered and said unto him, Are you a master of Israel, and know not these things? \textsuperscript{11} Verily, verily, I say unto you, We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and all of you receive not our witness. \textsuperscript{12} If I have told you earthly things, and all of you believe not, how shall all of you believe, if I tell you of heavenly things? \textsuperscript{13} And no man has ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven. \textsuperscript{14} And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: \textsuperscript{15} That whosoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life. \textsuperscript{16} For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believes in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. \textsuperscript{17} For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. \textsuperscript{18} He that believes on him is not condemned: but he that believes not is condemned already, because he has not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God. \textsuperscript{19} And this is the condemnation, that light has come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. \textsuperscript{20} For every one that does evil hates the light, neither comes to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. \textsuperscript{21} But he that does truth comes to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God. \textsuperscript{22} After these things came Jesus and his disciples into the land of Judaea; and there he tarried with them, and baptized. \textsuperscript{23} And John also was baptizing in Aenon near to Salim, because there was much water there: and they came, and were baptized. \textsuperscript{24} For John was not yet cast into prison. \textsuperscript{25} Then there arose a question between some of John's disciples and the Jews about purifying. \textsuperscript{26} And they came unto John, and said unto him, Rabbi, he that was with you beyond Jordan, to whom you bare witness, behold, the same baptizes, and all men come to him. \textsuperscript{27} John answered and said, A man can receive nothing, except it be given him from heaven. \textsuperscript{28} All of you yourselves bear me witness, that I said, I am not the Christ, but that I am sent before him. \textsuperscript{29} He that has the bride is the bridegroom: but the friend of the bridegroom, which stands and hears him, rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom's voice: this my joy therefore is fulfilled. \textsuperscript{30} He must increase, but I must decrease. \textsuperscript{31} He that comes from above is above all: he that is of the earth is earthly, and speaks of the earth: he that comes from heaven is above all. \textsuperscript{32} And what he has seen and heard, that he testifies; and no man receives his testimony. \textsuperscript{33} He that has received his testimony has set to his seal that God is true. \textsuperscript{34} For he whom God has sent speaks the words (o. rhema) of God: for God gives not the Spirit (o. pneuma) by measure unto him. \textsuperscript{35} The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into his hand. \textsuperscript{36} He that believes on the Son has everlasting life: and he that believes not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abides on him.\par

\subsection*{John 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} When therefore the LORD knew how the Pharisees had heard that Jesus made and baptized more disciples than John, \textsuperscript{2} (Though Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples,) \textsuperscript{3} He left Judaea, and departed again into Galilee. \textsuperscript{4} And he must essentially go through Samaria. \textsuperscript{5} Then comes he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph. \textsuperscript{6} Now Jacob's well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well: and it was about the sixth hour. \textsuperscript{7} There comes a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus says unto her, Give me to drink. \textsuperscript{8} (For his disciples were gone away unto the city to buy food.) \textsuperscript{9} Then says the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it that you, being a Jew, ask drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans. \textsuperscript{10} Jesus answered and said unto her, If you knew the gift of God, and who it is that says to you, Give me to drink; you would have asked of him, and he would have given you living water. \textsuperscript{11} The woman says unto him, Sir, you have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: from whence then have you that living water? \textsuperscript{12} Are you greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattle? \textsuperscript{13} Jesus answered and said unto her, Whosoever drinks of this water shall thirst again: \textsuperscript{14} But whosoever drinks of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. \textsuperscript{15} The woman says unto him, Sir, give me this water, that I thirst not, neither come here to draw. \textsuperscript{16} Jesus says unto her, Go, call your husband, and come here. \textsuperscript{17} The woman answered and said, I have no husband. Jesus said unto her, You have well said, I have no husband: \textsuperscript{18} For you have had five husbands; and he whom you now have is not your husband: in that said you truly. \textsuperscript{19} The woman says unto him, Sir, I perceive that you are a prophet. \textsuperscript{20} Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and all of you say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship. \textsuperscript{21} Jesus says unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour comes, when all of you shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. \textsuperscript{22} All of you worship all of you know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews. \textsuperscript{23} But the hour comes, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit (o. pneuma) and in truth: for the Father seeks such to worship him. \textsuperscript{24} God is a Spirit: (o. pneuma) and they that worship him must worship him in spirit (o. pneuma) and in truth. \textsuperscript{25} The woman says unto him, I know that Messiah comes, which is called Christ: when he has come, he will tell us all things. \textsuperscript{26} Jesus says unto her, I that speak unto you am he. \textsuperscript{27} And upon this came his disciples, and marvelled that he talked with the woman: yet no man said, What seek you? or, Why talk you with her? \textsuperscript{28} The woman then left her water pot, and went her way into the city, and says to the men, \textsuperscript{29} Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ? \textsuperscript{30} Then they went out of the city, and came unto him. \textsuperscript{31} In the mean while his disciples prayed him, saying, Master, eat. \textsuperscript{32} But he said unto them, I have food to eat that all of you know not of. \textsuperscript{33} Therefore said the disciples one to another, Has any man brought him ought to eat? \textsuperscript{34} Jesus says unto them, My food is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work. \textsuperscript{35} Say not all of you, There are yet four months, and then comes harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest. \textsuperscript{36} And he that reaps receives wages, and gathers fruit unto life eternal: that both he that sows and he that reaps may rejoice together. \textsuperscript{37} And herein is that saying (o. logos) true, One sows, and another reaps. \textsuperscript{38} I sent you to reap that whereon all of you bestowed no labour: other men laboured, and all of you are entered into their labours. \textsuperscript{39} And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him for the saying (o. logos) of the woman, which testified, He told me all that ever I did. \textsuperscript{40} So when the Samaritans were come unto him, they besought him that he would tarry with them: and he abode there two days. \textsuperscript{41} And many more believed because of his own word; (o. logos) \textsuperscript{42} And said unto the woman, Now we believe, not because of your saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world. \textsuperscript{43} Now after two days he departed thence, and went into Galilee. \textsuperscript{44} For Jesus himself testified, that a prophet has no honour in his own country. \textsuperscript{45} Then when he was come into Galilee, the Galilaeans received him, having seen all the things that he did at Jerusalem at the feast: for they also went unto the feast. \textsuperscript{46} So Jesus came again into Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman, whose son was sick at Capernaum. \textsuperscript{47} When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judaea into Galilee, he went unto him, and besought him that he would come down, and heal his son: for he was at the point of death. \textsuperscript{48} Then said Jesus unto him, Except all of you see signs and wonders, all of you will not believe. \textsuperscript{49} The nobleman says unto him, Sir, come down before my child die. \textsuperscript{50} Jesus says unto him, Go your way; your son lives. And the man believed the word (o. logos) that Jesus had spoken unto him, and he went his way. \textsuperscript{51} And as he was now going down, his servants met him, and told him, saying, Your son lives. \textsuperscript{52} Then enquired he of them the hour when he began to amend. And they said unto him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him. \textsuperscript{53} So the father knew that it was at the same hour, in the which Jesus said unto him, Your son lives: and himself believed, and his whole house. \textsuperscript{54} This is again the second miracle that Jesus did, when he was come out of Judaea into Galilee.\par

\subsection*{John 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} After this there was a feast of the Jews; and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{2} Now there is at Jerusalem by the sheep market a pool, which is called in the Hebrew tongue Bethesda, having five porches. \textsuperscript{3} In these lay a great multitude of impotent folk, of blind, halt, withered, waiting for the moving of the water. \textsuperscript{4} For an angel went down at a certain season into the pool, and troubled the water: whosoever then first after the troubling of the water stepped in was made whole of whatsoever disease he had. \textsuperscript{5} And a certain man was there, which had an infirmity thirty and eight years. \textsuperscript{6} When Jesus saw him lie, and knew that he had been now a long time in that case, he says unto him, Will you be made whole? \textsuperscript{7} The impotent man answered him, Sir, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool: but while I am coming, another steps down before me. \textsuperscript{8} Jesus says unto him, Rise, take up your bed, and walk. \textsuperscript{9} And immediately the man was made whole, and took up his bed, and walked: and on the same day was the sabbath. \textsuperscript{10} The Jews therefore said unto him that was cured, It is the sabbath day: it is not lawful for you to carry your bed. \textsuperscript{11} He answered them, He that made me whole, the same said unto me, Take up your bed, and walk. \textsuperscript{12} Then asked they him, What man is that which said unto you, Take up your bed, and walk? \textsuperscript{13} And he that was healed know not who it was: for Jesus had conveyed himself away, a multitude being in that place. \textsuperscript{14} Afterward Jesus finds him in the temple, and said unto him, Behold, you are made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto you. \textsuperscript{15} The man departed, and told the Jews that it was Jesus, which had made him whole. \textsuperscript{16} And therefore did the Jews persecute Jesus, and sought to slay him, because he had done these things on the sabbath day. \textsuperscript{17} But Jesus answered them, My Father works until now, and I work. \textsuperscript{18} Therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only had broken the sabbath, but said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God. \textsuperscript{19} Then answered Jesus and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he sees the Father do: for what things whatsoever he does, these also does the Son likewise. \textsuperscript{20} For the Father loves the Son, and shows him all things that himself does: and he will show him greater works than these, that all of you may marvel. \textsuperscript{21} For as the Father raises up the dead, and replenishes life to them; even so the Son gives life to whom he will. \textsuperscript{22} For the Father judges no man, but has committed all judgment unto the Son: \textsuperscript{23} That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He that honors not the Son honors not the Father which has sent him. \textsuperscript{24} Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that hears my word, (o. logos) and believes on him that sent me, has everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life. \textsuperscript{25} Verily, verily, I say unto you, The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live. \textsuperscript{26} For as the Father has life in himself; so has he given to the Son to have life in himself; \textsuperscript{27} And has given him authority to execute judgment also, because he is the Son of man. \textsuperscript{28} Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, \textsuperscript{29} And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation. \textsuperscript{30} I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which has sent me. \textsuperscript{31} If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true. \textsuperscript{32} There is another that bears witness of me; and I know that the witness which he witnesses of me is true. \textsuperscript{33} All of you sent unto John, and he bare witness unto the truth. \textsuperscript{34} But I receive not testimony from man: but these things I say, that all of you might be saved. \textsuperscript{35} He was a burning and a shining light: and all of you were willing for a season to rejoice in his light. \textsuperscript{36} But I have greater witness than that of John: for the works which the Father has given me to finish, the same works that I do, bear witness of me, that the Father has sent me. \textsuperscript{37} And the Father himself, which has sent me, has borne witness of me. All of you have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape. \textsuperscript{38} And all of you have not his word (o. logos) abiding in you: for whom he has sent, him all of you believe not. \textsuperscript{39} Search the scriptures; for in them all of you think all of you have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me. \textsuperscript{40} And all of you will not come to me, that all of you might have life. \textsuperscript{41} I receive not honour from men. \textsuperscript{42} But I know you, that all of you have not the love (o. agape) of God in you. \textsuperscript{43} I am come in my Father's name, and all of you receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him all of you will receive. \textsuperscript{44} How can all of you believe, which receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that comes from God only? \textsuperscript{45} Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuses you, even Moses, in whom all of you trust. \textsuperscript{46} For had all of you believed Moses, all of you would have believed me; for he wrote of me. \textsuperscript{47} But if all of you believe not his writings, how shall all of you believe my words? (o. rhema)\par

John 5:2 TSK note: market or, gate, pool, Bethesda The supposed remains of the pool of Bethesda are situated on the east of Jerusalem, contiguous on one side to St. Stephen's gate, and on the other to the area of the temple. Maundrell states that, "it is 120 paces long, and forty broad, and at least eight deep, but void of water. At its west end it discovers some old arches, now damned up. These some will have to be porches, in which sat that multitude of lame, halt, and blind. But it is not likely, for instead of five, there are but three."\par
John 5:4 TSK note: whosoever The sanative property of this pool has been supposed by some to have been communicated by the blood of the sacrifices, and others have referred it to the mineral properties of the waters. But: 1. The beasts for sacrifice were not washed here, but in a laver in the temple. 2. No natural property could cure all manner of diseases. 3. The cure only extended to the first who entered. 4. It took place only at one particular time. 5. As the healing was effected by immersion, it must have been instantaneous; and it was never failing in it effects. All which, not being observed in medicinal waters, determine the cures to have been miraculous, as expressly stated in the text. first;, ; , ;, was made\par

\subsection*{John 6}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} After these things Jesus went over the sea of Galilee, which is the sea of Tiberias. \textsuperscript{2} And a great multitude followed him, because they saw his miracles which he did on them that were diseased. \textsuperscript{3} And Jesus went up into a mountain, and there he sat with his disciples. \textsuperscript{4} And the passover, a feast of the Jews, was nigh. \textsuperscript{5} When Jesus then lifted up his eyes, and saw a great company come unto him, he says unto Philip, Whence shall we buy bread, that these may eat? \textsuperscript{6} And this he said to prove him: for he himself knew what he would do. \textsuperscript{7} Philip answered him, Two hundred pennyworth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may take a little. \textsuperscript{8} One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, says unto him, \textsuperscript{9} There is a lad here, which has five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many? \textsuperscript{10} And Jesus said, Make the men sit down. Now there was much grass in the place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand. \textsuperscript{11} And Jesus took the loaves; and when he had given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to them that were set down; and likewise of the fishes as much as they would. \textsuperscript{12} When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost. \textsuperscript{13} Therefore they gathered them together, and filled twelve baskets with the fragments of the five barley loaves, which remained over and above unto them that had eaten. \textsuperscript{14} Then those men, when they had seen the miracle that Jesus did, said, This is truthfully that prophet that should come into the world. \textsuperscript{15} When Jesus therefore perceived that they would come and take him by force, to make him a king, he departed again into a mountain himself alone. \textsuperscript{16} And when even was now come, his disciples went down unto the sea, \textsuperscript{17} And entered into a ship, and went over the sea toward Capernaum. And it was now dark, and Jesus was not come to them. \textsuperscript{18} And the sea arose by reason of a great wind that blew. \textsuperscript{19} So when they had rowed about five and twenty or thirty furlongs, they see Jesus walking on the sea, and drawing nigh unto the ship: and they were afraid. \textsuperscript{20} But he says unto them, It is I; be not afraid. \textsuperscript{21} Then they willingly received him into the ship: and immediately the ship was at the land where they went. \textsuperscript{22} The day following, when the people which stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there, save that one into where his disciples were entered, and that Jesus went not with his disciples into the boat, but that his disciples were gone away alone; \textsuperscript{23} (nevertheless there came other boats from Tiberias nigh unto the place where they did eat bread, after that the Lord had given thanks:) \textsuperscript{24} When the people therefore saw that Jesus was not there, neither his disciples, they also went on board ships, and came to Capernaum, seeking for Jesus. \textsuperscript{25} And when they had found him on the other side of the sea, they said unto him, Rabbi, when came you here? \textsuperscript{26} Jesus answered them and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, All of you seek me, not because all of you saw the miracles, but because all of you did eat of the loaves, and were filled. \textsuperscript{27} Labour not for the food which perishes, but for that food which endures unto everlasting life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him has God the Father sealed. \textsuperscript{28} Then said they unto him, What shall we do, that we might work the works of God? \textsuperscript{29} Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that all of you believe on him whom he has sent. \textsuperscript{30} They said therefore unto him, What sign show you then, that we may see, and believe you? what do you work? \textsuperscript{31} Our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat. \textsuperscript{32} Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven. \textsuperscript{33} For the bread of God is he which comes down from heaven, and gives life unto the world. \textsuperscript{34} Then said they unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread. \textsuperscript{35} And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that comes to me shall never hunger; and he that believes on me shall never thirst. \textsuperscript{36} But I said unto you, That all of you also have seen me, and believe not. \textsuperscript{37} All that the Father gives me shall come to me; and him that comes to me I will in no wise cast out. \textsuperscript{38} For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. \textsuperscript{39} And this is the Father's will which has sent me, that of all which he has given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. \textsuperscript{40} And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which sees the Son, and believes on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day. \textsuperscript{41} The Jews then murmured at him, because he said, I am the bread which came down from heaven. \textsuperscript{42} And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he says, I came down from heaven? \textsuperscript{43} Jesus therefore answered and said unto them, Murmur not among yourselves. \textsuperscript{44} No man can come to me, except the Father which has sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day. \textsuperscript{45} It is written in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God. Every man therefore that has heard, and has learned of the Father, comes unto me. \textsuperscript{46} Not that any man has seen the Father, save he which is of God, he has seen the Father. \textsuperscript{47} Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believes on me has everlasting life. \textsuperscript{48} I am that bread of life. \textsuperscript{49} Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness, and are dead. \textsuperscript{50} This is the bread which comes down from heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die. \textsuperscript{51} I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world. \textsuperscript{52} The Jews therefore strove among themselves, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat? \textsuperscript{53} Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except all of you eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, all of you have no life in you. \textsuperscript{54} Whoso eats my flesh, and drinks my blood, has eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day. \textsuperscript{55} For my flesh is food indeed, and my blood is drink indeed. \textsuperscript{56} He that eats my flesh, and drinks my blood, dwells in me, and I in him. \textsuperscript{57} As the living Father has sent me, and I live by the Father: so he that eats me, even he shall live by me. \textsuperscript{58} This is that bread which came down from heaven: not as your fathers did eat manna, and are dead: he that eats of this bread shall live for ever. \textsuperscript{59} These things said he in the synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum. \textsuperscript{60} Many therefore of his disciples, when they had heard this, said, This is an hard saying; (o. logos) who can hear it? \textsuperscript{61} When Jesus knew in himself that his disciples murmured at it, he said unto them, Does this offend you? \textsuperscript{62} What and if all of you shall see the Son of man ascend up where he was before? \textsuperscript{63} It is the spirit that gives life; (o. pneuma) the flesh profits nothing: the words (o. rhema) that I speak unto you, they are spirit, (o. pneuma) and they are life. \textsuperscript{64} But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who should betray him. \textsuperscript{65} And he said, Therefore said I unto you, that no man can come unto me, except it were given unto him of my Father. \textsuperscript{66} From that time many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him. \textsuperscript{67} Then said Jesus unto the twelve, Will all of you also go away? \textsuperscript{68} Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? you have the words (o. rhema) of eternal life. \textsuperscript{69} And we believe and are sure that you are that Christ, the Son of the living God. \textsuperscript{70} Jesus answered them, Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil? \textsuperscript{71} He spoke of Judas Iscariot the son of Simon: for he it was that should betray him, being one of the twelve.\par

\subsection*{John 7}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} After these things Jesus walked in Galilee: for he would not walk in Jewry, because the Jews sought to kill him. \textsuperscript{2} Now the Jew's feast of tabernacles was at hand. \textsuperscript{3} His brethren therefore said unto him, Depart behind, and go into Judaea, that your disciples also may see the works that you do. \textsuperscript{4} For there is no man that does any thing in secret, and he himself seeks to be known openly. If you do these things, show yourself to the world. \textsuperscript{5} For neither did his brethren believe in him. \textsuperscript{6} Then Jesus said unto them, My time is not yet come: but your time is always ready. \textsuperscript{7} The world cannot hate you; but me it hates, because I testify of it, that the works thereof are evil. \textsuperscript{8} Go all of you up unto this feast: I go not up yet unto this feast: for my time is not yet full come. \textsuperscript{9} When he had said these words unto them, he abode still in Galilee. \textsuperscript{10} But when his brethren were gone up, then went he also up unto the feast, not openly, but as it were in secret. \textsuperscript{11} Then the Jews sought him at the feast, and said, Where is he? \textsuperscript{12} And there was much murmuring among the people concerning him: for some said, He is a good man: others said, Nay; but he deceives the people. \textsuperscript{13} Nevertheless no man spoke openly of him for fear of the Jews. \textsuperscript{14} Now about the midst of the feast Jesus went up into the temple, and taught. \textsuperscript{15} And the Jews marvelled, saying, How knows this man letters, having never learned? \textsuperscript{16} Jesus answered them, and said, My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me. \textsuperscript{17} If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself. \textsuperscript{18} He that speaks of himself seeks his own glory: but he that seeks his glory that sent him, the same is true, and no unrighteousness is in him. \textsuperscript{19} Did not Moses give you the law, and yet none of you keeps the law? Why go all of you about to kill me? \textsuperscript{20} The people answered and said, You have a devil: who goes about to kill you? \textsuperscript{21} Jesus answered and said unto them, I have done one work, and all of you all marvel. \textsuperscript{22} Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and all of you on the sabbath day circumcise a man. \textsuperscript{23} If a man on the sabbath day receive circumcision, that the law of Moses should not be broken; are all of you angry at me, because I have made a man everything whole on the sabbath day? \textsuperscript{24} Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment. \textsuperscript{25} Then said some of them of Jerusalem, Is not this he, whom they seek to kill? \textsuperscript{26} But, lo, he speaks boldly, and they say nothing unto him. Do the rulers know indeed that this is the very Christ? \textsuperscript{27} Nevertheless we know this man whence he is: but when Christ comes, no man knows whence he is. \textsuperscript{28} Then cried Jesus in the temple as he taught, saying, All of you both know me, and all of you know whence I am: and I am not come of myself, but he that sent me is true, whom all of you know not. \textsuperscript{29} But I know him: for I am from him, and he has sent me. \textsuperscript{30} Then they sought to take him: but no man laid hands on him, because his hour was not yet come. \textsuperscript{31} And many of the people believed on him, and said, When Christ comes, will he do more miracles than these which this man has done? \textsuperscript{32} The Pharisees heard that the people murmured such things concerning him; and the Pharisees and the chief priests sent officers to take him. \textsuperscript{33} Then said Jesus unto them, Yet a little while am I with you, and then I go unto him that sent me. \textsuperscript{34} All of you shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, thither all of you cannot come. \textsuperscript{35} Then said the Jews among themselves, Where will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles? \textsuperscript{36} What manner of saying (o. logos) is this that he said, All of you shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, thither all of you cannot come? \textsuperscript{37} In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. \textsuperscript{38} He that believes on me, as the scripture has said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. \textsuperscript{39} (But this spoke he of the Spirit, (o. pneuma) which they that believe on him should receive: for the Holy Spirit (o. pneuma) was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.) \textsuperscript{40} Many of the people therefore, when they heard this saying, (o. logos) said, Truthfully this is the Prophet. \textsuperscript{41} Others said, This is the Christ. But some said, Shall Christ come out of Galilee? \textsuperscript{42} Has not the scripture said, That Christ comes of the seed of David, and out of the town of Bethlehem, where David was? \textsuperscript{43} So there was a division among the people because of him. \textsuperscript{44} And some of them would have taken him; but no man laid hands on him. \textsuperscript{45} Then came the officers to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said unto them, Why have all of you not brought him? \textsuperscript{46} The officers answered, Never man spoke like this man. \textsuperscript{47} Then answered them the Pharisees, Are all of you also deceived? \textsuperscript{48} Have any of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed on him? \textsuperscript{49} But this people who knows not the law are cursed. \textsuperscript{50} Nicodemus says unto them, (he that came to Jesus by night, being one of them,) \textsuperscript{51} Does our law judge any man, before it hear him, and know what he does? \textsuperscript{52} They answered and said unto him, Are you also of Galilee? Search, and look: for out of Galilee arises no prophet. \textsuperscript{53} And every man went unto his own house.\par

This reasoning was in perfect accordance with the principles of the Jews. So Tanchuma, "Circumcision, which is performed on one of the 248 members of man, vacates the sabbath; how much more the whole body of a man!"\par

\subsection*{John 8}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Jesus went unto the mount of Olives. \textsuperscript{2} And early in the morning he came again into the temple, and all the people came unto him; and he sat down, and taught them. \textsuperscript{3} And the scribes and Pharisees brought unto him a woman taken in adultery; and when they had set her in the midst, \textsuperscript{4} They say unto him, Master, this woman was taken in adultery, in the very act. \textsuperscript{5} Now Moses in the law commanded us, that such should be stoned: but what says you? \textsuperscript{6} This they said, tempting him, that they might have to accuse him. But Jesus stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground, as though he heard them not. \textsuperscript{7} So when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her. \textsuperscript{8} And again he stooped down, and wrote on the ground. \textsuperscript{9} And they which heard it, being convicted by their own conscience, went out one by one, beginning at the eldest, even unto the last: and Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst. \textsuperscript{10} When Jesus had lifted up himself, and saw none but the woman, he said unto her, Woman, where are those yours accusers? has no man condemned you? \textsuperscript{11} She said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said unto her, Neither do I condemn you: go, and sin no more. \textsuperscript{12} Then spoke Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that follows me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life. \textsuperscript{13} The Pharisees therefore said unto him, You bear record of yourself; your record is not true. \textsuperscript{14} Jesus answered and said unto them, Though I bear record of myself, yet my record is true: for I know whence I came, and where I go; but all of you cannot tell whence I come, and where I go. \textsuperscript{15} All of you judge after the flesh; I judge no man. \textsuperscript{16} And yet if I judge, my judgment is true: for I am not alone, but I and the Father that sent me. \textsuperscript{17} It is also written in your law, that the testimony of two men is true. \textsuperscript{18} I am one that bear witness of myself, and the Father that sent me bears witness of me. \textsuperscript{19} Then said they unto him, Where is your Father? Jesus answered, All of you neither know me, nor my Father: if all of you had known me, all of you should have known my Father also. \textsuperscript{20} These words (o. rhema) spoke Jesus in the treasury, as he taught in the temple: and no man laid hands on him; for his hour was not yet come. \textsuperscript{21} Then said Jesus again unto them, I go my way, and all of you shall seek me, and shall die in your sins: where I go, all of you cannot come. \textsuperscript{22} Then said the Jews, Will he kill himself? because he says, Where I go, all of you cannot come. \textsuperscript{23} And he said unto them, All of you are from beneath; I am from above: all of you are of this world; I am not of this world. \textsuperscript{24} I said therefore unto you, that all of you shall die in your sins: for if all of you believe not that I am he, all of you shall die in your sins. \textsuperscript{25} Then said they unto him, Who are you? And Jesus says unto them, Even the same that I said unto you from the beginning. \textsuperscript{26} I have many things to say and to judge of you: but he that sent me is true; and I speak to the world those things which I have heard of him. \textsuperscript{27} They understood not that he spoke to them of the Father. \textsuperscript{28} Then said Jesus unto them, When all of you have lifted up the Son of man, then shall all of you know that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself; but as my Father has taught me, I speak these things. \textsuperscript{29} And he that sent me is with me: the Father has not left me alone; for I do always those things that please him. \textsuperscript{30} As he spoke these words, many believed on him. \textsuperscript{31} Then said Jesus to those Jews which believed on him, If all of you continue in my word, (o. logos) then are all of you my disciples indeed; \textsuperscript{32} And all of you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free. \textsuperscript{33} They answered him, We be Abraham's seed, and were never in bondage to any man: how says you, All of you shall be made free? \textsuperscript{34} Jesus answered them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever commits sin is the servant of sin. \textsuperscript{35} And the servant abides not in the house for ever: but the Son abides ever. \textsuperscript{36} If the Son therefore shall make you free, all of you shall be free indeed. \textsuperscript{37} I know that all of you are Abraham's seed; but all of you seek to kill me, because my word (o. logos) has no place in you. \textsuperscript{38} I speak that which I have seen with my Father: and all of you do that which all of you have seen with your father. \textsuperscript{39} They answered and said unto him, Abraham is our father. Jesus says unto them, If all of you were Abraham's children, all of you would do the works of Abraham. \textsuperscript{40} But now all of you seek to kill me, a man that has told you the truth, which I have heard of God: this did not Abraham. \textsuperscript{41} All of you do the deeds of your father. Then said they to him, We be not born of fornication; we have one Father, even God. \textsuperscript{42} Jesus said unto them, If God were your Father, all of you would love me: for I proceeded forth and came from God; neither came I of myself, but he sent me. \textsuperscript{43} Why do all of you not understand my speech? even because all of you cannot hear my word. (o. logos) \textsuperscript{44} All of you are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father all of you will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it. \textsuperscript{45} And because I tell you the truth, all of you believe me not. \textsuperscript{46} Which of you convinces me of sin? And if I say the truth, why do all of you not believe me? \textsuperscript{47} He that is of God hears God's words: (o. rhema) all of you therefore hear them not, because all of you are not of God. \textsuperscript{48} Then answered the Jews, and said unto him, Say we not well that you are a Samaritan, and have a devil? \textsuperscript{49} Jesus answered, I have not a devil; but I honour my Father, and all of you do dishonour me. \textsuperscript{50} And I seek not mine own glory: there is one that seeks and judges. \textsuperscript{51} Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, (o. logos) he shall never see death. \textsuperscript{52} Then said the Jews unto him, Now we know that you have a devil. Abraham is dead, and the prophets; and you says, If a man keep my saying, (o. logos) he shall never taste of death. \textsuperscript{53} Are you greater than our father Abraham, which is dead? and the prophets are dead: whom make you yourself? \textsuperscript{54} Jesus answered, If I honour myself, my honour is nothing: it is my Father that honors me; of whom all of you say, that he is your God: \textsuperscript{55} Yet all of you have not known him; but I know him: and if I should say, I know him not, I shall be a liar like unto you: but I know him, and keep his saying. (o. logos) \textsuperscript{56} Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad. \textsuperscript{57} Then said the Jews unto him, You are not yet fifty years old, and have you seen Abraham? \textsuperscript{58} Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am. \textsuperscript{59} Then took they up stones to cast at him: but Jesus hid himself, and went out of the temple, going through the midst of them, and so passed by.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
John 8:12 TSK note: I am, ;, ; , ;, shall not, ;, ; , ;, shall have\par
John 8:20 TSK note: in the treasury; , and no\par
John 8:21 TSK note: I go, ; , and shall die; , ; whither\par
John 8:23 TSK note: Ye are from, ; ye are of\par
John 8:26 TSK note: have many; to judge, but, ; and I\par
John 8:28 TSK note: When, then;, ; and that, ; but\par
John 8:41 TSK note: do, We be; , ; we have\par
John 8:44 TSK note: are, ; , He was; , ;, and abode; When\par
John 8:54 TSK note: If, ; it is, ;, ; , ; ye say\par
John 8:55 TSK note: ye have not, ;, ; but, ; shall;, ; and keep\par
John 8:58 Brenton note: Name of God: Ho On (ὁ ὤν) — The One who is Common English renderings: I am; which is. Echoes the divine self-existence revealed in Exodus and becomes especially significant in Johannine Christology.\par
John 8:58 TSK note: Verily, Before, ; , I am That our Lord by this expression asserted his divinity and eternal existence, as the great I AM, appears evident from the use of the present tense, instead of the past tense, from its being in answer to the Jews, who enquired whether he had seen Abraham, and from its being thus understood by the multitude, who were exasperated at it to such a degree that they took up stones to stone him. The ancient Jews not only believed that the Messiah was superior to and Lord of all the patriarchs, and even of angels, but that his celestial nature existed with God from whom it emanated, before the creation, and that the creation was effected by his ministry.\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{John 9}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth. \textsuperscript{2} And his disciples asked him, saying, Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind? \textsuperscript{3} Jesus answered, Neither has this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him. \textsuperscript{4} I must work the works of him that sent me, while it is day: the night comes, when no man can work. \textsuperscript{5} As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world. \textsuperscript{6} When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay, \textsuperscript{7} And said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam, (which is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing. \textsuperscript{8} The neighbours therefore, and they which before had seen him that he was blind, said, Is not this he that sat and begged? \textsuperscript{9} Some said, This is he: others said, He is like him: but he said, I am he. \textsuperscript{10} Therefore said they unto him, How were yours eyes opened? \textsuperscript{11} He answered and said, A man that is called Jesus made clay, and anointed mine eyes, and said unto me, Go to the pool of Siloam, and wash: and I went and washed, and I received sight. \textsuperscript{12} Then said they unto him, Where is he? He said, I know not. \textsuperscript{13} They brought to the Pharisees him that in old times was blind. \textsuperscript{14} And it was the sabbath day when Jesus made the clay, and opened his eyes. \textsuperscript{15} Then again the Pharisees also asked him how he had received his sight. He said unto them, He put clay upon mine eyes, and I washed, and do see. \textsuperscript{16} Therefore said some of the Pharisees, This man is not of God, because he keeps not the sabbath day. Others said, How can a man that is a sinner do such miracles? And there was a division among them. \textsuperscript{17} They say unto the blind man again, What says you of him, that he has opened yours eyes? He said, He is a prophet. \textsuperscript{18} But the Jews did not believe concerning him, that he had been blind, and received his sight, until they called the parents of him that had received his sight. \textsuperscript{19} And they asked them, saying, Is this your son, who all of you say was born blind? how then does he now see? \textsuperscript{20} His parents answered them and said, We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind: \textsuperscript{21} But by what means he now sees, we know not; or who has opened his eyes, we know not: he is of age; ask him: he shall speak for himself. \textsuperscript{22} These words spoke his parents, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had agreed already, that if any man did confess that he was Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue. \textsuperscript{23} Therefore said his parents, He is of age; ask him. \textsuperscript{24} Then again called they the man that was blind, and said unto him, Give God the praise: we know that this man is a sinner. \textsuperscript{25} He answered and said, Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see. \textsuperscript{26} Then said they to him again, What did he to you? how opened he yours eyes? \textsuperscript{27} He answered them, I have told you already, and all of you did not hear: wherefore would all of you hear it again? will all of you also be his disciples? \textsuperscript{28} Then they reviled him, and said, You are his disciple; but we are Moses' disciples. \textsuperscript{29} We know that God spoke unto Moses: as for this fellow, we know not from whence he is. \textsuperscript{30} The man answered and said unto them, Why herein is a marvellous thing, that all of you know not from whence he is, and yet he has opened mine eyes. \textsuperscript{31} Now we know that God hears not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and does his will, him he hears. \textsuperscript{32} Since the world began was it not heard that any man opened the eyes of one that was born blind. \textsuperscript{33} If this man were not of God, he could do nothing. \textsuperscript{34} They answered and said unto him, You were altogether born in sins, and do you teach us? And they cast him out. \textsuperscript{35} Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when he had found him, he said unto him, Do you believe on the Son of God? \textsuperscript{36} He answered and said, Who is he, Lord, that I might believe on him? \textsuperscript{37} And Jesus said unto him, You have both seen him, and it is he that talks with you. \textsuperscript{38} And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him. \textsuperscript{39} And Jesus said, For judgment I am come into this world, that they which see not might see; and that they which see might be made blind. \textsuperscript{40} And some of the Pharisees which were with him heard these words, and said unto him, Are we blind also? \textsuperscript{41} Jesus said unto them, If all of you were blind, all of you should have no sin: but now all of you say, We see; therefore your sin remains.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
John 9:5 TSK note: long, ;, ; , ; I am Our Lord here claims one of the titles given by the Jews to the Divine Being. So in Bammidbar Rabba, § 15, fol. 229.1, "The Israelites said to God, O Lord of the universe, thou commandest us to light lamps to thee, yet thou art the light of the world." It was also a title of the Messiah (see; ); and in a remarkable passage of Yalkut Rubeni, fol. 6, it is said on, "From this we learn that the holy and blessed God saw the light of the Messiah, and his works, before the world was created; and reserved it for the Messiah, and his generation, under the throne of his glory. Satan said to the holy and blessed God, For whom dost thou reserve that light which is under the throne of thy glory? God answered, For him who shall subdue thee, and overwhelm thee with confusion. Satan rejoined, Lord of the universe, shew that person to me. God said, Come, and see him. When he saw him, he was greatly agitated, and fell upon his face, saying, Truly this is the Messiah, who shall cast me and idolaters into hell."\par

John 9:7 TSK note: Go the pool;, Siloah, Shiloah Sent; and came\par

John 9:29 TSK note: know;, ; , ; , ; as for, ; , ; we know not\par

John 9:32 TSK note: Since It is worthy of remark, that, from the foundation of the world, no person born blind had been restored to sight, even by surgical operation, till about the year 1728; when the celebrated Dr. Cheselden, by couching the eyes of a young man fourteen years of age, restored them to perfect vision. This was the effect of well-directed surgery; that performed by Christ was wholly a miracle, effected by the power of God. The simple means employed could have had no effect in this case, and were merely employed as symbols. the world\par

\subsection*{John 10}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that enters not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbs up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber. \textsuperscript{2} But he that enters in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep. \textsuperscript{3} To him the gate keeper opens; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calls his own sheep by name, and leads them out. \textsuperscript{4} And when he puts forth his own sheep, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice. \textsuperscript{5} And a stranger will they not follow, but will flee from him: for they know not the voice of strangers. \textsuperscript{6} This parable spoke Jesus unto them: but they understood not what things they were which he spoke unto them. \textsuperscript{7} Then said Jesus unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep. \textsuperscript{8} All that ever came before me are thieves and robbers: but the sheep did not hear them. \textsuperscript{9} I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture. \textsuperscript{10} The thief comes not, but in order to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly. \textsuperscript{11} I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd gives his life for the sheep. \textsuperscript{12} But he that is a worker, and not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, sees the wolf coming, and left the sheep, and flees: and the wolf catches them, and scatters the sheep. \textsuperscript{13} The worker flees, because he is a worker, and cares not for the sheep. \textsuperscript{14} I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine. \textsuperscript{15} As the Father knows me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep. \textsuperscript{16} And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd. \textsuperscript{17} Therefore does my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again. \textsuperscript{18} No man takes it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment have I received of my Father. \textsuperscript{19} There was a division therefore again among the Jews for these sayings. (o. logos) \textsuperscript{20} And many of them said, He has a devil, and is mad; why hear all of you him? \textsuperscript{21} Others said, These are not the words (o. rhema) of him that has a devil. Can a devil open the eyes of the blind? \textsuperscript{22} And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter. \textsuperscript{23} And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon's porch. \textsuperscript{24} Then came the Jews round about him, and said unto him, How long do you make us to doubt? If you be the Christ, tell us plainly. \textsuperscript{25} Jesus answered them, I told you, and all of you believed not: the works that I do in my Father's name, they bear witness of me. \textsuperscript{26} But all of you believe not, because all of you are not of my sheep, as I said unto you. \textsuperscript{27} My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: \textsuperscript{28} And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. \textsuperscript{29} My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand. \textsuperscript{30} I and my Father are one. \textsuperscript{31} Then the Jews took up stones again to stone him. \textsuperscript{32} Jesus answered them, Many good works have I showed you from my Father; for which of those works do all of you stone me? \textsuperscript{33} The Jews answered him, saying, For a good work we stone you not; but for blasphemy; and because that you, being a man, make yourself God. \textsuperscript{34} Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, All of you are gods? \textsuperscript{35} If he called them gods, unto whom the word (o. logos) of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken; \textsuperscript{36} Say all of you of him, whom the Father has sanctified, and sent into the world, You blaspheme; because I said, I am the Son of God? \textsuperscript{37} If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not. \textsuperscript{38} But if I do, though all of you believe not me, believe the works: that all of you may know, and believe, that the Father is in me, and I in him. \textsuperscript{39} Therefore they sought again to take him: but he escaped out of their hand, \textsuperscript{40} And went away again beyond Jordan into the place where John at first baptized; and there he abode. \textsuperscript{41} And many resorted unto him, and said, John did no miracle: but all things that John spoke of this man were true. \textsuperscript{42} And many believed on him there.\par
