\subsection*{John 11}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now a certain man was sick, named Lazarus, of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha. \textsuperscript{2} (It was that Mary which anointed the Lord with ointment, and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.) \textsuperscript{3} Therefore his sisters sent unto him, saying, Lord, behold, he whom you love is sick. \textsuperscript{4} When Jesus heard that, he said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby. \textsuperscript{5} Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus. \textsuperscript{6} When he had heard therefore that he was sick, he abode two days still in the same place where he was. \textsuperscript{7} Then after that says he to his disciples, Let us go into Judaea again. \textsuperscript{8} His disciples say unto him, Master, the Jews of late sought to stone you; and go you thither again? \textsuperscript{9} Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours in the day? If any man walk in the day, he stumbles not, because he sees the light of this world. \textsuperscript{10} But if a man walk in the night, he stumbles, because there is no light in him. \textsuperscript{11} These things said he: and after that he says unto them, Our friend Lazarus sleeps; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep. \textsuperscript{12} Then said his disciples, Lord, if he sleep, he shall do well. \textsuperscript{13} Nevertheless Jesus spoke of his death: but they thought that he had spoken of taking of rest in sleep. \textsuperscript{14} Then said Jesus unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead. \textsuperscript{15} And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent all of you may believe; nevertheless let us go unto him. \textsuperscript{16} Then said Thomas, which is called Didymus, unto his fellow disciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him. \textsuperscript{17} Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already. \textsuperscript{18} Now Bethany was nigh unto Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off: \textsuperscript{19} And many of the Jews came to Martha and Mary, to comfort them concerning their brother. \textsuperscript{20} Then Martha, as soon as she heard that Jesus was coming, went and met him: but Mary sat still in the house. \textsuperscript{21} Then said Martha unto Jesus, Lord, if you had been here, my brother had not died. \textsuperscript{22} But I know, that even now, whatsoever you will ask of God, God will give it you. \textsuperscript{23} Jesus says unto her, Your brother shall rise again. \textsuperscript{24} Martha says unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day. \textsuperscript{25} Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believes in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: \textsuperscript{26} And whosoever lives and believes in me shall never die. Believe you this? \textsuperscript{27} She says unto him, Yea, Lord: I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world. \textsuperscript{28} And when she had so said, she went her way, and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, The Master has come, and calls for you. \textsuperscript{29} As soon as she heard that, she arose quickly, and came unto him. \textsuperscript{30} Now Jesus was not yet come into the town, but was in that place where Martha met him. \textsuperscript{31} The Jews then which were with her in the house, and comforted her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up hastily and went out, followed her, saying, She goes unto the grave to weep there. \textsuperscript{32} Then when Mary was come where Jesus was, and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying unto him, Lord, if you had been here, my brother had not died. \textsuperscript{33} When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping which came with her, he groaned in the spirit, (o. pneuma) and was troubled. \textsuperscript{34} And said, Where have all of you laid him? They said unto him, Lord, come and see. \textsuperscript{35} Jesus wept. \textsuperscript{36} Then said the Jews, Behold how he loved him! \textsuperscript{37} And some of them said, Could not this man, which opened the eyes of the blind, have caused that even this man should not have died? \textsuperscript{38} Jesus therefore again groaning in himself comes to the grave. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it. \textsuperscript{39} Jesus said, Take all of you away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, says unto him, Lord, by this time he stinks: for he has been dead four days. \textsuperscript{40} Jesus says unto her, Said I not unto you, that, if you would believe, you should see the glory of God? \textsuperscript{41} Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid. And Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank you that you have heard me. \textsuperscript{42} And I knew that you hear me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, that they may believe that you have sent me. \textsuperscript{43} And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth. \textsuperscript{44} And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with grave clothes: and his face was bound about with a cloth. Jesus says unto them, Loose him, and let him go. \textsuperscript{45} Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, believed on him. \textsuperscript{46} But some of them went their ways to the Pharisees, and told them what things Jesus had done. \textsuperscript{47} Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man does many miracles. \textsuperscript{48} If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation. \textsuperscript{49} And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, All of you know nothing at all, \textsuperscript{50} Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not. \textsuperscript{51} And this spoke he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; \textsuperscript{52} And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad. \textsuperscript{53} Then from that day forth they took counsel together in order to put him to death. \textsuperscript{54} Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews; but went thence unto a country near to the wilderness, into a city called Ephraim, and there continued with his disciples. \textsuperscript{55} And the Jews' passover was nigh at hand: and many went out of the country up to Jerusalem before the passover, to purify themselves. \textsuperscript{56} Then sought they for Jesus, and spoke among themselves, as they stood in the temple, What think all of you, that he will not come to the feast? \textsuperscript{57} Now both the chief priests and the Pharisees had given a commandment, that, if any man knew where he were, he should show it, that they might take him.\par

Accordingly we find that a desert, or wilderness, extended from Jericho to Bethel ( ), called the wilderness of Bethaven ( ), in which Joshua and the Israelites slew the inhabitants of Ai. ( .)\par

\subsection*{John 12}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then Jesus six days before the passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, which had been dead, whom he raised from the dead. \textsuperscript{2} There they made him a supper; and Martha served: but Lazarus was one of them that sat at the table with him. \textsuperscript{3} Then took Mary a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the odour of the ointment. \textsuperscript{4} Then says one of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, Simon's son, which should betray him, \textsuperscript{5} Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given to the poor? \textsuperscript{6} This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein. \textsuperscript{7} Then said Jesus, Let her alone: against the day of my burying has she kept this. \textsuperscript{8} For the poor always all of you have with you; but me all of you have not always. \textsuperscript{9} Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus' sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead. \textsuperscript{10} But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death; \textsuperscript{11} Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus. \textsuperscript{12} On the next day much people that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, \textsuperscript{13} Took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that comes in the name of the Lord. \textsuperscript{14} And Jesus, when he had found a young ass, sat thereon; as it is written, \textsuperscript{15} Fear not, daughter of Sion: behold, your King comes, sitting on an ass's colt. \textsuperscript{16} These things understood not his disciples at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him, and that they had done these things unto him. \textsuperscript{17} The people therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of his grave, and raised him from the dead, bare record. \textsuperscript{18} For this cause the people also met him, for that they heard that he had done this miracle. \textsuperscript{19} The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive all of you how all of you prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him. \textsuperscript{20} And there were certain Greeks among them that came up to worship at the feast: \textsuperscript{21} The same came therefore to Philip, which was of Bethsaida of Galilee, and desired him, saying, Sir, we would see Jesus. \textsuperscript{22} Philip comes and tells Andrew: and again Andrew and Philip tell Jesus. \textsuperscript{23} And Jesus answered them, saying, The hour has come, that the Son of man should be glorified. \textsuperscript{24} Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abides alone: but if it die, it brings forth much fruit. \textsuperscript{25} He that loves his life shall lose it; and he that hates his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal. \textsuperscript{26} If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be: if any man serve me, him will my Father honour. \textsuperscript{27} Now is my soul troubled; and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour: but for this cause came I unto this hour. \textsuperscript{28} Father, glorify your name. Then came there a voice from heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again. \textsuperscript{29} The people therefore, that stood by, and heard it, said that it thundered: others said, An angel spoke to him. \textsuperscript{30} Jesus answered and said, This voice came not because of me, but for your sakes. \textsuperscript{31} Now is the judgment of this world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out. \textsuperscript{32} And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me. \textsuperscript{33} This he said, signifying what death he should die. \textsuperscript{34} The people answered him, We have heard out of the law that Christ abides for ever: and how says you, The Son of man must be lifted up? who is this Son of man? \textsuperscript{35} Then Jesus said unto them, Yet a little while is the light with you. Walk while all of you have the light, lest darkness come upon you: for he that walks in darkness knows not where he goes. \textsuperscript{36} While all of you have light, believe in the light, that all of you may be the children of light. These things spoke Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them. \textsuperscript{37} But though he had done so many miracles before them, yet they believed not on him: \textsuperscript{38} That the saying (o. logos) of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spoke, Lord, who has believed our report? and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? \textsuperscript{39} Therefore they could not believe, because that Isaiah said again, \textsuperscript{40} He has blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them. \textsuperscript{41} These things said Isaiah, when he saw his glory, and spoke of him. \textsuperscript{42} Nevertheless among the chief rulers also many believed on him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess him, lest they should be put out of the synagogue: \textsuperscript{43} For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God. \textsuperscript{44} Jesus cried and said, He that believes on me, believes not on me, but on him that sent me. \textsuperscript{45} And he that sees me sees him that sent me. \textsuperscript{46} I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believes on me should not abide in darkness. \textsuperscript{47} And if any man hear my words, (o. rhema) and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world. \textsuperscript{48} He that rejects me, and receives not my words, (o. rhema) has one that judges him: the word (o. logos) that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day. \textsuperscript{49} For I have not spoken of myself; but the Father which sent me, he gave me a commandment, what I should say, and what I should speak. \textsuperscript{50} And I know that his commandment is life everlasting: whatsoever I speak therefore, even as the Father said unto me, so I speak.\par

John 12:3 TSK note: took, ;, ; ointment;, spikenard Spikenard is a highly a romatic plant growing in India, whence was made a very valuable unguent or perfume, used at the ancient baths and feasts. It is identified by Sir W. Jones with the sumbul of the Persians and Arabs, and jatamansi of the Hindoos; and he considers it a species of the valerian, of the triandria monogynia class of plants. The root is from three to twelve inches long, fibrous, sending up above the earth between thirty and forty ears or spikes, from which it has its name; stem, lower part perennial, upper part herbaceous, sub-erect, simple, from six to twelve inches long; leaves entire, smooth, fourfold, the inner radical pair petioled and cordate, the rest sessile and lanceolate; pericarp, a single seed crowned with a pappus. anointed;, filled\par

\subsection*{John 13}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now before the feast of the passover, when Jesus knew that his hour was come that he should depart out of this world unto the Father, having loved his own which were in the world, he loved them unto the end. \textsuperscript{2} And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon's son, to betray him; \textsuperscript{3} Jesus knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he was come from God, and went to God; \textsuperscript{4} He rises from supper, and laid aside his garments; and took a towel, and girded himself. \textsuperscript{5} After that he pours water into a basin, and began to wash the disciples' feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith he was girded. \textsuperscript{6} Then comes he to Simon Peter: and Peter says unto him, Lord, do you wash my feet? \textsuperscript{7} Jesus answered and said unto him, What I do you know not now; but you shall know hereafter. \textsuperscript{8} Peter says unto him, You shall never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, If I wash you not, you have no part with me. \textsuperscript{9} Simon Peter says unto him, Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head. \textsuperscript{10} Jesus says to him, He that is washed needs not save to wash his feet, but is clean everything: and all of you are clean, but not all. \textsuperscript{11} For he knew who should betray him; therefore said he, All of you are not all clean. \textsuperscript{12} So after he had washed their feet, and had taken his garments, and was set down again, he said unto them, Know all of you what I have done to you? \textsuperscript{13} All of you call me Master and Lord: and all of you say well; for so I am. \textsuperscript{14} If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; all of you also ought to wash one another's feet. \textsuperscript{15} For I have given you an example, that all of you should do as I have done to you. \textsuperscript{16} Verily, verily, I say unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord; neither he that is sent greater than he that sent him. \textsuperscript{17} If all of you know these things, happy are all of you if all of you do them. \textsuperscript{18} I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me. \textsuperscript{19} Now I tell you before it come, that, when it has come to pass, all of you may believe that I am he. \textsuperscript{20} Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receives whomsoever I send receives me; and he that receives me receives him that sent me. \textsuperscript{21} When Jesus had thus said, he was troubled in spirit, (o. pneuma) and testified, and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me. \textsuperscript{22} Then the disciples looked one on another, doubting of whom he spoke. \textsuperscript{23} Now there was leaning on Jesus' bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved. \textsuperscript{24} Simon Peter therefore beckoned to him, that he should ask who it should be of whom he spoke. \textsuperscript{25} He then lying on Jesus' breast says unto him, Lord, who is it? \textsuperscript{26} Jesus answered, He it is, to whom I shall give a morsel, when I have dipped it. And when he had dipped the morsel, he gave it to Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon. \textsuperscript{27} And after the morsel Satan entered into him. Then said Jesus unto him, That you do, do quickly. \textsuperscript{28} Now no man at the table knew for what intent he spoke this unto him. \textsuperscript{29} For some of them thought, because Judas had the bag, that Jesus had said unto him, Buy those things that we have need of against the feast; or, that he should give something to the poor. \textsuperscript{30} He then having received the morsel went immediately out: and it was night. \textsuperscript{31} Therefore, when he was gone out, Jesus said, Now is the Son of man glorified, and God is glorified in him. \textsuperscript{32} If God be glorified in him, God shall also glorify him in himself, and shall immediately glorify him. \textsuperscript{33} Little children, yet a little while I am with you. All of you shall seek me: and as I said unto the Jews, Where I go, all of you cannot come; so now I say to you. \textsuperscript{34} A new commandment I give unto you, That all of you love one another; as I have loved you, that all of you also love one another. \textsuperscript{35} By this shall all men know that all of you are my disciples, if all of you have love (o. agape) one to another. \textsuperscript{36} Simon Peter said unto him, Lord, where go you? Jesus answered him, Where I go, you can not follow me now; but you shall follow me afterwards. \textsuperscript{37} Peter said unto him, Lord, why cannot I follow you now? I will lay down my life for your sake. \textsuperscript{38} Jesus answered him, Will you lay down your life for my sake? Verily, verily, I say unto you, The cock shall not crow, till you have denied me three times.\par

\subsection*{John 14}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Let not your heart be troubled: all of you believe in God, believe also in me. \textsuperscript{2} In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. \textsuperscript{3} And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there all of you may be also. \textsuperscript{4} And where I go all of you know, and the way all of you know. \textsuperscript{5} Thomas says unto him, Lord, we know not where you go; and how can we know the way? \textsuperscript{6} Jesus says unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man comes unto the Father, but by me. \textsuperscript{7} If all of you had known me, all of you should have known my Father also: and from henceforth all of you know him, and have seen him. \textsuperscript{8} Philip says unto him, Lord, show us the Father, and it satisfies us. \textsuperscript{9} Jesus says unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet have you not known me, Philip? he that has seen me has seen the Father; and how says you then, Show us the Father? \textsuperscript{10} Believe you not that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? the (o. rhema) words that I speak unto you I speak not of myself: but the Father that dwells in me, he does the works. \textsuperscript{11} Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me: or else believe me for the very works' sake. \textsuperscript{12} Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believes on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father. \textsuperscript{13} And whatsoever all of you shall ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son. \textsuperscript{14} If all of you shall ask any thing in my name, I will do it. \textsuperscript{15} If all of you love me, keep my commandments. \textsuperscript{16} And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; \textsuperscript{17} Even the Spirit (o. pneuma) of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it sees him not, neither knows him: but all of you know him; for he dwells with you, and shall be in you. \textsuperscript{18} I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you. \textsuperscript{19} Yet a little while, and the world sees me no more; but all of you see me: because I live, all of you shall live also. \textsuperscript{20} At that day all of you shall know that I am in my Father, and all of you in me, and I in you. \textsuperscript{21} He that has my commandments, and keeps them, he it is that loves me: and he that loves me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him. \textsuperscript{22} Judas says unto him, not Iscariot, Lord, how is it that you will manifest yourself unto us, and not unto the world? \textsuperscript{23} Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my words: (o. logos) and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him. \textsuperscript{24} He that loves me not keeps not my sayings: (o. logos) and the word (o. logos) which all of you hear is not mine, but the Father's which sent me. \textsuperscript{25} These things have I spoken unto you, being yet present with you. \textsuperscript{26} But the Comforter, which is the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you. \textsuperscript{27} Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world gives, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid. \textsuperscript{28} All of you have heard how I said unto you, I go away, and come again unto you. If all of you loved me, all of you would rejoice, because I said, I go unto the Father: for my Father is greater than I. \textsuperscript{29} And now I have told you before it come to pass, that, when it has come to pass, all of you might believe. \textsuperscript{30} Hereafter I will not talk much with you: for the prince of this world comes, and has nothing in me. \textsuperscript{31} But that the world may know that I love the Father; and as the Father gave me commandment, even so I do. Arise, let us go behind.\par

\subsection*{John 15}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer. \textsuperscript{2} Every branch in me that bears not fruit he takes away: and every branch that bears fruit, he purges it, that it may bring forth more fruit. \textsuperscript{3} Now all of you are clean through the word (o. logos) which I have spoken unto you. \textsuperscript{4} Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can all of you, except all of you abide in me. \textsuperscript{5} I am the vine, all of you are the branches: He that abides in me, and I in him, the same brings forth much fruit: for without me all of you can do nothing. \textsuperscript{6} If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned. \textsuperscript{7} If all of you abide in me, and my words (o. rhema) abide in you, all of you shall ask what all of you will, and it shall be done unto you. \textsuperscript{8} Herein is my Father glorified, that all of you bear much fruit; so shall all of you be my disciples. \textsuperscript{9} As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you: continue all of you in my love. (o. agape) \textsuperscript{10} If all of you keep my commandments, all of you shall abide in my love; (o. agape) even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love. (o. agape) \textsuperscript{11} These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full. \textsuperscript{12} This is my commandment, That all of you love one another, as I have loved you. \textsuperscript{13} Greater love (o. agape) has no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends. \textsuperscript{14} All of you are my friends, if all of you do whatsoever I command you. \textsuperscript{15} Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knows not what his lord does: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you. \textsuperscript{16} All of you have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that all of you should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatsoever all of you shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you. \textsuperscript{17} These things I command you, that all of you love one another. \textsuperscript{18} If the world hate you, all of you know that it hated me before it hated you. \textsuperscript{19} If all of you were of the world, the world would love his own: but because all of you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hates you. \textsuperscript{20} Remember the word (o. logos) that I said unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they have kept my saying, (o. logos) they will keep yours also. \textsuperscript{21} But all these things will they do unto you for my name's sake, because they know not him that sent me. \textsuperscript{22} If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloak for their sin. \textsuperscript{23} He that hates me hates my Father also. \textsuperscript{24} If I had not done among them the works which no other man did, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen and hated both me and my Father. \textsuperscript{25} But this comes to pass, that the word (o. logos) might be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated me without a cause. \textsuperscript{26} But when the Comforter has come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit (o. pneuma) of truth, which proceeds from the Father, he shall testify of me: \textsuperscript{27} And all of you also shall bear witness, because all of you have been with me from the beginning.\par

\subsection*{John 16}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} These things have I spoken unto you, that all of you should not be offended. \textsuperscript{2} They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time comes, that whosoever kills you will think that he does God service. \textsuperscript{3} And these things will they do unto you, because they have not known the Father, nor me. \textsuperscript{4} But these things have I told you, that when the time shall come, all of you may remember that I told you of them. And these things I said not unto you at the beginning, because I was with you. \textsuperscript{5} But now I go my way to him that sent me; and none of you asks me, Where go you? \textsuperscript{6} But because I have said these things unto you, sorrow has filled your heart. \textsuperscript{7} Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. \textsuperscript{8} And when he has come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: \textsuperscript{9} Of sin, because they believe not on me; \textsuperscript{10} Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and all of you see me no more; \textsuperscript{11} Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged. \textsuperscript{12} I have yet many things to say unto you, but all of you cannot bear them now. \textsuperscript{13} Nevertheless when he, the Spirit (o. pneuma) of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will show you things to come. \textsuperscript{14} He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall show it unto you. \textsuperscript{15} All things that the Father has are mine: therefore said I, that he shall take of mine, and shall show it unto you. \textsuperscript{16} A little while, and all of you shall not see me: and again, a little while, and all of you shall see me, because I go to the Father. \textsuperscript{17} Then said some of his disciples among themselves, What is this that he says unto us, A little while, and all of you shall not see me: and again, a little while, and all of you shall see me: and, Because I go to the Father? \textsuperscript{18} They said therefore, What is this that he says, A little while? we cannot tell what he says. \textsuperscript{19} Now Jesus knew that they were desirous to ask him, and said unto them, Do all of you enquire among yourselves of that I said, A little while, and all of you shall not see me: and again, a little while, and all of you shall see me? \textsuperscript{20} Verily, verily, I say unto you, That all of you shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and all of you shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy. \textsuperscript{21} A woman when she is in travail has sorrow, because her hour has come: but as soon as she is delivered of the child, she remembers no more the anguish, for joy that a man is born into the world. \textsuperscript{22} And all of you now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man takes from you. \textsuperscript{23} And in that day all of you shall ask me nothing. Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whatsoever all of you shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it you. \textsuperscript{24} Until now have all of you asked nothing in my name: ask, and all of you shall receive, that your joy may be full. \textsuperscript{25} These things have I spoken unto you in proverbs: but the time comes, when I shall no more speak unto you in proverbs, but I shall show you plainly of the Father. \textsuperscript{26} At that day all of you shall ask in my name: and I say not unto you, that I will pray the Father for you: \textsuperscript{27} For the Father himself loves you, because all of you have loved me, and have believed that I came out from God. \textsuperscript{28} I came forth from the Father, and am come into the world: again, I leave the world, and go to the Father. \textsuperscript{29} His disciples said unto him, Lo, now speak you plainly, and speak no proverb. \textsuperscript{30} Now are we sure that you know all things, and need not that any man should ask you: by this we believe that you came forth from God. \textsuperscript{31} Jesus answered them, Do all of you now believe? \textsuperscript{32} Behold, the hour comes, yea, is now come, that all of you shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me. \textsuperscript{33} These things I have spoken unto you, that in me all of you might have peace. In the world all of you shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.\par

\subsection*{John 17}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} These words spoke Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son, that your Son also may glorify you: \textsuperscript{2} As you have given him power over all flesh, that he should give eternal life to as many as you have given him. \textsuperscript{3} And this is life eternal, that they might know you the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent. \textsuperscript{4} I have glorified you on the earth: I have finished the work which you gave me to do. \textsuperscript{5} And now, O Father, glorify you me with yours own self with the glory which I had with you before the world was. \textsuperscript{6} I have manifested your name unto the men which you gave me out of the world: yours they were, and you gave them me; and they have kept your word. (o. logos) \textsuperscript{7} Now they have known that all things whatsoever you have given me are of you. \textsuperscript{8} For I have given unto them the words (o. rhema) which you gave me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from you, and they have believed that you did send me. \textsuperscript{9} I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which you have given me; for they are yours. \textsuperscript{10} And all mine are yours, and yours are mine; and I am glorified in them. \textsuperscript{11} And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to you. Holy Father, keep through yours own name those whom you have given me, that they may be one, as we are. \textsuperscript{12} While I was with them in the world, I kept them in your name: those that you gave me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled. \textsuperscript{13} And now come I to you; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves. \textsuperscript{14} I have given them your word; (o. logos) and the world has hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. \textsuperscript{15} I pray not that you should take them out of the world, but that you should keep them from the evil. \textsuperscript{16} They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world. \textsuperscript{17} Sanctify them through your truth: your word (o. logos) is truth. \textsuperscript{18} As you have sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world. \textsuperscript{19} And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also might be sanctified through the truth. \textsuperscript{20} Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; (o. logos) \textsuperscript{21} That they all may be one; as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that you have sent me. \textsuperscript{22} And the glory which you gave me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one: \textsuperscript{23} I in them, and you in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that you have sent me, and have loved them, as you have loved me. \textsuperscript{24} Father, I will that they also, whom you have given me, be with me where I am; that they may behold my glory, which you have given me: for you loved me before the foundation of the world. \textsuperscript{25} O righteous Father, the world has not known you: but I have known you, and these have known that you have sent me. \textsuperscript{26} And I have declared unto them your name, and will declare it: that the love (o. agape) wherewith you have loved me may be in them, and I in them.\par

\subsection*{John 18}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} When Jesus had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Cedron, where was a garden, into the which he entered, and his disciples. \textsuperscript{2} And Judas also, which betrayed him, knew the place: for Jesus frequently resorted thither with his disciples. \textsuperscript{3} Judas then, having received a band of men and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, comes thither with lanterns and torches and weapons. \textsuperscript{4} Jesus therefore, knowing all things that should come upon him, went forth, and said unto them, Whom seek all of you? \textsuperscript{5} They answered him, Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus says unto them, I am he. And Judas also, which betrayed him, stood with them. \textsuperscript{6} As soon then as he had said unto them, I am he, they went backward, and fell to the ground. \textsuperscript{7} Then asked he them again, Whom seek all of you? And they said, Jesus of Nazareth. \textsuperscript{8} Jesus answered, I have told you that I am he: if therefore all of you seek me, let these go their way: \textsuperscript{9} That the saying (o. logos) might be fulfilled, which he spoke, Of them which you gave me have I lost none. \textsuperscript{10} Then Simon Peter having a sword drew it, and stroke the high priest's servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus. \textsuperscript{11} Then said Jesus unto Peter, Put up your sword into the sheath: the cup which my Father has given me, shall I not drink it? \textsuperscript{12} Then the band and the captain and officers of the Jews took Jesus, and bound him, \textsuperscript{13} And led him away to Annas first; for he was father in law to Caiaphas, which was the high priest that same year. \textsuperscript{14} Now Caiaphas was he, which gave counsel to the Jews, that it was expedient that one man should die for the people. \textsuperscript{15} And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple: that disciple was known unto the high priest, and went in with Jesus into the palace of the high priest. \textsuperscript{16} But Peter stood at the door without. Then went out that other disciple, which was known unto the high priest, and spoke unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter. \textsuperscript{17} Then says the damsel that kept the door unto Peter, Are not you also one of this man's disciples? He says, I am not. \textsuperscript{18} And the servants and officers stood there, who had made a fire of coals; for it was cold: and they warmed themselves: and Peter stood with them, and warmed himself. \textsuperscript{19} The high priest then asked Jesus of his disciples, and of his doctrine. \textsuperscript{20} Jesus answered him, I spoke openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, where the Jews always resort; and in secret have I said nothing. \textsuperscript{21} Why ask you me? ask them which heard me, what I have said unto them: behold, they know what I said. \textsuperscript{22} And when he had thus spoken, one of the officers which stood by struck Jesus with the palm of his hand, saying, Answer you the high priest so? \textsuperscript{23} Jesus answered him, If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil: but if well, why smite you me? \textsuperscript{24} Now Annas had sent him bound unto Caiaphas the high priest. \textsuperscript{25} And Simon Peter stood and warmed himself. They said therefore unto him, Are not you also one of his disciples? He denied it, and said, I am not. \textsuperscript{26} One of the servants of the high priest, being his kinsman whose ear Peter cut off, says, Did not I see you in the garden with him? \textsuperscript{27} Peter then denied again: and immediately the cock crew. \textsuperscript{28} Then led they Jesus from Caiaphas unto the hall of judgment: and it was early; and they themselves went not into the judgment hall, lest they should be defiled; but that they might eat the passover. \textsuperscript{29} Pilate then went out unto them, and said, What accusation bring all of you against this man? \textsuperscript{30} They answered and said unto him, If he were not a villain, we would not have delivered him up unto you. \textsuperscript{31} Then said Pilate unto them, Take all of you him, and judge him according to your law. The Jews therefore said unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death: \textsuperscript{32} That the saying (o. logos) of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spoke, signifying what death he should die. \textsuperscript{33} Then Pilate entered into the judgment hall again, and called Jesus, and said unto him, Are you the King of the Jews? \textsuperscript{34} Jesus answered him, Says you this thing of yourself, or did others tell it you of me? \textsuperscript{35} Pilate answered, Am I a Jew? Yours own nation and the chief priests have delivered you unto me: what have you done? \textsuperscript{36} Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from behind. \textsuperscript{37} Pilate therefore said unto him, Are you a king then? Jesus answered, You says that I am a king. To this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth hears my voice. \textsuperscript{38} Pilate says unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Jews, and says unto them, I find in him no fault at all. \textsuperscript{39} But all of you have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the passover: will all of you therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews? \textsuperscript{40} Then cried they all again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.\par

\subsection*{John 19}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged him. \textsuperscript{2} And the soldiers intertwined a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple robe, \textsuperscript{3} And said, Hail, King of the Jews! and they stroke him with their hands. \textsuperscript{4} Pilate therefore went forth again, and says unto them, Behold, I bring him forth to you, that all of you may know that I find no fault in him. \textsuperscript{5} Then came Jesus forth, wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple robe. And Pilate says unto them, Behold the man! \textsuperscript{6} When the chief priests therefore and officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify him, crucify him. Pilate says unto them, Take all of you him, and crucify him: for I find no fault in him. \textsuperscript{7} The Jews answered him, We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God. \textsuperscript{8} When Pilate therefore heard that saying, (o. logos) he was the more afraid; \textsuperscript{9} And went again into the judgment hall, and says unto Jesus, Whence are you? But Jesus gave him no answer. \textsuperscript{10} Then says Pilate unto him, Speak you not unto me? know you not that I have power to crucify you, and have power to release you? \textsuperscript{11} Jesus answered, You could have no power at all against me, except it were given you from above: therefore he that delivered me unto you has the greater sin. \textsuperscript{12} And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If you let this man go, you are not Caesar's friend: whosoever makes himself a king speaks against Caesar. \textsuperscript{13} When Pilate therefore heard that saying, (o. logos) he brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha. \textsuperscript{14} And it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he says unto the Jews, Behold your King! \textsuperscript{15} But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate says unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Caesar. \textsuperscript{16} Then delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away. \textsuperscript{17} And he bearing his cross went forth into a place called the place of a skull, which is called in the Hebrew Golgotha: \textsuperscript{18} Where they crucified him, and two other with him, on either side one, and Jesus in the midst. \textsuperscript{19} And Pilate wrote a title, and put it on the cross. And the writing was JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS. \textsuperscript{20} This title then read many of the Jews: for the place where Jesus was crucified was nigh to the city: and it was written in Hebrew, and Greek, and Latin. \textsuperscript{21} Then said the chief priests of the Jews to Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but that he said, I am King of the Jews. \textsuperscript{22} Pilate answered, What I have written I have written. \textsuperscript{23} Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments, and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also his coat: now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout. \textsuperscript{24} They said therefore among themselves, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: that the scripture might be fulfilled, which says, They parted my raiment among them, and for my vesture they did cast lots. These things therefore the soldiers did. \textsuperscript{25} Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene. \textsuperscript{26} When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he says unto his mother, Woman, behold your son! \textsuperscript{27} Then says he to the disciple, Behold your mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home. \textsuperscript{28} After this, Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, says, I thirst. \textsuperscript{29} Now there was set a vessel full of vinegar: and they filled a sponge with vinegar, and put it upon hyssop, and put it to his mouth. \textsuperscript{30} When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{31} The Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath day, (for that sabbath day was an high day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away. \textsuperscript{32} Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him. \textsuperscript{33} But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs: \textsuperscript{34} But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water. \textsuperscript{35} And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true: and he knows that he says true, that all of you might believe. \textsuperscript{36} For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken. \textsuperscript{37} And again another scripture says, They shall look on him whom they pierced. \textsuperscript{38} And after this Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave him leave. He came therefore, and took the body of Jesus. \textsuperscript{39} And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Jesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight. \textsuperscript{40} Then took they the body of Jesus, and wound it in linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury. \textsuperscript{41} Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden; and in the garden a new tomb, wherein was never man yet laid. \textsuperscript{42} There laid they Jesus therefore because of the Jews' preparation day; for the tomb was nigh at hand.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
John 19:6 TSK note: the chief priests; , ; Take Pilate neither did nor could say this seriously; for crucifixion was not a Jewish but a Roman mode of punishment. The cross was made of two beams, either crossing at the top, at right angles, like a T, or in the middle of their length like an X; with a piece on the centre of the transverse beam for the accusation, and another piece projecting from the middle, on which the person sat. The cross on which our Lord suffered was of the former kind, being thus represented on all old monuments, coins, and crosses. The body was usually fastened to the upright beam by nailing the feet to it, and on the transverse piece by nailing the hands; and the person was frequently permitted to hang in this situation till he perished through agony and lack of food. This horrible punishment was usually inflicted only on slaves for the worst of crimes.\par
John 19:14 TSK note: the preparation, ; the sixth Instead of εκτη, sixth, several manuscripts and fathers have τριτη, third, as in the parallel place., Behold\par
John 19:17 TSK note: he, ;, ;, ;, went, ; Golgotha, of which Κρανιον and Calvaria are merely translations, is supposed to have been a hill, or a rising on a greater hill, on the north-west of Jerusalem.\par
John 19:19 TSK note: wrote; And the The apparent discrepancy between the accounts of this title given by the Evangelists, which has been urged as an objection against their inspiration and veracity, has been most satisfactorily accounted for by Dr. Townson; who supposes that, as it was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin, it might have slightly varied in each language; and that, as Luke and John wrote for the Gentiles, they would prefer the Greek inscription, that Matthew, addressing the Jews, would use the Hebrew, and that Mark, writing to the Romans, would naturally give the Latin. Jesus\par

\subsection*{John 20}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} The first day of the week comes Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the tomb, and sees the stone taken away from the tomb. \textsuperscript{2} Then she runs, and comes to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and says unto them, They have taken away the LORD out of the tomb, and we know not where they have laid him. \textsuperscript{3} Peter therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came to the tomb. \textsuperscript{4} So they ran both together: and the other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the tomb. \textsuperscript{5} And he stooping down, and looking in, saw the linen clothes lying; yet went he not in. \textsuperscript{6} Then comes Simon Peter following him, and went into the tomb, and sees the linen clothes lie, \textsuperscript{7} And the cloth, that was about his head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself. \textsuperscript{8} Then went in also that other disciple, which came first to the tomb, and he saw, and believed. \textsuperscript{9} For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead. \textsuperscript{10} Then the disciples went away again unto their own home. \textsuperscript{11} But Mary stood without at the tomb weeping: and as she wept, she stooped down, and looked into the tomb, \textsuperscript{12} And sees two angels in white sitting, the one at the head, and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain. \textsuperscript{13} And they say unto her, Woman, why weep you? She says unto them, Because they have taken away my LORD, and I know not where they have laid him. \textsuperscript{14} And when she had thus said, she turned herself back, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus. \textsuperscript{15} Jesus says unto her, Woman, why weep you? whom seek you? She, supposing him to be the gardener, says unto him, Sir, if you have borne him behind, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away. \textsuperscript{16} Jesus says unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and says unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master. \textsuperscript{17} Jesus says unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God. \textsuperscript{18} Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the LORD, and that he had spoken these things unto her. \textsuperscript{19} Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus and stood in the midst, and says unto them, Peace be unto you. \textsuperscript{20} And when he had so said, he showed unto them his hands and his side. Then were the disciples glad, when they saw the LORD. \textsuperscript{21} Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you: as my Father has sent me, even so send I you. \textsuperscript{22} And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and says unto them, Receive all of you the Holy Spirit: (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{23} Whomsoever sins all of you remit, they are remitted unto them; and whomsoever sins all of you retain, they are retained. \textsuperscript{24} But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came. \textsuperscript{25} The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the LORD. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe. \textsuperscript{26} And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you. \textsuperscript{27} Then says he to Thomas, Reach here your finger, and behold my hands; and reach here your hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing. \textsuperscript{28} And Thomas answered and said unto him, My LORD and my God. \textsuperscript{29} Jesus says unto him, Thomas, because you have seen me, you have believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed. \textsuperscript{30} And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book: \textsuperscript{31} But these are written, that all of you might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing all of you might have life through his name.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
John 20:1 TSK note: first, ; cometh Mary Magdalene, as well as Peter, was evidently at the sepulchre twice on that morning of the resurrection. The first time of her going was some short time before her companions, the other Mary and Salome ( ); and observing that the stone had been removed, she returned to inform Peter and John. In the meantime, the other Mary and Salome came to the sepulchre, and saw the angel, as recorded by Matthew and Mark. While these women returned to the city, Peter and John went to the sepulchre, passing them at some distance, or going another way, followed by Mary Magdalene, who stayed after their return. This was her second journey; when she saw two angels, and then Jesus himself, as here related; and immediately after Jesus appeared to the other women, as they returned to the city ( ). In the meantime Joanna and her company arrived at the sepulchre, when two angels appeared to them, and addressed them as the one angel had done the other women ( ). They immediately returned to the city, and by some means found the apostles before the others arrived, and informed them of what they had seen; upon which Peter went a second time to the sepulchre, but saw only the linen clothes lying ( ).;, ; the stone\par

For I am not yet immediately going to ascend to my Father; you will have several opportunities of seeing me again; but go and tell my disciples that I shall depart to my Father and your Father.";, ;, ; my brethren;, ; I ascend, ;, ; , ; your Father; , ; your God\par

John 20:28 TSK note: My Lord The disbelief of the apostle is the means of furnishing us with a full and satisfactory demonstration of the resurrection of our Lord. Throughout the divine dispensations every doctrine and ever important truth is gradually revealed; and here we have a conspicuous instance of the progressive system. An angel first declares the glorious event; the empty sepulchre confirms the women's report. Christ's appearance to Mary Magdalene shewed that he was alive; that to the disciples at Emmaus proved that it was at the least the spirit of Christ; that to the eleven shewed the reality of his body; and the conviction given to Thomas proved it the self-same body that had been crucified. Incredulity itself is satisfied; and the convinced apostle exclaims, in the joy of his heart, "My Lord and my God!"\par
\end{quote}
\subsection*{John 21}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} After these things Jesus showed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and likewise showed he himself. \textsuperscript{2} There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples. \textsuperscript{3} Simon Peter says unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with you. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. \textsuperscript{4} But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus. \textsuperscript{5} Then Jesus says unto them, Children, have all of you any food? They answered him, No. \textsuperscript{6} And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and all of you shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes. \textsuperscript{7} Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved says unto Peter, It is the Lord. Now when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt his fisher's coat unto him, (for he was naked,) and did cast himself into the sea. \textsuperscript{8} And the other disciples came in a little ship; (for they were not far from land, but as it were two hundred cubits,) dragging the net with fishes. \textsuperscript{9} As soon then as they were come to land, they saw a fire of coals there, and fish laid thereon, and bread. \textsuperscript{10} Jesus says unto them, Bring of the fish which all of you have now caught. \textsuperscript{11} Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land full of great fishes, an hundred and fifty and three: and for all there were so many, yet was not the net broken. \textsuperscript{12} Jesus says unto them, Come and dine. And none of the disciples durst ask him, Who are you? knowing that it was the Lord. \textsuperscript{13} Jesus then comes, and takes bread, and gives them, and fish likewise. \textsuperscript{14} This is now the third time that Jesus showed himself to his disciples, after that he was risen from the dead. \textsuperscript{15} So when they had dined, Jesus says to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, love you me more than these? He says unto him, Yea, Lord; you know that I love you. He says unto him, Feed my lambs. \textsuperscript{16} He says to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, love you me? He says unto him, Yea, Lord; you know that I love you. He says unto him, Feed my sheep. \textsuperscript{17} He says unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, love you me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Love you me? And he said unto him, Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you. Jesus says unto him, Feed my sheep. \textsuperscript{18} Verily, verily, I say unto you, When you were young, you gird yourself, and walked where you would: but when you shall be old, you shall stretch forth your hands, and another shall gird you, and carry you where you would not. \textsuperscript{19} This spoke he, signifying by what death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he says unto him, Follow me. \textsuperscript{20} Then Peter, turning about, sees the disciple whom Jesus loved following; which also leaned on his breast at supper, and said, Lord, which is he that betrays you? \textsuperscript{21} Peter seeing him says to Jesus, Lord, and what shall this man do? \textsuperscript{22} Jesus says unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to you? follow you me. \textsuperscript{23} Then went this saying (o. logos) abroad among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, He shall not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to you? \textsuperscript{24} This is the disciple which testifies of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his testimony is true. \textsuperscript{25} And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen.\par

\subsection*{Acts 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. \textsuperscript{2} And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. \textsuperscript{3} And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like of fire, and it sat upon each of them. \textsuperscript{4} And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit (o. pneuma) gave them utterance. \textsuperscript{5} And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven. \textsuperscript{6} Now when this was noised abroad, the multitude came together, and were confounded, because that every man heard them speak in his own language. \textsuperscript{7} And they were all amazed and marvelled, saying one to another, Behold, are not all these which speak Galilaeans? \textsuperscript{8} And how hear we every man in our own tongue, wherein we were born? \textsuperscript{9} Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia, and in Judaea, and Cappadocia, in Pontus, and Asia, \textsuperscript{10} Phrygia, and Pamphylia, in Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and strangers of Rome, Jews and proselytes, \textsuperscript{11} Cretes and Arabians, we do hear them speak in our tongues the wonderful works of God. \textsuperscript{12} And they were all amazed, and were in doubt, saying one to another, What means this? \textsuperscript{13} Others mocking said, These men are full of new wine. \textsuperscript{14} But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and said unto them, All of you men of Judaea, and all you that dwell at Jerusalem, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words: (o. rhema) \textsuperscript{15} For these are not drunken, as all of you suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day. \textsuperscript{16} But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel; \textsuperscript{17} And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, I will pour out of my Spirit (o. pneuma) upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams: \textsuperscript{18} And on my servants and on my handmaidens I will pour out in those days of my Spirit; (o. pneuma) and they shall prophesy: \textsuperscript{19} And I will show wonders in heaven above, and signs in the earth beneath; blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke: \textsuperscript{20} The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and notable day of the Lord come: \textsuperscript{21} And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved. \textsuperscript{22} All of you men of Israel, hear these words; (o. logos) Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God among you by miracles and wonders and signs, which God did by him in the midst of you, as all of you yourselves also know: \textsuperscript{23} Him, being delivered by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, all of you have taken, and by wicked hands have crucified and slain: \textsuperscript{24} Whom God has raised up, having loosed the pains of death: because it was not possible that he should be held of it. \textsuperscript{25} For David speaks concerning him, I foresaw the Lord always before my face, for he is on my right hand, that I should not be moved: \textsuperscript{26} Therefore did my heart rejoice, and my tongue was glad; moreover also my flesh shall rest in hope: \textsuperscript{27} Because you will not leave my soul in hell, neither will you suffer yours Holy One to see corruption. \textsuperscript{28} You have made known to me the ways of life; you shall make me full of joy with your countenance. \textsuperscript{29} Men and brethren, let me freely speak unto you of the patriarch David, that he is both dead and buried, and his tomb is with us unto this day. \textsuperscript{30} Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne; \textsuperscript{31} He seeing this before spoke of the resurrection of Christ, that his soul was not left in hell, neither his flesh did see corruption. \textsuperscript{32} This Jesus has God raised up, whereof we all are witnesses. \textsuperscript{33} Therefore being by the right hand of God exalted, and having received of the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) he has shed forth this, which all of you now see and hear. \textsuperscript{34} For David is not ascended into the heavens: but he says himself, The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit you on my right hand, \textsuperscript{35} Until I make your foes your footstool. \textsuperscript{36} Therefore let all the house of Israel know assuredly, that God has made the same Jesus, whom all of you have crucified, both Lord and Christ. \textsuperscript{37} Now when they heard this, they were pricked in their heart, and said unto Peter and to the rest of the apostles, Men and brethren, what shall we do? \textsuperscript{38} Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and all of you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{39} For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are far off, even as many as the LORD our God shall call. \textsuperscript{40} And with many other words (o. logos) did he testify and exhort, saying, Save yourselves from this untoward generation. \textsuperscript{41} Then they that gladly received his word (o. logos) were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls. \textsuperscript{42} And they continued steadfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers. \textsuperscript{43} And fear came upon every soul: and many wonders and signs were done by the apostles. \textsuperscript{44} And all that believed were together, and had all things common; \textsuperscript{45} And sold their possessions and goods, and parted them to all men, as every man had need. \textsuperscript{46} And they, continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, did eat their food with gladness and singleness of heart, \textsuperscript{47} Praising God, and having favour with all the people. And the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved.\par

\subsection*{Acts 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour. \textsuperscript{2} And a certain man lame from his mother's womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple; \textsuperscript{3} Who seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple asked an alms. \textsuperscript{4} And Peter, fastening his eyes upon him with John, said, Look on us. \textsuperscript{5} And he gave heed unto them, expecting to receive something of them. \textsuperscript{6} Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I you: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk. \textsuperscript{7} And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength. \textsuperscript{8} And he leaping up stood, and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God. \textsuperscript{9} And all the people saw him walking and praising God: \textsuperscript{10} And they knew that it was he which sat for alms at the Beautiful gate of the temple: and they were filled with wonder and amazement at that which had happened unto him. \textsuperscript{11} And as the lame man which was healed held Peter and John, all the people ran together unto them in the porch that is called Solomon's, greatly wondering. \textsuperscript{12} And when Peter saw it, he answered unto the people, All of you men of Israel, why marvel all of you at this? or why look all of you so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man to walk? \textsuperscript{13} The God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified his Son Jesus; whom all of you delivered up, and denied him in the presence of Pilate, when he was determined to let him go. \textsuperscript{14} But all of you denied the Holy One and the Just, and desired a murderer to be granted unto you; \textsuperscript{15} And killed the Prince of life, whom God has raised from the dead; whereof we are witnesses. \textsuperscript{16} And his name through faith in his name has made this man strong, whom all of you see and know: yea, the faith which is by him has given him this perfect soundness in the presence of you all. \textsuperscript{17} And now, brethren, I know that through ignorance all of you did it, as did also your rulers. \textsuperscript{18} But those things, which God before had showed by the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he has so fulfilled. \textsuperscript{19} Repent all of you therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord. \textsuperscript{20} And he shall send Jesus Christ, which before was preached unto you: \textsuperscript{21} Whom the heaven must receive until the times of restitution of all things, which God has spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets since the world began. \textsuperscript{22} For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall all of you hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you. \textsuperscript{23} And it shall come to pass, that every soul, which will not hear that prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people. \textsuperscript{24} Yea, and all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days. \textsuperscript{25} All of you are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in your seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed. \textsuperscript{26} Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities.\par

And whatever man shall not hearken to whatsoever words that prophet shall speak in my name, I will take vengeance on him.”\par

And it shall come to pass, [that] whosoever will not hearken unto my words which he shall speak in my name, I will require [it] of him.”\par

\subsection*{Acts 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And as they spoke unto the people, the priests, and the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees, came upon them, \textsuperscript{2} Being grieved that they taught the people, and preached through Jesus the resurrection from the dead. \textsuperscript{3} And they laid hands on them, and put them in hold unto the next day: for it was now evening. \textsuperscript{4} Nevertheless many of them which heard the word (o. logos) believed; and the number of the men was about five thousand. \textsuperscript{5} And it came to pass on the next day, that their rulers, and elders, and scribes, \textsuperscript{6} And Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the kindred of the high priest, were gathered together at Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{7} And when they had set them in the midst, they asked, By what power, or by what name, have all of you done this? \textsuperscript{8} Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) said unto them, All of you rulers of the people, and elders of Israel, \textsuperscript{9} If we this day be examined of the good deed done to the impotent man, by what means he is made whole; \textsuperscript{10} Be it known unto you all, and to all the people of Israel, that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom all of you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, even by him does this man stand here before you whole. \textsuperscript{11} This is the stone which was set at nothing of you builders, which is become the head of the corner. \textsuperscript{12} Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is no other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved. \textsuperscript{13} Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus. \textsuperscript{14} And beholding the man which was healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it. \textsuperscript{15} But when they had commanded them to go aside out of the council, they conferred among themselves, \textsuperscript{16} Saying, What shall we do to these men? for that indeed a notable miracle has been done by them is manifest to all them that dwell in Jerusalem; and we cannot deny it. \textsuperscript{17} But that it spread no further among the people, let us strictly threaten them, that they speak henceforth to no man in this name. \textsuperscript{18} And they called them, and commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus. \textsuperscript{19} But Peter and John answered and said unto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge all of you. \textsuperscript{20} For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard. \textsuperscript{21} So when they had further threatened them, they let them go, finding nothing how they might punish them, because of the people: for all men glorified God for that which was done. \textsuperscript{22} For the man was above forty years old, on whom this miracle of healing was showed. \textsuperscript{23} And being let go, they went to their own company, and reported all that the chief priests and elders had said unto them. \textsuperscript{24} And when they heard that, they lifted up their voice to God with one accord, and said, Lord, you are God, which have made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all that in them is: \textsuperscript{25} Who by the mouth of your servant David have said, Why did the heathen rage, and the people imagine vain things? \textsuperscript{26} The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord, and against his Christ. \textsuperscript{27} For truthfully against your holy child Jesus, whom you have anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, and the people of Israel, were gathered together, \textsuperscript{28} In order to do whatsoever your hand and your counsel determined before to be done. \textsuperscript{29} And now, Lord, behold their threatenings: and grant unto your servants, that with all boldness they may speak your word, (o. logos) \textsuperscript{30} By stretching forth yours hand to heal; and that signs and wonders may be done by the name of your holy child Jesus. \textsuperscript{31} And when they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were assembled together; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) and they spoke the word (o. logos) of God with boldness. \textsuperscript{32} And the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul: neither said any of them that ought of the things which he possessed was his own; but they had all things common. \textsuperscript{33} And with great power gave the apostles witness of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus: and great grace was upon them all. \textsuperscript{34} Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold, \textsuperscript{35} And laid them down at the apostles' feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need. \textsuperscript{36} And Joses, who by the apostles was surnamed Barnabas, (which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation,) a Levite, and of the country of Cyprus, \textsuperscript{37} Having land, sold it, and brought the money, and laid it at the apostles' feet.\par
