\subsection*{Galatians 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also. \textsuperscript{2} And I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain. \textsuperscript{3} But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised: \textsuperscript{4} And that because of false brethren unexpectedly brought in, who came in privately to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage: \textsuperscript{5} To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you. \textsuperscript{6} But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it makes no matter to me: God accepts no man's person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me: \textsuperscript{7} But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter; \textsuperscript{8} (For he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles:) \textsuperscript{9} And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision. \textsuperscript{10} Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do. \textsuperscript{11} But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. \textsuperscript{12} For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. \textsuperscript{13} And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation. \textsuperscript{14} But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If you, being a Jew, live after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compell you the Gentiles to live as do the Jews? \textsuperscript{15} We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles, \textsuperscript{16} Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. \textsuperscript{17} But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid. \textsuperscript{18} For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor. \textsuperscript{19} For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God. \textsuperscript{20} I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ lives in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me. \textsuperscript{21} I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.\par

\subsection*{Galatians 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you, that all of you should not obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ has been evidently set forth, crucified among you? \textsuperscript{2} This only would I learn of you, Received all of you the Spirit (o. pneuma) by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? \textsuperscript{3} Are all of you so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, (o. pneuma) are all of you now made perfect by the flesh? \textsuperscript{4} Have all of you suffered so many things in vain? if it be yet in vain. \textsuperscript{5} He therefore that ministers to you the Spirit, (o. pneuma) and works miracles among you, does he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? \textsuperscript{6} Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. \textsuperscript{7} Know all of you therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham. \textsuperscript{8} And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In you shall all nations be blessed. \textsuperscript{9} So then they which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham. \textsuperscript{10} For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse: for it is written, Cursed is every one that continues not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them. \textsuperscript{11} But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith. \textsuperscript{12} And the law is not of faith: but, The man that does them shall live in them. \textsuperscript{13} Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangs on a tree: \textsuperscript{14} That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit (o. pneuma) through faith. \textsuperscript{15} Brethren, I speak after the manner of men; Though it be but a man's covenant, yet if it be confirmed, no man nullifies, or adds thereto. \textsuperscript{16} Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He says not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to your seed, which is Christ. \textsuperscript{17} And this I say, that the covenant, that was confirmed before of God in Christ, the law, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot nullify, that it should make the promise of no effect. \textsuperscript{18} For if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise: but God gave it to Abraham by promise. \textsuperscript{19} Wherefore then serves the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made; and it was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator. \textsuperscript{20} Now a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one. \textsuperscript{21} Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law. \textsuperscript{22} But the scripture has concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe. \textsuperscript{23} But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed. \textsuperscript{24} Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith. \textsuperscript{25} But after that faith has come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster. \textsuperscript{26} For all of you are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. \textsuperscript{27} For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. \textsuperscript{28} There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for all of you are all one in Christ Jesus. \textsuperscript{29} And if all of you be Christ's, then are all of you Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.\par

\end{quote}
\subsection*{Galatians 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now I say, That the heir, as long as he is a child, differs nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; \textsuperscript{2} But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father. \textsuperscript{3} Even so we, when we were children, were in bondage under the elements of the world: \textsuperscript{4} But when the fullness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, \textsuperscript{5} To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. \textsuperscript{6} And because all of you are sons, God has sent forth the Spirit (o. pneuma) of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. \textsuperscript{7} Wherefore you are no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ. \textsuperscript{8} Nevertheless then, when all of you knew not God, all of you did service unto them which by nature are no gods. \textsuperscript{9} But now, after that all of you have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn all of you again to the weak and beggarly elements, unto which all of you desire again to be in bondage? \textsuperscript{10} All of you observe days, and months, and times, and years. \textsuperscript{11} I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain. \textsuperscript{12} Brethren, I plead to you, be as I am; for I am as all of you are: all of you have not injured me at all. \textsuperscript{13} All of you know how through infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel unto you at the first. \textsuperscript{14} And my temptation which was in my flesh all of you despised not, nor rejected; but received me as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus. \textsuperscript{15} Where is then the blessedness all of you spoke of? for I bear you record, that, if it had been possible, all of you would have plucked out your own eyes, and have given them to me. \textsuperscript{16} Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth? \textsuperscript{17} They zealously affect you, but not well; yea, they would exclude you, that all of you might affect them. \textsuperscript{18} But it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you. \textsuperscript{19} My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you, \textsuperscript{20} I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you. \textsuperscript{21} Tell me, all of you that desire to be under the law, do all of you not hear the law? \textsuperscript{22} For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman. \textsuperscript{23} But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman was by promise. \textsuperscript{24} Which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants; the one from the mount Sinai, which genders to bondage, which is Agar. \textsuperscript{25} For this Agar is mount Sinai in Arabia, and answers to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children. \textsuperscript{26} But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all. \textsuperscript{27} For it is written, Rejoice, you barren that bear not; break forth and cry, you that travail not: for the desolate has many more children than she which has an husband. \textsuperscript{28} Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise. \textsuperscript{29} But as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him that was born after the Spirit, (o. pneuma) even so it is now. \textsuperscript{30} Nevertheless what says the scripture? Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman. \textsuperscript{31} So then, brethren, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free.\par

\subsection*{Galatians 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ has made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage. \textsuperscript{2} Behold, I Paul say unto you, that if all of you be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing. \textsuperscript{3} For I testify again to every man that is circumcised, that he is a debtor to do the whole law. \textsuperscript{4} Christ is become of no effect unto you, whosoever of you are justified by the law; all of you are fallen from grace. \textsuperscript{5} For we through the Spirit (o. pneuma) wait for the hope of righteousness by faith. \textsuperscript{6} For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision avails any thing, nor uncircumcision; but faith which works by love. (o. agape) \textsuperscript{7} All of you did run well; who did hinder you that all of you should not obey the truth? \textsuperscript{8} This persuasion comes not of him that calls you. \textsuperscript{9} A little leaven leavens the whole lump. \textsuperscript{10} I have confidence in you through the Lord, that all of you will be none otherwise minded: but he that troubles you shall bear his judgment, whosoever he be. \textsuperscript{11} And I, brethren, if I yet preach circumcision, why do I yet suffer persecution? then is the offence of the cross ceased. \textsuperscript{12} I would they were even cut off which trouble you. \textsuperscript{13} For, brethren, all of you have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love (o. agape) serve one another. \textsuperscript{14} For all the law is fulfilled in one word, (o. logos) even in this; You shall love your neighbour as yourself. \textsuperscript{15} But if all of you bite and devour one another, take heed that all of you be not consumed one of another. \textsuperscript{16} This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, (o. pneuma) and all of you shall not fulfill the lust of the flesh. \textsuperscript{17} For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, (o. pneuma) and the Spirit (o. pneuma) against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other: so that all of you cannot do the things that all of you would. \textsuperscript{18} But if all of you be led of the Spirit, (o. pneuma) all of you are not under the law. \textsuperscript{19} Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these; Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness, \textsuperscript{20} Idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, worldy jealousies, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies, \textsuperscript{21} Envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God. \textsuperscript{22} But the fruit of the Spirit (o. pneuma) is love, (o. agape) joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, \textsuperscript{23} Meekness, wilful restrain: against such there is no law. \textsuperscript{24} And they that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts. \textsuperscript{25} If we live in the Spirit, (o. pneuma) let us also walk in the Spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{26} Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.\par

\subsection*{Galatians 6}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, all of you which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit (o. pneuma) of meekness; considering yourself, lest you also be tempted. \textsuperscript{2} Bear all of you one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ. \textsuperscript{3} For if a man think himself to be something, when he is nothing, he deceives himself. \textsuperscript{4} But let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another. \textsuperscript{5} For every man shall bear his own burden. \textsuperscript{6} Let him that is taught in the word (o. logos) communicate unto him that teaches in all good things. \textsuperscript{7} Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man sows, that shall he also reap. \textsuperscript{8} For he that sows to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that sows to the Spirit (o. pneuma) shall of the Spirit (o. pneuma) reap life everlasting. \textsuperscript{9} And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not. \textsuperscript{10} As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith. \textsuperscript{11} All of you see how large a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand. \textsuperscript{12} As many as desire to make a fair show in the flesh, they constrain you to be circumcised; only lest they should suffer persecution for the cross of Christ. \textsuperscript{13} For neither they themselves who are circumcised keep the law; but desire to have you circumcised, that they may glory in your flesh. \textsuperscript{14} But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world. \textsuperscript{15} For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision avails any thing, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature. \textsuperscript{16} And as many as walk according to this rule, peace be on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God. \textsuperscript{17} From henceforth let no man trouble me: for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus. \textsuperscript{18} Brethren, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. (o. pneuma) Amen.\par

\section*{Ephesians}
\subsection*{Ephesians 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus: \textsuperscript{2} Grace be to you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ. \textsuperscript{3} Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ: \textsuperscript{4} According as he has chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: (o. agape) \textsuperscript{5} Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will, \textsuperscript{6} To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he has made us accepted in the beloved. \textsuperscript{7} In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace; \textsuperscript{8} Wherein he has abounded toward us in all wisdom and prudence; \textsuperscript{9} Having made known unto us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he has purposed in himself: \textsuperscript{10} That in the dispensation of the fullness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him: \textsuperscript{11} In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who works all things after the counsel of his own will: \textsuperscript{12} That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ. \textsuperscript{13} In whom all of you also trusted, after that all of you heard the word (o. logos) of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that all of you believed, all of you were sealed with that holy Spirit (o. pneuma) of promise, \textsuperscript{14} Which is the earn of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory. \textsuperscript{15} Wherefore I also, after I heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus, and love (o. agape) unto all the saints, \textsuperscript{16} Cease not to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers; \textsuperscript{17} That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit (o. pneuma) of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him: \textsuperscript{18} The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that all of you may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints, \textsuperscript{19} And what is the exceeding greatness of his power toward us who believe, according to the working of his mighty power, \textsuperscript{20} Which he wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places, \textsuperscript{21} Far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come: \textsuperscript{22} And has put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, \textsuperscript{23} Which is his body, the fullness of him that fills all in all.\par

\subsection*{Ephesians 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And you has he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; \textsuperscript{2} Wherein in time past all of you walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit (o. pneuma) that now works in the children of disobedience: \textsuperscript{3} Among whom also we all had our conversation in times past in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind; and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others. \textsuperscript{4} But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love (o. agape) wherewith he loved us, \textsuperscript{5} Even when we were dead in sins, has quickened us together with Christ, (by grace all of you are saved;) \textsuperscript{6} And has raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus: \textsuperscript{7} That in the ages to come he might show the exceeding riches of his grace in his kindness toward us through Christ Jesus. \textsuperscript{8} For by grace are all of you saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: \textsuperscript{9} Not of works, lest any man should boast. \textsuperscript{10} For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God has before ordained that we should walk in them. \textsuperscript{11} Wherefore remember, that all of you being in time past Gentiles in the flesh, who are called Uncircumcision by that which is called the Circumcision in the flesh made by hands; \textsuperscript{12} That at that time all of you were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world: \textsuperscript{13} But now in Christ Jesus all of you who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ. \textsuperscript{14} For he is our peace, who has made both one, and has broken down the middle wall of partition between us; \textsuperscript{15} Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; in order to make in himself of two one new man, so making peace; \textsuperscript{16} And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby: \textsuperscript{17} And came and preached peace to you which were far off, and to them that were nigh. \textsuperscript{18} For through him we both have access by one Spirit (o. pneuma) unto the Father. \textsuperscript{19} Now therefore all of you are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints, and of the household of God; \textsuperscript{20} And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone; \textsuperscript{21} In whom all the building fitly framed together grows unto an holy temple in the Lord: \textsuperscript{22} In whom all of you also are built together for an habitation of God through the Spirit. (o. pneuma)\par

\subsection*{Ephesians 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} For this cause I Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles, \textsuperscript{2} If all of you have heard of the dispensation of the grace of God which is given me toward you: \textsuperscript{3} How that by revelation he made known unto me the mystery; (as I wrote before in few words, \textsuperscript{4} Whereby, when all of you read, all of you may understand my knowledge in the mystery of Christ) \textsuperscript{5} Which in other ages was not made known unto the sons of men, as it is now revealed unto his holy apostles and prophets by the Spirit; (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{6} That the Gentiles should be join heirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel: \textsuperscript{7} Whereof I was made a minister, according to the gift of the grace of God given unto me by the effectual working of his power. \textsuperscript{8} Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ; \textsuperscript{9} And to make all men see what is the fellowship of the mystery, which from the beginning of the world has been hid in God, who created all things by Jesus Christ: \textsuperscript{10} To the intent that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly places might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God, \textsuperscript{11} According to the eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus our Lord: \textsuperscript{12} In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him. \textsuperscript{13} Wherefore I desire that all of you faint not at my tribulations for you, which is your glory. \textsuperscript{14} For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, \textsuperscript{15} Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named, \textsuperscript{16} That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit (o. pneuma) in the inner man; \textsuperscript{17} That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that all of you, being rooted and grounded in love, (o. agape) \textsuperscript{18} May be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height; \textsuperscript{19} And to know the love (o. agape) of Christ, which passes knowledge, that all of you might be filled with all the fullness of God. \textsuperscript{20} Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us, \textsuperscript{21} Unto him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen.\par

\subsection*{Ephesians 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, plead to you that all of you walk worthy of the vocation wherewith all of you are called, \textsuperscript{2} With all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love; (o. agape) \textsuperscript{3} Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit (o. pneuma) in the bond of peace. \textsuperscript{4} There is one body, and one Spirit, (o. pneuma) even as all of you are called in one hope of your calling; \textsuperscript{5} One Lord, one faith, one baptism, \textsuperscript{6} One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all. \textsuperscript{7} But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ. \textsuperscript{8} Wherefore he says, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men. \textsuperscript{9} (Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth? \textsuperscript{10} He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.) \textsuperscript{11} And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; \textsuperscript{12} For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: \textsuperscript{13} Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ: \textsuperscript{14} That we henceforth be no more children, tossed back and forth, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive; \textsuperscript{15} But speaking the truth in love, (o. agape) may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ: \textsuperscript{16} From whom the whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplies, according to the effectual working in the measure of every part, makes increase of the body unto the edifying of itself in love. (o. agape) \textsuperscript{17} This I say therefore, and testify in the Lord, that all of you henceforth walk not as other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind, \textsuperscript{18} Having the understanding darkened, being alienated from the life of God through the ignorance that is in them, because of the blindness of their heart: \textsuperscript{19} Who being past feeling have given themselves over unto lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness. \textsuperscript{20} But all of you have not so learned Christ; \textsuperscript{21} If so be that all of you have heard him, and have been taught by him, as the truth is in Jesus: \textsuperscript{22} That all of you put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts; \textsuperscript{23} And be renewed in the spirit (o. pneuma) of your mind; \textsuperscript{24} And that all of you put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness. \textsuperscript{25} Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another. \textsuperscript{26} Be all of you angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath: \textsuperscript{27} Neither give place to the devil. \textsuperscript{28} Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needs. \textsuperscript{29} Let no corrupt communication (o. logos) proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers. \textsuperscript{30} And grieve not the holy Spirit (o. pneuma) of God, whereby all of you are sealed unto the day of redemption. \textsuperscript{31} Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice: \textsuperscript{32} And be all of you kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake has forgiven you.\par

\subsection*{Ephesians 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Be all of you therefore followers of God, as dear children; \textsuperscript{2} And walk in love, (o. agape) as Christ also has loved us, and has given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweet smelling savour. \textsuperscript{3} But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becomes saints; \textsuperscript{4} Neither filthiness, nor foolish talking, nor jesting, which are not convenient: but rather giving of thanks. \textsuperscript{5} For this all of you know, that no whoremonger, nor unclean person, nor covetous man, who is an idolater, has any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God. \textsuperscript{6} Let no man deceive you with vain words: (o. logos) for because of these things comes the wrath of God upon the children of disobedience. \textsuperscript{7} Be not all of you therefore partakers with them. \textsuperscript{8} For all of you were sometimes darkness, but now are all of you light in the Lord: walk as children of light: \textsuperscript{9} (For the fruit of the Spirit (o. pneuma) is in all goodness and righteousness and truth;) \textsuperscript{10} Proving what is acceptable unto the Lord. \textsuperscript{11} And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them. \textsuperscript{12} For it is a shame even to speak of those things which are done of them in secret. \textsuperscript{13} But all things that are reproved are made manifest by the light: for whatsoever does make manifest is light. \textsuperscript{14} Wherefore he says, Awake you that sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give you light. \textsuperscript{15} See then that all of you walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, \textsuperscript{16} Redeeming the time, because the days are evil. \textsuperscript{17} Wherefore be all of you not unwise, but understanding what the will of the Lord is. \textsuperscript{18} And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit; (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{19} Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; \textsuperscript{20} Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ; \textsuperscript{21} Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God. \textsuperscript{22} Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. \textsuperscript{23} For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body. \textsuperscript{24} Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing. \textsuperscript{25} Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it; \textsuperscript{26} That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word, (o. rhema) \textsuperscript{27} That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish. \textsuperscript{28} So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loves his wife loves himself. \textsuperscript{29} For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourishes and cherishes it, even as the Lord the church: \textsuperscript{30} For we are members of his body, of his flesh, and of his bones. \textsuperscript{31} For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh. \textsuperscript{32} This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church. \textsuperscript{33} Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.\par

\subsection*{Ephesians 6}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. \textsuperscript{2} Honour your father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; \textsuperscript{3} That it may be well with you, and you may live long on the earth. \textsuperscript{4} And, all of you fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. \textsuperscript{5} Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ; \textsuperscript{6} Not with eye-service, as men-pleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart; \textsuperscript{7} With good will doing service, as to the Lord, and not to men: \textsuperscript{8} Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man does, the same shall he receive of the Lord, whether he be bond or free. \textsuperscript{9} And, all of you masters, do the same things unto them, forbearing threatening: knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him. \textsuperscript{10} Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. \textsuperscript{11} Put on the whole armour of God, that all of you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. \textsuperscript{12} For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. \textsuperscript{13} Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that all of you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand. \textsuperscript{14} Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness; \textsuperscript{15} And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace; \textsuperscript{16} Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith all of you shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked. \textsuperscript{17} And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, (o. pneuma) which is the word (o. rhema) of God: \textsuperscript{18} Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, (o. pneuma) and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints; \textsuperscript{19} And for me, that utterance (o. logos) may be given unto me, that I may open my mouth boldly, to make known the mystery of the gospel, \textsuperscript{20} For which I am an ambassador in bonds: that therein I may speak boldly, as I ought to speak. \textsuperscript{21} But that all of you also may know my affairs, and how I do, Tychicus, a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, shall make known to you all things: \textsuperscript{22} Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that all of you might know our affairs, and that he might comfort your hearts. \textsuperscript{23} Peace be to the brethren, and love (o. agape) with faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. \textsuperscript{24} Grace be with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in sincerity. Amen.\par

\section*{Philippians}
\subsection*{Philippians 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Paul and Timotheus, the servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus which are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons: \textsuperscript{2} Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ. \textsuperscript{3} I thank my God upon every remembrance of you, \textsuperscript{4} Always in every prayer of mine for you all making request with joy, \textsuperscript{5} For your fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now; \textsuperscript{6} Being confident of this very thing, that he which has begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ: \textsuperscript{7} Even as it is meet for me to think this of you all, because I have you in my heart; inasmuch as both in my bonds, and in the defence and confirmation of the gospel, all of you all are partakers of my grace. \textsuperscript{8} For God is my record, how greatly I long after you all in the bowels of Jesus Christ. \textsuperscript{9} And this I pray, that your love (o. agape) may abound yet more and more in knowledge and in all judgment; \textsuperscript{10} That all of you may approve things that are excellent; that all of you may be sincere and without offence till the day of Christ. \textsuperscript{11} Being filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are by Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God. \textsuperscript{12} But I would all of you should understand, brethren, that the things which happened unto me have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel; \textsuperscript{13} So that my bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace, and in all other places; \textsuperscript{14} And many of the brethren in the Lord, waxing confident by my bonds, are much more bold to speak the word (o. logos) without fear. \textsuperscript{15} Some indeed preach Christ even of envy and strife; and some also of good will: \textsuperscript{16} The one preach Christ of contention, not sincerely, supposing to add affliction to my bonds: \textsuperscript{17} But the other of love, (o. agape) knowing that I am set for the defence of the gospel. \textsuperscript{18} What then? notwithstanding, every way, whether in pretence, or in truth, Christ is preached; and I therein do rejoice, yea, and will rejoice. \textsuperscript{19} For I know that this shall turn to my salvation through your prayer, and the supply of the Spirit (o. pneuma) of Jesus Christ, \textsuperscript{20} According to my earn expectation and my hope, that in nothing I shall be ashamed, but that with all boldness, as always, so now also Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether it be by life, or by death. \textsuperscript{21} In order to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain. \textsuperscript{22} But if I live in the flesh, this is the fruit of my labour: yet what I shall choose I know not. \textsuperscript{23} For I am in a strait between two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better: \textsuperscript{24} Nevertheless to abide in the flesh is more necessary for you. \textsuperscript{25} And having this confidence, I know that I shall abide and continue with you all for your furtherance and joy of faith; \textsuperscript{26} That your rejoicing may be more abundant in Jesus Christ for me by my coming to you again. \textsuperscript{27} Only let your conversation be as it becomes the gospel of Christ: that whether I come and see you, or else be absent, I may hear of your affairs, that all of you stand fast in one spirit, (o. pneuma) with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel; \textsuperscript{28} And in nothing terrified by your adversaries: which is to them an evident token of perdition, but to you of salvation, and that of God. \textsuperscript{29} For unto you it is given in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on him, but also to suffer for his sake; \textsuperscript{30} Having the same conflict which all of you saw in me, and now hear to be in me.\par

\subsection*{Philippians 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} If there be therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, (o. agape) if any fellowship of the Spirit, (o. pneuma) if any bowels and mercies, \textsuperscript{2} Fulfill all of you my joy, that all of you be likeminded, having the same love, (o. agape) being of one accord, of one mind. \textsuperscript{3} Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. \textsuperscript{4} Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. \textsuperscript{5} Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: \textsuperscript{6} Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: \textsuperscript{7} But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: \textsuperscript{8} And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. \textsuperscript{9} Wherefore God also has highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: \textsuperscript{10} That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; \textsuperscript{11} And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. \textsuperscript{12} Wherefore, my beloved, as all of you have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling. \textsuperscript{13} For it is God which works in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure. \textsuperscript{14} Do all things without murmurings and disputings: \textsuperscript{15} That all of you may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom all of you shine as lights in the world; \textsuperscript{16} Holding forth the word (o. logos) of life; that I may rejoice in the day of Christ, that I have not run in vain, neither laboured in vain. \textsuperscript{17} Yea, and if I be offered upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I joy, and rejoice with you all. \textsuperscript{18} For the same cause also do all of you joy, and rejoice with me. \textsuperscript{19} But I trust in the Lord Jesus to send Timotheus shortly unto you, that I also may be of good comfort, when I know your state. \textsuperscript{20} For I have no man likeminded, who will naturally care for your state. \textsuperscript{21} For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's. \textsuperscript{22} But all of you know the proof of him, that, as a son with the father, he has served with me in the gospel. \textsuperscript{23} Him therefore I hope to send presently, so soon as I shall see how it will go with me. \textsuperscript{24} But I trust in the Lord that I also myself shall come shortly. \textsuperscript{25} Yet I supposed it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother, and companion in labour, and fellow soldier, but your messenger, and he that ministered to my wants. \textsuperscript{26} For he longed after you all, and was full of heaviness, because that all of you had heard that he had been sick. \textsuperscript{27} For indeed he was sick nigh unto death: but God had mercy on him; and not on him only, but on me also, lest I should have sorrow upon sorrow. \textsuperscript{28} I sent him therefore the more carefully, that, when all of you see him again, all of you may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful. \textsuperscript{29} Receive him therefore in the Lord with all gladness; and hold such in reputation: \textsuperscript{30} Because for the work of Christ he was nigh unto death, not regarding his life, to supply your lack of service toward me.\par

\subsection*{Philippians 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Finally, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you, to me indeed is not grievous, but for you it is safe. \textsuperscript{2} Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision. \textsuperscript{3} For we are the circumcision, which worship God in the spirit, (o. pneuma) and rejoice in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh. \textsuperscript{4} Though I might also have confidence in the flesh. If any other man thinks that he has whereof he might trust in the flesh, I more: \textsuperscript{5} Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as concerning the law, a Pharisee; \textsuperscript{6} Concerning zeal, persecuting the church; concerning the righteousness which is in the law, blameless. \textsuperscript{7} But what things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ. \textsuperscript{8} Yea doubtless, and I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung, that I may win Christ, \textsuperscript{9} And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith: \textsuperscript{10} That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death; \textsuperscript{11} If by any means I might attain unto the resurrection of the dead. \textsuperscript{12} Not as though I had already attained, either were already perfect: but I follow after, if that I may apprehend that for which also I am apprehended of Christ Jesus. \textsuperscript{13} Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, \textsuperscript{14} I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus. \textsuperscript{15} Let us therefore, as many as be perfect, be thus minded: and if in any thing all of you be otherwise minded, God shall reveal even this unto you. \textsuperscript{16} Nevertheless, whereto we have already attained, let us walk by the same rule, let us mind the same thing. \textsuperscript{17} Brethren, be followers together of me, and mark them which walk so as all of you have us for an example. \textsuperscript{18} (For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ: \textsuperscript{19} Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.) \textsuperscript{20} For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ: \textsuperscript{21} Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body, according to the working whereby he is able even to subdue all things unto himself.\par

\subsection*{Philippians 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Therefore, my brethren dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved. \textsuperscript{2} I plead to Euodias, and plead to Syntyche, that they be of the same mind in the Lord. \textsuperscript{3} And I implore you also, true yokefellow, help those women which laboured with me in the gospel, with Clement also, and with other my fellow labourers, whose names are in the book of life. \textsuperscript{4} Rejoice in the Lord always: and again I say, Rejoice. \textsuperscript{5} Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand. \textsuperscript{6} Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. \textsuperscript{7} And the peace of God, which passes all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus. \textsuperscript{8} Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things. \textsuperscript{9} Those things, which all of you have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, do: and the God of peace shall be with you. \textsuperscript{10} But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly, that now at the last your care of me has flourished again; wherein all of you were also careful, but all of you lacked opportunity. \textsuperscript{11} Not that I speak in respect of lack: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content. \textsuperscript{12} I know both how to be brought low, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. \textsuperscript{13} I can do all things through Christ which strengthens me. \textsuperscript{14} Notwithstanding all of you have well done, that all of you did communicate with my affliction. \textsuperscript{15} Now all of you Philippians know also, that in the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church communicated with me as concerning (o. logos) giving and receiving, but all of you only. \textsuperscript{16} For even in Thessalonica all of you sent once and again unto my necessity. \textsuperscript{17} Not because I desire a gift: but I desire fruit that may abound to your account. (o. logos) \textsuperscript{18} But I have all, and abound: I am full, having received of Epaphroditus the things which were sent from you, an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, well-pleasing to God. \textsuperscript{19} But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus. \textsuperscript{20} Now unto God and our Father be glory for ever and ever. Amen. \textsuperscript{21} Salute every saint in Christ Jesus. The brethren which are with me greet you. \textsuperscript{22} All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Caesar's household. \textsuperscript{23} The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.\par

Jerome states (in Philemon) that St. Paul had converted many in Caesar's family; for "being by the emperor cast into prison, he became more known to his family, and turned the house of Christ's persecutor into a church."\par

\section*{Colossians}
\subsection*{Colossians 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timotheus our brother, \textsuperscript{2} To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. \textsuperscript{3} We give thanks to God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you, \textsuperscript{4} Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus, and of the (o. agape) love which all of you have to all the saints, \textsuperscript{5} For the hope which is laid up for you in heaven, whereof all of you heard before in the (o. logos) word of the truth of the gospel; \textsuperscript{6} Which has come unto you, as it is in all the world; and brings forth fruit, as it does also in you, since the day all of you heard of it, and knew the grace of God in truth: \textsuperscript{7} As all of you also learned of Epaphras our dear fellow servant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ; \textsuperscript{8} Who also declared unto us your (o. agape) love in the (o. pneuma) Spirit. \textsuperscript{9} For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that all of you might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding; \textsuperscript{10} That all of you might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God; \textsuperscript{11} Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness; \textsuperscript{12} Giving thanks unto the Father, which has made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light: \textsuperscript{13} Who has delivered us from the power of darkness, and has translated us into the kingdom of his (o. agape) dear Son: \textsuperscript{14} In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins: \textsuperscript{15} Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: \textsuperscript{16} For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: \textsuperscript{17} And he is before all things, and by him all things consist. \textsuperscript{18} And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence. \textsuperscript{19} For it pleased the Father that in him should all fullness dwell; \textsuperscript{20} And, having made peace through the blood of his cross, by him to reconcile all things unto himself; by him, I say, whether they be things in earth, or things in heaven. \textsuperscript{21} And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works, yet now has he reconciled \textsuperscript{22} In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and irreproachable in his sight: \textsuperscript{23} If all of you continue in the faith grounded and settled, and be not moved away from the hope of the gospel, which all of you have heard, and which was preached to every creature which is under heaven; whereof I Paul am made a minister; \textsuperscript{24} Who now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and fill up that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his body's sake, which is the church: \textsuperscript{25} Whereof I am made a minister, according to the dispensation of God which is given to me for you, to fulfill the (o. logos) word of God; \textsuperscript{26} Even the mystery which has been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints: \textsuperscript{27} To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory: \textsuperscript{28} Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom; that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus: \textsuperscript{29} Unto which I also labour, striving according to his working, which works in me mightily.\par

\subsection*{Colossians 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} For I would that all of you knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh; \textsuperscript{2} That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in (o. agape) love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ; \textsuperscript{3} In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. \textsuperscript{4} And this I say, lest any man should beguile you with enticing words. \textsuperscript{5} For though I be absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the (o. pneuma) spirit, rejoicing and beholding your order, and the steadfastness of your faith in Christ. \textsuperscript{6} As all of you have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk all of you in him: \textsuperscript{7} Rooted and built up in him, and established in the faith, as all of you have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving. \textsuperscript{8} Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ. \textsuperscript{9} For in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily. \textsuperscript{10} And all of you are complete in him, which is the head of all principality and power: \textsuperscript{11} In whom also all of you are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ: \textsuperscript{12} Buried with him in baptism, wherein also all of you are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God, who has raised him from the dead. \textsuperscript{13} And you, being dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, has he quickened together with him, having forgiven you all trespasses; \textsuperscript{14} Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross; \textsuperscript{15} And having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a show of them openly, triumphing over them in it. \textsuperscript{16} Let no man therefore judge you in food, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: \textsuperscript{17} Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ. \textsuperscript{18} Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he has not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind, \textsuperscript{19} And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increases with the increase of God. \textsuperscript{20} Wherefore if all of you be dead with Christ from the rudiments of the world, why, as though living in the world, are all of you subject to ordinances, \textsuperscript{21} (Touch not; taste not; handle not; \textsuperscript{22} Which all are to perish with the using;) after the commandments and doctrines of men? \textsuperscript{23} Which things have indeed a (o. logos) show of wisdom religious outlook, and humility, and neglecting of the body: not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh.\par

\subsection*{Colossians 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} If all of you then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sits on the right hand of God. \textsuperscript{2} Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth. \textsuperscript{3} For all of you are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God. \textsuperscript{4} When Christ, who is our life, shall appear, then shall all of you also appear with him in glory. \textsuperscript{5} Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry: \textsuperscript{6} For which things' sake the wrath of God comes on the children of disobedience: \textsuperscript{7} In the which all of you also walked some time, when all of you lived in them. \textsuperscript{8} But now all of you also put off all these; anger, wrath, malice, blasphemy, filthy communication out of your mouth. \textsuperscript{9} Lie not one to another, seeing that all of you have put off the old man with his deeds; \textsuperscript{10} And have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him: \textsuperscript{11} Where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Savages, bond nor free: but Christ is all, and in all. \textsuperscript{12} Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; \textsuperscript{13} Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do all of you. \textsuperscript{14} And above all these things put on (o. agape) love, which is the bond of perfection. \textsuperscript{15} And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also all of you are called in one body; and be all of you thankful. \textsuperscript{16} Let the (o. logos) word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. \textsuperscript{17} And whatsoever all of you do in (o. logos) word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him. \textsuperscript{18} Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as it is fit in the Lord. \textsuperscript{19} Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them. \textsuperscript{20} Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing unto the Lord. \textsuperscript{21} Fathers, provoke not your children to anger, lest they be discouraged. \textsuperscript{22} Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eye-service, as men-pleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God; \textsuperscript{23} And whatsoever all of you do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men; \textsuperscript{24} Knowing that of the Lord all of you shall receive the reward of the inheritance: for all of you serve the Lord Christ. \textsuperscript{25} But he that does wrong shall receive for the wrong which he has done: and there is no respect of persons.\par

\subsection*{Colossians 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal; knowing that all of you also have a Master in heaven. \textsuperscript{2} Continue in prayer, and watch in the same with thanksgiving; \textsuperscript{3} Likewise praying also for us, that God would open unto us a door of (o. logos) utterance, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in bonds: \textsuperscript{4} That I may make it manifest, as I ought to speak. \textsuperscript{5} Walk in wisdom toward them that are without, redeeming the time. \textsuperscript{6} Let your (o. logos) speech be always with grace, seasoned with salt, that all of you may know how all of you ought to answer every man. \textsuperscript{7} All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, who is a beloved brother, and a faithful minister and fellow servant in the Lord: \textsuperscript{8} Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that he might know your estate, and comfort your hearts; \textsuperscript{9} With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They shall make known unto you all things which are done here. \textsuperscript{10} Aristarchus my fellow-prisoner salutes you, and Marcus, sister's (concerning whom all of you received commandments: if he comes unto you, receive him;) \textsuperscript{11} And Jesus, which is called Justus, who are of the circumcision. These only are my fellow workers unto the kingdom of God, which have been a comfort unto me. \textsuperscript{12} Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, salutes you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that all of you may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God. \textsuperscript{13} For I bear him record, that he has a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis. \textsuperscript{14} Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas, greet you. \textsuperscript{15} Salute the brethren which are in Laodicea, and Nymphas, and the church which is in his house. \textsuperscript{16} And when this epistle is read among you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans; and that all of you likewise read the epistle from Laodicea. \textsuperscript{17} And say to Archippus, Take heed to the ministry which you have received in the Lord, that you fulfill it. \textsuperscript{18} The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.\par
\begin{quote}\footnotesize
Colossians 4:3 TSK note: praying; that; a door The term door is used metaphorically for an entrance to any business, or occasion or opportunity of doing any thing; and consequently "a door of utterance" is an opportunity of preaching the gospel successfully. See the parallel texts. the mystery, ; for\par
Colossians 4:7 TSK note: my Tychicus; a beloved, ; a faithful\par
Colossians 4:9 Brenton note: Name meaning: Onesimus (Onesimos) — Useful; profitable The runaway slave who became useful.\par
Colossians 4:10 TSK note: Aristarchus, ; saluteth and Marcus, ; receive\par
Colossians 4:12 TSK note: Epaphras; a servant; always; labouring or, striving, that; see note on, ; , *Gr:; *Gr:; complete or, filled\par
Colossians 4:13 TSK note: I bear; Laodicea and Hierapolis were both cities of Phrygia in Asia Minor, between which, and equidistant from each, was situated Colosse. Laodicea was seated near the Lycus, about 63 miles east of Ephesus; and became one of the largest and richest towns in Phrygia, vying in power with the maritime cities. It is now called Eski-hissar, the old castle; and besides the whole surface within the city's wall being strewed with pedestals and fragments, the ruins of an amphitheatre, a magnificent odeum, and other public buildings, attest its former splendour and magnificence. But, when visited by Dr. Chandler, all was silence and solitude; and a fox, first discovered by his ears peeping over a brow, was the only inhabitant of Laodicea. Hierapolis, now Pambouk-Kaiesi, was situated, according to the Itinerary, six miles n of Laodicea; and its ruins are now about a mile and a half in circumference.\par
Colossians 4:14 Brenton note: Name meaning: Demas (Demas) — Popular Loved this present world and forsook Paul.\par
Colossians 4:14 Brenton note: Name meaning: Luke (Loukas) — Light-giving; from Lucania Beloved physician who brought gospel light.\par
Colossians 4:15 Brenton note: Name meaning: Nymphas (Nymphas) — Bridegroom Hosted a house church.\par
Colossians 4:17 TSK note: Archippus Take; , ; the ministry, ; , ;, fulfil\par
\end{quote}
\section*{1 Thessalonians}
\subsection*{1 Thessalonians 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Paul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians which is in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ. \textsuperscript{2} We give thanks to God always for you all, making mention of you in our prayers; \textsuperscript{3} Remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labour of love, (o. agape) and patience of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, in the sight of God and our Father; \textsuperscript{4} Knowing, brethren beloved, your election of God. \textsuperscript{5} For our gospel came not unto you in word (o. logos) only, but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit, (o. pneuma) and in much assurance; as all of you know what manner of men we were among you for your sake. \textsuperscript{6} And all of you became followers of us, and of the Lord, having received the word (o. logos) in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{7} So that all of you were ensamples to all that believe in Macedonia and Achaia. \textsuperscript{8} For from you sounded out the word (o. logos) of the Lord not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith toward God is spread abroad; so that we need not to speak any thing. \textsuperscript{9} For they themselves show of us what manner of entering in we had unto you, and how all of you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God; \textsuperscript{10} And to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, even Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come.\par

\subsection*{1 Thessalonians 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} For yourselves, brethren, know our entrance in unto you, that it was not in vain: \textsuperscript{2} But even after that we had suffered before, and were shamefully pleaded, as all of you know, at Philippi, we were bold in our God to speak unto you the gospel of God with much contention. \textsuperscript{3} For our exhortation was not of deceit, nor of uncleanness, nor in guile: \textsuperscript{4} But as we were allowed of God to be put in trust with the gospel, even so we speak; not as pleasing men, but God, which tries our hearts. \textsuperscript{5} For neither at any time used we flattering words, (o. logos) as all of you know, nor a coat of covetousness; God is witness: \textsuperscript{6} Nor of men sought we glory, neither of you, nor yet of others, when we might have been burdensome, as the apostles of Christ. \textsuperscript{7} But we were gentle among you, even as a nurse cherishes her children: \textsuperscript{8} So being affectionately desirous of you, we were willing to have imparted unto you, not the gospel of God only, but also our own souls, because all of you were dear unto us. \textsuperscript{9} For all of you remember, brethren, our labour and travail: for labouring night and day, because we would not be chargeable unto any of you, we preached unto you the gospel of God. \textsuperscript{10} All of you are witnesses, and God also, how holily and justly and unblameably we behaved ourselves among you that believe: \textsuperscript{11} As all of you know how we exhorted and comforted and charged every one of you, as a father does his children, \textsuperscript{12} That all of you would walk worthy of God, who has called you unto his kingdom and glory. \textsuperscript{13} For this cause also thank we God without ceasing, because, when all of you received the word (o. logos) of God which all of you heard of us, all of you received it not as the word (o. logos) of men, but as it is in truth, the word (o. logos) of God, which effectually works also in you that believe. \textsuperscript{14} For all of you, brethren, became followers of the churches of God which in Judaea are in Christ Jesus: for all of you also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they have of the Jews: \textsuperscript{15} Who both killed the Lord Jesus, and their own prophets, and have persecuted us; and they please not God, and are contrary to all men: \textsuperscript{16} Forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles that they might be saved, to fill up their sins always: for the wrath has come upon them to the uttermost. \textsuperscript{17} But we, brethren, being taken from you for a short time in presence, not in heart, endeavoured the more abundantly to see your face with great desire. \textsuperscript{18} Wherefore we would have come unto you, even I Paul, once and again; but Satan hindered us. \textsuperscript{19} For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Are not even all of you in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming? \textsuperscript{20} For all of you are our glory and joy.\par

\subsection*{1 Thessalonians 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Wherefore when we could no longer forbear, we thought it good to be left at Athens alone; \textsuperscript{2} And sent Timotheus, our brother, and minister of God, and our fellow labourer in the gospel of Christ, to establish you, and to comfort you concerning your faith: \textsuperscript{3} That no man should be moved by these afflictions: for yourselves know that we are appointed thereunto. \textsuperscript{4} For verily, when we were with you, we told you before that we should suffer tribulation; even as it came to pass, and all of you know. \textsuperscript{5} For this cause, when I could no longer forbear, I sent to know your faith, lest by some means the tempter have tempted you, and our labour be in vain. \textsuperscript{6} But now when Timotheus came from you unto us, and brought us good tidings of your faith and love, (o. agape) and that all of you have good remembrance of us always, desiring greatly to see us, as we also to see you: \textsuperscript{7} Therefore, brethren, we were comforted over you in all our affliction and distress by your faith: \textsuperscript{8} For now we live, if all of you stand fast in the Lord. \textsuperscript{9} For what thanks can we render to God again for you, for all the joy wherewith we joy for your sakes before our God; \textsuperscript{10} Night and day praying exceedingly that we might see your face, and might perfect that which is lacking in your faith? \textsuperscript{11} Now God himself and our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ, direct our way unto you. \textsuperscript{12} And the Lord make you to increase and abound in love (o. agape) one toward another, and toward all men, even as we do toward you: \textsuperscript{13} To the end he may establish your hearts unblameable in holiness before God, even our Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints.\par

\subsection*{1 Thessalonians 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Furthermore then we plead to you, brethren, and exhort you by the Lord Jesus, that as all of you have received of us how all of you ought to walk and to please God, so all of you would abound more and more. \textsuperscript{2} For all of you know what commandments we gave you by the Lord Jesus. \textsuperscript{3} For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that all of you should abstain from fornication: \textsuperscript{4} That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour; \textsuperscript{5} Not in the lust of concupiscence, even as the Gentiles which know not God: \textsuperscript{6} That no man go beyond and defraud his brother in any matter: because that the Lord is the avenger of all such, as we also have forewarned you and testified. \textsuperscript{7} For God has not called us unto uncleanness, but unto holiness. \textsuperscript{8} He therefore that despises, despises not man, but God, who has also given unto us his holy Spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{9} But as concerning brotherly love all of you need not that I write unto you: for all of you yourselves are taught of God to love one another. \textsuperscript{10} And indeed all of you do it toward all the brethren which are in all Macedonia: but we plead to you, brethren, that all of you increase more and more; \textsuperscript{11} And that all of you study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you; \textsuperscript{12} That all of you may walk honestly toward them that are without, and that all of you may have lack of nothing. \textsuperscript{13} But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that all of you sorrow not, even as others which have no hope. \textsuperscript{14} For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him. \textsuperscript{15} For this we say unto you by the word (o. logos) of the Lord, that we which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep. \textsuperscript{16} For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: \textsuperscript{17} Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord. \textsuperscript{18} Wherefore comfort one another with these words. (o. logos)\par

\subsection*{1 Thessalonians 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} But of the times and the seasons, brethren, all of you have no need that I write unto you. \textsuperscript{2} For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so comes as a thief in the night. \textsuperscript{3} For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction comes upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape. \textsuperscript{4} But all of you, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief. \textsuperscript{5} All of you are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness. \textsuperscript{6} Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober. \textsuperscript{7} For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night. \textsuperscript{8} But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love; (o. agape) and for an helmet, the hope of salvation. \textsuperscript{9} For God has not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ, \textsuperscript{10} Who died for us, that, whether we wake or sleep, we should live together with him. \textsuperscript{11} Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also all of you do. \textsuperscript{12} And we plead to you, brethren, to know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you; \textsuperscript{13} And to esteem them very highly in love (o. agape) for their work's sake. And be at peace among yourselves. \textsuperscript{14} Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men. \textsuperscript{15} See that none render evil for evil unto any man; but ever follow that which is good, both among yourselves, and to all men. \textsuperscript{16} Rejoice evermore. \textsuperscript{17} Pray without ceasing. \textsuperscript{18} In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you. \textsuperscript{19} Quench not the Spirit. (o. pneuma) \textsuperscript{20} Despise not prophesyings. \textsuperscript{21} Prove all things; hold fast that which is good. \textsuperscript{22} Abstain from all appearance of evil. \textsuperscript{23} And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit (o. pneuma) and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. \textsuperscript{24} Faithful is he that calls you, who also will do it. \textsuperscript{25} Brethren, pray for us. \textsuperscript{26} Greet all the brethren with an holy kiss. \textsuperscript{27} I charge you by the Lord that this epistle be read unto all the holy brethren. \textsuperscript{28} The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.\par
