\noindent \textsuperscript{11} And my wife Anna did take women's works to do. \textsuperscript{12} And when she had sent them home to the owners, they paid her wages, giving her also besides a kid. \textsuperscript{13} And when it was in my house, and began to cry, I said unto her, From whence is this kid? is it not stolen? render it to the owners; for it is not lawful to eat any thing that is stolen.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} But she replied upon me, It was given for a gift more than the wages. Howbeit I did not believe her, but bade her render it to the owners: and I was abashed at her. But she replied upon me, Where are thine alms and thy righteous deeds? behold, thou and all thy works are known.\par
\subsection*{Tobit 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then I being grieved did weep, and in my sorrow prayed, saying, \textsuperscript{2} O Lord, thou art just, and all thy works and all thy ways are mercy and truth, and thou judgest truly and justly for ever. \textsuperscript{3} Remember me, and look on me; punish me not for my sins and ignorances, and the sins of my fathers, who have sinned before thee: \textsuperscript{4} for they obeyed not thy commandments: wherefore thou hast delivered us for a spoil, and unto captivity, and unto death, and for a proverb of reproach to all the nations among whom we are dispersed.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} And now thy judgments are many and true: deal with me according to my sins and my fathers'; because we have not kept thy commandments, neither have walked in truth before thee. \textsuperscript{6} Now therefore deal with me as seemeth best unto thee, and command my spirit to be taken from me, that I may be dissolved, and become earth: for it is profitable for me to die rather than to live, because I have heard false reproaches, and have much sorrow: command therefore that I may now be delivered out of this distress, and go into the everlasting place: turn not thy face away from me.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} It came to pass the same day, that in Ecbatane a city of Media, Sara the daughter of Raguel was also reproached by her father's maids; \textsuperscript{8} because that she had been married to seven husbands, whom Asmodeus the evil spirit had killed, before they had lain with her. Dost thou not know, said they, that thou hast strangled thine husbands? thou hast had already seven husbands, neither wast thou named after any of them. \textsuperscript{9} Wherefore dost thou beat us for them? if they be dead, go thy ways after them, let us never see of thee either son or daughter. \textsuperscript{10} When she heard these things she was very sorrowful, so that she thought to have strangled herself; and she said, I am the only daughter of my father, and if I do this, it shall be a reproach unto him, and I shall bring his old age with sorrow unto the grave.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Then she prayed toward the window, and said, Blessed art thou, O Lord my God, and thine holy and glorious name is blessed and honourable for ever: let all thy works praise thee for ever. \textsuperscript{12} And now, O Lord, I set mine eyes and my face toward thee, \textsuperscript{13} and say, Take me out of the earth, that I may hear no more the reproach. \textsuperscript{14} Thou knowest, Lord, that I am pure from all sin with man, \textsuperscript{15} and that I never polluted my name, nor the name of my father, in the land of my captivity: I am the only daughter of my father, neither hath he any child to be his heir, neither any near kinsman, nor any son of his alive, to whom I may keep myself for a wife: my seven husbands are already dead; and why should I live? but if it please not thee that I should die, command some regard to be had of me, and pity taken of me, that I hear no more reproach.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} So the prayers of them both were heard before the majesty of the great God. \textsuperscript{17} And Raphael was sent to heal them both, that is, to scale away the whiteness of Tobit's eyes, and to give Sara the daughter of Raguel for a wife to Tobias the son of Tobit: and to bind Asmodeus the evil spirit; because she belonged to Tobias by right of inheritance. The self-same time came Tobit home, and entered into his house, and Sara the daughter of Raguel came down from her upper chamber.\par
\subsection*{Tobit 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} In that day Tobit remembered the money which he had committed to Gabael in Rages of Media, \textsuperscript{2} and said with himself, I have wished for death; wherefore do I not call for my son Tobias, that I may signify to him of the money before I die?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} And when he had called him, he said, My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not thy mother, but honour her all the days of thy life, and do that which shall please her, and grieve her not. \textsuperscript{4} Remember, my son, that she saw many dangers for thee, when thou wast in her womb; and when she is dead, bury her by me in one grave.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} My son, be mindful of the Lord our God all thy days, and let not thy will be set to sin, or to transgress his commandments: do uprightly all thy life long, and follow not the ways of unrighteousness. \textsuperscript{6} For if thou deal truly, thy doings shall prosperously succeed to thee, and to all them that live justly. \textsuperscript{7} Give alms of thy substance; and when thou givest alms, let not thine eye be envious, neither turn thy face from any poor, and the face of God shall not be turned away from thee.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} Bless the Lord thy God alway, and desire of him that thy ways may be directed, and that all thy paths and counsels may prosper: for every nation hath not counsel; but the Lord himself giveth all good things, and he humbleth whom he will, as he will; now therefore, my son, remember my commandments, neither let them be put out of thy mind.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} And now I signify this to thee, that I committed ten talents to Gabael the son of Gabrias at Rages in Media. \textsuperscript{21} And fear not, my son, that we are made poor: for thou hast much wealth, if thou fear God, and depart from all sin, and do that which is pleasing in his sight.\par
\subsection*{Tobit 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Tobias then answered and said, Father, I will do all things which thou hast commanded me: \textsuperscript{2} but how can I receive the money, seeing I know him not? \textsuperscript{3} Then he gave him the handwriting, and said unto him, Seek thee a man which may go with thee, and I will give him wages whiles I yet live: and go and receive the money.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Therefore when he went to seek a man, he found Raphael that was an angel. \textsuperscript{5} But he knew not; and he said unto him, Canst thou go with me to Rages? and knowest thou those places well? \textsuperscript{6} To whom the angel said, I will go with thee, and I know the way well: for I have lodged with our brother Gabael.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Then Tobias said unto him, Tarry for me, till I tell my father. \textsuperscript{8} Then he said unto him, Go, and tarry not. So he went in and said to his father, Behold, I have found one which will go with me. Then he said, Call him unto me, that I may know of what tribe he is, and whether he be a trusty man to go with thee. \textsuperscript{9} So he called him, and he came in, and they saluted one another.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} Then Tobit said unto him, Brother, shew me of what tribe and family thou art. \textsuperscript{11} To whom he said, Dost thou seek for a tribe or family, or an hired man to go with thy son? Then Tobit said unto him, I would know, brother, thy kindred and name.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} Then he said, I am Azarias, the son of Ananias the great, and of thy brethren. \textsuperscript{13} Then Tobit said, Thou art welcome, brother; be not now angry with me, because I have enquired to know thy tribe and thy family; for thou art my brother, of an honest and good stock: for I know Ananias and Jonathas, sons of that great Samaias, as we went together to Jerusalem to worship, and offered the firstborn, and the tenths of the fruits; and they were not seduced with the error of our brethren: my brother, thou art of a good stock. \textsuperscript{14} But tell me, what wages shall I give thee? wilt thou a drachm a day, and things necessary, as to mine own son? \textsuperscript{15} Yea, moreover, if ye return safe, I will add something to thy wages.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} So they were well pleased. Then said he to Tobias, Prepare thyself for the journey, and God send you a good journey. And when his son had prepared all things for the journey, his father said, Go thou with this man, and God, which dwelleth in heaven, prosper your journey, and the angel of God keep you company. So they went forth both, and the young man's dog with them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} But Anna his mother wept, and said to Tobit, Why hast thou sent away our son? is he not the staff of our hand, in going in and out before us? \textsuperscript{18} Be not greedy to add money to money: but let it be as refuse in respect of our child. \textsuperscript{19} For that which the Lord hath given us to live with doth suffice us. \textsuperscript{20} Then said Tobit to her, Take no care, my sister; he shall return in safety, and thine eyes shall see him. \textsuperscript{21} For the good angel will keep him company, and his journey shall be prosperous, and he shall return safe. \textsuperscript{22} Then she made an end of weeping.\par
\subsection*{Tobit 6}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And as they went on their journey, they came in the evening to the river Tigris, and they lodged there. \textsuperscript{2} And when the young man went down to wash himself, a fish leaped out of the river, and would have devoured him. \textsuperscript{3} Then the angel said unto him, Take the fish. And the young man laid hold of the fish, and drew it to land. \textsuperscript{4} To whom the angel said, Open the fish, and take the heart and the liver and the gall, and put them up safely. \textsuperscript{5} So the young man did as the angel commanded him; and when they had roasted the fish, they did eat it: then they both went on their way, till they drew near to Ecbatane.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} Then the young man said to the angel, Brother Azarias, to what use is the heart and the liver and the gall of the fish? \textsuperscript{7} And he said unto him, Touching the heart and the liver, if a devil or an evil spirit trouble any, we must make a smoke thereof before the man or the woman, and the party shall be no more vexed. \textsuperscript{8} As for the gall, it is good to anoint a man that hath whiteness in his eyes, and he shall be healed.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} And when they were come near to Rages, \textsuperscript{10} the angel said to the young man, Brother, to day we shall lodge with Raguel, who is thy cousin; he also hath one only daughter, named Sara; I will speak for her, that she may be given thee for a wife. \textsuperscript{11} For to thee doth the right of her appertain, seeing thou only art of her kindred. \textsuperscript{12} And the maid is fair and wise: now therefore hear me, and I will speak to her father; and when we return from Rages we will celebrate the marriage: for I know that Raguel cannot marry her to another according to the law of Moses, but he shall be guilty of death, because the right of inheritance doth rather appertain to thee than to any other.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Then the young man answered the angel, I have heard, brother Azarias, that this maid hath been given to seven men, who all died in the marriage chamber. \textsuperscript{14} And now I am the only son of my father, and I am afraid, lest, if I go in unto her, I die, as the others before: for a wicked spirit loveth her, which hurteth no one except those which come unto her: wherefore I also fear lest I die, and bring my father's and my mother's life because of me to the grave with sorrow: for they have no other son to bury them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} Then the angel said to him, Dost thou not remember the precepts that thy father gave thee, that thou shouldest marry a wife of thine own kindred? wherefore hear me, O my brother; for she shall be given thee to wife; and make thou no reckoning of the evil spirit; for this same night shall she be given thee in marriage. \textsuperscript{16} And when thou shalt come into the marriage chamber, thou shalt take the ashes of perfume, and shalt lay upon them some of the heart and liver of the fish, and shalt make a smoke with it: \textsuperscript{17} and the devil shall smell it, and flee away, and never come again any more: but when thou shalt come to her, rise up both of you, and pray to God which is merciful, who will have pity on you, and save you: fear not, for she is appointed unto thee from the beginning; and thou shalt preserve her, and she shall go with thee. Moreover I suppose that she shall bear thee children. Now when Tobias had heard these things, he loved her, and his heart was effectually joined to her. And he came to Ecbatane.\par
\subsection*{Tobit 7}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And he came to the house of Raguel; and Sara met him: and saluted him, and he them; and she brought them into the house. \textsuperscript{2} Then said Raguel to Edna his wife, How like is this young man to Tobit my cousin!\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} And Raguel asked them, From whence are ye, brethren? To whom they said, We are of the sons of Nephthali, which are captives in Nineve. \textsuperscript{4} Then he said to them, Do ye know Tobit our kinsman? And they said, We know him. Then said he, Is he in good health? \textsuperscript{5} And they said, He is both alive, and in good health: and Tobias said, He is my father. \textsuperscript{6} Then Raguel leaped up, and kissed him, and wept, \textsuperscript{7} and blessed him, and said unto him, Thou art the son of an honest and good man. But when he had heard that Tobit was blind, he was sorrowful, and wept.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} And likewise Edna his wife and Sara his daughter wept. Moreover they entertained them cheerfully; and after that they had killed a ram of the flock, they set store of meat on the table. Then said Tobias to Raphael, Brother Azarias, speak of those things of which thou didst talk in the way, and let this business be dispatched.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} So he communicated the matter with Raguel: and Raguel said to Tobias, Eat and drink, and make merry: \textsuperscript{10} for it is meet that thou shouldest marry my daughter: nevertheless I will declare unto thee the truth. \textsuperscript{11} I have given my daughter in marriage to seven men, who died that night they came in unto her: nevertheless for the present be merry. But Tobias said, I will eat nothing here, till we agree and swear one to another. \textsuperscript{12} And Raguel said, Then take her from henceforth according to the manner, for thou art her cousin, and she is thine, and the merciful God give you good success in all things.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Then he called his daughter Sara, and she came to her father, and he took her by the hand, and gave her to be wife to Tobias, saying, Behold, take her after the law of Moses, and lead her away to thy father. And he blessed them; \textsuperscript{14} and called Edna his wife, and took paper, and did write an instrument of covenants , and sealed it. \textsuperscript{15} Then they began to eat.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} After Raguel called his wife Edna, and said unto her, Sister, prepare another chamber, and bring her in thither. \textsuperscript{17} Which when she had done as he had bidden her, she brought her thither: and she wept, and she received the tears of her daughter, and said unto her, \textsuperscript{18} Be of good comfort, my daughter; the Lord of heaven and earth give thee joy for this thy sorrow: be of good comfort, my daughter.\par
\subsection*{Tobit 8}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And when they had supped, they brought Tobias in unto her. \textsuperscript{2} And as he went, he remembered the words of Raphael, and took the ashes of the perfumes, and put the heart and the liver of the fish thereupon, and made a smoke therewith . \textsuperscript{3} The which smell when the evil spirit had smelled, he fled into the utmost parts of Egypt, and the angel bound him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} And after that they were both shut in together, Tobias rose out of the bed, and said, Sister, arise, and let us pray that God would have pity on us. \textsuperscript{5} Then began Tobias to say, Blessed art thou, O God of our fathers, and blessed is thy holy and glorious name for ever; let the heavens bless thee, and all thy creatures. \textsuperscript{6} Thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: thou hast said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make unto him an aid like unto himself. \textsuperscript{7} And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust, but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together. \textsuperscript{8} And she said with him, Amen.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} So they slept both that night. And Raguel arose, and went and made a grave, \textsuperscript{10} saying, I fear lest he also be dead. \textsuperscript{11} But when Raguel was come into his house, \textsuperscript{12} he said unto his wife Edna, Send one of the maids, and let her see whether he be alive: if he be not, that we may bury him, and no man know it. \textsuperscript{13} So the maid opened the door, and went in, and found them both asleep, \textsuperscript{14} and came forth, and told them that he was alive.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} Then Raguel praised God, and said, O God, thou art worthy to be praised with all pure and holy praise: therefore let thy saints praise thee with all thy creatures: and let all thine angels and thine elect praise thee for ever. \textsuperscript{16} Thou art to be praised, for thou hast made me joyful; and that is not come to me which I suspected; but thou hast dealt with us according to thy great mercy. \textsuperscript{17} Thou art to be praised, because thou hast had mercy of two that were the only begotten children of their fathers: grant them mercy, O Lord, and finish their life in health with joy and mercy. \textsuperscript{18} Then Raguel bade his servants to fill the grave.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} And he kept the wedding feast fourteen days. \textsuperscript{20} For before the days of the marriage were finished, Raguel had said unto him by an oath, that he should not depart till the fourteen days of the marriage were expired; \textsuperscript{21} and then he should take the half of his goods, and go in safety to his father; and should have the rest when I and my wife be dead.\par
\subsection*{Tobit 9}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then Tobias called Raphael, and said unto him, \textsuperscript{2} Brother Azarias, take with thee a servant, and two camels, and go to Rages of Media to Gabael, and bring me the money, and bring him to the wedding. \textsuperscript{3} For Raguel hath sworn that I shall not depart. \textsuperscript{4} But my father counteth the days; and if I tarry long, he will be very sorry. \textsuperscript{5} So Raphael went out, and lodged with Gabael, and gave him the handwriting: who brought forth bags which were sealed up, and gave them to him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} And early in the morning they went forth both together, and came to the wedding: and Tobias blessed his wife.\par
\subsection*{Tobit 10}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now Tobit his father counted every day: and when the days of the journey were expired, and they came not, \textsuperscript{2} then Tobit said, Are they detained? or is Gabael dead, and there is no man to give him the money? \textsuperscript{3} Therefore he was very sorry. \textsuperscript{4} Then his wife said unto him, My son is dead, seeing he stayeth long; and she began to bewail him, and said, \textsuperscript{5} Now I care for nothing, my son, since I have let thee go, the light of mine eyes.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} To whom Tobit said, Hold thy peace, take no care, for he is safe. \textsuperscript{7} But she said, Hold thy peace, and deceive me not; my son is dead. And she went out every day into the way which they went, and did eat no meat in the daytime, and ceased not whole nights to bewail her son Tobias, until the fourteen days of the wedding were expired, which Raguel had sworn that he should spend there. Then Tobias said to Raguel, \textsuperscript{8} Let me go, for my father and my mother look no more to see me. \textsuperscript{9} But his father in law said unto him, Tarry with me, and I will send to thy father, and they shall declare unto him how things go with thee. \textsuperscript{10} But Tobias said, No; but let me go to my father.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Then Raguel arose, and gave him Sara his wife, and half his goods, servants, and cattle, and money: \textsuperscript{12} and he blessed them, and sent them away, saying, The God of heaven give you a prosperous journey, my children. \textsuperscript{13} And he said to his daughter, Honour thy father and thy mother in law, which are now thy parents, that I may hear good report of thee. And he kissed her. Edna also said to Tobias, The Lord of heaven restore thee, my dear brother, and grant that I may see thy children of my daughter Sara before I die, that I may rejoice before the Lord: behold, I commit my daughter unto thee, of special trust; wherefore do not entreat her evil.\par
\subsection*{Tobit 11}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} After these things Tobias went his way, praising God that he had given him a prosperous journey, and blessed Raguel and Edna his wife, and went on his way till they drew near unto Nineve.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} Then Raphael said to Tobias, Dost thou not know, brother, how thou didst leave thy father? \textsuperscript{3} let us haste before thy wife, and prepare the house; \textsuperscript{4} and take in thine hand the gall of the fish. So they went their way, and the dog went after them. \textsuperscript{5} Now Anna sat looking about toward the way for her son. \textsuperscript{6} And when she espied him coming, she said to his father, Behold, thy son cometh, and the man that went with him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Then said Raphael, I know, Tobias, that thy father will open his eyes. \textsuperscript{8} Therefore anoint thou his eyes with the gall, and being pricked therewith, he shall rub, and the whiteness shall fall away, and he shall see thee.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Then Anna ran forth, and fell upon the neck of her son, and said unto him, Seeing I have seen thee, my son, from henceforth I am content to die. And they wept both. \textsuperscript{10} Tobit also went forth toward the door, and stumbled: but his son ran unto him, \textsuperscript{11} and took hold of his father: and he strake of the gall on his father's eyes, saying, Be of good hope, my father. \textsuperscript{12} And when his eyes began to smart, he rubbed them; \textsuperscript{13} and the whiteness pilled away from the corners of his eyes: and when he saw his son, he fell upon his neck.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} And he wept, and said, Blessed art thou, O God, and blessed is thy name for ever; and blessed are all thine holy angels: \textsuperscript{15} for thou hast scourged, and hast taken pity on me : for, behold, I see my son Tobias. And his son went in rejoicing, and told his father the great things that had happened to him in Media.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} Then Tobit went out to meet his daughter in law at the gate of Nineve, rejoicing, and praising God: and they which saw him go marvelled, because he had received his sight. \textsuperscript{17} But Tobit gave thanks before them, because God had mercy on him. And when he came near to Sara his daughter in law, he blessed her, saying, Thou art welcome, daughter: God be blessed, which hath brought thee unto us, and blessed be thy father and thy mother. And there was joy among all his brethren which were at Nineve. \textsuperscript{18} And Achiacharus, and Nasbas his brother's son, came: \textsuperscript{19} and Tobias' wedding was kept seven days with great joy.\par
\subsection*{Tobit 12}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then Tobit called his son Tobias, and said unto him, My son, see that the man have his wages, which went with thee, and thou must give him more. \textsuperscript{2} And Tobias said unto him, O father, it is no harm to me to give him half of those things which I have brought: \textsuperscript{3} for he hath brought me again to thee in safety, and made whole my wife, and brought me the money, and likewise healed thee.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Then the old man said, It is due unto him. \textsuperscript{5} So he called the angel, and he said unto him, Take half of all that ye have brought, and go away in safety. \textsuperscript{6} Then he took them both apart, and said unto them, Bless God, praise him, and magnify him, and praise him for the things which he hath done unto you in the sight of all that live. It is good to praise God, and exalt his name, and honourably to shew forth the works of God; therefore be not slack to praise him. \textsuperscript{7} It is good to keep close the secret of a king, but it is honourable to reveal the works of God. Do that which is good, and no evil shall touch you. \textsuperscript{8} Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold: \textsuperscript{9} for alms doth deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life: \textsuperscript{10} but they that sin are enemies to their own life.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Surely I will keep close nothing from you. For I said, It was good to keep close the secret of a king, but that it was honourable to reveal the works of God. \textsuperscript{12} Now therefore, when thou didst pray, and Sara thy daughter in law, I did bring the remembrance of your prayers before the Holy One: and when thou didst bury the dead, I was with thee likewise. \textsuperscript{13} And when thou didst not delay to rise up, and leave thy dinner, to go and cover the dead, thy good deed was not hid from me: but I was with thee. \textsuperscript{14} And now God hath sent me to heal thee and Sara thy daughter in law. \textsuperscript{15} I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} Then they were both troubled, and fell upon their faces: for they feared. \textsuperscript{17} But he said unto them, Fear not, for it shall go well with you; praise God therefore. \textsuperscript{18} For not of any favour of mine, but by the will of our God I came; wherefore praise him for ever. \textsuperscript{19} All these days I did appear unto you; but I did neither eat nor drink, but ye did see a vision. \textsuperscript{20} Now therefore give God thanks: for I go up to him that sent me; but write all things which are done in a book. \textsuperscript{21} And when they arose, they saw him no more. \textsuperscript{22} Then they confessed the great and wonderful works of God, and how the angel of the Lord had appeared unto them.\par
\subsection*{Tobit 13}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then Tobit wrote a prayer of rejoicing, and said,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} For he doth scourge, and hath mercy: he leadeth down to hell, and bringeth up again: neither is there any that can avoid his hand. \textsuperscript{3} Confess him before the Gentiles, ye children of Israel: for he hath scattered us among them. \textsuperscript{4} There declare his greatness, and extol him before all the living: for he is our Lord, and he is the God our Father for ever. \textsuperscript{5} And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he hath scattered us.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} If ye turn to him with your whole heart, and with your whole mind, and deal uprightly before him, then will he turn unto you, and will not hide his face from you. Therefore see what he will do with you, and confess him with your whole mouth, and praise the Lord of might, and extol the everlasting King. In the land of my captivity do I praise him, and declare his might and majesty to a sinful nation. O ye sinners, turn and do justice before him: who can tell if he will accept you, and have mercy on you?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} I will extol my God, and my soul shall praise the King of heaven, and shall rejoice in his greatness.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Many nations shall come from far to the name of the Lord God with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise thee with great joy. \textsuperscript{12} Cursed are all they which hate thee, and blessed shall all be which love thee for ever. \textsuperscript{13} Rejoice and be glad for the children of the just: for they shall be gathered together, and shall bless the Lord of the just. \textsuperscript{14} O blessed are they which love thee, for they shall rejoice in thy peace: blessed are they which have been sorrowful for all thy scourges; for they shall rejoice for thee, when they have seen all thy glory, and shall be glad for ever.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} Let my soul bless God the great King. \textsuperscript{16} For Jerusalem shall be built up with sapphire, and emerald, and precious stone: thy walls and towers and battlements with pure gold. \textsuperscript{17} And the streets of Jerusalem shall be paved with beryl and carbuncle and stone of Ophir. \textsuperscript{18} And all her streets shall say, Alleluia; and they shall praise him, saying, Blessed be God, which hath extolled it for ever.\par
\subsection*{Tobit 14}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} So Tobit made an end of praising God. \textsuperscript{2} And he was eight and fifty years old when he lost his sight, which was restored to him after eight years: and he gave alms, and he increased in the fear of the Lord God, and praised him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} And when he was very aged, he called his son, and the sons of his son, and said to him, My son, take thy children; for, behold, I am aged, and am ready to depart out of this life. \textsuperscript{4} Go into Media, my son, for I surely believe those things which Jonas the prophet spake of Nineve, that it shall be overthrown; and that for a time peace shall rather be in Media; and that our brethren shall lie scattered in the earth from that good land: and Jerusalem shall be desolate, and the house of God in it shall be burned, and shall be desolate for a time; \textsuperscript{5} and that again God will have mercy on them, and bring them again into the land, where they shall build a temple, but not like to the first, until the time of that age be fulfilled; and afterward they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Jerusalem gloriously, and the house of God shall be built in it with a glorious building, as the prophets have spoken thereof.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} And all nations shall turn, and fear the Lord God truly, and shall bury their idols. \textsuperscript{7} So shall all nations praise the Lord, and his people shall confess God, and the Lord shall exalt his people; and all those which love the Lord God in truth and justice shall rejoice, shewing mercy to our brethren.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} And now, my son, depart out of Nineve, because that those things which the prophet Jonas spake shall surely come to pass. \textsuperscript{9} But keep thou the law and the commandments, and shew thyself merciful and just, that it may go well with thee. \textsuperscript{10} And bury me decently, and thy mother with me; but tarry no longer at Nineve. Remember, my son, how Aman handled Achiacharus that brought him up, how out of light he brought him into darkness, and how he rewarded him again: yet Achiacharus was saved, but the other had his reward: for he went down into darkness. Manasses gave alms, and escaped the snares of death which they had set for him: but Aman fell into the snare, and perished.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Wherefore now, my son, consider what alms doeth, and how righteousness doth deliver. When he had said these things, he gave up the ghost in the bed, being an hundred and eight and fifty years old; and he buried him honourably. \textsuperscript{12} And when Anna his mother was dead, he buried her with his father.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} where he became old with honour; and he buried his father and mother in law honourably, and he inherited their substance, and his father Tobit's. \textsuperscript{14} And he died at Ecbatane in Media, being an hundred and seven and twenty years old. \textsuperscript{15} But before he died he heard of the destruction of Nineve, which was taken by Nabuchodonosor and Assuerus: and before his death he rejoiced over Nineve.\par
\section*{Judith}
\subsection*{Judith 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} In the twelfth year of the reign of Nabuchodonosor, who reigned in Nineve, the great city; in the days of Arphaxad, which reigned over the Medes in Ecbatane, \textsuperscript{2} and built in Ecbatane walls round about of stones hewn three cubits broad and six cubits long, and made the height of the wall seventy cubits, and the breadth thereof fifty cubits: \textsuperscript{3} and set the towers thereof upon the gates of it, an hundred cubits high , and the breadth thereof in the foundation threescore cubits: \textsuperscript{4} and he made the gates thereof, even gates that were raised to the height of seventy cubits, and the breadth of them was forty cubits, for the going forth of his mighty armies, and for the setting in array of his footmen:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Even in those days king Nabuchodonosor made war with king Arphaxad in the great plain, which is the plain in the borders of Ragau. \textsuperscript{6} And there came unto him all they that dwelt in the hill country, and all that dwelt by Euphrates, and Tigris, and Hydaspes, and the plain of Arioch the king of the Elymeans, and very many nations of the sons of Cheleul, assembled themselves to the battle.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Then Nabuchodonosor king of the Assyrians sent unto all that dwelt in Persia, and to all that dwelt westward, and to those that dwelt in Cilicia, and Damascus, and Libanus, and Antilibanus, and to all that dwelt upon the sea coast, \textsuperscript{8} and to those among the nations that were of Carmel, and Galaad, and the higher Galilee, and the great plain of Esdrelom, \textsuperscript{9} and to all that were in Samaria and the cities thereof, and beyond Jordan unto Jerusalem, and Betane, and Chellus, and Kades, and the river of Egypt, and Taphnes, and Ramesse, and all the land of Gesem, \textsuperscript{10} until ye come beyond Tanis and Memphis, and to all the inhabitants of Egypt, until ye come to the borders of Ethiopia.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} But all the inhabitants of the land made light of the commandment of Nabuchodonosor king of the Assyrians, neither went they with him to the battle; for they were not afraid of him: yea, he was before them as one man, and they sent away his ambassadors from them without effect, and with disgrace. \textsuperscript{12} Therefore Nabuchodonosor was very angry with all this country, and sware by his throne and kingdom, that he would surely be avenged upon all those coasts of Cilicia, and Damascus, and Syria, and that he would slay with the sword all the inhabitants of the land of Moab, and the children of Ammon, and all Judea, and all that were in Egypt, till ye come to the borders of the two seas.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Then he marched in battle array with his power against king Arphaxad in the seventeenth year, and he prevailed in his battle: for he overthrew all the power of Arphaxad, and all his horsemen, and all his chariots, \textsuperscript{14} and became lord of his cities, and came unto Ecbatane, and took the towers, and spoiled the streets thereof, and turned the beauty thereof into shame. \textsuperscript{15} He took also Arphaxad in the mountains of Ragau, and smote him through with his darts, and destroyed him utterly that day.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} So he returned afterward to Nineve , both he and all his company of sundry nations, being a very great multitude of men of war, and there he took his ease, and banqueted, both he and his army, an hundred and twenty days.\par
\subsection*{Judith 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And in the eighteenth year, the two and twentieth day of the first month, there was talk in the house of Nabuchodonosor king of the Assyrians, that he should, as he said, avenge himself on all the earth. \textsuperscript{2} So he called unto him all his officers, and all his nobles, and communicated with them his secret counsel, and concluded the afflicting of the whole earth out of his own mouth. \textsuperscript{3} Then they decreed to destroy all flesh, that did not obey the commandment of his mouth.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} And when he had ended his counsel, Nabuchodonosor king of the Assyrians called Holofernes the chief captain of his army, which was next unto him, and said unto him, \textsuperscript{5} Thus saith the great king, the lord of the whole earth, Behold, thou shalt go forth from my presence, and take with thee men that trust in their own strength, of footmen an hundred and twenty thousand; and the number of horses with their riders twelve thousand. \textsuperscript{6} And thou shalt go against all the west country, because they disobeyed my commandment: \textsuperscript{7} and thou shalt declare unto them, that they prepare for me earth and water: for I will go forth in my wrath against them, and will cover the whole face of the earth with the feet of mine army, and I will give them for a spoil unto them: \textsuperscript{8} so that their slain shall fill their valleys and brooks, and the river shall be filled with their dead, till it overflow: \textsuperscript{9} and I will lead them captives to the utmost parts of all the earth. \textsuperscript{10} Thou therefore shalt go forth, and take beforehand for me all their coasts: and if they will yield themselves unto thee, thou shalt reserve them for me till the day of their punishment.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} But concerning them that rebel, let not thine eye spare them; but put them to the slaughter, and spoil them wheresoever thou goest. \textsuperscript{12} For as I live, and by the power of my kingdom, whatsoever I have spoken, that will I do by mine hand. \textsuperscript{13} And take thou heed that thou transgress none of the commandments of thy lord, but accomplish them fully, as I have commanded thee, and defer not to do them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} Then Holofernes went forth from the presence of his lord, and called all the governors and captains, and the officers of the army of Assur; \textsuperscript{15} and he mustered the chosen men for the battle, as his lord had commanded him, unto an hundred and twenty thousand, and twelve thousand archers on horseback; \textsuperscript{16} and he ranged them, as a great army is ordered for the war. \textsuperscript{17} And he took camels and asses for their carriages, a very great number; and sheep and oxen and goats without number for their provision: \textsuperscript{18} and plenty of victual for every man of the army, and very much gold and silver out of the king's house.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} Then he went forth and all his power to go before king Nabuchodonosor in the voyage, and to cover all the face of the earth westward with their chariots, and horsemen and their chosen footmen. \textsuperscript{20} A great number also of sundry countries came with them like locusts, and like the sand of the earth: for the multitude was without number.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} And they went forth of Nineve three days' journey toward the plain of Bectileth, and pitched from Bectileth near the mountain which is at the left hand of the upper Cilicia. \textsuperscript{22} Then he took all his army, his footmen, and horsemen, and chariots, and went from thence into the hill country; \textsuperscript{23} and destroyed Phud and Lud, and spoiled all the children of Rasses, and the children of Ismael, which were toward the wilderness at the south of the land of the Chellians.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} Then he went over Euphrates, and went through Mesopotamia, and destroyed all the high cities that were upon the river Arbonai, till ye come to the sea.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} And he took the borders of Cilicia, and killed all that resisted him, and came to the borders of Japheth, which were toward the south, over against Arabia.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{26} He compassed also all the children of Madian, and burned up their tabernacles, and spoiled their sheepcotes.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} Then he went down into the plain of Damascus in the time of wheat harvest, and burnt up all their fields, and destroyed their flocks and herds, also he spoiled their cities, and utterly wasted their countries, and smote all their young men with the edge of the sword.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} Therefore the fear and dread of him fell upon all the inhabitants of the sea coasts, which were in Sidon and Tyrus, and them that dwelt in Sur and Ocina, and all that dwelt in Jemnaan; and they that dwelt in Azotus and Ascalon feared him greatly.\par
\subsection*{Judith 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} So they sent ambassadors unto him to treat of peace, saying, \textsuperscript{2} Behold, we the servants of Nabuchodonosor the great king lie before thee; use us as shall be good in thy sight. \textsuperscript{3} Behold, our houses, and all our places, and all our fields of wheat, and flocks, and herds, and all the lodges of our tents, lie before thy face; use them as it pleaseth thee. \textsuperscript{4} Behold, even our cities and the inhabitants thereof are thy servants; come and deal with them as seemeth good unto thee.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} So the men came to Holofernes, and declared unto him after this manner. \textsuperscript{6} Then came he down toward the sea coast, both he and his army, and set garrisons in the high cities, and took out of them chosen men for aid. \textsuperscript{7} So they and all the country round about received him with garlands, with dances, and with timbrels. \textsuperscript{8} Yet he did cast down their frontiers, and cut down their groves: for he had decreed to destroy all the gods of the land, that all nations should worship Nabuchodonosor only, and that all tongues and tribes should call upon him as a god.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Also he came over against Esdraelon near unto Judea, over against the great strait of Judea. \textsuperscript{10} And he pitched between Geba and Scythopolis, and there he tarried a whole month, that he might gather together all the carriages of his army.\par
\subsection*{Judith 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now the children of Israel, that dwelt in Judea, heard all that Holofernes the chief captain of Nabuchodonosor king of the Assyrians had done to the nations, and after what manner he had spoiled all their temples, and brought them to nought. \textsuperscript{2} Therefore they were exceedingly afraid of him, and were troubled for Jerusalem, and for the temple of the Lord their God: \textsuperscript{3} for they were newly returned from the captivity, and all the people of Judea were lately gathered together: and the vessels, and the altar, and the house, were sanctified after the profanation. \textsuperscript{4} Therefore they sent into all the coasts of Samaria, and the villages, and to Bethoron, and Belmen, and Jericho, and to Choba, and Esora, and to the valley of Salem: \textsuperscript{5} and possessed themselves beforehand of all the tops of the high mountains, and fortified the villages that were in them, and laid up victuals for the provision of war: for their fields were of late reaped.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} Also Joacim the high priest, which was in those days in Jerusalem, wrote to them that dwelt in Bethulia, and Betomestham, which is over against Esdraelon toward the open country, near to Dothaim, \textsuperscript{7} charging them to keep the passages of the hill country: for by them there was an entrance into Judea, and it was easy to stop them that would come up, because the passage was strait, for two men at the most. \textsuperscript{8} And the children of Israel did as Joacim the high priest had commanded them, with the ancients of all the people of Israel, which dwelt at Jerusalem.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Then every man of Israel cried to God with great fervency, and with great vehemency did they humble their souls: \textsuperscript{10} both they, and their wives, and their children, and their cattle, and every stranger and hireling, and their servants bought with money, put sackcloth upon their loins.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Thus every man and woman, and the little children, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, fell before the temple, and cast ashes upon their heads, and spread out their sackcloth before the face of the Lord: also they put sackcloth about the altar, \textsuperscript{12} and cried to the God of Israel all with one consent earnestly, that he would not give their children for a prey, and their wives for a spoil, and the cities of their inheritance to destruction, and the sanctuary to profanation and reproach, and for the nations to rejoice at.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} So God heard their prayers, and looked upon their afflictions: for the people fasted many days in all Judea and Jerusalem before the sanctuary of the Lord Almighty.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} And Joacim the high priest, and all the priests that stood before the Lord, and they which ministered unto the Lord, had their loins girt with sackcloth, and offered the daily burnt offerings, with the vows and free gifts of the people, \textsuperscript{15} and had ashes on their mitres, and cried unto the Lord with all their power, that he would look upon all the house of Israel graciously.\par
\subsection*{Judith 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then was it declared to Holofernes, the chief captain of the army of Assur, that the children of Israel had prepared for war, and had shut up the passages of the hill country, and had fortified all the tops of the high hills, and had laid impediments in the champaign countries: \textsuperscript{2} wherewith he was very angry, and called all the princes of Moab, and the captains of Ammon, and all the governors of the sea coast, \textsuperscript{3} and he said unto them, Tell me now, ye sons of Chanaan, who this people is, that dwelleth in the hill country, and what are the cities that they inhabit, and what is the multitude of their army, and wherein is their power and strength, and what king is set over them, or captain of their army; \textsuperscript{4} and why have they determined not to come and meet me, more than all the inhabitants of the west?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Then said Achior, the captain of all the sons of Ammon, Let my lord now hear a word from the mouth of thy servant, and I will declare unto thee the truth concerning this people, which dwelleth near thee, and inhabiteth the hill countries: and there shall no lie come out of the mouth of thy servant. \textsuperscript{6} This people are descended of the Chaldeans: \textsuperscript{7} and they sojourned heretofore in Mesopotamia, because they would not follow the gods of their fathers, which were in the land of Chaldea. \textsuperscript{8} For they left the way of their ancestors, and worshipped the God of heaven, the God whom they knew: so they cast them out from the face of their gods, and they fled into Mesopotamia, and sojourned there many days.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Then their God commanded them to depart from the place where they sojourned, and to go into the land of Chanaan: where they dwelt, and were increased with gold and silver, and with very much cattle. \textsuperscript{10} But when a famine covered all the land of Chanaan, they went down into Egypt, and sojourned there, while they were nourished, and became there a great multitude, so that one could not number their nation. \textsuperscript{11} Therefore the king of Egypt rose up against them, and dealt subtilly with them, and brought them low with labouring in brick, and made them slaves.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} Then they cried unto their God, and he smote all the land of Egypt with incurable plagues: so the Egyptians cast them out of their sight. \textsuperscript{13} And God dried the Red sea before them, \textsuperscript{14} and brought them to mount Sina, and Cades-Barne, and cast forth all that dwelt in the wilderness.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} So they dwelt in the land of the Amorites, and they destroyed by their strength all them of Esebon, and passing over Jordan they possessed all the hill country. \textsuperscript{16} And they cast forth before them the Chanaanite, the Pherezite, the Jebusite, and the Sychemite, and all the Gergesites, and they dwelt in that country many days.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} And whilst they sinned not before their God, they prospered, because the God that hateth iniquity was with them. \textsuperscript{18} But when they departed from the way which he appointed them, they were destroyed in many battles very sore, and were led captives into a land that was not their's, and the temple of their God was cast to the ground, and their cities were taken by the enemies.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} But now are they returned to their God, and are come up from the places where they were scattered, and have possessed Jerusalem, where their sanctuary is, and are seated in the hill country; for it was desolate. \textsuperscript{20} Now therefore, my lord and governor, if there be any error in this people, and they sin against their God, let us consider that this shall be their ruin, and let us go up, and we shall overcome them. \textsuperscript{21} But if there be no iniquity in their nation, let my lord now pass by, lest their Lord defend them, and their God be for them, and we become a reproach before all the world.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} And when Achior had finished these sayings, all the people standing round about the tent murmured, and the chief men of Holofernes, and all that dwelt by the sea side, and in Moab, spake that he should kill him. \textsuperscript{23} For, say they , we will not be afraid of the face of the children of Israel: for, lo, it is a people that have no strength nor power for a strong battle.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} Now therefore, lord Holofernes, we will go up, and they shall be a prey to be devoured of all thine army.\par
\subsection*{Judith 6}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And when the tumult of men that were about the council was ceased, Holofernes the chief captain of the army of Assur said unto Achior and all the Moabites before all the company of other nations, \textsuperscript{2} And who art thou, Achior, and the hirelings of Ephraim, that thou hast prophesied among us as to day, and hast said, that we should not make war with the people of Israel, because their God will defend them? and who is God but Nabuchodonosor? \textsuperscript{3} He will send his power, and will destroy them from the face of the earth, and their God shall not deliver them: but we his servants will destroy them as one man; for they are not able to sustain the power of our horses. \textsuperscript{4} For with them we will tread them under foot, and their mountains shall be drunken with their blood, and their fields shall be filled with their dead bodies, and their footsteps shall not be able to stand before us, for they shall utterly perish, saith king Nabuchodonosor, lord of all the earth: for he said, None of my words shall be in vain.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} And thou, Achior, an hireling of Ammon, which hast spoken these words in the day of thine iniquity, shalt see my face no more from this day, until I take vengeance of this nation that came out of Egypt. \textsuperscript{6} And then shall the sword of mine army, and the multitude of them that serve me, pass through thy sides, and thou shalt fall among their slain, when I return. \textsuperscript{7} Now therefore my servants shall bring thee back into the hill country, and shall set thee in one of the cities of the passages: \textsuperscript{8} and thou shalt not perish, till thou be destroyed with them. \textsuperscript{9} And if thou persuade thyself in thy mind that they shall not be taken, let not thy countenance fall: I have spoken it, and none of my words shall be in vain.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} Then Holofernes commanded his servants, that waited in his tent, to take Achior, and bring him to Bethulia, and deliver him into the hands of the children of Israel. \textsuperscript{11} So his servants took him, and brought him out of the camp into the plain, and they went from the midst of the plain into the hill country, and came unto the fountains that were under Bethulia. \textsuperscript{12} And when the men of the city saw them, they took up their weapons, and went out of the city to the top of the hill: and every man that used a sling kept them from coming up by casting of stones against them. \textsuperscript{13} Nevertheless having gotten privily under the hill, they bound Achior, and cast him down, and left him at the foot of the hill, and returned to their lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} But the Israelites descended from their city, and came unto him, and loosed him, and brought him into Bethulia, and presented him to the governors of the city: \textsuperscript{15} which were in those days Ozias the son of Micha, of the tribe of Simeon, and Chabris the son of Gothoniel, and Charmis the son of Melchiel.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} And they called together all the ancients of the city, and all their youth ran together, and their women, to the assembly, and they set Achior in the midst of all their people. Then Ozias asked him of that which was done. \textsuperscript{17} And he answered and declared unto them the words of the council of Holofernes, and all the words that he had spoken in the midst of the princes of Assur, and whatsoever Holofernes had spoken proudly against the house of Israel.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Then the people fell down and worshipped God, and cried unto God, saying, \textsuperscript{19} O Lord God of heaven, behold their pride, and pity the low estate of our nation, and look upon the face of those that are sanctified unto thee this day.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} And they comforted Achior, and praised him greatly. \textsuperscript{21} And Ozias took him out of the assembly unto his house, and made a feast to the elders; and they called on the God of Israel all that night for help.\par
\subsection*{Judith 7}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} The next day Holofernes commanded all his army, and all his people which were come to take his part, that they should remove their camp against Bethulia, to take aforehand the ascents of the hill country, and to make war against the children of Israel. \textsuperscript{2} Then their strong men removed their camps in that day, and the army of the men of war was an hundred and seventy thousand footmen, and twelve thousand horsemen, beside the baggage, and other men that were afoot among them, a very great multitude. \textsuperscript{3} And they camped in the valley near unto Bethulia, by the fountain, and they spread themselves in breadth over Dothaim even to Belthem, and in length from Bethulia unto Cyamon, which is over against Esdraelom.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Now the children of Israel, when they saw the multitude of them, were greatly troubled, and said every one to his neighbour, Now will these men lick up the face of the earth; for neither the high mountains, nor the valleys, nor the hills, are able to bear their weight. \textsuperscript{5} Then every man took up his weapons of war, and when they had kindled fires upon their towers, they remained and watched all that night. \textsuperscript{6} But in the second day Holofernes brought forth all his horsemen in the sight of the children of Israel which were in Bethulia, \textsuperscript{7} and viewed the passages up to the city, and came to the fountains of their waters, and took them, and set garrisons of men of war over them, and he himself removed toward his people.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} Then came unto him all the chief of the children of Esau, and all the governors of the people of Moab, and the captains of the sea coast, and said, \textsuperscript{9} Let our lord now hear a word, that there be not an overthrow in thine army. \textsuperscript{10} For this people of the children of Israel do not trust in their spears, but in the height of the mountains wherein they dwell, because it is not easy to come up to the tops of their mountains.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Now therefore, my lord, fight not against them in battle array, and there shall not so much as one man of thy people perish. \textsuperscript{12} Remain in thy camp, and keep all the men of thine army, and let thy servants get into their hands the fountain of water, which issueth forth of the foot of the mountain: \textsuperscript{13} for all the inhabitants of Bethulia have their water thence; so shall thirst kill them, and they shall give up their city, and we and our people shall go up to the tops of the mountains that are near, and will camp upon them, to watch that none go out of the city. \textsuperscript{14} So they and their wives and their children shall be consumed with famine, and before the sword come against them, they shall be overthrown in the streets where they dwell. \textsuperscript{15} Thus shalt thou render them an evil reward; because they rebelled, and met not thy person peaceably.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} And these words pleased Holofernes and all his servants, and he appointed to do as they had spoken. \textsuperscript{17} So the camp of the children of Ammon departed, and with them five thousand of the Assyrians, and they pitched in the valley, and took the waters, and the fountains of the waters of the children of Israel.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Then the children of Esau went up with the children of Ammon, and camped in the hill country over against Dothaim: and they sent some of them toward the south, and toward the east, over against Ekrebel, which is near unto Chusi, that is upon the brook Mochmur; and the rest of the army of the Assyrians camped in the plain, and covered the face of the whole land; and their tents and carriages were pitched to a very great multitude.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} Then the children of Israel cried unto the Lord their God, because their heart failed, for all their enemies had compassed them round about, and there was no way to escape out from among them. \textsuperscript{20} Thus all the company of Assur remained about them, both their footmen, chariots, and horsemen, four and thirty days, so that all their vessels of water failed all the inhabitants of Bethulia. \textsuperscript{21} And the cisterns were emptied, and they had not water to drink their fill for one day; for they gave them drink by measure. \textsuperscript{22} Therefore their young children were out of heart, and their women and young men fainted for thirst, and fell down in the streets of the city, and by the passages of the gates, and there was no longer any strength in them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} Then all the people assembled to Ozias, and to the chief of the city, both young men, and women, and children, and cried with a loud voice, and said before all the elders, \textsuperscript{24} God be judge between us and you: for ye have done us great injury, in that ye have not required peace of the children of Assur. \textsuperscript{25} For now we have no helper: but God hath sold us into their hands, that we should be thrown down before them with thirst and great destruction.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{26} Now therefore call them unto you, and deliver the whole city for a spoil to the people of Holofernes, and to all his army. \textsuperscript{27} For it is better for us to be made a spoil unto them, than to die for thirst: for we will be his servants, that our souls may live, and not see the death of our infants before our eyes, nor our wives nor our children to die. \textsuperscript{28} We take to witness against you the heaven and the earth, and our God and Lord of our fathers, which punisheth us according to our sins and the sins of our fathers, that he do not according as we have said this day. \textsuperscript{29} Then there was great weeping with one consent in the midst of the assembly; and they cried unto the Lord God with a loud voice.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} Then said Ozias to them, Brethren, be of good courage, let us yet endure five days, in the which space the Lord our God may turn his mercy toward us; for he will not forsake us utterly. \textsuperscript{31} And if these days pass, and there come no help unto us, I will do according to your word. \textsuperscript{32} And he dispersed the people, every one to their own charge; and they went unto the walls and towers of their city, and sent the women and children into their houses; and they were brought very low in the city.\par
\subsection*{Judith 8}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now at that time Judith heard thereof, which was the daughter of Merari, the son of Ox, the son of Joseph, the son of Oziel, the son of Elcia, the son of Eliu, the son of Chelcias, the son of Eliab, the son of Nathanael, the son of Salamiel, the son of Sarasadai, the son of Israel.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} And Manasses was her husband, of her tribe and kindred, who died in the barley harvest. \textsuperscript{3} For as he stood overseeing them that bound sheaves in the field, the heat came upon his head, and he fell on his bed, and died in his city of Bethulia: and they buried him with his fathers in the field between Dothaim and Balamo.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} So Judith was a widow in her house three years and four months. \textsuperscript{5} And she made her a tent upon the top of her house, and put on sackcloth upon her loins, and ware her widow's apparel. \textsuperscript{6} And she fasted all the days of her widowhood, save the eves of the sabbaths, and the sabbaths, and the eves of the new moons, and the new moons, and the feasts and solemn days of the house of Israel. \textsuperscript{7} She was also of a goodly countenance, and very beautiful to behold: and her husband Manasses had left her gold, and silver, and menservants, and maidservants, and cattle, and lands; and she remained upon them. \textsuperscript{8} And there was none that gave her an ill word; for she feared God greatly.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Now when she heard the evil words of the people against the governor, that they fainted for lack of water; for Judith had heard all the words that Ozias had spoken unto them, and that he had sworn to deliver the city unto the Assyrians after five days; \textsuperscript{10} then she sent her waiting-woman, that had the government of all things that she had, to call Ozias and Chabris and Charmis, the ancients of the city. \textsuperscript{11} And they came unto her, and she said unto them, Hear me now, O ye governors of the inhabitants of Bethulia: for your words that ye have spoken before the people this day are not right, touching this oath which ye made and pronounced between God and you, and have promised to deliver the city to our enemies, unless within these days the Lord turn to help you. \textsuperscript{12} And now who are ye that have tempted God this day, and stand instead of God among the children of men?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} And now try the Lord Almighty, but ye shall never know any thing. \textsuperscript{14} For ye cannot find the depth of the heart of man, neither can ye perceive the things that he thinketh: then how can ye search out God, that hath made all these things, and know his mind, or comprehend his purpose? Nay, my brethren, provoke not the Lord our God to anger. \textsuperscript{15} For if he will not help us within these five days, he hath power to defend us when he will, even every day, or to destroy us before our enemies.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} Do not bind the counsels of the Lord our God: for God is not as man, that he may be threatened; neither is he as the son of man, that he should be wavering. \textsuperscript{17} Therefore let us wait for salvation of him, and call upon him to help us, and he will hear our voice, if it please him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} For there arose none in our age, neither is there any now in these days, neither tribe, nor family, nor people, nor city, among us, which worship gods made with hands, as hath been aforetime. \textsuperscript{19} For the which cause our fathers were given to the sword, and for a spoil, and had a great fall before our enemies. \textsuperscript{20} But we know none other God, therefore we trust that he will not despise us, nor any of our nation.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} For if we be taken so, all Judea shall lie waste, and our sanctuary shall be spoiled; and he will require the profanation thereof at our mouth. \textsuperscript{22} And the slaughter of our brethren, and the captivity of the country, and the desolation of our inheritance, will he turn upon our heads among the Gentiles, wheresoever we shall be in bondage; and we shall be an offence and a reproach to all them that possess us. \textsuperscript{23} For our servitude shall not be directed to favour; but the Lord our God shall turn it to dishonour.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} Now therefore, O brethren, let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us, and the sanctuary, and the house, and the altar, rest upon us.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} Moreover let us give thanks to the Lord our God, which trieth us, even as he did our fathers. \textsuperscript{26} Remember what things he did to Abraham, and how he tried Isaac, and what happened to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria, when he kept the sheep of Laban his mother's brother. \textsuperscript{27} For he hath not tried us in the fire, as he did them, for the examination of their hearts, neither hath he taken vengeance on us: but the Lord doth scourge them that come near unto him, to admonish them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} Then said Ozias to her, All that thou hast spoken hast thou spoken with a good heart, and there is none that may gainsay thy words. \textsuperscript{29} For this is not the first day wherein thy wisdom is manifested; but from the beginning of thy days all the people have known thy understanding, because the disposition of thine heart is good. \textsuperscript{30} But the people were very thirsty, and compelled us to do unto them as we have spoken, and to bring an oath upon ourselves, which we will not break. \textsuperscript{31} Therefore now pray thou for us, because thou art a godly woman, and the Lord will send us rain to fill our cisterns, and we shall faint no more.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{32} Then said Judith unto them, Hear me, and I will do a thing, which shall go throughout all generations to the children of our nation. \textsuperscript{33} Ye shall stand this night in the gate, and I will go forth with my waitingwoman: and within the days that ye have promised to deliver the city to our enemies the Lord will visit Israel by mine hand. \textsuperscript{34} But enquire not ye of mine act: for I will not declare it unto you, till the things be finished that I do.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{35} Then said Ozias and the princes unto her, Go in peace, and the Lord God be before thee, to take vengeance on our enemies. \textsuperscript{36} So they returned from the tent, and went to their wards.\par
\subsection*{Judith 9}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then Judith fell upon her face, and put ashes upon her head, and uncovered the sackcloth wherewith she was clothed; and about the time that the incense of that evening was offered in Jerusalem in the house of the Lord, Judith cried with a loud voice, and said, \textsuperscript{2} O Lord God of my father Simeon, to whom thou gavest a sword to take vengeance of the strangers, who loosened the girdle of a maid to defile her, and discovered the thigh to her shame, and polluted her virginity to her reproach; for thou saidst, It shall not be so; and yet they did so: \textsuperscript{3} wherefore thou gavest their rulers to be slain, so that they dyed their bed in blood, being deceived, and smotest the servants with their lords, and the lords upon their thrones; \textsuperscript{4} and hast given their wives for a prey, and their daughters to be captives, and all their spoils to be divided among thy dear children; which were moved with thy zeal, and abhorred the pollution of their blood, and called upon thee for aid: O God, O my God, hear me also a widow.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} For thou hast wrought not only those things, but also the things which fell out before, and which ensued after; thou hast thought upon the things which are now, and which are to come. \textsuperscript{6} Yea, what things thou didst determine were ready at hand, and said, Lo, we are here: for all thy ways are prepared, and thy judgments are in thy foreknowledge.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} For, behold, the Assyrians are multiplied in their power; they are exalted with horse and man; they glory in the strength of their footmen; they trust in shield, and spear, and bow, and sling; and know not that thou art the Lord that breakest the battles: the Lord is thy name. \textsuperscript{8} Throw down their strength in thy power, and bring down their force in thy wrath: for they have purposed to defile thy sanctuary and to pollute the tabernacle where thy glorious name resteth, and to cast down with sword the horn of thy altar.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Behold their pride, and send thy wrath upon their heads: give into mine hand, which am a widow, the power that I have conceived. \textsuperscript{10} Smite by the deceit of my lips the servant with the prince, and the prince with the servant: break down their stateliness by the hand of a woman. \textsuperscript{11} For thy power standeth not in multitude, nor thy might in strong men: for thou art a God of the afflicted, thou art an helper of the oppressed, an upholder of the weak, a protector of the forlorn, a saviour of them that are without hope.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} I pray thee, I pray thee, O God of my father, and God of the inheritance of Israel, Lord of the heavens and earth, Creator of the waters, King of every creature, hear thou my prayer: \textsuperscript{13} and make my speech and deceit to be their wound and stripe, who have purposed cruel things against thy covenant, and thy hallowed house, and against the top of Sion, and against the house of the possession of thy children.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} And make every nation and tribe to acknowledge that thou art the God of all power and might, and that there is none other that protecteth the people of Israel but thou.\par
\subsection*{Judith 10}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now after that she had ceased to cry unto the God of Israel, and had made an end of all these words, \textsuperscript{2} she rose where she had fallen down, and called her maid, and went down into the house, in the which she abode in the sabbath days, and in her feast days, \textsuperscript{3} and pulled off the sackcloth which she had on, and put off the garments of her widowhood, and washed her body all over with water, and anointed herself with precious ointment, and braided the hair of her head, and put on a tire upon it, and put on her garments of gladness, wherewith she was clad during the life of Manasses her husband. \textsuperscript{4} And she took sandals upon her feet, and put about her her bracelets, and her chains, and her rings, and her earrings, and all her ornaments, and decked herself bravely, to allure the eyes of all men that should see her.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Then she gave her maid a bottle of wine, and a cruse of oil, and filled a bag with parched corn, and lumps of figs, and with fine bread; so she folded all these things together, and laid them upon her. \textsuperscript{6} Thus they went forth to the gate of the city of Bethulia, and found standing there Ozias, and the ancients of the city, Chabris and Charmis.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} And when they saw her, that her countenance was altered, and her apparel was changed, they wondered at her beauty very greatly, and said unto her, \textsuperscript{8} The God, the God of our fathers, give thee favour, and accomplish thine enterprizes to the glory of the children of Israel, and to the exaltation of Jerusalem. Then they worshipped God.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} And she said unto them, Command the gates of the city to be opened unto me, that I may go forth to accomplish the things whereof ye have spoken with me. So they commanded the young men to open unto her, as she had spoken.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} And when they had done so, Judith went out, she, and her maid with her; and the men of the city looked after her, until she was gone down the mountain, and till she had passed the valley, and could see her no more. \textsuperscript{11} Thus they went straight forth in the valley: and the first watch of the Assyrians met her; \textsuperscript{12} and they took her, and asked her, Of what people art thou? and whence comest thou? and whither goest thou? And she said, I am a woman of the Hebrews, and am fled from them: for they shall be given you to be consumed: \textsuperscript{13} and I am coming before Holofernes the chief captain of your army, to declare words of truth; and I will shew him a way, whereby he shall go, and win all the hill country, without losing the body or life of any one of his men.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} Now when the men heard her words, and beheld her countenance, they wondered greatly at her beauty, and said unto her, \textsuperscript{15} Thou hast saved thy life, in that thou hast hasted to come down to the presence of our lord: now therefore come to his tent, and some of us shall conduct thee, until they have delivered thee to his hands. \textsuperscript{16} And when thou standest before him, be not afraid in thine heart, but shew unto him according to thy word; and he will entreat thee well.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Then they chose out of them an hundred men to accompany her and her maid; and they brought her to the tent of Holofernes. \textsuperscript{18} Then was there a concourse throughout all the camp: for her coming was noised among the tents, and they came about her, as she stood without the tent of Holofernes, till they told him of her. \textsuperscript{19} And they wondered at her beauty, and admired the children of Israel because of her, and every one said to his neighbour, Who would despise this people, that have among them such women? surely it is not good that one man of them be left, who being let go might deceive the whole earth. \textsuperscript{20} And they that lay near Holofernes went out, and all his servants, and they brought her into the tent.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} Now Holofernes rested upon his bed under a canopy, which was woven with purple, and gold, and emeralds, and precious stones. \textsuperscript{22} So they shewed him of her; and he came out before his tent with silver lamps going before him. \textsuperscript{23} And when Judith was come before him and his servants, they all marvelled at the beauty of her countenance; and she fell down upon her face, and did reverence unto him: and his servants took her up.\par
\subsection*{Judith 11}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then said Holofernes unto her, Woman, be of good comfort, fear not in thine heart: for I never hurt any that was willing to serve Nabuchodonosor, the king of all the earth. \textsuperscript{2} Now therefore, if thy people that dwelleth in the mountains had not set light by me, I would not have lifted up my spear against them: but they have done these things to themselves. \textsuperscript{3} But now tell me wherefore thou art fled from them, and art come unto us: for thou art come for safeguard; be of good comfort, thou shalt live this night, and hereafter: \textsuperscript{4} for none shall hurt thee, but entreat thee well, as they do the servants of king Nabuchodonosor my lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Then Judith said unto him, Receive the words of thy servant, and suffer thine handmaid to speak in thy presence, and I will declare no lie to my lord this night. \textsuperscript{6} And if thou wilt follow the words of thine handmaid, God will bring the thing perfectly to pass by thee; and my lord shall not fail of his purposes.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} As Nabuchodonosor king of all the earth liveth, and as his power liveth, who hath sent thee for the upholding of every living thing: for not only men shall serve him by thee, but also the beasts of the field, and the cattle, and the fowls of the air, shall live by thy power under Nabuchodonosor and all his house. \textsuperscript{8} For we have heard of thy wisdom and thy policies, and it is reported in all the earth, that thou only art excellent in all the kingdom, and mighty in knowledge, and wonderful in feats of war.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Now as concerning the matter, which Achior did speak in thy council, we have heard his words; for the men of Bethulia saved him, and he declared unto them all that he had spoken unto thee. \textsuperscript{10} Therefore, O lord and governor, reject not his word; but lay it up in thine heart, for it is true: for our nation shall not be punished, neither can the sword prevail against them, except they sin against their God.\par
