\noindent \textsuperscript{11} And now, that my lord be not defeated and frustrate of his purpose, even death is now fallen upon them, and their sin hath overtaken them, wherewith they will provoke their God to anger, whensoever they shall do that which is not fit to be done: \textsuperscript{12} for their victuals fail them, and all their water is scant, and they have determined to lay hands upon their cattle, and purposed to consume all those things, that God hath forbidden them to eat by his laws: \textsuperscript{13} and are resolved to spend the firstfruits of the corn, and the tenths of wine and oil, which they had sanctified, and reserved for the priests that serve in Jerusalem before the face of our God; the which things it is not lawful for any of the people so much as to touch with their hands. \textsuperscript{14} For they have sent some to Jerusalem, because they also that dwell there have done the like, to bring them a licence from the senate. \textsuperscript{15} Now when they shall bring them word, they will forthwith do it, and they shall be given thee to be destroyed the same day.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} Wherefore I thine handmaid, knowing all this, am fled from their presence; and God hath sent me to work things with thee, whereat all the earth shall be astonished, and whosoever shall hear it. \textsuperscript{17} For thy servant is religious, and serveth the God of heaven day and night: now therefore, my lord, I will remain with thee, and thy servant will go out by night into the valley, and I will pray unto God, and he will tell me when they have committed their sins: \textsuperscript{18} and I will come and shew it unto thee: then thou shalt go forth with all thine army, and there shall be none of them that shall resist thee. \textsuperscript{19} And I will lead thee through the midst of Judea, until thou come before Jerusalem; and I will set thy throne in the midst thereof; and thou shalt drive them as sheep that have no shepherd, and a dog shall not so much as open his mouth at thee: for these things were told me according to my foreknowledge, and they were declared unto me, and I am sent to tell thee.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} Then her words pleased Holofernes and all his servants; and they marvelled at her wisdom, and said, \textsuperscript{21} There is not such a woman from one end of the earth to the other, both for beauty of face, and wisdom of words. \textsuperscript{22} Likewise Holofernes said unto her, God hath done well to send thee before the people, that strength might be in our hands, and destruction upon them that lightly regard my lord. \textsuperscript{23} And now thou art both beautiful in thy countenance, and witty in thy words: surely if thou do as thou hast spoken, thy God shall be my God, and thou shalt dwell in the house of king Nabuchodonosor, and shalt be renowned through the whole earth.\par
\subsection*{Judith 12}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then he commanded to bring her in where his plate was set; and bade that they should prepare for her of his own meats, and that she should drink of his own wine.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} And Judith said, I will not eat thereof, lest there be an offence: but provision shall be made for me of the things that I have brought. \textsuperscript{3} Then Holofernes said unto her, If thy provision should fail, how should we give thee the like? for there be none with us of thy nation.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Then said Judith unto him, As thy soul liveth, my lord, thine handmaid shall not spend those things that I have, before the Lord work by mine hand the things that he hath determined.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Then the servants of Holofernes brought her into the tent, and she slept till midnight, and she arose when it was toward the morning watch, \textsuperscript{6} and sent to Holofernes, saying, Let my lord now command that thine handmaid may go forth unto prayer.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Then Holofernes commanded his guard that they should not stay her: thus she abode in the camp three days, and went out in the night into the valley of Bethulia, and washed herself in a fountain of water by the camp. \textsuperscript{8} And when she came out, she besought the Lord God of Israel to direct her way to the raising up of the children of her people. \textsuperscript{9} So she came in clean, and remained in the tent, until she did eat her meat at evening.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} And in the fourth day Holofernes made a feast to his own servants only, and called none of the officers to the banquet. \textsuperscript{11} Then said he to Bagoas the eunuch, who had charge over all that he had, Go now, and persuade this Hebrew woman which is with thee, that she come unto us, and eat and drink with us. \textsuperscript{12} For, lo, it will be a shame for our person, if we shall let such a woman go, not having had her company; for if we draw her not unto us, she will laugh us to scorn.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Then went Bagoas from the presence of Holofernes, and came to her, and he said, Let not this fair damsel fear to come to my lord, and to be honoured in his presence, and drink wine, and be merry with us, and be made this day as one of the daughters of the Assyrians, which serve in the house of Nabuchodonosor.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} Then said Judith unto him, Who am I now, that I should gainsay my lord? surely whatsoever pleaseth him I will do speedily, and it shall be my joy unto the day of my death. \textsuperscript{15} So she arose, and decked herself with her apparel and all her woman's attire, and her maid went and laid soft skins on the ground for her over against Holofernes, which she had received of Bagoas for her daily use, that she might sit and eat upon them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} Now when Judith came in and sat down, Holofernes his heart was ravished with her, and his mind was moved, and he desired greatly her company: for he waited a time to deceive her, from the day that he had seen her.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Then said Holofernes unto her, Drink now, and be merry with us. \textsuperscript{18} So Judith said, I will drink now, my lord, because my life is magnified in me this day more than all the days since I was born. \textsuperscript{19} Then she took and ate and drank before him what her maid had prepared.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} And Holofernes took great delight in her, and drank much more wine than he had drunk at any time in one day since he was born.\par
\subsection*{Judith 13}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now when the evening was come, his servants made haste to depart, and Bagoas shut his tent without, and dismissed the waiters from the presence of his lord; and they went to their beds: for they were all weary, because the feast had been long. \textsuperscript{2} And Judith was left alone in the tent, and Holofernes lying along on his bed: for he was filled with wine.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} Now Judith had commanded her maid to stand without her bedchamber, and to wait for her coming forth, as she did daily: for she said she would go forth to her prayers, and she spake to Bagoas according to the same purpose.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} So all went forth, and none was left in the bedchamber, neither little nor great. Then Judith, standing by his bed, said in her heart, O Lord God of all power, look at this present upon the work of mine hands for the exaltation of Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{5} For now is the time to help thine inheritance, and to execute my enterprise to the destruction of the enemies which are risen against us.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} Then she came to the pillar of the bed, which was at Holofernes' head, and took down his fauchion from thence, \textsuperscript{7} and approached to his bed, and took hold of the hair of his head, and said, Strengthen me, O Lord God of Israel, this day.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} And she smote twice upon his neck with all her might, and she took away his head from him, \textsuperscript{9} and tumbled his body down from the bed, and pulled down the canopy from the pillars; and anon after she went forth, and gave Holofernes his head to her maid; \textsuperscript{10} and she put it in her bag of meat: so they twain went together according to their custom unto prayer : and when they passed the camp, they compassed the valley, and went up the mountain of Bethulia, and came to the gates thereof.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Then said Judith afar off to the watchmen at the gate, Open, open now the gate: God, even our God, is with us, to shew his power yet in Israel, and his strength against the enemy, as he hath even done this day.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} Now when the men of her city heard her voice, they made haste to go down to the gate of their city, and they called the elders of the city. \textsuperscript{13} And then they ran all together, both small and great, for it was strange unto them that she was come: so they opened the gate, and received them, and made a fire for a light, and stood round about them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} Then she said to them with a loud voice, Praise, praise God, praise God, I say, for he hath not taken away his mercy from the house of Israel, but hath destroyed our enemies by mine hands this night. \textsuperscript{15} So she took the head out of the bag, and shewed it, and said unto them, Behold the head of Holofernes, the chief captain of the army of Assur, and behold the canopy, wherein he did lie in his drunkenness; and the Lord hath smitten him by the hand of a woman. \textsuperscript{16} As the Lord liveth, who hath kept me in my way that I went, my countenance hath deceived him to his destruction, and yet hath he not committed sin with me, to defile and shame me.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Then all the people were wonderfully astonished, and bowed themselves, and worshipped God, and said with one accord, Blessed be thou, O our God, which hast this day brought to nought the enemies of thy people. \textsuperscript{18} Then said Ozias unto her, O daughter, blessed art thou of the most high God above all the women upon the earth; and blessed be the Lord God, which hath created the heavens and the earth, which hath directed thee to the cutting off of the head of the chief of our enemies. \textsuperscript{19} For this thy confidence shall not depart from the heart of men, which remember the power of God for ever. \textsuperscript{20} And God turn these things to thee for a perpetual praise, to visit thee in good things, because thou hast not spared thy life for the affliction of our nation, but hast revenged our ruin, walking a straight way before our God. And all the people said, So be it, so be it.\par
\subsection*{Judith 14}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then said Judith unto them, Hear me now, my brethren, and take this head, and hang it upon the highest place of your walls.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} And so soon as the morning shall appear, and the sun shall come forth upon the earth, take ye every one his weapons, and go forth every valiant man out of the city, and set ye a captain over them, as though ye would go down into the field toward the watch of the Assyrians; but go not down. \textsuperscript{3} Then they shall take their armour, and shall go into their camp, and raise up the captains of the army of Assur, and they shall run to the tent of Holofernes, but shall not find him: then fear shall fall upon them, and they shall flee before your face. \textsuperscript{4} So ye, and all that inherit the coast of Israel, shall pursue them, and overthrow them as they go. \textsuperscript{5} But before ye do these things, call me Achior the Ammonite, that he may see and know him that despised the house of Israel, and that sent him to us, as it were to his death.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} Then they called Achior out of the house of Ozias; and when he was come, and saw the head of Holofernes in a man's hand in the assembly of the people, he fell down on his face, and his spirit failed.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} But when they had recovered him, he fell at Judith's feet, and reverenced her, and said, Blessed art thou in all the tabernacle of Juda, and in all nations, which hearing thy name shall be astonished. \textsuperscript{8} Now therefore tell me all the things that thou hast done in these days. Then Judith declared unto him in the midst of the people all that she had done, from the day that she went forth until that hour she spake unto them. \textsuperscript{9} And when she had left off speaking, the people shouted with a loud voice, and made a joyful noise in their city.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} And when Achior had seen all that the God of Israel had done, he believed in God greatly, and circumcised the flesh of his foreskin, and was joined unto the house of Israel unto this day.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} And as soon as the morning arose, they hanged the head of Holofernes upon the wall, and every man took his weapons, and they went forth by bands unto the straits of the mountain.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} But when the Assyrians saw them, they sent to their leaders, which came to their captains and tribunes, and to every one of their rulers.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} So they came to Holofernes' tent, and said to him that had the charge of all his things, Waken now our lord: for the slaves have been bold to come down upon us to battle, that they may be utterly destroyed.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} Then went in Bagoas, and knocked at the door of the tent; for he thought that he had slept with Judith. \textsuperscript{15} But because none answered, he opened it, and went into the bedchamber, and found him cast upon the floor dead, and his head was taken from him. \textsuperscript{16} Therefore he cried with a loud voice, with weeping, and sighing, and a mighty cry, and rent his garments.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} After he went into the tent where Judith lodged: and when he found her not, he leaped out to the people, and cried, \textsuperscript{18} These slaves have dealt treacherously; one woman of the Hebrews hath brought shame upon the house of king Nabuchodonosor: for, behold, Holofernes lieth upon the ground without a head. \textsuperscript{19} When the captains of the Assyrians' army heard these words, they rent their coats, and their minds were wonderfully troubled, and there was a cry and a very great noise throughout the camp.\par
\subsection*{Judith 15}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And when they that were in the tents heard, they were astonished at the thing that was done. \textsuperscript{2} And fear and trembling fell upon them, so that there was no man that durst abide in the sight of his neighbour, but rushing out all together, they fled into every way of the plain, and of the hill country. \textsuperscript{3} They also that had camped in the mountains round about Bethulia fled away. Then the children of Israel, every one that was a warrior among them, rushed out upon them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Then sent Ozias to Betomasthem, and to Chobai, and Chola, and to all the coasts of Israel, such as should tell the things that were done, and that all should rush forth upon their enemies to destroy them. \textsuperscript{5} Now when the children of Israel heard it, they all fell upon them with one consent, and slew them unto Chobai: likewise also they that came from Jerusalem, and from all the hill country, (for men had told them what things were done in the camp of their enemies,) and they that were in Galaad, and in Galilee, chased them with a great slaughter, until they were past Damascus and the borders thereof.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} And the residue that dwelt at Bethulia, fell upon the camp of Assur, and spoiled them, and were greatly enriched. \textsuperscript{7} And the children of Israel that returned from the slaughter had that which remained; and the villages and the cities, that were in the mountains and in the plain, gat many spoils: for the multitude was very great.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} Then Joacim the high priest, and the ancients of the children of Israel that dwelt in Jerusalem, came to behold the good things that God had shewed to Israel, and to see Judith, and to salute her. \textsuperscript{9} And when they came unto her, they blessed her with one accord, and said unto her, Thou art the exaltation of Israel, thou art the great glory of Israel, thou art the great rejoicing of our nation: \textsuperscript{10} thou hast done all these things by thine hand: thou hast done much good to Israel, and God is pleased therewith: blessed be thou of the Almighty Lord for evermore. And all the people said, So be it.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} And the people spoiled the camp the space of thirty days: and they gave unto Judith Holofernes his tent, and all his plate, and beds, and vessels, and all his stuff: and she took it, and laid it on her mule; and made ready her carts, and laid them thereon.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} Then all the women of Israel ran together to see her, and blessed her, and made a dance among them for her: and she took branches in her hand, and gave also to the women that were with her. \textsuperscript{13} And they put a garland of olive upon her and her maid that was with her, and she went before all the people in the dance, leading all the women: and all the men of Israel followed in their armour with garlands, and with songs in their mouths.\par
\subsection*{Judith 16}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then Judith began to sing this thanksgiving in all Israel, and all the people sang after her this song of praise.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} And Judith said,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} For God breaketh the battles: for among the camps in the midst of the people he hath delivered me out of the hands of them that persecuted me.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Assur came out of the mountains from the north, he came with ten thousands of his army, the multitude whereof stopped the torrents, and their horsemen have covered the hills. \textsuperscript{5} He bragged that he would burn up my borders, and kill my young men with the sword, and dash the sucking children against the ground, and make mine infants as a prey, and my virgins as a spoil.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} But the Almighty Lord hath disappointed them by the hand of a woman. \textsuperscript{7} For the mighty one did not fall by the young men, neither did the sons of the Titans smite him, nor high giants set upon him: but Judith the daughter of Merari weakened him with the beauty of her countenance. \textsuperscript{8} For she put off the garment of her widowhood for the exaltation of those that were oppressed in Israel, and anointed her face with ointment, and bound her hair in a tire, and took a linen garment to deceive him. \textsuperscript{9} Her sandals ravished his eyes, her beauty took his mind prisoner, and the fauchion passed through his neck.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} The Persians quaked at her boldness, and the Medes were daunted at her hardiness. \textsuperscript{11} Then my afflicted shouted for joy, and my weak ones cried aloud; but they were astonished: these lifted up their voices, but they were overthrown. \textsuperscript{12} The sons of the damsels have pierced them through, and wounded them as fugitives' children: they perished by the battle of my Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} I will sing unto my God a new song: O Lord, thou art great and glorious, wonderful in strength, and invincible. \textsuperscript{14} Let all creatures serve thee: for thou spakest, and they were made: thou didst send forth thy spirit, and it created them, and there is none that can resist thy voice. \textsuperscript{15} For the mountains shall be moved from their foundations with the waters, the rocks shall melt as wax at thy presence: yet thou art merciful to them that fear thee. \textsuperscript{16} For all sacrifice is too little for a sweet savour unto thee, and all the fat is not sufficient for thy burnt offering: but he that feareth the Lord is great at all times.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Woe to the nations that rise up against my kindred! the Lord Almighty will take vengeance of them in the day of judgment, in putting fire and worms in their flesh; and they shall feel them, and weep for ever.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Now as soon as they entered into Jerusalem, they worshipped the Lord; and as soon as the people were purified, they offered their burnt offerings, and their free offerings, and their gifts.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} Judith also dedicated all the stuff of Holofernes, which the people had given her, and gave the canopy which she had taken out of his bedchamber, for a gift unto God.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} So the people continued feasting in Jerusalem before the sanctuary for the space of three months, and Judith remained with them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} After this time every one returned to his own inheritance, and Judith went to Bethulia, and remained in her own possession, and was in her time honourable in all the country. \textsuperscript{22} And many desired her, but none knew her all the days of her life, after that Manasses her husband was dead, and was gathered to his people.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} But she increased more and more in honour, and waxed old in her husband's house, being an hundred and five years old, and made her maid free; so she died in Bethulia: and they buried her in the cave of her husband Manasses. \textsuperscript{24} And the house of Israel lamented her seven days: and before she died, she did distribute her goods to all them that were nearest of kindred to Manasses her husband, and to them that were the nearest of her kindred. \textsuperscript{25} And there was none that made the children of Israel any more afraid in the days of Judith, nor a long time after her death.\par
\section*{Wisdom of Solomon}
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Love righteousness, ye that be judges of the earth: think of the Lord with a good (heart,) and in simplicity of heart seek him. \textsuperscript{2} For he will be found of them that tempt him not; and sheweth himself unto such as do not distrust him. \textsuperscript{3} For froward thoughts separate from God: and his power, when it is tried, reproveth the unwise.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter: nor dwell in the body that is subject unto sin. \textsuperscript{5} For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} For wisdom is a loving spirit; and will not acquit a blasphemer of his words: for God is witness of his reins, and a true beholder of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue. \textsuperscript{7} For the Spirit of the Lord filleth the world: and that which containeth all things hath knowledge of the voice.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} Therefore he that speaketh unrighteous things cannot be hidden: neither shall vengeance, when it punisheth, pass by him. \textsuperscript{9} For inquisition shall be made into the counsels of the ungodly: and the sound of his words shall come unto the Lord for the manifestation of his wicked deeds. \textsuperscript{10} For the ear of jealousy heareth all things: and the noise of murmurings is not hid.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} Seek not death in the error of your life: and pull not upon yourselves destruction with the works of your hands. \textsuperscript{13} For God made not death: neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living. \textsuperscript{14} For he created all things, that they might have their being: and the generations of the world were healthful; and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor the kingdom of death upon the earth: \textsuperscript{15} (for righteousness is immortal:) \textsuperscript{16} but ungodly men with their works and words called it to them: for when they thought to have it their friend, they consumed to nought, and made a covenant with it, because they are worthy to take part with it.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} For the ungodly said, reasoning with themselves, but not aright, Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedy: neither was there any man known to have returned from the grave. \textsuperscript{2} For we are born at all adventure: and we shall be hereafter as though we had never been: for the breath in our nostrils is as smoke, and a little spark in the moving of our heart: \textsuperscript{3} which being extinguished, our body shall be turned to ashes, and our spirit shall vanish as the soft air, \textsuperscript{4} and our name shall be forgotten in time, and no man shall have our works in remembrance, and our life shall pass away as the trace of a cloud, and shall be dispersed as a mist, that is driven away with the beams of the sun, and overcome with the heat thereof.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} For our time is a very shadow that passeth away; and after our end there is no returning: for it is fast sealed, so that no man cometh again.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} Come on therefore, let us enjoy the good things that are present: and let us speedily use the creatures like as in youth. \textsuperscript{7} Let us fill ourselves with costly wine and ointments: and let no flower of the spring pass by us. \textsuperscript{8} Let us crown ourselves with rosebuds, before they be withered: \textsuperscript{9} let none of us go without his part of our voluptuousness: let us leave tokens of our joyfulness in every place: for this is our portion, and our lot is this.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} Let us oppress the poor righteous man, let us not spare the widow, nor reverence the ancient grey hairs of the aged. \textsuperscript{11} Let our strength be the law of justice: for that which is feeble is found to be nothing worth.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education. \textsuperscript{13} He professeth to have the knowledge of God: and he calleth himself the child of the Lord. \textsuperscript{14} He was made to reprove our thoughts. \textsuperscript{15} He is grievous unto us even to behold: for his life is not like other men's, his ways are of another fashion. \textsuperscript{16} We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and maketh his boast that God is his father.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Let us see if his words be true: and let us prove what shall happen in the end of him. \textsuperscript{18} For if the just man be the son of God, he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies. \textsuperscript{19} Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience. \textsuperscript{20} Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} Such things they did imagine, and were deceived: for their own wickedness hath blinded them. \textsuperscript{22} As for the mysteries of God, they knew them not: neither hoped they for the wages of righteousness, nor discerned a reward for blameless souls.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} For God created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity. \textsuperscript{24} Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that are of his side do find it.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them. \textsuperscript{2} In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery, \textsuperscript{3} and their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace. \textsuperscript{4} For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself. \textsuperscript{6} As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble. \textsuperscript{8} They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Lord shall reign for ever. \textsuperscript{9} They that put their trust in him shall understand the truth: and such as be faithful in love shall abide with him: for grace and mercy is to his saints, and he hath care for his elect. \textsuperscript{10} But the ungodly shall be punished according to their own imaginations, which have neglected the righteous, and forsaken the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} For whoso despiseth wisdom and nurture, he is miserable, and their hope is vain, their labours unfruitful, and their works unprofitable: \textsuperscript{12} their wives are foolish, and their children wicked:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Their offspring is cursed. Wherefore blessed is the barren that is undefiled, which hath not known the sinful bed: she shall have fruit in the visitation of souls.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} And blessed is the eunuch, which with his hands hath wrought no iniquity, nor imagined wicked things against God: for unto him shall be given the special gift of faith, and an inheritance in the temple of the Lord more acceptable to his mind. \textsuperscript{15} For glorious is the fruit of good labours: and the root of wisdom shall never fall away.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} As for the children of adulterers, they shall not come to their perfection, and the seed of an unrighteous bed shall be rooted out. \textsuperscript{17} For though they live long, yet shall they be nothing regarded: and their last age shall be without honour. \textsuperscript{18} Or, if they die quickly, they have no hope, neither comfort in the day of trial. \textsuperscript{19} For horrible is the end of the unrighteous generation.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Better it is to have no children, and to have virtue: for the memorial thereof is immortal: because it is known with God, and with men. \textsuperscript{2} When it is present, men take example at it; and when it is gone, they desire it: it weareth a crown, and triumpheth for ever, having gotten the victory, striving for undefiled rewards.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} But the multiplying brood of the ungodly shall not thrive, nor take deep rooting from bastard slips, nor lay any fast foundation. \textsuperscript{4} For though they flourish in branches for a time; yet standing not fast, they shall be shaken with the wind, and through the force of winds they shall be rooted out. \textsuperscript{5} The imperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit unprofitable, not ripe to eat, yea, meet for nothing. \textsuperscript{6} For children begotten of unlawful beds are witnesses of wickedness against their parents in their trial. \textsuperscript{7} But though the righteous be prevented with death, yet shall he be in rest.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} For honourable age is not that which standeth in length of time, nor that is measured by number of years. \textsuperscript{9} But wisdom is the grey hair unto men, and an unspotted life is old age. \textsuperscript{10} He pleased God, and was beloved of him: so that living among sinners he was translated. \textsuperscript{11} Yea, speedily was he taken away, lest that wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul. \textsuperscript{12} For the bewitching of naughtiness doth obscure things that are honest; and the wandering of concupiscence doth undermine the simple mind. \textsuperscript{13} He, being made perfect in a short time, fulfilled a long time: \textsuperscript{14} for his soul pleased the Lord: therefore hasted he to take him away from among the wicked. \textsuperscript{15} This the people saw, and understood not, neither laid they up this in their minds, That his grace and mercy is with his saints, and that he hath respect unto his chosen.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} Thus the righteous that is dead shall condemn the ungodly which are living; and youth that is soon perfected the many years and old age of the unrighteous. \textsuperscript{17} For they shall see the end of the wise, and shall not understand what God in his counsel hath decreed of him, and to what end the Lord hath set him in safety. \textsuperscript{18} They shall see him, and despise him; but God shall laugh them to scorn; and they shall hereafter be a vile carcase, and a reproach among the dead for evermore. \textsuperscript{19} For he shall rend them, and cast them down headlong, that they shall be speechless; and he shall shake them from the foundation; and they shall be utterly laid waste, and be in sorrow; and their memorial shall perish. \textsuperscript{20} And when they cast up the account of their sins, they shall come with fear: and their own iniquities shall convince them to their face.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours. \textsuperscript{2} When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for. \textsuperscript{3} And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} we fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: \textsuperscript{5} how is he numbered among the children of God, and his lot is among the saints! \textsuperscript{6} Therefore have we erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness hath not shined unto us, and the sun of righteousness rose not upon us. \textsuperscript{7} We wearied ourselves in the way of wickedness and destruction: yea, we have gone through deserts, where there lay no way: but as for the way of the Lord, we have not known it.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} What hath pride profited us? or what good hath riches with our vaunting brought us? \textsuperscript{9} All those things are passed away like a shadow, and as a post that hasted by; \textsuperscript{10} and as a ship that passeth over the waves of the water, which when it is gone by, the trace thereof cannot be found, neither the pathway of the keel in the waves: \textsuperscript{11} or as when a bird hath flown through the air, there is no token of her way to be found, but the light air being beaten with the stroke of her wings, and parted with the violent noise and motion of them, is passed through, and therein afterwards no sign where she went is to be found; \textsuperscript{12} or like as when an arrow is shot at a mark, it parteth the air, which immediately cometh together again, so that a man cannot know where it went through: \textsuperscript{13} even so we in like manner, as soon as we were born, began to draw to our end, and had no sign of virtue to shew; but were consumed in our own wickedness.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High. \textsuperscript{16} Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the Lord's hand: for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} He shall take to him his jealousy for complete armour, and make the creature his weapon for the revenge of his enemies. \textsuperscript{18} He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, and true judgment instead of an helmet. \textsuperscript{19} He shall take holiness for an invincible shield. \textsuperscript{20} His severe wrath shall he sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with him against the unwise.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} Then shall the right aiming thunderbolts go abroad; and from the clouds, as from a well drawn bow, shall they fly to the mark. \textsuperscript{22} And hailstones full of wrath shall be cast as out of a stone bow, and the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the floods shall cruelly drown them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} Yea, a mighty wind shall stand up against them, and like a storm shall blow them away: thus iniquity shall lay waste the whole earth, and ill dealing shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 6}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Hear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye that be judges of the ends of the earth. \textsuperscript{2} Give ear, ye that rule the people, and glory in the multitude of nations. \textsuperscript{3} For power is given you of the Lord, and sovereignty from the Highest, who shall try your works, and search out your counsels. \textsuperscript{4} Because, being ministers of his kingdom, ye have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsel of God; \textsuperscript{5} horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places. \textsuperscript{6} For mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented. \textsuperscript{7} For he which is Lord over all shall fear no man's person, neither shall he stand in awe of any man's greatness: for he hath made the small and great, and careth for all alike. \textsuperscript{8} But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Unto you therefore, O kings, do I speak, that ye may learn wisdom, and not fall away. \textsuperscript{10} For they that keep holiness holily shall be judged holy: and they that have learned such things shall find what to answer. \textsuperscript{11} Wherefore set your affection upon my words; desire them, and ye shall be instructed.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away: yea, she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} She preventeth them that desire her, in making herself first known unto them. \textsuperscript{14} Whoso seeketh her early shall have no great travail: for he shall find her sitting at his doors. \textsuperscript{15} To think therefore upon her is the perfection of wisdom: and whoso watcheth for her shall quickly be without care. \textsuperscript{16} For she goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably unto them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought. \textsuperscript{17} For the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline; and the care of discipline is love; \textsuperscript{18} and love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed unto her laws is the assurance of incorruption; \textsuperscript{19} and incorruption maketh us near unto God: \textsuperscript{20} therefore the desire of wisdom bringeth to a kingdom.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} If your delight be then in thrones and sceptres, O ye kings of the people, honour wisdom, that ye may reign for evermore. \textsuperscript{22} As for wisdom, what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you: but will seek her out from the beginning of her nativity, and bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not pass over the truth. \textsuperscript{23} Neither will I go with consuming envy; for such a man shall have no fellowship with wisdom. \textsuperscript{24} But the multitude of the wise is the welfare of the world: and a wise king is the upholding of the people. \textsuperscript{25} Receive therefore instruction through my words, and it shall do you good.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 7}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} I myself also am a mortal man, like to all, and the offspring of him that was first made of the earth, \textsuperscript{2} and in my mother's womb was fashioned to be flesh in the time of ten months, being compacted in blood, of the seed of man, and the pleasure that came with sleep. \textsuperscript{3} And when I was born, I drew in the common air, and fell upon the earth, which is of like nature, and the first voice which I uttered was crying, as all others do. \textsuperscript{4} I was nursed in swaddling clothes, and that with cares. \textsuperscript{5} For there is no king that had any other beginning of birth. \textsuperscript{6} For all men have one entrance into life, and the like going out.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God , and the spirit of wisdom came to me. \textsuperscript{8} I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her. \textsuperscript{9} Neither compared I unto her any precious stone, because all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her. \textsuperscript{10} I loved her above health and beauty, and chose to have her instead of light: for the light that cometh from her never goeth out.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands. \textsuperscript{12} And I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goeth before them: and I knew not that she was the mother of them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches. \textsuperscript{14} For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of God, being commended for the gifts that come from learning.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} God hath granted me to speak as I would, and to conceive as is meet for the things that are given me: because it is he that leadeth unto wisdom, and directeth the wise. \textsuperscript{16} For in his hand are both we and our words; all wisdom also, and knowledge of workmanship. \textsuperscript{17} For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements: \textsuperscript{18} the beginning, ending, and midst of the times: the alterations of the turning of the sun , and change of seasons: \textsuperscript{19} the circuits of years, and positions of stars: \textsuperscript{20} the natures of living creatures, and the furies of wild beasts: the violence of winds, and the reasonings of men: the diversities of plants, and the virtues of roots: \textsuperscript{21} and all such things as are either secret or manifest, them I know.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} For wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit, holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled, plain, not subject to hurt, loving the thing that is good, quick, which cannot be letted, ready to do good, \textsuperscript{23} kind to man, stedfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things, and going through all understanding, pure, and most subtil, spirits.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness. \textsuperscript{25} For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her. \textsuperscript{26} For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness. \textsuperscript{27} And being but one, she can do all things: and remaining in herself, she maketh all things new: and in all ages entering into holy souls, she maketh them friends of God, and prophets.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} For God loveth none but him that dwelleth with wisdom. \textsuperscript{29} For she is more beautiful than the sun, and above all the order of stars: being compared with the light, she is found before it. \textsuperscript{30} For after this cometh night: but vice shall not prevail against wisdom.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 8}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Wisdom reacheth from one end to another mightily; and sweetly doth she order all things.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} I loved her, and sought her out from my youth, I desired to make her my spouse, and I was a lover of her beauty. \textsuperscript{3} In that she is conversant with God, she magnifieth her nobility: yea, the Lord of all things himself loved her. \textsuperscript{4} For she is privy to the mysteries of the knowledge of God, and a lover of his works.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} If riches be a possession to be desired in this life; what is richer than wisdom, that worketh all things? \textsuperscript{6} And if prudence work; who of all that are is a more cunning workman than she? \textsuperscript{7} And if a man love righteousness, her labours are virtues: for she teacheth temperance and prudence, justice and fortitude: which are such things, as men can have nothing more profitable in their life. \textsuperscript{8} If a man desire much experience, she knoweth things of old, and conjectureth aright what is to come: she knoweth the subtilties of speeches, and can expound dark sentences: she foreseeth signs and wonders, and the events of seasons and times.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Therefore I purposed to take her to me to live with me, knowing that she would be a counsellor of good things, and a comfort in cares and grief. \textsuperscript{10} For her sake I shall have estimation among the multitude, and honour with the elders, though I be young. \textsuperscript{11} I shall be found of a quick conceit in judgment, and shall be admired in the sight of great men. \textsuperscript{12} When I hold my tongue, they shall bide my leisure, and when I speak, they shall give good ear unto me: if I talk much, they shall lay their hands upon their mouth.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Moreover by the means of her I shall obtain immortality, and leave behind me an everlasting memorial to them that come after me. \textsuperscript{14} I shall set the people in order, and the nations shall be subject unto me. \textsuperscript{15} Horrible tyrants shall be afraid when they do but hear of me; I shall be found good among the multitude, and valiant in war. \textsuperscript{16} After I am come into mine house, I will repose myself with her: for her conversation hath no bitterness: and to live with her hath no sorrow, but mirth and joy.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Now when I considered these things in myself, and pondered them in my heart, how that to be allied unto wisdom is immortality; \textsuperscript{18} and great pleasure it is to have her friendship; and in the works of her hands are infinite riches; and in the exercise of conference with her, prudence; and in talking with her, a good report; I went about seeking how to take her to me.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} For I was a witty child, and had a good spirit. \textsuperscript{20} Yea rather, being good, I came into a body undefiled. \textsuperscript{21} Nevertheless, when I perceived that I could not otherwise obtain her, except God gave her me; and that was a point of wisdom also to know whose gift she was; I prayed unto the Lord, and besought him, and with my whole heart I said,\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 9}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} O God of my fathers, and Lord of mercy, who hast made all things with thy word, \textsuperscript{2} and ordained man through thy wisdom, that he should have dominion over the creatures which thou hast made, \textsuperscript{3} and order the world according to equity and righteousness, and execute judgment with an upright heart: \textsuperscript{4} give me wisdom, that sitteth by thy throne; and reject me not from among thy children: \textsuperscript{5} for I thy servant and son of thine handmaid am a feeble person, and of a short time, and too young for the understanding of judgment and laws.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} For though a man be never so perfect among the children of men, yet if thy wisdom be not with him, he shall be nothing regarded.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Thou hast chosen me to be a king of thy people, and a judge of thy sons and daughters: \textsuperscript{8} thou hast commanded me to build a temple upon thy holy mount, and an altar in the city wherein thou dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which thou hast prepared from the beginning. \textsuperscript{9} And wisdom was with thee: which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in thy sight, and right in thy commandments. \textsuperscript{10} O send her out of thy holy heavens, and from the throne of thy glory, that being present she may labour with me, that I may know what is pleasing unto thee. \textsuperscript{11} For she knoweth and understandeth all things, and she shall lead me soberly in my doings, and preserve me in her power. \textsuperscript{12} So shall my works be acceptable, and then shall I judge thy people righteously, and be worthy to sit in my father's seat.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} For what man is he that can know the counsel of God? or who can think what the will of the Lord is? \textsuperscript{14} For the thoughts of mortal men are miserable, and our devices are but uncertain. \textsuperscript{15} For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things. \textsuperscript{16} And hardly do we guess aright at things that are upon earth, and with labour do we find the things that are before us: but the things that are in heaven who hath searched out? \textsuperscript{17} And thy counsel who hath known, except thou give wisdom, and send thy Holy Spirit from above? \textsuperscript{18} For so the ways of them which lived on the earth were reformed, and men were taught the things that are pleasing unto thee, and were saved through wisdom.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 10}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} She preserved the first formed father of the world, that was created alone, and brought him out of his fall, \textsuperscript{2} and gave him power to rule all things.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother. \textsuperscript{4} For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood, wisdom again preserved it, and directed the course of the righteous in a piece of wood of small value. \textsuperscript{5} Moreover, the nations in their wicked conspiracy being confounded, she found out the righteous, and preserved him blameless unto God, and kept him strong against his tender compassion toward his son.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} When the ungodly perished, she delivered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities. \textsuperscript{7} Of whose wickedness, even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul. \textsuperscript{8} For regarding not wisdom, they gat not only this hurt, that they knew not the things which were good; but also left behind them to the world a memorial of their foolishness: so that in the things wherein they offended they could not so much as be hid. \textsuperscript{9} But wisdom delivered from pain those that attended upon her.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} When the righteous fled from his brother's wrath, she guided him in right paths, shewed him the kingdom of God, and gave him knowledge of holy things, made him rich in his travels, and multiplied the fruit of his labours. \textsuperscript{11} In the covetousness of such as oppressed him she stood by him, and made him rich. \textsuperscript{12} She defended him from his enemies, and kept him safe from those that lay in wait, and in a sore conflict she gave him the victory; that he might know that godliness is stronger than all.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} When the righteous was sold, she forsook him not, but delivered him from sin: she went down with him into the pit, \textsuperscript{14} and left him not in bonds, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom, and power against those that oppressed him: as for them that had accused him, she shewed them to be liars, and gave him perpetual glory.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} She delivered the righteous people and blameless seed from the nation that oppressed them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} She entered into the soul of the servant of the Lord, and withstood dreadful kings in wonders and signs; \textsuperscript{17} rendered to the righteous a reward of their labours, guided them in a marvellous way, and was unto them for a cover by day, and a light of stars in the night season; \textsuperscript{18} brought them through the Red sea, and led them through much water: \textsuperscript{19} but she drowned their enemies, and cast them up out of the bottom of the deep. \textsuperscript{20} Therefore the righteous spoiled the ungodly, and praised thy holy name, O Lord, and magnified with one accord thine hand, that fought for them. \textsuperscript{21} For wisdom opened the mouth of the dumb, and made the tongues of them that cannot speak eloquent.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 11}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} She prospered their works in the hand of the holy prophet. \textsuperscript{2} They went through the wilderness that was not inhabited, and pitched tents in places where there lay no way. \textsuperscript{3} They stood against their enemies, and were avenged of their adversaries. \textsuperscript{4} When they were thirsty, they called upon thee, and water was given them out of the flinty rock, and their thirst was quenched out of the hard stone. \textsuperscript{5} For by what things their enemies were punished, by the same they in their need were benefited. \textsuperscript{6} For instead of a fountain of a perpetual running river troubled with foul blood, \textsuperscript{7} for a manifest reproof of that commandment, whereby the infants were slain, thou gavest unto them abundance of water by a means which they hoped not for: \textsuperscript{8} declaring by that thirst then how thou hadst punished their adversaries.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} For when they were tried, albeit but in mercy chastised, they knew how the ungodly were judged in wrath and tormented, thirsting in another manner than the just. \textsuperscript{10} For these thou didst admonish and try, as a father: but the others, as a severe king, thou didst condemn and punish. \textsuperscript{11} Whether they were absent or present, they were vexed alike. \textsuperscript{12} For a double grief came upon them, and a groaning for the remembrance of things past. \textsuperscript{13} For when they heard by their own punishments the other to be benefited, they had some feeling of the Lord. \textsuperscript{14} For whom they rejected with scorn, when he was long before thrown out at the casting forth of the infants , him in the end, when they saw what came to pass, they admired.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} But for the foolish devices of their wickedness, wherewith being deceived they worshipped serpents void of reason, and vile beasts, thou didst send a multitude of unreasonable beasts upon them for vengeance: \textsuperscript{16} that they might know, that wherewithal a man sinneth, by the same shall he be punished.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} For thy Almighty hand, that made the world of matter without form, wanted not means to send among them a multitude of bears, or fierce lions, \textsuperscript{18} or unknown wild beasts, full of rage, newly created, breathing out either a fiery vapour, or filthy scents of scattered smoke, or shooting horrible sparkles out of their eyes: \textsuperscript{19} whereof not only the harm might dispatch them at once, but also the terrible sight utterly destroy them. \textsuperscript{20} Yea, and without these might they have fallen down with one blast, being persecuted of vengeance, and scattered abroad through the breath of thy power: but thou hast ordered all things in measure and number and weight. \textsuperscript{21} For thou canst shew thy great strength at all times when thou wilt; and who may withstand the power of thine arm? \textsuperscript{22} For the whole world before thee is as a little grain of the balance, yea, as a drop of the morning dew that falleth down upon the earth.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} But thou hast mercy upon all; for thou canst do all things, and winkest at the sins of men, because they should amend. \textsuperscript{24} For thou lovest all the things that are, and abhorrest nothing which thou hast made: for never wouldest thou have made any thing, if thou hadst hated it. \textsuperscript{25} And how could any thing have endured, if it had not been thy will? or been preserved, if not called by thee? \textsuperscript{26} But thou sparest all: for they are thine, O Lord, thou lover of souls.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 12}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} For thine incorruptible Spirit is in all things. \textsuperscript{2} Therefore chastenest thou them by little and little that offend, and warnest them by putting them in remembrance wherein they have offended, that leaving their wickedness they may believe on thee, O Lord. \textsuperscript{3} For it was thy will to destroy by the hands of our fathers both those old inhabitants of thy holy land, \textsuperscript{4} whom thou hatedst for doing most odious works of witchcrafts, and wicked sacrifices; \textsuperscript{5} and also those merciless murderers of children, and devourers of man's flesh, and the feasts of blood, \textsuperscript{6} with their priests out of the midst of their idolatrous crew, and the parents, that killed with their own hands souls destitute of help: \textsuperscript{7} that the land, which thou esteemedst above all other, might receive a worthy colony of God's children.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} Nevertheless even those thou sparedst as men, and didst send wasps, forerunners of thine host, to destroy them by little and little. \textsuperscript{9} Not that thou wast unable to bring the ungodly under the hand of the righteous in battle, or to destroy them at once with cruel beasts, or with one rough word: \textsuperscript{10} but executing thy judgments upon them by little and little, thou gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed. \textsuperscript{11} For it was a cursed seed from the beginning; neither didst thou for fear of any man give them pardon for those things wherein they sinned. \textsuperscript{12} For who shall say, What hast thou done? or who shall withstand thy judgment? or who shall accuse thee for the nations that perish, whom thou hast made? or who shall come to stand against thee, to be revenged for the unrighteous men? \textsuperscript{13} For neither is there any God but thou that careth for all, to whom thou mightest shew that thy judgment is not unright.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} Neither shall king or tyrant be able to set his face against thee for any whom thou hast punished. \textsuperscript{15} Forsomuch then as thou art righteous thyself, thou orderest all things righteously: thinking it not agreeable with thy power to condemn him that hath not deserved to be punished. \textsuperscript{16} For thy power is the beginning of righteousness, and because thou art the Lord of all, it maketh thee to be gracious unto all. \textsuperscript{17} For when men will not believe that thou art of a full power, thou shewest thy strength, and among them that know it thou makest their boldness manifest. \textsuperscript{18} But thou, mastering thy power, judgest with equity, and orderest us with great favour: for thou mayest use power when thou wilt.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} But by such works hast thou taught thy people that the just man should be merciful, and hast made thy children to be of a good hope that thou givest repentance for sins. \textsuperscript{20} For if thou didst punish the enemies of thy children, and the condemned to death, with such deliberation, giving them time and place whereby they might be delivered from their malice: \textsuperscript{21} with how great circumspection didst thou judge thine own sons, unto whose fathers thou hast sworn, and made covenants of good promises? \textsuperscript{22} Therefore, whereas thou dost chasten us, thou scourgest our enemies a thousand times more, to the intent that, when we judge, we should carefully think of thy goodness, and when we ourselves are judged, we should look for mercy.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} Wherefore, whereas men have lived dissolutely and unrighteously, thou hast tormented them with their own abominations. \textsuperscript{24} For they went astray very far in the ways of error, and held them for gods, which even among the beasts of their enemies were despised, being deceived, as children of no understanding. \textsuperscript{25} Therefore unto them, as to children without the use of reason, thou didst send a judgment to mock them. \textsuperscript{26} But they that would not be reformed by that correction, wherein he dallied with them, shall feel a judgment worthy of God. \textsuperscript{27} For, look, for what things they grudged, when they were punished, that is, for them whom they thought to be gods; [now] being punished in them, when they saw it, they acknowledged him to be the true God, whom before they denied to know; and therefore came extreme damnation upon them.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 13}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Surely vain are all men by nature, who are ignorant of God, and could not out of the good things that are seen know him that is: neither by considering the works did they acknowledge the workmaster; \textsuperscript{2} but deemed either fire, or wind, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars, or the violent water, or the lights of heaven, to be the gods which govern the world. \textsuperscript{3} With whose beauty if they being delighted took them to be gods; let them know how much better the Lord of them is: for the first author of beauty hath created them. \textsuperscript{4} But if they were astonished at their power and virtue, let them understand by them, how much mightier he is that made them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} For by the greatness and beauty of the creatures proportionably the maker of them is seen. \textsuperscript{6} But yet for this they are the less to be blamed: for they peradventure err, seeking God, and desirous to find him. \textsuperscript{7} For being conversant in his works they search him diligently, and believe their sight: because the things are beautiful that are seen. \textsuperscript{8} Howbeit neither are they to be pardoned. \textsuperscript{9} For if they were able to know so much, that they could aim at the world; how did they not sooner find out the Lord thereof?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} But miserable are they, and in dead things is their hope, who called them gods, which are the works of men's hands, gold and silver, to shew art in, and resemblances of beasts, or a stone good for nothing, the work of an ancient hand. \textsuperscript{11} Now a carpenter that felleth timber, after he hath sawn down a tree meet for the purpose, and taken off all the bark skilfully round about, and hath wrought it handsomely, and made a vessel thereof fit for the service of man's life; \textsuperscript{12} and after spending the refuse of his work to dress his meat, hath filled himself; \textsuperscript{13} and taking the very refuse among those which served to no use, being a crooked piece of wood, and full of knots, hath carved it diligently when he had nothing else to do, and formed it by the skill of his understanding, and fashioned it to the image of a man; \textsuperscript{14} or made it like some vile beast, laying it over with vermilion, and with paint colouring it red, and colouring every spot therein; \textsuperscript{15} and when he had made a convenient room for it, set it in a wall, and made it fast with iron: \textsuperscript{16} for he provided for it that it might not fall, knowing that it was unable to help itself; for it is an image, and hath need of help.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Then maketh he prayer for his goods, for his wife and children, and is not ashamed to speak to that which hath no life. \textsuperscript{18} For health he calleth upon that which is weak: for life prayeth to that which is dead: for aid humbly beseecheth that which hath least means to help: and for a good journey he asketh of that which cannot set a foot forward: \textsuperscript{19} and for gaining and getting, and for good success of his hands, asketh ability to do of him, that is most unable to do any thing.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 14}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Again, one preparing himself to sail, and about to pass through the raging waves, calleth upon a piece of wood more rotten than the vessel that carrieth him. \textsuperscript{2} For verily desire of gain devised that, and the workman built it by his skill. \textsuperscript{3} But thy providence, O Father, governeth it: for thou hast made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves; \textsuperscript{4} shewing that thou canst save from all danger: yea, though a man went to sea without art. \textsuperscript{5} Nevertheless thou wouldest not that the works of thy wisdom should be idle, and therefore do men commit their lives to a small piece of wood, and passing the rough sea in a weak vessel are saved.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} For in the old time also, when the proud giants perished, the hope of the world governed by thy hand escaped in a weak vessel, and left to all ages a seed of generation. \textsuperscript{7} For blessed is the wood whereby righteousness cometh.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} But that which is made with hands is cursed, as well it, as he that made it: he, because he made it: and it, because, being corruptible, it was called God. \textsuperscript{9} For the ungodly and his ungodliness are both alike hateful unto God. \textsuperscript{10} For that which is made shall be punished together with him that made it. \textsuperscript{11} Therefore even upon the idols of the Gentiles shall there be a visitation: because in the creature of God they are become an abomination, and stumblingblocks to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the unwise.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life. \textsuperscript{13} For neither were they from the beginning, neither shall they be for ever. \textsuperscript{14} For by the vain glory of men they entered into the world, and therefore shall they come shortly to an end. \textsuperscript{15} For a father afflicted with untimely mourning, when he hath made an image of his child soon taken away, now honoured him as a god, which was then a dead man, and delivered to those that were under him ceremonies and sacrifices. \textsuperscript{16} Thus in process of time an ungodly custom grown strong was kept as a law, and graven images were worshipped by the commandments of kings. \textsuperscript{17} Whom men could not honour in presence, because they dwelt far off, they took the counterfeit of his visage from far, and made an express image of a king whom they honoured, to the end that by this their forwardness they might flatter him that was absent, as if he were present.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Also the singular diligence of the artificer did help to set forward the ignorant to more superstition. \textsuperscript{19} For he, peradventure willing to please one in authority, forced all his skill to make the resemblance of the best fashion. \textsuperscript{20} And so the multitude, allured by the grace of the work, took him now for a god, which a little before was but honoured as a man. \textsuperscript{21} And this was an occasion to deceive the world: for men, serving either calamity or tyranny, did ascribe unto stones and stocks the incommunicable name.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} Moreover this was not enough for them, that they erred in the knowledge of God; but whereas they lived in the great war of ignorance, those so great plagues called they peace. \textsuperscript{23} For whilst they slew their children in sacrifices, or used secret ceremonies, or made revellings of strange rites; \textsuperscript{24} they kept neither lives nor marriages any longer undefiled: but either one slew another traiterously or grieved him by adultery. \textsuperscript{25} So that there reigned in all men without exception, blood, manslaughter, theft, and dissimulation, corruption, unfaithfulness, tumults, perjury, \textsuperscript{26} disquieting of good men, forgetfulness of good turns, defiling of souls, changing of kind, disorder in marriages, adultery, and shameless uncleanness. \textsuperscript{27} For the worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil. \textsuperscript{28} For either they are mad when they be merry, or prophesy lies, or live unjustly, or else lightly forswear themselves. \textsuperscript{29} For insomuch as their trust is in idols which have no life, though they swear falsely, yet they look not to be hurt.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} Howbeit for both causes shall they be justly punished: both because they thought not well of God, giving heed unto idols, and also unjustly swore in deceit, despising holiness. \textsuperscript{31} For it is not the power of them by whom they swear: but it is the just vengeance of sinners, that punisheth always the offence of the ungodly.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 15}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} But thou, our God, art gracious and true, long-suffering, and in mercy ordering all things. \textsuperscript{2} For if we sin, we are thine, knowing thy power: but we will not sin, knowing that we are counted thine. \textsuperscript{3} For to know thee is perfect righteousness: yea, to know thy power is the root of immortality. \textsuperscript{4} For neither did the mischievous invention of men deceive us, nor an image spotted with divers colours, the painter's fruitless labour; \textsuperscript{5} the sight whereof enticeth fools to lust after it, and so they desire the form of a dead image, that hath no breath.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} Both they that make them, they that desire them, and they that worship them, are lovers of evil things, and are worthy to have such things to trust upon. \textsuperscript{7} For the potter, tempering soft earth, fashioneth every vessel with much labour for our service: yea, of the same clay he maketh both the vessels that serve for clean uses, and likewise also all such as serve to the contrary: but what is the use of either sort, the potter himself is the judge. \textsuperscript{8} And employing his labours lewdly, he maketh a vain god of the same clay, even he which a little before was made of earth himself, and within a little while after returneth to the same, out of the which he was taken, when his life which was lent him shall be demanded.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Notwithstanding his care is, not that he shall have much labour, nor that his life is short: but striveth to excel goldsmiths and silversmiths, and endeavoureth to do like the workers in brass, and counteth it his glory to make counterfeit things. \textsuperscript{10} His heart is ashes, his hope is more vile than earth, and his life of less value than clay: \textsuperscript{11} forasmuch as he knew not his Maker, and him that inspired into him an active soul, and breathed in a living spirit. \textsuperscript{12} But they counted our life a pastime, and our time here a market for gain: for, say they, we must be getting every way, though it be by evil means. \textsuperscript{13} For this man, that of earthly matter maketh brittle vessels and graven images, knoweth himself to offend above all others.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} And all the enemies of thy people, that hold them in subjection, are most foolish, and are more miserable than very babes. \textsuperscript{15} For they counted all the idols of the heathen to be gods: which neither have the use of eyes to see, nor noses to draw breath, nor ears to hear, nor fingers of hands to handle; and as for their feet, they are slow to go. \textsuperscript{16} For man made them, and he that borrowed his own spirit fashioned them: but no man can make a god like unto himself. \textsuperscript{17} For being mortal, he worketh a dead thing with wicked hands: for he himself is better than the things which he worshippeth: whereas he lived once, but they never. \textsuperscript{18} Yea, they worshipped those beasts also that are most hateful: for being compared together, some are worse than others. \textsuperscript{19} Neither are they beautiful, so much as to be desired in respect of beasts: but they went without the praise of God and his blessing.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 16}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Therefore by the like were they punished worthily, and by the multitude of beasts tormented. \textsuperscript{2} Instead of which punishment, dealing graciously with thine own people, thou preparedst for them meat of a strange taste, even quails to stir up their appetite: \textsuperscript{3} to the end that they, desiring food, might for the ugly sight of the beasts sent among them lothe even that, which they must needs desire; but these, suffering penury for a short space, might be made partakers of a strange taste. \textsuperscript{4} For it was requisite, that upon them exercising tyranny should come penury, which they could not avoid: but to these it should only be shewed how their enemies were tormented. \textsuperscript{5} For when the horrible fierceness of beasts came upon these, and they perished with the stings of crooked serpents, thy wrath endured not for ever:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} But they were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished, having a sign of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of thy law. \textsuperscript{7} For he that turned himself toward it was not saved by the thing that he saw, but by thee, that art the Saviour of all. \textsuperscript{8} And in this thou madest thine enemies confess, that it is thou who deliverest from all evil: \textsuperscript{9} for them the bitings of grasshoppers and flies killed, neither was there found any remedy for their life: for they were worthy to be punished by such. \textsuperscript{10} But thy sons not the very teeth of venomous dragons overcame: for thy mercy was by them, and healed them. \textsuperscript{11} For they were pricked, that they should remember thy words; and were quickly saved, that not falling into deep forgetfulness, they might be continually mindful of thy goodness.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} For it was neither herb, nor mollifying plaister, that restored them to health: but thy word, O Lord, which healeth all things. \textsuperscript{13} For thou hast power of life and death: thou leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again. \textsuperscript{14} A man indeed killeth through his malice: and the spirit, when it is gone forth, returneth not; neither the soul received up cometh again. \textsuperscript{15} But it is not possible to escape thine hand.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} For the ungodly, that denied to know thee, were scourged by the strength of thine arm: with strange rains, hails, and showers, were they persecuted, that they could not avoid, and through fire were they consumed.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} For, which is most to be wondered at, the fire had more force in the water, that quencheth all things: for the world fighteth for the righteous. \textsuperscript{18} For sometime the flame was mitigated, that it might not burn up the beasts that were sent against the ungodly; but themselves might see and perceive that they were persecuted with the judgment of God. \textsuperscript{19} And at another time it burneth even in the midst of water above the power of fire, that it might destroy the fruits of an unjust land. \textsuperscript{20} Instead whereof thou feddest thine own people with angels' food, and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man's delight, and agreeing to every taste. \textsuperscript{21} For thy sustenance declared thy sweetness unto thy children, and serving to the appetite of the eater, tempered itself to every man's liking. \textsuperscript{22} But snow and ice endured the fire, and melted not, that they might know that fire burning in the hail, and sparkling in the rain, did destroy the fruits of the enemies.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} But this again did even forget his own strength, that the righteous might be nourished. \textsuperscript{24} For the creature that serveth thee, who art the Maker, increaseth his strength against the unrighteous for their punishment, and abateth his strength for the benefit of such as put their trust in thee.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} Therefore even then was it altered into all fashions, and was obedient to thy grace, that nourisheth all things, according to the desire of them that had need: \textsuperscript{26} that thy children, O Lord, whom thou lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourisheth man: but that it is thy word, which preserveth them that put their trust in thee.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} For that which was not destroyed of the fire, being warmed with a little sunbeam, soon melted away: \textsuperscript{28} that it might be known, that we must prevent the sun to give thee thanks, and at the dayspring pray unto thee. \textsuperscript{29} For the hope of the unthankful shall melt away as the winter's hoar frost, and shall run away as unprofitable water.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 17}
