\noindent \textsuperscript{1} For great are thy judgments, and cannot be expressed: therefore unnurtured souls have erred. \textsuperscript{2} For when unrighteous men thought to oppress the holy nation; they being shut up in their houses, the prisoners of darkness, and fettered with the bonds of a long night, lay [there] exiled from the eternal providence. \textsuperscript{3} For while they supposed to lie hid in their secret sins, they were scattered under a dark veil of forgetfulness, being horribly astonished, and troubled with [strange] apparitions. \textsuperscript{4} For neither might the corner that held them keep them from fear: but noises [as of waters] falling down sounded about them, and sad visions appeared unto them with heavy countenances.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} No power of the fire might give them light: neither could the bright flames of the stars endure to lighten that horrible night. \textsuperscript{6} Only there appeared unto them a fire kindled of itself, very dreadful: for being much terrified, they thought the things which they saw to be worse than the sight they saw not. \textsuperscript{7} As for the illusions of art magic, they were put down, and their vaunting in wisdom was reproved with disgrace. \textsuperscript{8} For they, that promised to drive away terrors and troubles from a sick soul, were sick themselves of fear, worthy to be laughed at.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} For though no terrible thing did fear them; yet being scared with beasts that passed by, and hissing of serpents, \textsuperscript{10} they died for fear, denying that they saw the air, which could of no side be avoided.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} For wickedness, condemned by her own witness, is very timorous, and being pressed with conscience, always forecasteth grievous things. \textsuperscript{12} For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth. \textsuperscript{13} And the expectation from within, being less, counteth the ignorance more than the cause which bringeth the torment. \textsuperscript{14} But they sleeping the same sleep that night, which was indeed intolerable, and which came upon them out of the bottoms of inevitable hell, \textsuperscript{15} were partly vexed with monstrous apparitions, and partly fainted, their heart failing them: for a sudden fear, and not looked for, came upon them. \textsuperscript{16} So then whosoever there fell down was straitly kept, shut up in a prison without iron bars. \textsuperscript{17} For whether he were husbandman, or shepherd, or a labourer in the field, he was overtaken, and endured that necessity, which could not be avoided: for they were all bound with one chain of darkness.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Whether it were a whistling wind, or a melodious noise of birds among the spreading branches, or a pleasing fall of water running violently, \textsuperscript{19} or a terrible sound of stones cast down, or a running that could not be seen of skipping beasts, or a roaring voice of most savage wild beasts, or a rebounding echo from the hollow mountains: these things made them to swoon for fear. \textsuperscript{20} For the whole world shined with clear light, and none were hindered in their labour: \textsuperscript{21} over them only was spread a heavy night, an image of that darkness which should afterward receive them: but yet were they unto themselves more grievous than the darkness.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 18}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Nevertheless thy saints had a very great light, whose voice they hearing, and not seeing their shape, because they also had not suffered the same things, they counted them happy. \textsuperscript{2} But for that they did not hurt them now , of whom they had been wronged before, they thanked them, and besought them pardon for that they had been enemies. \textsuperscript{3} Instead whereof thou gavest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey, and a harmless sun to entertain them honourably. \textsuperscript{4} For they were worthy to be deprived of light, and imprisoned in darkness, who had kept thy sons shut up, by whom the uncorrupt light of the law was to be given unto the world.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} And when they had determined to slay the babes of the saints, one child being cast forth, and saved, to reprove them, thou tookest away the multitude of their children, and destroyedst them all together in a mighty water. \textsuperscript{6} Of that night were our fathers certified afore, that assuredly knowing unto what oaths they had given credence, they might afterwards be of good cheer.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies. \textsuperscript{8} For wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us, whom thou hadst called. \textsuperscript{9} For the righteous children of good men did sacrifice secretly, and with one consent made a holy law, that the saints should be like partakers of the same good and evil, the fathers now singing out the songs of praise.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} But on the other side there sounded an ill according cry of the enemies, and a lamentable noise was carried abroad for children that were bewailed. \textsuperscript{11} The master and the servant were punished after one manner; and like as the king, so suffered the common person.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} So they all together had innumerable dead with one kind of death; neither were the living sufficient to bury them: for in one moment the noblest offspring of them was destroyed. \textsuperscript{13} For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments; upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God. \textsuperscript{14} For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, \textsuperscript{15} thine Almighty word leaped from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction, \textsuperscript{16} and brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth. \textsuperscript{17} Then suddenly visions of horrible dreams troubled them sore, and terrors came upon them unlooked for. \textsuperscript{18} And one thrown here, and another there, half dead, shewed the cause of his death. \textsuperscript{19} For the dreams that troubled them did foreshew this, lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} Yea, the tasting of death touched the righteous also, and there was a destruction of the multitude in the wilderness: but the wrath endured not long. \textsuperscript{21} For then the blameless man made haste, and stood forth to defend them; and bringing the shield of his proper ministry, even prayer, and the propitiation of incense, set himself against the wrath, and so brought the calamity to an end, declaring that he was thy servant.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} So he overcame the destroyer, not with might of body, nor force of arms, but with a word subdued him that punished, alleging the oaths and covenants made with the fathers. \textsuperscript{23} For when the dead were now fallen down by heaps one upon another, standing between, he stayed the wrath, and parted the way to the living. \textsuperscript{24} For in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven, and thy Majesty upon the diadem of his head. \textsuperscript{25} Unto these the destroyer gave place, and they were afraid of them: for it was enough that they only tasted of the wrath.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom of Solomon 19}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} As for the ungodly, wrath came upon them without mercy unto the end: for he knew before what they would do; \textsuperscript{2} how that having given them leave to depart, and sent them hastily away, they would repent and pursue them. \textsuperscript{3} For whilst they were yet mourning and making lamentation at the graves of the dead, they added another foolish device, and pursued them as fugitives, whom they had intreated to be gone. \textsuperscript{4} For the destiny, whereof they were worthy, drew them unto this end, and made them forget the things that had already happened, that they might fulfil the punishment which was wanting to their torments: \textsuperscript{5} and that thy people might pass through a wonderful way: but they might find a strange death.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them, that thy children might be kept without hurt: \textsuperscript{7} as namely , a cloud shadowing the camp; and where water stood before, dry land appeared; and out of the Red sea a way without impediment; and out of the violent stream a green field: \textsuperscript{8} through which all the people went that were defended with thy hand, seeing thy marvellous strange wonders. \textsuperscript{9} For they went at large like horses, and leaped like lambs, praising thee, O Lord, who hadst delivered them. \textsuperscript{10} For they were yet mindful of the things that were done while they sojourned in the strange land, how the ground brought forth flies instead of cattle, and how the river cast up a multitude of frogs instead of fishes.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} But afterward they saw a new generation of fowls, when, being led with their appetite, they asked delicate meats. \textsuperscript{12} For quails came up unto them from the sea for their contentment. \textsuperscript{13} And punishments came upon the sinners not without former signs by the force of thunders: for they suffered justly according to their own wickedness, insomuch as they used a more hard and hateful behaviour toward strangers. \textsuperscript{14} For the Sodomites did not receive those, whom they knew not when they came: but these brought friends into bondage, that had well deserved of them. \textsuperscript{15} And not only so, but peradventure some respect shall be had of those, because they used strangers not friendly: \textsuperscript{16} but these very grievously afflicted them, whom they had received with feastings, and were already made partakers of the same laws with them. \textsuperscript{17} Therefore even with blindness were these stricken, as those were at the doors of the righteous man: when, being compassed about with horrible great darkness, every one sought the passage of his own doors.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} For the elements were changed in themselves by a kind of harmony, like as in a psaltery notes change the name of the tune, and yet are always sounds; which may well be perceived by the sight of the things that have been done. \textsuperscript{19} For earthly things were turned into watery, and the things, that before swam in the water, now went upon the ground. \textsuperscript{20} The fire had power in the water, forgetting his own virtue: and the water forgat his own quenching nature. \textsuperscript{21} On the other side, the flames wasted not the flesh of the corruptible living things, though they walked therein; neither melted they the icy kind of heavenly meat, that was of nature apt to melt. \textsuperscript{22} For in all things, O Lord, thou didst magnify thy people, and glorify them, neither didst thou lightly regard them: but didst assist them in every time and place.\par
\section*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus)}
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Whereas many and great things have been delivered unto us by the law and the prophets, and by others that have followed their steps, for the which things Israel ought to be commended for learning and wisdom: and whereof not only the readers must needs become skilful themselves,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity? \textsuperscript{3} Who can find out the height of heaven, and the breadth of the earth, and the deep, and wisdom?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Wisdom hath been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting. \textsuperscript{6} To whom hath the root of wisdom been revealed? or who hath known her wise counsels?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} There is one wise and greatly to be feared, the Lord sitting upon his throne. \textsuperscript{9} He created her, and saw her, and numbered her, and poured her out upon all his works. \textsuperscript{10} She is with all flesh according to his gift, and he hath given her to them that love him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} The fear of the Lord is honour, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing. \textsuperscript{12} The fear of the Lord maketh a merry heart, and giveth joy, and gladness, and long life. \textsuperscript{13} Whoso feareth the Lord, it shall go well with him at the last, and he shall find favour in the day of his death.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} To fear the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb. \textsuperscript{15} She hath built an everlasting foundation with men, and she shall continue with their seed. \textsuperscript{16} To fear the Lord is fulness of wisdom, and filleth men with her fruits. \textsuperscript{17} She filleth all their house with things desirable, and the garners with her increase. \textsuperscript{18} The fear of the Lord is a crown of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish. \textsuperscript{19} Wisdom raineth down skill and knowledge of understanding, and exalteth them to honour that hold her fast.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and the branches thereof are long life. \textsuperscript{22} A furious man cannot be justified; for the sway of his fury shall be his destruction. \textsuperscript{23} A patient man will bear for a time, and afterward joy shall spring up unto him. \textsuperscript{24} He will hide his words for a time, and the lips of many shall declare his wisdom. \textsuperscript{25} The parables of knowledge are in the treasures of wisdom: but godliness is an abomination to a sinner. \textsuperscript{26} If thou desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord shall give her unto thee. \textsuperscript{27} For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction: and faith and meekness are his delight.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} Distrust not the fear of the Lord when thou art poor; and come not unto him with a double heart. \textsuperscript{29} Be not a hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what thou speakest. \textsuperscript{30} Exalt not thyself, lest thou fall, and bring dishonour upon thy soul, and so the Lord discover thy secrets, and cast thee down in the midst of the congregation, because thou camest not in truth to the fear of the Lord, but thy heart is full of deceit.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} My son, if thou come to serve the Lord God, prepare thy soul for temptation. \textsuperscript{2} Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble. \textsuperscript{3} Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. \textsuperscript{4} Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate. \textsuperscript{5} For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity. \textsuperscript{6} Believe in him, and he will help thee; order thy way aright, and trust in him. \textsuperscript{7} Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest ye fall. \textsuperscript{8} Ye that fear the Lord, believe him; and your reward shall not fail. \textsuperscript{9} Ye that fear the Lord, hope for good, and for everlasting joy and mercy.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him? \textsuperscript{11} For the Lord is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saveth in time of affliction. \textsuperscript{12} Woe be to fearful hearts, and faint hands, and the sinner that goeth two ways!\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Woe unto him that is fainthearted! for he believeth not; therefore shall he not be defended. \textsuperscript{14} Woe unto you that have lost patience! and what will ye do when the Lord shall visit you?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} They that fear the Lord will not disobey his word; and they that love him will keep his ways. \textsuperscript{16} They that fear the Lord will seek that which is wellpleasing unto him; and they that love him shall be filled with the law. \textsuperscript{17} They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight, \textsuperscript{18} saying , We will fall into the hands of the Lord, and not into the hands of men: for as his majesty is, so is his mercy.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that ye may be safe. \textsuperscript{2} For the Lord hath given the father honour over the children, and hath confirmed the authority of the mother over the sons. \textsuperscript{3} Whoso honoureth his father maketh an atonement for his sins: \textsuperscript{4} and he that honoureth his mother is as one that layeth up treasure.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Whoso honoureth his father shall have joy of his own children; and when he maketh his prayer, he shall be heard. \textsuperscript{6} He that honoureth his father shall have a long life; and he that is obedient unto the Lord shall be a comfort to his mother, \textsuperscript{7} and will do service unto his parents, as to his masters.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} Honour thy father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon thee from them. \textsuperscript{9} For the blessing of the father establisheth the houses of children; but the curse of the mother rooteth out foundations. \textsuperscript{10} Glory not in the dishonour of thy father; for thy father's dishonour is no glory unto thee. \textsuperscript{11} For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father; and a mother in dishonour is a reproach to the children.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} My son, help thy father in his age, and grieve him not as long as he liveth. \textsuperscript{13} And if his understanding fail, have patience with him; and despise him not when thou art in thy full strength. \textsuperscript{14} For the relieving of thy father shall not be forgotten: and instead of sins it shall be added to build thee up. \textsuperscript{15} In the day of thine affliction it shall be remembered; thy sins also shall melt away, as the ice in the fair warm weather.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer; and he that angereth his mother is cursed of God.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} My son, go on with thy business in meekness; so shalt thou be beloved of him that is approved. \textsuperscript{18} The greater thou art, the more humble thyself, and thou shalt find favour before the Lord. \textsuperscript{20} For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honoured of the lowly.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} Seek not out the things that are too hard for thee, neither search the things that are above thy strength. \textsuperscript{22} But what is commanded thee, think thereupon with reverence ; for it is not needful for thee to see with thine eyes the things that are in secret. \textsuperscript{23} Be not curious in unnecessary matters; for more things are shewed unto thee than men understand. \textsuperscript{24} For many are deceived by their own vain opinion; and an evil suspicion hath overthrown their judgment.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{26} A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last; and he that loveth danger shall perish therein. \textsuperscript{27} An obstinate heart shall be laden with sorrows; and the wicked man shall heap sin upon sin. \textsuperscript{28} In the punishment of the proud there is no remedy; for the plant of wickedness hath taken root in him. \textsuperscript{29} The heart of the prudent will understand a parable; and an attentive ear is the desire of a wise man.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms maketh an atonement for sins. \textsuperscript{31} And he that requiteth good turns is mindful of that which may come hereafter; and when he falleth, he shall find a stay.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long. \textsuperscript{2} Make not a hungry soul sorrowful; neither provoke a man in his distress. \textsuperscript{3} Add not more trouble to a heart that is vexed; and defer not to give to him that is in need. \textsuperscript{4} Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away thy face from a poor man. \textsuperscript{5} Turn not away thine eye from the needy, and give him none occasion to curse thee: \textsuperscript{6} for if he curse thee in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him. \textsuperscript{7} Get thyself the love of the congregation, and bow thy head to a great man. \textsuperscript{8} Let it not grieve thee to bow down thine ear to the poor, and give him a friendly answer with meekness.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Deliver him that suffereth wrong from the hand of the oppressor; and be not fainthearted when thou sittest in judgment. \textsuperscript{10} Be as a father unto the fatherless, and instead of a husband unto their mother: so shalt thou be as the son of the most High, and he shall love thee more than thy mother doth.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her. \textsuperscript{12} He that loveth her loveth life; and they that seek to her early shall be filled with joy.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} He that holdeth her fast shall inherit glory; and wheresoever she entereth, the Lord will bless. \textsuperscript{14} They that serve her shall minister to the Holy One: and them that love her the Lord doth love. \textsuperscript{15} Whoso giveth ear unto her shall judge the nations: and he that attendeth unto her shall dwell securely. \textsuperscript{16} If a man commit himself unto her, he shall inherit her; and his generation shall hold her in possession. \textsuperscript{17} For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws. \textsuperscript{18} Then will she return the straight way unto him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets. \textsuperscript{19} But if he go wrong, she will forsake him, and give him over to his own ruin.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} Observe the opportunity, and beware of evil; and be not ashamed when it concerneth thy soul. \textsuperscript{21} For there is a shame that bringeth sin; and there is a shame which is glory and grace. \textsuperscript{22} Accept no person against thy soul, and let not the reverence of any man cause thee to fall. \textsuperscript{23} And refrain not to speak, when there is occasion to do good, and hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. \textsuperscript{24} For by speech wisdom shall be known: and learning by the word of the tongue. \textsuperscript{25} In no wise speak against the truth; but be abashed of the error of thine ignorance. \textsuperscript{26} Be not ashamed to confess thy sins; and force not the course of the river. \textsuperscript{27} Make not thyself an underling to a foolish man; neither accept the person of the mighty. \textsuperscript{28} Strive for the truth unto death, and the Lord shall fight for thee.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{29} Be not hasty in thy tongue, and in thy deeds slack and remiss. \textsuperscript{30} Be not as a lion in thy house, nor frantic among thy servants. \textsuperscript{31} Let not thine hand be stretched out to receive, and shut when thou shouldest repay.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Set not thy heart upon thy goods; and say not, I have enough for my life. \textsuperscript{2} Follow not thine own mind and thy strength, to walk in the ways of thy heart: \textsuperscript{3} and say not, Who shall control me for my works? for the Lord will surely revenge thy pride. \textsuperscript{4} Say not, I have sinned, and what harm hath happened unto me? for the Lord is longsuffering, he will in no wise let thee go. \textsuperscript{5} Concerning propitiation, be not without fear to add sin unto sin: \textsuperscript{6} and say not, His mercy is great; he will be pacified for the multitude of my sins: for mercy and wrath come from him, and his indignation resteth upon sinners.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Make no tarrying to turn to the Lord, and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of the Lord come forth, and in thy security thou shalt be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance. \textsuperscript{8} Set not thine heart upon goods unjustly gotten; for they shall not profit thee in the day of calamity.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Winnow not with every wind, and go not into every way: for so doth the sinner that hath a double tongue. \textsuperscript{10} Be stedfast in thy understanding; and let thy word be the same. \textsuperscript{11} Be swift to hear; and let thy life be sincere; and with patience give answer. \textsuperscript{12} If thou hast understanding, answer thy neighbour; if not, lay thy hand upon thy mouth. \textsuperscript{13} Honour and shame is in talk: and the tongue of man is his fall. \textsuperscript{14} Be not called a whisperer, and lie not in wait with thy tongue: for a foul shame is upon the thief, and an evil condemnation upon the double tongue. \textsuperscript{15} Be not ignorant of any thing in a great matter or a small.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 6}
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} Thou shalt eat up thy leaves, and lose thy fruit, and leave thyself as a dry tree.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} A wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it, and shall make him to be laughed to scorn of his enemies. \textsuperscript{5} Sweet language will multiply friends: and a fairspeaking tongue will increase kind greetings. \textsuperscript{6} Be in peace with many: nevertheless have but one counsellor of a thousand.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} If thou wouldest get a friend, prove him first, and be not hasty to credit him. \textsuperscript{8} For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of thy trouble. \textsuperscript{9} And there is a friend, who being turned to enmity and strife will discover thy reproach. \textsuperscript{10} Again, some friend is a companion at the table, and will not continue in the day of thy affliction. \textsuperscript{11} But in thy prosperity he will be as thyself, and will be bold over thy servants. \textsuperscript{12} If thou be brought low, he will be against thee, and will hide himself from thy face.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Separate thyself from thine enemies, and take heed of thy friends. \textsuperscript{14} A faithful friend is a strong defence: and he that hath found such an one hath found a treasure. \textsuperscript{15} Nothing doth countervail a faithful friend, and his excellency is invaluable. \textsuperscript{16} A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear the Lord shall find him. \textsuperscript{17} Whoso feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} My son, gather instruction from thy youth up: so shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age. \textsuperscript{19} Come unto her as one that ploweth and soweth, and wait for her good fruits: for thou shalt not toil much in labouring about her, but thou shalt eat of her fruits right soon. \textsuperscript{20} She is very unpleasant to the unlearned: he that is without understanding will not remain with her. \textsuperscript{21} She will lie upon him as a mighty stone of trial; and he will cast her from him ere it be long. \textsuperscript{22} For wisdom is according to her name, and she is not manifest unto many.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} Give ear, my son, receive my advice, and refuse not my counsel, \textsuperscript{24} and put thy feet into her fetters, and thy neck into her chain. \textsuperscript{25} Bow down thy shoulder, and bear her, and be not grieved with her bonds. \textsuperscript{26} Come unto her with thy whole heart, and keep her ways with all thy power. \textsuperscript{27} Search, and seek, and she shall be made known unto thee: and when thou hast got hold of her, let her not go. \textsuperscript{28} For at the last thou shalt find her rest, and that shall be turned to thy joy. \textsuperscript{29} Then shall her fetters be a strong defence for thee, and her chains a robe of glory. \textsuperscript{30} For there is a golden ornament upon her, and her bands are purple lace. \textsuperscript{31} Thou shalt put her on as a robe of honour, and shalt put her about thee as a crown of joy.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{32} My son, if thou wilt, thou shalt be taught: and if thou wilt apply thy mind, thou shalt be prudent. \textsuperscript{33} If thou love to hear, thou shalt receive understanding: and if thou bow thine ear, thou shalt be wise. \textsuperscript{34} Stand in the multitude of the elders; and cleave unto him that is wise. \textsuperscript{35} Be willing to hear every godly discourse: and let not the parables of understanding escape thee. \textsuperscript{36} And if thou seest a man of understanding, get thee betimes unto him, and let thy foot wear the steps of his door. \textsuperscript{37} Let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord, and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish thine heart, and give thee wisdom at thine own desire.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 7}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Do no evil, so shall no harm come unto thee. \textsuperscript{2} Depart from the unjust, and iniquity shall turn away from thee.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} My son, sow not upon the furrows of unrighteousness, and thou shalt not reap them sevenfold. \textsuperscript{4} Seek not of the Lord preeminence, neither of the king the seat of honour. \textsuperscript{5} Justify not thyself before the Lord; and boast not of thy wisdom before the king. \textsuperscript{6} Seek not to be judge, being not able to take away iniquity; lest at any time thou fear the person of the mighty, and lay a stumblingblock in the way of thy uprightness. \textsuperscript{7} Offend not against the multitude of a city, and then thou shalt not cast thyself down among the people. \textsuperscript{8} Bind not one sin upon another; for in one thou shalt not be unpunished. \textsuperscript{9} Say not, God will look upon the multitude of my oblations, and when I offer to the most high God, he will accept it. \textsuperscript{10} Be not fainthearted when thou makest thy prayer, and neglect not to give alms.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Laugh no man to scorn in the bitterness of his soul: for there is one which humbleth and exalteth. \textsuperscript{12} Devise not a lie against thy brother; neither do the like to thy friend. \textsuperscript{13} Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good. \textsuperscript{14} Use not many words in a multitude of elders, and make not much babbling when thou prayest. \textsuperscript{15} Hate not laborious work, neither husbandry, which the most High hath ordained. \textsuperscript{16} Number not thyself among the multitude of sinners, but remember that wrath will not tarry long. \textsuperscript{17} Humble thy soul greatly: for the vengeance of the ungodly is fire and worms. \textsuperscript{18} Change not a friend for any good by no means; neither a faithful brother for the gold of Suphir. \textsuperscript{19} Forego not a wise and good woman: for her grace is above gold. \textsuperscript{20} Whereas thy servant worketh truly, entreat him not evil, nor the hireling that bestoweth himself wholly for thee.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} Let thy soul love a good servant, and defraud him not of liberty. \textsuperscript{22} Hast thou cattle? have an eye to them: and if they be for thy profit, keep them with thee. \textsuperscript{23} Hast thou children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth. \textsuperscript{24} Hast thou daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them. \textsuperscript{25} Marry thy daughter, and so shalt thou have performed a weighty matter: but give her to a man of understanding. \textsuperscript{26} Hast thou a wife after thy mind? forsake her not.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} Honour thy father with thy whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of thy mother. \textsuperscript{28} Remember that thou wast begotten of them; and how canst thou recompense them the things that they have done for thee? \textsuperscript{29} Fear the Lord with all thy soul, and reverence his priests. \textsuperscript{30} Love him that made thee with all thy strength, and forsake not his ministers. \textsuperscript{31} Fear the Lord, and honour the priest: and give him his portion, as it is commanded thee: the firstfruits, and the trespass offering, and the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits of the holy things. \textsuperscript{32} And stretch thine hand unto the poor, that thy blessing may be perfected. \textsuperscript{33} A gift hath grace in the sight of every man living; and for the dead detain it not. \textsuperscript{34} Fail not to be with them that weep, and mourn with them that mourn. \textsuperscript{35} Be not slow to visit the sick: for that shall make thee to be beloved. \textsuperscript{36} Whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 8}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Strive not with a mighty man, lest thou fall into his hands. \textsuperscript{2} Be not at variance with a rich man, lest he overweigh thee: for gold hath destroyed many, and perverted the hearts of kings. \textsuperscript{3} Strive not with a man that is full of tongue, and heap not wood upon his fire. \textsuperscript{4} Jest not with a rude man, lest thy ancestors be disgraced. \textsuperscript{5} Reproach not a man that turneth from sin, but remember that we are all worthy of punishment. \textsuperscript{6} Dishonour not a man in his old age: for even some of us wax old. \textsuperscript{7} Rejoice not over thy greatest enemy being dead, but remember that we die all. \textsuperscript{8} Despise not the discourse of the wise, but acquaint thyself with their proverbs: for of them thou shalt learn instruction, and how to serve great men with ease.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Miss not the discourse of the elders: for they also learned of their fathers, and of them thou shalt learn understanding, and to give answer as need requireth. \textsuperscript{10} Kindle not the coals of a sinner, lest thou be burnt with the flame of his fire. \textsuperscript{11} Rise not up [in anger] at the presence of an injurious person, lest he lie in wait to entrap thee in thy words. \textsuperscript{12} Lend not unto him that is mightier than thyself; for if thou lendest him, count it but lost. \textsuperscript{13} Be not surety above thy power: for if thou be surety, take care to pay it. \textsuperscript{14} Go not to law with a judge; for they will judge for him according to his honour. \textsuperscript{15} Travel not by the way with a bold fellow, lest he become grievous unto thee: for he will do according to his own will, and thou shalt perish with him through his folly.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} Strive not with an angry man, and go not with him into a solitary place: for blood is as nothing in his sight; and where there is no help, he will overthrow thee. \textsuperscript{17} Consult not with a fool; for he cannot keep counsel. \textsuperscript{18} Do no secret thing before a stranger: for thou knowest not what he will bring forth. \textsuperscript{19} Open not thine heart to every man, lest he requite thee with a shrewd turn.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 9}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Be not jealous over the wife of thy bosom, and teach her not an evil lesson against thyself. \textsuperscript{2} Give not thy soul unto a woman to set her foot upon thy substance. \textsuperscript{3} Meet not with an harlot, lest thou fall into her snares. \textsuperscript{4} Use not much the company of a woman that is a singer, lest thou be taken with her attempts. \textsuperscript{5} Gaze not on a maid, that thou fall not by those things that are precious in her. \textsuperscript{6} Give not thy soul unto harlots, that thou lose not thine inheritance. \textsuperscript{7} Look not round about thee in the streets of the city, neither wander thou in the solitary places thereof. \textsuperscript{8} Turn away thine eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another's beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Sit not at all with another man's wife, nor sit down with her in thine arms, and spend not thy money with her at the wine; lest thine heart incline unto her, and so through thy desire thou fall into destruction. \textsuperscript{10} Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, thou shalt drink it with pleasure. \textsuperscript{11} Envy not the glory of a sinner: for thou knowest not what shall be his end. \textsuperscript{12} Delight not in the thing that the ungodly have pleasure in; but remember they shall not go unpunished unto their grave. \textsuperscript{13} Keep thee far from the man that hath power to kill: so shalt thou not doubt the fear of death: and if thou come unto him, make no fault, lest he take away thy life presently: remember that thou goest in the midst of snares, and that thou walkest upon the battlements of the city.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} As near as thou canst, guess at thy neighbour, and consult with the wise. \textsuperscript{15} Let thy talk be with the wise, and all thy communication in the law of the most High. \textsuperscript{16} And let just men eat and drink with thee; and let thy glorying be in the fear of the Lord. \textsuperscript{17} For the hand of the artificer the work shall be commended; and the wise ruler of the people for his speech. \textsuperscript{18} A man of an ill tongue is dangerous in his city; and he that is rash in his talk shall be hated.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 10}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered. \textsuperscript{2} As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein. \textsuperscript{3} An unwise king destroyeth his people; but through the prudence of them which are in authority the city shall be inhabited. \textsuperscript{4} The power of the earth is in the hand of the Lord, and in due time he will set over it one that is profitable. \textsuperscript{5} In the hand of God is the prosperity of man: and upon the person of the scribe shall he lay his honour.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} Bear not hatred to thy neighbour for every wrong; and do nothing at all by injurious practices. \textsuperscript{7} Pride is hateful before God and man: and by both doth one commit iniquity. \textsuperscript{8} Because of unrighteous dealings, injuries, and riches got by deceit, the kingdom is translated from one people to another.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Why is earth and ashes proud? There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for such an one setteth his own soul to sale; because while he liveth he casteth away his bowels. \textsuperscript{10} The physician cutteth off a long disease: and he that is to day a king to morrow shall die. \textsuperscript{11} For when a man is dead, he shall inherit creeping things, beasts, and worms. \textsuperscript{12} The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker. \textsuperscript{13} For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that hath it shall pour out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} The Lord hath cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead. \textsuperscript{15} The Lord hath plucked up the roots of the proud nations, and planted the lowly in their place. \textsuperscript{16} The Lord overthrew countries of the heathen, and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth. \textsuperscript{17} He took some of them away, and destroyed them, and hath made their memorial to cease from the earth. \textsuperscript{18} Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are born of a woman. \textsuperscript{19} They that fear the Lord are a sure seed, and they that love him an honourable plant: they that regard not the law are a dishonourable seed; they that transgress the commandments are a deceivable seed. \textsuperscript{20} Among brethren he that is chief is honourable; so are they that fear the Lord in his eyes. \textsuperscript{22} Whether he be rich, noble or poor, their glory is the fear of the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} It is not meet to despise the poor man that hath understanding; neither is it convenient to magnify a sinful man. \textsuperscript{24} Great men, and judges, and potentates, shall be honoured; yet is there none of them greater than he that feareth the Lord. \textsuperscript{25} Unto the servant that is wise shall they that are free do service: and he that hath knowledge will not grudge when he is reformed. \textsuperscript{26} Be not overwise in doing thy business; and boast not thyself in the time of thy distress. \textsuperscript{27} Better is he that laboureth, and aboundeth in all things, than he that boasteth himself, and wanteth bread.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} My son, glorify thy soul in meekness, and give it honour according to the dignity thereof. \textsuperscript{29} Who will justify him that sinneth against his own soul? and who will honour him that dishonoureth his own life? \textsuperscript{30} The poor man is honoured for his skill, and the rich man is honoured for his riches. \textsuperscript{31} He that is honoured in poverty, how much more in riches? and he that is dishonourable in riches, how much more in poverty?\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 11}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Wisdom lifteth up the head of him that is of low degree, and maketh him to sit among great men. \textsuperscript{2} Commend not a man for his beauty; neither abhor a man for his outward appearance. \textsuperscript{3} The bee is little among such as fly; but her fruit is the chief of sweet things. \textsuperscript{4} Boast not of thy clothing and raiment, and exalt not thyself in the day of honour: for the works of the Lord are wonderful, and his works among men are hidden. \textsuperscript{5} Many kings have sat down upon the ground; and one that was never thought of hath worn the crown. \textsuperscript{6} Many mighty men have been greatly disgraced; and the honourable delivered into other men's hands. \textsuperscript{7} Blame not before thou hast examined the truth: understand first, and then rebuke. \textsuperscript{8} Answer not before thou hast heard the cause: neither interrupt men in the midst of their talk. \textsuperscript{9} Strive not in a matter that concerneth thee not; and sit not in judgment with sinners.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} My son, meddle not with many matters: for if thou meddle much, thou shalt not be innocent; and if thou follow after, thou shalt not obtain, neither shalt thou escape by fleeing. \textsuperscript{11} There is one that laboureth, and taketh pains, and maketh haste, and is so much the more behind. \textsuperscript{12} Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty; yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate, \textsuperscript{13} and lifted up his head from misery; so that many that saw it marvelled at him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of the Lord. \textsuperscript{17} The gift of the Lord remaineth with the godly, and his favour bringeth prosperity for ever. \textsuperscript{18} There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward: \textsuperscript{19} whereas he saith, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die. \textsuperscript{20} Be stedfast in thy covenant, and be conversant therein, and wax old in thy work. \textsuperscript{21} Marvel not at the works of sinners; but trust in the Lord, and abide in thy labour: for it is an easy thing in the sight of the Lord on the sudden to make a poor man rich.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} The blessing of the Lord is in the reward of the godly, and suddenly he maketh his blessing to flourish. \textsuperscript{23} Say not, What profit is there of my service? and what good things shall I have hereafter? \textsuperscript{24} Again, say not, I have enough, and possess many things, and what evil can come to me hereafter? \textsuperscript{25} In the day of prosperity there is a forgetfulness of affliction: and in the day of affliction there is no more remembrance of prosperity. \textsuperscript{26} For it is an easy thing unto the Lord in the day of death to reward a man according to his ways. \textsuperscript{27} The affliction of an hour maketh a man forget pleasure: and in his end his deeds shall be discovered. \textsuperscript{28} Judge none blessed before his death: for a man shall be known in his children.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{29} Bring not every man into thine house: for the deceitful man hath many trains. \textsuperscript{30} Like as a partridge taken [and kept] in a cage, so is the heart of the proud: and like as a spy, watcheth he for thy fall: \textsuperscript{31} for he lieth in wait, and turneth good into evil, and in things worthy praise will lay blame upon thee. \textsuperscript{32} Of a spark of fire a heap of coals is kindled: and a sinful man layeth wait for blood. \textsuperscript{33} Take heed of a mischievous man, for he worketh wickedness: lest he bring upon thee a perpetual blot. \textsuperscript{34} Receive a stranger into thine house, and he will disturb thee, and turn thee out of thine own.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 12}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} When thou wilt do good, know to whom thou doest it; so shalt thou be thanked for thy benefits. \textsuperscript{2} Do good to the godly man, and thou shalt find a recompence; and if not from him, yet from the most High. \textsuperscript{3} There can no good come to him that is always occupied in evil, nor to him that giveth no alms. \textsuperscript{4} Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner. \textsuperscript{5} Do well unto him that is lowly, but give not to the ungodly: hold back thy bread, and give it not unto him, lest he overmaster thee thereby: for [else] thou shalt receive twice as much evil for all the good thou shalt have done unto him. \textsuperscript{6} For the most High hateth sinners, and will repay vengeance unto the ungodly, and keepeth them against the mighty day of their punishment.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Give unto the good, and help not the sinner. \textsuperscript{8} A friend cannot be known in prosperity: and an enemy cannot be hidden in adversity. \textsuperscript{9} In the prosperity of a man enemies will be grieved: but in his adversity even a friend will depart. \textsuperscript{10} Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness. \textsuperscript{11} Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him, and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a looking-glass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away. \textsuperscript{12} Set him not by thee, lest, when he hath overthrown thee, he stand up in thy place; neither let him sit at thy right hand, lest he seek to take thy seat, and thou at the last remember my words, and be pricked therewith.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Who will pity a charmer that is bitten with a serpent, or any such as come nigh wild beasts? \textsuperscript{14} So one that goeth to a sinner, and is defiled with him in his sins, who will pity? \textsuperscript{15} For a while he will abide with thee, but if thou begin to fall, he will not tarry. \textsuperscript{16} An enemy speaketh sweetly with his lips, but in his heart he imagineth how to throw thee into a pit: he will weep with his eyes, but if he find opportunity, he will not be satisfied with blood. \textsuperscript{17} If adversity come upon thee, thou shalt find him there first; and though he pretend to help thee, yet shall he undermine thee. \textsuperscript{18} He will shake his head, and clap his hands, and whisper much, and change his countenance.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 13}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} He that toucheth pitch shall be defiled therewith; and he that hath fellowship with a proud man shall be like unto him. \textsuperscript{2} Burden not thyself above thy power while thou livest; and have no fellowship with one that is mightier and richer than thyself: for how agree the kettle and the earthen pot together? for if the one be smitten against the other, it shall be broken.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} The rich man hath done wrong, and yet he threateneth withal: the poor is wronged, and he must intreat also. \textsuperscript{4} If thou be for his profit, he will use thee; but if thou have nothing, he will forsake thee. \textsuperscript{5} If thou have any thing, he will live with thee: yea, he will make thee bare, and will not be sorry for it. \textsuperscript{6} If he have need of thee, he will deceive thee, and smile upon thee, and put thee in hope; he will speak thee fair, and say, What wantest thou? \textsuperscript{7} And he will shame thee by his meats, until he have drawn thee dry twice or thrice, and at the last he will laugh thee to scorn: afterward, when he seeth thee, he will forsake thee, and shake his head at thee. \textsuperscript{8} Beware that thou be not deceived, and brought down in thy jollity.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} If thou be invited of a mighty man, withdraw thyself, and so much the more will he invite thee. \textsuperscript{10} Press thou not upon him, lest thou be put back; stand not far off, lest thou be forgotten. \textsuperscript{11} Affect not to be made equal unto him in talk, and believe not his many words: for with much communication will he tempt thee, and smiling upon thee will get out thy secrets: \textsuperscript{12} but cruelly he will lay up thy words, and will not spare to do thee hurt, and to put thee in prison. \textsuperscript{13} Observe, and take good heed, for thou walkest in peril of thy overthrowing: when thou hearest these things, awake in thy sleep.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} Every beast loveth his like, and every man loveth his neighbour. \textsuperscript{16} All flesh consorteth according to kind, and a man will cleave to his like. \textsuperscript{17} What fellowship hath the wolf with the lamb? so the sinner with the godly. \textsuperscript{18} What agreement is there between the hyena and a dog? and what peace between the rich and the poor? \textsuperscript{19} As the wild ass is the lion's prey in the wilderness: so the rich eat up the poor. \textsuperscript{20} As the proud hate humility: so doth the rich abhor the poor.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} A rich man beginning to fall is held up of his friends: but a poor man being down is thrust also away by his friends. \textsuperscript{22} When a rich man is fallen, he hath many helpers: he speaketh things not to be spoken, and yet men justify him: the poor man slipped, and yet they rebuked him too; he spake wisely, and could have no place. \textsuperscript{23} When a rich man speaketh, every man holdeth his tongue, and, look, what he saith, they extol it to the clouds: but if the poor man speak, they say, What fellow is this? and if he stumble, they will help to overthrow him. \textsuperscript{24} Riches are good unto him that hath no sin, and poverty is evil in the mouth of the ungodly.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} The heart of a man changeth his countenance, whether it be for good or evil. \textsuperscript{26} A cheerful countenance is a token of a heart that is in prosperity; and the finding out of parables is a wearisome labour of the mind.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 14}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Blessed is the man that hath not slipped with his mouth, and is not pricked with the multitude of sins. \textsuperscript{2} Blessed is he whose conscience hath not condemned him, and who is not fallen from his hope in the Lord .\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} Riches are not comely for a niggard: and what should an envious man do with money? \textsuperscript{4} He that gathereth by defrauding his own soul gathereth for others that shall spend his goods riotously. \textsuperscript{5} He that is evil to himself, to whom will he be good? he shall not take pleasure in his goods. \textsuperscript{6} There is none worse than he that envieth himself; and this is a recompence of his wickedness. \textsuperscript{7} And if he doeth good, he doeth it unwillingly; and at the last he will declare his wickedness. \textsuperscript{8} The envious man hath a wicked eye; he turneth away his face, and despiseth men. \textsuperscript{9} A covetous man's eye is not satisfied with his portion; and the iniquity of the wicked drieth up his soul. \textsuperscript{10} A wicked eye envieth [his] bread, and he is a niggard at his table.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} My son, according to thy ability do good to thyself, and give the Lord his due offering. \textsuperscript{12} Remember that death will not be long in coming, and that the covenant of the grave is not shewed unto thee. \textsuperscript{13} Do good unto thy friend before thou die, and according to thy ability stretch out thy hand and give to him. \textsuperscript{14} Defraud not thyself of the good day, and let not the part of a good desire overpass thee. \textsuperscript{15} Shalt thou not leave thy travails unto another? and thy labours to be divided by lot? \textsuperscript{16} Give, and take, and sanctify thy soul; for there is no seeking of dainties in the grave. \textsuperscript{17} All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, Thou shalt die the death. \textsuperscript{18} As of the green leaves on a thick tree, some fall, and some grow: so is the generation of flesh and blood, one cometh to an end, and another is born. \textsuperscript{19} Every work rotteth and consumeth away, and the worker thereof shall go withal.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} Blessed is the man that doth meditate good things in wisdom, and that reasoneth of holy things by his understanding. \textsuperscript{21} He that considereth her ways in his heart shall also have understanding in her secrets. \textsuperscript{22} Go after her as one that traceth, and lie in wait in her ways. \textsuperscript{23} He that prieth in at her windows shall also hearken at her doors. \textsuperscript{24} He that doth lodge near her house shall also fasten a pin in her walls. \textsuperscript{25} He shall pitch his tent nigh unto her, and shall lodge in a lodging where good things are. \textsuperscript{26} He shall set his children under her shelter, and shall lodge under her branches. \textsuperscript{27} By her he shall be covered from heat, and in her glory shall he dwell.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 15}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} He that feareth the Lord will do good; and he that hath the knowledge of the law shall obtain her; \textsuperscript{2} and as a mother shall she meet him, and receive him as a wife married of a virgin. \textsuperscript{3} With the bread of understanding shall she feed him, and give him the water of wisdom to drink. \textsuperscript{4} He shall be stayed upon her, and shall not be moved; and shall rely upon her, and shall not be confounded. \textsuperscript{5} She shall exalt him above his neighbours, and in the midst of the congregation shall she open his mouth. \textsuperscript{6} He shall find joy and a crown of gladness, and she shall cause him to inherit an everlasting name. \textsuperscript{7} But foolish men shall not attain unto her, and sinners shall not see her. \textsuperscript{8} For she is far from pride, and men that are liars cannot remember her.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner, for it was not sent him of the Lord. \textsuperscript{10} For praise shall be uttered in wisdom, and the Lord will prosper it. \textsuperscript{11} Say not thou, It is through the Lord that I fell away: for thou oughtest not to do the things that he hateth. \textsuperscript{12} Say not thou, He hath caused me to err: for he hath no need of the sinful man.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} The Lord hateth all abomination; and they that fear God love it not. \textsuperscript{14} He himself made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his counsel; \textsuperscript{15} if thou wilt, to keep the commandments, and to perform acceptable faithfulness. \textsuperscript{16} He hath set fire and water before thee: stretch forth thy hand unto whether thou wilt. \textsuperscript{17} Before man is life and death; and whether he liketh shall be given him. \textsuperscript{18} For the wisdom of the Lord is great, and he is mighty in power, and beholdeth all things: \textsuperscript{19} and his eyes are upon them that fear him, and he knoweth every work of man. \textsuperscript{20} He hath commanded no man to do wickedly, neither hath he given any man licence to sin.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 16}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons. \textsuperscript{2} Though they multiply, rejoice not in them, except the fear of the Lord be with them. \textsuperscript{3} Trust not thou in their life, neither respect their multitude: for one that is just is better than a thousand; and better it is to die without children, than to have them that are ungodly. \textsuperscript{4} For by one that hath understanding shall the city be replenished: but the kindred of the wicked shall speedily become desolate. \textsuperscript{5} Many such things have I seen with mine eyes, and mine ear hath heard greater things than these.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} In the congregation of the ungodly shall a fire be kindled; and in a rebellious nation wrath is set on fire. \textsuperscript{7} He was not pacified toward the old giants, who fell away in the strength of their foolishness. \textsuperscript{8} Neither spared he the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride. \textsuperscript{9} He pitied not the people of perdition, who were taken away in their sins: \textsuperscript{10} nor the six hundred thousand footmen, who were gathered together in the hardness of their hearts. \textsuperscript{11} And if there be one stiffnecked among the people, it is marvel if he escape unpunished: for mercy and wrath are with him; he is mighty to forgive and to pour out displeasure.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} As his mercy is great, so is his correction also: he judgeth a man according to his works. \textsuperscript{13} The sinner shall not escape with his spoils: and the patience of the godly shall not be frustrate. \textsuperscript{14} Make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Say not thou, I will hide myself from the Lord: shall any remember me from above? I shall not be remembered among so many people: for what is my soul among such an infinite number of creatures? \textsuperscript{18} Behold, the heaven, and the heaven of heavens, the deep, and the earth, and all that therein is, shall be moved when he shall visit. \textsuperscript{19} The mountains also and foundations of the earth shall be shaken with trembling, when he looketh upon them. \textsuperscript{20} No heart can think upon these things worthily: and who is able to conceive his ways? \textsuperscript{21} It is a tempest which no man can see: for the most part of his works are hid. \textsuperscript{22} Who can declare the works of his justice? or who can endure them? for his covenant is afar off. \textsuperscript{23} He that wanteth understanding will think upon vain things: and a foolish man erring imagineth follies.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} My son, hearken unto me, and learn knowledge, and mark my words with thy heart. \textsuperscript{25} I will shew forth doctrine in weight, and declare his knowledge exactly. \textsuperscript{26} The works of the Lord are done in judgment from the beginning: and from the time he made them he disposed the parts thereof. \textsuperscript{27} He garnished his works for ever, and the chief of them unto all generations: they neither labour, nor are weary, nor cease from their works. \textsuperscript{28} None of them hindereth another, and they shall never disobey his word. \textsuperscript{29} After this the Lord looked upon the earth, and filled it with his blessings. \textsuperscript{30} With all manner of living things hath he covered the face thereof; and they shall return into it again.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 17}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} The Lord created man of the earth, and turned him into it again. \textsuperscript{2} He gave them few days, and a short time, and power also over the things therein. \textsuperscript{3} He endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image, \textsuperscript{4} and put the fear of man upon all flesh, and gave him dominion over beasts and fowls. \textsuperscript{6} Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, gave he them to understand. \textsuperscript{7} Withal he filled them with the knowledge of understanding, and shewed them good and evil. \textsuperscript{8} He set his eye upon their hearts, that he might shew them the greatness of his works; \textsuperscript{10} and they shall praise his holy name, that they may search out his marvellous works.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage. \textsuperscript{12} He made an everlasting covenant with them, and shewed them his judgments. \textsuperscript{13} Their eyes saw the majesty of his glory, and their ears heard his glorious voice. \textsuperscript{14} And he said unto them, Beware of all unrighteousness; and he gave every man commandment concerning his neighbour. \textsuperscript{15} Their ways are ever before him, and shall not be hid from his eyes. \textsuperscript{17} For in the division of the nations of the whole earth he set a ruler over every people; but Israel is the Lord's portion: \textsuperscript{19} Therefore all their works are as the sun before him, and his eyes are continually upon their ways. \textsuperscript{20} None of their unrighteous deeds are hid from him, but all their sins are before the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} The alms of a man is as a signet with him, and he will keep the good deeds of man as the apple of the eye, and give repentance to his sons and daughters. \textsuperscript{23} Afterwards he will rise up and reward them, and render their recompence upon their heads. \textsuperscript{24} But unto them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} Return unto the Lord, and forsake thy sins, make thy prayer before his face, and offend less. \textsuperscript{26} Turn again to the most High, and turn away from iniquity: for he will lead thee out of darkness into the light of health, and hate thou abomination vehemently. \textsuperscript{27} Who shall praise the most High in the grave, instead of them which live and give thanks? \textsuperscript{28} Thanksgiving perisheth from the dead, as from one that is not: the living and sound in heart shall praise the Lord. \textsuperscript{29} How great is the lovingkindness of the Lord our God, and his compassion unto such as turn unto him in holiness! \textsuperscript{30} For all things cannot be in men, because the son of man is not immortal.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{31} What is brighter than the sun? yet the light thereof faileth: and flesh and blood will imagine evil. \textsuperscript{32} He vieweth the power of the height of heaven; and all men are but earth and ashes.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 18}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} He that liveth for ever created all things in general. \textsuperscript{2} The Lord only is righteous. \textsuperscript{4} To none hath he given power to declare his works; and who shall find out his noble acts? \textsuperscript{5} Who shall number the strength of his majesty? and who shall also tell out his mercies?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} As for the wondrous works of the Lord, there may nothing be taken from them, neither may any thing be put unto them, neither can the ground of them be found out. \textsuperscript{7} When a man hath done, then he beginneth; and when he leaveth off, then he shall be doubtful. \textsuperscript{8} What is man, and whereto serveth he; what is his good, and what is his evil? \textsuperscript{9} The number of a man's days at the most is an hundred years. \textsuperscript{10} As a drop of water unto the sea, and a gravel-stone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity. \textsuperscript{11} Therefore is God patient with them, and poureth forth his mercy upon them. \textsuperscript{12} He saw and perceived their end to be evil; therefore he multiplied his compassion. \textsuperscript{13} The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of the Lord is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teacheth, and bringeth again, as a shepherd his flock. \textsuperscript{14} He hath mercy on them that receive discipline, and that diligently seek after his judgments.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} My son, blemish not thy good deeds, neither use uncomfortable words when thou givest any thing. \textsuperscript{16} Shall not the dew assuage the heat? so is a word better than a gift. \textsuperscript{17} Lo, is not a word better than a gift? but both are with a gracious man. \textsuperscript{18} A fool will upbraid churlishly, and a gift of the envious consumeth the eyes. \textsuperscript{19} Learn before thou speak, and use physic or ever thou be sick. \textsuperscript{20} Before judgment examine thyself, and in the day of visitation thou shalt find mercy. \textsuperscript{21} Humble thyself before thou be sick, and in the time of sins shew repentance.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} Let nothing hinder thee to pay thy vow in due time, and defer not until death to be justified. \textsuperscript{23} Before thou prayest, prepare thyself; and be not as one that tempteth the Lord. \textsuperscript{24} Think upon the wrath that shall be at the end, and the time of vengeance, when he shall turn away his face. \textsuperscript{25} When thou hast enough, remember the time of hunger: and when thou art rich, think upon poverty and need. \textsuperscript{26} From the morning until the evening the time is changed, and all things are soon done before the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} A wise man will fear in every thing, and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence: but a fool will not observe time. \textsuperscript{28} Every man of understanding knoweth wisdom, and will give praise unto him that found her. \textsuperscript{29} They that had understanding in sayings became also wise themselves, and poured forth exquisite parables.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites. \textsuperscript{31} If thou givest thy soul the desires that please her, she will make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies that malign thee. \textsuperscript{32} Take not pleasure in much good cheer, neither be tied to the expence thereof. \textsuperscript{33} Be not made a beggar by banqueting upon borrowing, when thou hast nothing in thy purse.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 19}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} A labouring man that is given to drunkenness shall not be rich: and he that contemneth small things shall fall by little and little. \textsuperscript{2} Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away: and he that cleaveth to harlots will become impudent. \textsuperscript{3} Moths and worms shall have him to heritage, and a bold man shall be taken away.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} He that is hasty to give credit is light-minded; and he that sinneth shall offend against his own soul. \textsuperscript{5} Whoso taketh pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned: \textsuperscript{6} but he that hateth babbling hath less of evil.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Rehearse not unto another that which is told unto thee, and thou shalt fare never the worse. \textsuperscript{8} Whether it be to friend or foe, talk not of other men's lives; and if thou canst not without offence, reveal them not. \textsuperscript{9} For he heard and observed thee, and when time cometh he will hate thee. \textsuperscript{10} If thou hast heard a word, let it die with thee; and be bold, it will not burst thee. \textsuperscript{11} A fool travaileth with a word, as a woman in labour of a child. \textsuperscript{12} As an arrow that sticketh in a man's thigh, so is a word within a fool's belly. \textsuperscript{13} Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more. \textsuperscript{14} Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. \textsuperscript{15} Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} There is one that slippeth in his speech, but not from his heart; and who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Admonish thy neighbour before thou threaten him; and give place to the law of the most High. \textsuperscript{20} The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law. \textsuperscript{22} The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, neither at any time the counsel of sinners prudence. \textsuperscript{23} There is a wickedness, and the same an abomination; and there is a fool wanting in wisdom.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} He that hath small understanding, and feareth God, is better than one that hath much wisdom, and transgresseth the law of the most High. \textsuperscript{25} There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is unjust; and there is one that turneth aside to make judgment appear. \textsuperscript{26} There is a wicked man that hangeth down his head sadly; but inwardly he is full of deceit, \textsuperscript{27} casting down his countenance, and making as if he heard not: where he is not known, he will do thee a mischief before thou be aware. \textsuperscript{28} And if for want of power he be hindered from sinning, yet when he findeth opportunity he will do evil. \textsuperscript{29} A man may be known by his look, and one that hath understanding by his countenance, when thou meetest him. \textsuperscript{30} A man's attire, and excessive laughter, and gait, shew what he is.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 20}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} There is a reproof that is not comely: again, some man holdeth his tongue, and he is wise.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} It is much better to reprove, than to be angry secretly: \textsuperscript{3} and he that confesseth his fault shall be preserved from hurt. \textsuperscript{4} As is the lust of an eunuch to deflower a virgin; so is he that executeth judgment with violence.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becometh hateful. \textsuperscript{6} Some man holdeth his tongue, because he hath not to answer: and some keepeth silence, knowing his time. \textsuperscript{7} A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity: but a babbler and a fool will regard no time. \textsuperscript{8} He that useth many words shall be abhorred; and he that taketh to himself authority therein shall be hated. \textsuperscript{9} There is a sinner that hath good success in evil things; and there is a gain that turneth to loss. \textsuperscript{10} There is a gift that shall not profit thee; and there is a gift whose recompence is double. \textsuperscript{11} There is an abasement because of glory; and there is that lifteth up his head from a low estate. \textsuperscript{12} There is that buyeth much for a little, and repayeth it sevenfold.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} A wise man by his words maketh himself beloved: but the graces of fools shall be poured out. \textsuperscript{14} The gift of a fool shall do thee no good when thou hast it; neither yet of the envious for his necessity: for he looketh to receive many things for one. \textsuperscript{15} He giveth little, and upbraideth much; he openeth his mouth like a crier; to-day he lendeth, and to-morrow will he ask it again: such an one is to be hated of God and man. \textsuperscript{16} The fool saith, I have no friends, I have no thank for all my good deeds, and they that eat my bread speak evil of me. \textsuperscript{17} How oft, and of how many shall he be laughed to scorn!\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} To slip upon a pavement is better than to slip with the tongue: so the fall of the wicked shall come speedily. \textsuperscript{19} An unseasonable tale will always be in the mouth of the unwise. \textsuperscript{20} A wise sentence shall be rejected when it cometh out of a fool's mouth; for he will not speak it in due season. \textsuperscript{21} There is that is hindered from sinning through want: and when he taketh rest, he shall not be troubled. \textsuperscript{22} There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness, and by accepting of persons overthroweth himself. \textsuperscript{23} There is that for bashfulness promiseth to his friend, and maketh him his enemy for nothing. \textsuperscript{24} A lie is a foul blot in a man, yet it is continually in the mouth of the untaught.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} A thief is better than a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall have destruction to heritage. \textsuperscript{26} The disposition of a liar is dishonourable, and his shame is ever with him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} A wise man shall promote himself to honour with his words: and he that hath understanding will please great men. \textsuperscript{28} He that tilleth his land shall increase his heap: and he that pleaseth great men shall get pardon for iniquity. \textsuperscript{29} Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and stop up his mouth that he cannot reprove. \textsuperscript{30} Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both? \textsuperscript{31} Better is he that hideth his folly than a man that hideth his wisdom.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 21}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} My son, hast thou sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for thy former sins. \textsuperscript{2} Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men. \textsuperscript{3} All iniquity is as a two edged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed. \textsuperscript{4} To terrify and do wrong will waste riches: thus the house of proud men shall be made desolate. \textsuperscript{5} A prayer out of a poor man's mouth reacheth to the ears of God, and his judgment cometh speedily. \textsuperscript{6} He that hateth reproof is in the way of sinners: but he that feareth the Lord will repent from his heart.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} An eloquent man is known far and near ; but a man of understanding knoweth when he slippeth. \textsuperscript{8} He that buildeth his house with other men's money is like one that gathereth himself stones for the tomb of his burial. \textsuperscript{9} The congregation of the wicked is like tow wrapped together: and the end of them is a flame of fire to destroy them. \textsuperscript{10} The way of sinners is made plain with stones, but at the end thereof is the pit of hell. \textsuperscript{11} He that keepeth the law of the Lord getteth the understanding thereof: and the perfection of the fear of the Lord is wisdom. \textsuperscript{12} He that is not wise will not be taught: but there is a wisdom which multiplieth bitterness. \textsuperscript{13} The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood: and his counsel is like a pure fountain of life. \textsuperscript{14} The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he liveth.\par
