\noindent \textsuperscript{1} The pride of the height, the clear firmament, the beauty of heaven, with his glorious shew; \textsuperscript{2} the sun when it appeareth, declaring at his rising a marvellous instrument, the work of the most High: \textsuperscript{3} at noon it parcheth the country, and who can abide the burning heat thereof? \textsuperscript{4} A man blowing a furnace is in works of heat, but the sun burneth the mountains three times more; breathing out fiery vapours, and sending forth bright beams, it dimmeth the eyes. \textsuperscript{5} Great is the Lord that made it; and at his commandment it runneth hastily. \textsuperscript{6} He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world. \textsuperscript{7} From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection. \textsuperscript{8} The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven; \textsuperscript{9} the beauty of heaven, the glory of the stars, an ornament giving light in the highest places of the Lord. \textsuperscript{10} At the commandment of the Holy One they will stand in their order, and never faint in their watches. \textsuperscript{11} Look upon the rainbow, and praise him that made it; very beautiful it is in the brightness thereof. \textsuperscript{12} It compasseth the heaven about with a glorious circle, and the hands of the most High have bended it. \textsuperscript{13} By his commandment he maketh the snow to fall apace, and sendeth swiftly the lightnings of his judgment. \textsuperscript{14} Through this the treasures are opened: and clouds fly forth as fowls. \textsuperscript{15} By his great power he maketh the clouds firm, and the hailstones are broken small.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} At his sight the mountains are shaken, and at his will the south wind bloweth. \textsuperscript{17} The noise of the thunder maketh the earth to tremble: so doth the northern storm and the whirlwind: as birds flying he scattereth the snow, and the falling down thereof is as the lighting of grasshoppers: \textsuperscript{18} the eye marvelleth at the beauty of the whiteness thereof, and the heart is astonished at the raining of it. \textsuperscript{19} The hoarfrost also as salt he poureth on the earth, and being congealed, it becometh sharp peaks.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} When the cold north wind bloweth, and the water is congealed into ice, it abideth upon every gathering together of water, and clotheth the water as with a breastplate. \textsuperscript{21} It devoureth the mountains, and burneth the wilderness, and consumeth the grass as fire. \textsuperscript{22} A present remedy of all is a mist coming speedily: a dew coming after heat refresheth.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands therein. \textsuperscript{24} They that sail on the sea tell of the danger thereof; and when we hear it with our ears, we marvel thereat. \textsuperscript{25} For therein be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts, the race of whales. \textsuperscript{26} By him the end of them hath prosperous success, and by his word all things consist.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} We may speak much, and yet come short; wherefore in sum, he is all. \textsuperscript{28} How shall we be able to magnify him? for he is great above all his works. \textsuperscript{29} The Lord is terrible and very great, and marvellous is his power. \textsuperscript{30} When ye glorify the Lord, exalt him as much as ye can; for even yet will he far exceed: and when ye exalt him, put forth all your strength, and be not weary; for ye can never go far enough. \textsuperscript{31} Who hath seen him, that he might tell us? and who can magnify him as he is? \textsuperscript{32} There are yet hid greater things than these be, for we have seen but a few of his works. \textsuperscript{33} For the Lord hath made all things; and to the godly hath he given wisdom.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 44}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us. \textsuperscript{2} The Lord hath wrought great glory by them through his great power from the beginning. \textsuperscript{3} Such as did bear rule in their kingdoms, men renowned for their power, giving counsel by their understanding, and declaring prophecies: \textsuperscript{4} leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their knowledge of learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent in their instruction: \textsuperscript{5} such as found out musical tunes, and recited verses in writing: \textsuperscript{6} rich men furnished with ability, living peaceably in their habitations: \textsuperscript{7} all these were honoured in their generations, and were the glory of their times. \textsuperscript{8} There be of them that have left a name behind them, that their praises might be reported. \textsuperscript{9} And some there be, which have no memorial; who are perished, as though they had never been; and are become as though they had never been born; and their children after them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} But these were merciful men, whose righteousness hath not been forgotten. \textsuperscript{11} With their seed shall continually remain a good inheritance, and their children are within the covenant. \textsuperscript{12} Their seed standeth fast, and their children for their sakes. \textsuperscript{13} Their seed shall remain for ever, and their glory shall not be blotted out. \textsuperscript{14} Their bodies are buried in peace; but their name liveth for evermore. \textsuperscript{15} The people will tell of their wisdom, and the congregation will shew forth their praise.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, being an example of repentance to all generations. \textsuperscript{17} Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he was taken in exchange [for the world;] therefore was he left as a remnant unto the earth, when the flood came. \textsuperscript{18} An everlasting covenant was made with him, that all flesh shall perish no more by the flood.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} Abraham was a great father of many people: in glory was there none like unto him; \textsuperscript{20} who kept the law of the most High, and was in covenant with him: he established the covenant in his flesh; and when he was proved, he was found faithful. \textsuperscript{21} Therefore he assured him by an oath, that he would bless the nations in his seed, and that he would multiply him as the dust of the earth, and exalt his seed as the stars, and cause them to inherit from sea to sea, and from the river unto the utmost part of the land.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} With Isaac did he establish likewise, for Abraham his father's sake, the blessing of all men, and the covenant, \textsuperscript{23} and made it rest upon the head of Jacob. He acknowledged him in his blessing, and gave him an heritage, and divided his portions; among the twelve tribes did he part them.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 45}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And he brought out of him a merciful man, which found favour in the sight of all flesh; even Moses, beloved of God and men, whose memorial is blessed. \textsuperscript{2} He made him like to the glorious saints, and magnified him, so that his enemies stood in fear of him. \textsuperscript{3} By his words he caused the wonders to cease, and he made him glorious in the sight of kings, and gave him a commandment for his people, and shewed him part of his glory. \textsuperscript{4} He sanctified him in his faithfulness and meekness, and chose him out of all men. \textsuperscript{5} He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his covenants, and Israel his judgments.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} He exalted Aaron, an holy man like unto him, even his brother, of the tribe of Levi. \textsuperscript{7} An everlasting covenant he made with him, and gave him the priesthood among the people; he beautified him with comely ornaments, and clothed him with a robe of glory. \textsuperscript{8} He put upon him perfect glory; and strengthened him with rich garments, with breeches, with a long robe, and the ephod. \textsuperscript{9} And he compassed him with pomegranates and with many golden bells round about, that as he went there might be a sound, and a noise made that might be heard in the temple for a memorial to the children of his people; \textsuperscript{10} with a holy garment, with gold, and blue silk, and purple, the work of the embroiderer, with a breastplate of judgment, with the revealers of truth; \textsuperscript{11} with twisted scarlet, the work of the cunning workman, with precious stones graven like seals, and set in gold, the work of the jeweller, with a writing engraved for a memorial, after the number of the tribes of Israel. \textsuperscript{12} He set a crown of gold upon the mitre, wherein was engraven Holiness, an ornament of honour, a costly work, the desires of the eyes, goodly and beautiful.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Before him there were none such, neither did ever any stranger put them on, but only his children and his children's children perpetually. \textsuperscript{14} Their sacrifices shall be wholly consumed every day twice continually.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} Moses consecrated him, and anointed him with holy oil; this was appointed unto him by an everlasting covenant, and to his seed, so long as the heavens should remain, that they should minister unto him, and execute the office of the priesthood, and bless the people in his name.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} He chose him out of all men living to offer sacrifices to the Lord, incense, and a sweet savour, for a memorial, to make reconciliation for his people. \textsuperscript{17} He gave unto him his commandments, and authority in the statutes of judgments, that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and inform Israel in his laws.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Strangers conspired together against him, and maligned him in the wilderness, even the men that were of Dathan's and Abiron's side, and the congregation of Core, with fury and wrath.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} This the Lord saw, and it displeased him, and in his wrathful indignation were they consumed: he did wonders upon them, to consume them with the fiery flame. \textsuperscript{20} But he made Aaron more honourable, and gave him an heritage, and divided unto him the firstfruits of the increase; especially he prepared bread in abundance: \textsuperscript{21} for they eat of the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gave unto him and his seed. \textsuperscript{22} Howbeit in the land of the people he had no inheritance, neither had he any portion among the people: for the Lord himself is his portion and inheritance.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} The third in glory is Phinees the son of Eleazar, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord, and stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel. \textsuperscript{24} Therefore was there a covenant of peace made with him, that he should be the chief of the sanctuary and of his people, and that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever: \textsuperscript{25} according to the covenant made with David son of Jesse, of the tribe of Juda, that the inheritance of the king should be to his posterity alone: so the inheritance of Aaron should also be unto his seed. \textsuperscript{26} God give you wisdom in your heart to judge his people in righteousness, that their good things be not abolished, and that their glory may endure for ever.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 46}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Jesus the son of Nave was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God, and taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them, that he might set Israel in their inheritance. \textsuperscript{2} How great glory gat he, when he did lift up his hands, and stretched out his sword against the cities! \textsuperscript{3} Who before him has so stood? for the Lord himself brought his enemies over to him. \textsuperscript{4} Did not the sun go back by his means? and was not one day as long as two? \textsuperscript{5} He called upon the most high Lord, when the enemies pressed upon him on every side; and the great Lord heard him. \textsuperscript{6} And with hailstones of mighty power he made the battle to fall violently upon the nations, and by their falling he destroyed them that resisted, that the nations might know all their strength, because he fought in the sight of the Lord, and he followed the Mighty One.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} In the time of Moses also he did a work of mercy, he and Caleb the son of Jephunne, in that they withstood the enemy, and withheld the people from sin, and appeased the wicked murmuring. \textsuperscript{8} And of six hundred thousand people on foot, they two alone were preserved to bring them into the heritage, even unto the land that floweth with milk and honey.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} The Lord gave strength also unto Caleb, which remained with him unto his old age: so that he entered upon the high places of the land, and his seed obtained it for an heritage: \textsuperscript{10} that all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord. \textsuperscript{11} And concerning the judges, every one by name, whose heart went not a whoring, nor departed from the Lord, let their memory be blessed. \textsuperscript{12} Let their bones flourish out of their place, and let the name of them that were honoured be continued upon their children.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Samuel, the prophet of the Lord, beloved of his Lord, established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people. \textsuperscript{14} By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the Lord had respect unto Jacob. \textsuperscript{15} By his faithfulness he was found a true prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithful in vision. \textsuperscript{16} He called upon the mighty Lord, when his enemies pressed upon him on every side, when he offered the sucking lamb. \textsuperscript{17} And the Lord thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard. \textsuperscript{18} And he destroyed the rulers of the Tyrians, and all the princes of the Philistines.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} And before his long sleep he made protestation in the sight of the Lord and his anointed, I have not taken any man's goods, so much as a shoe: and no man did accuse him. \textsuperscript{20} And after his death he prophesied, and shewed the king his end, and lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy, to blot out the wickedness of the people.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 47}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel. \textsuperscript{3} He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs. \textsuperscript{4} Slew he not a giant, when he was yet but young? and did he not take away reproach from the people, when he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, and beat down the boasting of Goliath? \textsuperscript{5} for he called upon the most high Lord; and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior, and set up the horn of his people.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} So the people honoured him with ten thousands, and praised him in the blessings of the Lord in that he gave him a crown of glory. \textsuperscript{7} For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and brought to nought the Philistines his adversaries, and brake their horn in sunder unto this day. \textsuperscript{8} In all his works he praised the Holy One most high with words of glory; with his whole heart he sang songs, and loved him that made him. \textsuperscript{9} He set singers also before the altar, that by their voices they might make sweet melody, and daily sing praises in their songs. \textsuperscript{10} He beautified their feasts, and set in order the solemn times until the end, that they might praise his holy name, and that the temple might sound from morning.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel. \textsuperscript{12} After him rose up a wise son, and for his sake he dwelt at large. \textsuperscript{13} Solomon reigned in a peaceable time, and was honoured; for God made all quiet round about him, that he might build an house in his name, and prepare his sanctuary for ever. \textsuperscript{14} How wise wast thou in thy youth, and, as a flood, filled with understanding! \textsuperscript{15} Thy soul covered the whole earth, and thou filledst it with dark parables.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} Thy name went far unto the islands; and for thy peace thou wast beloved. \textsuperscript{17} The countries marvelled at thee for thy songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations. \textsuperscript{18} By the name of the Lord God, which is called the Lord God of Israel, thou didst gather gold as tin, and didst multiply silver as lead. \textsuperscript{19} Thou didst bow thy loins unto women, and by thy body thou wast brought into subjection. \textsuperscript{20} Thou didst stain thy honour, and pollute thy seed: so that thou broughtest wrath upon thy children, and wast grieved for thy folly. \textsuperscript{21} So the kingdom was divided, and out of Ephraim ruled a rebellious kingdom.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} But the Lord will never leave off his mercy, neither shall any of his works perish, neither will he abolish the posterity of his elect, and the seed of him that loveth him he will not take away: wherefore he gave a remnant unto Jacob, and out of him a root unto David.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} Thus rested Solomon with his fathers, and of his seed he left behind him Roboam, even the foolishness of the people, and one that had no understanding, who turned away the people through his counsel. There was also Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, and shewed Ephraim the way of sin: \textsuperscript{24} and their sins were multiplied exceedingly, that they were driven out of the land. \textsuperscript{25} For they sought out all wickedness, till the vengeance came upon them.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp. \textsuperscript{2} He brought a sore famine upon them, and by his zeal he diminished their number. \textsuperscript{3} By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven, and also three times brought down fire. \textsuperscript{4} O Elias, how wast thou honoured in thy wondrous deeds! and who may glory like unto thee! \textsuperscript{5} Who didst raise up a dead man from death, and his soul from the place of the dead, by the word of the most High: \textsuperscript{6} who broughtest kings to destruction, and honourable men from their bed: \textsuperscript{7} who heardest the rebuke of the Lord in Sinai, and in Horeb the judgment of vengeance: \textsuperscript{8} who anointedst kings to take revenge, and prophets to succeed after him: \textsuperscript{9} who wast taken up in a whirlwind of fire, and in a chariot of fiery horses: \textsuperscript{10} who wast ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the Lord's judgment, before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob. \textsuperscript{11} Blessed are they that saw thee, and slept in love; for we shall surely live.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind; and Eliseus was filled with his spirit: whilst he lived, he was not moved with the presence of any prince, neither could any bring him into subjection. \textsuperscript{13} No word could overcome him; and after his death his body prophesied. \textsuperscript{14} He did wonders in his life, and at his death were his works marvellous.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} For all this the people repented not, neither departed they from their sins, till they were spoiled and carried out of their land, and were scattered through all the earth: yet there remained a small people, and a ruler in the house of David: \textsuperscript{16} of whom some did that which was pleasing to God , and some multiplied sins.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Ezekias fortified his city, and brought in water into the midst thereof: he digged the hard rock with iron, and made wells for waters. \textsuperscript{18} In his time Sennacherib came up, and sent Rabsaces, and lifted up his hand against Sion, and boasted proudly. \textsuperscript{19} Then trembled their hearts and hands, and they were in pain, as women in travail.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} But they called upon the Lord who is merciful, and stretched out their hands toward him: and immediately the Holy One heard them out of heaven, and delivered them by the ministry of Esay. \textsuperscript{21} He smote the host of the Assyrians, and his angel destroyed them. \textsuperscript{22} For Ezekias had done the thing that pleased the Lord, and was strong in the ways of David his father, as Esay the prophet, who was great and faithful in his vision, had commanded him. \textsuperscript{23} In his time the sun went backward, and he lengthened the king's life. \textsuperscript{24} He saw by an excellent spirit what should come to pass at the last, and he comforted them that mourned in Sion. \textsuperscript{25} He shewed what should come to pass for ever, and secret things or ever they came.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 49}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} The remembrance of Josias is like the composition of the perfume that is made by the art of the apothecary: it is sweet as honey in all mouths, and as music at a banquet of wine. \textsuperscript{2} He behaved himself uprightly in the conversion of the people, and took away the abominations of iniquity. \textsuperscript{3} He directed his heart unto the Lord, and in the time of the ungodly he established the worship of God. \textsuperscript{4} All, except David and Ezekias and Josias, were defective: for they forsook the law of the most High, even the kings of Juda failed; \textsuperscript{5} for they gave their power unto others, and their glory to a strange nation.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} They burnt the chosen city of the sanctuary, and made the streets desolate, according to the prophecy of Jeremias. \textsuperscript{7} For they entreated him evil, who nevertheless was a prophet, sanctified in his mother's womb, that he might root out, and afflict, and destroy; and that he might build up also, and plant. \textsuperscript{8} It was Ezekiel who saw the glorious vision, which was shewed him upon the chariot of the cherubim. \textsuperscript{9} For he made mention of the enemies under the figure of the rain, and directed them that went right. \textsuperscript{10} And of the twelve prophets let the memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish again out of their place: for they comforted Jacob, and delivered them by assured hope. \textsuperscript{11} How shall we magnify Zorobabel? he was even as a signet on the right hand:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} So was Jesus the son of Josedec: who in their time builded the house, and set up an holy temple to the Lord, which was prepared for everlasting glory. \textsuperscript{13} And among the elect was Neemias, whose renown is great, who raised up for us the walls that were fallen, and set up the gates and the bars, and raised up our ruins again. \textsuperscript{14} But upon the earth was no man created like Enoch; for he was taken from the earth. \textsuperscript{15} Neither was there a man born like unto Joseph, a governor of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord. \textsuperscript{16} Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in the creation.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 50}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again, and in his days fortified the temple: \textsuperscript{2} and by him was built from the foundation the double height, the high fortress of the wall about the temple: \textsuperscript{3} in his days the cistern to receive water, being in compass as the sea, was covered with plates of brass: \textsuperscript{4} he took care of the temple that it should not fall, and fortified the city against besieging: \textsuperscript{5} how was he honoured in the midst of the people in his coming out of the sanctuary! \textsuperscript{6} He was as the morning star in the midst of a cloud, and as the moon at the full: \textsuperscript{7} as the sun shining upon the temple of the most High, and as the rainbow giving light in the bright clouds: \textsuperscript{8} and as the flower of roses in the spring of the year, as lilies by the rivers of waters, and as the branches of the frankincense tree in the time of summer: \textsuperscript{9} as fire and incense in the censer, and as a vessel of beaten gold set with all manner of precious stones: \textsuperscript{10} and as a fair olive tree budding forth fruit, and as a cypress tree which groweth up to the clouds.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} When he put on the robe of honour, and was clothed with the perfection of glory, when he went up to the holy altar, he made the garment of holiness honourable. \textsuperscript{12} When he took the portions out of the priests' hands, he himself stood by the hearth of the altar, compassed with his brethren round about, as a young cedar in Libanus; and as palm trees compassed they him round about. \textsuperscript{13} So were all the sons of Aaron in their glory, and the oblations of the Lord in their hands, before all the congregation of Israel. \textsuperscript{14} And finishing the service at the altar, that he might adorn the offering of the most high Almighty, \textsuperscript{15} he stretched out his hand to the cup, and poured of the blood of the grape, he poured out at the foot of the altar a sweetsmelling savour unto the most high King of all.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} Then shouted the sons of Aaron, and sounded the silver trumpets, and made a great noise to be heard, for a remembrance before the most High. \textsuperscript{17} Then all the people together hasted, and fell down to the earth upon their faces to worship their Lord God Almighty, the most High. \textsuperscript{18} The singers also sang praises with their voices, with great variety of sounds was there made sweet melody. \textsuperscript{19} And the people besought the Lord, the most High, by prayer before him that is merciful, till the solemnity of the Lord was ended, and they had finished his service.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} Then he went down, and lifted up his hands over the whole congregation of the children of Israel, to give the blessing of the Lord with his lips, and to rejoice in his name. \textsuperscript{21} And they bowed themselves down to worship the second time, that they might receive a blessing from the most High. \textsuperscript{22} Now therefore bless ye the God of all, which only doeth wondrous things every where, which exalteth our days from the womb, and dealeth with us according to his mercy. \textsuperscript{23} He grant us joyfulness of heart, and that peace may be in our days in Israel for ever: \textsuperscript{24} that he would confirm his mercy with us, and deliver us at his time!\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} There be two manner of nations which my heart abhorreth, and the third is no nation: \textsuperscript{26} they that sit upon the mountain of Samaria, and they that dwell among the Philistines, and that foolish people that dwell in Sichem.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} Jesus the son of Sirach of Jerusalem hath written in this book the instruction of understanding and knowledge, who out of his heart poured forth wisdom. \textsuperscript{28} Blessed is he that shall be exercised in these things: and he that layeth them up in his heart shall become wise. \textsuperscript{29} For if he do them, he shall be strong to all things: for the light of the Lord is his path.\par
\subsection*{Wisdom Of Jesus The Son Of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 51}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} I will thank thee, O Lord and King, and praise thee, O God my Saviour: I do give praise unto thy name: \textsuperscript{2} for thou art my defender and helper, and hast preserved my body from destruction, and from the snare of the slanderous tongue, and from the lips that forge lies, and hast been mine helper against mine adversaries: \textsuperscript{3} and hast delivered me, according to the multitude of thy mercies and greatness of thy name, from the teeth of them that were ready to devour me, and out of the hands of such as sought after my life, and from the manifold afflictions which I had; \textsuperscript{4} from the choking of fire on every side, and from the midst of the fire which I kindled not; \textsuperscript{5} from the depth of the belly of hell, from an unclean tongue, and from lying words.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} By an accusation to the king from an unrighteous tongue my soul drew near even unto death, my life was near to the hell beneath. \textsuperscript{7} They compassed me on every side, and there was no man to help me: I looked for the succour of men, but there was none. \textsuperscript{8} Then thought I upon thy mercy, O Lord, and upon thy acts of old, how thou deliverest such as wait for thee, and savest them out of the hands of the enemies. \textsuperscript{9} Then lifted I up my supplication from the earth, and prayed for deliverance from death. \textsuperscript{10} I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the days of my trouble, and in the time of the proud, when there was no help. \textsuperscript{11} I will praise thy name continually, and will sing praise with thanksgiving; and so my prayer was heard: \textsuperscript{12} for thou savedst me from destruction, and deliveredst me from the evil time: therefore will I give thanks, and praise thee, and bless thy name, O Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} When I was yet young, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer. \textsuperscript{14} I prayed for her before the temple, and will seek her out even to the end. \textsuperscript{15} Even from the flower till the grape was ripe hath my heart delighted in her: my foot went the right way, from my youth up sought I after her. \textsuperscript{16} I bowed down mine ear a little, and received her, and gat much learning. \textsuperscript{17} I profited therein, therefore will I ascribe the glory unto him that giveth me wisdom. \textsuperscript{18} For I purposed to do after her, and earnestly I followed that which is good; so shall I not be confounded.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} My soul hath wrestled with her, and in my doings I was exact: I stretched forth my hands to the heaven above, and bewailed my ignorances of her. \textsuperscript{20} I directed my soul unto her, and I found her in pureness: I have had my heart joined with her from the beginning, therefore shall I not be forsaken. \textsuperscript{21} My heart was troubled in seeking her: therefore have I gotten a good possession. \textsuperscript{22} The Lord hath given me a tongue for my reward, and I will praise him therewith.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} Draw near unto me, ye unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning. \textsuperscript{24} Wherefore are ye slow, and what say ye of these things, seeing your souls are very thirsty? \textsuperscript{25} I opened my mouth, and said, Buy her for yourselves without money. \textsuperscript{26} Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find. \textsuperscript{27} Behold with your eyes, how that I have had but little labour, and have gotten unto me much rest. \textsuperscript{28} Get learning with a great sum of money, and get much gold by her.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{29} Let your soul rejoice in his mercy, and be not ashamed of his praise. \textsuperscript{30} Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.\par
\section*{Baruch}
\subsection*{Baruch 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And these are the words of the book, which Baruch the son of Nerias, the son of Maasias, the son of Sedecias, the son of Asadias, the son of Chelcias, wrote in Babylon, \textsuperscript{2} in the fifth year, and in the seventh day of the month, what time as the Chaldeans took Jerusalem, and burnt it with fire.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} And Baruch did read the words of this book in the hearing of Jechonias the son of Joachim king of Juda, and in the ears of all the people that came to hear the book, \textsuperscript{4} and in the hearing of the nobles, and of the king's sons, and in the hearing of the elders, and of all the people, from the lowest unto the highest, even of all them that dwelt at Babylon by the river Sud. \textsuperscript{5} Whereupon they wept, fasted, and prayed before the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} They made also a collection of money according to every man's power: \textsuperscript{7} and they sent it to Jerusalem unto Joachim the high priest, the son of Chelcias, son of Salom, and to the priests, and to all the people which were found with him at Jerusalem, \textsuperscript{8} at the same time when he received the vessels of the house of the Lord, that were carried out of the temple, to return them into the land of Juda, the tenth day of the month Sivan, namely , silver vessels, which Sedecias the son of Josias king of Juda had made, \textsuperscript{9} after that Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon had carried away Jechonias, and the princes, and the captives, and the mighty men, and the people of the land, from Jerusalem, and brought them unto Babylon.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} And they said, Behold, we have sent you money to buy you burnt offerings, and sin offerings, and incense, and prepare ye manna, and offer upon the altar of the Lord our God; \textsuperscript{11} and pray for the life of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and for the life of Balthasar his son, that their days may be upon earth as the days of heaven: \textsuperscript{12} and the Lord will give us strength, and lighten our eyes, and we shall live under the shadow of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and under the shadow of Balthasar his son, and we shall serve them many days, and find favour in their sight.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Pray for us also unto the Lord our God, for we have sinned against the Lord our God; and unto this day the fury of the Lord and his wrath is not turned from us. \textsuperscript{14} And ye shall read this book which we have sent unto you, to make confession in the house of the Lord, upon the feasts and solemn days.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} And ye shall say, To the Lord our God belongeth righteousness, but unto us the confusion of faces, as it is come to pass this day, unto them of Juda, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, \textsuperscript{16} and to our kings, and to our princes, and to our priests, and to our prophets, and to our fathers: \textsuperscript{17} for we have sinned before the Lord, \textsuperscript{18} and disobeyed him, and have not hearkened unto the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in the commandments that he gave us openly: \textsuperscript{19} since the day that the Lord brought our forefathers out of the land of Egypt, unto this present day, we have been disobedient unto the Lord our God, and we have been negligent in not hearing his voice.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} Wherefore the evils cleaved unto us, and the curse, which the Lord appointed by Moses his servant at the time that he brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt, to give us a land that floweth with milk and honey, like as it is to see this day. \textsuperscript{21} Nevertheless we have not hearkened unto the voice of the Lord our God, according unto all the words of the prophets, whom he sent unto us: \textsuperscript{22} but every man followed the imagination of his own wicked heart, to serve strange gods, and to do evil in the sight of the Lord our God.\par
\subsection*{Baruch 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Therefore the Lord hath made good his word, which he pronounced against us, and against our judges that judged Israel, and against our kings, and against our princes, and against the men of Israel and Juda, \textsuperscript{2} to bring upon us great plagues, such as never happened under the whole heaven, as it came to pass in Jerusalem, according to the things that were written in the law of Moses; \textsuperscript{3} that a man should eat the flesh of his own son, and the flesh of his own daughter. \textsuperscript{4} Moreover he hath delivered them to be in subjection to all the kingdoms that are round about us, to be as a reproach and desolation among all the people round about, where the Lord hath scattered them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Thus we were cast down, and not exalted, because we have sinned against the Lord our God, and have not been obedient unto his voice.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} To the Lord our God appertaineth righteousness: but unto us and to our fathers open shame, as appeareth this day. \textsuperscript{7} For all these plagues are come upon us, which the Lord hath pronounced against us. \textsuperscript{8} Yet have we not prayed before the Lord, that we might turn every one from the imaginations of his wicked heart. \textsuperscript{9} Wherefore the Lord watched over us for evil, and the Lord hath brought it upon us: for the Lord is righteous in all his works which he hath commanded us. \textsuperscript{10} Yet we have not hearkened unto his voice, to walk in the commandments of the Lord, that he hath set before us.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} And now, O Lord God of Israel, that hast brought thy people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and high arm, and with signs, and with wonders, and with great power, and hast gotten thyself a name, as appeareth this day: \textsuperscript{12} O Lord our God, we have sinned, we have done ungodly, we have dealt unrighteously in all thine ordinances.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Let thy wrath turn from us: for we are but a few left among the heathen, where thou hast scattered us.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} Hear our prayers, O Lord, and our petitions, and deliver us for thine own sake, and give us favour in the sight of them which have led us away: \textsuperscript{15} that all the earth may know that thou art the Lord our God, because Israel and his posterity is called by thy name.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} O Lord, look down from thine holy house, and consider us: bow down thine ear, O Lord, to hear us.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Open thine eyes, and behold; for the dead that are in the graves, whose souls are taken from their bodies, will give unto the Lord neither praise nor righteousness: \textsuperscript{18} but the soul that is greatly vexed, which goeth stooping and feeble, and the eyes that fail, and the hungry soul, will give thee praise and righteousness, O Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} Therefore we do not make our humble supplication before thee, O Lord our God, for the righteousness of our fathers, and of our kings, \textsuperscript{20} for thou hast sent out thy wrath and indignation upon us, as thou hast spoken by thy servants the prophets, saying ,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} Thus saith the Lord, Bow down your shoulders to serve the king of Babylon: so shall ye remain in the land that I gave unto your fathers. \textsuperscript{22} But if ye will not hear the voice of the Lord, to serve the king of Babylon, \textsuperscript{23} I will cause to cease out of the cities of Juda, and from without Jerusalem, the voice of mirth, and the voice of joy, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride: and the whole land shall be desolate of inhabitants. \textsuperscript{24} But we would not hearken unto thy voice, to serve the king of Babylon: therefore hast thou made good the words that thou spakest by thy servants the prophets, namely, that the bones of our kings, and the bones of our fathers, should be taken out of their places.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} And lo, they are cast out to the heat of the day, and to the frost of the night, and they died in great miseries by famine, by sword, and by pestilence. \textsuperscript{26} And the house which is called by thy name hast thou laid waste, as it is to be seen this day, for the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Juda.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} O Lord our God, thou hast dealt with us after all thy goodness, and according to all that great mercy of thine, \textsuperscript{28} as thou spakest by thy servant Moses in the day when thou didst command him to write thy law before the children of Israel, saying,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{29} If ye will not hear my voice, surely this very great multitude shall be turned into a small number among the nations, where I will scatter them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves, \textsuperscript{31} and shall know that I am the Lord their God: for I will give them an heart, and ears to hear: \textsuperscript{32} and they shall praise me in the land of their captivity, and think upon my name, \textsuperscript{33} and return from their stiff neck, and from their wicked deeds: for they shall remember the way of their fathers, which sinned before the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{34} And I will bring them again into the land which I promised with an oath unto their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they shall be lords of it: and I will increase them, and they shall not be diminished. \textsuperscript{35} And I will make an everlasting covenant with them to be their God, and they shall be my people: and I will no more drive my people of Israel out of the land that I have given them.\par
\subsection*{Baruch 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, the soul in anguish, the troubled spirit, crieth unto thee. \textsuperscript{2} Hear, O Lord, and have mercy; for thou art merciful: and have pity upon us, because we have sinned before thee. \textsuperscript{3} For thou endurest for ever, and we perish utterly.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites, and of their children, which have sinned before thee, and not hearkened unto the voice of thee their God: for the which cause these plagues cleave unto us. \textsuperscript{5} Remember not the iniquities of our forefathers: but think upon thy power and thy name now at this time. \textsuperscript{6} For thou art the Lord our God, and thee, O Lord, will we praise.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} And for this cause thou hast put thy fear in our hearts, to the intent that we should call upon thy name, and praise thee in our captivity: for we have called to mind all the iniquity of our forefathers, that sinned before thee.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} Behold, we are yet this day in our captivity, where thou hast scattered us, for a reproach and a curse, and to be subject to payments, according to all the iniquities of our fathers, which departed from the Lord our God.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Hear, Israel, the commandments of life: give ear to understand wisdom. \textsuperscript{10} How happeneth it, Israel, that thou art in thine enemies' land, that thou art waxen old in a strange country, that thou art defiled with the dead, \textsuperscript{11} that thou art counted with them that go down into the grave? \textsuperscript{12} Thou hast forsaken the fountain of wisdom. \textsuperscript{13} For if thou hadst walked in the way of God, thou shouldest have dwelled in peace for ever.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} Learn where is wisdom, where is strength, where is understanding; that thou mayest know also where is length of days, and life, where is the light of the eyes, and peace. \textsuperscript{15} Who hath found out her place? or who hath come into her treasures?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} Where are the princes of the heathen, and such as ruled the beasts upon the earth; \textsuperscript{17} they that had their pastime with the fowls of the air, and they that hoarded up silver and gold, wherein men trust, and made no end of their getting? \textsuperscript{18} For they that wrought in silver, and were so careful, and whose works are unsearchable, \textsuperscript{19} they are vanished and gone down to the grave, and others are come up in their stead.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} Young men have seen light, and dwelt upon the earth; but the way of knowledge have they not known, \textsuperscript{21} nor understood the paths thereof, nor laid hold of it: their children were far off from that way. \textsuperscript{22} It hath not been heard of in Chanaan, neither hath it been seen in Theman.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} The Agarenes that seek wisdom upon earth, the merchants of Meran and of Theman, the authors of fables, and searchers out of understanding; none of these have known the way of wisdom, or remembered her paths.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} O Israel, how great is the house of God! and how large is the place of his possession! \textsuperscript{25} Great, and hath none end; high, and unmeasurable. \textsuperscript{26} There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war. \textsuperscript{27} Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them: \textsuperscript{28} but they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{29} Who hath gone up into heaven, and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds? \textsuperscript{30} Who hath gone over the sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold? \textsuperscript{31} No man knoweth her way, nor thinketh of her path.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{32} But he that knoweth all things knoweth her, and hath found her out with his understanding: he that prepared the earth for evermore hath filled it with fourfooted beasts: \textsuperscript{33} he that sendeth forth light, and it goeth, calleth it again , and it obeyeth him with fear. \textsuperscript{34} The stars shined in their watches, and rejoiced: when he calleth them, they say, Here we be; and so with cheerfulness they shewed light unto him that made them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{35} This is our God, and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him. \textsuperscript{36} He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved. \textsuperscript{37} Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.\par
\subsection*{Baruch 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die. \textsuperscript{2} Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it: walk in the presence of the light thereof, that thou mayest be illuminated. \textsuperscript{3} Give not thine honour to another, nor the things that are profitable unto thee to a strange nation.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} O Israel, happy are we: for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us. \textsuperscript{5} Be of good cheer, my people, the memorial of Israel. \textsuperscript{6} Ye were sold to the nations, not for [your] destruction: but because ye moved God to wrath, ye were delivered unto the enemies. \textsuperscript{7} For ye provoked him that made you by sacrificing unto devils and not to God. \textsuperscript{8} Ye have forgotten the everlasting God, that brought you up; and ye have grieved Jerusalem, that nursed you.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} For when she saw the wrath of God coming upon you, she said, Hearken, O ye that dwell about Sion: God hath brought upon me great mourning; \textsuperscript{10} for I saw the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting brought upon them. \textsuperscript{11} With joy did I nourish them; but sent them away with weeping and mourning.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} Let no man rejoice over me, a widow, and forsaken of many, who for the sins of my children am left desolate; because they departed from the law of God. \textsuperscript{13} They knew not his statutes, nor walked in the ways of his commandments, nor trod in the paths of discipline in his righteousness.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} Let them that dwell about Sion come, and remember ye the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting hath brought upon them. \textsuperscript{15} For he hath brought a nation upon them from far, a shameless nation, and of a strange language, who neither reverenced old man, nor pitied child, \textsuperscript{16} and they have carried away the dear beloved children of the widow, and left her that was alone desolate without daughters. \textsuperscript{17} But what can I help you? \textsuperscript{18} For he that brought these plagues upon you will deliver you from the hands of your enemies. \textsuperscript{19} Go your way, O my children, go your way: for I am left desolate. \textsuperscript{20} I have put off the clothing of peace, and put upon me the sackcloth of my prayer: I will cry unto the Everlasting in my days.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} Be of good cheer, O my children, cry unto the Lord, and he shall deliver you from the power and hand of the enemies.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} For my hope is in the Everlasting, that he will save you: and joy is come unto me from the Holy One, because of the mercy which shall soon come unto you from the Everlasting your Saviour.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} For I sent you out with mourning and weeping: but God will give you to me again with joy and gladness for ever. \textsuperscript{24} Like as now the neighbours of Sion have seen your captivity: so shall they see shortly your salvation from your God, which shall come upon you with great glory, and brightness of the Everlasting.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you from God: for thine enemy hath persecuted thee; but shortly thou shalt see his destruction, and shalt tread upon his neck. \textsuperscript{26} My delicate ones have gone rough ways, and were taken away as a flock caught of the enemies.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} Be of good comfort, O my children, and cry unto God: for ye shall be remembered of him that brought these things upon you. \textsuperscript{28} For as it was your mind to go astray from God: so, being returned, seek him ten times more. \textsuperscript{29} For he that hath brought these plagues upon you shall bring you everlasting joy again with your salvation.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} Take a good heart, O Jerusalem: for he that gave thee that name will comfort thee. \textsuperscript{31} Miserable are they that afflicted thee, and rejoiced at thy fall. \textsuperscript{32} Miserable are the cities which thy children served: miserable is she that received thy sons. \textsuperscript{33} For as she rejoiced at thy ruin, and was glad of thy fall: so shall she be grieved for her own desolation. \textsuperscript{34} For I will take away the rejoicing of her great multitude, and her pride shall be turned into mourning. \textsuperscript{35} For fire shall come upon her from the Everlasting, long to endure; and she shall be inhabited of devils for a great time.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{36} O Jerusalem, look about thee toward the east, and behold the joy that cometh unto thee from God. \textsuperscript{37} Lo, thy sons come, whom thou sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.\par
\subsection*{Baruch 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Put off, O Jerusalem, the garment of thy mourning and affliction, and put on the comeliness of the glory that cometh from God for ever.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} Cast about thee a double garment of the righteousness which cometh from God; and set a diadem on thine head of the glory of the Everlasting. \textsuperscript{3} For God will shew thy brightness unto every country under heaven. \textsuperscript{4} For thy name shall be called of God for ever The peace of righteousness, and The glory of God's worship.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold thy children gathered from the west unto the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God. \textsuperscript{6} For they departed from thee on foot, and were led away of their enemies: but God bringeth them unto thee exalted with glory, as children of the kingdom.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} For God hath appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and vallies filled up, to make even the ground, that Israel may go safely in the glory of God. \textsuperscript{8} Moreover even the woods and every sweetsmelling tree shall overshadow Israel by the commandment of God. \textsuperscript{9} For God shall lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that cometh from him.\par
\section*{Epistle of Jeremy}
\subsection*{Epistle of Jeremy 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} A copy of an epistle, which Jeremy sent unto them which were to be led captives into Babylon by the king of the Babylonians, to certify them, as it was commanded him of God.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} Because of the sins which ye have committed before God, ye shall be led away captives into Babylon by Nabuchodonosor king of the Babylonians. \textsuperscript{3} So when ye be come unto Babylon, ye shall remain there many years, and for a long season, namely, seven generations: and after that I will bring you away peaceably from thence.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Now shall ye see in Babylon gods of silver, and of gold, and of wood, borne upon shoulders, which cause the nations to fear. \textsuperscript{5} Beware therefore that ye in no wise be like to strangers, neither be ye afraid of them, when ye see the multitude before them and behind them, worshipping them. \textsuperscript{6} But say ye in your hearts, O Lord, we must worship thee. \textsuperscript{7} For mine angel is with you, and I myself caring for your souls.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} As for their tongue, it is polished by the workman, and they themselves are gilded and laid over with gold; yet are they but false, and cannot speak. \textsuperscript{9} And taking gold, as it were for a virgin that loveth to go gay, they make crowns for the heads of their gods. \textsuperscript{10} Sometimes also the priests convey from their gods gold and silver, and bestow it upon themselves. \textsuperscript{11} Yea, they will give thereof to the common harlots, and deck them as men with garments, [being] gods of silver, and gods of gold, and wood.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} Yet cannot these gods save themselves from rust and moths, though they be covered with purple raiment. \textsuperscript{13} They wipe their faces because of the dust of the temple, when there is much upon them. \textsuperscript{14} And he that cannot put to death one that offendeth him holdeth a sceptre, as though he were a judge of the country. \textsuperscript{15} He hath also in his right hand a dagger and an axe: but cannot deliver himself from war and thieves. \textsuperscript{16} Whereby they are known not to be gods: therefore fear them not.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} For like as a vessel that a man useth is nothing worth when it is broken; even so it is with their gods: when they be set up in the temple, their eyes be full of dust through the feet of them that come in. \textsuperscript{18} And as the doors are made sure on every side upon him that offendeth the king, as being committed to suffer death; even so the priests make fast their temples with doors, with locks, and bars, lest their gods be spoiled with robbers.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} They light them candles, yea, more than for themselves, whereof they cannot see one. \textsuperscript{20} They are as one of the beams of the temple, yet they say their hearts are gnawed upon by things creeping out of the earth; and when they eat them and their clothes, they feel it not. \textsuperscript{21} Their faces are blacked through the smoke that cometh out of the temple. \textsuperscript{22} Upon their bodies and heads sit bats, swallows, and birds, and the cats also. \textsuperscript{23} By this ye may know that they are no gods: therefore fear them not.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} Notwithstanding the gold that is about them to make them beautiful, except they wipe off the rust, they will not shine: for neither when they were molten did they feel it. \textsuperscript{25} The things wherein there is no breath are bought for a most high price. \textsuperscript{26} They are borne upon shoulders, having no feet, whereby they declare unto men that they be nothing worth.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} They also that serve them are ashamed: for if they fall to the ground at any time, they cannot rise up again of themselves: neither, if one set them upright, can they move of themselves: neither, if they be bowed down, can they make themselves straight: but they set gifts before them, as unto dead men.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} As for the things that are sacrificed unto them, their priests sell and abuse; in like manner their wives lay up part thereof in salt; but unto the poor and impotent they give nothing of it. \textsuperscript{29} Menstruous women and women in childbed eat their sacrifices: by these things ye may know that they are no gods: fear them not. \textsuperscript{30} For how can they be called gods? because women set meat before the gods of silver, gold, and wood. \textsuperscript{31} And the priests sit in their temples, having their clothes rent, and their heads and beards shaven, and nothing upon their heads. \textsuperscript{32} They roar and cry before their gods, as men do at the feast when one is dead.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{33} The priests also take off their garments, and clothe their wives and children. \textsuperscript{34} Whether it be evil that one doeth unto them, or good, they are not able to recompense it: they can neither set up a king, nor put him down. \textsuperscript{35} In like manner, they can neither give riches nor money: though a man make a vow unto them, and keep it not, they will not require it. \textsuperscript{36} They can save no man from death, neither deliver the weak from the mighty. \textsuperscript{37} They cannot restore a blind man to his sight, nor help any man in his distress. \textsuperscript{38} They can shew no mercy to the widow, nor do good to the fatherless.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{39} Their gods of wood, and which are overlaid with gold and silver, are like the stones that be hewn out of the mountain: they that worship them shall be confounded.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{40} How should a man then think and say that they are gods, when even the Chaldeans themselves dishonour them? \textsuperscript{41} Who if they shall see one dumb that cannot speak, they bring him, and intreat Bel that he may speak, as though he were able to understand. \textsuperscript{42} Yet they cannot understand this themselves, and leave them: for they have no knowledge.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{43} The women also with cords about them, sitting in the ways, burn bran for perfume: but if any of them, drawn by some that passeth by, lie with him, she reproacheth her fellow, that she was not thought as worthy as herself, nor her cord broken. \textsuperscript{44} Whatsoever is done among them is false: how may it then be thought or said that they are gods?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{45} They are made of carpenters and goldsmiths: they can be nothing else than the workmen will have them to be. \textsuperscript{46} And they themselves that made them can never continue long; how should then the things that are made of them be gods?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{47} For they left lies and reproaches to them that come after. \textsuperscript{48} For when there cometh any war or plague upon them, the priests consult with themselves, where they may be hidden with them. \textsuperscript{49} How then cannot men perceive that they be no gods, which can neither save themselves from war, nor from plague? \textsuperscript{50} For seeing they be but of wood, and overlaid with silver and gold, it shall be known hereafter that they are false: \textsuperscript{51} and it shall manifestly appear to all nations and kings that they are no gods, but the works of men's hands, and that there is no work of God in them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{52} Who then may not know that they are no gods? \textsuperscript{53} For neither can they set up a king in the land, nor give rain unto men. \textsuperscript{54} Neither can they judge their own cause, nor redress a wrong, being unable: for they are as crows between heaven and earth.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{55} Whereupon when fire falleth upon the house of gods of wood, or laid over with gold or silver, their priests will flee away, and escape: but they themselves shall be burned asunder like beams. \textsuperscript{56} Moreover they cannot withstand any king or enemies: how can it then be thought or said that they be gods? \textsuperscript{57} Neither are those gods of wood, and laid over with silver or gold, able to escape either from thieves or robbers. \textsuperscript{58} Whose gold, and silver, and garments wherewith they are clothed, they that are strong do take, and go away withal: neither are they able to help themselves.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{59} Therefore it is better to be a king that sheweth his power, or else a profitable vessel in an house, which the owner shall have use of, than such false gods; or to be a door in an house, to keep such things safe as be therein, than such false gods; or a pillar of wood in a palace, than such false gods.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{60} For sun, moon, and stars, being bright, and sent to do their offices, are obedient. \textsuperscript{61} In like manner the lightning when it breaketh forth is easy to be seen: and after the same manner the wind bloweth in every country. \textsuperscript{62} And when God commandeth the clouds to go over the whole world, they do as they are bidden. \textsuperscript{63} And the fire sent from above to consume hills and woods doeth as it is commanded: but these are like unto them neither in shew nor power.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{64} Wherefore it is neither to be supposed nor said that they are gods, seeing they are able neither to judge causes, nor to do good unto men. \textsuperscript{65} Knowing therefore that they are no gods, fear them not.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{66} For they can neither curse nor bless kings: \textsuperscript{67} neither can they shew signs in the heavens among the heathen, nor shine as the sun, nor give light as the moon. \textsuperscript{68} The beasts are better than they: for they can get under a covert, and help themselves. \textsuperscript{69} It is then by no means manifest unto us that they are gods: therefore fear them not.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{70} For as a scarecrow in a garden of cucumbers keepeth nothing: so are their gods of wood, and laid over with silver and gold. \textsuperscript{71} And likewise their gods of wood, and laid over with silver and gold, are like to a white thorn in an orchard, that every bird sitteth upon; as also to a dead body, that is cast into the dark. \textsuperscript{72} And ye shall know them to be no gods by the bright purple that rotteth upon them: and they themselves afterward shall be eaten, and shall be a reproach in the country.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{73} Better therefore is the just man that hath no idols: for he shall be far from reproach.\par
\section*{Susanna}
\subsection*{Susanna 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} There dwelt a man in Babylon, called Joacim: \textsuperscript{2} and he took a wife, whose name was Susanna, the daughter of Chelcias, a very fair woman, and one that feared the Lord. \textsuperscript{3} Her parents also were righteous, and taught their daughter according to the law of Moses. \textsuperscript{4} Now Joacim was a very rich man, and had a fair garden joining unto his house; and to him resorted the Jews; because he was more honourable than all others.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} The same year were appointed two of the ancients of the people to be judges, such as the Lord spake of, that wickedness came from Babylon from ancient judges, who seemed to govern the people. \textsuperscript{6} These kept much at Joacim's house, and all that had any suits in law came unto them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Now when the people departed away at noon, Susanna went into her husband's garden to walk. \textsuperscript{8} And the two elders saw her going in every day, and walking; so that their lust was inflamed toward her. \textsuperscript{9} And they perverted their own mind, and turned away their eyes, that they might not look unto heaven, nor remember just judgments. \textsuperscript{10} And albeit they both were wounded with her love, yet durst not one shew another his grief. \textsuperscript{11} For they were ashamed to declare their lust, that they desired to have to do with her. \textsuperscript{12} Yet they watched diligently from day to day to see her.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} And the one said to the other, Let us now go home: for it is dinner time. \textsuperscript{14} So when they were gone out, they parted the one from the other, and turning back again they came to the same place; and after that they had asked one another the cause, they acknowledged their lust: then appointed they a time both together, when they might find her alone.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} And it fell out, as they watched a fit time, she went in as before with two maids only, and she was desirous to wash herself in the garden: for it was hot. \textsuperscript{16} And there was nobody there save the two elders, that had hid themselves, and watched her. \textsuperscript{17} Then she said to her maids, Bring me oil and washing balls, and shut the garden doors, that I may wash.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} And they did as she bade them, and shut the garden doors, and went out themselves at private doors to fetch the things that she had commanded them: but they saw not the elders, because they were hid.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} Now when the maids were gone forth, the two elders rose up, and ran unto her, saying, \textsuperscript{20} Behold, the garden doors are shut, that no man can see us, and we are in love with thee; therefore consent unto us, and lie with us. \textsuperscript{21} If thou wilt not, we will bear witness against thee, that a young man was with thee: and therefore thou didst send away thy maids from thee.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} Then Susanna sighed, and said, I am straitened on every side: for if I do this thing, it is death unto me: and if I do it not, I cannot escape your hands. \textsuperscript{23} It is better for me to fall into your hands, and not do it, than to sin in the sight of the Lord. \textsuperscript{24} With that Susanna cried with a loud voice: and the two elders cried out against her.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} Then ran the one, and opened the garden door. \textsuperscript{26} So when the servants of the house heard the cry in the garden, they rushed in at a private door, to see what was done unto her. \textsuperscript{27} But when the elders had declared their matter, the servants were greatly ashamed: for there was never such a report made of Susanna.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} And it came to pass the next day, when the people were assembled to her husband Joacim, the two elders came also full of mischievous imagination against Susanna to put her to death; \textsuperscript{29} and said before the people, Send for Susanna, the daughter of Chelcias, Joacim's wife. And so they sent. \textsuperscript{30} So she came with her father and mother, her children, and all her kindred.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{31} Now Susanna was a very delicate woman, and beauteous to behold. \textsuperscript{32} And these wicked men commanded to uncover her face (for she was covered), that they might be filled with her beauty. \textsuperscript{33} Therefore her friends and all that saw her wept.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{34} Then the two elders stood up in the midst of the people, and laid their hands upon her head. \textsuperscript{35} And she weeping looked up toward heaven: for her heart trusted in the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{36} And the elders said, As we walked in the garden alone, this woman came in with two maids, and shut the garden doors, and sent the maids away. \textsuperscript{37} Then a young man, who there was hid, came unto her, and lay with her. \textsuperscript{38} Then we that stood in a corner of the garden, seeing this wickedness, ran unto them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{39} And when we saw them together, the man we could not hold: for he was stronger than we, and opened the door, and leaped out. \textsuperscript{40} But having taken this woman, we asked who the young man was, but she would not tell us: these things do we testify. \textsuperscript{41} Then the assembly believed them, as those that were the elders and judges of the people: so they condemned her to death.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{42} Then Susanna cried out with a loud voice, and said, O everlasting God, that knowest the secrets, and knowest all things before they be: \textsuperscript{43} thou knowest that they have borne false witness against me, and, behold, I must die; whereas I never did such things as these men have maliciously invented against me. \textsuperscript{44} And the Lord heard her voice.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{45} Therefore when she was led to be put to death, the Lord raised up the holy spirit of a young youth, whose name was Daniel: \textsuperscript{46} who cried with a loud voice, I am clear from the blood of this woman.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{47} Then all the people turned them toward him, and said, What mean these words that thou hast spoken? \textsuperscript{48} So he standing in the midst of them said, Are ye such fools, ye sons of Israel, that without examination or knowledge of the truth ye have condemned a daughter of Israel? \textsuperscript{49} Return again to the place of judgment: for they have borne false witness against her.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{50} Wherefore all the people turned again in haste, and the elders said unto him, Come, sit down among us, and shew it us, seeing God hath given thee the honour of an elder. \textsuperscript{51} Then said Daniel unto them, Put these two aside one far from another, and I will examine them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{52} So when they were put asunder one from another, he called one of them, and said unto him, O thou that art waxen old in wickedness, now thy sins which thou hast committed aforetime are come to light : \textsuperscript{53} for thou hast pronounced false judgment, and hast condemned the innocent, and hast let the guilty go free; albeit the Lord saith, The innocent and righteous shalt thou not slay. \textsuperscript{54} Now then, if thou hast seen her, tell me, Under what tree sawest thou them companying together? And he said, Under a mastick tree.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{55} And Daniel said, Very well; thou hast lied against thine own head; for even now the angel of God hath received the sentence of God to cut thee in two. \textsuperscript{56} So he put him aside, and commanded to bring the other, and said unto him, O thou seed of Chanaan, and not of Juda, beauty hath deceived thee, and lust hath perverted thine heart. \textsuperscript{57} Thus have ye dealt with the daughters of Israel, and they for fear companied with you: but the daughter of Juda would not abide your wickedness. \textsuperscript{58} Now therefore tell me, Under what tree didst thou take them companying together? And he said, Under a holm tree.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{59} Then said Daniel unto him, Well; thou hast also lied against thine own head: for the angel of God waiteth with the sword to cut thee in two, that he may destroy you.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{60} With that all the assembly cried out with a loud voice, and praised God, who saveth them that trust in him. \textsuperscript{61} And they arose against the two elders, for Daniel had convicted them of false witness by their own mouth: \textsuperscript{62} and according to the law of Moses they did unto them in such sort as they maliciously intended to do to their neighbour: and they put them to death. Thus the innocent blood was saved the same day.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{63} Therefore Chelcias and his wife praised God for their daughter Susanna, with Joacim her husband, and all their kindred, because there was no dishonesty found in her. \textsuperscript{64} From that day forth was Daniel had in great reputation in the sight of the people.\par
\section*{Bel and the Dragon}
\subsection*{Bel and the Dragon 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And king Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus of Persia received his kingdom. \textsuperscript{2} And Daniel conversed with the king, and was honoured above all his friends.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} Now the Babylonians had an idol, called Bel, and there were spent upon him every day twelve great measures of fine flour, and forty sheep, and six vessels of wine. \textsuperscript{4} And the king worshipped it, and went daily to adore it: but Daniel worshipped his own God. And the king said unto him, Why dost not thou worship Bel? \textsuperscript{5} Who answered and said, Because I may not worship idols made with hands, but the living God, who hath created the heaven and the earth, and hath sovereignty over all flesh.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} Then said the king unto him, Thinkest thou not that Bel is a living god? seest thou not how much he eateth and drinketh every day? \textsuperscript{7} Then Daniel smiled, and said, O king, be not deceived: for this is but clay within, and brass without, and did never eat or drink any thing.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} So the king was wroth, and called for his priests, and said unto them, If ye tell me not who this is that devoureth these expences, ye shall die. \textsuperscript{9} But if ye can certify me that Bel devoureth them, then Daniel shall die: for he hath spoken blasphemy against Bel. And Daniel said unto the king, Let it be according to thy word.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} Now the priests of Bel were threescore and ten, beside their wives and children. And the king went with Daniel into the temple of Bel. \textsuperscript{11} So Bel's priests said, Lo, we go out: but thou, O king, set on the meat, and make ready the wine, and shut the door fast, and seal it with thine own signet; \textsuperscript{12} and to-morrow when thou comest in, if thou findest not that Bel hath eaten up all, we will suffer death: or else Daniel, that speaketh falsely against us. \textsuperscript{13} And they little regarded it: for under the table they had made a privy entrance, whereby they entered in continually, and consumed those things.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} So when they were gone forth, the king set meats before Bel. Now Daniel had commanded his servants to bring ashes, and those they strewed throughout all the temple in the presence of the king alone: then went they out, and shut the door, and sealed it with the king's signet, and so departed. \textsuperscript{15} Now in the night came the priests with their wives and children, as they were wont to do, and did eat and drink up all.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} In the morning betime the king arose, and Daniel with him. \textsuperscript{17} And the king said, Daniel, are the seals whole? And he said, Yea, O king, they be whole. \textsuperscript{18} And as soon as he had opened the door, the king looked upon the table, and cried with a loud voice, Great art thou, O Bel, and with thee is no deceit at all.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} Then laughed Daniel, and held the king that he should not go in, and said, Behold now the pavement, and mark well whose footsteps are these. \textsuperscript{20} And the king said, I see the footsteps of men, women, and children. And then the king was angry, \textsuperscript{21} and took the priests with their wives and children, who shewed him the private doors, where they came in, and consumed such things as were upon the table. \textsuperscript{22} Therefore the king slew them, and delivered Bel into Daniel's power, who destroyed him and his temple.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} And in that same place there was a great dragon, which they of Babylon worshipped. \textsuperscript{24} And the king said unto Daniel, Wilt thou also say that this is of brass? lo, he liveth, he eateth and drinketh; thou canst not say that he is no living god: therefore worship him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} Then said Daniel unto the king, I will worship the Lord my God: for he is the living God. \textsuperscript{26} But give me leave, O king, and I shall slay this dragon without sword or staff. The king said, I give thee leave. \textsuperscript{27} Then Daniel took pitch, and fat, and hair, and did seethe them together, and made lumps thereof: this he put in the dragon's mouth, and so the dragon burst in sunder: and Daniel said, Lo, these are the gods ye worship.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} When they of Babylon heard that, they took great indignation, and conspired against the king, saying, The king is become a Jew, and he hath destroyed Bel, he hath slain the dragon, and put the priests to death. \textsuperscript{29} So they came to the king, and said, Deliver us Daniel, or else we will destroy thee and thine house.\par
