\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Now the king came with a barbarous and haughty mind to do far worse to the Jews, than had been done in his father's time. \textsuperscript{10} Which things when Judas perceived, he commanded the multitude to call upon the Lord night and day, that if ever at any other time, he would now also help them, being at the point to be put from their law, from their country, and from the holy temple: \textsuperscript{11} and that he would not suffer the people, that had even now been but a little refreshed, to be in subjection to the blasphemous nations.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} So when they had all done this together, and besought the merciful Lord with weeping and fasting, and lying flat upon the ground three days long, Judas, having exhorted them, commanded they should be in a readiness.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} And Judas, being apart with the elders, determined, before the king's host should enter into Judea, and get the city, to go forth and try the matter in fight by the help of the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} So when he had committed all to the Creator of the world, and exhorted his soldiers to fight manfully, even unto death, for the laws, the temple, the city, the country, and the commonwealth, he camped by Modin: \textsuperscript{15} and having given the watchword to them that were about him, Victory is of God; with the most valiant and choice young men he went in into the king's tent by night, and slew in the camp about four thousand men, and the chiefest of the elephants, with all that were upon him. \textsuperscript{16} And at last they filled the camp with fear and tumult, and departed with good success. \textsuperscript{17} This was done in the break of the day, because the protection of the Lord did help him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} Now when the king had taken a taste of the manliness of the Jews, he went about to take the holds by policy, \textsuperscript{19} and marched toward Bethsura, which was a strong hold of the Jews: but he was put to flight, failed, and lost of his men: \textsuperscript{20} for Judas had conveyed unto them that were in it such things as were necessary.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} But Rhodocus, who was in the Jews' host, disclosed the secrets to the enemies; therefore he was sought out, and when they had gotten him, they put him in prison.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} The king treated with them in Bethsura the second time, gave his hand, took their's, departed, fought with Judas, was overcome: \textsuperscript{23} heard that Philip, who was left over the affairs in Antioch, was desperately bent, confounded, intreated the Jews, submitted himself, and sware to all equal conditions, agreed with them, and offered sacrifice, honoured the temple, and dealt kindly with the place, \textsuperscript{24} and accepted well of Maccabeus, made him principal governor from Ptolemais unto the Gerrhenians; \textsuperscript{25} came to Ptolemais: the people there were grieved for the covenants; for they stormed, because they would make their covenants void.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{26} Lysias went up to the judgment seat, said as much as could be in defence of the cause, persuaded, pacified, made them well affected, returned to Antioch. Thus it went touching the king's coming and departing.\par
\subsection*{Maccabees II 14}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} After three years was Judas informed, that Demetrius the son of Seleucus, having entered by the haven of Tripolis with a great power and navy, \textsuperscript{2} had taken the country, and killed Antiochus, and Lysias his protector.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} Now one Alcimus, who had been high priest, and had defiled himself wilfully in the times of their mingling with the Gentiles , seeing that by no means he could save himself, nor have any more access to the holy altar, \textsuperscript{4} came to king Demetrius in the hundred and one and fiftieth year, presenting unto him a crown of gold, and a palm, and also of the boughs which were used solemnly in the temple: and so that day he held his peace.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Howbeit, having gotten opportunity to further his foolish enterprise, and being called into council by Demetrius, and asked how the Jews stood affected, and what they intended, he answered thereunto: \textsuperscript{6} Those of the Jews that be called Assideans, whose captain is Judas Maccabeus, nourish war, and are seditious, and will not let the realm be in peace.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} Therefore I, being deprived of mine ancestors' honour, I mean the high priesthood, am now come hither: \textsuperscript{8} first, verily for the unfeigned care I have of things pertaining to the king; and secondly, even for that I intend the good of mine own citizens: for all our nation is in no small misery through the unadvised dealing of them aforesaid.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} Wherefore, O king, seeing thou knowest all these things, be careful for the country, and our nation, which is pressed on every side, according to the clemency that thou readily shewest unto all. \textsuperscript{10} For as long as Judas liveth, it is not possible that the state should be quiet. \textsuperscript{11} This was no sooner spoken of him, but others of the king's friends, being maliciously set against Judas, did more incense Demetrius.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} And forthwith calling Nicanor, who had been master of the elephants, and making him governor over Judea, he sent him forth, \textsuperscript{13} commanding him to slay Judas, and to scatter them that were with him, and to make Alcimus high priest of the great temple. \textsuperscript{14} Then the heathen, that had fled out of Judea from Judas, came to Nicanor by flocks, thinking the harm and calamities of the Jews to be their welfare.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} Now when the Jews heard of Nicanor's coming, and that the heathen were up against them, they cast earth upon their heads, and made supplication to him that had established his people for ever, and who always helpeth his portion with manifestation of his presence. \textsuperscript{16} So at the commandment of the captain they removed straightways from thence, and came near unto them at the town of Dessau.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Now Simon, Judas' brother, had joined battle with Nicanor, but was somewhat discomfited through the sudden silence of his enemies. \textsuperscript{18} Nevertheless Nicanor, hearing of the manliness of them that were with Judas, and the courageousness that they had to fight for their country, durst not try the matter by the sword. \textsuperscript{19} Wherefore he sent Posidonius, and Theodotus, and Mattathias, to make peace.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} So when they had taken long advisement thereupon, and the captain had made the multitude acquainted therewith, and it appeared that they were all of one mind, they consented to the covenants, \textsuperscript{21} and appointed a day to meet in together by themselves: and when the day came, and stools were set for either of them, \textsuperscript{22} Judas placed armed men ready in convenient places, lest some treachery should be suddenly practised by the enemies: so they made a peaceable conference.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} Now Nicanor abode in Jerusalem, and did no hurt, but sent away the people that came flocking unto him. \textsuperscript{24} And he would not willingly have Judas out of his sight: for he loved the man from his heart. \textsuperscript{25} He prayed him also to take a wife, and to beget children: so he married, was quiet, and took part of this life.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{26} But Alcimus, perceiving the love that was betwixt them, and considering the covenants that were made, came to Demetrius, and told him that Nicanor was not well affected toward the state: for that he had ordained Judas, a traitor to his realm, to be the king's successor. \textsuperscript{27} Then the king being in a rage, and provoked with the accusations of the most wicked man, wrote to Nicanor, signifying that he was much displeased with the covenants, and commanding him that he should send Maccabeus prisoner in all haste unto Antioch.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} When this came to Nicanor's hearing, he was much confounded in himself, and took it grievously that he should make void the articles which were agreed upon, the man being in no fault. \textsuperscript{29} But because there was no dealing against the king, he watched his time to accomplish this thing by policy.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} Notwithstanding, when Maccabeus saw that Nicanor began to be churlish unto him, and that he entreated him more roughly than he was wont, perceiving that such sour behaviour came not of good, he gathered together not a few of his men, and withdrew himself from Nicanor. \textsuperscript{31} But the other, knowing that he was notably prevented by Judas' policy, came into the great and holy temple, and commanded the priests, that were offering their usual sacrifices, to deliver him the man. \textsuperscript{32} And when they sware that they could not tell where the man was whom he sought, \textsuperscript{33} he stretched out his right hand toward the temple, and made an oath in this manner: If ye will not deliver me Judas as a prisoner, I will lay this temple of God even with the ground, and I will break down the altar, and erect a notable temple unto Bacchus.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{34} After these words, he departed. Then the priests lifted up their hands toward heaven, and besought him that was ever a defender of their nation, saying in this manner; \textsuperscript{35} Thou, O Lord of all things, who hast need of nothing, wast pleased that the temple of thine habitation should be among us: \textsuperscript{36} therefore now, O holy Lord of all holiness, keep this house ever undefiled, which lately was cleansed, and stop every unrighteous mouth.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{37} Now was there accused unto Nicanor one Razis, one of the elders of Jerusalem, a lover of his countrymen, and a man of very good report, who for his kindness was called a father of the Jews. \textsuperscript{38} For in the former times, when they mingled not themselves with the Gentiles, he had been accused of Judaism, and did boldly jeopard his body and life with all vehemency for the religion of the Jews.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{39} So Nicanor, willing to declare the hate that he bare unto the Jews, sent above five hundred men of war to take him: \textsuperscript{40} for he thought by taking him to do the Jews much hurt. \textsuperscript{41} Now when the multitude would have taken the tower, and violently broken into the outer door, and bade that fire should be brought to burn it, he being ready to be taken on every side fell upon his sword; \textsuperscript{42} choosing rather to die manfully, than to come into the hands of the wicked, to be abused otherwise than beseemed his noble birth: \textsuperscript{43} but missing his stroke through haste, the multitude also rushing within the doors, he ran boldly up to the wall, and cast himself down manfully among the thickest of them. \textsuperscript{44} But they quickly giving back, and a space being made, he fell down into the midst of the void place.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{45} Nevertheless, while there was yet breath within him, being inflamed with anger, he rose up; and though his blood gushed out like spouts of water, and his wounds were grievous, yet he ran through the midst of the throng; and standing upon a steep rock, \textsuperscript{46} when as his blood was now quite gone, he plucked out his bowels, and taking them in both his hands, he cast them upon the throng, and calling upon the Lord of life and spirit to restore him those again, he thus died.\par
\subsection*{Maccabees II 15}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} But Nicanor, hearing that Judas and his company were in the strong places about Samaria, resolved without any danger to set upon them on the sabbath day.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} Nevertheless the Jews that were compelled to go with him said, O destroy not so cruelly and barbarously, but give honour to that day, which he, that seeth all things, hath honoured with holiness above other days .\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} Then the most ungracious wretch demanded, if there were a Mighty one in heaven, that had commanded the sabbath day to be kept. \textsuperscript{4} And when they said, There is in heaven a living Lord, and mighty, who commanded the seventh day to be kept: \textsuperscript{5} then said the other, And I also am mighty upon earth, and I command to take arms, and to do the king's business. Yet he obtained not to have his wicked will done. \textsuperscript{6} So Nicanor in exceeding pride and haughtiness determined to set up a public monument of his victory over Judas and them that were with him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} But Maccabeus had ever sure confidence that the Lord would help him: \textsuperscript{8} wherefore he exhorted his people not to fear the coming of the heathen against them, but to remember the help which in former times they had received from heaven, and now to expect the victory and aid, which should come unto them from the Almighty. \textsuperscript{9} And so comforting them out of the law and the prophets, and withal putting them in mind of the battles that they won afore, he made them more cheerful.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} And when he had stirred up their minds, he gave them their charge, shewing them therewithal the falsehood of the heathen, and the breach of oaths. \textsuperscript{11} Thus he armed every one of them, not so much with defence of shields and spears, as with comfortable and good words: and beside that, he told them a dream worthy to be believed, as if it had been so indeed, which did not a little rejoice them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} And this was his vision: That Onias, who had been high priest, a virtuous and a good man, reverend in conversation, gentle in condition, well spoken also, and exercised from a child in all points of virtue, holding up his hands prayed for the whole body of the Jews. \textsuperscript{13} This done, in like manner there appeared a man with gray hairs, and exceeding glorious, who was of a wonderful and excellent majesty. \textsuperscript{14} Then Onias answered, saying, This is a lover of the brethren, who prayeth much for the people, and for the holy city, to wit , Jeremias the prophet of God. \textsuperscript{15} Whereupon Jeremias holding forth his right hand gave to Judas a sword of gold, and in giving it spake thus, \textsuperscript{16} Take this holy sword, a gift from God, with the which thou shalt wound the adversaries.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} Thus being well comforted by the words of Judas, which were very good, and able to stir them up to valour, and to encourage the hearts of the young men, they determined not to pitch camp, but courageously to set upon them, and manfully to try the matter by conflict, because the city and the sanctuary and the temple were in danger. \textsuperscript{18} For the care that they took for their wives, and their children, their brethren, and kinsfolks, was in least account with them: but the greatest and principal fear was for the holy temple. \textsuperscript{19} Also they that were in the city took not the least care, being troubled for the conflict abroad.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} And now, when as all looked what should be the trial, and the enemies were already come near, and the army was set in array, and the beasts conveniently placed, and the horsemen set in wings,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} Maccabeus seeing the coming of the multitude, and the divers preparations of armour, and the fierceness of the beasts, stretched out his hands toward heaven, and called upon the Lord that worketh wonders, knowing that victory cometh not by arms, but even as it seemeth good to him, he giveth it to such as are worthy: \textsuperscript{22} therefore in his prayer he said after this manner: O Lord, thou didst send thine angel in the time of Ezekias king of Judea, and didst slay in the host of Sennacherib an hundred fourscore and five thousand: \textsuperscript{23} wherefore now also, O Lord of heaven, send a good angel before us for a fear and dread unto them; \textsuperscript{24} and through the might of thine arm let those be stricken with terror, that come against thy holy people to blaspheme. And he ended thus.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} Then Nicanor and they that were with him came forward with trumpets and songs. \textsuperscript{26} But Judas and his company encountered the enemies with invocation and prayer. \textsuperscript{27} So that fighting with their hands, and praying unto God with their hearts, they slew no less than thirty and five thousand men: for through the appearance of God they were greatly cheered.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} Now when the battle was done, returning again with joy, they knew that Nicanor lay dead in his harness. \textsuperscript{29} Then they made a great shout and a noise, praising the Almighty in their own language.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} And Judas , who was ever the chief defender of the citizens both in body and mind, and who continued his love toward his countrymen all his life, commanded to strike off Nicanor's head, and his hand with his shoulder, and bring them to Jerusalem.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{31} So when he was there, and had called them of his nation together, and set the priests before the altar, he sent for them that were of the tower, \textsuperscript{32} and shewed them vile Nicanor's head, and the hand of that blasphemer, which with proud brags he had stretched out against the holy temple of the Almighty.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{33} And when he had cut out the tongue of that ungodly Nicanor, he commanded that they should give it by pieces unto the fowls, and hang up the reward of his madness before the temple. \textsuperscript{34} So every man praised toward the heaven the glorious Lord, saying, Blessed be he that hath kept his own place undefiled. \textsuperscript{35} He hanged also Nicanor's head upon the tower, an evident and manifest sign unto all of the help of the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{36} And they ordained all with a common decree in no case to let that day pass without solemnity, but to celebrate the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which in the Syrian tongue is called Adar, the day before Mardocheus' day. \textsuperscript{37} Thus went it with Nicanor: and from that time forth the Hebrews had the city in their power. And here will I make an end.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{38} And if I have done well, and as is fitting the story, it is that which I desired: but if slenderly and meanly, it is that which I could attain unto. \textsuperscript{39} For as it is hurtful to drink wine or water alone; and as wine mingled with water is pleasant, and delighteth the taste: even so speech finely framed delighteth the ears of them that read the story. And here shall be an end.\par
\section*{Esdras I}
\subsection*{Esdras I 1}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And Josias held the feast of the passover in Jerusalem unto his Lord, and offered the passover the fourteenth day of the first month; \textsuperscript{2} having set the priests according to their daily courses, being arrayed in long garments, in the temple of the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{3} And he spake unto the Levites, the holy ministers of Israel, that they should hallow themselves unto the Lord, to set the holy ark of the Lord in the house that king Solomon the son of David had built: \textsuperscript{4} and said , Ye shall no more bear the ark upon your shoulders: now therefore serve the Lord your God, and minister unto his people Israel, and prepare you after your families and kindreds, \textsuperscript{5} according as David the king of Israel prescribed, and according to the magnificence of Solomon his son: and standing in the temple according to the several dignity of the families of you the Levites, who minister in the presence of your brethren the children of Israel, \textsuperscript{6} offer the passover in order, and make ready the sacrifices for your brethren, and keep the passover according to the commandment of the Lord, which was given unto Moses.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} And unto the people that was found there Josias gave thirty thousand lambs and kids, and three thousand calves: these things were given of the king's allowance, according as he promised, to the people, to the priests and to the Levites. \textsuperscript{8} And Helkias, Zacharias, and Syelus, the governors of the temple, gave to the priests for the passover two thousand and six hundred sheep, and three hundred calves. \textsuperscript{9} And Jeconias, and Samaias, and Nathanael his brother, and Assabias, and Ochiel, and Joram, captains over thousands, gave to the Levites for the passover five thousand sheep, and seven hundred calves.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} And when these things were done, the priests and Levites, having the unleavened bread, stood in very comely order according to the kindreds, \textsuperscript{11} and according to the several dignities of the fathers, before the people, to offer to the Lord, as it is written in the book of Moses: and thus did they in the morning. \textsuperscript{12} And they roasted the passover with fire, as appertaineth: as for the sacrifices, they sod them in brass pots and pans with a good savour, \textsuperscript{13} and set them before all the people: and afterward they prepared for themselves, and for the priests their brethren, the sons of Aaron. \textsuperscript{14} For the priests offered the fat until night: and the Levites prepared for themselves, and the priests their brethren, the sons of Aaron. \textsuperscript{15} The holy singers also, the sons of Asaph, were in their order, according to the appointment of David, to wit, Asaph, Zacharias, and Jeduthun, who was of the king's retinue. \textsuperscript{16} Moreover the porters were at every gate; it was not lawful for any to go from his ordinary service: for their brethren the Levites prepared for them. \textsuperscript{17} Thus were the things that belonged to the sacrifices of the Lord accomplished in that day, that they might hold the passover, \textsuperscript{18} and offer sacrifices upon the altar of the Lord, according to the commandment of king Josias.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} So the children of Israel which were present held the passover at that time, and the feast of sweet bread seven days. \textsuperscript{20} And such a passover was not kept in Israel since the time of the prophet Samuel. \textsuperscript{21} Yea, all the kings of Israel held not such a passover as Josias, and the priests, and the Levites, and the Jews, held with all Israel that were found dwelling at Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{22} In the eighteenth year of the reign of Josias was this passover kept.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} And the works of Josias were upright before his Lord with an heart full of godliness. \textsuperscript{24} As for the things that came to pass in his time, they were written in former times, concerning those that sinned, and did wickedly against the Lord above all people and kingdoms, and how they grieved him exceedingly, so that the words of the Lord rose up against Israel.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} Now after all these acts of Josias it came to pass that Pharaoh the king of Egypt came to raise war at Carcamys upon Euphrates: and Josias went out against him. \textsuperscript{26} But the king of Egypt sent to him, saying, What have I to do with thee, O king of Judea? \textsuperscript{27} I am not sent out from the Lord God against thee; for my war is upon Euphrates: and now the Lord is with me, yea the Lord is with me hasting me forward: depart from me, and be not against the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} Howbeit Josias did not turn back his chariot from him, but undertook to fight with him, not regarding the words of the prophet Jeremy spoken by the mouth of the Lord: \textsuperscript{29} but joined battle with him in the plain of Mageddo, and the princes came against king Josias. \textsuperscript{30} Then said the king unto his servants, Carry me away out of the battle; for I am very weak. And immediately his servants took him away out of the battle. \textsuperscript{31} Then gat he up upon his second chariot; and being brought back to Jerusalem died, and was buried in his father's sepulchre. \textsuperscript{32} And in all Jewry they mourned for Josias, yea, Jeremy the prophet lamented for Josias, and the chief men with the women made lamentation for him unto this day: and this was given out for an ordinance to be done continually in all the nation of Israel.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{33} These things are written in the book of the stories of the kings of Judah, and every one of the acts that Josias did, and his glory, and his understanding in the law of the Lord; and the things that he had done before, and the things now recited, are reported in the book of the kings of Israel and Judea.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{34} And the people took Joachaz the son of Josias, and made him king instead of Josias his father when he was twenty and three years old. \textsuperscript{35} And he reigned in Judea and in Jerusalem three months: and then the king of Egypt deposed him from reigning in Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{36} And he set a tax upon the land of an hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{37} The king of Egypt also made king Joacim his brother king of Judea and Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{38} And he bound Joacim and the nobles: but Zaraces his brother he apprehended, and brought him out of Egypt. \textsuperscript{39} Five and twenty years old was Joacim when he was made king in the land of Judea and Jerusalem; and he did evil before the Lord. \textsuperscript{40} Wherefore against him Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon came up, and bound him with a chain of brass, and carried him into Babylon. \textsuperscript{41} Nabuchodonosor also took of the holy vessels of the Lord, and carried them away, and set them in his own temple at Babylon. \textsuperscript{42} But those things that are recorded of him, and of his uncleanness and impiety, are written in the chronicles of the kings.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{43} And Joacim his son reigned in his stead: he was made king being eighteen years old; \textsuperscript{44} and reigned but three months and ten days in Jerusalem; and did evil before the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{45} So after a year Nabuchodonosor sent and caused him to be brought into Babylon with the holy vessels of the Lord. \textsuperscript{46} And made Sedecias king of Judea and Jerusalem, when he was one and twenty years old; and he reigned eleven years: \textsuperscript{47} and he did evil also in the sight of the Lord, and cared not for the words that were spoken unto him by the prophet Jeremy from the mouth of the Lord. \textsuperscript{48} And after that king Nabuchodonosor had made him to swear by the name of the Lord, he forswore himself, and rebelled; and hardening his neck, and his heart, he transgressed the laws of the Lord God of Israel. \textsuperscript{49} The governors also of the people and of the priests did many things against the laws, and passed all the pollutions of all nations, and defiled the temple of the Lord, which was sanctified in Jerusalem.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{50} Nevertheless the God of their fathers sent by his messenger to call them back, because he spared them and his tabernacle also. \textsuperscript{51} But they had his messengers in derision; and, in the day that the Lord spake unto them, they made a sport of his prophets: \textsuperscript{52} so far forth, that he, being wroth with his people for their great ungodliness, commanded the kings of the Chaldees to come up against them; \textsuperscript{53} who slew their young men with the sword, yea, even within the compass of their holy temple, and spared neither young man nor maid, old man nor child, among them; for he delivered all into their hands. \textsuperscript{54} And they took all the holy vessels of the Lord, both great and small, with the vessels of the ark of God, and the king's treasures, and carried them away into Babylon. \textsuperscript{55} As for the house of the Lord, they burnt it, and brake down the walls of Jerusalem, and set fire upon her towers: \textsuperscript{56} and as for her glorious things, they never ceased till they had consumed and brought them all to nought; and the people that were not slain with the sword he carried into Babylon: \textsuperscript{57} who became servants to him and his children, till the Persians reigned, to fulfil the word of the Lord spoken by the mouth of Jeremy: \textsuperscript{58} until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths, the whole time of her desolation shall she rest, until the full term of seventy years.\par
\subsection*{Esdras I 2}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, that the word of the Lord might be accomplished, that he had promised by the mouth of Jeremy; \textsuperscript{2} the Lord raised up the spirit of Cyrus the king of the Persians, and he made proclamation through all his kingdom, and also by writing, \textsuperscript{3} saying, Thus saith Cyrus king of the Persians; The Lord of Israel, the most high Lord, hath made me king of the whole world, \textsuperscript{4} and commanded me to build him an house at Jerusalem in Jewry.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} If therefore there be any of you that are of his people, let his Lord be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem that is in Judea, and build the house of the Lord of Israel: for he is the Lord that dwelleth in Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{6} Whosoever then dwell in the places about, let them help him, those, I say, that are his neighbours, with gold, and with silver, \textsuperscript{7} with gifts, with horses, and with cattle, and other things, which have been set forth by vow, for the temple of the Lord at Jerusalem.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} Then the chief of the families of Judea and of the tribe of Benjamin stood up; the priests also, and the Levites, and all they whose mind the Lord had moved to go up, and to build an house for the Lord at Jerusalem, \textsuperscript{9} and they that dwelt round about them, and helped them in all things with silver and gold, with horses and cattle, and with very many free gifts of a great number whose minds were stirred up thereto. \textsuperscript{10} King Cyrus also brought forth the holy vessels which Nabuchodonosor had carried away from Jerusalem, and had set up in his temple of idols.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Now when Cyrus king of the Persians had brought them forth, he delivered them to Mithridates his treasurer: \textsuperscript{12} and by him they were delivered to Sanabassar the governor of Judea. \textsuperscript{13} And this was the number of them; A thousand golden cups, and a thousand of silver, censers of silver twenty-nine, vials of gold thirty, and of silver two thousand four hundred and ten, and a thousand other vessels. \textsuperscript{14} So all the vessels of gold and of silver, which were carried away, were five thousand four hundred threescore and nine. \textsuperscript{15} These were brought back by Sanabassar, together with them of the captivity, from Babylon to Jerusalem.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} But in the time of Artaxerxes king of the Persians Belemus, and Mithridates, and Tabellius, and Rathumus, and Beeltethmus, and Samellius the secretary, with the rest that were in commission with them, dwelling in Samaria and other places, wrote unto him against them that dwelt in Judea and Jerusalem this letter following; \textsuperscript{17} To king Artaxerxes our lord, Thy servants, Rathumus the storywriter, and Samellius the scribe, and the rest of their council, and the judges that are in Celosyria and Phenice. \textsuperscript{18} Be it now known to the lord the king, that the Jews that are come up from you to us, being come into Jerusalem, that rebellious and wicked city, do build the marketplaces, and repair the walls of it, and do lay the foundation of the temple. \textsuperscript{19} Now if this city and the walls thereof be made up again, they will not only refuse to give tribute, but also rebel against kings.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} And forasmuch as the things pertaining to the temple are now in hand, we think it meet not to neglect such a matter, \textsuperscript{21} but to speak unto our lord the king, to the intent that, if it be thy pleasure, it may be sought out in the books of thy fathers: \textsuperscript{22} and thou shalt find in the chronicles what is written concerning these things, and shalt understand that that city was rebellious, troubling both kings and cities: \textsuperscript{23} and that the Jews were rebellious, and raised always wars therein; for the which cause even this city was made desolate. \textsuperscript{24} Wherefore now we do declare unto thee, O lord the king, that if this city be built again, and the walls thereof set up anew, thou shalt from henceforth have no passage into Celosyria and Phenice.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} Then the king wrote back again to Rathumus the storywriter, to Beeltethmus, to Semellius the scribe, and to the rest that were in commission, and dwellers in Samaria and Syria and Phenice, after this manner; \textsuperscript{26} I have read the epistle which ye have sent unto me: therefore I commanded to make diligent search, and it hath been found that that city was from the beginning practising against kings; \textsuperscript{27} and the men therein were given to rebellion and war: and that mighty kings and fierce were in Jerusalem, who reigned and exacted tributes in Celosyria and Phenice. \textsuperscript{28} Now therefore I have commanded to hinder those men from building the city, and heed to be taken that there be no more done in it; \textsuperscript{29} and that those wicked workers proceed no further to the annoyance of kings.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} Then king Artaxerxes his letters being read, Rathumus, and Semellius the scribe, and the rest that were in commission with them, removing in haste toward Jerusalem with a troop of horsemen and a multitude of people in battle array, began to hinder the builders; and the building of the temple in Jerusalem ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.\par
\subsection*{Esdras I 3}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now when Darius reigned, he made a great feast unto all his subjects, and unto all his household, and unto all the princes of Media and Persia, \textsuperscript{2} and to all the governors and captains and lieutenants that were under him, from India unto Ethiopia, in the hundred twenty and seven provinces. \textsuperscript{3} And when they had eaten and drunken, and being satisfied were gone home, then Darius the king went into his bedchamber, and slept, and soon after awaked.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} Then three young men, that were of the guard that kept the king's body, spake one to another; \textsuperscript{5} Let every one of us speak a sentence: he that shall overcome, and whose sentence shall seem wiser than the others, unto him shall the king Darius give great gifts, and great things in token of victory: \textsuperscript{6} as to be clothed in purple, to drink in gold, and to sleep upon gold, and a chariot with bridles of gold, and an headtire of fine linen, and a chain about his neck: \textsuperscript{7} and he shall sit next to Darius because of his wisdom, and shall be called Darius's cousin.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} And then every one wrote his sentence, sealed it, and laid it under the pillow of king Darius; \textsuperscript{9} and said that, when the king is risen, some will give him the writing; and of whose side the king and the three princes of Persia shall judge that his sentence is the wisest, to him shall the victory be given, as was appointed. \textsuperscript{10} The first wrote, Wine is the strongest. \textsuperscript{11} The second wrote, The king is strongest. \textsuperscript{12} The third wrote, Women are strongest: but above all things Truth beareth away the victory.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Now when the king was risen up, they took their writings, and delivered them unto him, and so he read them : \textsuperscript{14} and sending forth he called all the princes of Persia and Media, and the governors, and the captains, and the lieutenants, and the chief officers; \textsuperscript{15} and sat him down in the royal seat of judgment; and the writing was read before them. \textsuperscript{16} And he said, Call the young men, and they shall declare their own sentences. So they were called, and came in. \textsuperscript{17} And he said unto them, Declare unto us your mind concerning the writings.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} and he said thus, O ye men, how exceeding strong is wine! it causeth all men to err that drink it: \textsuperscript{19} it maketh the mind of the king and of the fatherless child to be all one; of the bondman and of the freeman, of the poor man and of the rich: \textsuperscript{20} it turneth also every thought into jollity and mirth, so that a man remembereth neither sorrow nor debt: \textsuperscript{21} and it maketh every heart rich, so that a man remembereth neither king nor governor; and it maketh to speak all things by talents: \textsuperscript{22} and when they are in their cups, they forget their love both to friends and brethren, and a little after draw out swords: \textsuperscript{23} but when they are from the wine, they remember not what they have done. \textsuperscript{24} O ye men, is not wine the strongest, that enforceth to do thus? And when he had so spoken, he held his peace.\par
\subsection*{Esdras I 4}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then the second, that had spoken of the strength of the king, began to say, \textsuperscript{2} O ye men, do not men excel in strength, that bear rule over sea and land, and all things in them? \textsuperscript{3} But yet the king is more mighty: for he is lord of all these things, and hath dominion over them; and whatsoever he commandeth them they do. \textsuperscript{4} If he bid them make war the one against the other, they do it: if he send them out against the enemies, they go, and break down mountains, walls, and towers. \textsuperscript{5} They slay and are slain, and transgress not the king's commandment: if they get the victory, they bring all to the king, as well the spoil, as all things else.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} Likewise for those that are no soldiers, and have not to do with wars, but use husbandry, when they have reaped again that which they had sown, they bring it to the king, and compel one another to pay tribute unto the king. \textsuperscript{7} And yet he is but one man: if he command to kill, they kill; if he command to spare, they spare; \textsuperscript{8} if he command to smite, they smite; if he command to make desolate, they make desolate; if he command to build, they build; \textsuperscript{9} if he command to cut down, they cut down; if he command to plant, they plant. \textsuperscript{10} So all his people and his armies obey him: furthermore he lieth down, he eateth and drinketh, and taketh his rest: \textsuperscript{11} and these keep watch round about him, neither may any one depart, and do his own business, neither disobey they him in any thing. \textsuperscript{12} O ye men, how should not the king be mightiest, when in such sort he is obeyed? And he held his tongue.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} Then the third, who had spoken of women, and of the truth, (this was Zorobabel) began to speak. \textsuperscript{14} O ye men, it is not the great king, nor the multitude of men, neither is it wine, that excelleth: who is it then that ruleth them, or hath the lordship over them? are they not women? \textsuperscript{15} Women have borne the king and all the people that bear rule by sea and land. \textsuperscript{16} Even of them came they: and they nourished them up that planted the vineyards, from whence the wine cometh. \textsuperscript{17} These also make garments for men; these bring glory unto men; and without women cannot men be. \textsuperscript{18} Yea, and if men have gathered together gold and silver, or any other goodly thing, do they not love a woman which is comely in favour and beauty? \textsuperscript{19} And letting all those things go, do they not gape, and even with open mouth fix their eyes fast on her; and have not all men more desire unto her than unto silver or gold, or any goodly thing whatsoever?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} A man leaveth his own father that brought him up, and his own country, and cleaveth unto his wife. \textsuperscript{21} He sticketh not to spend his life with his wife, and remembereth neither father, nor mother, nor country. \textsuperscript{22} By this also ye must know that women have dominion over you: do ye not labour and toil, and give and bring all to the woman? \textsuperscript{23} Yea, a man taketh his sword, and goeth his way to rob and to steal, to sail upon the sea and upon rivers; \textsuperscript{24} and looketh upon a lion, and goeth in the darkness; and when he hath stolen, spoiled, and robbed, he bringeth it to his love. \textsuperscript{25} Wherefore a man loveth his wife better than father or mother. \textsuperscript{26} Yea, many there be that have run out of their wits for women, and become servants for their sakes. \textsuperscript{27} Many also have perished, have erred, and sinned, for women.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} And now do ye not believe me? is not the king great in his power? do not all regions fear to touch him? \textsuperscript{29} Yet did I see him and Apame the king's concubine, the daughter of the admirable Bartacus, sitting at the right hand of the king, \textsuperscript{30} and taking the crown from the king's head, and setting it upon her own head; she also struck the king with her left hand. \textsuperscript{31} And yet for all this the king gaped and gazed upon her with open mouth: if she laughed upon him, he laughed also: but if she took any displeasure at him, the king was fain to flatter, that she might be reconciled to him again. \textsuperscript{32} O ye men, how can it be but women should be strong, seeing they do thus?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{33} Then the king and the princes looked one upon another: so he began to speak of the truth. \textsuperscript{34} O ye men, are not women strong? great is the earth, high is the heaven, swift is the sun in his course, for he compasseth the heavens round about, and fetcheth his course again to his own place in one day. \textsuperscript{35} Is he not great that maketh these things? therefore great is the truth, and stronger than all things. \textsuperscript{36} All the earth calleth upon the truth, and the heaven blesseth it: all works shake and tremble at it, and with it is no unrighteous thing. \textsuperscript{37} Wine is wicked, the king is wicked, women are wicked, all the children of men are wicked; and such are all their wicked works, and there is no truth in them; in their unrighteousness also they shall perish.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{38} As for the truth, it endureth, and is always strong; it liveth and conquereth for evermore. \textsuperscript{39} With her there is no accepting of persons or rewards: but she doeth the things that are just, and refraineth from all unjust and wicked things; and all men do well like of her works. \textsuperscript{40} Neither in her judgment is any unrighteousness; and she is the strength, kingdom, power, and majesty of all ages. Blessed be the God of truth.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{41} And with that he held his peace. And all the people then shouted, and said, Great is Truth, and mighty above all things. \textsuperscript{42} Then said the king unto him, Ask what thou wilt more than is appointed in the writings, and we will give it thee, because thou art found wisest; and thou shalt sit next me, and shalt be called my cousin. \textsuperscript{43} Then said he unto the king, Remember thy vow, which thou hast vowed to build Jerusalem, in the day when thou camest to thy kingdom, \textsuperscript{44} and to send away all the vessels that were taken away out of Jerusalem, which Cyrus set apart, when he vowed to destroy Babylon, and to send them again thither. \textsuperscript{45} Thou also hast vowed to build up the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees. \textsuperscript{46} And now, O lord the king, this is that which I require, and which I desire of thee, and this is the princely liberality proceeding from thyself: I desire therefore that thou make good the vow, the performance whereof with thine own mouth thou hast vowed to the King of heaven.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{47} Then Darius the king stood up, and kissed him, and wrote letters for him unto all the treasurers and lieutenants and captains and governors, that they should safely convey on their way both him, and all those that go up with him to build Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{48} He wrote letters also unto the lieutenants that were in Celosyria and Phenice, and unto them in Libanus, that they should bring cedar wood from Libanus unto Jerusalem, and that they should build the city with him.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{49} Moreover he wrote for all the Jews that went out of his realm up into Jewry, concerning their freedom, that no officer, no ruler, no lieutenant, nor treasurer, should forcibly enter into their doors; \textsuperscript{50} and that all the country which they hold should be free without tribute; and that the Edomites should give over the villages of the Jews which then they held: \textsuperscript{51} yea, that there should be yearly given twenty talents to the building of the temple, until the time that it were built; \textsuperscript{52} and other ten talents yearly, to maintain the burnt offerings upon the altar every day, as they had a commandment to offer seventeen: \textsuperscript{53} and that all they that went from Babylon to build the city should have free liberty, as well they as their posterity, and all the priests that went away. \textsuperscript{54} He wrote also concerning the charges, and the priests' vestments wherein they minister; \textsuperscript{55} and likewise for the charges of the Levites, to be given them until the day that the house were finished, and Jerusalem builded up. \textsuperscript{56} And he commanded to give to all that kept the city pensions and wages. \textsuperscript{57} He sent away also all the vessels from Babylon, that Cyrus had set apart; and all that Cyrus had given in commandment, the same charged he also to be done, and sent unto Jerusalem.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{58} Now when this young man was gone forth, he lifted up his face to heaven toward Jerusalem, and praised the King of heaven, \textsuperscript{59} and said, From thee cometh victory, from thee cometh wisdom, and thine is the glory, and I am thy servant. \textsuperscript{60} Blessed art thou, who hast given me wisdom: and to thee I give thanks, O Lord of our fathers. \textsuperscript{61} And so he took the letters, and went out, and came unto Babylon, and told it all his brethren. \textsuperscript{62} And they praised the God of their fathers, because he had given them freedom and liberty \textsuperscript{63} to go up, and to build Jerusalem, and the temple which is called by his name: and they feasted with instruments of musick and gladness seven days.\par
\subsection*{Esdras I 5}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} After this were the principal men of the families chosen according to their tribes, to go up with their wives and sons and daughters, with their menservants and maidservants, and their cattle. \textsuperscript{2} And Darius sent with them a thousand horsemen, till they had brought them back to Jerusalem safely, and with musical instruments , tabrets and flutes. \textsuperscript{3} And all their brethren played, and he made them go up together with them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} And these are the names of the men which went up, according to their families, among their tribes, after their several heads. \textsuperscript{5} The priests, the sons of Phinees, the sons of Aaron: Jesus the son of Josedec, the son of Saraias, and Joacim the son of Zorobabel, the son of Salathiel, of the house of David, out of the kindred of Phares, of the tribe of Judah; \textsuperscript{6} who spake wise sentences before Darius the king of Persia in the second year of his reign, in the month Nisan, which is the first month. \textsuperscript{7} And these are they of Jewry that came up from the captivity, where they dwelt as strangers, whom Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon had carried away unto Babylon. \textsuperscript{8} And they returned unto Jerusalem, and to the other parts of Jewry, every man to his own city, who came with Zorobabel, and Jesus, Nehemias, Zaraias, Reesaias, Enenius, Mardocheus, Beelsarus, Aspharasus, Reelius, Roimus, and Baana, their guides.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} The number of them of the nation, and their governors: the sons of Phoros, two thousand an hundred seventy and two: the sons of Saphat, four hundred seventy and two:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} The sons of Ares, seven hundred fifty and six:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} The sons of Phaath Moab, among the sons of Jesus and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} The sons of Elam, a thousand two hundred fifty and four: the sons of Zathui, nine hundred seventy and five: the sons of Corbe, seven hundred and five: the sons of Bani, six hundred forty and eight:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{13} The sons of Bebai, six hundred thirty and three: the sons of Argai, one thousand three hundred twenty and two:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{14} The sons of Adonikan, six hundred thirty and seven: the sons of Bagoi, two thousand six hundred and six: the sons of Adin, four hundred fifty and four:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{15} The sons of Ater, son of Ezekias, ninety and two: the sons of Cilan and Azenan, threescore and seven: the sons of Azarus, four hundred thirty and two:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} The sons of Annis, an hundred and one: the sons of Arom, thirty-two: the sons of Bassai, three hundred twenty and three: the sons of Arsiphurith, an hundred and two:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} The sons of Beterus, three thousand and five: the sons of Bethlomon, an hundred twenty and three:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{18} They of Netophah, fifty and five: they of Anathoth, an hundred fifty and eight: they of Bethsamos, forty and two:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} They of Kiriathiarius, twenty and five: they of Caphira and Beroth, seven hundred forty and three.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{20} They of Chadias and Ammidoi, four hundred twenty and two: they of Cirama and Gabbes, six hundred twenty and one:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} They of Macalon, an hundred twenty and two: they of Betolius, fifty and two: the sons of Nephis, an hundred fifty and six:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{22} The sons of Calamolalus and Onus, seven hundred twenty and five: the sons of Jerechus, two hundred forty and five:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} The sons of Sanaas, three thousand three hundred and one.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{24} The priests: the sons of Jeddu, the son of Jesus, among the sons of Sanasib, eight hundred seventy and two: the sons of Emmeruth, two hundred fifty and two:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} The sons of Phassaron, a thousand forty and seven: the sons of Carme, two hundred and seventeen.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{26} The Levites: the sons of Jessue, and Cadmiel, and Banuas, and Sudias, seventy and four.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} The holy singers: the sons of Asaph, an hundred twenty and eight.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} The porters: the sons of Salum, the sons of Atar, the sons of Tolman, the sons of Dacobi, the sons of Ateta, the sons of Tobis, in all an hundred thirty and nine.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{29} The servants of the temple: the sons of Esau, the sons of Asipha, the sons of Tabaoth, the sons of Ceras, the sons of Sud, the sons of Phaleas, the sons of Labana, the sons of Agraba,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{30} The sons of Acud, the sons of Uta, the sons of Cetab, the sons of Agaba, the sons of Subai, the sons of Anan, the sons of Cathua, the sons of Geddur,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{31} The sons of Jairus, the sons of Daisan, the sons of Noeba, the sons of Chaseba, the sons of Cazera, the sons of Ozia, the sons of Phinees, the sons of Azara, the sons of Bastai, the sons of Assana, the sons of Mani, the sons of Naphisi, the sons of Acuph, the sons of Achiba, the sons of Asub, the sons of Pharacim, the sons of Basalem,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{32} The sons of Meedda, the sons of Coutha, the sons of Charea, the sons of Barcue, the sons of Serar, the sons of Thomoi, the sons of Nasith, the sons of Atipha.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{33} The sons of the servants of Solomon: the sons of Azaphioth, the sons of Pharira, the sons of Jeieli, the sons of Lozon, the sons of Isdael, the sons of Saphui,\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{34} The sons of Hagia, the sons of Phacareth, the sons of Sabi, the sons of Sarothi, the sons of Misaias, the sons of Gas, the sons of Addus, the sons of Suba, the sons of Apherra, the sons of Barodis, the sons of Saphag, the sons of Allom.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{35} All the ministers of the temple, and the sons of the servants of Solomon, were three hundred seventy and two.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{36} These came up from Thermeleth and Thelersas, Charaathalan leading them, and Aalar; \textsuperscript{37} they could not shew their families or their stock, how they were of Israel: the sons of Dalan, the son of Baenan, the sons of Necodan, six hundred fifty and two.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{38} And of the priests that usurped the office of the priesthood, and were not found: the sons of Obdia, the sons of Acbos, the sons of Jaddus, who married Augia one of the daughters of Phaezeldæus, and was named after his name.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{39} And when the description of the kindred of these men was sought in the register, and was not found, they were removed from executing the office of the priesthood: \textsuperscript{40} for unto them said Nehemias and Attharias, that they should not be partakers of the holy things, till there arose up an high priest clothed with doctrine and truth.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{41} So of Israel, from them of twelve years old and upward, beside menservants and womenservants, they were all in number forty thousand, two thousand three hundred and sixty. \textsuperscript{42} Their menservants and handmaids were seven thousand three hundred thirty and seven: the singing men and singing women, two hundred forty and five: \textsuperscript{43} four hundred thirty and five camels, seven thousand thirty and six horses, two hundred forty and five mules, five thousand five hundred twenty and five beasts used to the yoke:\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{44} And certain of the chief of their families, when they came to the temple of God that is in Jerusalem, vowed to set up the house again in his own place according to their ability, \textsuperscript{45} and to give into the holy treasury of the works a thousand pounds of gold, five thousand of silver, and an hundred priestly vestments. \textsuperscript{46} And so dwelt the priests and the Levites and the people in Jerusalem, and in the country, the singers also and the porters; and all Israel in their villages.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{47} But when the seventh month was at hand, and when the children of Israel were every man in his own place, they came altogether with one consent into the open place of the first gate which is toward the east. \textsuperscript{48} Then stood up Jesus the son of Josedec, and his brethren the priests, and Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and his brethren, and made ready the altar of the God of Israel, \textsuperscript{49} to offer burnt sacrifices upon it, according as it is expressly commanded in the book of Moses the man of God.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{50} And there were gathered unto them out of the other nations of the land, and they erected the altar upon his own place, because all the nations of the land were at enmity with them, and oppressed them; and they offered sacrifices according to the time, and burnt offerings to the Lord both morning and evening. \textsuperscript{51} Also they held the feast of tabernacles, as it is commanded in the law, and offered sacrifices daily, as was meet: \textsuperscript{52} and after that, the continual oblations, and the sacrifice of the sabbaths, and of the new moons, and of all holy feasts.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{53} And all they that had made any vow to God began to offer sacrifices to God from the first day of the seventh month, although the temple of the Lord was not yet built.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{54} And they gave unto the masons and carpenters money, meat, and drink, with cheerfulness. \textsuperscript{55} Unto them of Zidon also and Tyre they gave carrs, that they should bring cedar trees from Libanus, which should be brought by floats to the haven of Joppe, according as it was commanded them by Cyrus king of the Persians.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{56} And in the second year and second month after his coming to the temple of God at Jerusalem began Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and Jesus the son of Josedec, and their brethren, and the priests, and the Levites, and all they that were come unto Jerusalem out of the captivity: \textsuperscript{57} and they laid the foundation of the house of God in the first day of the second month, in the second year after they were come to Jewry and Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{58} And they appointed the Levites from twenty years old over the works of the Lord. Then stood up Jesus, and his sons and brethren, and Cadmiel his brother, and the sons of Emadabun, with the sons of Joda the son of Eliadud, with their sons and brethren, all Levites, with one accord setters forward of the business, labouring to advance the works in the house of the Lord. So the builders built the temple of the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{59} And the priests stood arrayed in their vestments with musical instruments and trumpets; and the Levites the sons of Asaph had cymbals, \textsuperscript{60} singing songs of thanksgiving, and praising the Lord, according as David the king of Israel had ordained.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{61} And they sung with loud voices songs to the praise of the Lord, because his mercy and glory is for ever in all Israel. \textsuperscript{62} And all the people sounded trumpets, and shouted with a loud voice, singing songs of thanksgiving unto the Lord for the rearing up of the house of the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{63} Also of the priests and Levites, and of the chief of their families, the ancients who had seen the former house came to the building of this with weeping and great crying. \textsuperscript{64} But many with trumpets and joy shouted with loud voice, \textsuperscript{65} insomuch that the trumpets might not be heard for the weeping of the people; yet the multitude sounded marvellously, so that it was heard afar off.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{66} Wherefore when the enemies of the tribe of Juda and Benjamin heard it, they came to know what the noise of trumpets should mean . \textsuperscript{67} And they perceived that they that were of the captivity did build the temple unto the Lord God of Israel. \textsuperscript{68} So they went to Zorobabel and Jesus, and to the chief of the families, and said unto them, We will build together with you. \textsuperscript{69} For we likewise, as ye, do obey your Lord, and do sacrifice unto him from the days of Azbazareth the king of the Assyrians, who brought us hither.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{70} Then Zorobabel and Jesus and the chief of the families of Israel said unto them, It is not for us and you to build together an house unto the Lord our God. \textsuperscript{71} We ourselves alone will build unto the Lord of Israel, according as Cyrus the king of the Persians hath commanded us. \textsuperscript{72} But the heathen of the land lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building; \textsuperscript{73} and by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions, they hindered the finishing of the building all the time that king Cyrus lived: so they were hindered from building for the space of two years, until the reign of Darius.\par
\subsection*{Esdras I 6}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Now in the second year of the reign of Darius, Aggeus and Zacharias the son of Addo, the prophets, prophesied unto the Jews in Jewry and Jerusalem in the name of the Lord God of Israel, which was upon them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{2} Then stood up Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and Jesus the son of Josedec, and began to build the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, the prophets of the Lord being with them, and helping them. \textsuperscript{3} At the same time came unto them Sisinnes the governor of Syria and Phenice, with Sathrabuzanes and his companions, and said unto them, \textsuperscript{4} By whose appointment do ye build this house and this roof, and perform all the other things? and who are the workmen that perform these things?\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} Nevertheless the elders of the Jews obtained favour, because the Lord had visited the captivity; \textsuperscript{6} and they were not hindered from building, until such time as signification was given unto Darius concerning them, and an answer received.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{7} The copy of the letters which Sisinnes, governor of Syria and Phenice, and Sathrabuzanes, with their companions, rulers in Syria and Phenice, wrote and sent unto Darius; To king Darius, greeting: \textsuperscript{8} Let all things be known unto our lord the king, that being come into the country of Judea, and entered into the city of Jerusalem, we found in the city of Jerusalem the ancients of the Jews that were of the captivity \textsuperscript{9} building an house unto the Lord, great and new, of hewn and costly stones, and the timber already laid upon the walls. \textsuperscript{10} And those works are done with great speed, and the work goeth on prosperously in their hands, and with all glory and diligence is it made.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{11} Then asked we these elders, saying, By whose commandment build ye this house, and lay the foundations of these works? \textsuperscript{12} Therefore to the intent that we might give knowledge unto thee by writing, we demanded of them who were the chief doers, and we required of them the names in writing of their principal men. \textsuperscript{13} So they gave us this answer, We are the servants of the Lord which made heaven and earth. \textsuperscript{14} And as for this house, it was builded many years ago by a king of Israel great and strong, and was finished. \textsuperscript{15} But when our fathers provoked God unto wrath, and sinned against the Lord of Israel which is in heaven, he gave them over into the power of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, king of the Chaldees; \textsuperscript{16} who pulled down the house, and burned it, and carried away the people captives unto Babylon.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{17} But in the first year that king Cyrus reigned over the country of Babylon, Cyrus the king wrote to build this house. \textsuperscript{18} And the holy vessels of gold and of silver, that Nabuchodonosor had carried away out of the house at Jerusalem, and had set them in his own temple, those Cyrus the king brought forth again out of the temple at Babylon, and they were delivered to Zorobabel, that is , to Sanabassarus the ruler, \textsuperscript{19} with commandment that he should carry away the same vessels, and put them in the temple at Jerusalem; and that the temple of the Lord should be built in that place. \textsuperscript{20} Then the same Sanabassarus, being come hither, laid the foundations of the house of the Lord at Jerusalem; and from that time to this being still building, it is not yet finished.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{21} Now therefore, if it seem good unto the king, let search be made among the records of king Cyrus: \textsuperscript{22} and if it be found that the building of the house of the Lord at Jerusalem hath been done with the consent of king Cyrus, and if our lord the king be so minded, let him signify unto us thereof.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} Then commanded king Darius to seek among the records at Babylon: and so at Ecbatana the palace, which is in the country of Media, there was found a roll wherein these things were recorded. \textsuperscript{24} In the first year of the reign of Cyrus, king Cyrus commanded that the house of the Lord at Jerusalem should be built again, where they do sacrifice with continual fire: \textsuperscript{25} whose height shall be sixty cubits, and the breadth sixty cubits, with three rows of hewn stones, and one row of new wood of that country; and the expences thereof to be given out of the house of king Cyrus: \textsuperscript{26} and that the holy vessels of the house of the Lord, both of gold and silver, that Nabuchodonosor took out of the house at Jerusalem, and brought to Babylon, should be restored to the house at Jerusalem, and be set in the place where they were before.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{27} And also he commanded that Sisinnes the governor of Syria and Phenice, and Sathrabuzanes, and their companions, and those which were appointed rulers in Syria and Phenice, should be careful not to meddle with the place, but suffer Zorobabel the servant of the Lord, and governor of Judea, and the elders of the Jews, to build the house of the Lord in that place. \textsuperscript{28} I have commanded also to have it built up whole again; and that they look diligently to help those that be of the captivity of the Jews, till the house of the Lord be finished: \textsuperscript{29} and out of the tribute of Celosyria and Phenice, a portion carefully to be given these men for the sacrifices of the Lord, that is , to Zorobabel the governor, for bullocks, and rams, and lambs; \textsuperscript{30} and also corn, salt, wine, and oil, and that continually every year without further question, according as the priests that be in Jerusalem shall signify to be daily spent: \textsuperscript{31} that offerings may be made to the most high God for the king and for his children, and that they may pray for their lives. \textsuperscript{32} And he commanded that whosoever should transgress, yea, or make light of any thing herein written, out of his own house should a tree be taken, and he thereon be hanged, and all his goods seized for the king.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{33} The Lord therefore, whose name is there called upon, utterly destroy every king and nation, that stretcheth out his hand to hinder or endamage that house of the Lord in Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{34} I Darius the king have ordained that according unto these things it be done with diligence.\par
\subsection*{Esdras I 7}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} Then Sisinnes the governor of Celosyria and Phenice, and Sathrabuzanes, with their companions, following the commandments of king Darius, \textsuperscript{2} did very carefully oversee the holy works, assisting the ancients of the Jews and governors of the temple. \textsuperscript{3} And so the holy works prospered, when Aggeus and Zacharias the prophets prophesied.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{4} And they finished these things by the commandment of the Lord God of Israel; and with the consent of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia, \textsuperscript{5} the holy house was finished in the three and twentieth day of the month Adar, in the sixth year of king Darius.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{6} And the children of Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and others that were of the captivity, that were added unto them, did according to the things written in the book of Moses. \textsuperscript{7} And to the dedication of the temple of the Lord they offered an hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; \textsuperscript{8} and twelve goats for the sin of all Israel, according to the number of the chief of the tribes of Israel. \textsuperscript{9} The priests also and the Levites stood arrayed in their vestments, according to their kindreds, in the service of the Lord God of Israel, according to the book of Moses: and the porters at every gate.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{10} And the children of Israel that were of the captivity held the passover the fourteenth day of the first month, after that the priests and the Levites were sanctified, \textsuperscript{11} together with all the children of the captivity; for they were sanctified, because the Levites were all sanctified together.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{12} And so they offered the passover for all them of the captivity, and for their brethren the priests, and for themselves. \textsuperscript{13} And the children of Israel that came out of the captivity did eat, even all they that had separated themselves from the abominations of the people of the land, and sought the Lord. \textsuperscript{14} And they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days, making merry before the Lord, \textsuperscript{15} for that he had turned the counsel of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the works of the Lord God of Israel.\par
\subsection*{Esdras I 8}
\noindent \textsuperscript{1} And after these things, when Artaxerxes the king of the Persians reigned, came Esdras the son of Azaraias, the son of Zechrias, the son of Helchias, the son of Salum, \textsuperscript{2} the son of Sadduc, the son of Achitob, the son of Amarias, the son of Ozias, the son of Boccas, the son of Abisai, the son of Phinees, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the chief priest. \textsuperscript{3} This Esdras went up from Babylon, as a scribe, being very ready in the law of Moses, that was given by the God of Israel. \textsuperscript{4} And the king did him honour: for he found grace in his sight in all his requests.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{5} There went up with him also certain of the children of Israel, of the priests, of the Levites, of the holy singers, porters, and ministers of the temple, unto Jerusalem, \textsuperscript{6} in the seventh year of the reign of Artaxerxes, in the fifth month, this was the king's seventh year; for they went from Babylon in the first day of the first month, and came to Jerusalem, according to the prosperous journey which the Lord gave to him. \textsuperscript{7} For Esdras had very great skill, so that he omitted nothing of the law and commandments of the Lord, but taught all Israel the ordinances and judgments.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{8} Now the copy of the commission, which was written from Artaxerxes the king, and came to Esdras the priest and reader of the law of the Lord, is this that followeth;\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{9} King Artaxerxes unto Esdras the priest and reader of the law of the Lord sendeth greeting: \textsuperscript{10} Having determined to deal graciously, I have given order, that such of the nation of the Jews, and of the priests and Levites, being within our realm, as are willing and desirous, should go with thee unto Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{11} As many therefore as have a mind thereunto, let them depart with thee, as it hath seemed good both to me and my seven friends the counsellors; \textsuperscript{12} that they may look unto the affairs of Judea and Jerusalem, agreeably to that which is in the law of the Lord; \textsuperscript{13} and carry the gifts unto the Lord of Israel to Jerusalem, which I and my friends have vowed, and all the gold and silver that in the country of Babylon can be found, to the Lord in Jerusalem, \textsuperscript{14} with that also which is given of the people for the temple of the Lord their God at Jerusalem: and that silver and gold may be collected for bullocks, rams, and lambs, and things thereunto appertaining; \textsuperscript{15} to the end that they may offer sacrifices unto the Lord upon the altar of the Lord their God, which is in Jerusalem.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{16} And whatsoever thou and thy brethren will do with the silver and gold, that do, according to the will of thy God. \textsuperscript{17} And the holy vessels of the Lord, which are given thee for the use of the temple of thy God, which is in Jerusalem, thou shalt set before thy God in Jerusalem. \textsuperscript{18} And whatsoever thing else thou shalt remember for the use of the temple of thy God, thou shalt give it out of the king's treasury.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{19} And I king Artaxerxes have also commanded the keepers of the treasures in Syria and Phenice, that whatsoever Esdras the priest and the reader of the law of the most high God shall send for, they should give it him with speed, \textsuperscript{20} to the sum of an hundred talents of silver, likewise also of wheat even to an hundred cors, and an hundred pieces of wine, and other things in abundance. \textsuperscript{21} Let all things be performed after the law of God diligently unto the most high God, that wrath come not upon the kingdom of the king and his sons. \textsuperscript{22} I command you also, that ye require no tax, nor any other imposition, of any of the priests, or Levites, or holy singers, or porters, or ministers of the temple, or of any that have doings in this temple, and that no man have authority to impose any thing upon them.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{23} And thou, Esdras, according to the wisdom of God ordain judges and justices, that they may judge in all Syria and Phenice all those that know the law of thy God; and those that know it not thou shalt teach. \textsuperscript{24} And whosoever shall transgress the law of thy God, and of the king, shall be punished diligently, whether it be by death, or other punishment, by penalty of money, or by imprisonment.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{25} Then said Esdras the scribe, Blessed be the only Lord God of my fathers, who hath put these things into the heart of the king, to glorify his house that is in Jerusalem: \textsuperscript{26} and hath honoured me in the sight of the king, and his counsellors, and all his friends and nobles. \textsuperscript{27} Therefore was I encouraged by the help of the Lord my God, and gathered together men of Israel to go up with me.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{28} And these are the chief according to their families and several dignities, that went up with me from Babylon in the reign of king Artaxerxes: \textsuperscript{29} of the sons of Phinees, Gerson: of the sons of Ithamar, Gamaliel: of the sons of David, Lettus the son of Sechenias: \textsuperscript{30} of the sons of Pharez, Zacharias; and with him were counted an hundred and fifty men: \textsuperscript{31} of the sons of Pahath Moab, Eliaonias, the son of Zaraias, and with him two hundred men: \textsuperscript{32} of the sons of Zathoe, Sechenias the son of Jezelus, and with him three hundred men: of the sons of Adin, Obeth the son of Jonathan, and with him two hundred and fifty men: \textsuperscript{33} of the sons of Elam, Josias son of Gotholias, and with him seventy men: \textsuperscript{34} of the sons of Saphatias, Zaraias son of Michael, and with him threescore and ten men: \textsuperscript{35} of the sons of Joab, Abadias son of Jezelus, and with him two hundred and twelve men: \textsuperscript{36} of the sons of Bania, Salimoth son of Josaphias, and with him an hundred and threescore men: \textsuperscript{37} of the sons of Babi, Zacharias son of Bebai, and with him twenty and eight men: \textsuperscript{38} of the sons of Astath, Johannes son of Acatan, and with him an hundred and ten men: \textsuperscript{39} of the sons of Adonikam the last, and these are the names of them, Eliphalet, son of Geuel, and Samaias, and with them seventy men: \textsuperscript{40} of the sons of Bago, Uthi the son of Istalcurus, and with him seventy men.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{41} And these I gathered together to the river called Theras, where we pitched our tents three days: and then I surveyed them. \textsuperscript{42} But when I had found there none of the priests and Levites, \textsuperscript{43} then sent I unto Eleazar, and Iduel, and Mæa, and Masman, \textsuperscript{44} and Alnathan, and Samaias, and Joribas, and Nathan, Ennatan, Zacharias, and Mosollamus, principal men and learned. \textsuperscript{45} And I bade them that they should go unto Loddeus the captain, who was in the place of the treasury: \textsuperscript{46} and commanded them that they should speak unto Loddeus, and to his brethren, and to the treasurers in that place, to send us such men as might execute the priests' office in the house of the Lord.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{47} And by the mighty hand of our Lord they brought unto us skilful men of the sons of Mooli the son of Levi, the son of Israel, Asebebia, and his sons, and his brethren, who were eighteen. \textsuperscript{48} And Asebia, and Annuus, and Osaias his brother, of the sons of Chanuneus, and their sons, were twenty men. \textsuperscript{49} And of the servants of the temple whom David had ordained, and the principal men for the service of the Levites to wit, the servants of the temple, two hundred and twenty, the catalogue of whose names were shewed.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{50} And there I vowed a fast unto the young men before our Lord, to desire of him a prosperous journey both for us and them that were with us, for our children, and for the cattle: \textsuperscript{51} for I was ashamed to ask the king footmen, and horsemen, and conduct for safeguard against our adversaries. \textsuperscript{52} For we had said unto the king, that the power of the Lord our God should be with them that seek him, to support them in all ways. \textsuperscript{53} And again we besought our Lord as touching these things, and found him favourable unto us.\par
\noindent \textsuperscript{54} Then I separated twelve of the chief of the priests, Esebrias, and Samias, and ten men of their brethren with them: \textsuperscript{55} and I weighed them the gold, and the silver, and the holy vessels of the house of our Lord, which the king, and his council, and the princes, and all Israel, had given. \textsuperscript{56} And when I had weighed it, I delivered unto them six hundred and sixty talents of silver, and silver vessels of an hundred talents, and an hundred talents of gold, \textsuperscript{57} and twenty golden vessels, and twelve vessels of brass, even of fine brass, glittering like gold.\par
